verses.text:
श्रुत्वा हनूमतो वाक्यं यथावदभिभाषितम्।
रामः प्रीतिसमायुक्तो वाक्यमुत्तरमब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Filled with delight to hear the story of Hanumān, faithfully narrated, Śrī Rāma made the following appropriate reply: (1)

verses.text:
कृतं हनूमता कार्यं सुमहद् भुवि दुर्लभम्।
मनसापि यदन्येन न शक्यं धरणीतले॥ २॥
verses.m: “A very great work, rare on earth, has been done by Hanumān, which could not be accomplished even in thought by another on the earth’s surface. (2)

verses.text:
नहि तं परिपश्यामि यस्तरेत महोदधिम्।
अन्यत्र गरुडाद् वायोरन्यत्र च हनूमतः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Indeed, I know of no other than Garuḍa (the king of birds and the carrier of Lord Viṣṇu) and the wind-god and of no other than Hanumān, who could cross the expansive sea. (3)

verses.text:
देवदानवयक्षाणां गन्धर्वोरगरक्षसाम्।
अप्रधृष्यां पुरीं लङ्कां रावणेन सुरक्षिताम्॥ ४॥
प्रविष्टः सत्त्वमाश्रित्य जीवन् को नाम निष्क्रमेत्।
को विशेत् सुदुराधर्षां राक्षसैश्च सुरक्षिताम्॥ ५॥
यो वीर्यबलसम्पन्नो न समः स्याद्धनूमतः।
भृत्यकार्यं हनुमता सुग्रीवस्य कृतं महत्।
एवं विधाय स्वबलं सदृशं विक्रमस्य च॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Having penetrated by dint of his courage deeply into Laṅkā, which cannot be taken violently even by gods, demons and Yakṣas nor by Gandharvas, Nāgas and ogres and is well-protected by Rāvaṇa, who else could actually escape alive? Who can, in fact, even enter the city, which is exceedingly difficult to assail and is strongly guarded by ogres, unless he is richly endowed with virility and strength like Hanumān? Nay, a momentous service has been rendered by Hanumān to Sugrīva by manifesting his strength in proportion to his valour in this way. (4—6)

verses.text:
यो हि भृत्यो नियुक्तः सन् भर्त्रा कर्मणि दुष्करे।
कुर्यात् तदनुरागेण तमाहुः पुरुषोत्तमम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “They speak of that servant as the foremost among men, who, when entrusted by his master with a duty difficult to perform, does even more; of course, in consonance with that work. (7)

verses.text:
यो नियुक्तः परं कार्यं न कुर्यान्नृपतेः प्रियम्।
भृत्यो युक्तः समर्थश्च तमाहुर्मध्यमं नरम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “The wise speak of that servant as a mediocre man, who, though qualified and capable, does not, when confided with some work, accomplish any other allied work liked by the king. (8)

verses.text:
नियुक्तो नृपतेः कार्यं न कुर्याद् यः समाहितः।
भृत्यो युक्तः समर्थश्च तमाहुः पुरुषाधमम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “People dub that servant as the lowest of men, who, though qualified and capable, does not, when entrusted with a duty, carry out the behest of a king with a composed mind. (9)

verses.text:
तन्नियोगे नियुक्तेन कृतं कृत्यं हनूमता।
न चात्मा लघुतां नीतः सुग्रीवश्चापि तोषितः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Extra work was also done by Hanumān when entrusted with the duty of search for Sītā; yet no dishonour was brought to his own self and Sugrīva too was gratified by him by his act of valour. (10)

verses.text:
अहं च रघुवंशश्च लक्ष्मणश्च महाबलः।
वैदेह्या दर्शनेनाद्य धर्मतः परिरक्षिताः॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Through the discovery of Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, the entire race of Raghu, as well as myself and Lakṣmaṇa too, who is endowed with extraordinary might, have been saved from destruction today in consonance with righteousness. (11)

verses.text:
इदं तु मम दीनस्य मनो भूयः प्रकर्षति।
यदिहास्य प्रियाख्यातुर्न कुर्मि सदृशं प्रियम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “It undoubtedly wrings my soul further, wretched that I am, to think that I have nothing worthwhile to offer to Hanumān, who has communicated to me this delightful news. (12)

verses.text:
एष सर्वस्वभूतस्तु परिष्वङ्गो हनूमतः।
मया कालमिमं प्राप्य दत्तस्तस्य महात्मनः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “This embrace, which is all that I can call my own at this moment, is unreservedly offered to this high-souled Hanumān.” (13)

verses.text:
इत्युक्त्वा प्रीतिहृष्टाङ्गो रामस्तं परिषस्वजे।
हनूमन्तं कृतात्मानं कृतकार्यमुपागतम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: Saying so, Śrī Rāma, whose limbs were thrilled with delight, embraced the celebrated Hanumān, who had disciplined his mind and who had just returned having carried out his behest. (14)

verses.text:
ध्यात्वा पुनरुवाचेदं वचनं रघुसत्तमः।
हरीणामीश्वरस्यापि सुग्रीवस्योपशृण्वतः॥ १५॥
verses.m: Exercising his mind awhile, Śrī Rāma, the foremost among the Raghus, once more spoke as follows, Sugrīva, the ruler of monkeys, too, listening: (15)

verses.text:
सर्वथा सुकृतं तावत् सीतायाः परिमार्गणम्।
सागरं तु समासाद्य पुनर्नष्टं मनो मम॥ १६॥
verses.m: “The search for Sītā has, of course, been conducted thoroughly well. On duly reaching the ocean, however, my mind gets dejected once more. (16)

verses.text:
कथं नाम समुद्रस्य दुष्पारस्य महाम्भसः।
हरयो दक्षिणं पारं गमिष्यन्ति समागताः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “How on earth will the monkeys, gather together for the purpose of recovering Sītā from the enemy’s hands, reach the southern shore of the sea, which is so difficult to cross and comprises a vast sheet of water? (17)

verses.text:
यद्यप्येष तु वृत्तान्तो वैदेह्या गदितो मम।
समुद्रपारगमने हरीणां किमिवोत्तरम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: Although this fact of the impassability of the sea has been mentioned even by Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, what step should be taken for the passage of the monkeys across the sea?” (18)

verses.text:
इत्युक्त्वा शोकसम्भ्रान्तो रामः शत्रुनिबर्हणः।
हनूमन्तं महाबाहुस्ततो ध्यानमुपागमत्॥ १९॥
verses.m: Having spoken as aforesaid to Hanumān, the mighty-armed Śrī Rāma, the exterminator of his foes, who felt perplexed through grief, then became thoughtful. (19)

verses.text:
तं तु शोकपरिद्यूनं रामं दशरथात्मजम्।
उवाच वचनं श्रीमान् सुग्रीवः शोकनाशनम्॥ १॥
verses.m: To the said Śrī Rāma, sprung from the loins of Daśaratha, who was sore stricken with grief, the glorious Sugrīva for his part made the following reply, which was calculated to drive away his grief: (1)

verses.text:
किं त्वया तप्यते वीर यथान्यः प्राकृतस्तथा।
मैवं भूस्त्यज संतापं कृतघ्न इव सौहृदम्॥ २॥
verses.m: “Why do you give way to sorrow, O hero, even as another common man would? Do not be sorrowful like this; shake of agony even as an ungrateful fellow would cast all goodwill to the winds. (2)

verses.text:
संतापस्य च ते स्थानं नहि पश्यामि राघव।
प्रवृत्तावुपलब्धायां ज्ञाते च निलये रिपोः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Moreover, I do not actually find any occasion for your agony, O scion of Raghu, intelligence about Sītā having been received and the enemy’s abode discovered. (3)

verses.text:
मतिमाञ्शास्त्रवित् प्राज्ञः पण्डितश्चासि राघव।
त्यजेमां प्राकृतां बुद्धिं कृतात्मेवार्थदूषिणीम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “You are endowed with prudence, well-versed in the sacred lore, exceedingly wise and learned, O scion of Raghu! As such like one who has disciplined one’s mind, give up this commonplace mentality, which is calculated to mar your very purpose. (4)

verses.text:
समुद्रं लङ्घयित्वा तु महानक्रसमाकुलम्।
लङ्कामारोहयिष्यामो हनिष्यामश्च ते रिपुम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Crossing the sea, infested with mighty crocodiles, we shall climb up the fortress of Laṅkā and make short work of your enemy, Rāvaṇa. (5)

verses.text:
निरुत्साहस्य दीनस्य शोकपर्याकुलात्मनः।
सर्वार्था व्यवसीदन्ति व्यसनं चाधिगच्छति॥ ६॥
verses.m: “All the affairs of a man who is lacking in spirit and miserable, and whose mind is puzzled through grief, come to nought and he meets with disaster. (6)

verses.text:
इमे शूराः समर्थाश्च सर्वतो हरियूथपाः।
त्वत्प्रियार्थं कृतोत्साहाः प्रवेष्टुमपि पावकम्।
एषां हर्षेण जानामि तर्कश्चापि दृढो मम॥ ७॥
verses.m: “These leaders of monkey troops are gallant and powerful in everyway; they are ready even to enter fire in order to oblige you. I conclude this from their joy on the proposal of an expedition against Laṅkā being made to them, and my reason in favour of this conclusion is also strong. (7)

verses.text:
विक्रमेण समानेष्ये सीतां हत्वा यथा रिपुम्।
रावणं पापकर्माणं तथा त्वं कर्तुमर्हसि॥ ८॥
verses.m: “You ought to manipulate things in such a way that I may after disposing of the enemy, Rāvaṇa of sinful deeds, be able to recover Sītā. (8)

verses.text:
सेतुरत्र यथा बद्ध्येद् यथा पश्येम तां पुरीम्।
तस्य राक्षसराजस्य तथा त्वं कुरु राघव॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Take steps, O scion of Raghu, to see that a bridge is constructed across the intervening sea and we behold that city of the aforesaid king of ogres. (9)

verses.text:
दृष्ट्वा तां हि पुरीं लङ्कां त्रिकूटशिखरे स्थिताम्।
हतं च रावणं युद्धे दर्शनादवधारय॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Know Rāvaṇa as killed as soon as he is seen in combat and immediately on our beholding that city of Laṅkā standing on a peak of the Trikūṭa mountain. (10)

verses.text:
अबद्ध्वा सागरे सेतुं घोरे च वरुणालये।
लङ्कां न मर्दितुं शक्या सेन्द्रैरपि सुरासुरैः॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Nay, without throwing a bridge over the sea, the formidable abode of Varuṇa (the god of water), Laṅkā cannot be overcome even by gods and demons, including Indra. (11)

verses.text:
सेतुबन्धः समुद्रे च यावल्लङ्कासमीपतः।
सर्वं तीर्णं च मे सैन्यं जितमित्युपधारय।
इमे हि समरे वीरा हरयः कामरूपिणः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Nay, know that the whole of my army will be borne across the sea and come out victorious the moment a bridge is built upto the vicinity of Laṅkā; for, the monkeys, who are capable of assuming any form at will, are all heroic in battle. (12)

verses.text:
तदलं विक्लवां बुद्धिं राजन् सर्वार्थनाशिनीम्।
पुरुषस्य हि लोकेऽस्मिन् शोकः शौर्यापकर्षणः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Therefore, have done with a timid mind, which defeats all purpose; for, grief in this world takes away the valour of a man, O king! (13)

verses.text:
यत् तु कार्यं मनुष्येण शौटीर्यमवलम्ब्यताम्।
तदलंकरणायैव कर्तुर्भवति सत्वरम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Heroism alone, which is worth resorting to, ought to be taken recourse to by a man. It is capable of bringing success without doubt to a doer quickly. (14)

verses.text:
अस्मिन् काले महाप्राज्ञ सत्त्वमातिष्ठ तेजसा।
शूराणां हि मनुष्याणां त्वद्विधानां महात्मनाम्।
विनष्टे वा प्रणष्टे वा शोकः सर्वार्थनाशनः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Have recourse to courage, O highly sagacious prince, at this moment, endowed that you already are with valour. Grief for something lost or utterly destroyed defeats all the purposes even of heroic and high-souled personages like you. (15)

verses.text:
तत्त्वं बुद्धिमतां श्रेष्ठः सर्वशास्त्रार्थकोविदः।
मद्विधैः सचिवैः सार्धमरिं जेतुं समर्हसि॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Hence you are perfectly able to conquer your enemy in conjunction with your friends like me, foremost that you are among those endowed with wisdom and well-versed in the teachings of all sacred books. (16)

verses.text:
नहि पश्याम्यहं कंचित् त्रिषु लोकेषु राघव।
गृहीतधनुषो यस्ते तिष्ठेदभिमुखो रणे॥ १७॥
verses.m: “I do not actually see anyone in all the three worlds (the earth, heaven and the intermediate region), who can stand face to face with you on a field of battle when you have seized a bow, O scion of Raghu! (17)

verses.text:
वानरेषु समासक्तं न ते कार्यं विपत्स्यते।
अचिराद् द्रक्ष्यसे सीतां तीर्त्वा सागरमक्षयम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Duly entrusted to the monkeys, your task will not suffer. Crossing the sea, which knows no destruction, you shall behold Sītā before long. (18)

verses.text:
तदलं शोकमालम्ब्य क्रोधमालम्ब भूपते।
निश्चेष्टाः क्षत्रिया मन्दाः सर्वे चण्डस्य बिभ्यति॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Therefore, give way no more to grief and have recourse to anger, O Lord of the earth! Spiritless Kṣatriyas (members of the warrior class) are inactive, while all fear the wrathful. (19)

verses.text:
लङ्घनार्थं च घोरस्य समुद्रस्य नदीपतेः।
सहास्माभिरिहोपेतः सूक्ष्मबुद्धिर्विचारय॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Nay, accompanied by us, consider here with us the means of crossing the dread sea, the lord of rivers, sharp-witted that you are. (20)

verses.text:
लङ्घिते तत्र तैः सैन्यैर्जितमित्येव निश्चिनु।
सर्वं तीर्णं च मे सैन्यं जितमित्यवधार्यताम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Once the sea has been crossed by my forces, conclude, our victory is certain. Nay, arrived beyond the sea, my entire army should be taken as victorious. (21)

verses.text:
इमे हि हरयः शूराः समरे कामरूपिणः।
तानरीन् विधमिष्यन्ति शिलापादपवृष्टिभिः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “These monkeys, heroic that they are in combat and capable of assuming any form at will, will surely blow away the aforesaid enemies by their volleys of rocks and trees. (22)

verses.text:
कथंचित् परिपश्यामि लङ्घितं वरुणालयम्।
हतमित्येव तं मन्ये युद्धे शत्रुनिबर्हण॥ २३॥
verses.m: “If I actually find the sea (the abode of Varuṇa) crossed by any means whatsoever, I count Rāvaṇa as definitely killed in battle, O exterminator of foes! (23)

verses.text:
किमुक्त्वा बहुधा चापि सर्वथा विजयी भवान्।
निमित्तानि च पश्यामि मनो मे सम्प्रहृष्यति॥ २४॥
verses.m: “What will be gained by speaking extensively on this topic? Nay, you will turnout victorious in everyway. For, I perceive good omens and my mind is excessively delighted.” (24)

verses.text:
सुग्रीवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा हेतुमत् परमार्थवत्।
प्रतिजग्राह काकुत्स्थो हनूमन्तमथाब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Hearing the appeal of Sugrīva, which was full of reason and exposition of the real truth, Śrī Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha) accepted it and spoke to Hanumān as follows: (1)

verses.text:
तपसा सेतुबन्धेन सागरोच्छोषणेन च।
सर्वथापि समर्थोऽस्मि सागरस्यास्य लङ्घने॥ २॥
verses.m: “I am capable in everyway of crossing this sea, either by strength of will acquired by virtue of my asceticism, or by throwing a bridge across it or even by drying up the sea by use of mystic missiles. (2)

verses.text:
कति दुर्गाणि दुर्गाया लङ्कायास्तद् ब्रवीष्व मे।
ज्ञातुमिच्छामि तत् सर्वं दर्शनादिव वानर॥ ३॥
verses.m: “How many fortifications are there in Laṅkā, which is so difficult of access? Please point it out to me. I wish to know all that as through sight, O Hanumān! (3)

verses.text:
बलस्य परिमाणं च द्वारदुर्गक्रियामपि।
गुप्तिकर्म च लङ्काया रक्षसां सदनानि च॥ ४॥
यथासुखं यथावच्च लङ्कायामसि दृष्टवान्।
सर्वमाचक्ष्व तत्त्वेन सर्वथा कुशलो ह्यसि॥ ५॥
verses.m: “You have seen according to your convenience the strength of the army as also the process by which the entrances have been rendered difficult of access, nay, the way in which Laṅkā is guarded, as well as the mansions of the ogres. Please relate everything in accordance with factual situation; for you are clever in everyway.” (4-5)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा रामस्य वचनं हनूमान् मारुतात्मजः।
वाक्यं वाक्यविदां श्रेष्ठो रामं पुनरथाब्रवीत्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Hearing the command of Śrī Rāma, Hanumān, sprung from the loins of the wind-god and the foremost among those adept in the art of expression, forthwith made the following submission to Śrī Rāma once more: (6)

verses.text:
श्रूयतां सर्वमाख्यास्ये दुर्गकर्म विधानतः।
गुप्ता पुरी यथा लङ्का रक्षिता च यथा बलैः॥ ७॥
राक्षसाश्च यथा स्निग्धा रावणस्य च तेजसा।
परां समृद्धिं लङ्कायाः सागरस्य च भीमताम्॥ ८॥
विभागं च बलौघस्य निर्देशं वाहनस्य च।
एवमुक्त्वा कपिश्रेष्ठः कथयामास तत्त्वतः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Please listen, my Lord! I shall relate to you everything—how the city of Laṅkā has been defended according to the technique of fortification and how it has been protected by troops and how the ogres are devoted to their king, and shall also describe the extreme prosperity of Laṅkā occasioned by Rāvaṇa’s glory, the dreadfulness of the sea, the division of the body of his forces into regiments and the strength of the animals carrying his forces other than the infantry.” Saying so, Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys, who knew the facts about Laṅkā, began as follows: (7—9)

verses.text:
हृष्टप्रमुदिता लङ्का मत्तद्विपसमाकुला।
महती रथसम्पूर्णा रक्षोगणनिषेविता॥ १०॥
verses.m: “The extensive city of Laṅkā is gay and in raptures and remains crowded with elephants in rut; nay, it is packed with chariots and is inhabited by hordes of ogres. (10)

verses.text:
दृढबद्धकपाटानि महापरिघवन्ति च।
चत्वारि विपुलान्यस्या द्वाराणि सुमहान्ति च॥ ११॥
verses.m: “There are four extensive and huge gates in it, which have been provided with strong doors closed with massive bars. (11)

verses.text:
तत्रेषूपलयन्त्राणि बलवन्ति महान्ति च।
आगतं प्रतिसैन्यं तैस्तत्र प्रतिनिवार्यते॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Powerful and enormous catapults discharging darts and stones have been attached to them; by them a hostile army arrived there is repulsed at the very gates. (12)

verses.text:
द्वारेषु संस्कृता भीमाः कालायसमयाः शिताः।
शतशो रचिता वीरैः शतघ्न्यो रक्षसां गणैः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Formidable sharp-edged steel clubs, known by the name of Śataghnīs*, which are four cubits long and bristle with iron spikes and are so-called because they are supposed to kill hundreds at a time, forged by the heroic hordes of ogres, have been kept in readiness in hundreds at the gates. (13)

verses.text:
सौवर्णस्तु महांस्तस्याः प्राकारो दुष्प्रधर्षणः।
मणिविद्रुमवैदूर्यमुक्ताविरचितान्तरः ॥ १४॥
verses.m: “A high protective wall of gold—which is difficult to assail by force and is inlaid at intervals with gems, corals, cat’s-eyes and pearls—encircles it. (14)

verses.text:
सर्वतश्च महाभीमाः शीततोया महाशुभाः।
अगाधा ग्राहवत्यश्च परिखा मीनसेविताः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Most formidable, fathomless moats, filled with cold water and fraught with great evil to the enemy, nay, infested with alligators and inhabited by fishes, are in existence all round the city. (15)

verses.text:
द्वारेषु तासां चत्वारः संक्रमाः परमायताः।
यन्त्रैरुपेता बहुभिर्महद्भिर्गृहपङ्क्तिभिः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “In front of the gateways there are four very extensive drawbridges across the moats, which are equipped with numerous engines and strengthened by many rows of stately buildings built on the protective wall and meant for those entrusted with the duty of guarding the entrances. (16)

verses.text:
त्रायन्ते संक्रमास्तत्र परसैन्यागते सति।
यन्त्रैस्तैरवकीर्यन्ते परिखासु समन्ततः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “On the arrival of hostile forces near them the drawbridges are defended by the aforesaid engines and the forces are flung into the moats on every side. (17)

verses.text:
एकस्त्वकम्प्यो बलवान् संक्रमः सुमहादृढः।
काञ्चनैर्बहुभिः स्तम्भैर्वेदिकाभिश्च शोभितः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “The principal (central) drawbridge before the northern gate, which is unshakable, strongly garrisoned and extremely strong, is embellished with numerous gold pillars and pedestals. (18)

verses.text:
स्वयं प्रकृतिमापन्नो युयुत्सू राम रावणः।
उत्थितश्चाप्रमत्तश्च बलानामनुदर्शने॥ १९॥
verses.m: “The bellicose Rāvaṇa, O Rāma, is himself self-possessed, and remains active and alert in reviewing his forces. (19)

verses.text:
लङ्का पुनर्निरालम्बा देवदुर्गा भयावहा।
नादेयं पार्वतं वान्यं कृत्रिमं च चतुर्विधम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Laṅkā again, offers no base for invasion, is difficult of access even for gods and inspires terror in the invader. It has a fourfold defence, consisting of (i) a river (which encircles it on all sides), (ii) a mountain, viz., the Trikūṭa mountain, on whose summit it stands, (iii) a belt of forests surrounding it and (iv) an artificial fortification in the form of an enclosing wall and moats. (20)

verses.text:
स्थिता पारे समुद्रस्य दूरपारस्य राघव।
नौपथश्चापि नास्त्यत्र निरुद्देशश्च सर्वतः॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Standing as it does beyond the sea with a distant shore, it offers no passage for vessels either and the sea is undivided too on all sides, O scion of Raghu! (21)

verses.text:
शैलाग्रे रचिता दुर्गा सा पूर्देवपुरोपमा।
वाजिवारणसम्पूर्णा लङ्का परमदुर्जया॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Built on a mountain peak, the aforesaid city of Laṅkā is difficult of access and vies with a celestial city, is packed with horses and elephants and is, therefore, most difficult to conquer. (22)

verses.text:
परिखाश्च शतघ्न्यश्च यन्त्राणि विविधानि च।
शोभयन्ति पुरीं लङ्कां रावणस्य दुरात्मनः॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Moats and Śataghnīs too as well as engines of various kinds adorn Laṅkā, the city of the evil-minded Rāvaṇa. (23)

verses.text:
अयुतं रक्षसामत्र पूर्वद्वारं समाश्रितम्।
शूलहस्ता दुराधर्षाः सर्वे खड्गाग्रयोधिनः॥ २४॥
verses.m: “A myriad ogres, all carrying darts in their hands, and contending with swords in the van of battle, nay, difficult to assail, are garrisoned at the eastern gate of this city. (24)

verses.text:
नियुतं रक्षसामत्र दक्षिणद्वारमाश्रितम्।
चतुरङ्गेण सैन्येन योधास्तत्राप्यनुत्तमाः॥ २५॥
verses.m: “A lakh of ogres, with a complete army of four limbs, viz., horses, foot soldiers, elephants and chariots, are garrisoned at the southern gate of this city. Warriors unsurpassed by others stand comprised in that army. (25)

verses.text:
प्रयुतं रक्षसामत्र पश्चिमद्वारमाश्रितम्।
चर्मखड्गधराः सर्वे तथा सर्वास्त्रकोविदाः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “A million of ogres, all carrying shields and swords and proficient in the use of all mystic missiles, are garrisoned at the western gate of this city. (26)

verses.text:
न्यर्बुदं रक्षसामत्र उत्तरद्वारमाश्रितम्।
रथिनश्चाश्ववाहाश्च कुलपुत्राः सुपूजिताः॥ २७॥
verses.m: “A hundred million of ogres, consisting of car-warriors and horse-soldiers, sons of noble families and greatly honoured for their skill in warfare are garrisoned at the northern gate. (27)

verses.text:
शतशोऽथ सहस्राणि मध्यमं स्कन्धमाश्रिताः।
यातुधाना दुराधर्षाः साग्रकोटिश्च रक्षसाम्॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Again, ogres, hundreds of thousands in number, difficult to assail, and totalling one and a quarter of a crore of ogres, are garrisoned at the central military station. (28)

verses.text:
ते मया संक्रमा भग्नाः परिखाश्चावपूरिताः।
दग्धा च नगरी लङ्का प्राकाराश्चावसादिताः।
बलैकदेशः क्षपितो राक्षसानां महात्मनाम्॥ २९॥
verses.m: “The aforesaid drawbridges were broken by me and the moats filled up with the wreckage. Nay, the city of Laṅkā was burnt, the defensive walls pulled down and a part of the army of the gigantic ogres destroyed. (29)

verses.text:
येन केन तु मार्गेण तराम वरुणालयम्।
हतेति नगरी लङ्का वानरैरुपधार्यताम्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Let us by any means whatsoever positively cross the sea, the abode of Varuṇa, the god of water. The city of Laṅkā should then be taken as destroyed by the monkeys. (30)

verses.text:
अङ्गदो द्विविदो मैन्दो जाम्बवान् पनसो नलः।
नीलः सेनापतिश्चैव बलशेषेण किं तव॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Aṅgada, Dvivida, Mainda, Jāmbavān, Panasa and Nala and Nīla, the Commander-in-Chief, alone will be able to storm Laṅkā and recover Sītā. What will be gained by the rest of your forces being taken across the sea? (31)

verses.text:
प्लवमाना हि गत्वा त्वां रावणस्य महापुरीम्।
सपर्वतवनां भित्त्वा सखातां च सतोरणाम्।
सप्राकारां सभवनामानयिष्यन्ति राघव॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Reaching the great city of Rāvaṇa, leaping and demolishing it with its mountains and woods, moats and archways, protective walls and buildings, they will bring back Sītā, O scion of Raghu! (32)

verses.text:
एवमाज्ञापय क्षिप्रं बलानां सर्वसंग्रहम्।
मुहूर्तेन तु युक्तेन प्रस्थानमभिरोचय॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “Command the aforesaid generals accordingly without delay, if the latter course finds favour with you, or, if you would take the whole army across the sea, order them all to get accumulated, and be inclined to march at an opportune hour.” (33)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा हनूमतो वाक्यं यथावदनुपूर्वशः।
ततोऽब्रवीन्महातेजा रामः सत्यपराक्रमः॥ १॥
verses.m: Having duly heard the account of Hanumān seriatim, Śrī Rāma of unfailing prowess, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, then spoke as follows: (1)

verses.text:
यन्निवेदयसे लङ्कां पुरीं भीमस्य रक्षसः।
क्षिप्रमेनां वधिष्यामि सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥ २॥
verses.m: “I shall destroy without delay Laṅkā, that city of the redoubtable ogre, Rāvaṇa, of which you have just spoken: I truly promise this to you. (2)

verses.text:
अस्मिन् मुहूर्ते सुग्रीव प्रयाणमभिरोचय।
युक्तो मुहूर्ते विजये प्राप्तो मध्यं दिवाकरः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Approve of our march at this very hour, O Sugrīva! The sun has reached the meridian and departure at this hour, known by the name of Abhijit (so-called because it brings victory to the departing person), is advisable. (3)

verses.text:
सीतां हृत्वा तु तद् यातु क्वासौ यास्यति जीवितः।
सीता श्रुत्वाभियानं मे आशामेष्यति जीविते।
जीवितान्तेऽमृतं स्पृष्ट्वा पीत्वामृतमिवातुरः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “That ogre for his part may return to his abode after abducting Sītā; but he cannot escape alive. Hearing from the mouth of Siddhas and others of my march to Laṅkā, Sītā too will regain her lost hope of survival, even as an ailing man would on touching an immortalizing herb or quaffing the drink of immortality at the close of his life. (4)

verses.text:
उत्तराफाल्गुनी ह्यद्य श्वस्तु हस्तेन योक्ष्यते।
अभिप्रयाम सुग्रीव सर्वानीकसमावृताः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “The constellation Uttarāphālgunī is actually in the ascendant today, while tomorrow the moon will be in conjunction with the constellation Hasta. Let us, therefore, march this very day, accompanied by all the troops, O Sugrīva! (5)

verses.text:
निमित्तानि च पश्यामि यानि प्रादुर्भवन्ति वै।
निहत्य रावणं सीतामानयिष्यामि जानकीम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “From the omens, which actually appear on my person and which I behold, I conclude that killing Rāvaṇa, I shall bring back Sītā, Janaka’s daughter. (6)

verses.text:
उपरिष्टाद्धि नयनं स्फुरमाणमिमं मम।
विजयं समनुप्राप्तं शंसतीव मनोरथम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Twitching in the upper lid, this right eye of mine actually foretells, as it were, my coveted victory as being near.” (7)

verses.text:
ततो वानरराजेन लक्ष्मणेन सुपूजितः।
उवाच रामो धर्मात्मा पुनरप्यर्थकोविदः॥ ८॥
verses.m: Warmly applauded by Sugrīva, the ruler of monkeys, as well as by Lakṣmaṇa, Śrī Rāma, whose mind was set on piety and who was well-versed in politics, then spoke once more as follows: (8)

verses.text:
अग्रे यातु बलस्यास्य नीलो मार्गमवेक्षितुम्।
वृतः शतसहस्रेण वानराणां तरस्विनाम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Let Nīla, accompanied by one lakh of agile monkeys, march at the head of this army to examine the passage. (9)

verses.text:
फलमूलवता नील शीतकाननवारिणा।
पथा मधुमता चाशु सेनां सेनापते नय॥ १०॥
verses.m: Addressing the Commander-in-Chief, Nīla, he said: “O Nīla, my generalissimo, lead the army speedily by a route full of fruits and roots as well as of honey and abounding in woods with a cool shade and fresh water. (10)

verses.text:
दूषयेयुर्दुरात्मानः पथि मूलफलोदकम्।
राक्षसाः पथि रक्षेथास्तेभ्यस्त्वं नित्यमुद्यतः॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Evil-minded ogres might vitiate the roots, fruits and water along that route. Remaining ever vigilant on the way, protect you the aforesaid substances from them.(11)

verses.text:
निम्नेषु वनदुर्गेषु वनेषु च वनौकसः।
अभिप्लुत्याभिपश्येयुः परेषां निहितं बलम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Leaping all round the monkeys should find out the enemy’s troops lying in ambush in ravines and thickets, nay, in parts of the forest which are difficult of access. (12)

verses.text:
यत्तु फल्गु बलं किंचित् तदत्रैवोपपद्यताम्।
एतद्धि कृत्यं घोरं नो विक्रमेण प्रयुज्यताम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Any weak element, which may be found, should, however, be left back at this very place, Kiṣkindhā; for this task of ours is formidable. Those troops alone, which are endowed with prowess should be utilized in this expedition. (13)

verses.text:
सागरौघनिभं भीममग्रानीकं महाबलाः।
कपिसिंहाः प्रकर्षन्तु शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Let the lions among monkeys, who are endowed with extraordinary might, in their hundreds and thousands, lead the redoubtable vanguard, resembling the tide of a sea. (14)

verses.text:
गजश्च गिरिसंकाशो गवयश्च महाबलः।
गवाक्षश्चाग्रतो यातु गवां दृप्त इवर्षभः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Let the monkeys Gaja, who closely resembles a mountain, and Gavaya, who is endowed with extraordinary might, as well as Gavākṣa march in the van even like a proud bull at the head of cows. (15)

verses.text:
यातु वानरवाहिन्या वानरः प्लवतां पतिः।
पालयन् दक्षिणं पार्श्वमृषभो वानरर्षभः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Let the monkey Ṛṣabha, a leader of monkeys, nay, who is a veritable bull among monkeys, proceed defending the right flank of the army of monkeys. (16)

verses.text:
गन्धहस्तीव दुर्धर्षस्तरस्वी गन्धमादनः।
यातु वानरवाहिन्याः सव्यं पार्श्वमधिष्ठितः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Let the impetuous Gandhamādana, who is difficult to assail like an elephant in rut, move along leading the left flank of the army of monkeys. (17)

verses.text:
यास्यामि बलमध्येऽहं बलौघमभिहर्षयन्।
अधिरुह्य हनूमन्तमैरावतमिवेश्वरः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Mounting the shoulders of Hanumān, even as Indra, the ruler of all the three worlds, would ride Airāvata, the king of elephants, and cheering the army, rushing like a flood, I shall march in the centre of the army. (18)

verses.text:
अङ्गदेनैष संयातु लक्ष्मणश्चान्तकोपमः।
सार्वभौमेन भूतेशो द्रविणाधिपतिर्यथा॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Nay, let Lakṣmaṇa, who vies with Death himself, march on the back of Aṅgada even as Kubera, the lord or controller of riches, the ruler of spirits, would ride his own elephant, Sārvabhauma (one of the elephants guarding the quarters). (19)

verses.text:
जाम्बवांश्च सुषेणश्च वेगदर्शी च वानरः।
ऋक्षराजो महाबाहुः कुक्षिं रक्षन्तु ते त्रयः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Nay, let the mighty-armed, Jāmbavān, the ruler of bears, and Suṣeṇa as well as the monkey, Vegadarśī, the aforesaid three defend the rear.” (20)

verses.text:
राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवो वाहिनीपतिः।
व्यादिदेश महावीर्यो वानरान् वानरर्षभः॥ २१॥
verses.m: Hearing the command of Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, Sugrīva, the foremost of monkeys and the ruler of the army, who was endowed with extraordinary prowess, gave detailed orders to the monkeys accordingly. (21)

verses.text:
ते वानरगणाः सर्वे समुत्पत्य महौजसः।
गुहाभ्यः शिखरेभ्यश्च आशु पुप्लुविरे तदा॥ २२॥
verses.m: Emerging from the caves as well as from mountain-tops, all the aforesaid monkey hordes, who were endowed with extraordinary might, speedily leapt forward on that occasion. (22)

verses.text:
ततो वानरराजेन लक्ष्मणेन च पूजितः।
जगाम रामो धर्मात्मा ससैन्यो दक्षिणां दिशम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: Placed ahead Sugrīva, the ruler of monkeys, as well as Lakṣmaṇa, Śrī Rāma, whose mind was set on piety, thereupon sallied forth with his army in a southerly direction. (23)

verses.text:
शतैः शतसहस्रैश्च कोटिभिश्चायुतैरपि।
वारणाभैश्च हरिभिर्ययौ परिवृतस्तदा॥ २४॥
verses.m: Surrounded by monkeys numbering hundreds and tens of thousands, nay, lakhs and crores, and looking like elephants, Śrī Rāma then moved along. (24)

verses.text:
तं यान्तमनुयान्ती सा महती हरिवाहिनी।
हृष्टाः प्रमुदिताः सर्वे सुग्रीवेणापि पालिताः॥ २५॥
verses.m: That huge army of monkeys followed Śrī Rāma, who was marching along with them. Protected as they were by Sugrīva, all felt rejoiced and enraptured. (25)

verses.text:
आप्लवन्तः प्लवन्तश्च गर्जन्तश्च प्लवंगमाः।
क्ष्वेलन्तो निनदन्तश्च जग्मुर्वै दक्षिणां दिशम्॥ २६॥
भक्षयन्तः सुगन्धीनि मधूनि च फलानि च।
उद्वहन्तो महावृक्षान् मञ्जरीपुञ्जधारिणः॥ २७॥
verses.m: The monkeys proceeded precisely in a southerly direction, some leaping on all sides in order to guard the army against any possible danger and others springing with a view to clearing the passage, thundering, nay, roaring like lions and bellowing like bulls, feasting on the fragrant honey and fruits and carrying huge trees bearing bunches of blossom. (26-27)

verses.text:
अन्योन्यं सहसा दृप्ता निर्वहन्ति क्षिपन्ति च।
पतन्तश्चोत्पतन्त्यन्ये पातयन्त्यपरे परान्॥ २८॥
verses.m: The proud monkeys would all of a sudden lift up and throw one another. Nay, moving along, some would spring up in the air, while others dashed down their companions, springing like them. (28)

verses.text:
रावणो नो निहन्तव्यः सर्वे च रजनीचराः।
इति गर्जन्ति हरयो राघवस्य समीपतः॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Rāvaṇa as well as all the rangers of the night must be killed by us” thus roared the monkeys in the presence of Śrī Rāma. (29)

verses.text:
पुरस्तादृषभो नीलो वीरः कुमुद एव च।
पन्थानं शोधयन्ति स्म वानरैर्बहुभिः सह॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Going ahead alongwith many other monkeys, Ṛṣabha, Nīla and the heroic Kumuda too cleared the way. (30)

verses.text:
मध्ये तु राजा सुग्रीवो रामो लक्ष्मण एव च।
बलिभिर्बहुभिर्भीमैर्वृतः शत्रुनिबर्हणः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Surrounded by many mighty and redoubtable monkeys for his part, Sugrīva, the exterminator of foes, marched in the centre alongwith Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa. (31)

verses.text:
हरिः शतबलिर्वीरः कोटिभिर्दशभिर्वृतः।
सर्वामेको ह्यवष्टभ्य ररक्ष हरिवाहिनीम्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Actually controlling the entire army, the valiant monkey, Śatabali, who was accompanied by ten crores of monkeys, protected it single-handed. (32)

verses.text:
कोटीशतपरीवारः केसरी पनसो गजः।
अर्कश्च बहुभिः पार्श्वमेकं तस्याभिरक्षति॥ ३३॥
verses.m: Followed by a hundred crores of monkeys, Kesarī and Panasa protected the right flank of that army; while Gaja and Arka, who were followed by numerous monkeys, guarded the other, left, flank. (33)

verses.text:
सुषेणो जाम्बवांश्चैव ऋक्षैर्बहुभिरावृतौ।
सुग्रीवं पुरतः कृत्वा जघनं संररक्षतुः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: Surrounded by numerous bears and placing Sugrīva at their head, Suṣeṇa as well as Jāmbavān carefully guarded the rear. (34)

verses.text:
तेषां सेनापतिर्वीरो नीलो वानरपुंगवः।
सम्पतन् प्लवतां श्रेष्ठस्तद् बलं पर्यवारयत्॥ ३५॥
verses.m: Marching ahead Śatabali and others, in order to clear the passage, the heroic Commander-in-Chief, Nīla, the foremost among monkeys, nay, a veritable bull among them, held that army in check lest it should do any harm to the cities etc., falling on the way. (35)

verses.text:
दरीमुखः प्रजङ्घश्च जम्भोऽथ रभसः कपिः।
सर्वतश्च ययुर्वीरास्त्वरयन्तः प्लवंगमान्॥ ३६॥
verses.m: The heroes, Darīmukha and Prajaṅgha, as well as Jambha and the monkey Rabhasa went about urging the monkeys move forward on all sides. (36)

verses.text:
एवं ते हरिशार्दूला गच्छन्ति बलदर्पिताः।
अपश्यन्त गिरिश्रेष्ठं सह्यं गिरिशतायुतम्॥ ३७॥
सरांसि च सुफुल्लानि तटाकानि वराणि च।
रामस्य शासनं ज्ञात्वा भीमकोपस्य भीतवत्॥ ३८॥
वर्जयन् नागराभ्याशांस्तथा जनपदानपि।
सागरौघनिभं भीमं तद् वानरबलं महत्॥ ३९॥
निःससर्प महाघोरं भीमघोषमिवार्णवम्।
तस्य दाशरथेः पार्श्वे शूरास्ते कपिकुञ्जराः॥ ४०॥
तूर्णमापुप्लुवुः सर्वे सदश्वा इव चोदिताः।
कपिभ्यामुह्यमानौ तौ शुशुभाते नरर्षभौ॥ ४१॥
महद्भ्यामिव संस्पृष्टौ ग्रहाभ्यां चन्द्रभास्करौ।
ततो वानरराजेन लक्ष्मणेन सुपूजितः॥ ४२॥
जगाम रामो धर्मात्मा ससैन्यो दक्षिणां दिशम्।
तमङ्गदगतो रामं लक्ष्मणः शुभया गिरा॥ ४३॥
उवाच परिपूर्णार्थं पूर्णार्थप्रतिभानवान्।
हृतामवाप्य वैदेहीं क्षिप्रं हत्वा च रावणम्॥ ४४॥
समृद्धार्थः समृद्धार्थामयोध्यां प्रतियास्यसि।
महान्ति च निमित्तानि दिवि भूमौ च राघव॥ ४५॥
शुभानि तव पश्यामि सर्वाण्येवार्थसिद्धये।
अनुवाति शिवो वायुः सेनां मृदुहितः सुखः॥ ४६॥
verses.m: In this way the aforesaid tigers among monkeys, who were all proud of their might, pressed forward. Meanwhile, they caught sight of the Sahya mountain, the foremost of mountains, surrounded by hundreds of other smaller mountains, as also lakes with full-blown lotuses and other flowers, as well as excellent ponds. Avoiding the precincts of cities as well as the rural parts like one seized with fear, knowing as it did the command of Śrī Rāma, whose wrath gave rise to fear, that redoubtable and huge monkey army, which resembled the tide of a sea, surged forward like an exceedingly dreadful ocean roaring terribly. Like swift steeds urged on with a spur, all those heroic elephants among monkeys bounded forward with agility to the side of the aforesaid Śrī Rāma, son of Daśaratha. Being borne by the two monkeys, Aṅgada and Hanumān, Lakṣmaṇa and Śrī Rāma, the aforesaid two jewels among men, shone brightly like the moon and the sun conjoined with two major planets, Jupiter and Venus, respectively. Highly honoured by Sugrīva, the king of monkeys, as well as by Lakṣmaṇa, and accompanied by the army, Śrī Rāma, whose mind was set on piety, thereupon proceeded towards the southern quarter. To the said Śrī Rāma, whose purpose ever stood fully accomplished, Lakṣmaṇa, who was mounted on the shoulders of Aṅgada and who had intuitive knowledge of the fruition of an undertaking, submitted as follows in happy accents: “Killing Rāvaṇa in no time and recovering the abducted princess of the Videha territory, you will return fully accomplished of purpose to Ayodhyā, which will also have its purpose accomplished by your safe and happy return. I perceive good omens of great moment, which all prognosticate the accomplishment of your purpose, O scion of Raghu! A benign, gentle, favourable, cool and agreeable, fragrant breeze is blowing in the same direction as the army is proceeding. (37—46)

verses.text:
पूर्णवल्गुस्वराश्चेमे प्रवदन्ति मृगद्विजाः।
प्रसन्नाश्च दिशः सर्वा विमलश्च दिवाकरः॥ ४७॥
verses.m: “Nay, these beasts and birds are emitting unbroken and agreeable sounds. Moreover the quarters are all serene and the sun is shining brightly. (47)

verses.text:
उशना च प्रसन्नार्चिरनु त्वां भार्गवो गतः।
ब्रह्मराशिर्विशुद्धश्च शुद्धाश्च परमर्षयः।
अर्चिष्मन्तः प्रकाशन्ते ध्रुवं सर्वे प्रदक्षिणम्॥ ४८॥
verses.m: “With its bright light, the planet Venus too, sprung from the Sage Bhṛgu (a mind-born son of Brahmā, the creator) has risen at your back, in the north. The very bright pole-star (which is distinguishable by the contiguity of the stars presided over by the seven Brāhmaṇa Ṛṣis or the Great Bear) as well as the stars presided over by the seven foremost Ṛṣis (and bearing the name of the Great Bear) are all shining clearly and brightly in the northern sky, while coursing clockwise round the pole-star. (48)

verses.text:
त्रिशङ्कुर्विमलो भाति राजर्षिः सपुरोहितः।
पितामहः पुरोऽस्माकमिक्ष्वाकूणां महात्मनाम्॥ ४९॥
verses.m: “A star presided over by the royal sage Triśaṅku, a forbear of the high-souled Ikṣwākus, is also shining brightly before us in the southern sky, accompanied by another star presided over by his family priest, Sage Vasiṣṭha. (49)

verses.text:
विमले च प्रकाशेते विशाखे निरुपद्रवे।
नक्षत्रं परमस्माकमिक्ष्वाकूणां महात्मनाम्॥ ५०॥
verses.m: “The two bright stars, the Viśākhās, the foremost constellation in the eyes of the Ikṣwākus (being their tutelary constellation), are also gleaming over there, free from the evil influence of malevolent planets (Mars etc.,). (50)

verses.text:
नैर्ऋतं नैर्ऋतानां च नक्षत्रमतिपीड्यते।
मूलो मूलवता स्पृष्टो धूप्यते धूमकेतुना॥ ५१॥
verses.m: “The constellation Mūla, presided over by the ogre Nirṛti (the deity presiding over the south-west) and as such ruling the destinies of the ogres, is badly aspected, in that it is touched by a comet risen with a tail of light and tormenting it. (51)

verses.text:
सर्वं चैतद् विनाशाय राक्षसानामुपस्थितम्।
काले कालगृहीतानां नक्षत्रं ग्रहपीडितम्॥ ५२॥
verses.m: “And all this has come about for the extermination of ogres; for the star ruling the destiny of those caught in the grip of Death is oppressed by a malevolent planet at the hour of death. (52)

verses.text:
प्रसन्नाः सुरसाश्चापो वनानि फलवन्ति च।
प्रवान्ति नाधिका गन्धा यथर्तुकुसुमा द्रुमाः॥ ५३॥
verses.m: “The water of lakes etc., is pellucid and sweet and the woodlands are laden with fruit; fragrant breezes do not blow violently, while trees bear blossom according to season. (53)

verses.text:
व्यूढानि कपिसैन्यानि प्रकाशन्तेऽधिकं प्रभो।
देवानामिव सैन्यानि संग्रामे तारकामये।
एवमार्य समीक्ष्यैतत् प्रीतो भवितुमर्हसि॥ ५४॥
verses.m: “Disposed like the forces of gods arrayed in the battle, which brought destruction to the demon Tāraka (at the hands of Kārtikeya, son of Lord Śiva, the Commander-in-Chief of the celestial army), the forces of the monkeys shine brightly, O lord! Observing this fully, you ought to be pleased, O noble prince!” (54)

verses.text:
इति भ्रातरमाश्वास्य हृष्टः सौमित्रिरब्रवीत्।
अथावृत्य महीं कृत्स्नां जगाम हरिवाहिनी॥ ५५॥
verses.m: Thus spoke Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā), feeling cheerful on having reassured his eldest brother, Śrī Rāma. Meanwhile, the army of the monkeys moved along, covering the entire globe, as it were. (55)

verses.text:
ऋक्षवानरशार्दूलैर्नखद्रंष्ट्रायुधैरपि।
कराग्रैश्चरणाग्रैश्च वानरैरुद्धतं रजः॥ ५६॥
भीममन्तर्दधे लोकं निवार्य सवितुः प्रभाम्।
सपर्वतवनाकाशं दक्षिणां हरिवाहिनी॥ ५७॥
छादयन्ती ययौ भीमा द्यामिवाम्बुदसंततिः।
उत्तरन्त्याश्च सेनायाः सततं बहुयोजनम्॥ ५८॥
नदीस्रोतांसि सर्वाणि सस्यन्दुर्विपरीतवत्।
सरांसि विमलाम्भांसि द्रुमाकीर्णांश्च पर्वतान्॥ ५९॥
समान् भूमिप्रदेशांश्च वनानि फलवन्ति च।
मध्येन च समन्ताच्च तिर्यक् चाधश्च साविशत्॥ ६०॥
समावृत्य महीं कृत्स्नां जगाम महती चमूः।
ते हृष्टवदनाः सर्वे जग्मुर्मारुतरंहसः॥ ६१॥
हरयो राघवस्यार्थे समारोपितविक्रमाः।
हर्षं वीर्यं बलोद्रेकान् दर्शयन्तः परस्परम्॥ ६२॥
यौवनोत्सेकजाद् दर्पाद् विविधांश्चक्रुरध्वनि।
तत्र केचिद् द्रुतं जग्मुरुत्पेतुश्च तथापरे॥ ६३॥
केचित् किलकिलां चक्रुर्वानरा वनगोचराः।
प्रास्फोटयंश्च पुच्छानि संनिजघ्नुः पदान्यपि॥ ६४॥
verses.m: Intercepting the sunlight, the terrible dust raised by the monkeys—who consisted of some tiger-like bears and monkeys having nails and teeth for their weapons—with the fore parts of their hands and feet covered the earth. Like a continuous line of clouds enveloping the heavens, the formidable army of monkeys proceeded along encompassing the southern quarter alongwith the mountains, the woods and the sky. While the army crossed the rivers on the way, all their currents flowed in the opposite direction for many leagues continuously. The aforesaid army entered lakes with pellucid waters through the centre, mountains clothed with trees obliquely, level plains through every side and woodlands laden with fruit from underneath. The huge army thus advanced, covering the entire globe all over, as it were. Their prowess in the cause of Śrī Rāma having redoubled, all the aforesaid monkeys wore a cheerful countenance and moved with the swiftness of the wind. Exhibiting joy, prowess and superior strength in relation to one another through haughtiness born of high spirits natural to youth, they made various gestures on the way (as follows). Some of them walked quickly, while others sprang in the air. Still other monkeys, who ranged in the woods, emitted sounds expressive of joy, lashed their tail and also stamped their feet. (56—64)

verses.text:
भुजान् विक्षिप्य शैलांश्च द्रुमानन्ये बभञ्जिरे।
आरोहन्तश्च शृङ्गाणि गिरीणां गिरिगोचराः॥ ६५॥
verses.m: Stretching their arms, and climbing up the peaks of mountains, other monkeys (lit., rangers of mountains) broke off the rocks and trees. (65)

verses.text:
महानादान् प्रमुञ्चन्ति क्ष्वेडामन्ये प्रचक्रिरे।
ऊरुवेगैश्च ममृदुर्लताजालान्यनेकशः॥ ६६॥
verses.m: Some thundered at the top of their voice, while others roared like lions. Still others destroyed many networks of creepers with a jerk of their thighs. (66)

verses.text:
जृम्भमाणाश्च विक्रान्ता विचिक्रीडुः शिलाद्रुमैः।
ततः शतसहस्रैश्च कोटिभिश्च सहस्रशः॥ ६७॥
वानराणां सुघोराणां श्रीमत्परिवृता मही।
सा स्म याति दिवारात्रं महती हरिवाहिनी॥ ६८॥
verses.m: Even while stretching their limbs at the time of yawning, some powerful monkeys sported with rocks and trees. Presently the earth was splendidly covered by thousands, nay, lakhs and crores of most formidable monkeys. The huge army of monkeys thus moved on day and night. (67-68)

verses.text:
प्रहृष्टमुदिताः सर्वे सुग्रीवेणाभिपालिताः।
वानरास्त्वरिता यान्ति सर्वे युद्धाभिनन्दिनः।
प्रमोक्षयिषवः सीतां मुहूर्तं क्वापि नावसन्॥ ६९॥
verses.m: The monkeys, who all felt highly rejoiced and cheerful, protected as they were on all sides by Sugrīva, and who all welcomed war, eager as they were to get Sītā liberated, walked with quick steps and did not linger anywhere even for an hour. (69)

verses.text:
ततः पादपसम्बाधं नानावनसमायुतम्।
सह्यपर्वतमासाद्य वानरास्ते समारुहन्॥ ७०॥
verses.m: Then, reaching the Sahya mountain (identified with a part of the Western Ghats), thick with trees and rich in varied woodlands, the aforesaid monkeys climbed up to it. (70)

verses.text:
काननानि विचित्राणि नदीप्रस्रवणानि च।
पश्यन्नपि ययौ रामः सह्यस्य मलयस्य च॥ ७१॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma marched on, seeing diverse forests as well as the streams and cascades on the Sahya and Malaya mountains. (71)

verses.text:
चम्पकांस्तिलकांश्चूतानशोकान् सिन्दुवारकान्।
तिनिशान् करवीरांश्च भञ्जन्ति स्म प्लवंगमाः॥ ७२॥
verses.m: The monkeys broke down Campaka, Tilaka, Mango, Aśoka, Sinduvāra, Tiniśa and Karavīra trees standing on the aforesaid mountains. (72)

verses.text:
अङ्कोलांश्च करञ्चांश्च प्लक्षन्यग्रोधपादपान्।
जम्बूकामलकान् नीपान् भञ्जन्ति स्म प्लवंगमाः॥ ७३॥
verses.m: They also broke down Aṅkola, Karañja, Plakṣa and Nyagrodha, Jambū, Myrobalan and Nīpa trees. (73)

verses.text:
प्रस्तरेषु च रम्येषु विविधाः काननद्रुमाः।
वायुवेगप्रचलिताः पुष्पैरवकिरन्ति तान्॥ ७४॥
verses.m: Violently shaken by the fury of the winds, generated by the swift march of the monkeys, the various forest trees standing on lovely rocks covered the monkeys with their blossom. (74)

verses.text:
मारुतः सुखसंस्पर्शो वाति चन्दनशीतलः।
षट्पदैरनुकूजद्भिर्वनेषु मधुगन्धिषु॥ ७५॥
verses.m: Accompanied by humming bees, a breeze delightful to the touch and cool through the contact of sandalwood trees was blowing through the woods emitting the odour of honey. (75)

verses.text:
अधिकं शैलराजस्तु धातुभिस्तु विभूषितः।
धातुभ्यः प्रसृतो रेणुर्वायुवेगेन घट्टितः॥ ७६॥
सुमहद्वानरानीकं छादयामास सर्वतः।
गिरिप्रस्थेषु रम्येषु सर्वतः सम्प्रपुष्पिताः॥ ७७॥
केतक्यः सिन्दुवाराश्च वासन्त्यश्च मनोरमाः।
माधव्यो गन्धपूर्णाश्च कुन्दगुल्माश्च पुष्पिताः॥ ७८॥
verses.m: Richly adorned with minerals, the lord of mountains for its part shone all the brighter. The dust raised from the minerals and brought together by the wind covered the huge army of monkeys on all sides. Clothed with blossom on all sides on the lovely plateaux, the Ketakī and Sinduvāra trees and Vāsantī creepers ravished the soul. The Mādhavī creepers were charged with odour, while the Kunda (jasmine) shrubs were in blossom. (76—78)

verses.text:
चिरिबिल्वा मधूकाश्च वञ्जुला बकुलास्तथा।
रञ्जकास्तिलकाश्चैव नागवृक्षाश्च पुष्पिताः॥ ७९॥
verses.m: Nay, Ciribilva and Madhūka, Vañjula and Bakula, Rañjaka and Tilaka trees and Nāga trees too burst into blossom. (79)

verses.text:
चूताः पाटलिकाश्चैव कोविदाराश्च पुष्पिताः।
मुचुलिन्दार्जुनाश्चैव शिंशपाः कुटजास्तथा॥ ८०॥
हिन्तालास्तिनिशाश्चैव चूर्णका नीपकास्तथा।
नीलाशोकाश्च सरला अङ्कोलाः पद्मकास्तथा॥ ८१॥
verses.m: Mango as well as Pāṭala and Kovidāra, Muculinda as well as Arjuna, Śiṁśapā and Kuṭaja, Hintāla as well as Tiniśa, Cūrṇa and Nīpa, blue Aśoka, Sarala, Aṅkola and Padmaka trees too were in blossom. (80-81)

verses.text:
प्रीयमाणैः प्लवंगैस्तु सर्वे पर्याकुलीकृताः।
वाप्यस्तस्मिन् गिरौ रम्याः पल्वलानि तथैव च॥ ८२॥
चक्रवाकानुचरिताः कारण्डवनिषेविताः।
प्लवैः क्रौञ्चैश्च संकीर्णा वराहमृगसेविताः॥ ८३॥
verses.m: All the aforesaid trees on their part were set in commotion by the said monkeys, who felt pleased at the sight of their blossom. There were lovely wells with stairs as well as ponds on that mountain, which were frequented by Cakrawāka birds, the ruddy geese, inhabited by ducks, crowded with water-fowls and cranes and were haunted by boars and deer. (82-83)

verses.text:
ऋक्षैस्तरक्षुभिः सिंहैः शार्दूलैश्च भयावहैः।
व्यालैश्च बहुभिर्भीमैः सेव्यमानाः समन्ततः॥ ८४॥
verses.m: Nay, they were being visited on all sides by bears, hyenas, lions, tigers inspiring terror and many dreadful and vicious elephants. (84)

verses.text:
पद्मैः सौगन्धिकैः फुल्लैः कुमुदैश्चोत्पलैस्तथा।
वारिजैर्विविधैः पुष्पै रम्यास्तत्र जलाशयाः॥ ८५॥
verses.m: The reservoirs of water in the shape of lakes etc., on that mountain looked charming with expanded blue lotuses, water-lilies, white water-lilies and other aquatic flowers of various kinds. (85)

verses.text:
तस्य सानुषु कूजन्ति नानाद्विजगणास्तथा।
स्नात्वा पीत्वोदकान्यत्र जले क्रीडन्ति वानराः॥ ८६॥
अन्योन्यं प्लावयन्ति स्म शैलमारुह्य वानराः।
फलान्यमृतगन्धीनि मूलानि कुसुमानि च॥ ८७॥
बभञ्जुर्वानरास्तत्र पादपानां मदोत्कटाः।
द्रोणमात्रप्रमाणानि लम्बमानानि वानराः॥ ८८॥
ययुः पिबन्तः स्वस्थास्ते मधूनि मधुपिङ्गलाः।
पादपानवभञ्जन्तो विकर्षन्तस्तथा लताः॥ ८९॥
विधमन्तो गिरिवरान् प्रययुः प्लवगर्षभाः।
वृक्षेभ्योऽन्ये तु कपयो नदन्तो मधु दर्पिताः॥ ९०॥
अन्ये वृक्षान् प्रपद्यन्ते प्रपिबन्त्यपि चापरे।
बभूव वसुधा तैस्तु सम्पूर्णा हरिपुङ्गवैः।
यथा कमलकेदारैः पक्वैरिव वसुंधरा॥ ९१॥
verses.m: Nay, flocks of birds of various kinds sang on the peaks of that mountain. Having bathed and quaffed water, the monkeys sported and plunged one another in these lakes etc. Climbing the mountain, the monkeys broke down the fruits, fragrant as nectar, as well as the flowers of the trees as also the roots on that mountain. Nay, the aforesaid monkeys, who were drunk with pride of strength and were tawny like honey, quaffed honey from the hanging honeycombs, weighing about a maund* each, and went their way contented and happy. The jewels among monkeys marched on, smashing the trees, pulling the climbers and throwing away the foremost of mountains. Removing honey from the trees, other proud monkeys for their part thundered. Others proceeded to the trees to snatch away honey, while still others quaffed honey to their heart’s content. Entirely covered with those bulls among monkeys, the earth for its part looked like a piece of land covered with ripe fields of paddy. (86—91)

verses.text:
महेन्द्रमथ सम्प्राप्य रामो राजीवलोचनः।
आरुरोह महाबाहुः शिखरं द्रुमभूषितम्॥ ९२॥
verses.m: Duly reaching the Mahendra mountain, the mighty-armed Śrī Rāma with lotus-like eyes forthwith ascended its peak adorned with trees. (92)

verses.text:
ततः शिखरमारुह्य रामो दशरथात्मजः।
कूर्ममीनसमाकीर्णमपश्यत् सलिलाशयम्॥ ९३॥
verses.m: Having climbed up its peak, Śrī Rāma, son of King Daśaratha, beheld from it the sea crowded with turtle and fish. (93)

verses.text:
ते सह्यं समतिक्रम्य मलयं च महागिरिम्।
आसेदुरानुपूर्व्येण समुद्रं भीमनिःस्वनम्॥ ९४॥
verses.m: Having duly crossed in the first place the Sahya mountain as well as the great Malaya mountain, they reached in due course, after crossing the Mahendra mountain the sea, which was making a terrible noise. (94)

verses.text:
अवरुह्य जगामाशु वेलावनमनुत्तमम्।
रामो रमयतां श्रेष्ठः ससुग्रीवः सलक्ष्मणः॥ ९५॥
verses.m: Climbing down the Mahendra mountain, Śrī Rāma, the foremost of those who ravish the mind, accompanied by Sugrīva, the king of monkeys, and Lakṣmaṇa quickly sought the most excellent woodland adjoining the sea. (95)

verses.text:
अथ धौतोपलतलां तोयौघैः सहसोत्थितैः।
वेलामासाद्य विपुलां रामो वचनमब्रवीत्॥ ९६॥
verses.m: Having arrived at the vast sea-shore, the foot of whose rocks had been washed by volumes of water risen all of a sudden, Śrī Rāma spoke as follows: (96)

verses.text:
एते वयमनुप्राप्ताः सुग्रीव वरुणालयम्।
इहेदानीं विचिन्ता सा या नः पूर्वमुपस्थिता॥ ९७॥
verses.m: “We have now reached the sea, the abode of Varuṇa, the god of water, O Sugrīva! The same problem faces me here at the present moment, which stared us in the face before. (97)

verses.text:
अतः परमतीरोऽयं सागरः सरितां पतिः।
न चायमनुपायेन शक्यस्तरितुमर्णवः॥ ९८॥
verses.m: “Beyond this stretches the yonder shoreless sea, the lord of rivers, and this sea cannot be crossed without some device. (98)

verses.text:
तदिहैव निवेशोऽस्तु मन्त्रः प्रस्तूयतामिह।
यथेदं वानरबलं परं पारमवाप्नुयात्॥ ९९॥
verses.m: “Therefore, let an encampment be made at this very spot and let deliberation be set on foot here, so that this army of monkeys may reach the opposite shore.” (99)

verses.text:
इतीव स महाबाहुः सीताहरणकर्शितः।
रामः सागरमासाद्य वासमाज्ञापयत् तदा॥ १००॥
verses.m: In these words did the celebrated Śrī Rāma of mighty arms, who was emaciated due to the abduction of Sītā, enjoin the quartering of his army on reaching the sea. (100)

verses.text:
सर्वाः सेना निवेश्यन्तां वेलायां हरिपुङ्गव।
सम्प्राप्तो मन्त्रकालो नः सागरस्येह लङ्घने॥ १०१॥
verses.m: “Let all the forces be quartered on the strand, O bull among monkeys,” he continued. “The time is ripe for us to discuss the means of crossing the sea at this point. (101)

verses.text:
स्वां स्वां सेनां समुत्सृज्य मा च कश्चित् कुतो व्रजेत्।
गच्छन्तु वानराः शूरा ज्ञेयं छन्नं भयं च नः॥ १०२॥
verses.m: “Let no one slip away on any account whatsoever, leaving his unit of army. Let the gallant monkeys make a move to guard the army against any possible danger; and it should be known that there may be covert danger for us.” (102)

verses.text:
रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवः सहलक्ष्मणः।
सेनां निवेशयत् तीरे सागरस्य द्रुमायुते॥ १०३॥
verses.m: Hearing the command of Śrī Rāma, Sugrīva with Lakṣmaṇa caused the army to be quartered on the beach covered with trees. (103)

verses.text:
विरराज समीपस्थं सागरस्य च तद् बलम्।
मधुपाण्डुजलः श्रीमान् द्वितीय इव सागरः॥ १०४॥
verses.m: Quartered in the vicinity of the sea, that army shone brightly like a second glorious sea with its water pale-white as honey. (104)

verses.text:
वेलावनमुपागम्य ततस्ते हरिपुङ्गवाः।
निविष्टाश्च परं पारं काङ् क्षमाणा महोदधेः॥ १०५॥
verses.m: Having reached the forest adjoining the beach, the aforesaid bulls among monkeys then encamped there, seeking to reach the other shore of the vast sea. (105)

verses.text:
तेषां निविशमानानां सैन्यसंनाहनिःस्वनः।
अन्तर्धाय महानादमर्णवस्य प्रशुश्रुवे॥ १०६॥
verses.m: The noise of the movement of the army, while they were encamping, was distinctly heard drowning the roar of the sea. (106)

verses.text:
सा वानराणां ध्वजिनी सुग्रीवेणाभिपालिता।
त्रिधा निविष्टा महती रामस्यार्थपराभवत्॥ १०७॥
verses.m: Protected on all sides by Sugrīva and devoted to the cause of Śrī Rāma, that huge army of monkeys was encamped in three divisions viz., (i) bears, (ii) Go-Lāṅgūlas or long-tailed monkeys (लंगूर) and (iii) monkeys. (107)

verses.text:
सा महार्णवमासाद्य हृष्टा वानरवाहिनी।
वायुवेगसमाधूतं पश्यमाना महार्णवम्॥ १०८॥
verses.m: Having reached the vast sea and beholding the ocean lashed by the force of the winds, the said army of monkeys felt rejoiced. (108)

verses.text:
दूरपारमसम्बाधं रक्षोगणनिषेवितम्।
पश्यन्तो वरुणावासं निषेदुर्हरियूथपाः॥ १०९॥
चण्डनक्रग्राहघोरं क्षपादौ दिवसक्षये।
हसन्तमिव फेनौघैर्नृत्यन्तमिव चोर्मिभिः॥ ११०॥
चन्द्रोदये समुद्भूतं प्रतिचन्द्रसमाकुलम्।
चण्डानिलमहाग्राहैः कीर्णं तिमितिमिंगिलैः॥ १११॥
दीप्तभोगैरिवाकीर्णं भुजङ्गैर्वरुणालयम्।
अवगाढं महासत्त्वैर्नानाशैलसमाकुलम्॥ ११२॥
सुदुर्गं दुर्गमार्गं तमगाधमसुरालयम्।
मकरैर्नागभोगैश्च विगाढा वातलोलिताः।
उत्पेतुश्च निपेतुश्च प्रहृष्टा जलराशयः॥ ११३॥
verses.m: The leaders of the monkey troops sat surveying the sea (lit., the abode of Varuṇa, the god of water), with shores far apart, nay, stretching without any obstruction for hundreds of miles together and infested with hordes of ogres—the sea which looked terrible on account of its furious crocodiles and alligators; which was tossed high at the close of the day and the approach of night at moonrise and was full of images of the moon, reflected on its billows, which laughed as it were through volumes of foam produced * We read in the Purāṇas: by its waves and danced as it were through its billows; which was crowded with huge alligators, swift as a furious gale as well as with Timis* (a species of gigantic fish believed to be a hundred Yojanas or eight hundred miles long) and Timingilas (fish capable of devouring even Timis); which was swarmed with serpents endowed with flaming hoods and thus looked like Pātāla, the abode of Varuṇa; which was crowded with enormous aquatic creatures and thickly set with mountains (under water), which had excellent fastnesses like Laṅkā on its shore, which could not be easily crossed, and which was fathomless and an abode of demons. Volumes of its water, whipped into motion by the winds and penetrated into by sharks and the bodies of serpents, rose and fell joyfully. (109—113)

verses.text:
अग्निचूर्णमिवाविद्धं भास्वराम्बुमहोरगम्।
सुरारिनिलयं घोरं पातालविषयं सदा॥ ११४॥
सागरं चाम्बरप्रख्यमम्बरं सागरोपमम्।
सागरं चाम्बरं चेति निर्विशेषमदृश्यत॥ ११५॥
verses.m: With its sparkling spray, the sea, which is always the dread refuge of demons (the enemies of gods) and is infested with huge serpents and reaches in its depth up to Pātāla (the nethermost subterranean region), looked like a multitude of sparks thrown here and there and also presented the appearance of the firmament whose sparkling frozen dew-drops appeared like so many sparks thrown here and there, nay, which is frequented by Nāgas, is the abode of demons and is deep as Pātāla; while the firmament above looked like another sea. Nay, the sea as well as the firmament looked just the same. (114-115)

verses.text:
सम्पृक्तं नभसाप्यम्भः सम्पृक्तं च नभोऽम्भसा।
तादृग्रूपे स्म दृश्येते तारारत्नसमाकुले॥ ११६॥
verses.m: The water of the sea was linked with the firmament and the latter with the water of the sea. Full of stars and pearls, respectively, the two appeared identical. (116)

verses.text:
समुत्पतितमेघस्य वीचिमालाकुलस्य च।
विशेषो न द्वयोरासीत् सागरस्याम्बरस्य च॥ ११७॥
verses.m: No distinction could be made between the two, viz., the sea and the firmament, in the latter of which (the sky) clouds had sprung into existence, while the former was crowded with rows of waves. (117)

verses.text:
अन्योन्यैरहताः सक्ताः सस्वनुर्भीमनिःस्वनाः।
ऊर्मयः सिन्धुराजस्य महाभेर्य इवाम्बरे॥ ११८॥
verses.m: Having come in close contact with and collided against one another, the waves of the kingly sea roared with a terrible noise like huge kettledrums sounding in the air. (118)

verses.text:
रत्नौघजलसंनादं विषक्तमिव वायुना।
उत्पतन्तमिव क्रुद्धं यादोगणसमाकुलम्॥ ११९॥
verses.m: The monkeys saw the sea concentrated, as it were, at one place by the wind, nay, characterized by the noise of precious stones scattered by it as well as by the roaring of its waves, also infested with aquatic creatures and rising high as though infuriated. (119)

verses.text:
ददृशुस्ते महात्मानो वाताहतजलाशयम्।
अनिलोद्धूतमाकाशे प्रवलान्तमिवोर्मिभिः॥ १२०॥
verses.m: Those high-souled monkeys surveyed the sea lashed by the winds and tossed by them in the air, nay, dancing, as it were, through its waves. (120)

verses.text:
ततो विस्मयमापन्ना हरयो ददृशुः स्थिताः।
भ्रान्तोर्मिजालसंनादं प्रलोलमिव सागरम्॥ १२१॥
verses.m: Standing wonderstruck at this, the monkeys saw the sea full of noise produced by the rolling waves, riotous, as it were. (121)

verses.text:
सा तु नीलेन विधिवत्स्वारक्षा सुसमाहिता।
सागरस्योत्तरे तीरे साधु सा विनिवेशिता॥ १॥
verses.m: Properly guarded by itself and fully vigilant, the aforesaid army of monkeys for its part was comfortably quartered on the northern shore of the sea by Nīla, the Commander-in-Chief. (1)

verses.text:
मैन्दश्च द्विविदश्चोभौ तत्र वानरपुङ्गवौ।
विचेरतुश्च तां सेनां रक्षार्थं सर्वतोदिशम्॥ २॥
verses.m: Nay, both Mainda and Dwivida, the two bulls among monkeys, patrolled in that area on all sides of the army for its protection. (2)

verses.text:
निविष्टायां तु सेनायां तीरे नदनदीपतेः।
पार्श्वस्थं लक्ष्मणं दृष्ट्वा रामो वचनमब्रवीत्॥ ३॥
verses.m: The army having been quartered on the shore of the sea (the lord of all rivers and streams), Śrī Rāma for his part spoke as follows to Lakṣmaṇa on seeing him standing by his side: (3)

verses.text:
शोकश्च किल कालेन गच्छता ह्यपगच्छति।
मम चापश्यतः कान्तामहन्यहनि वर्धते॥ ४॥
verses.m: “As time passes, grief too, they say, undoubtedly disappears; in my case, however, even as I miss my darling, Sītā, it grows day by day. (4)

verses.text:
न मे दुःखं प्रिया दूरे न मे दुःखं हृतेति च।
एतदेवानुशोचामि वयोऽस्या ह्यतिवर्तते॥ ५॥
verses.m: “My agony does not exist because my beloved is away from me, nor is it due to the fact that she has been borne away. I grieve for this alone that the time allowed for her survival is actually passing away. (5)

verses.text:
वाहि वात यतः कान्ता तां स्पृष्ट्वा मामपि स्पृश।
त्वयि मे गात्रसंस्पर्शश्चन्द्रे दृष्टिसमागमः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Speed, O Breeze, to the spot where my love is; having fanned her, touch me as well. The touch of my body with you in that case will react in the same way as the meeting of one’s gaze with the moon i.e., reliever of all pain and exhilarating. (6)

verses.text:
तन्मे दहति गात्राणि विषं पीतमिवाशये।
हा नाथेति प्रिया सा मां ह्रियमाणा यदब्रवीत्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “The exclamation ‘Ah, my lord!’ which that darling addressed to me while being borne away by the ogre, consumes my limbs like poison swallowed by me and continuing in my stomach. (7)

verses.text:
तद्वियोगेन्धनवता तच्चिन्ताविमलार्चिषा।
रात्रिं दिवं शरीरं मे दह्यते मदनाग्निना॥ ८॥
verses.m: “My body is consumed night and day by the fire of love fed with the fuel of my separation from her and flaring up into the bright flame of my thought of her. (8)

verses.text:
अवगाह्यार्णवं स्वप्स्ये सौमित्रे भवता विना।
एवं च प्रज्वलन् कामो न मा सुप्तं जले दहेत्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Diving into the sea, without you as my companion, O darling of Sumitrā, I shall repose there. Flaming love will not certainly consume me lying asleep in water, as aforesaid. (9)

verses.text:
बह्वेतत् कामयानस्य शक्यमेतेन जीवितुम्।
यदहं सा च वामोरुरेकां धरणिमाश्रितौ॥ १०॥
verses.m: “That the said lady of charming limbs and myself repose on the selfsame earth is enough consolation for me, soliciting as I do her company (desolate that I am) and it will be possible for me to survive on this score alone. (10)

verses.text:
केदारस्येव केदारः सोदकस्य निरूदकः।
उपस्नेहेन जीवामि जीवन्तीं यच्छृणोमि ताम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Even as the crop in a field without water remains alive through contact with a field underwater, I too survive because I hear of her surviving. (11)

verses.text:
कदा नु खलु सुश्रोणीं शतपत्रायतेक्षणाम्।
विजित्य शत्रून् द्रक्ष्यामि सीतां स्फीतामिव श्रियम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “When on earth, having thoroughly conquered my enemies, shall I actually behold Sītā of excellent limbs and eyes large as a lotus, and welcome as abundant fortune? (12)

verses.text:
कदा सुचारुदन्तोष्ठं तस्याः पद्ममिवाननम्।
ईषदुन्नाम्य पास्यामि रसायनमिवातुरः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “When, raising a bit her lotus-like face with its extremely charming teeth and lips, shall I kiss it even as an ailing man would drink an elixir of life? (13)

verses.text:
तौ तस्याः सहितौ पीनौ स्तनौ तालफलोपमौ।
कदा न खलु सोत्कम्पौ श्लिष्यन्त्या मां भजिष्यतः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “O, when will her close, bulging and quivering breasts, resembling the palmyra fruit, actually press me even as she embraces me? (14)

verses.text:
सा नूनमसितापाङ्गी रक्षोमध्यगता सती।
मन्नाथा नाथहीनेव त्रातारं नाधिगच्छति॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Surely that virtuous lady with dark-cornered eyes, who has myself alone for her protector and has fallen in the midst of ogres, does not find a redeemer any more than a woman without a protector. (15)

verses.text:
कथं जनकराजस्य दुहिता मम च प्रिया।
राक्षसीमध्यगा शेते स्नुषा दशरथस्य च॥ १६॥
verses.m: “How does the daughter of Janaka, nay, my darling and the daughter-in-law of Daśaratha repose in the midst of ogresses? (16)

verses.text:
अविक्षोभ्याणि रक्षांसि सा विधूयोत्पतिष्यति।
विधूय जलदान् नीलाञ्शशिलेखा शरत्स्विव॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Will Sītā emerge into view destroying through me the unshakable ogres, in the same way as the crescent would shine forth during the autumn dispersing the dark clouds? (17)

verses.text:
स्वभावतनुका नूनं शोकेनानशनेन च।
भूयस्तनुतरा सीता देशकालविपर्ययात्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Sītā, who is slender by nature, must undoubtedly be leaner still from grief and abstinence from food due to adversity of time and place. (18)

verses.text:
कदा नु राक्षसेन्द्रस्य निधायोरसि सायकान्।
शोकं प्रत्याहरिष्यामि शोकमुत्सृज्य मानसम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: “O, when, digging shafts into the breast of Rāvaṇa (the ruler of ogres), and casting off my mental woe, shall I dispel the grief of Sītā? (19)

verses.text:
कदा नु खलु मे साध्वी सीतामरसुतोपमा।
सोत्कण्ठा कण्ठमालम्ब्य मोक्ष्यत्यानन्दजं जलम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “O when, clinging to my neck, full of longing, will my virtuous Sītā, who is like a daughter of the gods, shed tears of joy? (20)

verses.text:
कदा शोकमिमं घोरं मैथिलीविप्रयोगजम्।
सहसा विप्रमोक्ष्यामि वासः शुक्लेतरं यथा॥ २१॥
verses.m: “When shall I cast away thoroughly and for good all at once this terrible grief born of separation from Sītā, a princess of Mithilā, in the same way as one would discard a soiled garment?” (21)

verses.text:
एवं विलपतस्तस्य तत्र रामस्य धीमतः।
दिनक्षयान्मन्दवपुर्भास्करोऽस्तमुपागमत् ॥ २२॥
verses.m: While the sagacious Śrī Rāma was wailing as aforesaid on that spot, the sun, whose brilliance had grown dim due to the decline of the day, disappeared below the western horizon. (22)

verses.text:
आश्वासितो लक्ष्मणेन रामः संध्यामुपासत।
स्मरन् कमलपत्राक्षीं सीतां शोकाकुलीकृतः॥ २३॥
verses.m: Comforted by Lakṣmaṇa, Śrī Rāma, who was distracted with grief, performed his evening devotions, thinking all the time of Sītā, whose eyes resembled the petals of a lotus. (23)

verses.text:
लङ्कायां तु कृतं कर्म घोरं दृष्ट्वा भयावहम्।
राक्षसेन्द्रो हनुमता शक्रेणेव महात्मना।
अब्रवीद् राक्षसान् सर्वान् ह्रिया किंचिदवाङ् मुखः॥ १॥
verses.m: Perceiving the terrible and grisly feat accomplished in Laṅkā by the high-souled Hanumān, who vied with Indra in might, Rāvaṇa, the lord of ogres, spoke as follows to all the ogres, his looks directed a bit downwards from bashfulness: (1)

verses.text:
धर्षिता च प्रविष्टा च लङ्का दुष्प्रसहा पुरी।
तेन वानरमात्रेण दृष्टा सीता च जानकी॥ २॥
verses.m: “The city of Laṅkā, which was difficult to challenge, has been assailed and penetrated into and Sītā found out by Hanumān, a mere monkey. (2)

verses.text:
प्रासादो धर्षितश्चैत्यः प्रवरा राक्षसा हताः।
आविला च पुरी लङ्का सर्वा हनुमता कृता॥ ३॥
verses.m: “The edifice used as a sanctuary has been penetrated, the topmost ogres have been killed and the entire city of Laṅkā turned upside down by Hanumān. (3)

verses.text:
किं करिष्यामि भद्रं वः किं वो युक्तमनन्तरम्।
उच्यतां नः समर्थं यत् कृतं च सुकृतं भवेत्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “May good betide you, what shall I do next? What appeals to you as advisable to do next? Please suggest what is equal to us and what, if attempted, will be well executed. (4)

verses.text:
मन्त्रमूलं च विजयं प्रवदन्ति मनस्विनः।
तस्माद् वै रोचये मन्त्रं रामं प्रति महाबलाः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “The wise declare victory as dependent on good counsel. I, therefore, prefer to take your counsel with regard to Rāma, O ogres of extraordinary might! (5)

verses.text:
त्रिविधाः पुरुषा लोके उत्तमाधममध्यमाः।
तेषां तु समवेतानां गुणदोषौ वदाम्यहम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “There are three kinds of men in the world—the good, the bad and the mediocre. I, for my part, describe the good points as well as the shortcomings of them all as follows: (6)

verses.text:
मन्त्रस्त्रिभिर्हि संयुक्तः समर्थैर्मन्त्रनिर्णये।
मित्रैर्वापि समानार्थैर्बान्धवैरपि वाधिकैः॥ ७॥
सहितो मन्त्रयित्वा यः कर्मारम्भान् प्रवर्तयेत्।
दैवे च कुरुते यत्नं तमाहुः पुरुषोत्तमम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “The wise declare him to be the foremost of men, whose counsel is actually endowed with the following three characteristics, and who prosecutes his undertakings after deliberating with his friends, who are capable of deciding a point at issue or with relations having common interests or even with his superiors and exerts himself depending on Providence. (7-8)

verses.text:
एकोऽर्थं विमृशेदेको धर्मे प्रकुरुते मनः।
एकः कार्याणि कुरुते तमाहुर्मध्यमं नरम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “They call him mediocre, who ponders his interests by himself, sets his mind on virtue all by himself and executes his designs single-handed. (9)

verses.text:
गुणदोषौ न निश्चित्य त्यक्त्वा दैवव्यपाश्रयम्।
करिष्यामीति यः कार्यमुपेक्षेत् स नराधमः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Failing to ascertain the advantages and the disadvantages of a scheme, nay, renouncing his dependence on Providence and merely saying ‘I shall do it’, he who neglects his duty is the vilest of men. (10)

verses.text:
यथेमे पुरुषा नित्यमुत्तमाधममध्यमाः।
एवं मन्त्रोऽपि विज्ञेय उत्तमाधममध्यमः॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Even as the aforementioned people are either ever good, bad or mediocre, so the conclusion arrived at by them is also good, bad or mediocre. (11)

verses.text:
ऐकमत्यमुपागम्य शास्त्रदृष्टेन चक्षुषा।
मन्त्रिणो यत्र निरतास्तमाहुर्मन्त्रमुत्तमम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “The wise declare that conclusion to be excellent in which the counsellors feel specially interested, after reaching an agreement based on a point of view supported by the scriptures. (12)

verses.text:
बह्वीरपि मतीर्गत्वा मन्त्रिणामर्थनिर्णयः।
पुनर्यत्रैकतां प्राप्तः स मन्त्रो मध्यमः स्मृतः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “That conclusion is declared to be mediocre in arriving at which the judgment of the counsellors with regard to the point at issue reaches unanimity only after meeting with different angles of views. (13)

verses.text:
अन्योन्यमतिमास्थाय यत्र सम्प्रतिभाष्यते।
न चैकमत्ये श्रेयोऽस्ति मन्त्रः सोऽधम उच्यते॥ १४॥
verses.m: “That conclusion, again, is declared to be third-rate, in arriving at which speeches and counter-speeches are made emphasising different points of view and from which good fortune does not follow even in the event of unanimity being arrived at somehow. (14)

verses.text:
तस्मात् सुमन्त्रितं साधु भवन्तो मतिसत्तमाः।
कार्यं सम्प्रतिपद्यन्तमेतत् कृत्यं मतं मम॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Therefore, determine you, who are foremost in point of intelligence, a course of conduct which is well-deliberated and, therefore, right. This alone is reckoned by me as worth adopting. (15)

verses.text:
वानराणां हि धीराणां सहस्रैः परिवारितः।
रामोऽभ्येति पुरीं लङ्कामस्माकमुपरोधकः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Surrounded by thousands of heroic monkeys, Rāma is actually advancing towards the city of Laṅkā in order to besiege us. (16)

verses.text:
तरिष्यति च सुव्यक्तं राघवः सागरं सुखम्।
तरसा युक्तरूपेण सानुजः सबलानुगः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Clearly enough, by virtue of his might, which is worthy of him, Rāma (a scion of Raghu) will cross the sea with ease alongwith his younger brother as well as with his forces and entourage. (17)

verses.text:
समुद्रमुच्छोषयति वीर्येणान्यत्करोति वा।
तस्मिन्नेवंविधे कार्ये विरुद्धे वानरैः सह।
हितं पुरे च सैन्ये च सर्वं सम्मन्त्र्यतां मम॥ १८॥
verses.m: “He will either dry up the sea by dint of his prowess or do something else to bridge the sea. The aforesaid work of invading Laṅkā having commenced in this way and antagonism with the monkeys having been set on foot, advice may be tendered to me on whatever is good for the city and the army.” (18)

verses.text:
इत्युक्ता राक्षसेन्द्रेण राक्षसास्ते महाबलाः।
ऊचुः प्राञ्जलयः सर्वे रावणं राक्षसेश्वरम्॥ १॥
द्विषत्पक्षमविज्ञाय नीतिबाह्यास्त्वबुद्धयः।
राजन् परिघशक्त्यृष्टिशूलपट्टिशकुन्तलम्॥ २॥
सुमहन्नो बलं कस्माद् विषादं भजते भवान्।
त्वया भोगवतीं गत्वा निर्जिताः पन्नगा युधि॥ ३॥
verses.m: Not knowing in full about the strength of the enemy’s army, all the aforesaid ogres, who, though endowed with extraordinary might, were unaware of political wisdom and lacked intelligence, submitted, when commanded thus by Rāvaṇa, the lord of ogres, with joined palms as follows: “There exists with us, O king, a huge army equipped with iron bars, javelins, double-edged swords, darts, sharp-edged spears and lances. Why then do you give way to despondency. After proceeding to Bhogavatī (the city of the Nāgas in Pātāla), the Nāgas were completely subdued by you in combat. (1—3)

verses.text:
कैलासशिखरावासी यक्षैर्बहुभिरावृतः।
सुमहत्कदनं कृत्वा वश्यस्ते धनदः कृतः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Nay, after waging a terrible conflict, even Kubera, the bestower of riches, who dwells on a peak of Mount Kailāsa and remains surrounded by numerous Yakṣas (a class of demigods), was reduced to submission by you. (4)

verses.text:
स महेश्वरसख्येन श्लाघमानस्त्वया विभो।
निर्जितः समरे रोषाल्लोकपालो महाबलः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Priding, as he did, on his friendship with Lord Śiva, the Supreme Lord, the aforesaid Kubera (a guardian of the world), who is endowed with extraordinary might, was utterly subdued by you on the field of battle in indignation, O powerful king! (5)

verses.text:
विनिपात्य च यक्षौघान् विक्षोभ्य विनिगृह्य च।
त्वया कैलासशिखराद् विमानमिदमाहृतम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “After causing a stir among the Yakṣa hordes, nay, taking them as prisoners and overthrowing them—this aerial car (Puṣpaka) was taken away by you from the peak of Mount Kailāsa. (6)

verses.text:
मयेन दानवेन्द्रेण त्वद्भयात् सख्यमिच्छता।
दुहिता तव भार्यार्थे दत्ता राक्षसपुङ्गव॥ ७॥
verses.m: “By Maya (मय), a ruler of the Dānavas (the son of Dānu), who sought an alliance with you out of fear of you, O bull among ogres, his daughter, Mandodarī, was given to you in marraige as your wife. (7)

verses.text:
दानवेन्द्रो महाबाहो वीर्योत्सिक्तो दुरासदः।
विगृह्य वशमानीतः कुम्भीनस्याः सुखावहः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Madhu (another ruler of the Dānavas), the husband (lit., the joy) of Kumbhīnasī, your beloved sister, who was proud of his virility and was difficult to approach, was subjugated by you by offering battle to him, O mighty-armed one! (8)

verses.text:
निर्जितास्ते महाबाहो नागा गत्वा रसातलम्।
वासुकिस्तक्षकः शङ्खो जटी च वशमाहृताः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “After descending into Rasātala (the penultimate subterranean region) the serpent-demons Vāsuki, Takṣaka, Śaṅkha and Jaṭī were completely subdued and reduced to submission by you, O mighty-armed one! (9)

verses.text:
अक्षया बलवन्तश्च शूरा लब्धवराः पुनः।
त्वया संवत्सरं युद्ध्वा समरे दानवा विभो॥ १०॥
स्वबलं समुपाश्रित्य नीता वशमरिंदम।
मायाश्चाधिगतास्तत्र बह्व्यो वै राक्षसाधिप॥ ११॥
verses.m: “After carrying on a struggle for a whole year on the field of battle, O powerful suzerain lord of ogres, Dānavas (sons of Kālakā) who were beyond destruction, mighty and valiant and had obtained boons (of immortality), were reduced to submission by you by resorting to your own strength, O tamer of foes, and many conjuring tricks were learnt from them. (10-11)

verses.text:
शूराश्च बलवन्तश्च वरुणस्य सुता रणे।
निर्जितास्ते महाभाग चतुर्विधबलानुगाः॥ १२॥
verses.m: Those heroic and mighty sons of Varuṇa, who were followed by an army consisting of four limbs, viz., elephants, chariots, cavalry and infantry, were completely subdued by you, O highly blessed one! (12)

verses.text:
मृत्युदण्डमहाग्राहं शाल्मलीद्रुममण्डितम्।
कालपाशमहावीचिं यमकिंकरपन्नगम्॥ १३॥
महाज्वरेण दुर्धर्षं यमलोकमहार्णवम्।
अवगाह्य त्वया राजन् यमस्य बलसागरम्॥ १४॥
जयश्च विपुलः प्राप्तो मृत्युश्च प्रतिषेधितः।
सुयुद्धेन च ते सर्वे लोकस्तत्र सुतोषिताः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “After plunging into the ocean in the shape of Yama’s realm with an enormous alligator in the form of Death’s rod of punishment, nay, adorned with Śālmalī (silk cotton) trees (bristling with thorns to tear the bodies of damned sinners with), turbulent with a huge billow in the shape of the noose of Kāla (the Time-Spirit) infested with serpents in the form of Yama’s servants and difficult to overcome on account of the mighty Jwara (the spirit presiding over fevers), and churning the sea in the shape of Yama’s forces, a momentous victory was scored and Death repulsed by you; nay, all those people there were highly gratified through your excellent fighting skill. (13—15)

verses.text:
क्षत्रियैर्बहुभिर्वीरैः शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमैः।
आसीद् वसुमती पूर्णा महद्भिरिव पादपैः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “The earth was formerly filled with numerous Kṣatriya heroes, equal in prowess to Indra (the ruler of gods), as with gigantic trees. (16)

verses.text:
तेषां वीर्यगुणोत्साहैर्न समो राघवो रणे।
प्रसह्य ते त्वया राजन् हताः समरदुर्जयाः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Rāma, a scion of Raghu, is not equal to them on the battlefield in point of prowess, martial qualities and bellicose spirit. Even though difficult to conquer in an encounter, they were violently made short work of by you at once. (17)

verses.text:
तिष्ठ वा किं महाराज श्रमेण तव वानरान्।
अयमेको महाबाहुरिन्द्रजित् क्षपयिष्यति॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Or, remain where you are, O king! What is the use of your exerting yourself? This mighty-armed Indrajit, your eldest son, will extirpate all the monkeys, single-handed. (18)

verses.text:
अनेन च महाराज माहेश्वरमनुत्तमम्।
इष्ट्वा यज्ञं वरो लब्धो लोके परमदुर्लभः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Nay, after performing a sacrifice intended to propitiate Lord Śiva (the Supreme Lord), a boon, which was supremely difficult to win in the world, was secured by him from Lord Śiva, O mighty sovereign! (19)

verses.text:
शक्तितोमरमीनं च विनिकीर्णान्त्रशैवलम्।
गजकच्छपसम्बाधमश्वमण्डूकसंकुलम् ॥ २०॥
रुद्रादित्यमहाग्राहं मरुद्वसुमहोरगम्।
रथाश्वगजतोयौघं पदातिपुलिनं महत्॥ २१॥
अनेन हि समासाद्य देवानां बलसागरम्।
गृहीतो दैवतपतिर्लङ्कां चापि प्रवेशितः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “After assailing the sea in the form of the celestial army with javelins and spears for its fish and entrails thrown asunder for duck-weeds, nay, full of turtles in the form of elephants, teeming with frogs in the form of horses, infested with alligators in the form of the eleven Rudras (gods of destruction) and twelve Ādityas (sons of Aditi), and with huge serpents in the form of the forty-nine Maruts (wind-gods) and the eight Vasus, and having chariots, horses and elephants for its volume of water and foot-soldiers for its sandy beach, Indra, the ruler of gods, was actually captured by him and thrust into Laṅkā as a detenu. (20—22)

verses.text:
पितामहनियोगाच्च मुक्तः शम्बरवृत्रहा।
गतस्त्रिविष्टपं राजन् सर्वदेवनमस्कृतः॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Nay, liberated by the command of Brahmā (the grandfather of all created beings, the whole creation having been brought into existence by his ten mind-born sons, the Prajāpatis), Indra (the destroyer of the demons Śambara and Vṛtra), who is adored by all the gods, returned to heaven, O king! (23)

verses.text:
तमेव त्वं महाराज विसृजेन्द्रजितं सुतम्।
यावद् वानरसेनां तां सरामां नयति क्षयम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Therefore, dispatch, O mighty ruler, your aforesaid son, Indrajit, alone, so that he may bring to an end the said army of the monkeys, including Rāma (even before it dares to cross the sea). (24)

verses.text:
राजन्नापदयुक्तेयमागता प्राकृताज्जनात्।
हृदि नैव त्वया कार्या त्वं वधिष्यसि राघवम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: “This adversity, which has come from ordinary beings (like human beings and monkeys), O king, does not deserve your concern. It should not at all be given any corner in your heart; for, you shall kill Rāma without doubt.” (25)

verses.text:
ततो नीलाम्बुदप्रख्यः प्रहस्तो नाम राक्षसः।
अब्रवीत् प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं शूरः सेनापतिस्तदा॥ १॥
verses.m: The valiant ogre, Prahasta by name, the Commander-in-Chief, who resembled a dark cloud, then submitted as follows with joined palms on that occasion: (1)

verses.text:
देवदानवगन्धर्वाः पिशाचपतगोरगाः।
सर्वे धर्षयितुं शक्याः किं पुनर्मानवौ रणे॥ २॥
verses.m: “The gods, Dānavas (sons of Danu) and Gandharvas, fiends, birds and serpents, all are capable of being easily overpowered by us in an encounter, much less a couple of mortals. (2)

verses.text:
सर्वे प्रमत्ता विश्वस्ता वञ्चिताः स्म हनूमता।
नहि मे जीवतो गच्छेज्जीवन् स वनगोचरः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “We were all hoodwinked by Hanūmān because we were unwary and unsuspecting. That monkey (a denizen of the forest) could not otherwise escape alive so long as I am living. (3)

verses.text:
सर्वां सागरपर्यन्तां सशैलवनकाननाम्।
करोम्यवानरां भूमिमाज्ञापयतु मां भवान्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “I can sweep the entire globe, bounded by the oceans, with its mountains, forests and woodlands, clear it of all monkeys. Command me, if you will. (4)

verses.text:
रक्षां चैव विधास्यामि वानराद् रजनीचर।
नागमिष्यति ते दुःखं किंचिदात्मापराधजम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Nay, I shall certainly protect you against the monkey race, O ranger of the night! No calamity of any kind born of your own crime (in the shape of Sītā’s abduction) will come to you.” (5)

verses.text:
अब्रवीत् तु सुसंक्रुद्धो दुर्मुखो नाम राक्षसः।
इदं न क्षमणीयं हि सर्वेषां नः प्रधर्षणम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Feeling extremely enraged, another ogre, Durmukha by name, for his part submitted: “This outrage committed against us all is not worth pocketing, indeed. (6)

verses.text:
अयं परिभवो भूयः पुरस्यान्तःपुरस्य च।
श्रीमतो राक्षसेन्द्रस्य वानरेण प्रधर्षणम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Furthermore, this assault by a monkey is an affront to the city of Laṅkā, to the royal gynaeceum as well as to the glorious ruler of ogres. (7)

verses.text:
अस्मिन् मुहूर्ते गत्वैको निवर्तिष्यामि वानरान्।
प्रविष्टान् सागरं भीममम्बरं वा रसातलम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Marching alone at this very hour, I shall repulse the monkeys, even if they have taken refuge in the dreaded deep, in the heavens or in Rasātala (the penultimate subterranean region).” (8)

verses.text:
ततोऽब्रवीत् सुसंक्रुद्धो वज्रदंष्ट्रो महाबलः।
प्रगृह्य परिघं घोरं मांसशोणितरूषितम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: Then spoke as follows Vajradaṁṣṭra, who was endowed with extraordinary might, extremely enraged and clasping his terrible iron bludgeon stained with flesh and blood: (9)

verses.text:
किं नो हनूमता कार्यं कृपणेन तपस्विना।
रामे तिष्ठति दुर्धर्षे सुग्रीवेऽपि सलक्ष्मणे॥ १०॥
verses.m: “What have we got to do with the miserable and poor Hanumān, so long as there is Rāma, who is difficult to assail, as well as Sugrīva, accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa? (10)

verses.text:
अद्य रामं ससुग्रीवं परिघेण सलक्ष्मणम्।
आगमिष्यामि हत्वैको विक्षोभ्य हरिवाहिनीम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Having disposed of single-handed with my iron bludgeon, Rāma, accompanied by Sugrīva and Lakṣmaṇa, and having caused panic in the army of monkeys, I shall return today. (11)

verses.text:
इदं ममापरं वाक्यं शृणु राजन् यदिच्छसि।
उपायकुशलो ह्येव जयेच्छत्रूनतन्द्रितः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Pray, listen, if you will, O king, to this further submision of mine; for he alone who is resourceful is able to conquer his enemies if he is vigilant. (12)

verses.text:
कामरूपधराः शूराः सुभीमा भीमदर्शनाः।
राक्षसा वा सहस्राणि राक्षसाधिप निश्चिताः॥ १३॥
काकुत्स्थमुपसंगम्य बिभ्रतो मानुषं वपुः।
सर्वे ह्यसम्भ्रमा भूत्वा ब्रुवन्तु रघुसत्तमम्॥ १४॥
प्रेषिता भरतेनैव भ्रात्रा तव यवीयसा।
स हि सेनां समुत्थाप्य क्षिप्रमेवोपयास्यति॥ १५॥
