verses.m: “Assuming a human semblance, nay, approaching Rāma, a scion of Kakutstha, and feeling altogether free from embarrassment, O suzerain lord of ogres, heroic and most formidable ogres, terrible to look at, nay, capable of assuming any form at will and determined of purpose, should speak as follows to Rāma, the foremost of Raghus: ‘We have been sent by your younger brother, Bharata, himself, and, ordering his army to march, Rāma too will surely sally forth apace.’ (13—15)

verses.text:
ततो वयमितस्तूर्णं शूलशक्तिगदाधराः।
चापबाणासिहस्ताश्च त्वरितास्तत्र यामहे॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Carrying pikes, javelins and maces and with arrows and swords in hand, we should then speedily reach there with quick steps from this side. (16)

verses.text:
आकाशे गणशः स्थित्वा हत्वा तां हरिवाहिनीम्।
अश्मशस्त्रमहावृष्ट्या प्रापयाम यमक्षयम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Taking our stand in the airspace in battalions and battering the army of monkeys with a mighty hail of stones and missiles, we should send them to the abode of Death. (17)

verses.text:
एवं चेदुपसर्पेतामनयं रामलक्ष्मणौ।
अवश्यमपनीतेन जहतामेव जीवितम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “If Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa fall into our trap, they need must succumb to our wily stratagem. (18)

verses.text:
कौम्भकर्णिस्ततो वीरो निकुम्भो नाम वीर्यवान्।
अब्रवीत् परमक्रुद्धो रावणं लोकरावणम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Extremely enraged, the heroic and powerful son of Kumbhakarṇa, Nikumbha by name, thereupon submitted as follows to Rāvaṇa, who made people cry by his oppression: (19)

verses.text:
सर्वे भवन्तस्तिष्ठन्तु महाराजेन संगताः।
अहमेको हनिष्यामि राघवं सहलक्ष्मणम्॥ २०॥
सुग्रीवं सहनूमन्तं सर्वांश्चैवात्र वानरान्।
ततो वज्रहनुर्नाम राक्षसः पर्वतोपमः॥ २१॥
क्रुद्धः परिलिहन् सृक्कां जिह्वया वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
स्वैरं कुर्वन्तु कार्याणि भवन्तो विगतज्वराः॥ २२॥
एकोऽहं भक्षयिष्यामि तां सर्वां हरिवाहिनीम्।
स्वस्थाः क्रीडन्तु निश्चिन्ताः पिबन्तु मधु वारुणीम्॥ २३॥
अहमेको वधिष्यामि सुग्रीवं सहलक्ष्मणम्।
साङ्गदं च हनूमन्तं सर्वांश्चैवात्र वानरान्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Let you all tarry here in the company of our mighty ruler. I shall presently kill single-handed, Rāma, a scion of Raghu, as well as Lakṣmaṇa, Sugrīva alongwith Hanumān and all the other monkeys too.” Then an ogre, Vajrahanu by name, who looked like a mountain, submitted as follows, licking his lips with his tongue in rage: “Completely rid of all anxiety, you discharge your duties without constraint. I shall devour single-handed the whole of that army of monkeys. Divert yourself confidently and drink wine, getting free from anxiety. Alone I shall kill Sugrīva with Lakṣmaṇa, and Hanumān with Aṅgada as well as all the monkeys this very moment.” (20—24)

verses.text:
ततो निकुम्भो रभसः सूर्यशत्रुर्महाबलः।
सुप्तघ्नो यज्ञकोपश्च महापार्श्वमहोदरौ॥ १॥
अग्निकेतुश्च दुर्धर्षो रश्मिकेतुश्च राक्षसः।
इन्द्रजिच्च महातेजा बलवान् रावणात्मजः॥ २॥
प्रहस्तोऽथ विरूपाक्षो वज्रदंष्ट्रो महाबलः।
धूम्राक्षश्चातिकायश्च दुर्मुखश्चैव राक्षसः॥ ३॥
परिघान् पट्टिशान् शूलान् प्रासान् शक्तिपरश्वधान्।
चापानि च सुबाणानि खड्गांश्च विपुलाम्बुभान्॥ ४॥
प्रगृह्य परमक्रुद्धाः समुत्पत्य च राक्षसाः।
अब्रुवन् रावणं सर्वे प्रदीप्ता इव तेजसा॥ ५॥
verses.m: Firmly grasping iron clubs, sharp-edged spears, pikes, darts, javelins and axes as also bows with excellent arrows as well as swords shining like a vast expanse of water, and jumping up, the ogres Nikumbha, Rabhasa, Sūryaśatru, who was endowed with extraordinary strength, Suptaghna and Yajñakopa, Mahāpārśwa and Mahodara, nay, Agniketu, who was difficult to overpower, and the ogre Raśmiketu, as also Indrajit, the lusty eldest son of Rāvaṇa, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, Prahasta and Virūpākṣa, Vajradaṁṣṭra, who was endowed with extraordinary might, and Dhūmrākṣa as also Atikāya as well as the ogre Durmukha, who were all extremely enraged, and were flaming as it were with glory, thereupon submitted to Rāvaṇa as follows: (1—5)

verses.text:
अद्य रामं वधिष्यामः सुग्रीवं च सलक्ष्मणम्।
कृपणं च हनूमन्तं लङ्का येन प्रधर्षिता॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Today we shall dispose of Rāma and Sugrīva with Lakṣmaṇa, as well as the wretched Hanumān, by whom Laṅkā was outraged.” (6)

verses.text:
तान् गृहीतायुधान् सर्वान् वारयित्वा विभीषणः।
अब्रवीत् प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं पुनः प्रत्युपवेश्य तान्॥ ७॥
verses.m: Restraining them all, who stood seizing hold of their weapons, and then pressing them to resume their seats, Vibhīṣaṇa (Rāvaṇa’s youngest half-brother) submitted as follows with joined palms: (7)

verses.text:
अप्युपायैस्त्रिभिस्तात योऽर्थः प्राप्तुं न शक्यते।
तस्य विक्रमकालांस्तान् युक्तानाहुर्मनीषिणः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “The wise declare the well-known occasions for exhibiting prowess appropriate to that end only which cannot be attained with all the other three expedients, viz., conciliation, gift and sowing seeds of dissension, O dear brother! (8)

verses.text:
प्रमत्तेष्वभियुक्तेषु दैवेन प्रहतेषु च।
विक्रमास्तात सिद्ध्यन्ति परीक्ष्य विधिना कृताः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Deeds of valour which are performed according to the prescribed method, after being duly tested, O dear brother, succeed only against those who are wanton, who have already been attacked by another enemy or who stand doomed by an adverse fate. (9)

verses.text:
अप्रमत्तं कथं तं तु विजिगीषुं बले स्थितम्।
जितरोषं दुराधर्षं तं धर्षयितुमिच्छथ॥ १०॥
verses.m: “How do you seek to overcome the celebrated Rāma, who is, on the contrary, watchful, is keen to conquer, is supported by divine power, has subdued anger and is difficult to overpower? (10)

verses.text:
समुद्रं लङ्घयित्वा तु घोरं नदनदीपतिम्।
गतिं हनूमतो लोके को विद्यात् तर्कयेत वा॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Who in the world can know or even conceive the speed of Hanumān, who for his part came over to Laṅkā, leaping across the sea, the formidable lord of rivers and streams? (11)

verses.text:
बलान्यपरिमेयानि वीर्याणि च निशाचराः।
परेषां सहसावज्ञा न कर्तव्या कथंचन॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Inestimable are the troops at the disposal of Rāma and so is his power, O rangers of the night! Underestimation should not be precipitately made in any case in respect of enemies. (12)

verses.text:
किं च राक्षसराजस्य रामेणापकृतं पुरा।
आजहार जनस्थानाद् यस्य भार्यां यशस्विनः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Moreover, what offence was given to the ruler of ogres by the illustrious Rāma, whose consort the former bore away from Janasthāna? (13)

verses.text:
खरो यद्यतिवृत्तस्तु स रामेण हतो रणे।
अवश्यं प्राणिनां प्राणा रक्षितव्या यथाबलम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “If it is urged in reply that Rāvaṇa abducted Rāma’s wife because Rāma had killed Khara, our half-brother, my rejoinder is that Khara was made short work of by Rāma in an encounter because the former had, for his part, gone beyond his limits, in that he had attacked Rāma in the latter’s own hermitage. Life needs must be protected by living beings according to their might. (14)

verses.text:
एतन्निमित्तं वैदेही भयं नः सुमहद् भवेत्।
आहृता सा परित्याज्या कलहार्थे कृते नु किम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “If Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, was borne away because of this grudge, she deserves to be yielded up inasmuch as she may prove to be a peril to us. What on earth will be gained if anything is done which has strife for its object? (15)

verses.text:
न तु क्षमं वीर्यवता तेन धर्मानुवर्तिना।
वैरं निरर्थकं कर्तुं दीयतामस्य मैथिली॥ १६॥
verses.m: “It is not at all desirable to make enmity without any purpose with that powerful prince, who follows the moral code. Sītā, a princess of Mithilā, may, therefore, be restored to him. (16)

verses.text:
यावन्न सगजां साश्वां बहुरत्नसमाकुलाम्।
पुरीं दारयते बाणैर्दीयतामस्य मैथिली॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Let Sītā, a princess of Mithilā, be made over to him before he tears asunder with his arrows Laṅkā, full of many precious stones, with its elephants and horses. (17)

verses.text:
यावत् सुघोरा महती दुर्धर्षा हरिवाहिनी।
नावस्कन्दति नो लङ्कां तावत् सीता प्रदीयताम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Let Sītā be given back to Rāma before the huge army of monkeys, which is most formidable and difficult to overpower, besieges Laṅkā. (18)

verses.text:
विनश्येद्धि पुरी लङ्का शूराः सर्वे च राक्षसाः।
रामस्य दयिता पत्नी न स्वयं यदि दीयते॥ १९॥
verses.m: “If the beloved consort of Rāma is not restored of your own accord, the city of Laṅkā as well as all the heroic ogres will surely perish. (19)

verses.text:
प्रसादये त्वां बन्धुत्वात् कुरुष्व वचनं मम।
हितं तथ्यं त्वहं ब्रूमि दीयतामस्य मैथिली॥ २०॥
verses.m: “I seek to propitiate you because of your being my relation; pray, follow my counsel. I suggest only that which is true and conducive to your good: let Sītā, a princess of Mithilā, be surrendered to Rāma. (20)

verses.text:
पुरा शरत्सूर्यमरीचिसंनिभान्
नवाग्रपुङ्खान् सुदृढान् नृपात्मजः।
सृजत्यमोघान् विशिखान् वधाय ते
प्रदीयतां दाशरथाय मैथिली॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Let Sītā, a princess of Mithilā, be restored to Rāma (son of Daśaratha) before the prince looses for your destruction most stiff and unfailing arrows, shining brightly like the rays of the autumnal sun and provided with new heads and shafts. (21)

verses.text:
त्यजाशु कोपं सुखधर्मनाशनं
भजस्व धर्मं रतिकीर्तिवर्धनम्।
प्रसीद जीवेम सपुत्रबान्धवाः
प्रदीयतां दाशरथाय मैथिली॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Pray, renounce at once anger, which destroys happiness and virtues. Pursue righteousness, which enhances joy and fame. Be pacified, so that we may survive with our sons and relations; and let Sītā, a princess of Mithilā, be restored to Rāma (son of Daśaratha).” (22)

verses.text:
विभीषणवचः श्रुत्वा रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः।
विसर्जयित्वा तान् सर्वान् प्रविवेश स्वकं गृहम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: Dismissing them all on hearing the submission of Vibhīṣaṇa, Rāvaṇa, the lord of ogres, retired to his own palace. (23)

verses.text:
ततः प्रत्युषसि प्राप्ते प्राप्तधर्मार्थनिश्चयः।
राक्षसाधिपतेर्वेश्म भीमकर्मा विभीषणः॥ १॥
शैलाग्रचयसंकाशं शैलशृङ्गमिवोन्नतम्।
सुविभक्तमहाकक्षं महाजनपरिग्रहम्॥ २॥
मतिमद्भिर्महामात्रैरनुरक्तैरधिष्ठितम्।
राक्षसैराप्तपर्याप्तैः सर्वतः परिरक्षितम्॥ ३॥
मत्तमातङ्गनिःश्वासैर्व्याकुलीकृतमारुतम्।
शङ्खघोषमहाघोषं तूर्यसम्बाधनादितम्॥ ४॥
प्रमदाजनसम्बाधं प्रजल्पितमहापथम्।
तप्तकाञ्चननिर्यूहं भूषणोत्तमभूषितम्॥ ५॥
गन्धर्वाणामिवावासमालयं मरुतामिव।
रत्नसंचयसम्बाधं भवनं भोगिनामिव॥ ६॥
तं महाभ्रमिवादित्यस्तेजोविस्तृतरश्मिवान्।
अग्रजस्यालयं वीरः प्रविवेश महाद्युतिः॥ ७॥
verses.m: After that, when the morning came, even as the sun with its rays diffused through their brilliance would penetrate into a huge cloud, the heroic Vibhīṣaṇa of valiant deeds, who was clothed with extraordinary splendour and who had ascertained the truth about righteousness and material gain, penetrated deep into the well-known palace of his eldest (half-) brother, the suzerain ruler of ogres, which looked like a mass of crags, was lofty like a mountain top and symmetrically divided into spacious apartments; which was inhabited by a gathering of learned men, superintended by wise and devoted ministers and guarded on all sides by trusted and competent ogres; whose air was rendered tempestuous by the breath of elephants in rut, which resounded with a loud noise made by the ogres, resembling the blast of conches and was rendered noisy by the blare of trumpets; which remained crowded with young women; whose broad passages were noisy (with the talk of passers-by) and which was provided with gates of refined gold; which was decked with the foremost of jewels and looked like an abode of Gandharvas (celestial musicians) or a mansion of gods; and which, abounding, as it did, in collections of precious stones, resembled a house of Nāgas. (1—7)

verses.text:
पुण्यान् पुण्याहघोषांश्च वेदविद्भिरुदाहृतान्।
शुश्राव सुमहातेजा भ्रातुर्विजयसंश्रितान्॥ ८॥
verses.m: There Vibhīṣaṇa (who was clothed with exceptional splendour) heard the holy sounds of prayers wishing a propitious day to the king and invoking the victory of his eldest half-brother, uttered by the knowers of Veda. (8)

verses.text:
पूजितान् दधिपात्रैश्च सर्पिभिः सुमनोऽक्षतैः।
मन्त्रवेदविदो विप्रान् ददर्श स महाबलः॥ ९॥
verses.m: Vibhīṣaṇa, who was endowed with extraordinary might, beheld Brāhmaṇas versed in Mantras (sacred texts) as well as in the Brāhmaṇas (the portion of the Vedas containing rules for the recitation of the Mantras at various sacrifices) and worshipped with ghee, flowers and unbroken grains of rice as well as with vessels full of curds. (9)

verses.text:
स पूज्यमानो रक्षोभिर्दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा।
आसनस्थं महाबाहुर्ववन्दे धनदानुजम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: While being glorified by ogres, the mighty-armed Vibhīṣaṇa saluted Rāvaṇa (a younger half-brother of Kubera, the bestower of riches), seated on a throne, and shining with native splendour. (10)

verses.text:
स राजदृष्टिसम्पन्नमासनं हेमभूषितम्।
जगाम समुदाचारं प्रयुज्याचारकोविदः॥ ११॥
verses.m: Going through the customary formalities, Vibhīṣaṇa, who was well-versed in the code of conduct, made for a seat decked with gold and blessed by a glance from the king. (11)

verses.text:
स रावणं महात्मानं विजने मन्त्रिसंनिधौ।
उवाच हितमत्यर्थं वचनं हेतुनिश्चितम्॥ १२॥
प्रसाद्य भ्रातरं ज्येष्ठं सान्त्वेनोपस्थितक्रमः।
देशकालार्थसंवादि दृष्टलोकपरावरः॥ १३॥
verses.m: Having sought the favour of his eldest (half-) brother by means of soothing words, Vibhīṣaṇa, who knew what is good and bad in the world and had observed the customary rites (in the form of salutations etc.), tendered to the eminent Rāvaṇa in the presence of the latter’s ministers in seclusion the following advice, which was exceedingly wholesome and based on logical grounds and was in consonance with place, time and purpose: (12-13)

verses.text:
यदाप्रभृति वैदेही सम्प्राप्तेह परंतप।
तदाप्रभृति दृश्यन्ते निमित्तान्यशुभानि नः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Ever since Sītā (a princess of the Videha territory) arrived here, evil portents are being observed by us. (14)

verses.text:
सस्फुलिङ्गः सधूमार्चिः सधूमकलुषोदयः।
मन्त्रसंधुक्षितोऽप्यग्निर्न सम्यगभिवर्धते॥ १५॥
verses.m: “The sacrificial fire emits sparks, its flames are enveloped in smoke, its manifestation (as a result of rubbing two pieces of wood against each other) is also obscure, accompanied as it is by smoke, and it does not flare up properly even when fed with oblations while uttering sacred formulas. (15)

verses.text:
अग्निष्टेष्वग्निशालासु तथा ब्रह्मस्थलीषु च।
सरीसृपाणि दृश्यन्ते हव्येषु च पिपीलिकाः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Reptiles are observed in kitchens and fire-sanctuaries and, likewise, in the places where the Vedas are taught, and ants are discovered in the substances to be offered as oblations into the sacrificial fire. (16)

verses.text:
गवां पयांसि स्कन्नानि विमदा वरकुञ्जराः।
दीनमश्वाः प्रहेषन्ते नवग्रासाभिनन्दिनः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “The milk of cows has dried up, ichor no longer flows from the temples of the best of elephants; while horses, though feeling satisfied with their fresh supply of fodder, neigh dolefully. (17)

verses.text:
खरोष्ट्राश्वतरा राजन् भिन्नरोमाः स्रवन्ति च।
न स्वभावेऽवतिष्ठन्ते विधानैरपि चिन्तिताः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Nay, donkeys, camels and mules, O king, shed tears, their hair standing on end. Even though treated with care according to medical directions, they do not return to normalcy. (18)

verses.text:
वायसाः संघशः क्रूरा व्याहरन्ति समन्ततः।
समवेताश्च दृश्यन्ते विमानाग्रेषु संघशः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Crows in flock utter harsh cries on all sides and are seen gathered in swarms on the tops of seven-storeyed buildings. (19)

verses.text:
गृध्राश्च परिलीयन्ते पुरीमुपरि पिण्डिताः।
उपपन्नाश्च संध्ये द्वे व्याहरन्त्यशिवं शिवाः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Nay, vultures collected in swarms hover over the city; while, arrived near the city, she-jackals howl ominously both morning and evening. (20)

verses.text:
क्रव्यादानां मृगाणां च पुरीद्वारेषु संघशः।
श्रूयन्ते विपुला घोषाः सविस्फूर्जितनिःस्वनाः॥ २१॥
verses.m: “At the gates of the city are heard the loud cries of carnivorous animals (such as wolves and hyenās) gathered in herds alongwith peals of thunder. (21)

verses.text:
तदेवं प्रस्तुते कार्ये प्रायश्चित्तमिदं क्षमम्।
रोचये वीर वैदेही राघवाय प्रदीयताम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Therefore, when the action of evil forces has started in this way, O gallant brother, this atonement is desirable that Sītā (a princess of the Videha territory) be restored to Rāma (a scion of Raghu) and I like it.(22)

verses.text:
इदं च यदि वा मोहाल्लोभाद् वा व्याहृतं मया।
तत्रापि च महाराज न दोषं कर्तुमर्हसि॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Even if this submission has been made through infatuation or greed, you ought not to find fault with me, O eminent monarch! (23)

verses.text:
अयं हि दोषः सर्वस्य जनस्यास्योपलक्ष्यते।
रक्षसां राक्षसीनां च पुरस्यान्तःपुरस्य च॥ २४॥
verses.m: “This offence in the shape of Sītā’s abduction is recognized by all the people here, the ogres and the ogresses, the whole city and the gynaeceum. (24)

verses.text:
प्रापणे चास्य मन्त्रस्य निवृत्ताः सर्वमन्त्रिणः।
अवश्यं च मया वाच्यं यद् दृष्टमथवा श्रुतम्।
सम्प्रधार्य यथान्यायं तद् भवान् कर्तुमर्हति॥ २५॥
verses.m: “True, all your counsellors have refrained from tendering this advice to you for fear of incurring your displeasure; yet that which has been perceived or heard by me needs must be submitted. Determining the propriety or otherwise of my counsel according to the principles of equity, you ought to act accordingly.” (25)

verses.text:
इति स्वमन्त्रिणां मध्ये भ्राता भ्रातरमूचिवान्।
रावणं रक्षसां श्रेष्ठं पथ्यमेतद् विभीषणः॥ २६॥
verses.m: Thus in the midst of his half-brother’s counsellors, Vibhīṣaṇa, brother of Rāvaṇa, tendered the aforesaid salutary advice to his (eldest half-) brother, Rāvaṇa, the foremost of ogres. (26)

verses.text:
हितं महार्थं मृदु हेतुसंहितं
व्यतीतकालायतिसम्प्रतिक्षमम्।
निशम्य तद्वाक्यमुपस्थितज्वरः
प्रसङ्गवानुत्तरमेतदब्रवीत् ॥ २७॥
verses.m: Hearing the foregoing submission of Vibhīṣaṇa, which was wholesome, full of great significance, gentle, logical and capable of doing good in the past, present and future, Rāvaṇa (who was seized with fever in the form of anger and) who was full of passion (for Sītā), made the following reply: (27)

verses.text:
भयं न पश्यामि कुतश्चिदप्यहं
न राघवः प्राप्स्यति जातु मैथिलीम्।
सुरैः सहेन्द्रैरपि संगरे कथं
ममाग्रतः स्थास्यति लक्ष्मणाग्रजः॥ २८॥
verses.m: “I see no cause for fear from any quarter whatsoever. Rāma (a scion of Raghu) shall in no case get back Sītā (a princess of Mithilā). How can Rāma (the eldest half-brother of Lakṣmaṇa) stand before me in an encounter even though aided by gods including Indra (their ruler)?” (28)

verses.text:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा सुरसैन्यनाशनो
महाबलः संयति चण्डविक्रमः।
दशाननो भ्रातरमाप्तवादिनं
विसर्जयामास तदा विभीषणम्॥ २९॥
verses.m: Having spoken as aforesaid, Rāvaṇa, the ten-headed monster, the destroyer of the celestial forces, who was endowed with extraordinary valour and exhibited terrific prowess in combat, forthwith dismissed his younger half-brother, Vibhīṣaṇa, who had elucidated the truth. (29)

verses.text:
स बभूव कृशो राजा मैथिलीकाममोहितः।
असन्मानाच्च सुहृदां पापः पापेन कर्मणा॥ १॥
verses.m: King Rāvaṇa, who was infatuated with passion for Sītā (a princess of Mithilā) and had begun to be looked upon as sinful because of his evil doing in the shape of Sītā’s abduction, grew emaciated through disrespect shown to him by his near and dear ones and his consuming passion for Sītā. (1)

verses.text:
अतीव कामसम्पन्नो वैदेहीमनुचिन्तयन्।
अतीतसमये काले तस्मिन् वै युधि रावणः।
अमात्यैश्च सुहृद्भिश्च प्राप्तकालममन्यत॥ २॥
verses.m: The time for holding consultation having elapsed, war being actually imminent, Rāvaṇa, who was exceedingly full of longing for Sītā and was constantly thinking of Sītā (a princess of the Videha territory), thought consultation with his ministers and well-wishers to be opportune. (2)

verses.text:
स हेमजालविततं मणिविद्रुमभूषितम्।
उपगम्य विनीताश्वमारुरोह महारथम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Approaching a huge chariot overlaid with a lattice-work of gold, decked with gems and corals and drawn by trained horses, he ascended it. (3)

verses.text:
तमास्थाय रथश्रेष्ठं महामेघसमस्वनम्।
प्रययौ रक्षसां श्रेष्ठो दशग्रीवः सभां प्रति॥ ४॥
verses.m: Taking his seat in that excellent chariot, which produced a rattling sound resembling the rumbling of a large cloud, Rāvaṇa, the ten-headed monster, the foremost of ogres, drove towards the assembly hall. (4)

verses.text:
असिचर्मधरा योधाः सर्वायुधधरास्ततः।
राक्षसा राक्षसेन्द्रस्य पुरस्तात् सम्प्रतस्थिरे॥ ५॥
verses.m: At that time ogre troops carrying swords and bucklers and all kinds of weapons marched in order at the head of the ruler of ogres. (5)

verses.text:
नानाविकृतवेषाश्च नानाभूषणभूषिताः।
पार्श्वतः पृष्ठतश्चैनं परिवार्य ययुस्तदा॥ ६॥
verses.m: Nay, ogres attired in various strange robes and adorned with all kinds of jewels, marched giving cover to him at his sides as well as at his back at that time. (6)

verses.text:
रथैश्चातिरथाः शीघ्रं मत्तैश्च वरवारणैः।
अनूत्पेतुर्दशग्रीवमाक्रीडद्भिश्च वाजिभिः॥ ७॥
verses.m: Car-warriors of a superior order* also rushed apace in the wake of Rāvaṇa (the ten-headed monster) in chariots as well as on excellent elephants in rut as also on (the back of) horses sportively following in different gaits. (7)

verses.text:
गदापरिघहस्ताश्च शक्तितोमरपाणयः।
परश्वधधराश्चान्ये तथान्ये शूलपाणयः।
ततस्तूर्यसहस्राणां संजज्ञे निःस्वनो महान्॥ ८॥
verses.m: Some had maces and iron bars in their hands, while others followed with javelins and iron clubs. Nay, still others carried axes, while some had darts in their hands. Then broke forth a loud blare of thousands of trumpets. (8)

verses.text:
तुमुलः शङ्खशब्दश्च सभां गच्छति रावणे।
स नेमिघोषेण महान् सहसाभिनिनादयन्॥ ९॥
राजमार्गं श्रिया जुष्टं प्रतिपेदे महारथः।
विमलं चातपत्रं च प्रगृहीतमशोभत॥ १०॥
पाण्डुरं राक्षसेन्द्रस्य पूर्णस्ताराधिपो यथा।
हेममञ्जरिगर्भे च शुद्धस्फटिकविग्रहे॥ ११॥
चामरव्यजने तस्य रेजतुः सव्यदक्षिणे।
ते कृताञ्जलयः सर्वे रथस्थं पृथिवीस्थिताः॥ १२॥
राक्षसा राक्षसश्रेष्ठं शिरोभिस्तं ववन्दिरे।
राक्षसैः स्तूयमानः सञ्जयाशीर्भिररिंदमः॥ १३॥
आससाद महातेजाः सभां विरचितां तदा।
सुवर्णरजतास्तीर्णां विशुद्धस्फटिकान्तराम्॥ १४॥
विराजमानो वपुषा रुक्मपट्टोत्तरच्छदाम्।
तां पिशाचशतैः षड्भिरभिगुप्तां सदाप्रभाम्॥ १५॥
प्रविवेश महातेजाः सुकृतां विश्वकर्मणा।
तस्यां तु वैदूर्यमयं प्रियकाजिनसंवृतम्॥ १६॥
महत्सोपाश्रयं भेजे रावणः परमासनम्।
ततः शशासेश्वरवद्दूताँल्लघुपराक्रमान्॥ १७॥
verses.m: As Rāvaṇa drove to the assembly hall, a tumultuous blast of conches also followed. * An Atiratha has been defined thus: That eminent and great car-warrior presently reached the splendid highway, causing it to echo with the rattling of the felloes of his chariot. Nay, held over the head of Rāvaṇa (the ruler of ogres), a spotless white canopy shone like the full moon (lit., the suzerain lord of stars). On his left and right shone a pair of whisks with handles of pure crystal and having bunches of golden threads in the middle. Standing on the ground (on the way) with joined palms, all the aforesaid ogres saluted Rāvaṇa, the foremost of ogres, with their heads bent low. Being hailed by ogres by means of shouts of victory and benedictions, Rāvaṇa (the scourge of his foes), who was endowed with extraordinary energy, presently reached the assembly hall constructed by Viśwakarmā (the architect of gods). With his body shining brightly, Rāvaṇa, who was endowed with extraordinary splendour, made his solemn entry into that assembly hall, which was paved with gold and silver, whose interior was wrought in pure crystal, whose floor was carpeted with silk, interwoven with threads of gold, and which was guarded on all sides by six hundred fiends, was full of perennial splendour and had been beautifully constructed by Viśwakarmā. Rāvaṇa for his part occupied in that hall a big and excellent throne made of cat’s-eye, nay, covered with the skin of Priyakas (a species of deer) and provided with cushions, and forthwith authoritatively commanded fleet-footed messengers as follows: (9—17)

verses.text:
समानयत मे क्षिप्रमिहैतान् राक्षसानिति।
कृत्यमस्ति महज्जाने कर्तव्यमिति शत्रुभिः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Duly bring hither with all speed the well-known ogres to my presence. I know that momentous action has to be taken with regard to the enemies.” (18)

verses.text:
राक्षसास्तद्वचः श्रुत्वा लङ्कायां परिचक्रमुः।
अनुगेहमवस्थाय विहारशयनेषु च।
उद्यानेषु च रक्षांसि चोदयन्तो ह्यभीतवत्॥ १९॥
verses.m: Hearing his command, the ogres coursed through Laṅkā, making their way into every single house, nay, penetrating into places of recreation and bedrooms as well as into gardens, and actually calling upon the ogres in an undaunted way to proceed to the assembly hall. (19)

verses.text:
ते रथान्तचरा एके दृप्तानेके दृढान् हयान्।
नागानेकेऽधिरुरुहुर्जग्मुश्चैके पदातयः॥ २०॥
verses.m: Some of the invited ogres sallied forth in the foremost of chariots, others rode on proud elephants, still others on sturdy horses, while yet others proceeded on foot. (20)

verses.text:
सा पुरी परमाकीर्णा रथकुञ्जरवाजिभिः।
सम्पतद्भिर्विरुरुचे गरुत्मद्भिरिवाम्बरम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: Fully crowded with chariots, elephants and horses running in a line, that city looked very charming like the sky crowded with birds flying in a row. (21)

verses.text:
ते वाहनान्यवस्थाय यानानि विविधानि च।
सभां पद्भिः प्रविविशुः सिंहा गिरिगुहामिव॥ २२॥
verses.m: Leaving their mounts as well as conveyances of every description outside, they made their way into the assembly hall on foot as lions would enter a rocky cave. (22)

verses.text:
राज्ञः पादौ गृहीत्वा तु राज्ञा ते प्रतिपूजिताः।
पीठेष्वन्ये बृसीष्वन्ये भूमौ केचिदुपाविशन्॥ २३॥
verses.m: Touching the king’s feet (as an act of submission) and greeted in their turn by the king, they, for their part, took their seat, some on seats of gold, others on mats of Kuśa grass and still others on the carpeted ground. (23)

verses.text:
ते समेत्य सभायां वै राक्षसा राजशासनात्।
यथार्हमुपतस्थुस्ते रावणं राक्षसाधिपम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: Gathering in the assembly hall at the king’s command, the aforesaid ogres actually took their position round Rāvaṇa, their suzerain lord, each according to his rank. (24)

verses.text:
मन्त्रिणश्च यथामुख्या निश्चितार्थेषु पण्डिताः।
अमात्याश्च गुणोपेताः सर्वज्ञा बुद्धिदर्शनाः॥ २५॥
समीयुस्तत्र शतशः शूराश्च बहवस्तथा।
सभायां हेमवर्णायां सर्वार्थस्य सुखाय वै॥ २६॥
verses.m: Counsellors foremost in their own sphere and clever in deciding affairs and qualified ministers, well-versed in all subjects and capable of viewing things with their understanding and likewise numerous warriors too actually gathered in hundreds in that assembly hall sparkling with gold for discussing all matters for a happy conclusion. (25-26)

verses.text:
ततो महात्मा विपुलं सुयुग्यं
रथं वरं हेमविचित्रिताङ्गम्।
शुभं समास्थाय ययौ यशस्वी
विभीषणः संसदमग्रजस्य॥ २७॥
verses.m: Then arrived the high-souled and illustrious Vibhīṣaṇa in the assembly presided over by his eldest (half-) brother, Rāvaṇa, mounting a huge, bright and excellent chariot drawn by peerless horses, its various parts decked with gold. (27)

verses.text:
स पूर्वजायावरजः शशंस
नामाथ पश्चाच्चरणौ ववन्दे।
शुकः प्रहस्तश्च तथैव तेभ्यो
ददौ यथार्हं पृथगासनानि॥ २८॥
verses.m: Younger as he was, he mentioned his name by way of courtesy to his eldest (half-) brother and then bowed at the latter’s feet. Śuka and Prahasta too did just the same. Rāvaṇa, for his part, offered them separate seats according to their respective rank. (28)

verses.text:
सुवर्णनानामणिभूषणानां
सुवाससां संसदि राक्षसानाम्।
तेषां परार्घ्यागुरुचन्दनानां
स्रजां च गन्धाः प्रववुः समन्तात्॥ २९॥
verses.m: The fragrance of most excellent aloe and sandal-paste painted on the persons, and garlands worn round the necks of those ogres adorned with ornaments of gold as well as of various gems and attired in excellent robes, spread all round. (29)

verses.text:
न चुक्रुशुर्नानृतमाह कश्चित्
सभासदो नापि जजल्पुरुच्चैः।
संसिद्धार्थाः सर्व एवोग्रवीर्या
भर्तुः सर्वे ददृशुश्चाननं ते॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Those present in the assembly did not make noise nor did they talk loudly nor (again) did any of them tell a lie. They were all fully accomplished of purpose and endowed with terrible prowess and all gazed on the face of their ruler. (30)

verses.text:
स रावणः शस्त्रभृतां मनस्विनां
महाबलानां समितौ मनस्वी।
तस्यां सभायां प्रभया चकाशे
मध्ये वसूनामिव वज्रहस्तः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: In the gathering of armed heroes, who were endowed with extraordinary might, in that assembly hall, the aforesaid heroic Rāvaṇa shone with his lustre like Indra, who holds the thunderbolt in his hand, in the midst of the Vasus (a class of gods). (31)

verses.text:
स तां परिषदं कृत्स्नां समीक्ष्य समितिंजयः।
प्रचोदयामास तदा प्रहस्तं वाहिनीपतिम्॥ १॥
verses.m: Surveying the entire assembly mentioned above, Rāvaṇa, who came out victorious in battle, presently ordered Prahasta, the Commander-in-Chief of his forces as follows: (1)

verses.text:
सेनापते यथा ते स्युः कृतविद्याश्चतुर्विधाः।
योधा नगररक्षायां तथा व्यादेष्टुमर्हसि॥ २॥
verses.m: “You ought to issue special order, O generalissimo, to see that troops belonging to the four divisions of the army (viz., cavalry, infantry, chariots and elephants), who are trained warriors, are entrusted with the defence of the city.” (2)

verses.text:
स प्रहस्तः प्रणीतात्मा चिकीर्षन् राजशासनम्।
विनिक्षिपद् बलं सर्वं बहिरन्तश्च मन्दिरे॥ ३॥
verses.m: Keen to carry out the royal command, the celebrated Prahasta, who had disciplined his mind, posted the entire army outside as well as inside the city. (3)

verses.text:
ततो विनिक्षिप्य बलं सर्वं नगरगुप्तये।
प्रहस्तः प्रमुखे राज्ञो निषसाद जगाद च॥ ४॥
verses.m: Having told off the entire army for the defence of the city, Prahasta presently resumed his seat in front of the king and submitted as follows: (4)

verses.text:
विहितं बहिरन्तश्च बलं बलवतस्तव।
कुरुष्वाविमनाः क्षिप्रं यदभिप्रेतमस्ति ते॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Your army, powerful as you are, has been stationed outside as well as inside the city. Therefore, accomplish at once with an undistracted mind what is intended by you.” (5)

verses.text:
प्रहस्तस्य वचः श्रुत्वा राजा राज्यहितैषिणः।
सुखेप्सुः सुहृदां मध्ये व्याजहार स रावणः॥ ६॥
verses.m: Hearing the submission of Prahasta, a well-wisher of the State, the celebrated Rāvaṇa, who aspired for happiness, spoke as follows in the midst of his near and dear ones: (6)

verses.text:
प्रियाप्रिये सुखे दुःखे लाभालाभे हिताहिते।
धर्मकामार्थकृच्छ्रेषु यूयमर्हथ वेदितुम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “You ought to know your duty in the face of that which is agreeable and that which is not, as also in the midst of happiness and misery, gain and loss, what is wholesome and otherwise and when virtue, pleasure and self-interest are at stake. (7)

verses.text:
सर्वकृत्यानि युष्माभिः समारब्धानि सर्वदा।
मन्त्रकर्मनियुक्तानि न जातु विफलानि मे॥ ८॥
verses.m: “My undertakings of all kinds, duly set afoot by you, have never proved futile, planned as they have always been according to deliberations. (8)

verses.text:
ससोमग्रहनक्षत्रैर्मरुद्भिरिव वासवः।
भवद्भिरहमत्यर्थं वृतः श्रियमवाप्नुयाम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Accompanied by you even as Indra is by deities presiding over the planets and lunar mansions including the moon-god as well as the forty-nine wind-gods, I wish to enjoy royal fortune excessively. (9)

verses.text:
अहं तु खलु सर्वान् वः समर्थयितुमुद्यतः।
कुम्भकर्णस्य तु स्वप्नान्नेममर्थमचोदयम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: “I was, on my part, actually ready to apprise you all of what I have done; but due to Kumbhakarṇa’s slumber I did not broach the matter. (10)

verses.text:
अयं हि सुप्तः षण्मासान् कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः।
सर्वशस्त्रभृतां मुख्यः स इदानीं समुत्थितः॥ ११॥
verses.m: “The said Kumbhakarṇa, the foremost of all those who bear arms, who is endowed with extraordinary might, remained actually asleep for six long months. He is now fully awake. (11)

verses.text:
इयं च दण्डकारण्याद् रामस्य महिषी प्रिया।
रक्षोभिश्चरितोद्देशादानीता जनकात्मजा॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Moreover, Sītā (Janaka’s daughter), the beloved consort of Rāma, has been borne away by me from the Daṇḍaka forest, a region frequented by ogres. (12)

verses.text:
सा मे न शय्यामारोढुमिच्छत्यलसगामिनी।
त्रिषु लोकेषु चान्या मे न सीतासदृशी तथा॥ १३॥
verses.m: “That lady of languid pace does not, however, feel inclined to lay her foot on my bed; and no other woman in the three worlds is charming in my eyes as Sītā. (13)

verses.text:
तनुमध्या पृथुश्रोणी शरदिन्दुनिभानना।
हेमबिम्बनिभा सौम्या मायेव मयनिर्मिता॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Slender-waisted with well developed hips and a countenance resembling the autumnal full moon, the gentle lady looks like an image of gold. It appears as though she were an enchantment conjured by the demon Maya, a past master in conjuring tricks. (14)

verses.text:
सुलोहिततलौ श्लक्ष्णौ चरणौ सुप्रतिष्ठितौ।
दृष्ट्वा ताम्रनखौ तस्या दीप्यते मे शरीरजः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “On seeing her feet, soft and well set, with deep red soles and coppery nails, love is kindled in my heart. (15)

verses.text:
हुताग्नेरर्चिसंकाशामेनां सौरीमिव प्रभाम्।
उन्नसं विमलं वल्गु वदनं चारुलोचनम्॥ १६॥
पश्यंस्तदवशस्तस्याः कामस्य वशमेयिवान्।
क्रोधहर्षसमानेन दुर्वर्णकरणेन च॥ १७॥
शोकसंतापनित्येन कामेन कलुषीकृतः।
सा तु संवत्सरं कालं मामयाचत भामिनी॥ १८॥
प्रतीक्षमाणा भर्तारं राममायतलोचना।
तन्मया चारुनेत्रायाः प्रतिज्ञातं वचः शुभम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Beholding her, who closely resembles the flame of a sacred fire fed with oblations and rivals the splendour of the sun, and gazing on her well-known fair and lovely countenance with a prominent nose and charming eyes, I am no longer master of myself and have become a slave of passion. Nay, I have been unnerved by love, which is uniform in anger and joy, makes one pale and is ever present even in grief and agony. Expecting, as she does, to meet in the meantime Rāma, her husband, that large-eyed lovely woman, however, asked of me a time-limit* of one year. That pleasing request of that lovely-eyed lady has been solemnly granted by me. (16—19)

verses.text:
श्रान्तोऽहं सततं कामाद् यातो हय इवाध्वनि।
कथं सागरमक्षोभ्यं तरिष्यन्ति वनौकसः॥ २०॥
बहुसत्त्वझषाकीर्णं तौ वा दशरथात्मजौ।
अथवा कपिनैकेन कृतं नः कदनं महत्॥ २१॥
दुर्ज्ञेयाः कार्यगतयो ब्रूत यस्य यथामति।
मानुषान्नो भयं नास्ति तथापि तु विमृश्यताम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Like a horse that has travelled over a long distance, I, however, constantly feel worn-out through love. Although Rāma is reported to be on his way to Laṅkā with an army of monkeys and bears, how will the monkeys (lit., denizens of the forest) or even Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, the two sons of Daśaratha, be able to cross the sea, which is unassailable and infested with numerous aquatic creatures, including large fish? The other side of the picture is that a great havoc was wrought on our side by a single monkey, Hanumān. The ways of accomplishing one’s purpose are thus difficult to ascertain. Therefore, speak what is there in whosoever’s mind according to the belief of each. There is no cause for apprehension to us from a human being; nevertheless let us ponder over the question, in any case. (20—22)

verses.text:
तदा देवासुरे युद्धे युष्माभिः सहितोऽजयम्।
ते मे भवन्तश्च तथा सुग्रीवप्रमुखान् हरीन्॥ २३॥
परे पारे समुद्रस्य पुरस्कृत्य नृपात्मजौ।
सीतायाः पदवीं प्राप्य सम्प्राप्तौ वरुणालयम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “The other day, assisted by you, I came out victorious in a conflict between the gods and the demons. You, who are the same, stand likewise by my side even today. Having discovered the whereabouts of Sītā, through Hanumān, after crossing the sea and placing ahead the monkeys led by Sugrīva (their chief), the two princes have duly arrived on the other side of the sea. (23-24)

verses.text:
अदेया च यथा सीता वध्यौ दशरथात्मजौ।
भवद्भिर्मन्त्र्यतां मन्त्रः सुनीतं चाभिधीयताम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Consultations should, therefore, be held by you and a judicious line of conduct suggested, so that Sītā may not have to be given back and Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, the two sons of Daśaratha, may be killed. (25)

verses.text:
नहि शक्तिं प्रपश्यामि जगत्यन्यस्य कस्यचित्।
सागरं वानरैस्तीर्त्वा निश्चयेन जयो मम॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Surely, I do not see the capacity of anyone in the world other than Rāma to cross the sea alongwith the monkeys. But even if he succeeds in doing so, victory is surely mine.” (26)

verses.text:
तस्य कामपरीतस्य निशम्य परिदेवितम्।
कुम्भकर्णः प्रचुक्रोध वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्॥ २७॥
verses.m: Hearing the wail of Rāvaṇa, who was overwhelmed with passion, Kumbhakarṇa flew into a rage and spoke the following words: (27)

verses.text:
यदा तु रामस्य सलक्ष्मणस्य
प्रसह्य सीता खलु सा इहाहृता।
सकृत् समीक्ष्यैव सुनिश्चितं तदा
भजेत चित्तं यमुनेव यामुनम्॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Even as the river Yamunā fills the depression near its source the moment it descends on earth, your mind ought to have sought careful deliberation with us that very moment when the aforesaid Sītā was actually borne away here by force (when she was alone in the cottage) after a single impulsive thought from the hermitage of Rāma; Rāma, who was accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa. (28)

verses.text:
सर्वमेतन्महाराज कृतमप्रतिमं तव।
विधीयेत सहास्माभिरादावेवास्य कर्मणः॥ २९॥
verses.m: “All this doing of yours, O great king, is unworthy of you. Deliberation ought to have been held with us at the very beginning of this act. (29)

verses.text:
न्यायेन राजकार्याणि यः करोति दशानन।
न स संतप्यते पश्चान्निश्चितार्थमतिर्नृपः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “A monarch who discharges his kingly duties with justice, his mind having determined his purpose in consultation with his counsellors, does not have to repent O Rāvaṇa! (30)

verses.text:
अनुपायेन कर्माणि विपरीतानि यानि च।
क्रियमाणानि दुष्यन्ति हवींष्यप्रयतेष्विव॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Actions which are undertaken without recourse to fair means and run counter to the principles of righteousness beget sin even as oblations used in impure sacrifices undertaken for malevolent purposes. (31)

verses.text:
यः पश्चात् पूर्वकार्याणि कर्माण्यभिचिकीर्षति।
पूर्वं चापरकार्याणि स न वेद नयानयौ॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “He who seeks to perform at a later date duties requiring to be performed earlier and those which ought to be performed later, performs at an early date, does not know right and wrong. (32)

verses.text:
चपलस्य तु कृत्येषु प्रसमीक्ष्याधिकं बलम्।
छिद्रमन्ये प्रपद्यन्ते क्रौञ्चस्य खमिव द्विजाः॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “Observing the superior strength of an enemy who is hasty in actions, others for their part look for his weak point even as swans seek the fissure* in the Krauñca mountain in order to cross it. (33)

verses.text:
त्वयेदं महदारब्धं कार्यमप्रतिचिन्तितम्।
दिष्ट्या त्वां नावधीद् रामो विषमिश्रमिवामिषम्॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “This great undertaking, which was not duly considered, has been set on foot by you. By your good luck Rāma did not kill you, even as food mixed with poison would kill the consumer. (34)

verses.text:
तस्मात् त्वया समारब्धं कर्म ह्यप्रतिमं परैः।
अहं समीकरिष्यामि हत्वा शत्रूंस्तवानघ॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “Therefore, making short work of your enemies, O brother, who are free from sorrow, I shall actually neutralize the unworthy action that has been started by you in relation to your enemies. (35)

verses.text:
अहमुत्सादयिष्यामि शत्रूंस्तव निशाचर।
यदि शक्रविवस्वन्तौ यदि पावकमारुतौ।
तावहं योधयिष्यामि कुबेरवरुणावपि॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “I shall exterminate all your foes, O ranger of the night! I shall encounter the two brothers in combat even if they happen to be Indra and the sun-god or the god of fire and the wind-god or Kubera (the god of riches and the deity presiding over the northern quarter) and Varuṇa (the god of water and the deity presiding over the western quarter). (36)

verses.text:
गिरिमात्रशरीरस्य महापरिघयोधिनः।
नर्दतस्तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रस्य बिभीयाद् वै पुरंदरः॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “Even Indra (the destroyer of strongholds) would be afraid of me as I, with my body having the size of a mountain and sharp teeth, roar while fighting with a huge iron bludgeon. (37)

verses.text:
पुनर्मां स द्वितीयेन शरेण निहनिष्यति।
ततोऽहं तस्य पास्यामि रुधिरं काममाश्वस॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “Before Rāma strikes me violently once more with a second arrow I shall drink his blood. Therefore, be fully restored to confidence. (38)

verses.text:
वधेन वै दाशरथेः सुखावहं
जयं तवाहर्तुमहं यतिष्ये।
हत्वा च रामं सह लक्ष्मणेन
खादामि सर्वान् हरियूथमुख्यान्॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “By making short work of Rāma (son of Daśaratha) I shall try my best to bring victory which will conduce to your happiness. Nay, having killed Rāma alongwith Lakṣmaṇa, I shall devour all the leaders of monkey hordes. (39)

verses.text:
रमस्व कामं पिब चाग्र्यवारुणीं
कुरुष्व कार्याणि हितानि विज्वरः।
मया तु रामे गमिते यमक्षयं
चिराय सीता वशगा भविष्यति॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “Enjoy life fully, drink the most excellent wine and, rid of anxiety, perform actions which are conducive to your welfare. When Rāma for his part has been dispatched to the abode of Death by me, Sītā will submit to your will for long.” (40)

verses.text:
रावणं क्रुद्धमाज्ञाय महापार्श्वो महाबलः।
मुहूर्तमनुसंचिन्त्य प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Reflecting awhile on finding Rāvaṇa enraged, Mahāpārśwa, who was endowed with extraordinary might, submitted with joined palms as follows: (1)

verses.text:
यः खल्वपि वनं प्राप्य मृगव्यालनिषेवितम्।
न पिबेन्मधु सम्प्राप्य स नरो बालिशो भवेत्॥ २॥
verses.m: “That man is a fool, who, even after reaching a forest infested by wild beasts of prey and reptiles and having duly found honey does not drink it. (2)

verses.text:
ईश्वरस्येश्वरः कोऽस्ति तव शत्रुनिर्बहण।
रमस्व सह वैदेह्या शत्रूनाक्रम्य मूर्धसु॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Who can lord it over you, a sovereign, O destroyer of foes? Setting your foot on the heads of your enemies, revel with Sītā (a princess of the Videha territory). (3)

verses.text:
बलात् कुक्कुटवृत्तेन प्रवर्तस्व महाबल।
आक्रम्याक्रम्य सीतां वै तां भुङ्क्ष्व च रमस्व च॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Act in the manner of a cock, using force against her, O ruler endowed with extraordinary might! Assaulting Sītā again and again, enjoy her and revel with her. (4)

verses.text:
लब्धकामस्य ते पश्चादागमिष्यति किं भयम्।
प्राप्तमप्राप्तकालं वा सर्वं प्रतिविधास्यसे॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Once you have attained your desired end, what peril will come upon you afterwards? And you will surely be able to meet every risk, no matter whether it is already present or is yet to come. (5)

verses.text:
कुम्भकर्णः सहास्माभिरिन्द्रजिच्च महाबलः।
प्रतिषेधयितुं शक्तौ सवज्रमपि वज्रिणम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “In conjunction with us Kumbhakarṇa and Indrajit, who are endowed with extraordinary might, are capable of keeping back even Indra, armed with his thunderbolt. (6)

verses.text:
उपप्रदानं सान्त्वं वा भेदं वा कुशलैः कृतम्।
समतिक्रम्य दण्डेन सिद्धिमर्थेषु रोचये॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Leaving aside gift, conciliation or even the policy of sowing dissension in the enemy’s ranks, resorted to by the wise, I prefer to achieve success in our concerns by use of force. (7)

verses.text:
इह प्राप्तान् वयं सर्वाञ्छत्रूंस्तव महाबल।
वशे शस्त्रप्रतापेन करिष्यामो न संशयः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “We shall reduce to submission by the strength of our arms all your enemies arrived here, O ruler endowed with extraordinary might! There is no doubt about it.” (8)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तदा राजा महापार्श्वेन रावणः।
तस्य सम्पूजयन् वाक्यमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ ९॥
verses.m: Acclaiming his counsel when exhorted in the foregoing words by Mahāpārśwa on that occasion, King Rāvaṇa made the following reply: (9)

verses.text:
महापार्श्व निबोध त्वं रहस्यं किंचिदात्मनः।
चिरवृत्तं तदाख्यास्ये यदवाप्तं पुरा मया॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Hear you, O Mahāpārśwa, of a certain secret of mine, of an incident which took place long ago, of a fruit which was gathered by me in the past. I shall presently confide it to you. (10)

verses.text:
पितामहस्य भवनं गच्छन्तीं पुञ्जिकस्थलाम्।
चञ्चूर्यमाणामद्राक्षमाकाशेऽग्निशिखामिव ॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Once I beheld a celestial nymph, Puñjikasthalā by name, flashing like a flame and sneaking away for fear of me through the heavens to the abode of Brahmā (the grandfather of the entire creation, which was evolved by his mind-born sons, Marīci and others). (11)

verses.text:
सा प्रसह्य मया भुक्ता कृता विवसना ततः।
स्वयम्भूभवनं प्राप्ता लोलिता नलिनी यथा॥ १२॥
verses.m: “She was stripped of her garment and ravished by me. She then reached the abode of Brahmā, the self-born creator, like a lotus plant violently shaken by an elephant. (12)

verses.text:
तच्च तस्य तथा मन्ये ज्ञातमासीन्महात्मनः।
अथ संकुपितो वेधा मामिदं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “The aforesaid incident, I presume, came to be known precisely as it had occurred to that exalted soul. Highly enraged, the creator forthwith addressed the following words to me: (13)

verses.text:
अद्यप्रभृति यामन्यां बलान्नारीं गमिष्यसि।
तदा ते शतधा मूर्धा फलिष्यति न संशयः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “ ‘If you happen to violate any other woman henceforward, your head will be forthwith split into a hundred pieces; there is no doubt about it’. (14)

verses.text:
इत्यहं तस्य शापस्य भीतः प्रसभमेव ताम्।
नारोहये बलात् सीतां वैदेहीं शयने शुभे॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Hence, afraid, as I am, of his curse, I do not violently put Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, on my charming bed by force. (15)

verses.text:
सागरस्येव मे वेगो मारुतस्येव मे गतिः।
नैतद् दाशरथिर्वेद ह्यासादयति तेन माम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “My fury resembles that of the sea, and my speed resembles the speed of the wind. Surely Rāma (son of Daśaratha) does not know of it, hence he is attacking me. (16)

verses.text:
को हि सिंहमिवासीनं सुप्तं गिरिगुहाशये।
क्रुद्धं मृत्युमिवासीनं प्रबोधयितुमिच्छति॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Otherwise, who will actually seek to arouse me to martial activity as one would awaken a lion asleep in a sitting posture in its abode in the shape of a mountain cavern or arouse into activity Death sitting in rage? (17)

verses.text:
न मत्तो निर्गतान् बाणान् द्विजिह्वान् पन्नगानिव।
रामः पश्यति संग्रामे तेन मामभिगच्छति॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Rāma has not seen arrows like serpents with forked tongues shot in a combat from my bow. Hence he is marching against me. (18)

verses.text:
क्षिप्रं वज्रसमैर्बाणैः शतधा कार्मुकच्युतैः।
राममादीपयिष्यामि उल्काभिरिव कुञ्जरम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: “I shall consume Rāma in no time with my arrows shot in hundreds like the thunderbolt from my bow even as one would torment an elephant with firebrands. (19)

verses.text:
तच्चास्य बलमादास्ये बलेन महता वृतः।
उदितः सविता काले नक्षत्राणां प्रभामिव॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Nay, surrounded by a huge army, I shall split up his army even as, risen in the morning, the sun disperses the light of the stars. (20)

verses.text:
न वासवेनापि सहस्रचक्षुषा
युधास्मि शक्यो वरुणेन वा पुनः।
मया त्वियं बाहुबलेन निर्जिता
पुरा पुरी वैश्रवणेन पालिता॥ २१॥
verses.m: “I am not capable of being conquered in an encounter even by the thousand-eyed Indra, the ruler of gods, nor, again, by Varuṇa, the god of water. Again, this city of Laṅkā, which was formerly ruled by Kubera (son of Sage Viśravā), was won by me on the strength of my arms.” (21)

verses.text:
निशाचरेन्द्रस्य निशम्य वाक्यं
स कुम्भकर्णस्य च गर्जितानि।
विभीषणो राक्षसराजमुख्य-
मुवाच वाक्यं हितमर्थयुक्तम्॥ १॥
verses.m: Having listened to the braggadocio of Rāvaṇa, the ruler of ogres, and the thundering of Kumbhakarṇa, Vibhīṣaṇa made the following salutary and significant submission to Rāvaṇa, the foremost of the rulers of ogres: (1)

verses.text:
वृतो हि बाह्वन्तरभोगराशि-
श्चिन्ताविषः सुस्मिततीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रः।
पञ्चाङ्गुलीपञ्चशिरोऽतिकायः
सीतामहाहिस्तव केन राजन्॥ २॥
verses.m: “By whom, O king, has the huge serpent of gigantic proportions in the form of Sītā—her bosom for its coils, her remaining plunged in thought for its poison, her sweet smiles for its sharp fangs, her five fingers for its five hoods—been tied to your neck? (2)

verses.text:
यावन्न लङ्कां समभिद्रवन्ति
बलीमुखाः पर्वतकूटमात्राः।
दंष्ट्रायुधाश्चैव नखायुधाश्च
प्रदीयतां दाशरथाय मैथिली॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Let Sītā, a princess of Mithilā, be given back to Rāma (son of Daśaratha) while the monkeys, who are tall as mountain-tops and have teeth and claws for their weapons, have not yet invaded Laṅkā. (3)

verses.text:
यावन्न गृह्णन्ति शिरांसि बाणा
रामेरिता राक्षसपुंगवानाम्।
वज्रोपमा वायुसमानवेगाः
प्रदीयतां दाशरथाय मैथिली॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Let Sītā, a princess of Mithilā, be restored to Rāma (son of Daśaratha) till the arrows propelled by Rāma, which resemble the thunderbolt in their fury and are swift as the wind, do not catch the heads of the foremost among the ogres. (4)

verses.text:
न कुम्भकर्णेन्द्रजितौ च राजं-
स्तथा महापार्श्वमहोदरौ वा।
निकुम्भकुम्भौ च तथातिकायः
स्थातुं समर्था युधि राघवस्य॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Nay, neither Kumbhakarṇa and Indrajit nor even Mahāpārśwa and Mahodara nor Nikumbha and Kumbha, nor even Atikāya are capable of withstanding Rāma (a scion of Raghu) in combat, O king! (5)

verses.text:
जीवंस्तु रामस्य न मोक्ष्यसे त्वं
गुप्तः सवित्राप्यथवा मरुद्भिः।
न वासवस्याङ्कगतो न मृत्यो-
र्नभो न पातालमनुप्रविष्टः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “You shall not be spared by the arrows of Śrī Rāma even though protected by the sun-god or the wind-gods nor if seated in the lap of Indra or Death nor if you have penetrated into the heavens or Pātāla, the nethermost subterranean region.” (6)

verses.text:
निशम्य वाक्यं तु विभीषणस्य
ततः प्रहस्तो वचनं बभाषे।
न नो भयं विद्म न दैवतेभ्यो
न दानवेभ्योऽप्यथवा कदाचित्॥ ७॥
verses.m: Hearing the submission of Vibhīṣaṇa, Prahasta for his part forthwith observed as follows: “We do not know if there is ever any cause for fear to us from gods or even from demons. (7)

verses.text:
न यक्षगन्धर्वमहोरगेभ्यो
भयं न संख्ये पतगोरगेभ्यः।
कथं नु रामाद् भविता भयं नो
नरेन्द्रपुत्रात् समरे कदाचित्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Nor is there any fear to us on the field of battle from Yakṣas (a class of demigods), Gandharvas (celestial musicians) and eminent Nāgas (serpent-demons) nor even from birds and reptiles. How, then, can there be any fear to us at any time on the battlefield from Rāma, the son of a ruler of mortals?” (8)

verses.text:
प्रहस्तवाक्यं त्वहितं निशम्य
विभीषणो राजहितानुकाङ्क्षी।
ततो महार्थं वचनं बभाषे
धर्मार्थकामेषु निविष्टबुद्धिः॥ ९॥
verses.m: Hearing the noxious braggadocio of Prahasta, Vibhīṣaṇa for his part, who was a well-wisher of the king and whose mind penetrated into the domains of righteousness, material prosperity and sensuous enjoyment, immediately made the following speech, which was full of great significance: (9)

verses.text:
प्रहस्त राजा च महोदरश्च
त्वं कुम्भकर्णश्च यथार्थजातम्।
ब्रवीत रामं प्रति तन्न शक्यं
यथा गतिः स्वर्गमधर्मबुद्धेः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “The actions which the king as well as Mahodara as also yourself and Kumbhakarṇa propose to take against Rāma are not capable of being accomplished by you any more than the entry into heaven of one whose mind is set on unrighteousness, O Prahasta. (10)

verses.text:
वधस्तु रामस्य मया त्वया च
प्रहस्त सर्वैरपि राक्षसैर्वा।
कथं भवेदर्थविशारदस्य
महार्णवं तर्तुमिवाप्लवस्य॥ ११॥
verses.m: “How can the destruction of Rāma, who is adept in achieving his object, be compassed, O Prahasta, by yourself, myself or even by all the ogres taken together any more than it is possible for anyone to cross the ocean without a bark? (11)

verses.text:
धर्मप्रधानस्य महारथस्य
इक्ष्वाकुवंशप्रभवस्य राज्ञः।
पुरोऽस्य देवाश्च तथाविधस्य
कृत्येषु शक्तस्य भवन्ति मूढाः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Even gods would feel nonplussed when placed in front of the aforesaid king, Rāma, who gives the foremost place to piety, is a great chariot-warrior, has taken his descent in the race of Ikṣwāku, is a replica of the latter in valour and other virtues and is capable of accomplishing his objects. (12)

verses.text:
तीक्ष्णा न तावत् तव कङ्कपत्रा
दुरासदा राघवविप्रमुक्ताः।
भित्त्वा शरीरं प्रविशन्ति बाणाः
प्रहस्त तेनैव विकत्थसे त्वम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “The sharp arrows furiously discharged with vehemence by Rāma (a scion of Raghu), which are furnished with the feathers of a buzzard and are dangerous to approach, have not yet penetrated deep in your body after piercing it. That is why you indulge in boastful talk, O Prahasta! (13)

verses.text:
भित्त्वा न तावत् प्रविशन्ति कायं
प्राणान्तिकास्तेऽशनितुल्यवेगाः।
शिताः शरा राघवविप्रमुक्ताः
प्रहस्त तेनैव विकत्थसे त्वम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “The deadly and sharp arrows furiously discharged with vehemence by Rāma (a scion of Raghu), which are equal in velocity to the thunderbolt, have not yet made their way deep into your body. That is why you play the braggart, O Prahasta! (14)

verses.text:
न रावणो नातिबलस्त्रिशीर्षो
न कुम्भकर्णस्य सुतो निकुम्भः।
न चेन्द्रजिद् दाशरथिं प्रवोढुं
त्वं वा रणे शक्रसमं समर्थः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Neither Rāvaṇa nor Triśirā of exceeding might nor Nikumbha, son of Kumbhakarṇa, nor Indrajit nor even yourself shall be able to bear the onrush of Rāma (son of Daśaratha), who is equal to Indra in combat. (15)

verses.text:
देवान्तको वापि नरान्तको वा
तथातिकायोऽतिरथो महात्मा।
अकम्पनश्चाद्रिसमानसारः
स्थातुं न शक्ता युधि राघवस्य॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Neither Devāntaka nor even Narāntaka nor Atikāya nor Atiratha of gigantic proportions nor Akampana, who is mighty as a mountain, is able to stand before Rāma (a scion of Raghu) on the field of battle. (16)

verses.text:
अयं च राजा व्यसनाभिभूतो
मित्रैरमित्रप्रतिमैर्भवद्भिः।
अन्वास्यते राक्षसनाशनार्थे
तीक्ष्णः प्रकृत्या ह्यसमीक्षकारी॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Nay, this king, Rāvaṇa, who is overpowered by evil addictions*, is violent by nature and acts inconsiderately—is waited upon by friends in you, who are no better than foes, to the destruction of ogres. (17)

verses.text:
अनन्तभोगेन सहस्रमूर्ध्ना
नागेन भीमेन महाबलेन।
बलात् परिक्षिप्तमिमं भवन्तो
राजानमुत्क्षिप्य विमोचयन्तु॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Extricating this king entwined with violence by a formidable cobra of infinite strength and extraordinary energy and endowed with a thousand hoods, you make him completely free. (18)

verses.text:
यावद्धि केशग्रहणात् सुहृद्भिः
समेत्य सर्वैः परिपूर्णकामैः।
निगृह्य राजा परिरक्षितव्यो
भूतैर्यथा भीमबलैर्गृहीतः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “The king should be collectively protected all round by all his well-wishers, whose desires have been fully gratified by him, even by using force against him and catching him by the hair (if necessary), even as one, possessed by spirits of terrible might, is protected by one’s near and dear ones. (19)

verses.text:
सुवारिणा राघवसागरेण
प्रच्छाद्यमानस्तरसा भवद्भिः।
युक्तस्त्वयं तारयितुं समेत्य
काकुत्स्थपातालमुखे पतन् सः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Rāvaṇa, for his part, who is going to be engulfed by the sea in the shape of Rāma (a scion of Raghu)—which is full of excellent water (in the shape of high moral character), and who is about to fall into the mouth of Pātāla (the nethermost sub-terranean region) in the shape of Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha), is worthy of being unitedly rescued by you. (20)

verses.text:
इदं पुरस्यास्य सराक्षसस्य
राज्ञश्च पथ्यं ससुहृज्जनस्य।
सम्यग्धि वाक्यं स्वमतं ब्रवीमि
नरेन्द्रपुत्राय ददातु मैथिलीम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Indeed, I tender this advice, embodying my own opinion, which is highly conducive to the good of this city including the ogres, as well as of the king with his near and dear ones; let him give Sītā (a princess of Mithilā) back to Rāma (son of a ruler of men). (21)

verses.text:
परस्य वीर्यं स्वबलं च बुद्ध्वा
स्थानं क्षयं चैव तथैव वृद्धिम्।
तथा स्वपक्षेऽप्यनुमृश्य बुद्ध्या
वदेत् क्षमं स्वामिहितं स मन्त्री॥ २२॥
verses.m: “A counsellor is he who after ascertaining the relative strength of the enemy as well as his own master and, even so, duly considering with his acumen the status quo, set-back or rise of military power in the enemy’s ranks as well as on his own side tenders an advice which is proper as well as conducive to the interests of his master.” (22)

verses.text:
बृहस्पतेस्तुल्यमतेर्वचस्त-
न्निशम्य यत्नेन विभीषणस्य।
ततो महात्मा वचनं बभाषे
तत्रेन्द्रजिन्नैर्ऋतयूथमुख्यः ॥ १॥
verses.m: Listening with restraint the foregoing speech of Vibhīṣaṇa, who was equal in wisdom to Sage Bṛhaspati (the preceptor of gods), the high-spirited Indrajit, the leader of ogre hordes, forthwith spoke as follows on that occasion: (1)

verses.text:
किं नाम ते तात कनिष्ठ वाक्य-
मनर्थकं वै बहुभीतवच्च।
अस्मिन् कुले योऽपि भवेन्न जातः
सोऽपीदृशं नैव वदेन्न कुर्यात्॥ २॥
verses.m: “Why on earth should you actually utter meaningless words like one who is greatly alarmed, O youngest uncle? Even he who is not born in this race of Pulastya would not utter such words or do such a thing as is suggested by you. (2)

verses.text:
सत्त्वेन वीर्येण पराक्रमेण
धैर्येण शौर्येण च तेजसा च।
एकः कुलेऽस्मिन् पुरुषो विमुक्तो
विभीषणस्तात कनिष्ठ एषः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “This Vibhīṣaṇa, the youngest of my uncles including father, is the only individual in this race who is utterly devoid of courage, virility, prowess, fortitude, heroism and spirit. (3)

verses.text:
किं नाम तौ मानुषराजपुत्रा-
वस्माकमेकेन हि राक्षसेन।
सुप्राकृतेनापि निहन्तुमेतौ
शक्यौ कुतो भीषयसे स्म भीरो॥ ४॥
verses.m: “What are, in fact, those two sons of a king of men? Actually they are capable of being killed even by a single ogre, the most insignificant amongst us. Why then should you frighten us, O coward? (4)

verses.text:
त्रिलोकनाथो ननु देवराजः
शक्रो मया भूमितले निविष्टः।
भयार्पिताश्चापि दिशः प्रपन्नाः
सर्वे तदा देवगणाः समग्राः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Even the powerful Indra, the ruler of gods and the protector of all the three worlds, was cast by me to the ground. Nay, struck with terror, all the divine hordes too fled in all directions on that occasion. (5)

verses.text:
ऐरावतो निःस्वनमुन्नदन् स
निपातितो भूमितले मया तु।
विकृष्य दन्तौ तु मया प्रसह्य
वित्रासिता देवगणाः समग्राः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “After forcibly extracting his tusks with a crash, the celebrated Airāvata (the elephant of Indra) for his part, who was trumpeting all the time, was actually dashed to the ground by me and all the celestial hordes were thrown into panic by me. (6)

verses.text:
सोऽहं सुराणामपि दर्पहन्ता
दैत्योत्तमानामपि शोककर्ता।
कथं नरेन्द्रात्मजयोर्न शक्तो
मनुष्ययोः प्राकृतयोः सुवीर्यः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “How am I, who have crushed the pride even of gods and brought grief even to the foremost of Daityas, and am rich in manliness, not capable of subduing the two princes, insignificant mortals that they are?” (7)

verses.text:
अथेन्द्रकल्पस्य दुरासदस्य
महौजसस्तद् वचनं निशम्य।
ततो महार्थं वचनं बभाषे
विभीषणः शस्त्रभृतां वरिष्ठः॥ ८॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid braggadocio of Indrajit (a rival of Indra), who was dangerous to approach in combat and was endowed with extraordinary energy, Vibhīṣaṇa, the foremost of armed soldiers, forthwith made the following reply, which was full of great significance: (8)

verses.text:
न तात मन्त्रे तव निश्चयोऽस्ति
बालस्त्वमद्याप्यविपक्वबुद्धिः।
तस्मात् त्वयाप्यात्मविनाशनाय
वचोऽर्थहीनं बहु विप्रलप्तम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Being a mere boy whose intellect is not yet ripe, my child, you are not able to decide what should be done and what should not be done. Therefore, much incoherent talk has been poured forth by you leading to your own destruction. (9)

verses.text:
पुत्रप्रवादेन तु रावणस्य
त्वमिन्द्रजिन्मित्रमुखोऽसि शत्रुः।
यस्येदृशं राघवतो विनाशं
निशम्य मोहादनुमन्यसे त्वम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Though passing by the name of a son, O Indrajit, you are an enemy to Rāvaṇa under the cloak of a friend, in that even on hearing from me of his impending destruction at the hands of Rāma, a scion of Raghu, you are saying ditto to him through infatuation. (10)

verses.text:
त्वमेव वध्यश्च सुदुर्मतिश्च
स चापि वध्यो य इहानयत् त्वाम्।
बालं दृढं साहसिकं च योऽद्य
प्रावेशयन्मन्त्रकृतां समीपम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “You are certainly deserving of death and grossly evil-minded too. Nay, he too is deserving of death, who brought you here, who ushered you, an utterly reckless boy, into the presence of counsellors today. (11)

verses.text:
मूढोऽप्रगल्भोऽविनयोपपन्न-
स्तीक्ष्णस्वभावोऽल्पमतिर्दुरात्मा।
मूर्खस्त्वमत्यन्तसुदुर्मतिश्च
त्वमिन्द्रजिद् बालतया ब्रवीषि॥ १२॥
verses.m: “You are indiscriminate, dull-witted, un-cultured, violent by nature, of poor intelligence, wicked, ignorant and extremely evil-minded, and talk like a child, O Indrajit! (12)

verses.text:
को ब्रह्मदण्डप्रतिमप्रकाशा-
नर्चिष्मतः कालनिकाशरूपान्।
सहेत बाणान् यमदण्डकल्पान्
समक्षमुक्तान् युधि राघवेण॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Who can withstand the flaming arrows, discharged by Rāma, a scion of Raghu, in combat right in front of the enemy, who resemble the rod of Brahmā (the creator) in glory, that present a look similar to that of Death and are equal to the rod of Yama (the god of retribution)? (13)

verses.text:
धनानि रत्नानि सुभूषणानि
वासांसि दिव्यानि मणींश्च चित्रान्।
सीतां च रामाय निवेद्य देवीं
वसेम राजन्निह वीतशोकाः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Offering riches, precious stones, excellent jewels, celestial garments and various gems, as well as the godlike Sītā to Rāma, let us live here free from grief, O king!” (14)

verses.text:
सुनिविष्टं हितं वाक्यमुक्तवन्तं विभीषणम्।
अब्रवीत् परुषं वाक्यं रावणः कालचोदितः॥ १॥
verses.m: Rāvaṇa, who was under the influence of Death, addressed the following harsh words to Vibhīṣaṇa, who had rendered an advice which was wholesome and impregnated with meaning: (1)

verses.text:
वसेत् सह सपत्नेन क्रुद्धेनाशीविषेण च।
न तु मित्रप्रवादेन संवसेच्छत्रुसेविना॥ २॥
verses.m: “One would rather live with an avowed enemy and even with an enraged venomous serpent than with an individual who, though professing himself to be a friend, is devoted to the enemy. (2)

verses.text:
जानामि शीलं ज्ञातीनां सर्वलोकेषु राक्षस।
हृष्यन्ति व्यसनेष्वेते ज्ञातीनां ज्ञातयः सदा॥ ३॥
verses.m: “I know, O ranger of the night, the disposition of one’s relatives in all the worlds. These latter always rejoice in the misfortunes of their relatives. (3)

verses.text:
प्रधानं साधकं वैद्यं धर्मशीलं च राक्षस।
ज्ञातयोऽप्यवमन्यन्ते शूरं परिभवन्ति च॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Kinsfolk (as a rule) despise their chief, even though he carries on his duties as a ruler, is learned and given to piety, O ogre, and try to humiliate him, if he is a hero. (4)

verses.text:
नित्यमन्योन्यसंहृष्टा व्यसनेष्वाततायिनः।
प्रच्छन्नहृदया घोरा ज्ञातयस्तु भयावहाः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Feeling highly rejoiced in the misfortunes of one another, having secret designs and turning desperadoes any moment, kinsfolk are generally cruel and formidable. (5)

verses.text:
श्रूयन्ते हस्तिभिर्गीताः श्लोकाः पद्मवने पुरा।
पाशहस्तान् नरान् दृष्ट्वा शृणुष्व गदतो मम॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Couplets uttered in the past by elephants in a bed of lotuses on seeing men with snares in their hands (to catch them) have been heard by me. Listen to them from me even as I repeat them: (6)

verses.text:
नाग्निर्नान्यानि शस्त्राणि न नः पाशा भयावहाः।
घोराः स्वार्थप्रयुक्तास्तु ज्ञातयो नो भयावहाः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “ ‘Neither fire nor other arms nor snares strike terror in us; but those of our own kind, who are cruel and actuated by self-interest, are dangerous. (7)

verses.text:
उपायमेते वक्ष्यन्ति ग्रहणे नात्र संशयः।
कृत्स्नाद् भयाज्ज्ञातिभयं कुकष्टं विहितं च नः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “ ‘These (latter) will point out the device of catching us; there is no doubt about it. Nay, the peril from those of our kind is known to us as the most formidable of all perils.’ (8)

verses.text:
विद्यते गोषु सम्पन्नं विद्यते ज्ञातितो भयम्।
विद्यते स्त्रीषु चापल्यं विद्यते ब्राह्मणे तपः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “There exists wealth in the cow; there exists peril from one’s own kinsfolk; there exists capriciousness in women; and there exists asceticism in the Brāhmaṇa. (9)

verses.text:
ततो नेष्टमिदं सौम्य यदहं लोकसत्कृतः।
ऐश्वर्यमभिजातश्च रिपूणां मूर्ध्नि च स्थितः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Therefore, it is not to your liking, my good brother, that I am honoured by the whole world, have attained power and pelf and have set my foot on the heads of my enemies. (10)

verses.text:
यथा पुष्करपत्रेषु पतितास्तोयबिन्दवः।
न श्लेषमभिगच्छन्ति तथानार्येषु सौहृदम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Love bestowed on the unworthy does not moisten their heart any more than drops of water fallen on lotus leaves penetrate the latter. (11)

verses.text:
यथा शरदि मेघानां सिञ्चतामपि गर्जताम्।
न भवत्यम्बुसंक्लेदस्तथानार्येषु सौहृदम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Even as the earth is not saturated with the water of clouds thundering and raining in autumn, so love bestowed on the unworthy fails to moisten their heart. (12)

verses.text:
यथा मधुकरस्तर्षाद् रसं विन्दन्न तिष्ठति।
तथा त्वमपि तत्रैव तथानार्येषु सौहृदम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Affection does not abide in the heart of the unworthy any more than a black bee stays with a flower even though sucking its nectar with avidity. You too are of that type. (13)

verses.text:
यथा मधुकरस्तर्षात् काशपुष्पं पिबन्नपि।
रसमत्र न विन्देत तथानार्येषु सौहृदम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “One bestowing love on the unworthy does not attain happiness any more than a black bee, though sucking the flowers of a grass known by the name of Kāśa gets nectar there. (14)

verses.text:
यथा पूर्वं गजः स्नात्वा गृह्य हस्तेन वै रजः।
दूषयत्यात्मनो देहं तथानार्येषु सौहृदम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Just as picking up sand in its proboscis immediately after taking a dip in water in the first instance, an elephant soils its body again, so the affection bestowed on the unworthy gets clogged. (15)

verses.text:
योऽन्यस्त्वेवंविधं ब्रूयाद् वाक्यमेतन्निशाचर।
अस्मिन् मुहूर्ते न भवेत् त्वां तु धिक् कुलपांसन॥ १६॥
verses.m: “He who, other than you, actually utters the aforesaid words in the way you have done, O ranger of the night, would have undoubtedly ceased to be this very moment. As for you, a curse upon you, O obloquy of your race!” (16)

verses.text:
इत्युक्तः परुषं वाक्यं न्यायवादी विभीषणः।
उत्पपात गदापाणिश्चतुर्भिः सह राक्षसैः॥ १७॥
verses.m: Rebuked in these harsh words, Vibhīṣaṇa, who had spoken what is right, rose in the airspace, mace in hand, alongwith four other ogres, his ministers. (17)

verses.text:
अब्रवीच्च तदा वाक्यं जातक्रोधो विभीषणः।
अन्तरिक्षगतः श्रीमान् भ्राता वै राक्षसाधिपम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: Nay, standing in airspace, the glorious Vibhīṣaṇa, (half-) brother of Rāvaṇa, who was filled with indignation, actually addressed the following words at that moment to Rāvaṇa (the suzerain lord of ogres): (18)

verses.text:
स त्वं भ्रान्तोऽसि मे राजन् ब्रूहि मां यद् यदिच्छसि।
ज्येष्ठो मान्यः पितृसमो न च धर्मपथे स्थितः।
इदं हि परुषं वाक्यं न क्षमाम्यग्रजस्य ते॥ १९॥
verses.m: “You, who have spoken harsh words to me, O king, are deluded. Rebuke me in whatever words you will. Being my eldest brother, you are worthy of respect to me like a father; yet you are not steadfast on the path of virtue. I, therefore, cannot tolerate your abusive speech, even though you are my elder. (19)

verses.text:
सुनीतं हितकामेन वाक्यमुक्तं दशानन।
न गृह्णन्त्यकृतात्मानः कालस्य वशमागताः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Those who have not mastered their self and have fallen under the sway of Death do not heed the excellent words of wisdom uttered by a well-wisher, O Rāvaṇa (endowed with ten heads)! (20)

verses.text:
सुलभाः पुरुषा राजन् सततं प्रियवादिनः।
अप्रियस्य च पथ्यस्य वक्ता श्रोता च दुर्लभः॥ २१॥
verses.m: “People ever given to uttering palatable words, O king, can be easily had. He, however, who utters and listens to words which, though unpleasant to hear, yet are conducive to one’s good are difficult to find. (21)

verses.text:
बद्धं कालस्य पाशेन सर्वभूतापहारिणः।
न नश्यन्तमुपेक्षे त्वां प्रदीप्तं शरणं यथा॥ २२॥
verses.m: “I could not ignore you, held fast in the noose of Death—who snatches away all beings—and going to perish like a house in flames. Hence I went out of my way to tell you all this. (22)

verses.text:
दीप्तपावकसंकाशैः शितैः काञ्चनभूषणैः।
न त्वामिच्छाम्यहं द्रष्टुं रामेण निहतं शरैः॥ २३॥
verses.m: “I did not wish to see you killed by Rāma with sharp arrows glowing like a flaming fire and ornamented with gold. (23)

verses.text:
शूराश्च बलवन्तश्च कृतास्त्राश्च नरा रणे।
कालाभिपन्नाः सीदन्ति यथा वालुकसेतवः॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Seized by death, even gallant and mighty men, nay, those who are skilled in archery fall in battle like dams of sand. (24)

verses.text:
तन्मर्षयतु यच्चोक्तं गुरुत्वाद्धितमिच्छता।
आत्मानं सर्वथा रक्ष पुरीं चेमां सराक्षसाम्।
स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु गमिष्यामि सुखी भव मया विना॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Being my elder brother, pray, forgive what has been said by me, wishing you well, as I do. Now protect yourself in every way, as well as this city including the ogres. May prosperity attend on you. Be happy in my absence. (25)

verses.text:
निवार्यमाणस्य मया हितैषिणा
न रोचते ते वचनं निशाचर।
परान्तकाले हि गतायुषो नरा
हितं न गृह्णन्ति सुहृद्भिरीरितम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: “While you were being restrained by me as I wished you well, my warning did not find favour with you, O ranger of the night! At the hour of death men whose life has run its course do not, as a rule, heed the salutary advice tendered by their well-wishers.” (26)

verses.text:
इत्युक्त्वा परुषं वाक्यं रावणं रावणानुजः।
आजगाम मुहूर्तेन यत्र रामः सलक्ष्मणः॥ १॥
verses.m: Addressing the aforesaid harsh words to Rāvaṇa, Vibhīṣaṇa, (the youngest half-brother of Rāvaṇa) arrived in less than an hour where Śrī Rāma was with Lakṣmaṇa (on the opposite shore). (1)

verses.text:
तं मेरुशिखराकारं दीप्तामिव शतह्रदाम्।
गगनस्थं महीस्थास्ते ददृशुर्वानराधिपाः॥ २॥
verses.m: Stationed on the ground (below), the celebrated leaders of monkeys espied Vibhīṣaṇa, who looked like a peak of Mount Meru in size and stood in the air like a dazzling flash of lightning. (2)

verses.text:
ते चाप्यनुचरास्तस्य चत्वारो भीमविक्रमाः।
तेऽपि वर्मायुधोपेता भूषणोत्तमभूषिताः॥ ३॥
verses.m: His four well-known attendants too were endowed with redoubtable prowess. They too were furnished with armour and weapons and adorned with the foremost of jewels. (3)

verses.text:
स च मेघाचलप्रख्यो वज्रायुधसमप्रभः।
वरायुधधरो वीरो दिव्याभरणभूषितः॥ ४॥
verses.m: The valiant Vibhīṣaṇa resembled a cloud and a mountain, vied with Indra (who wields the thunderbolt) in splendour, bore excellent arms and was adorned with heavenly jewels. (4)

verses.text:
तमात्मपञ्चमं दृष्ट्वा सुग्रीवो वानराधिपः।
वानरैः सह दुर्धर्षश्चिन्तयामास बुद्धिमान्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Finding him to be the fifth (besides four others), the wise Sugrīva, the suzerain lord of monkeys, who was difficult to overpower and stood with monkeys, became thoughtful. (5)

verses.text:
चिन्तयित्वा मुहूर्तं तु वानरांस्तानुवाच ह।
हनुमत्प्रमुखान् सर्वानिदं वचनमुत्तमम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Reflecting a while, he, for his part, they say, addressed the following excellent words to all those monkeys with Hanumān at their head: (6)

verses.text:
एष सर्वायुधोपेतश्चतुर्भिः सह राक्षसैः।
राक्षसोभ्येति पश्यध्वमस्मान् हन्तुं न संशयः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Lo, armed with all kinds of weapons and accompanied by four of his kind, this ogre is undoubtedly approaching to kill us.”(7)

verses.text:
सुग्रीवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा सर्वे ते वानरोत्तमाः।
सालानुद्यम्य शैलांश्च इदं वचनमब्रुवन्॥ ८॥
verses.m: Lifting up sal trees and rocks on hearing the words of Sugrīva, all those jewels among monkeys submitted as follows: (8)

verses.text:
शीघ्रं व्यादिश नो राजन् वधायैषां दुरात्मनाम्।
निपतन्ति हता यावद् धरण्यामल्पचेतनाः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Command us at once, O king, to kill these evil-minded ones, so that on being killed, they may fall down on earth, endowed as they are with poor vitality.” (9)

verses.text:
तेषां सम्भाषमाणानामन्योन्यं स विभीषणः।
उत्तरं तीरमासाद्य खस्थ एव व्यतिष्ठत॥ १०॥
verses.m: Reaching the northern shore even as they were talking with one another in this strain, the aforesaid Vibhīṣaṇa stopped short while he was yet in the air. (10)

verses.text:
स उवाच महाप्राज्ञः स्वरेण महता महान्।
सुग्रीवं तांश्च सम्प्रेक्ष्य खस्थ एव विभीषणः॥ ११॥
verses.m: Gazing on Sugrīva and those monkeys, the aforesaid Vibhīṣaṇa, highly intelligent and great as he was, spoke as follows in a loud voice while still remaining in the air: (11)

verses.text:
रावणो नाम दुर्वृत्तो राक्षसो राक्षसेश्वरः।
तस्याहमनुजो भ्राता विभीषण इति श्रुतः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “There is an ogre of evil conduct, Rāvaṇa by name, who is the lord of ogres. I am his youngest (half-) brother, known by the name of Vibhīṣaṇa. (12)

verses.text:
तेन सीता जनस्थानाद् हृता हत्वा जटायुषम्।
रुद्धा च विवशा दीना राक्षसीभिः सुरक्षिता॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Carried off from Janasthāna after killing Jaṭāyu, the poor and helpless Sītā has been detained by him and is being jealously guarded by ogresses. (13)

verses.text:
तमहं हेतुभिर्वाक्यैर्विविधैश्च न्यदर्शयम्।
साधु निर्यात्यतां सीता रामायेति पुनः पुनः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “I thoroughly admonished him time and again by recourse to various arguments in the following words: ‘Let Sītā be restored to Rāma.’ (14)

verses.text:
स च न प्रतिजग्राह रावणः कालचोदितः।
उच्यमानं हितं वाक्यं विपरीत इवौषधम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Impelled by fate, Rāvaṇa, however, would not listen to the salutary advice which was being tendered to him, any more than a man who is doomed would accept a medicine, which is calculated to do him good. (15)

verses.text:
सोऽहं परुषितस्तेन दासवच्चावमानितः।
त्यक्त्वा पुत्रांश्च दारांश्च राघवं शरणं गतः॥ १६॥
verses.m: Abandoning my sons and wife, when spoken to harshly and treated with disrespect like a slave by him, though wishing him well, I have sought Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, as my refuge. (16)

verses.text:
निवेदयत मां क्षिप्रं राघवाय महात्मने।
सर्वलोकशरण्याय विभीषणमुपस्थितम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Therefore, communicate to the high-souled Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), who is capable of protecting all the worlds, the fact of myself, Vibhīṣaṇa, being present.” (17)

verses.text:
एतत्तु वचनं श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवो लघुविक्रमः।
लक्ष्मणस्याग्रतो रामं संरब्धमिदमब्रवीत्॥ १८॥
verses.m: Hearing this appeal, the swift-footed Sugrīva for his part ran up to the presence of Śrī Rāma and indignantly submitted as follows to Śrī Rāma in the presence of Lakṣmaṇa: (18)

verses.text:
प्रविष्टः शत्रुसैन्यं हि प्राप्तः शत्रुरतर्कितः।
निहन्यादन्तरं लब्ध्वा उलूको वायसानिव॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Indeed an enemy, who has belonged to the hostile ranks, has unexpectedly made his appearance. Finding an opportune moment he may kill us even as an owl would destroy crows. (19)

verses.text:
मन्त्रे व्यूहे नये चारे युक्तो भवितुमर्हसि।
वानराणां च भद्रं ते परेषां च परंतप॥ २०॥
verses.m: “For conferring benefits on the monkeys, as well as for the subjugation of the enemy, O scourge of your foes, you ought to remain alert in the matter of holding deliberations as to what ought to be done and what ought not to be done, deployment of troops, employing the four expedients against the enemy in their own sphere as well as in espionage: this will ensure your welfare.(20)

verses.text:
अन्तर्धानगता ह्येते राक्षसाः कामरूपिणः।
शूराश्च निकृतिज्ञाश्च तेषां जातु न विश्वसेत्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Since these ogres move about unperceived, are able to change their form at will and are valiant and crafty, one should never repose trust in them. (21)

verses.text:
प्रणिधी राक्षसेन्द्रस्य रावणस्य भवेदयम्।
अनुप्रविश्य सोऽस्मासु भेदं कुर्यान्न संशयः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “He may be a spy of Rāvaṇa, the ruler of ogres. Finding his way in our midst, he may doubtless sow dissension amongst us. (22)

verses.text:
अथ वा स्वयमेवैष छिद्रमासाद्य बुद्धिमान्।
अनुप्रविश्य विश्वस्ते कदाचित् प्रहरेदपि॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Or, discovering our weak points on entering our ranks, this fellow, shrewd as he is, may even strike us himself some day when we have reposed faith in him. (23)

verses.text:
मित्राटविबलं चैव मौलभृत्यबलं तथा।
सर्वमेतद् बलं ग्राह्यं वर्जयित्वा द्विषद्बलम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “A contingent supplied by allies, that provided by the foresters, that furnished by hereditary servants and the one supplied by paid servants—all these are worth accepting, but not the one supplied by an enemy. (24)

verses.text:
प्रकृत्या राक्षसो ह्येष भ्रातामित्रस्य वै प्रभो।
आगतश्च रिपुः साक्षात् कथमस्मिंश्च विश्वसेत्॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Indeed, he is an ogre by birth and a brother of the enemy to boot, my lord! The enemy himself has in this way made his appearance before us. How can one repose trust in him in such circumstances? (25)

verses.text:
रावणस्यानुजो भ्राता विभीषण इति श्रुतः।
चतुर्भिः सह रक्षोभिर्भवन्तं शरणं गतः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Rāvaṇa’s own younger brother, known by the name of Vibhīṣaṇa, has sought you as his refuge alongwith four other ogres. (26)

verses.text:
रावणेन प्रणीतं हि तमवेहि विभीषणम्।
तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये क्षमं क्षमवतां वर॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Know the said Vibhīṣaṇa to have been dispatched by Rāvaṇa himself. I, therefore, deem it fit to arrest him, O the foremost of the indulgent! (27)

verses.text:
राक्षसो जिह्मया बुद्ध्या संदिष्टोऽयमिहागतः।
प्रहर्तुं मायया छन्नो विश्वस्ते त्वयि चानघ॥ २८॥
verses.m: “This ogre has evidently made his appearance here as directed by Rāvaṇa with crooked intent in order to strike you when you have reposed faith in him, remaining concealed by his witchcraft all the time, O sinless one! (28)

verses.text:
वध्यतामेष तीव्रेण दण्डेन सचिवैः सह।
रावणस्य नृशंसस्य भ्राता ह्येष विभीषणः॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Let this Vibhīṣaṇa be killed alongwith his ministers by recourse to severe punishment, inasmuch as he is a brother of the cruel Rāvaṇa.” (29)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा तु तं रामं संरब्धो वाहिनीपतिः।
वाक्यज्ञो वाक्यकुशलं ततो मौनमुपागमत्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Having submitted as aforesaid to Śrī Rāma, who was adept in expression, Sugrīva, the Commander-in-Chief, for his part, who knew how to speak and felt agitated, then assumed silence. (30)

verses.text:
सुग्रीवस्य तु तद् वाक्यं श्रुत्वा रामो महाबलः।
समीपस्थानुवाचेदं हनुमत्प्रमुखान् कपीन्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Hearing the foregoing speech of Sugrīva, Śrī Rāma, who was endowed with extraordinary might, spoke as follows to the monkeys headed by Hanumān, who stood near him: (31)

verses.text:
यदुक्तं कपिराजेन रावणावरजं प्रति।
वाक्यं हेतुमदत्यर्थं भवद्भिरपि च श्रुतम्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “The advice which has been tendered by Sugrīva, the king of monkeys, regarding Vibhīṣaṇa (Rāvaṇa’s youngest half-brother) is extremely reasonable and has been heard by you, too. (32)

verses.text:
सुहृदामर्थकृच्छ्रेषु युक्तं बुद्धिमता सदा।
समर्थेनोपसंदेष्टुं शाश्वतीं भूतिमिच्छता॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “It is always desirable for one who is intelligent and capable of judgment and seeks the lasting good of one’s near and dear ones to express one’s honest opinion on knotty points in regard to duty.” (33)

verses.text:
इत्येवं परिपृष्टास्ते स्वं स्वं मतमतन्द्रिताः।
सोपचारं तदा राममूचुः प्रियचिकीर्षवः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: Consulted in these words, the monkeys, who were free from lassitude and keen to oblige Śrī Rāma, forthwith expressed each his own opinion politely as follows: (34)

verses.text:
अज्ञातं नास्ति ते किंचित् त्रिषु लोकेषु राघव।
आत्मानं पूजयन् राम पृच्छस्यस्मान् सुहृत्तया॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “Nothing is unknown to you in all the three worlds, O scion of Raghu! You consult us all the same because of your goodwill towards us, thereby bestowing honour on us, who are your very selves, O Rāma! (35)

verses.text:
त्वं हि सत्यव्रतः शूरो धार्मिको दृढविक्रमः।
परीक्ष्यकारी स्मृतिमान् निसृष्टात्मा सुहृत्सु च॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “Indeed, you are a man of unfailing vows, gallant, pious, endowed with unyielding prowess and discreet; you take action after full investigation, and have offered your very self to your near and dear ones. (36)

verses.text:
तस्मादेकैकशस्तावद् ब्रुवन्तु सचिवास्तव।
हेतुतो मतिसम्पन्नाः समर्थाश्च पुनः पुनः॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “Therefore, let your counsellors, who are all richly endowed with intelligence and capable of judgment, too, likewise argue with reason, one after another, first of all. (37)

verses.text:
इत्युक्ते राघवायाथ मतिमानङ्गदोऽग्रतः।
विभीषणपरीक्षार्थमुवाच वचनं हरिः॥ ३८॥
verses.m: This having been said, the sagacious monkey, Aṅgada, to begin with, immediately tendered to Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) the following advice, which suggested the means of testing the bona fides of Vibhīṣaṇa: (38)

verses.text:
शत्रोः सकाशात् सम्प्राप्तः सर्वथा तर्क्य एव हि।
विश्वासनीयः सहसा न कर्तव्यो विभीषणः॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “Vibhīṣaṇa should not be dealt with as trustworthy all at once inasmuch as, having arrived direct from the enemy’s presence, he yet deserves to be viewed with suspicion in every way. (39)

verses.text:
छादयित्वाऽऽत्मभावं हि चरन्ति शठबुद्धयः।
प्रहरन्ति च रन्ध्रेषु सोऽनर्थः सुमहान् भवेत्॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “For, people of perfidious mind move about concealing their motive and direct their blow at one’s weak points: that may prove to be a disaster of no small magnitude. (40)

verses.text:
अर्थानर्थौ विनिश्चित्य व्यवसायं भजेत ह।
गुणतः संग्रहं कुर्याद् दोषतस्तु विसर्जयेत्॥ ४१॥
verses.m: “Definitely ascertaining the advantages and disadvantages, which are likely to follow from a certain course of action, one should actually take one’s decision in the matter. One should adopt a course of action if advantages are likely to follow from it, and should reject it if it is thought to be disadvantageous. (41)

verses.text:
यदि दोषो महांस्तस्मिंस्त्यज्यतामविशङ्कितम्।
गुणान् वापि बहून् ज्ञात्वा संग्रहः क्रियतां नृप॥ ४२॥
verses.m: “If there is great harm in accepting him, let him be boldly rejected. Or, let him be accepted, on the other hand, on coming to know of the many benefits that are likely to accrue from him, O protector of men!”(42)

verses.text:
शरभस्त्वथ निश्चित्य सार्थं वचनमब्रवीत्।
क्षिप्रमस्मिन् नरव्याघ्र चारः प्रतिविधीयताम्॥ ४३॥
