एवमुक्तस्तथेत्याह विद्युज्जिह्वो निशाचरः।
दर्शयामास तां मायां सुप्रयुक्तां स रावणे॥ ९॥
verses.m: Commanded thus by Rāvaṇa, the ogre Vidyujjihva said, “Amen!” Nay, he displayed before Rāvaṇa the said conjuring trick, dexterously managed. (9)

verses.text:
तस्य तुष्टोऽभवद् राजा प्रददौ च विभूषणम्।
अशोकवनिकायां च सीतादर्शनलालसः॥ १०॥
नैर्ऋतानामधिपतिः संविवेश महाबलः।
ततो दीनामदैन्यार्हां ददर्श धनदानुजः॥ ११॥
अधोमुखीं शोकपरामुपविष्टां महीतले।
भर्तारं समनुध्यान्तीमशोकवनिकां गताम्॥ १२॥
उपास्यमानां घोराभी राक्षसीभिरदूरतः।
उपसृत्य ततः सीतां प्रहर्षं नाम कीर्तयन्॥ १३॥
इदं च वचनं धृष्टमुवाच जनकात्मजाम्।
सान्त्व्यमाना मया भद्रे यमाश्रित्य विमन्यसे॥ १४॥
खरहन्ता स ते भर्ता राघवः समरे हतः।
छिन्नं ते सर्वथा मूलं दर्पश्च निहतो मया॥ १५॥
verses.m: The king, Rāvaṇa, was pleased with him and parted in his favour with a precious ornament. Nay, eagerly longing, as he did, for a sight of Sītā, Rāvaṇa, the suzerain lord of ogres, who was endowed with extraordinary might, duly entered the Aśoka grove. Thereupon Rāvaṇa (a younger brother of Kubera, the bestower of riches) beheld the wretched princess, Sītā, who did not deserve the miserable plight to which she was being subjected, seated on the earth’s surface in the Aśoka grove with her head bent low, given over, as she was, to grief and thinking all the time of her husband and being kept on eye on at close quarters by hideous ogresses. Approaching Sītā, and mentioning his own name with great delight, he then addressed the following impudent words to Janaka’s daughter: “That husband of yours, Rāma (a scion of Raghu), the slayer of Khara, relying on whom you have been treating me with disdain while being coaxed by me, O blessed lady, has been killed in combat. Your roots stand completely severed and your vanity has been crushed by me. (10—15)

verses.text:
व्यसनेनात्मनः सीते मम भार्या भविष्यसि।
विसृजैतां मतिं मूढे किं मृतेन करिष्यसि॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Compelled by your misfortune in the shape of your husband’s death, you will become my wife (of your own accord). Give up your present resolution of spurning my advances, O stupid woman! What will you do with your deceased husband?(16)

verses.text:
भवस्व भद्रे भार्याणां सर्वासामीश्वरी मम।
अल्पपुण्ये निवृत्तार्थे मूढे पण्डितमानिनि।
शृणु भर्तृवधं सीते घोरं वृत्रवधं यथा॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Become, O blessed lady, the queen of all my consorts, now that your object in the shape of getting re-united with your husband has come to an end, O stupid woman of scant virtue, who deem yourself wise. Now hear, if you so please, the story of how your husband was killed, which is as hideous as that relating to the destruction of the demon Vṛtra at the hands of Indra. (17)

verses.text:
समायातः समुद्रान्तं हन्तुं मां किल राघवः।
वानरेन्द्रप्रणीतेन बलेन महता वृतः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Surrounded by a huge army collected by Sugrīva (the ruler of monkeys), they say, Rāma, a scion of Raghu, duly reached the sea-shore to destroy me. (18)

verses.text:
संनिविष्टः समुद्रस्य पीड्य तीरमथोत्तरम्।
बलेन महता रामो व्रजत्यस्तं दिवाकरे॥ १९॥
verses.m: “While the sun was going to set, Rāma with his vast army forthwith duly struck camp encroaching upon the northern shore. (19)

verses.text:
अथाध्वनि परिश्रान्तमर्धरात्रे स्थितं बलम्।
सुखसुप्तं समासाद्य चरितं प्रथमं चरैः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Duly making their way at midnight to the army, which lay comfortably asleep, completely exhausted as it had been in the course of the journey, my spies first reconnoitred it. (20)

verses.text:
तत्प्रहस्तप्रणीतेन बलेन महता मम।
बलमस्य हतं रात्रौ यत्र रामः सलक्ष्मणः॥ २१॥
verses.m: “The said army of Rāma was eventually destroyed during the night itself on the very spot where Rāma was encamping with Lakṣmaṇa, by my huge army led by Prahasta. (21)

verses.text:
पट्टिशान् परिघांश्चक्रानृष्टीन् दण्डान् महायुधान्।
बाणजालानि शूलानि भास्वरान् कूटमुद्गरान्॥ २२॥
यष्टीश्च तोमरान् प्रासांश्चक्राणि मुसलानि च।
उद्यम्योद्यम्य रक्षोभिर्वानरेषु निपातिताः॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Uplifting again and again scimitars, iron bars, small discuses, javelins, staffs, large weapons, bundles of arrows, darts, sparkling maces bristling with nails, sticks, iron clubs, lances, large discuses and Musalas, the ogres hurled them against the monkeys. (22-23)

verses.text:
अथ सुप्तस्य रामस्य प्रहस्तेन प्रमाथिना।
असक्तं कृतहस्तेन शिरश्छिन्नं महासिना॥ २४॥
verses.m: “The head of Rāma, who was lying asleep at that moment, was then severed at once with a big sword by the ferocious Prahasta, who is skilled in archery. (24)

verses.text:
विभीषणः समुत्पत्य निगृहीतो यदृच्छया।
दिशः प्रव्राजितः सैन्यैर्लक्ष्मणः प्लवगैः सह॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Springing up, he casually took Vibhīṣaṇa captive; while Lakṣmaṇa with the monkey troops was made to flee in all directions. (25)

verses.text:
सुग्रीवो ग्रीवया सीते भग्नया प्लवगाधिपः।
निरस्तहनुकः सीते हनूमान् राक्षसैर्हतः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Sugrīva, the suzerain lord of monkeys, lies prostrate with his neck broken; while Hanumān, with his lower jaw dashed off, has been killed by the ogres, O Sītā! (26)

verses.text:
जाम्बवानथ जानुभ्यामुत्पतन् निहतो युधि।
पट्टिशैर्बहुभिश्छिन्नो निकृत्तः पादपो यथा॥ २७॥
verses.m: “While springing up, Jāmbavān was forthwith struck violently at the knees in a melee and, cut with many scimitars, was felled like a tree. (27)

verses.text:
मैन्दश्च द्विविदश्चोभौ तौ वानरवरर्षभौ।
निःश्वसन्तौ रुदन्तौ च रुधिरेण परिप्लुतौ॥ २८॥
असिना व्यायतौ छिन्नौ मध्ये ह्यरिनिषूदनौ।
अनुश्वसिति मेदिन्यां पनसः पनसो यथा॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Nay, the gigantic Mainda and Dwivida, the foremost among the best of monkeys and the well-known slayers of their foes, who were breathing hard and groaning, bathed as they were in blood, have both been actually cut into two with a sword at the waist. Burst open like a ripe jack fruit, Panasa lies on the ground gasping for breath (28-29)

verses.text:
नाराचैर्बहुभिश्छिन्नः शेते दर्यां दरीमुखः।
कुमुदस्तु महातेजा निष्कूजन् सायकैर्हतः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Pierced with numerous steel arrows, Darīmukha is lying in a ravine; while Kumuda, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, lies shrieking, struck down with arrows. (30)

verses.text:
अङ्गदो बहुभिश्छिन्नः शरैरासाद्य राक्षसैः।
परितो रुधिरोद्गारी क्षितौ निपतितोऽङ्गदः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Pierced by the ogres with many arrows after marching towards him, Aṅgada, who was adorned with armlets, lies fallen down on the ground, vomiting blood on all sides. (31)

verses.text:
हरयो मथिता नागै रथजालैस्तथापरे।
शयाना मृदितास्तत्र वायुवेगैरिवाम्बुदाः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Lying asleep there, other monkeys were crushed by elephants and multitudes of chariots even as clouds are rent asunder by force of wind. (32)

verses.text:
प्रसृताश्च परे त्रस्ता हन्यमाना जघन्यतः।
अनुद्रुतास्तु रक्षोभिः सिंहैरिव महाद्विपाः॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “Nay, pursued by ogres as huge elephants are by lions, still other monkeys fled panic-stricken while being struck in the back. (33)

verses.text:
सागरे पतिताः केचित् केचिद् गगनमाश्रिताः।
ऋक्षा वृक्षानुपारूढा वानरीं वृत्तिमाश्रिताः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “Some took a plunge into the sea, while others sought refuge in the air, nay, resorting to the ways of monkeys, the bears climbed up trees (in order to escape destruction at the hands of the ogres). (34)

verses.text:
सागरस्य च तीरेषु शैलेषु च वनेषु च।
पिङ्गलास्ते विरूपाक्षै राक्षसैर्बहवो हताः॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “Nay, many more well-known monkeys have been killed by the ogres with fierce eyes on the shores of the sea, as well as in the midst of rocks as also in the woods. (35)

verses.text:
एवं तव हतो भर्ता ससैन्यो मम सेनया।
क्षतजार्द्रं रजोध्वस्तमिदं चास्याहृतं शिरः॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “In this way has your husband been destroyed with his forces by my army. Soaked in blood and smeared with dust, his head too has been brought here to convince you of his death.” (36)

verses.text:
ततः परमदुर्धर्षो रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः।
सीतायामुपशृण्वत्यां राक्षसीमिदमब्रवीत्॥ ३७॥
verses.m: Rāvaṇa, the lord of ogres, who was most difficult to overpower, then spoke as follows to an ogress within the close hearing of Sītā: (37)

verses.text:
राक्षसं क्रूरकर्माणं विद्युज्जिह्वं समानय।
येन तद्राघवशिरः संग्रामात् स्वयमाहृतम्॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “Bring politely to my presence the ogre Vidyujjihva of cruel deeds, by whom has the well-known head of Rāma (a scion of Raghu) been personally brought from the field of battle.” (38)

verses.text:
विद्युज्जिह्वस्तदा गृह्य शिरस्तत्सशरासनम्।
प्रणामं शिरसा कृत्वा रावणस्याग्रतः स्थितः॥ ३९॥
verses.m: Holding the aforesaid head alongwith a bow, and making a respectful salute with his head bent low, Vidyujjihva now stood in front of Rāvaṇa. (39)

verses.text:
तमब्रवीत् ततो राजा रावणो राक्षसं स्थितम्।
विद्युज्जिह्वं महाजिह्वं समीपपरिवर्तिनम्॥ ४०॥
अग्रतः कुरु सीतायाः शीघ्रं दाशरथेः शिरः।
अवस्थां पश्चिमां भर्तुः कृपणा साधु पश्यतु॥ ४१॥
verses.m: King Rāvaṇa thereupon spoke as follows to the said ogre, Vidyujjihva, who had a long tongue and stood nearby: “Place at once in front of Sītā the head of Rāma (son of Daśaratha). Let the poor woman clearly behold the ultimate condition of her husband.” (40-41)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तं तु तद् रक्षः शिरस्तत् प्रियदर्शनम्।
उपनिक्षिप्य सीतायाः क्षिप्रमन्तरधीयत॥ ४२॥
verses.m: Placing that head, which was agreeable to look at, by the side of Sītā, when commanded as aforesaid, the said ogre for his part instantly vanished out of sight (42)

verses.text:
रावणश्चापि चिक्षेप भास्वरं कार्मुकं महत्।
त्रिषु लोकेषु विख्यातं रामस्यैतदिति ब्रुवन्॥ ४३॥
verses.m: Nay, Rāvaṇa too cast down the brilliant and mighty bow, saying: “This is the bow, famed in all the three worlds, belonging to Rāma.” (43)

verses.text:
इदं तत् तव रामस्य कार्मुकं ज्यासमावृतम्।
इह प्रहस्तेनानीतं तं हत्वा निशि मानुषम्॥ ४४॥
verses.m: “This is the bow,” he added, “belonging to your Rāma, duly provided with a string and brought hither by Prahasta after disposing of that mortal at night.” (44)

verses.text:
स विद्युज्जिह्वेन सहैव तच्छिरो
धनुश्च भूमौ विनिकीर्यमाणः।
विदेहराजस्य सुतां यशस्विनीं
ततोऽब्रवीत् तां भव मे वशानुगा॥ ४५॥
verses.m: Casting the bow too on the ground at the same place where the aforesaid head had been placed by Vidyujjihva, Rāvaṇa then said to that illustrious daughter of Janaka (the ruler of the Videha territory), “Now submit to my will.” (45)

verses.text:
सा सीता तच्छिरो दृष्ट्वा तच्च कार्मुकमुत्तमम्।
सुग्रीवप्रतिसंसर्गमाख्यातं च हनूमता॥ १॥
नयने मुखवर्णं च भर्तुस्तत्सदृशं मुखम्।
केशान् केशान्तदेशं च तं च चूडामणिं शुभम्॥ २॥
एतैः सर्वैरभिज्ञानैरभिज्ञाय सुदुःखिता।
विजगर्हेऽत्र कैकेयीं क्रोशन्ती कुररी यथा॥ ३॥
verses.m: Beholding that head as well as that excellent bow, nay, recalling the alliance of Śrī Rāma with Sugrīva, which accounted for the destruction of monkeys by the ogres, spoken of by Hanumān, the eyes, the hue of the countenance, the said countenance resembling that of her husband, the locks as well as the brow as also the well-known splendid jewel on the top, nay, identifying the head of her husband by means of these distinguishing marks, the aforesaid Sītā felt sore distressed and, crying like a female osprey, began to reproach Kaikeyī for this as follows: (1—3)

verses.text:
सकामा भव कैकेयि हतोऽयं कुलनन्दनः।
कुलमुत्सादितं सर्वं त्वया कलहशीलया॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Be now satisfied, now that your desire has been fulfilled, O Kaikeyī, in that this delight of his House has been killed. The entire race has been uprooted by you, given as you were to quarrelling. (4)

verses.text:
आर्येण किं नु कैकेय्याः कृतं रामेण विप्रियम्।
यन्मया चीरवसनं दत्त्वा प्रव्राजितो वनम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “What offence, I wonder, was given by the noble Śrī Rāma to Kaikeyī, for which he was exiled into the forest with me, after presenting him with a robe of bark!” (5)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा तु वैदेही वेपमाना तपस्विनी।
जगाम जगतीं बाला छिन्ना तु कदली यथा॥ ६॥
verses.m: Trembling all over while saying so, the youthful lady, the poor Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, for her part fell prostrate to the ground like a plantain tree cut to the root. (6)

verses.text:
सा मुहूर्तात् समाश्वस्य परिलभ्याथ चेतनाम्।
तच्छिरः समुपास्थाय विललापायतेक्षणा॥ ७॥
verses.m: Regaining consciousness after a while and taking heart, nay, sitting very near the head, that large-eyed lady began to lament as follows: “Alas! I am undone, O mighty-armed prince, faithful to your heroic vow of carrying out the command of your father till the last moment of your life! I have witnessed your final state, widowed as I am. (8)

verses.text:
हा हतास्मि महाबाहो वीरव्रतमनुव्रत।
इमां ते पश्चिमावस्थां गतास्मि विधवा कृता॥ ८॥
verses.m: “The death of a husband before that of his wife is declared to be a catastrophe. A man of noble conduct, you have died before me, a woman of virtuous conduct! (9)

verses.text:
प्रथमं मरणं नार्या भर्तुर्वैगुण्यमुच्यते।
सुवृत्तः साधुवृत्तायाः संवृत्तस्त्वं ममाग्रतः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Even you, who were actually intent on delivering me, fallen in great adversity and swallowed up in an ocean of grief, have been struck down by the enemies! (10)

verses.text:
महद् दुःखं प्रपन्नाया मग्नायाः शोकसागरे।
यो हि मामुद्यतस्त्रातुं सोऽपि त्वं विनिपातितः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “My celebrated mother-in-law, Kausalyā, who was so fond of her offspring, O scion of Raghu, has been disunited from you, her son, even as a cow, who is fond of its calf, would get disunited from its calf. (11)

verses.text:
सा श्वश्रूर्मम कौसल्या त्वया पुत्रेण राघव।
वत्सेनेव यथा धेनुर्विवत्सा वत्सला कृता॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Your life was predicted to be long by astrologers, O scion of Raghu! Their prophecy, however, has proved to be false since your life has been so short, O Rāma! (12)

verses.text:
उद्दिष्टं दीर्घमायुस्ते दैवज्ञैरपि राघव।
अनृतं वचनं तेषामल्पायुरसि राघव॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Or, even though you were extremely sagacious, perhaps prudence disappeared in you, in that you fell into the enemy’s hands while asleep. Indeed, this Time-Spirit alone, who is the cause of existence of all created beings, brings them to an end. (13)

verses.text:
अथवा नश्यति प्रज्ञा प्राज्ञस्यापि सतस्तव।
पचत्येनं तथा कालो भूतानां प्रभवो ह्ययम्॥ १३॥
अदृष्टं मृत्युमापन्नः कस्मात् त्वं नयशास्त्रवित्।
व्यसनानामुपायज्ञः कुशलो ह्यसि वर्जने॥ १४॥
verses.m: “How did you meet with an unforeseen death—you, who were well-versed in the science of political ethics, nay, who knew the ways and means of warding off calamities and were skilled in employing them? (14)

verses.text:
तथा त्वं सम्परिष्वज्य रौद्रयातिनृशंसया।
कालरात्र्या ममाच्छिद्य हृतः कमललोचन॥ १५॥
verses.m: “After tearing you from me and closely embracing you, O lotus-eyed one, you were in that condition of lying buried in sleep, borne away by the horrible and most cruel deity presiding over the night of destruction. (15)

verses.text:
इह शेषे महाबाहो मां विहाय तपस्विनीम्।
प्रियामिव यथा नारीं पृथिवीं पुरुषर्षभ॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Having deserted me, a pitiable woman, and embracing the earth like a darling, you are lying here, O mighty-armed jewel among men! (16)

verses.text:
अर्चितं सततं यत्नाद् गन्धमाल्यैर्मया तव।
इदं ते मत्प्रियं वीर धनुः काञ्चनभूषितम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Here lies your bow decked with gold, which was always meticulously worshipped by me with sandal paste and wreaths of flowers and which was so dear to me, O gallant prince! (17)

verses.text:
पित्रा दशरथेन त्वं श्वशुरेण ममानघ।
सर्वैश्च पितृभिः सार्धं नूनं स्वर्गे समागतः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “You have surely been re-united in heaven with your father and my father-in-law, King Daśaratha, as well as with all the manes, O sinless one! (18)

verses.text:
दिवि नक्षत्रभूतं च महत्कर्मकृतं तथा।
पुण्यं राजर्षिवंशं त्वमात्मनः समुपेक्षसे॥ १९॥
verses.m: “What a pity that you are deserting the saintly race of royal sages to which you belong—you, by whom such extraordinary exploits have been performed, which shine like luminaries in the sky! (19)

verses.text:
किं मां न प्रेक्षसे राजन् किं वा न प्रतिभाषसे।
बालां बालेन सम्प्राप्तां भार्यां मां सहचारिणीम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Why don’t you look at me, O prince? And why don’t you answer me, won by you when you were a mere boy, as a wife and companion of a tender age? (20)

verses.text:
संश्रुतं गृह्णता पाणिं चरिष्यामीति यत् त्वया।
स्मर तन्नाम काकुत्स्थ नय मामपि दुःखिताम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Call to mind, O scion of Kakutstha, the solemn promise that was actually made by you while taking my hand in yours, viz., that ‘I shall practise virtue with you’ and take me, the wretched one, too with you to the other world. (21)

verses.text:
कस्मान्मामपहाय त्वं गतो गतिमतां वर।
अस्माल्लोकादमुं लोकं त्यक्त्वा मामपि दुःखिताम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Wherefore, having brought me all the way from Ayodhyā to Janasthāna, O jewel among the resourceful, have you departed from this world to the other, deserting even me, the miserable woman? (22)

verses.text:
कल्याणै रुचिरं गात्रं परिष्वक्तं मयैव तु।
क्रव्यादैस्तच्छरीरं ते नूनं विपरिकृष्यते॥ २३॥
verses.m: “That body of yours, which looked charming with festive decorations, and was till now embraced by me alone, is surely being violently dragged here and there by carnivorous beasts. (23)

verses.text:
अग्निष्टोमादिभिर्यज्ञैरिष्टवानाप्तदक्षिणैः।
अग्निहोत्रेण संस्कारं केन त्वं न तु लप्स्यसे॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Why are you not really going to secure the privilege of being cremated with a sacrificial fire even though you have worshipped the Lord through sacrificial performances such as Agniṣṭoma, in which handsome fees were paid to the officiating priests? (24)

verses.text:
प्रव्रज्यामुपपन्नानां त्रयाणामेकमागतम्।
परिप्रेक्ष्यति कौसल्या लक्ष्मणं शोकलालसा॥ २५॥
verses.m: “What a pity that completely given up to grief, Kausalyā (your mother) will eagerly see returned Lakṣmaṇa alone of the three who went into exile from Ayodhyā! (25)

verses.text:
स तस्याः परिपृच्छन्त्या वधं मित्रबलस्य ते।
तव चाख्यास्यते नूनं निशायां राक्षसैर्वधम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: “To her, when she keenly inquires about you, he will undoubtedly communicate to her the extermination at night by the ogres of the army of your ally, Sugrīva, as well as your own death. (26)

verses.text:
सा त्वां सुप्तं हतं ज्ञात्वा मां च रक्षोगृहं गताम्।
हृदयेनावदीर्णेन न भविष्यति राघव॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Coming to know of your having been killed while asleep and of myself having found my way into the abode of the ogre, Rāvaṇa, she with a broken heart will not survive, O scion of Raghu! (27)

verses.text:
मम हेतोरनार्याया अनघः पार्थिवात्मजः।
रामः सागरमुत्तीर्य वीर्यवान् गोष्पदे हतः॥ २८॥
verses.m: “How strange that having crossed the sea on my account, unworthy as I am, Śrī Rāma, a sinless prince, who was full of valour, has been killed in the footprint of a cow (without any struggle). (28)

verses.text:
अहं दाशरथेनोढा मोहात् स्वकुलपांसनी।
आर्यपुत्रस्य रामस्य भार्या मृत्युरजायत॥ २९॥
verses.m: “The obloquy of my race, I was wedded by Śrī Rāma (a son of Daśaratha) through ignorance. The wife has eventually proved to be the death of Śrī Rāma, her consort, the son of a worthy father! (29)

verses.text:
नूनमन्यां मया जातिं वारितं दानमुत्तमम्।
याहमद्यैव शोचामि भार्या सर्वातिथेरिह॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Undoubtedly in some other brith a supreme gift, viz., the gift of a girl in marriage, was obstructed by me in that I, the consort of one who was hospitable to all, grieve even at this age on this spot. (30)

verses.text:
साधु घातय मां क्षिप्रं रामस्योपरि रावण।
समानय पतिं पत्न्या कुरु कल्याणमुत्तमम्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Kill me at once by all means, laying me on the body of Śrī Rāma, O Rāvaṇa! Unite a husband with his wife and thus practise a supreme virtue. (31)

verses.text:
शिरसा मे शिरश्चास्य कायं कायेन योजय।
रावणानुगमिष्यामि गतिं भर्तुर्महात्मनः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Join my head with his head and my body with his body. I shall follow the way of my high-souled husband, O Rāvaṇa!” (32)

verses.text:
इतीव दुःखसंतप्ता विललापायतेक्षणा।
भर्तुः शिरो धनुश्चैव ददर्श जनकात्मजा॥ ३३॥
verses.m: In these words did the large-eyed daughter of Janaka lament, tormented as she was with agony, and looked on her husband’s head and bow. (33)

verses.text:
एवं लालप्यमानायां सीतायां तत्र राक्षसः।
अभिचक्राम भर्तारमनीकस्थः कृताञ्जलिः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: While Sītā was wailing, as aforesaid, an ogre guarding the gate approached his master, Rāvaṇa, on that spot with joined palms. (34)

verses.text:
विजयस्वार्यपुत्रेति सोऽभिवाद्य प्रसाद्य च।
न्यवेदयदनुप्राप्तं प्रहस्तं वाहिनीपतिम्॥ ३५॥
verses.m: Greeting Rāvaṇa with the words “Be victorious, my lord !” and thereby winning his pleasure, the ogre reported to him in the following words about Prahasta, the Commander-in-Chief, having arrived: (35)

verses.text:
अमात्यैः सहितः सर्वैः प्रहस्तस्त्वामुपस्थितः।
तेन दर्शनकामेन अहं प्रस्थापितः प्रभो॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “Accompanied by all the ministers, Prahasta has sought your presence. I have been dispatched by him, eager as he is to see you, my lord! (36)

verses.text:
नूनमस्ति महाराज राजभावात् क्षमान्वित।
किंचिदात्ययिकं कार्यं तेषां त्वं दर्शनं कुरु॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “Surely there is some urgent work, O great monarch endowed with forgiveness as a mark of royalty, therefore, be pleased to see them.” (37)

verses.text:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा दशग्रीवो राक्षसप्रतिवेदितम्।
अशोकवनिकां त्यक्त्वा मन्त्रिणां दर्शनं ययौ॥ ३८॥
verses.m: Leaving the Aśoka grove on hearing the aforesaid submission of the ogre, Rāvaṇa (the ten-headed monster) left to see the counsellors. (38)

verses.text:
स तु सर्वं समर्थ्यैव मन्त्रिभिः कृत्यमात्मनः।
सभां प्रविश्य विदधे विदित्वा रामविक्रमम्॥ ३९॥
verses.m: Having come to know the prowess of Śrī Rāma, nay, entering the council-chamber and deciding upon his course of action in consultation with his counsellors, Rāvaṇa for his part proceeded to act accordingly. (39)

verses.text:
अन्तर्धानं तु तच्छीर्षं तच्च कार्मुकमुत्तमम्।
जगाम रावणस्यैव निर्याणसमनन्तरम्॥ ४०॥
verses.m: Immediately after the departure of Rāvaṇa, the aforesaid (illusory) head as well as that excellent bow vanished. (40)

verses.text:
राक्षसेन्द्रस्तु तैः सार्धं मन्त्रिभिर्भीमविक्रमैः।
समर्थयामास तदा रामकार्यविनिश्चयम्॥ ४१॥
verses.m: In consultation with the aforesaid counsellors of terrible prowess, Rāvaṇa (the ruler of ogres) for his part then arrived at a definite conclusion regarding the course of action to be taken against Śrī Rāma. (41)

verses.text:
अविदूरस्थितान् सर्वान् बलाध्यक्षान् हितैषिणः।
अब्रवीत् कालसदृशं रावणो राक्षसाधिपः॥ ४२॥
verses.m: Rāvaṇa, the suzerain lord of ogres, thereupon spoke in the following opprotune words to all the troop commanders, who wished him well and stood not very far from him: (42)

verses.text:
शीघ्रं भेरीनिनादेन स्फुटं कोणाहतेन मे।
समानयध्वं सैन्यानि वक्तव्यं च न कारणम्॥ ४३॥
verses.m: “Speedily collect in my presence the forces through the sounding of kettledrums, produced by beating them with drum-sticks. The reason for collecting the forces should not, however, be pointed out.” (43)

verses.text:
ततस्तथेति प्रतिगृह्य तद्वच-
स्तदैव दूताः सहसा महद् बलम्।
समानयंश्चैव समागतं च
न्यवेदयन् भर्तरि युद्धकाङ् क्षिणि॥ ४४॥
verses.m: Bowing to his command in the words “Amen!”, the envoys, who were present there, thereupon immediately collected a huge army in an unpremeditated way and further reported to their bellicose lord about the army having assembled. (44)

verses.text:
सीतां तु मोहितां दृष्ट्वा सरमा नाम राक्षसी।
आससादाथ वैदेहीं प्रियां प्रणयिनी सखीम्॥ १॥
verses.m: Seeing Sītā distraught, an ogress, Saramā* by name, for her part, who was full of love for Sītā, forthwith approached the princess of the Videha territory, her beloved friend. (1)

verses.text:
मोहितां राक्षसेन्द्रेण सीतां परमदुःखिताम्।
आश्वासयामास तदा सरमा मृदुभाषिणी॥ २॥
verses.m: Saramā, who was sweet of expression, then comforted Sītā, who, having been put off the scent by Rāvaṇa (the ruler of ogres), was feeling extremely distressed. (2)

verses.text:
सा हि तत्र कृता मित्रं सीतया रक्ष्यमाणया।
रक्षन्ती रावणादिष्टा सानुक्रोशा दृढव्रता॥ ३॥
verses.m: Taking care, as she did, of Sītā, as enjoined by Rāvaṇa (who was afraid lest Sītā might succumb to her grief, which was too much for her), nay, full of compassion and firm of resolve, she had actually been made friends with by Sītā, who was being taken care of by her. (3)

verses.text:
सा ददर्श सखी सीतां सरमा नष्टचेतनाम्।
उपावृत्योत्थितां ध्वस्तां वडवामिव पांसुषु॥ ४॥
verses.m: Saramā, that friendly lady, found Sītā stupefied and just risen, as it were, after rolling in the dust and soiled like a mare. (4)

verses.text:
तां समाश्वासयामास सखीस्नेहेन सुव्रताम्।
समाश्वसिहि वैदेहि मा भूत् ते मनसो व्यथा।
उक्ता यद् रावणेन त्वं प्रयुक्तश्च स्वयं त्वया॥ ५॥
सखीस्नेहेन तद् भीरु मया सर्वं प्रतिश्रुतम्।
लीनया गहने शून्ये भयमुत्सृज्य रावणात्।
तव हेतोर्विशालाक्षि नहि मे रावणाद् भयम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Out of affection for her friend, Saramā began to console that princess of noble vows as follows: “Be fully restored to confidence, O princess of the Videha territory! Let there be no anguish in your mind. All that which you were told by Rāvaṇa and that which he was told in return by yourself was overheard by me out of affection for my friend, viz., yourself, while remaining concealed in a lonely thicket for your sake, O large-eyed lady, and shaking of all fear of Rāvaṇa; really speaking, I have no fear of Rāvaṇa (5-6)

verses.text:
स सम्भ्रान्तश्च निष्क्रान्तो यत्कृते राक्षसेश्वरः।
तत्र मे विदितं सर्वमभिनिष्क्रम्य मैथिलि॥ ७॥
verses.m: “The reason for which that ruler of ogres has sallied forth agitated has also been ascertained by me on the spot after going out, O princess of Mithilā ! (7)

verses.text:
न शक्यं सौप्तिकं कर्तुं रामस्य विदितात्मनः।
वधश्च पुरुषव्याघ्रे तस्मिन् नैवोपपद्यते॥ ८॥
verses.m: “It is not at all possible to kill Śrī Rāma, a knower of his Self, while he is asleep. Nay, even death is not possible in the case of that tiger among men. (8)

verses.text:
न त्वेवं वानरा हन्तुं शक्याः पादपयोधिनः।
सुरा देवर्षभेणेव रामेण हि सुरक्षिताः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Fighting, as they do, with trees, the monkeys too are not capable of being killed in that wise inasmuch as they stand fully protected by Śrī Rāma even as gods are by Indra, the foremost of gods. (9)

verses.text:
दीर्घवृत्तभुजः श्रीमान् महोरस्कः प्रतापवान्।
धन्वी संनहनोपेतो धर्मात्मा भुवि विश्रुतः॥ १०॥
विक्रान्तो रक्षिता नित्यमात्मनश्च परस्य च।
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा कुलीनो नयशास्त्रवित्॥ ११॥
हन्ता परबलौघानामचिन्त्यबलपौरुषः।
न हतो राघवः श्रीमान् सीते शत्रुनिबर्हणः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Endowed with long rounded arms, a broad chest and a muscular body, the glorious and triumphant Śrī Rāma, an archer well-known in the world, the exterminator of hostile armies and the destroyer of his foes—who is full of fire and valour, whose mind is set on virtue, who, with his younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa, is ever capable of defending himself as well as others, is well-born and well-versed in the science of politics and is possessed of inconceivable might and manliness, has not been killed, O Sītā! (10—12)

verses.text:
अयुक्तबुद्धिकृत्येन सर्वभूतविरोधिना।
एवं प्रयुक्ता रौद्रेण माया मायाविना त्वयि॥ १३॥
verses.m: “In this way a conjuring trick was played on you by the cruel Rāvaṇa, who is skilled in employing conjuring tricks, who is perverse in thought and action and is antagonistic to all created beings. (13)

verses.text:
शोकस्ते विगतः सर्वकल्याणं त्वामुपस्थितम्।
ध्रुवं त्वां भजते लक्ष्मीः प्रियं ते भवति शृणु॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Your grief is now gone once for all, nay, every form of goodluck awaits you. Prosperity will surely attend on you and something agreeable is going to happen to you, hark! (14)

verses.text:
उत्तीर्य सागरं रामः सह वानरसेनया।
संनिविष्टः समुद्रस्य तीरमासाद्य दक्षिणम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Having crossed the sea alongwith the army of monkeys and reached its southern shore, Śrī Rāma is settled in camp there. (15)

verses.text:
दृष्टो मे परिपूर्णार्थः काकुत्स्थः सहलक्ष्मणः।
सहितैः सागरान्तस्थैर्बलैस्तिष्ठति रक्षितः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Śrī Rāma, a scion of Kakutstha, who stands fully accomplished of purpose, has been seen by me with Lakṣmaṇa. He stands protected by troops gathered together and stationed on the seashore. (16)

verses.text:
अनेन प्रेषिता ये च राक्षसा लघुविक्रमाः।
राघवस्तीर्ण इत्येवं प्रवृत्तिस्तैरिहाहृता॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Nay, by the swift-footed ogres, who were dispatched by Rāvaṇa, this very intelligence has been brought here that Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, has crossed the sea. (17)

verses.text:
स तां श्रुत्वा विशालाक्षि प्रवृत्तिं राक्षसाधिपः।
एष मन्त्रयते सर्वैः सचिवैः सह रावणः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Hearing the aforesaid news, O large-eyed lady, yonder Rāvaṇa, the suzerain lord of ogres, is busy holding consultation with all his ministers.” (18)

verses.text:
इति ब्रुवाणा सरमा राक्षसी सीतया सह।
सर्वोद्योगेन सैन्यानां शब्दं शुश्राव भैरवम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: While talking thus with Sītā, the ogress Saramā heard the terrible noise of troops engaged in every effort for war. (19)

verses.text:
दण्डनिर्घातवादिन्याः श्रुत्वा भेर्या महास्वनम्।
उवाच सरमा सीतामिदं मधुरभाषिणी॥ २०॥
verses.m: Hearing the crash of kettledrums sounding when beaten with a stick, Saramā, who had a sweet tongue, spoke to Sītā as follows: (20)

verses.text:
संनाहजननी ह्येषा भैरवा भीरु भेरिका।
भेरीनादं च गम्भीरं शृणु तोयदनिःस्वनम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Indeed, here is a fearful kettledrum, producing a sound signifying preparations for war, being beaten, O timid lady! Also hear the deep-sounding crash of kettledrums, which resembles the rumbling of clouds. (21)

verses.text:
कल्प्यन्ते मत्तमातङ्गा युज्यन्ते रथवाजिनः।
दृश्यन्ते तुरगारूढाः प्रासहस्ताः सहस्रशः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Elephants in rut are being decorated and horses are being yoked to the chariots. Nay, carrying spears in their hands, horsemen are seen in their thousands. (22)

verses.text:
तत्र तत्र च संनद्धाः सम्पतन्ति सहस्रशः।
आपूर्यन्ते राजमार्गाः सैन्यैरद्भुतदर्शनैः॥ २३॥
वेगवद्भिर्नदद्भिश्च तोयौघैरिव सागरः।
शस्त्राणां च प्रसन्नानां चर्मणां वर्मणां तथा॥ २४॥
रथवाजिगजानां च राक्षसेन्द्रानुयायिनाम्।
सम्भ्रमो रक्षसामेष हृषितानां तरस्विनाम्॥ २५॥
प्रभां विसृजतां पश्य नानावर्णसमुत्थिताम्।
वनं निर्दहतो घर्मे यथा रूपं विभावसोः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Prepared for a fight, warriors are rushing hither and thither in their thousands. Nay, the principal roads are getting choked with roaring troops presenting a weird appearance and full of impetuosity, even as sea is filled with streams of water. Look at the sheen of polished weapons, shields and coats of mail, sending forth a lustre of many hues resembling the splendour of fire consuming a forest in summer. And here is seen the flurry of chariots, horses and elephants following the lead of Rāvaṇa (the ruler of ogres) as well as of ogres thrilled with joy and full of impetuosity. (23—26)

verses.text:
घण्टानां शृणु निर्घोषं रथानां शृणु निःस्वनम्।
हयानां हेषमाणानां शृणु तूर्यध्वनिं तथा॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Hear the ringing of bells, also hear the rattling of chariots, nay, listen to the cry of neighing horses as also to the flourish of trumpets. (27)

verses.text:
उद्यतायुधहस्तानां राक्षसेन्द्रानुयायिनाम्।
सम्भ्रमो रक्षसामेष तुमुलो लोमहर्षणम्॥ २८॥
श्रीस्त्वां भजति शोकघ्नी रक्षसां भयमागतम्।
रामः कमलपत्राक्षो दैत्यानामिव वासवः॥ २९॥
अवजित्य जितक्रोधस्तमचिन्त्यपराक्रमः।
रावणं समरे हत्वा भर्ता त्वाधिगमिष्यति॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Here is the bustle of ogres carrying uplifted weapons in their hands and following the lead of Rāvaṇa (the lord of ogres). Good fortune, which will bring your grief to an end, awaits you and a danger, which will make one’s hair stand on end, threatens the ogres. Vanquishing and killing the notorious Rāvaṇa in combat, even as Indra vanquished the Daityas, your husband, Śrī Rāma, whose eyes resemble the petals of a lotus, nay, who has conquered anger and whose prowess is inconceivable, will win you back. (28-30)

verses.text:
विक्रमिष्यति रक्षःसु भर्ता ते सहलक्ष्मणः।
यथा शत्रुषु शत्रुघ्नो विष्णुना सह वासवः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa, your husband will show his valour against the ogres, even as Indra, the destroyer of his foes, exhibited his prowess against his enemies (the demons) alongwith Lord Viṣṇu, who descended as his younger brother. (31)

verses.text:
आगतस्य हि रामस्य क्षिप्रमङ्कागतां सतीम्।
अहं द्रक्ष्यामि सिद्धार्थां त्वां शत्रौ विनिपातिते॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “On the enemy being killed, I shall soon behold you, a virtuous lady, mounted on the lap of Śrī Rāma, actually arrived, your object being thus accomplished. (32)

verses.text:
अस्राण्यानन्दजानि त्वं वर्तयिष्यसि जानकि।
समागम्य परिष्वक्ता तस्योरसि महोरसः॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “Hugged by him on getting united with him, you will shed tears of joy, O daughter of Janaka, on the bosom of that broad-chested prince. (33)

verses.text:
अचिरान्मोक्ष्यते सीते देवि ते जघनं गताम्।
धृतामेकां बहून् मासान् वेणीं रामो महाबलः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “Śrī Rāma, who is endowed with extraordinary might, will before long disentangle your single plait, which has been worn by you for many months past and has reached your very hinder part, O godlike Sītā! (34)

verses.text:
तस्य दृष्ट्वा मुखं देवि पूर्णचन्द्रमिवोदितम्।
मोक्ष्यसे शोकजं वारि निर्मोकमिव पन्नगी॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “Beholding his countenance resembling the full moon just risen, O godlike lady, you will bid adieu to tears of grief even as the female snake casts off its slough. (35)

verses.text:
रावणं समरे हत्वा नचिरादेव मैथिलि।
त्वया समग्रः प्रियया सुखार्हो लप्स्यते सुखम्॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “Killing Rāvaṇa in combat before long, O princess of Mithilā, Śrī Rāma, who deserves felicity, will enjoy happiness in the company of his darling, viz., yourself, his desire being fulfilled. (36)

verses.text:
सभाजिता त्वं रामेण मोदिष्यसि महात्मना।
सुवर्षेण समायुक्ता यथा सस्येन मेदिनी॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “Honoured by the high-souled Śrī Rāma, you will rejoice in the same way as the earth becomes green with crops when blessed with a copious downpour. (37)

verses.text:
गिरिवरमभितो विवर्तमानो
हय इव मण्डलमाशु यः करोति।
तमिह शरणमभ्युपैहि देवि
दिवसकरं प्रभवो ह्ययं प्रजानाम्॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “Seek at this juncture as your refuge the well-known sun-god (lit., he who brings the day), who, while coursing round the Meru (the foremost of mountains), revolves quickly like a horse, for he is the source of joy and suffering of all created beings.” (38)

verses.text:
अथ तां जातसंतापां तेन वाक्येन मोहिताम्।
सरमा ह्लादयामास महीं दग्धामिवाम्भसा॥ १॥
verses.m: In this way Saramā gladdened Sītā, who had been put off the scent by the aforesaid speech of Rāvaṇa and had felt agonized, even as the monsoon would gladden the parched earth with water (in the shape of rain). (1)

verses.text:
ततस्तस्या हितं सख्याश्चिकीर्षन्ती सखी वचः।
उवाच काले कालज्ञा स्मितपूर्वाभिभाषिणी॥ २॥
verses.m: Wishing to do a good turn to her friend, Sītā, Saramā (who was her friend), who knew the time when a thing should be done and always smiled before she opened her lips, then spoke in time as follows: (2)

verses.text:
उत्सहेयमहं गत्वा त्वद्वाक्यमसितेक्षणे।
निवेद्य कुशलं रामे प्रतिच्छन्ना निवर्तितुम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Going to the presence of Śrī Rāma and delivering your message as well as communicating your welfare to Śrī Rāma, I can come back hidden from view, O dark-eyed lady! (3)

verses.text:
नहि मे क्रममाणाया निरालम्बे विहायसि।
समर्थो गतिमन्वेतुं पवनो गरुडोऽपि वा॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Neither the wind nor even Garuḍa (the king of winged creatures and the carrier of Lord Viṣṇu) will be able to follow my movement even as I course in the sky extending without any support.” (4)

verses.text:
एवं ब्रुवाणां तां सीता सरमामिदमब्रवीत्।
मधुरं श्लक्ष्णया वाचा पूर्वशोकाभिपन्नया॥ ५॥
verses.m: To the aforesaid Saramā, who was speaking in this strain, Sītā sweetly replied as follows in gentle tones, overcome by former grief : (5)

verses.text:
समर्था गगनं गन्तुमपि च त्वं रसातलम्।
अवगच्छाद्य कर्तव्यं कर्तव्यं ते मदन्तरे॥ ६॥
verses.m: “You are capable of ascending to the heavens and even of descending to the penultimate subterranean region. Know from me today the duty which has got to be performed by you with regard to myself. (6)

verses.text:
मत्प्रियं यदि कर्तव्यं यदि बुद्धिः स्थिरा तव।
ज्ञातुमिच्छामि तं गत्वा किं करोतीति रावणः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “If what is pleasing to me must be done by you, and if your resolve is firm, I wish to know what Rāvaṇa is doing now. Approaching him, let me know this. (7)

verses.text:
स हि मायाबलः क्रूरो रावणः शत्रुरावणः।
मां मोहयति दुष्टात्मा पीतमात्रेव वारुणी॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Rāvaṇa, who makes his enemies cry by his tyranny, is indeed cruel and is equipped with strength in the shape of conjuring tricks. The evil-minded fellow has confounded me in the same way as spirituous liquor confounds one the moment it is imbibed. (8)

verses.text:
तर्जापयति मां नित्यं भर्त्सापयति चासकृत्।
राक्षसीभिः सुघोराभिर्यो मां रक्षति नित्यशः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “He causes me to be threatened all the time and snubbed off and on by most frightful ogresses, and keeps watch on me everyday. (9)

verses.text:
उद्विग्ना शङ्किता चास्मि न स्वस्थं च मनो मम।
तद्भयाच्चाहमुद्विग्ना अशोकवनिकां गता॥ १०॥
verses.m: “I remain perturbed and apprehensive, and my mind is not at ease. Nay, even though living in the Aśoka grove (far from his view), I continue to be agitated through fear of him. (10)

verses.text:
यदि नाम कथा तस्य निश्चितं वापि यद् भवेत्।
निवेदयेथाः सर्वं तद् वरो मे स्यादनुग्रहः॥ ११॥
verses.m: “If his talk is going on with his ministers about releasing me or keeping me confined, report to me all that is decided. That would be a great act of kindness to me.” (11)

verses.text:
साप्येवं ब्रुवतीं सीतां सरमा मृदुभाषिणी।
उवाच वदनं तस्याः स्पृशन्ती बाष्पविक्लवम्॥ १२॥
एष ते यद्यभिप्रायस्तस्माद् गच्छामि जानकि।
गृह्य शत्रोरभिप्रायमुपावर्तामि मैथिलि॥ १३॥
verses.m: Wiping Sītā’s face covered with tears, Saramā too, who was gentle of expression, replied as follows to the former, who was hitherto speaking as aforesaid: “If such is your will, I leave in that case, O daughter of Janaka! Discovering the enemy’s mind, I shall presently return, O princess of Mithilā!” (12-13)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा ततो गत्वा समीपं तस्य रक्षसः।
शुश्राव कथितं तस्य रावणस्य समन्त्रिणः॥ १४॥
verses.m: Saying so, and then moving to the presence of that ogre, she overheard the talk of the said Rāvaṇa as well as of his ministers. (14)

verses.text:
सा श्रुत्वा निश्चयं तस्य निश्चयज्ञा दुरात्मनः।
पुनरेवागमत् क्षिप्रमशोकवनिकां शुभाम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Having overheard the decision of that evil-minded fellow and understood it, she hastened once more to the charming Aśoka grove. (15)

verses.text:
सा प्रविष्टा ततस्तत्र ददर्श जनकात्मजाम्।
प्रतीक्षमाणां स्वामेव भ्रष्टपद्मामिव श्रियम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: Having made good her entry in that grove, she then saw the daughter of Janaka waiting for her alone like Lakṣmī (the goddess of fortune and the spouse of Lord Viṣṇu) without the lotus. (16)

verses.text:
तां तु सीता पुनः प्राप्तां सरमां प्रियभाषिणीम्।
परिष्वज्य च सुस्निग्धं ददौ च स्वयमासनम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: Embracing Saramā, who always spoke kindly to Sītā, and who had just come back, Sītā for her part personally and most tenderly offered her seat, saying: (17)

verses.text:
इहासीना सुखं सर्वमाख्याहि मम तत्त्वतः।
क्रूरस्य निश्चयं तस्य रावणस्य दुरात्मनः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Seated here at ease, communicate to me accurately in toto the decision of that cruel and evil-minded Rāvaṇa.” (18)

verses.text:
एवमुक्ता तु सरमा सीतया वेपमानया।
कथितं सर्वमाचष्ट रावणस्य समन्त्रिणः॥ १९॥
verses.m: Requested in these words by Sītā, who was trembling all the while, Saramā for her part reproduced to her all the talk of Rāvaṇa as well as of his ministers in the following words: (19)

verses.text:
जनन्या राक्षसेन्द्रो वै त्वन्मोक्षार्थं बृहद्वचः।
अतिस्निग्धेन वैदेहि मन्त्रिवृद्धेन चोदितः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Rāvaṇa, the ruler of ogres, O princess of the Videha territory, was actually tendered a lengthy advice in favour of discharging you by his own mother, Kaikasī, as well as by an exceedingly affectionate and aged counsellor. (20)

verses.text:
दीयतामभिसत्कृत्य मनुजेन्द्राय मैथिली।
निदर्शनं ते पर्याप्तं जनस्थाने यदद्भुतम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: (They said) ‘Let Sītā, a princess of Mithilā, be restored to Rāma (a ruler of men) after receiving him hospitably. The astonishing exploit which was performed by him in Janasthāna (in the shape of exterminating fourteen thousand ogres led by such great warriors as Khara and Dūṣaṇa) should serve as a sufficient eye-opener to you. (21)

verses.text:
लङ्घनं च समुद्रस्य दर्शनं च हनूमतः।
वधं च रक्षसां युद्धे कः कुर्यान्मानुषो युधि॥ २२॥
verses.m: ‘What mortal could leap across the sea, discover Sītā and destroy the ogres in combat, which was accomplished by Hanumān?’ (22)

verses.text:
एवं स मन्त्रिवृद्धैश्च मात्रा च बहुबोधितः।
न त्वामुत्सहते मोक्तुमर्थमर्थपरो यथा॥ २३॥
verses.m: Even though exhorted at length in the foregoing words by elderly counsellors as well as by his own mother, Rāvaṇa is not inclined to set you free any more than a miser would leave his hold on his treasure. (23)

verses.text:
नोत्सहत्यमृतो मोक्तुं युद्धे त्वामिति मैथिलि।
सामात्यस्य नृशंसस्य निश्चयो ह्येष वर्तते॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Rāvaṇa is not prepared to leave you unless he gives up his ghost in combat, O princess of Mithilā! Such indeed is the resolve of the ruthless ogre made in consultation with his ministers. (24)

verses.text:
तदेषा सुस्थिरा बुद्धिर्मृत्युलोभादुपस्थिता।
भयान्न शक्तस्त्वां मोक्तुमनिरस्तः स संयुगे॥ २५॥
राक्षसानां च सर्वेषामात्मनश्च वधेन हि।
निहत्य रावणं संख्ये सर्वथा निशितैः शरैः।
प्रतिनेष्यति रामस्त्वामयोध्यामसितेक्षणे॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Therefore, due to infatuation caused by his impending death, his aforesaid determination is very steady. Unless and until he is actually frustrated in combat through the extermination of all the ogres as well as of himself, he will not be able to leave you through sheer fear. Wiping out Rāvaṇa with his sharp arrows in combat, Śrī Rāma will take you back to Ayodhyā, O dark-eyed lady!” (25-26)

verses.text:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे शब्दो भेरीशङ्खसमाकुलः।
श्रुतो वै सर्वसैन्यानां कम्पयन् धरणीतलम्॥ २७॥
verses.m: In the meantime was actually heard the clamour of all the monkey troops, blended with the roll of kettledrums and the blast of conches, causing the earth to shake. (27)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा तु तं वानरसैन्यनादं
लङ्कागता राक्षसराजभृत्याः।
हतौजसो दैन्यपरीतचेष्टाः
श्रेयो न पश्यन्ति नृपस्य दोषात्॥ २८॥
verses.m: Hearing the tumult of the monkey forces, the servants of Rāvaṇa (the ruler of ogres) present in Laṅkā felt debilitated and their movements were overcome by depression. Owing to the folly of their ruler they did not see any prospect of prosperity. (28)

verses.text:
तेन शङ्खविमिश्रेण भेरीशब्देन नादिना।
उपयाति महाबाहू रामः परपुरंजयः॥ १॥
verses.m: With the resonant roll of kettledrums blended with the blast of conches the mighty-armed Śrī Rāma, the conqueror of hostile cities, sallied forth against Laṅkā. (1)

verses.text:
तं निनादं निशम्याथ रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः।
मुहूर्तं ध्यानमास्थाय सचिवानभ्युदैक्षत॥ २॥
verses.m: Reflecting awhile on hearing that tumult, Rāvaṇa, the ruler of ogres, now looked at his ministers. (2)

verses.text:
अथ तान् सचिवांस्तत्र सर्वानाभाष्य रावणः।
सभां संनादयन् सर्वामित्युवाच महाबलः॥ ३॥
जगत्संतापनः क्रूरोऽगर्हयन् राक्षसेश्वरः।
तरणं सागरस्यास्य विक्रमं बलपौरुषम्॥ ४॥
यदुक्तवन्तो रामस्य भवन्तस्तन्मया श्रुतम्।
भवतश्चाप्यहं वेद्मि युद्धे सत्यपराक्रमान्।
तूष्णीकानीक्षतोऽन्योन्यं विदित्वा रामविक्रमम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Addressing all the aforesaid ministers present there and causing the entire council-chamber to resound, Rāvaṇa, the cruel ruler of ogres and the scourge of the entire world, who was endowed with extraordinary might, spoke as follows, reproaching none: “That which you have said about Rāma’s crossing the yonder sea, his prowess, might and virility has been heard by me. Nay, I know you too—who on coming to know of Rāma’s prowess, stand mute, looking at one another—to be of unfailing prowess on the field of battle.” (3—5)

verses.text:
ततस्तु सुमहाप्राज्ञो माल्यवान् नाम राक्षसः।
रावणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा इति मातामहोऽब्रवीत्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Hearing the speech of Rāvaṇa, an ogre Mālyavān by name, his maternal grandfather, for his part, who was exceptionally sagacious, then submitted as follows: (6)

verses.text:
विद्यास्वभिविनीतो यो राजा राजन् नयानुगः।
स शास्ति चिरमैश्वर्यमरींश्च कुरुते वशे॥ ७॥
verses.m: “That monarch, O king, who is well-versed in the fourteen sciences and follows the path of prudence, enjoys sovereignty for a long time and brings his enemies under subjection. (7)

verses.text:
संदधानो हि कालेन विगृह्णंश्चारिभिः सह।
स्वपक्षे वर्धनं कुर्वन्महदैश्वर्यमश्नुते॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Concluding peace or contending with his enemies as occasion demands, and strengthening his own party, a ruler enjoys great power. (8)

verses.text:
हीयमानेन कर्तव्यो राज्ञा संधिः समेन च।
न शत्रुमवमन्येत ज्यायान् कुर्वीत विग्रहम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Peace should be concluded by a ruler who is losing strength as well as by him who is equally matched in strength with his enemy. He should in no case under-rate his enemy and should wage war against him if he is superior in strength to his enemy. (9)

verses.text:
तन्मह्यं रोचते संधिः सह रामेण रावण।
यदर्थमभियुक्तोऽसि सीता तस्मै प्रदीयताम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Therefore, O Rāvaṇa, alliance with Rāma finds favour with me. Let Sītā, for whose sake you have been attacked by him, be restored to him. (10)

verses.text:
तस्य देवर्षयः सर्वे गन्धर्वाश्च जयैषिणः।
विरोधं मा गमस्तेन संधिस्ते तेन रोचताम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Celestial sages as well as Gandharvas (heavenly musicians) all wish him victory. Therefore, do not antagonize him; let an alliance with him find favour with you. (11)

verses.text:
असृजद् भगवान् पक्षौ द्वावेव हि पितामहः।
सुराणामसुराणां च धर्माधर्मौ तदाश्रयौ॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Indeed, the glorious Brahmā, the grandfather of the universe, which owes its existence to his mind-born sons, the ten Prajāpatis, evolved only two orders of creation, the celestial order and the devilish order. They take their stand on virtue and vice respectively. (12)

verses.text:
धर्मो हि श्रूयते पक्ष अमराणां महात्मनाम्।
अधर्मो रक्षसां पक्षो ह्यसुराणां च राक्षस॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Virtue is actually known to be the sheet-anchor of the high-souled immortals; while unrighteousness indeed is the sheet-anchor of ogres as well as of demons, O ogre! (13)

verses.text:
धर्मो वै ग्रसतेऽधर्मं यदा कृतमभूद् युगम्।
अधर्मो ग्रसते धर्मं यदा तिष्यः प्रवर्तते॥ १४॥
verses.m: “When Satya Yuga prevails, virtue actually eclipses evil. When, on the other hand, the Kali age prevails, evil swallows up virtue. (14)

verses.text:
तत् त्वया चरता लोकान् धर्मोऽपि निहतो महान्।
अधर्मः प्रगृहीतश्च तेनास्मद् बलिनः परे॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Even virtue, which is so exalted, was struck at the root and evil embraced by you while ranging the worlds for conquest. Hence it is that our enemies, who have embraced virtue and renounced evil, are stronger than we. (15)

verses.text:
स प्रमादात् प्रवृद्धस्तेऽधर्मोऽहिर्ग्रसते हि नः।
विवर्धयति पक्षं च सुराणां सुरभावनः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Nourished through your error, the aforesaid python in the form of evil is actually going to swallow us up; while virtue which is being practised by the gods is promoting the cause of the gods in the form of the monkeys, who are all sprung from the loins of gods. (16)

verses.text:
विषयेषु प्रसक्तेन यत्किंचित्कारिणा त्वया।
ऋषीणामग्निकल्पानामुद्वेगो जनितो महान्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Great molestation was caused to the Ṛṣis (the seers of Vedic Mantras), who resemble the god of fire in brilliance, by you, who are devoted to the pleasures of sense and do whatever you please. (17)

verses.text:
तेषां प्रभावो दुर्धर्षः प्रदीप्त इव पावकः।
तपसा भावितात्मानो धर्मस्यानुग्रहे रताः॥ १८॥
मुख्यैर्यज्ञैर्यजन्त्येते तैस्तैर्यत्ते द्विजातयः।
जुह्वत्यग्नींश्च विधिवद् वेदांश्चोच्चैरधीयते॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Their power is difficult to overcome like a blazing fire. Having purified their self through asceticism, they are intent on acquiring virtue, inasmuch as these afore said Brāhmaṇas (lit., the members of the twice-born class) worship the Lord through different principal sacrifices, also pour oblations into the sacred fires with due ceremony and read the Vedas in a loud voice. (18-19)

verses.text:
अभिभूय च रक्षांसि ब्रह्मघोषानुदीरयन्।
दिशो विप्रद्रुताः सर्वाः स्तनयित्नुरिवोष्णगे॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Having subdued the ogres, they continued to chant the Vedas, on hearing which the former got scattered in all directions as clouds during the hot season. (20)

verses.text:
ऋषीणामग्निकल्पानामग्निहोत्रसमुत्थितः।
आदत्ते रक्षसां तेजो धूमो व्याप्य दिशो दश॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Enveloping the ten directions, the smoke risen from the oblations poured into the sacred fires by the Ṛṣis, who resemble the fire in brilliance, takes away the energy of the ogres. (21)

verses.text:
तेषु तेषु च देशेषु पुण्येष्वेव दृढव्रतैः।
चर्यमाणं तपस्तीव्रं संतापयति राक्षसान्॥ २२॥
verses.m: “The burning austerities which are being practised in the various sacred regions by Ṛṣis firm of resolve are tormenting the ogres. (22)

verses.text:
देवदानवयक्षेभ्यो गृहीतश्च वरस्त्वया।
मनुष्या वानरा ऋक्षा गोलाङ्गूला महाबलाः।
बलवन्त इहागम्य गर्जन्ति दृढविक्रमाः॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Nay, a boon has been secured by you of immunity from death at the hands of gods, demons and Yakṣas (a class of demigods); while human beings, monkeys, bears and Golāṅgūlas (a species of monkeys with dark faces and tails as long as the tail of a cow), full of might, leading a large army and endowed with unyielding prowess are thundering after coming here. (23)

verses.text:
उत्पातान् विविधान् दृष्ट्वा घोरान् बहुविधान् बहून्।
विनाशमनुपश्यामि सर्वेषां रक्षसामहम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Beholding numerous and multifarious dreadful portents foreboding evils of various kinds, I foresee the extermination of all the ogres. (24)

verses.text:
खराभिस्तनिता घोरा मेघाः प्रतिभयंकराः।
शोणितेनाभिवर्षन्ति लङ्कामुष्णेन सर्वतः॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Formidable clouds striking horror and emitting a harsh peal of thunder are drenching Laṅkā with hot blood on all sides. (25)

verses.text:
रुदतां वाहनानां च प्रपतन्त्यश्रुबिन्दवः।
रजोध्वस्ता विवर्णाश्च न प्रभान्ति यथापुरम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Tear-drops are falling from the eyes of weeping horses and elephants. Soiled with dust and discoloured, the quarters do not shine brightly as before. (26)

verses.text:
व्याला गोमायवो गृध्रा वाश्यन्ति च सुभैरवम्।
प्रविश्य लङ्कामारामे समवायांश्च कुर्वते॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Carnivorous animals, jackals and vultures are emitting exceedingly frightful shrieks; nay, penetrating deep into Laṅkā, they gather in gardens. (27)

verses.text:
कालिकाः पाण्डुरैर्दन्तैः प्रहसन्त्यग्रतः स्थिताः।
स्त्रियः स्वप्नेषु मुष्णन्त्यो गृहाणि प्रतिभाष्य च॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Pillaging the dwellings after uttering unpleasant notes, coal-black women with yellowish teeth stand before us in dreams laughing heartily. (28)

verses.text:
गृहाणां बलिकर्माणि श्वानः पर्युपभुञ्जते।
खरा गोषु प्रजायन्ते मूषका नकुलेषु च॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Dogs devour the offerings of food made to gods and other beings before the daily meal in houses. Donkeys are born of cows and rats of mongooses. (29)

verses.text:
मार्जारा द्वीपिभिः सार्धं सूकराः शुनकैः सह।
किंनरा राक्षसैश्चापि समेयुर्मानुषैः सह॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Cats mate with leopards, pigs with dogs and Kinnaras (a species of demigods with a human figure and the head of a horse or with a horse’s body and the head of a man) with ogres as well as with human beings. (30)

verses.text:
पाण्डुरा रक्तपादाश्च विहगाः कालचोदिताः।
राक्षसानां विनाशाय कपोता विचरन्ति च॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Nay, impelled by the Time-Spirit, white and red-footed doves move about in the air, boding the extermination of the ogres. (31)

verses.text:
चीचीकूचीति वाशन्त्यः शारिका वेश्मसु स्थिताः।
पतन्ति ग्रथिताश्चापि निर्जिताः कलहैषिभिः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Making a chirping sound, minas living in households grapple with other bellicose birds and, ultimately drop down vanquished by them. (32)

verses.text:
पक्षिणश्च मृगाः सर्वे प्रत्यादित्यं रुदन्ति ते।
करालो विकटो मुण्डः पुरुषः कृष्णपिङ्गलः॥ ३३॥
कालो गृहाणि सर्वेषां काले कालेऽन्ववेक्षते।
एतान्यन्यानि दुष्टानि निमित्तान्युत्पतन्ति च॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “Birds and beasts all utter plaintive cries, facing the sun. In the form of a frightful, monstrous blackish fellow with a shaven head, the Time-Spirit casts his eyes on the dwellings of us all at times. These and other sinister portents appear before us. (33-34)

verses.text:
विष्णुं मन्यामहे रामं मानुषं रूपमास्थितम्।
नहि मानुषमात्रोऽसौ राघवो दृढविक्रमः॥ ३५॥
येन बद्धः समुद्रे च सेतुः स परमाद्भुतः।
कुरुष्व नरराजेन संधिं रामेण रावण।
ज्ञात्वावधार्य कर्माणि क्रियतामायतिक्षमम्॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “We look upon Śrī Rāma as Lord Viṣṇu having assumed a human semblance. The aforesaid Śrī Rāma of unyielding prowess, by whom that most wonderful bridge has been constructed over the deep, is no mere human being. Therefore, conclude peace, O Rāvaṇa, with Śrī Rāma, a ruler of men. Having come to know of his exploits, as well as of the evil portents in Laṅkā, let that which is good for the future be done after mature consideration.” (35-36)

verses.text:
इदं वचस्तस्य निगद्य माल्यवान्
परीक्ष्य रक्षोधिपतेर्मनः पुनः।
अनुत्तमेषूत्तमपौरुषो बली
बभूव तूष्णीं समवेक्ष्य रावणम्॥ ३७॥
verses.m: Having tendered this salutary advice and sounding the mind of Rāvaṇa (the suzerain lord of ogres), once more, the mighty Mālyavān, who was foremost in virility among the foremost of his counsellors, became silent after eyeing him. (37)

verses.text:
तत् तु माल्यवतो वाक्यं हितमुक्तं दशाननः।
न मर्षयति दुष्टात्मा कालस्य वशमागतः॥ १॥
verses.m: The evil-minded Rāvaṇa (the ten-headed monster), who had fallen under the sway of Death could not for his part brook the salutary advice tendered by Mālyavān. (1)

verses.text:
स बद्ध्वा भ्रुकुटिं वक्त्रे क्रोधस्य वशमागतः।
अमर्षात् परिवृत्ताक्षो माल्यवन्तमथाब्रवीत्॥ २॥
verses.m: Knitting his brows on his face, Rāvaṇa, who had fallen a prey to anger, presently spoke as follows to Mālyavān, his eyes rolling through anger: (2)

verses.text:
हितबुद्ध्या यदहितं वचः परुषमुच्यते।
परपक्षं प्रविश्यैव नैतच्छ्रोत्रगतं मम॥ ३॥
verses.m: “This noxious and harsh utterance, which has been made by you, taking it to be salutary for me and taking sides with the enemy, has not caught my ears. (3)

verses.text:
मानुषं कृपणं राममेकं शाखामृगाश्रयम्।
समर्थं मन्यसे केन त्यक्तं पित्रा वनाश्रयम्॥ ४॥
रक्षसामीश्वरं मां च देवानां च भयंकरम्।
हीनं मां मन्यसे केन अहीनं सर्वविक्रमैः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “On what grounds do you hold as powerful Rāma, a forlorn, wretched human being, who, having been forsaken by his father, has sought the protection of monkeys and has found his asylum in the forest? And how do you consider as deficient me, the ruler of ogres, the terror of gods, and endowed with all kinds of prowess? (4-5)

verses.text:
वीरद्वेषेण वा शङ्के पक्षपातेन वा रिपोः।
त्वयाहं परुषाण्युक्तो परप्रोत्साहनेन वा॥ ६॥
verses.m: “I fear I have been told such harsh words by you either because of spitefulness to me, an illustrious warrior, or because of your predilection to the foe or because you were incited by the enemy to do so. (6)

verses.text:
प्रभवन्तं पदस्थं हि परुषं कोऽभिभाषते।
पण्डितः शास्त्रतत्त्वज्ञो विना प्रोत्साहनेन वा॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Indeed without such instigation what learned man, who has grasped the truth of the scriptures would address harsh words to a mighty man still in power? (7)

verses.text:
आनीय च वनात् सीतां पद्महीनामिव श्रियम्।
किमर्थं प्रतिदास्यामि राघवस्य भयादहम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Nay, having borne away from the forest Sītā, who is like Lakṣmī (the goddess of fortune) without the lotus, wherefore shall I give her back through fear of Rāma (a scion of Raghu)? (8)

verses.text:
वृतं वानरकोटीभिः ससुग्रीवं सलक्ष्मणम्।
पश्य कैश्चिदहोभिश्च राघवं निहतं मया॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Nay, see Rāma (a scion of Raghu) killed by me in a few days alongwith Sugrīva and Lakṣmaṇa in the midst of crores of monkeys. (9)

verses.text:
द्वन्द्वे यस्य न तिष्ठन्ति दैवतान्यपि संयुगे।
स कस्माद् रावणो युद्धे भयमाहारयिष्यति॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Of whom will Rāvaṇa entertain fear in an encounter—Rāvaṇa, whom even gods dare not withstand in a duel? (10)

verses.text:
द्विधा भज्येयमप्येवं न नमेयं तु कस्यचित्।
एष मे सहजो दोषः स्वभावो दुरतिक्रमः॥ ११॥
verses.m: “I would fain break into two but would never bend before anyone. This is my inherent weakness. Nature is hard to overcome. (11)

verses.text:
यदि तावत् समुद्रे तु सेतुर्बद्धो यदृच्छया।
रामेण विस्मयः कोऽत्र येन ते भयमागतम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “If at all by chance a bridge has been thrown over the sea by Rāma, what marvel is there in it due to which fear has taken possession of you ? (12)

verses.text:
स तु तीर्त्वार्णवं रामः सह वानरसेनया।
प्रतिजानामि ते सत्यं न जीवन् प्रतियास्यति॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Having crossed the sea alongwith an army of monkeys, Rāma, however, will not be able to return alive: I truly promise to you.” (13)

verses.text:
एवं ब्रुवाणं संरब्धं रुष्टं विज्ञाय रावणम्।
व्रीडितो माल्यवान् वाक्यं नोत्तरं प्रत्यपद्यत॥ १४॥
verses.m: Abashed to find Rāvaṇa full of keenness for war and offended while speaking, as aforesaid, Mālyavān made no reply. (14)

verses.text:
जयाशिषा तु राजानं वर्धयित्वा यथोचितम्।
माल्यवानभ्यनुज्ञातो जगाम स्वं निवेशनम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Having cheered the king with benedictions of triumph in accordance with the rules of propriety, and duly permitted by him, Mālyavān for his part withdrew to his own residence. (15)

verses.text:
रावणस्तु सहामात्यो मन्त्रयित्वा विमृश्य च।
लङ्कायास्तु तदा गुप्तिं कारयामास राक्षसः॥ १६॥
verses.m: Having deliberated with his ministers and reflected awhile, the ogre Rāvaṇa for his part then actually made adequate arrangements for the defence of Laṅkā. (16)

verses.text:
व्यादिदेश च पूर्वस्यां प्रहस्तं द्वारि राक्षसम्।
दक्षिणस्यां महावीर्यौ महापार्श्वमहोदरौ॥ १७॥
पश्चिमायामथ द्वारि पुत्रमिन्द्रजितं तदा।
व्यादिदेश महामायं राक्षसैर्बहुभिर्वृतम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: He then posted the ogre Prahasta at the eastern gate, Mahāpārśwa and Mahodara, who were both endowed with extraordinary virility, at the southern and posted his eldest son, Indrajit, who was a great conjurer and was surrounded by numerous ogres, at the western gate at that juncture. (17-18)

verses.text:
उत्तरस्यां पुरद्वारि व्यादिश्य शुकसारणौ।
स्वयं चात्र गमिष्यामि मन्त्रिणस्तानुवाच ह॥ १९॥
verses.m: Nay, having placed Śuka and Sāraṇa at the northern gate of the city, he said to the aforesaid counsellors, “I shall personally visit and take up my position at the northern gate. (19)

verses.text:
राक्षसं तु विरूपाक्षं महावीर्यपराक्रमम्।
मध्यमेऽस्थापयद गल्मेबहभिः सह राक्षसैः॥ २०॥
verses.m: Again at the central military post he placed the ogre Virūpākṣa, who was endowed with extraordinary virility and prowess, alongwith numerous other ogres. (20)

verses.text:
एवं विधानं लङ्कायां कृत्वा राक्षसपुंगवः।
कृतकृत्यमिवात्मानं मन्यते कालचोदितः॥ २१॥
verses.m: Having made arrangements as aforesaid in Laṅkā, Rāvaṇa (a bull among the ogres), under the sway of destiny, deemed his purpose accomplished, as it were. (21)

verses.text:
विसर्जयामास ततः स मन्त्रिणो
विधानमाज्ञाप्य पुरस्य पुष्कलम्।
जयाशिषा मन्त्रिगणेन पूजितो
विवेश सोऽन्तःपुरमृद्धिमन्महत्॥ २२॥
verses.m: Having ordered adequate arrangements for the defence of the city of Laṅkā, he then let his counsellors depart. Nay, acclaimed by the body of counsellors with benedictions of triumph, he entered his sumptuous and extensive gynaeceum. (22)

verses.text:
नरवानरराजानौ स तु वायुसुतः कपिः।
जाम्बवानृक्षराजश्च राक्षसश्च विभीषणः॥ १॥
अङ्गदो वालिपुत्रश्च सौमित्रिः शरभः कपिः।
सुषेणः सहदायादो मैन्दो द्विविद एव च॥ २॥
गजो गवाक्षः कुमुदो नलोऽथ पनसस्तथा।
अमित्रविषयं प्राप्ताः समवेताः समर्थयन्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Arrived in the enemy’s territory and gathered together, Śrī Rāma and Sugrīva, the rulers of men and monkeys, respectively as also the celebrated monkey, Hanumān, son of the wind-god, also Jāmbavān, the king of bears, as well as the ogre Vibhīṣaṇa, nay, Aṅgada, son of Vāli, Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā), the monkey Śarabha, Suṣeṇa accompanied by his kinsfolk, Mainda as well as Dwivida, Gaja, Gavākṣa, Kumuda and Nala as also Panasa said to one another: (1—3)

verses.text:
इयं सा लक्ष्यते लङ्का पुरी रावणपालिता।
सासुरोरगगन्धर्वैरमरैरपि दुर्जया॥ ४॥
कार्यसिद्धिं पुरस्कृत्य मन्त्रयध्वं विनिर्णये।
नित्यं संनिहितो यत्र रावणो राक्षसाधिपः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Here is to be seen the city of Laṅkā, protected by Rāvaṇa, which is hard to conquer even for the immortals accompanied by the demons, the Nāgas (serpent-demons) and Gandharvas (celestial musicians) and in which Rāvaṇa, the suzerain lord of ogres, is ever present. Now take counsel for determining our duty with a view to achieving success in our mission (viz., the overthrow of Rāvaṇa and the recovery of Sītā).” (4-5)

verses.text:
अथ तेषु ब्रुवाणेषु रावणावरजोऽब्रवीत्।
वाक्यमग्राम्यपदवत् पुष्कलार्थं विभीषणः॥ ६॥
verses.m: While they were speaking as aforesaid, Vibhīṣaṇa, the youngest brother of Rāvaṇa, made the following submission, consisting of polished words and full of ample meaning: (6)

verses.text:
अनलः पनसश्चैव सम्पातिः प्रमतिस्तथा।
गत्वा लङ्कां ममामात्याः पुरीं पुनरिहागताः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Having gone to the city of Laṅkā, my four ministers, Anala as well as Panasa, Sampāti and Pramati, have returned to this place. (7)

verses.text:
भूत्वा शकुनयः सर्वे प्रविष्टाश्च रिपोर्बलम्।
विधानं विहितं यच्च तद् दृष्ट्वा समुपस्थिताः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Nay, assuming the semblance of birds, they all penetrated deep into the enemy’s ranks, and have duly turned up after seeing with their own eyes the arrangements which have been made for the defence of Laṅkā. (8)

verses.text:
संविधानं यथाहुस्ते रावणस्य दुरात्मनः।
राम तद् ब्रुवतः सर्वं याथातथ्येन मे शृणु॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Hear from me, O Rāma, as I speak in accordance with facts of all the defences organized by the evil-minded Rāvaṇa even as my ministers have described them to me. (9)

verses.text:
पूर्वं प्रहस्तः सबलो द्वारमासाद्य तिष्ठति।
दक्षिणं च महावीर्यौ महापार्श्वमहोदरौ॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Having reached the eastern gate with a division of the army, Prahasta (the Commander-in-Chief) stands there; while Mahāpārśwa and Mahodara, who are endowed with extraordinary virility, stand at the southern gate. (10)

verses.text:
इन्द्रजित् पश्चिमं द्वारं राक्षसैर्बहुभिर्वृतः।
पट्टिशासिधनुष्मद्भिः शूलमुद्गरपाणिभिः॥ ११॥
नानाप्रहरणैः शूरैरावृतो रावणात्मजः।
राक्षसानां सहस्रैस्तु बहुभिः शस्त्रपाणिभिः॥ १२॥
युक्तः परमसंविग्नो राक्षसैः सह मन्त्रवित्।
उत्तरं नगरद्वारं रावणः स्वयमास्थितः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Surrounded by numerous ogres wielding sharp-edged spears, swords and bows and carrying darts and mallets in their hands, nay, accompanied by champions wielding various weapons, Indrajit, the eldest son of Rāvaṇa, is stationed at the western gate. Nay, accompanied by many thousands of ogres, bearing weapons in their hands, and extremely agitated, Rāvaṇa himself, who is skilled in counsel, has taken up his position at the northern gate. (11—13)

verses.text:
विरूपाक्षस्तु महता शूलखड्गधनुष्मता।
बलेन राक्षसैः सार्धं मध्यमं गुल्ममाश्रितः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Virūpākṣa for his part is stationed with a huge force armed with pikes, swords and bows, as well as with other ogres at the central military post. (14)

verses.text:
एतानेवं विधान् गुल्माँल्लङ्कायां समुदीक्ष्य ते।
मामका मन्त्रिणः सर्वे शीघ्रं पुनरिहागताः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Having keenly observed these garrisons of the aforesaid description at Laṅkā, all my ministers returned apace to this place. (15)

verses.text:
गजानां दशसाहस्रं रथानामयुतं तथा।
हयानामयुते द्वे च साग्रकोटिश्च रक्षसाम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “The strength of elephants in the army of Rāvaṇa is ten thousand, that of chariots is also ten thousand; nay, that of horses is twenty thousand, while that of ogre-foot soldiers is over one crore. (16)

verses.text:
विक्रान्ता बलवन्तश्च संयुगेष्वाततायिनः।
इष्टा राक्षसराजस्य नित्यमेते निशाचराः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “These rangers of the night, viz., Prahasta and others, are all valiant and mighty, cruel on the field of battle and are ever beloved of Rāvaṇa, the ruler of ogres. (17)

verses.text:
एकैकस्यात्र युद्धार्थे राक्षसस्य विशाम्पते।
परीवारः सहस्राणां सहस्रमुपतिष्ठते॥ १८॥
verses.m: “A body of adherents consisting of ten lakhs stands at the beck and call of each ogre of the afore-mentioned generals, O protector of the people!” (18)

verses.text:
एतां प्रवृत्तिं लङ्कायां मन्त्रिप्रोक्तां विभीषणः।
एवमुक्त्वा महाबाहू राक्षसांस्तानदर्शयत्॥ १९॥
लङ्कायां सचिवैः सर्वं रामाय प्रत्यवेदयत्।
रामं कमलपत्राक्षमिदमुत्तरमब्रवीत्॥ २०॥
रावणावरजः श्रीमान् रामप्रियचिकीर्षया।
कुबेरं तु यदा राम रावणः प्रतियुद्ध्यति॥ २१॥
षष्टिः शतसहस्राणि तदा निर्यान्ति राक्षसाः।
पराक्रमेण वीर्येण तेजसा सत्त्वगौरवात्।
सदृशा ह्यत्र दर्पेण रावणस्य दुरात्मनः॥ २२॥
verses.m: Having conveyed as above the aforesaid information concerning Laṅkā, furnished by his ministers, the mighty-armed Vibhīṣaṇa produced the said ogres before Śrī Rāma and caused everything concerning Laṅkā to be made known to Śrī Rāma by his ministers themselves. With intent to please Śrī Rāma, the glorious Vibhīṣaṇa (the youngest half-brother of Rāvaṇa) further submitted as follows to Śrī Rāma, whose eyes resembled the petals of a lotus: “When Rāvaṇa for his part, O Rāma, launched an offensive against (his own half-brother) Kubera (the god of riches), sixty lakh ogres sallied forth with him at that time—ogres who were actually compeers of the evil-minded Rāvaṇa in prowess, virility, energy, abundance of courage and steadfastness in battle. (19—22)

verses.text:
अत्र मन्युर्न कर्तव्यः कोपये त्वां न भीषये।
समर्थो ह्यसि वीर्येण सुराणामपि निग्रहे॥ २३॥
verses.m: “No depression or indignation should be resorted to by you on this report. I do not mean to terrify you but am simply rousing your wrath; for, I know, you are capable of subduing even gods by virtue of your valour. (23)

verses.text:
तद्भवांश्चतुरङ्गेण बलेन महता वृतम्।
व्यूह्येदं वानरानीकं निर्मथिष्यसि रावणम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Disposing the yonder simian army in battle array in the same way as has been done by Rāvaṇa, you shall be able to crush Rāvaṇa who is surrounded by a huge army consisting of four limbs viz., elephants, chariots, cavalry and foot soldiers.” (24)

verses.text:
रावणावरजे वाक्यमेवं ब्रुवति राघवः।
शत्रूणां प्रतिघातार्थमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ २५॥
verses.m: When Vibhīṣaṇa (the youngest half-brother of Rāvaṇa) made the foregoing speech, Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) issued orders as follows for attacking the enemy: (25)

verses.text:
पूर्वद्वारं तु लङ्काया नीलो वानरपुङ्गवः।
प्रहस्तं प्रतियोद्धा स्याद् वानरैर्बहुभिर्वृतः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Making his way to the eastern gate, surrounded by numerous monkeys, Nīla, a veritable bull among the monkeys, for his part should fight against Prahasta. (26)

verses.text:
अङ्गदो वालिपुत्रस्तु बलेन महता वृतः।
दक्षिणे बाधतां द्वारे महापार्श्वमहोदरौ॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Nay, surrounded by a large army, Aṅgada, son of Vāli, should press and drive away Mahāpārśwa and Mahodara posted at the southern gate. (27)

verses.text:
हनूमान् पश्चिमद्वारं निष्पीड्य पवनात्मजः।
प्रविशत्वप्रमेयात्मा बहुभिः कपिभिर्वृतः॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Pressing against the western gate, surrounded by numerous monkeys, Hanumān, an offspring of the wind-god, who is endowed with immeasurable firmness and sturdiness, should make good his entry into it. (28)

verses.text:
दैत्यदानवसङ्घानामृषीणां च महात्मनाम्।
विप्रकारप्रियः क्षुद्रो वरदानबलान्वितः॥ २९॥
परिक्रमति यः सर्वान् लोकान् संतापयन् प्रजाः।
तस्याहं राक्षसेन्द्रस्य स्वयमेव वधे धृतः॥ ३०॥
उत्तरं नगरद्वारमहं सौमित्रिणा सह।
निपीड्याभिप्रवेक्ष्यामि सबलो यत्र रावणः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Pressing against the northern gate of the city of Laṅkā alongwith Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā), personally bent as I am on the destruction of that petty-minded ruler of ogres—who is fond of oppressing multitudes of Daityas (giants) and Dānavas (demons) as well as the high-souled Ṛṣis, nay, who is armed with power derived from boons (conferred on him by Brahmā and others) and who ranges all the worlds persecuting created beings—I shall force my entry into that gate, where Rāvaṇa himself is stationed with his army. (29—31)

verses.text:
वानरेन्द्रश्च बलवानृक्षराजश्च वीर्यवान्।
राक्षसेन्द्रानुजश्चैव गुल्मे भवतु मध्यमे॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Nay, let the mighty Sugrīva, the ruler of monkeys and the powerful Jāmbavān, the king of bears, as well as Vibhīṣaṇa (the youngest half-brother of Rāvaṇa) be stationed at the central post. (32)

verses.text:
न चैव मानुषं रूपं कार्यं हरिभिराहवे।
एषा भवतु नः संज्ञा युद्धेऽस्मिन् वानरे बले॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “No human semblance should be assumed at any event by the monkeys on the field of battle. In the simian ranks let this serve as our distinctive mark in this battle. (33)

verses.text:
वानरा एव नश्चिह्नं स्वजनेऽस्मिन् भविष्यति।
वयं तु मानुषेणैव सप्त योत्स्यामहे परान्॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “The monkeys alone will be the sign of recognition in distinguishing our ranks in this conflict. Only we seven shall, however, fight the enemies in a human form. (34)

verses.text:
अहमेव सह भ्रात्रा लक्ष्मणेन महौजसा।
आत्मना पञ्चमश्चायं सखा मम विभीषणः॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “I myself will be one, with my younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa, who is endowed with extraordinary energy and who will be the second; while, of the other five, this friend of mine, Vibhīṣaṇa, in his own person will be the fifth over and above his four ministers.” (35)

verses.text:
स रामः कृत्यसिद्ध्यर्थमेवमुक्त्वा विभीषणम्।
सुवेलारोहणे बुद्धिं चकार मतिमान् प्रभुः।
रमणीयतरं दृष्ट्वा सुवेलस्य गिरेस्तटम्॥ ३६॥
verses.m: Having spoken to Vibhīṣaṇa as aforesaid with a view to the success of his undertaking, and beholding the excessively charming slopes of the Suvela mountain, the aforesaid sagacious and powerful Śrī Rāma made up his mind to climb up the Suvela mountain. (36)

verses.text:
ततस्तु रामो महता बलेन
प्रच्छाद्य सर्वां पृथिवीं महात्मा।
प्रहृष्टरूपोऽभिजगाम लङ्कां
कृत्वा मतिं सोऽरिवधे महात्मा॥ ३७॥
verses.m: Having fully covered the entire land of that region with his huge army and having resolved upon the destruction of his foes, that high-souled Śrī Rāma for his part, who was endowed with great firmness, then sallied forth towards Laṅkā with an exultant air. (37)

verses.text:
स तु कृत्वा सुवेलस्य मतिमारोहणं प्रति।
लक्ष्मणानुगतो रामः सुग्रीवमिदमब्रवीत्॥ १॥
विभीषणं च धर्मज्ञमनुरक्तं निशाचरम्।
मन्त्रज्ञं च विधिज्ञं च श्लक्ष्णया परया गिरा॥ २॥
verses.m: Having made up his mind to climb up the Suvela mountain, Śrī Rāma for his part, who was followed by Lakṣmaṇa, spoke as follows in soft and excellent tone to Sugrīva, as well as to the devoted night-ranger, Vibhīṣaṇa, who knew what is right, was experienced in counsel and learned in ritual: (1-2)

verses.text:
सुवेलं साधु शैलेन्द्रमिमं धातुशतैश्चितम्।
अध्यारोहामहे सर्वे वत्स्यामोऽत्र निशामिमाम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Let us all duly ascend this ruler of mountains, Suvela, which is covered with hundreds of minerals. We shall spend this night on it. (3)

verses.text:
लङ्कां चालोकयिष्यामो निलयं तस्य रक्षसः।
येन मे मरणान्ताय हता भार्या दुरात्मना॥ ४॥
verses.m: “We shall also be able to survey from its top Laṅkā, the abode of that ogre, Rāvaṇa, by whom, evil-minded as he is, was my consort borne away to his own destruction, the inevitable result of his action. (4)

verses.text:
येन धर्मो न विज्ञातो न वृत्तं न कुलं तथा।
राक्षस्या नीचया बुद्ध्या येन तद् गर्हितं कृतम्॥ ५॥
तस्मिन् मे वर्तते रोषः कीर्तिते राक्षसाधमे।
यस्यापराधान्नीचस्य वधं द्रक्ष्यामि रक्षसाम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “The moment his name is mentioned, my wrath is aroused towards that vile ogre, Rāvaṇa, by whom neither was virtue rightly understood, nor morality, nor was pedigree taken into consideration, but by whom the aforesaid reproachful act was perpetrated as prompted by his mean ogre-like mentality. I shall perceive with my own eyes the extermination of all the ogres due to the crime of that mean fellow. (5-6)

verses.text:
एको हि कुरुते पापं कालपाशवशं गतः।
नीचेनात्मापचारेण कुलं तेन विनश्यति॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Fallen in the grip of the noose of Death, a single individual actually perpetrates a sin; while the entire race perishes on account of that vile fellow due to his wrong doing.” (7)

verses.text:
एवं सम्मन्त्रयन्नेव सक्रोधो रावणं प्रति।
रामः सुवेलं वासाय चित्रसानुमुपारुहत्॥ ८॥
verses.m: Talking as aforesaid, full of wrath as he was towards Rāvaṇa, Śrī Rāma ascended the Suvela mountain, distinguished by its lovely peaks, with a view to halting there. (8)

verses.text:
पृष्ठतो लक्ष्मणश्चैनमन्वगच्छत् समाहितः।
सशरं चापमुद्यम्य सुमहद्विक्रमे रतः॥ ९॥
verses.m: Lifting his bow alongwith an arrow, Lakṣmaṇa, who was fully alert and fond of showing extraordinary prowess, followed him at his back. (9)

verses.text:
तमन्वारोहत् सुग्रीवः सामात्यः सविभीषणः।
हनुमानङ्गदो नीलो मैन्दो द्विविद एव च॥ १०॥
गजो गवाक्षो गवयः शरभो गन्धमादनः।
पनसः कुमुदश्चैव हरो रम्भश्च यूथपः॥ ११॥
जाम्बवांश्च सुषेणश्च ऋषभश्च महामतिः।
दुर्मुखश्च महातेजास्तथा शतवलिः कपिः॥ १२॥
एते चान्ये च बहवो वानराः शीघ्रगामिनः।
ते वायुवेगप्रवणास्तं गिरिं गिरिचारिणः॥ १३॥
अध्यारोहन्त शतशः सुवेलं यत्र राघवः।
ते त्वदीर्घेण कालेन गिरिमारुह्य सर्वतः॥ १४॥
ददृशुः शिखरे तस्य विषक्तामिव खे पुरीम्।
तां शुभां प्रवरद्वारां प्राकारवरशोभिताम्॥ १५॥
लङ्कां राक्षससम्पूर्णां ददृशुर्हरियूथपाः।
प्राकारवरसंस्थैश्च तथा नीलैश्च राक्षसैः॥ १६॥
ददृशुस्ते हरिश्रेष्ठाः प्राकारमपरं कृतम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: Following him, Sugrīva with his ministers and Vibhīṣaṇa, nay, Hanumān, Aṅgada, Nīla, Mainda as well as Dwivida, Gaja, Gavākṣa, Gavaya, Śarabha, Gandhamādana, Panasa and Kumuda as well, Hara and the troop-commander, Rambha, as also Jāmbavān and Suṣeṇa as well as the highly intelligent Ṛṣabha, as also Durmukha, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, and the monkey Śatabali—these as well as many other well-known swift-footed monkeys, who moved with the speed of the wind and used to range on hills, scaled the Suvela mountain in hundreds, reaching the spot where Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, was. Climbing up the mountain in a short time on all sides, and taking their stand on the top of that mountain, they, for their part, beheld the city suspended as it were in the air. The leaders of monkey-troops saw the splendid Laṅkā provided with most excellent gates, graced with an excellent defensive wall and packed with ogres. Nay, the aforesaid jewels among the monkeys noticed another wall formed (as it were on the original one) by the dark-hued ogres ranged in compact rows for defence on the excellent defensive walls. (10—17)

verses.text:
ते दृष्ट्वा वानराः सर्वे राक्षसान् युद्धकाङ्क्षिणः।
मुमुचुर्विविधान् नादांस्तस्य रामस्य पश्यतः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Beholding the ogres burning to fight, all the aforesaid monkeys raised clamours of various kinds while Śrī Rāma stood looking on. (18)

verses.text:
ततोऽस्तमगमत् सूर्यः संध्यया प्रतिरञ्जितः।
पूर्णचन्द्रप्रदीप्ता च क्षपा समतिवर्तत॥ १९॥
verses.m: Reddened by the evening twilight, the sun presently sank below the horizon, and, illumined by the full moon, the night duly set in. (19)

verses.text:
ततः स रामो हरिवाहिनीपति-
र्विभीषणेन प्रतिनन्द्य सत्कृतः।
सलक्ष्मणो यूथपयूथसंयुतः
सुवेलपृष्ठे न्यवसद् यथासुखम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: Honoured by Vibhīṣaṇa after greeting him joyfully, nay, accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa and joined by a company of troop-commanders, the celebrated Śrī Rāma thenceforward sojourned happily on the top of the Suvela mountain. (20)

verses.text:
तां रात्रिमुषितास्तत्र सुवेले हरियूथपाः।
लङ्कायां ददृशुर्वीरा वनान्युपवनानि च॥ १॥
verses.m: Having passed that night on the said Suvela mountain, the valiant monkey generals surveyed the woods and groves of Laṅkā. (1)

verses.text:
समसौम्यानि रम्याणि विशालान्यायतानि च।
दृष्टिरम्याणि ते दृष्ट्वा बभूवुर्जातविस्मयाः॥ २॥
verses.m: They were amazed to find them level and free from molestation by beasts of prey, lovely, long, extensive and agreeable to behold. (2)

verses.text:
चम्पकाशोकबकुलशालतालसमाकुला।
तमालवनसंछन्ना नागमालासमावृता॥ ३॥
हिन्तालैरर्जुनैर्नीपैः सप्तपर्णैः सुपुष्पितैः।
तिलकैः कर्णिकारैश्च पाटलैश्च समन्ततः॥ ४॥
शुशुभे पुष्पिताग्रैश्च लतापरिगतैर्द्रुमैः।
लङ्का बहुविधैर्दिव्यैर्यथेन्द्रस्यामरावती॥ ५॥
विचित्रकुसुमोपेतै रक्तकोमलपल्लवैः।
शाद्वलैश्च तथा नीलैश्चित्राभिर्वनराजिभिः॥ ६॥
verses.m: Thick with Campaka, Aśoka, Bakula, sal and palmyra trees, nay, covered with groves of Tamāla trees and surrounded with rows of Nāgakesara trees, Laṅkā looked charming on all sides like the city of Amarāvatī ruled over by Indra, the ruler of gods, with green grassy spots and charming avenues as well as with beautiful trees of various kinds, viz., Hintāla, Arjuna, Nīpa and Saptaparṇa in full blossom, Tilaka, Karṇikāra and Pāṭala whose crests were laden with flowers and which were intertwined with climbers, nay, which were laden with diverse flowers and clothed with red tender leaves. (3—6)

verses.text:
गन्धाढ्यान्यतिरम्याणि पुष्पाणि च फलानि च।
धारयन्त्यगमास्तत्र भूषणानीव मानवाः॥ ७॥
verses.m: The trees in that city bore fragrant and most lovely flowers and fruits in the same way as human beings wear ornaments. (7)

verses.text:
तच्चैत्ररथसंकाशं मनोज्ञं नन्दनोपमम्।
वनं सर्वर्तुकं रम्यं शुशुभे षट्पदायुतम्॥ ८॥
दात्यूहकोयष्टिबकैर्नृत्यमानैश्च बर्हिणैः।
रुतं परभृतानां च शुश्रुवे वननिर्झरे॥ ९॥
verses.m: Vying with Caitraratha (the garden of Kubera, the god of riches) and resembling Nandana (the garden of Indra, the ruler of gods), the principal garden of Laṅkā—which was lovely and delightful to the mind, green in all seasons and full of bees—looked charming with gallinules, lapwings, herons and dancing peacocks. The warbling of cuckoos was also heard in that garden abounding in cascades. (8-9)

verses.text:
नित्यमत्तविहंगानि भ्रमराचरितानि च।
कोकिलाकुलखण्डानि विहंगाभिरुतानि च॥ १०॥
भृङ्गराजाधिगीतानि कुररस्वनितानि च।
कोणालकविघुष्टानि सारसाभिरुतानि च।
विविशुस्ते ततस्तानि वनान्युपवनानि च॥ ११॥
हृष्टाः प्रमुदिता वीरा हरयः कामरूपिणः।
तेषां प्रविशतां तत्र वानराणां महौजसाम्॥ १२॥
पुष्पसंसर्गसुरभिर्ववौ घ्राणसुखोऽनिलः।
अन्ये तु हरिवीराणां यूथान्निष्क्रम्य यूथपाः।
सुग्रीवेणाभ्यनुज्ञाता लङ्कां जग्मुः पताकिनीम्॥ १३॥
वित्रासयन्तो विहगान् ग्लापयन्तो मृगद्विपान्।
कम्पयन्तश्च तां लङ्कां नादैः स्वैर्नदतां वराः॥ १४॥
कुर्वन्तस्ते महावेगा महीं चरणपीडिताम्।
रजश्च सहसैवोर्ध्वं जगाम चरणोत्थितम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Moving from that mountain-top the valiant monkeys, who were able to change their form at will and felt highly rejoiced and thrilled with joy, entered the aforesaid groves and gardens, which were inhabited by birds constantly in heat and frequented by bees, whose clusters of trees were crowded with cuckoos, nay, which were rendered noisy by birds and filled with the music of fork-tailed drongoes and the cries of ospreys, and which resounded with the noise of wagtails and the cries of cranes. As the monkeys, who were all endowed with extraordinary energy, penetrated deep into that grove, a breeze redolent through contact with flowers and gentle as breath, blew. Breaking away from the company of monkey heroes, as permitted by Sugrīva, other well-kṅown monkey leaders, however, the foremost of those capable of roaring sought Laṅkā, dressed with pennons, terrifying the birds, dispiriting the deer and elephants and shaking the aforesaid Laṅkā with their roars, nay, trampling down the earth in their great impetuosity. Nay, the dust raised by their footfalls rose upwards all at once. (10—15)

verses.text:
ऋक्षाः सिंहाश्च महिषा वारणाश्च मृगाः खगाः।
तेन शब्देन वित्रस्ता जग्मुर्भीता दिशो दश॥ १६॥
verses.m: Alarmed by that roar, bears and lions, buffaloes, elephants, deer and birds ran in panic in all the ten directions. (16)

verses.text:
शिखरं तु त्रिकूटस्य प्रांशु चैकं दिविस्पृशम्।
समन्तात् पुष्पसंछन्नं महारजतसंनिभम्॥ १७॥
शतयोजनविस्तीर्णं विमलं चारुदर्शनम्।
श्लक्ष्णं श्रीमन्महच्चैव दुष्प्रापं शकुनैरपि॥ १८॥
मनसापि दुरारोहं किं पुनः कर्मणा जनैः।
निविष्टा तस्य शिखरे लङ्का रावणपालिता॥ १९॥
verses.m: There was a lofty peak of the Trikūṭa mountain, which seemed to touch the skies, which was thickly covered with blossom on all sides and sparkled like gold, which extended over an area of one hundred Yojanas (or eight hundred miles), which was stainless, graceful to behold, smooth, splendid and vast too, difficult of access even to birds and hard to scale even in thought, much less in action, for men. Laṅkā, which was ruled over by Rāvaṇa, was situated on this peak of the aforesaid mountain. (17—19)

verses.text:
दशयोजनविस्तीर्णा विंशद्योजनमायता।
सा पुरी गोपुरैरुच्चैः पाण्डुराम्बुदसंनिभैः।
काञ्चनेन च शालेन राजतेन च शोभते॥ २०॥
verses.m: Ten Yojanas (or eighty miles) wide and twenty Yojanas (or one hundred and sixty miles) long*, the said city looked charming with its towering gates, closely resembling white clouds and its gold and silver fortifications. (20)

verses.text:
प्रासादैश्च विमानैश्च लङ्का परमभूषिता।
घनैरिवातपापाये मध्यमं वैष्णवं पदम्॥ २१॥
