रावणिर्भ्रातरौ वाक्यमन्तर्धानगतोऽब्रवीत्॥ १०॥
verses.m: Thereupon Indrajit (son of Rāvaṇa), the outer corners of whose eyes had turned red through rage and looked like a mass of collyrium, spoke as follows to the two brothers, while remaining still invisible: (10)

verses.text:
युध्यमानमनालक्ष्यं शक्रोऽपि त्रिदशेश्वरः।
द्रष्टुमासादितुं वापि न शक्तः किं पुनर्युवाम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Even Indra, the ruler of gods, will not be able even to discern me, much less approach me, while I am fighting imperceptibly, how much less you two! (11)

verses.text:
प्रापिताविषुजालेन राघवौ कङ्कपत्रिणा।
एष रोषपरीतात्मा नयामि यमसादनम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “My mind seized with anger, I hereby dispatch to the abode of Yama you two scions of Raghu, who have been enmeshed in a network of darts provided with the plumes of buzzards.” (12)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा तु धर्मज्ञौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।
निर्बिभेद शितैर्बाणैः प्रजहर्ष ननाद च॥ १३॥
verses.m: Having spoken as aforesaid, Indrajit, for his part, was exulted and roared and began to pierce with his pointed arrows the two brothers, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇ, who knew what is right. (13)

verses.text:
भिन्नाञ्जनचयश्यामो विस्फार्य विपुलं धनुः।
भूय एव शरान् घोरान् विससर्ज महामृधे॥ १४॥
verses.m: Stretching his huge bow, Indrajit, who was dark as a mass of collyrium, let fly once more formidable arrows in that major conflict. (14)

verses.text:
ततो मर्मसु मर्मज्ञो मज्जयन् निशितान् शरान्।
रामलक्ष्मणयोर्वीरो ननाद च मुहुर्मुहुः॥ १५॥
verses.m: Nay, digging sharp arrows into the vital parts of Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇ, roared again and again. (15)

verses.text:
बद्धौ तु शरबन्धेन तावुभौ रणमूर्धनि।
निमेषान्तरमात्रेण न शेकतुरवेक्षितुम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: Enmeshed in a net of arrows in the forefront of battle, both the princes for their part became incapable, in the mere twinkling of an eye, even of looking up. (16)

verses.text:
ततो विभिन्नसर्वाङ्गौ शरशल्याचितौ कृतौ।
ध्वजाविव महेन्द्रस्य रज्जुमुक्तौ प्रकम्पितौ॥ १७॥
verses.m: Pierced in all their limbs and covered all over with the heads of arrows (transfixed in their bodies). the two princes then began to shake violently like a pair of banners raised in honour of the mighty Indra (the ruler of gods) and freed from their cords. (17)

verses.text:
तौ सम्प्रचलितौ वीरौ मर्मभेदेन कर्शितौ।
निपेततुर्महेष्वासौ जगत्यां जगतीपती॥ १८॥
verses.m: Staggered and enfeebled on account of being pierced in their vital parts, the two gallant princes, who were sovereigns of the globe and wielded mighty bows, fell to the ground. (18)

verses.text:
तौ वीरशयने वीरौ शयानौ रुधिरोक्षितौ।
शरवेष्टितसर्वाङ्गावार्तौ परमपीडितौ॥ १९॥
verses.m: Laying on the heroes’ bed (in the form of the battle-ground), bathed in blood with all their limbs enmeshed by arrows (in the form of serpents) the aforesaid two heroes, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, felt distressed and exceedingly afflicted. (19)

verses.text:
नह्यविद्धं तयोर्गात्रे बभूवाङ्गुलमन्तरम्।
नानिर्विण्णं न चाध्वस्तमाकराग्रादजिह्मगैः॥ २०॥
verses.m: Not a finger’s breadth of space was left on their person, which was not actually pierced: and there was no organ from the tips of their fingers which remained unlacerated and unshaken by arrows. (20)

verses.text:
तौ तु क्रूरेण निहतौ रक्षसा कामरूपिणा।
असृक् सुस्रुवतुस्तीव्रं जलं प्रस्रवणाविव॥ २१॥
verses.m: Struck down by that cruel ogre, who was able to change his form at will, the two princes for their part emitted blood copiously even as a pair of springs would pour forth water. (21)

verses.text:
पपात प्रथमं रामो विद्धो मर्मसु मार्गणैः।
क्रोधादिन्द्रजिता येन पुरा शक्रो विनिर्जितः॥ २२॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma fell first, pierced as he was in his vital parts with shafts discharged in fury by Indrajit, by whom Indra (the ruler of gods) was utterly vanquished of yore. (22)

verses.text:
रुक्मपुङ्खैः प्रसन्नाग्रै रजोगतिभिराशुगैः।
नाराचैरर्धनाराचैर्भल्लैरञ्जलिकैरपि।
विव्याध वत्सदन्तैश्च सिंहदंष्ट्रैः क्षुरैस्तथा॥ २३॥
verses.m: Indrajit pierced him with arrows known as Nārācas (with even and circular heads), Ardhanārācas (shaped as Nārācas only one-half their length), Bhallas (with axe-like heads), also Añjalikas (with heads shaped like joined palms), Vatsadantas (with heads resembling the teeth of a calf), Siṁhadaṁṣṭras (with heads resembling a lion’s teeth) and also Kṣuras (with heads sharp as the edge of a razor), furnished with gold feathers, those with polished heads and those descending (unobstructed) like dust. (23)

verses.text:
स वीरशयने शिश्येऽविज्यमाविध्य कार्मुकम्।
भिन्नमुष्टिपरीणाहं त्रिनतं रुक्मभूषितम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma lay on the heroes’ bed, leaving his gold-plated bow, which was still strung and bent at three places (viz., the two ends and the middle), in that the grip of his fist had now relaxed due to his feebleness. (24)

verses.text:
बाणपातान्तरे रामं पतितं पुरुषर्षभम्।
स तत्र लक्ष्मणो दृष्ट्वा निराशो जीवितेऽभवत्॥ २५॥
verses.m: Beholding Śrī Rāma, the foremost of human beings, fallen at an arrow’s throw from him on the field of battle, the celebrated Lakṣmaṇa became despondent about his own life. (25)

verses.text:
रामं कमलपत्राक्षं शरण्यं रणतोषिणम्।
शुशोच भ्रातरं दृष्ट्वा पतितं धरणीतले॥ २६॥
verses.m: He gave way to grief on seeing his eldest brother, Śrī Rāma, whose eyes resembled the petals of a lotus, who afforded shelter to all and whoever rejoiced in fighting. (26)

verses.text:
हरयश्चापि तं दृष्ट्वा संतापं परमं गताः।
शोकार्ताश्चुक्रुशुर्घोरमश्रुपूरितलोचनाः ॥ २७॥
verses.m: Nay, the monkeys too gave way to extreme agony on beholding him in that sad plight. Stricken with grief, they shrieked in agony, their eyes filled with tears. (27)

verses.text:
बद्धौ तु तौ वीरशये शयानौ
ते वानराः सम्परिवार्य तस्थुः।
समागता वायुसुतप्रमुख्या
विषादमार्ताः परमं च जग्मुः॥ २८॥
verses.m: The aforesaid monkeys for their part, who had collected there with Hanumān (son of the wind-god) as their foremost leader, stood completely surrounding the two princes lying bound in a net of snakes on the heroes’ bed and gave way to extreme despondency, distressed as they were. (28)

verses.text:
ततो द्यां पृथिवीं चैव वीक्षमाणा वनौकसः।
ददृशुः संततौ बाणैर्भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ॥ १॥
verses.m: The ten monkeys (lit., denizens of the woods) who had been surveying the heavens and the earth in search of Indrajit, found on returning from their quest the two brothers, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, covered all over with arrows. (1)

verses.text:
वृष्ट्वेवोपरते देवे कृतकर्मणि राक्षसे।
आजगामाथ तं देशं ससुग्रीवो विभीषणः॥ २॥
verses.m: The ogre, Indrajit, having retired after accomplishing his work even as Indra, the god of rain, would after raining. Vibhīṣaṇa, accompanied by Sugrīva, forthwith came to that spot. (2)

verses.text:
नीलश्च द्विविदो मैन्दः सुषेणः कुमुदोऽङ्गदः।
तूर्णं हनुमता सार्धमन्वशोचन्त राघवौ॥ ३॥
अचेष्टौ मन्दनिःश्वासौ शोणितेन परिप्लुतौ।
शरजालाचितौ स्तब्धौ शयानौ शरतल्पगौ॥ ४॥
verses.m: Nīla and Dwivida, Mainda, Suṣeṇa, Kumuda and Aṅgada alongwith Hanumān forthwith began to grieve for the two scions of Raghu, who were lying inactive and motionless on a bed of arrows, breathing faintly, bathed in blood and covered all over with a network of darts. (3-4)

verses.text:
निःश्वसन्तौ यथा सर्पौ निश्चेष्टौ मन्दविक्रमौ।
रुधिरस्रावदिग्धाङ्गौ तपनीयाविव ध्वजौ॥ ५॥
तौ वीरशयने वीरौ शयानौ मन्दचेष्टितौ।
यूथपैः स्वैः परिवृतौ बाष्पव्याकुललोचनैः॥ ६॥
राघवौ पतितौ दृष्ट्वा शरजालसमन्वितौ।
बभूवुर्व्यथिताः सर्वे वानराः सविभीषणाः॥ ७॥
verses.m: All the monkeys alongwith Vibhīṣaṇa were pained to see the two celebrated and heroic scions of Raghu fallen motionless, and sometimes with a feeble movement, covered with a network of arrows, sighing like a pair of serpents, their prowess having grown faint, all their limbs smeared with a stream of blood and lying stretched on a heroes’ couch like two golden standards, surrounded by their own generals, whose eyes were suffused with tears. (5—7)

verses.text:
अन्तरिक्षं निरीक्षन्तो दिशः सर्वाश्च वानराः।
न चैनं मायया छन्नं ददृशू रावणिं रणे॥ ८॥
verses.m: Though surveying the sky as well as all the quarters, the monkeys could not even discover Indrajit (son of Rāvaṇa), who was veiled by his occult power during the fight.(8)

verses.text:
तं तु मायाप्रतिच्छन्नं माययैव विभीषणः।
वीक्षमाणो ददर्शाग्रे भ्रातुः पुत्रमवस्थितम्।
तमप्रतिमकर्माणमप्रतिद्वन्द्वमाहवे ॥ ९॥
verses.m: Looking round with an occult eye (capable of discerning hidden objects) itself, Vibhīṣaṇa for his part beheld standing nearby his aforesaid nephew of incomparable exploits, unrivalled in combat, and veiled by his own occult power. (9)

verses.text:
ददर्शान्तर्हितं वीरं वरदानाद् विभीषणः।
तेजसा यशसा चैव विक्रमेण च संयुतः॥ १०॥
verses.m: Vibhiṣaṇa who was richly endowed with energy, as well as with glory and prowess, perceived the champion, who was hidden from view by virtue of a boon (conferred on him by Brahmā). (10)

verses.text:
इन्द्रजित् त्वात्मनः कर्म तौ शयानौ समीक्ष्य च।
उवाच परमप्रीतो हर्षयन् सर्वराक्षसान्॥ ११॥
verses.m: Nay, supremely rejoiced to observe the two princes lying on the battlefied, Indrajit for his part proclaimed as follows his own feat, thereby bringing delight to all the ogres: (11)

verses.text:
दूषणस्य च हन्तारौ खरस्य च महाबलौ।
सादितौ मामकैर्बाणैर्भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ॥ १२॥
verses.m: “The two brothers, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, the slayers of Dūṣaṇa as well as of Khara, who were endowed with extraordinary might, have been struck down by my darts! (12)

verses.text:
नेमौ मोक्षयितुं शक्यावेतस्मादिषुबन्धनात्।
सर्वैरपि समागम्य सर्षिसङ्घैः सुरासुरैः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “They cannot be disengaged from this network of arrows even by all the gods, demons, including hosts of Ṛṣis (the seers of Vedic Mantras), exerting together. (13)

verses.text:
यत्कृते चिन्तयानस्य शोकार्तस्य पितुर्मम।
अस्पृष्ट्वा शयनं गात्रैस्त्रियामा याति शर्वरी॥ १४॥
कृत्स्नेयं यत्कृते लङ्का नदी वर्षास्विवाकुला।
सोऽयं मूलहरोऽनर्थः सर्वेषां शमितो मया॥ १५॥
verses.m: “This well-known pest,—which was wearing away the very roots of us all, nay, on whose account the whole night (consisting of three watches of three hours each) slipped past my father, who remains absorbed in this thought and stricken with grief, so much so that he is unable even to touch his couch with his restless limbs—and because of whom the entire city of Laṅkā remains agitated like a river during rains—has at last been got rid of by me! (14-15)

verses.text:
रामस्य लक्ष्मणस्यैव सर्वेषां च वनौकसाम्।
विक्रमा निष्फलाः सर्वे यथा शरदि तोयदाः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “All the exploits of Rāma and Lakṣmana as also of all the monkeys (lit., the dwellers of the woods) have been rendered void like the clouds in autumn.” (16)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा तु तान् सर्वान् राक्षसान् परिपश्यतः।
यूथपानपि तान् सर्वांस्ताडयत् स च रावणिः॥ १७॥
verses.m: Nay, having spoken as aforesaid to all the ogres, who were looking at him, the aforesaid son of Rāvaṇa began to strike all the well-known monkey generals too. (17)

verses.text:
नीलं नवभिराहत्य मैन्दं सद्विविदं तथा।
त्रिभिस्त्रिभिरमित्रघ्नस्तताप परमेषुभिः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Hitting Nīla, the commander-in-Chief of the monkey forces, with nine excellent shafts, Indrajit (the slayer of his foes) tormented Mainda as well as Dwivida with three darts each. (18)

verses.text:
जाम्बवन्तं महेष्वासो विद्ध्वा बाणेन वक्षसि।
हनूमतो वेगवतो विससर्ज शरान् दश॥ १९॥
verses.m: Having pierced Jāmbavān with an arrow in the breast, the ogre (who wielded a mighty bow) discharged ten shafts on the impetuous Hanumān. (19)

verses.text:
गवाक्षं शरभं चैव तावप्यमितविक्रमौ।
द्वाभ्यां द्वाभ्यां महावेगो विव्याध युधि रावणिः॥ २०॥
verses.m: Indrajit (son of Rāvaṇa), who was endowed with great agility, pierced Gavākṣa as well as Śarabha too, the two monkeys of immeasurable prowess, with two arrows each on the field of battle. (20)

verses.text:
गोलाङ्गूलेश्वरं चैव वालिपुत्रमथाङ्गदम्।
विव्याध बहुभिर्बाणैस्त्वरमाणोऽथ रावणिः॥ २१॥
verses.m: Nay, coursing swiftly, Indrajit pierced once more with numerous darts Gavākṣa, the ruler of Golāṅgūlas, and then Añgada (son of Vālī) too. (21)

verses.text:
तान् वानरवरान् भित्त्वा शरैरग्निशिखोपमैः।
ननाद बलवांस्तत्र महासत्त्वः स रावणिः॥ २२॥
verses.m: Having transfixed the aforesaid jewels among monkeys with his arrows resembling the tongues of fire, that mighty son of Rāvaṇa, who was endowed with great courage, began to roar in triumph. (22)

verses.text:
तानर्दयित्वा बाणौघैस्त्रासयित्वा च वानरान्।
प्रजहास महाबाहुर्वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्॥ २३॥
verses.m: Having hurt the monkeys with hails of arrows and struck terror into them, the mighty-armed ogre heartily laughed and exclaimed as follows: (23)

verses.text:
शरबन्धेन घोरेण मया बद्धौ चमूमुखे।
सहितौ भ्रातरावेतौ निशामयत राक्षसाः॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Behold, O ogres, these two brothers bound by me together in a formidable net of arrows in the forefront of battle.” (24)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तास्तु ते सर्वे राक्षसाः कूटयोधिनः।
परं विस्मयमापन्नाः कर्मणा तेन हर्षिताः॥ २५॥
verses.m: Spoken to as aforesaid, all those ogres for their part, who fought treacherously, were seized with great wonder and felt delighted by that exploit of his. (25)

verses.text:
विनेदुश्च महानादान् सर्वे ते जलदोपमाः।
हतो राम इति ज्ञात्वा रावणिं समपूजयन्॥ २६॥
verses.m: They all thudered like clouds, emitting loud shouts. Knowing that Śrī Rāma had been killed, they acclaimed Indrajit, son of Rāvaṇa. (26)

verses.text:
निष्पन्दौ तु तदा दृष्ट्वा भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।
वसुधायां निरुच्छ्वासौ हतावित्यन्वमन्यत॥ २७॥
verses.m: Beholding Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa lying on the ground without movement or breath at that time, Indrajit for his part concluded the two brothers to be dead. (27)

verses.text:
हर्षेण तु समाविष्ट इन्द्रजित् समितिञ्जयः।
प्रविवेश पुरीं लङ्कां हर्षयन् सर्वनैर्ऋतान्॥ २८॥
verses.m: Filled with joy, Indrajit, for his part, who was victorious in battles, entered in state the city of Laṅkā, bringing joy to all ogres. (28)

verses.text:
रामलक्ष्मणयोर्दृष्ट्वा शरीरे सायकैश्चिते।
सर्वाणि चाङ्गोपाङ्गानि सुग्रीवं भयमाविशत्॥ २९॥
verses.m: Fear took possession of Sugrīva on beholding the bodies as well as all the limbs and minor limbs of Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa riddled with arrows. (29)

verses.text:
तमुवाच परित्रस्तं वानरेन्द्रं विभीषणः।
सबाष्पवदनं दीनं शोकव्याकुललोचनम्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Vibhīṣaṇa spoke as follows to Sugrīva (the ruler of monkeys), whose face was bathed in tears, alarmed and afflicted as he was, his eyes bewildered with grief: (30)

verses.text:
अलं त्रासेन सुग्रीव बाष्पवेगो निगृह्यताम्।
एवं प्रायाणि युद्धानि विजयो नास्ति नैष्ठिकः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Have done with fear, O Sugrīva! Let the gush of tears be controlled. Conflicts are mostly of this nature (uncertain in their issue). Victory is never certain. (31)

verses.text:
सभाग्यशेषतास्माकं यदि वीर भविष्यति।
मोहमेतौ प्रहास्येते महात्मानौ महाबलौ॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “If the stock of our good fortune is not yet exhausted, these two high-souled princes, who are endowed with extraordinary might, shall shake off their swoon, O gallant monkey-king! (32)

verses.text:
पर्यवस्थापयात्मानमनाथं मां च वानर।
सत्यधर्माभिरक्तानां नास्ति मृत्युकृतं भयम्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “Restore yourself to confidence, as well as me, forlorn as I am, O monkey! Fear of death does not haunt those who are devoted to truthfulness and piety.” (33)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा ततस्तस्य जलक्लिन्नेन पाणिना।
सुग्रीवस्य शुभे नेत्रे प्रममार्ज विभीषणः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: Having spoken as aforesaid, Vibhīṣaṇa then wiped clean with his hand dipped in water the beautiful eyes of the celebrated Sugrīva. (34)

verses.text:
ततः सलिलमादाय विद्यया परिजप्य च।
सुग्रीवनेत्रे धर्मात्मा प्रममार्ज विभीषणः॥ ३५॥
verses.m: Taking water in his hand and consecrating it with the utterance of a sacred text, Vibhīṣaṇa, whose mind was set on virtue, then washed with it the eyes of Sugrīva. (35)

verses.text:
विमृज्य वदनं तस्य कपिराजस्य धीमतः।
अब्रवीत् कालसम्प्राप्तमसम्भ्रान्तमिदं वचः॥ ३६॥
verses.m: Having wiped clean the face of that sagacious ruler of monkeys, Vibhīṣaṇa addressed to him the following opportune words, which were free from perplexity: (36)

verses.text:
न कालः कपिराजेन्द्र वैक्लव्यमवलम्बितुम्।
अतिस्नेहोऽपि कालेऽस्मिन् मरणायोपकल्पते॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “This is not the moment to give way to faint-heartedness, O suzerain lord of monkeys! Excessive emotion too at this juncture will lead to destruction. (37)

verses.text:
तस्मादुत्सृज्य वैक्लव्यं सर्वकार्यविनाशनम्।
हितं रामपुरोगाणां सैन्यानामनुचिन्तय॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “Therefore, shaking off faint-heartedness, which frustrates all one’s ends, contemplate the good of the troops, which have Śrī Rāma for their leader. (38)

verses.text:
अथ वा रक्ष्यतां रामो यावत्संज्ञाविपर्ययः।
लब्धसंज्ञौ हि काकुत्स्थौ भयं नौ व्यपनेष्यतः॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “Or, let Śrī Rāma be protected till his unconsciousness lasts. Having regained their consciousness, the two scions of Kakutstha will undoubtedly dispel our fear once for all. (39)

verses.text:
नैतत् किंचन रामस्य न च रामो मुमूर्षति।
नह्येनं हास्यते लक्ष्मीर्दुर्लभा या गतायुषाम्॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “This calamity is nothing to Śrī Rāma nor is Śrī Rāma going to die; for bodily splendour, which is difficult to retain for those whose sands of life have run out, is not abandoning him. (40)

verses.text:
तस्मादाश्वासयात्मानं बलं चाश्वासय स्वकम्।
यावत् सैन्यानि सर्वाणि पुनः संस्थापयाम्यहम्॥ ४१॥
verses.m: “Therefore, reassure yourself and steady your life-breath till I restore all the ranks to confidence. (41)

verses.text:
एते हि फुल्लनयनास्त्रासादागतसाध्वसाः।
कर्णे कर्णे प्रकथिता हरयो हरिसत्तम॥ ४२॥
verses.m: “Their eyes dilated through fear, the monkeys, who are seized with consternation, are actually carrying the news about Śrī Rāma’s swoon from ear to ear, O jewel among monkeys! (42)

verses.text:
मां तु दृष्ट्वा प्रधावन्तमनीकं सम्प्रहर्षितम्।
त्यजन्तु हरयस्त्रासं भुक्तपूर्वामिव स्रजम्॥ ४३॥
verses.m: “Let the monkeys for their part shed all fear, even as one would discard a garland already enjoyed, on seeing me running about to reassure the ranks and beholding the army overjoyed on being reassured by me”. (43)

verses.text:
समाश्वास्य तु सुग्रीवं राक्षसेन्द्रो विभीषणः।
विद्रुतं वानरानीकं तत् समाश्वासयत् पुनः॥ ४४॥
verses.m: Having restored Sugrīva to confidence, Vibhīṣaṇa the prospective ruler of ogres, for his part reassured once again the afore said army of monkeys, which had taken to its heels. (44)

verses.text:
इन्द्रजित् तु महामायः सर्वसैन्यसमावृतः।
विवेश नगरीं लङ्कां पितरं चाभ्युपागमत्॥ ४५॥
verses.m: Indrajit, on the other side, who was a great conjuer, entered the city of Laṅkā, accompanied by all his troops, and approached his father. (45)

verses.text:
तत्र रावणमासाद्य अभिवाद्य कृताञ्जलिः।
आचचक्षे प्रियं पित्रे निहतौ रामलक्ष्मणौ॥ ४६॥
verses.m: Reaching the presence of Rāvaṇa there, and greeting him with joined palms, he broke to his father the delightful news that Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa had been killed.(46)

verses.text:
उत्पपात ततो हृष्टः पुत्रं च परिषस्वजे।
रावणो रक्षसां मध्ये श्रुत्वा शत्रू निपातितौ॥ ४७॥
verses.m: Rejoiced to hear of his two enemies (Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa) having been thrown down, Rāvaṇa forthwith sprang on his feet in the midst of other ogres and hugged his son, Indrajit. (47)

verses.text:
उपाघ्राय च तं मूर्ध्नि पप्रच्छ प्रीतमानसः।
पृच्छते च यथावृत्तं पित्रे तस्मै न्यवेदयत्॥ ४८॥
यथा तौ शरबन्धेन निश्चेष्टौ निष्प्रभौ कृतौ॥ ४९॥
verses.m: Nay, smelling him on the head, Rāvaṇa made inquiries in the matter with a delighted mind. And to his inquisitive father, Rāvaṇa, Indrajit submitted, in accordance with facts, how the two princes (Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa) had been deprived of all movement and splendour by being entwined with arrows in the form of sankes. (48-49)

verses.text:
स हर्षवेगानुगतान्तरात्मा
श्रुत्वा गिरं तस्य महारथस्य।
जहौ ज्वरं दाशरथेः समुत्थं
प्रहृष्टवाचाभिननन्द पुत्रम्॥ ५०॥
verses.m: His inmost being flooded with a gush of joy on hearing the report of that great car-warrior, Rāvaṇa shed his agony caused on account of Śrī Rāma (son of Daśaratha) and acclaimed his son, Indrajit, with words full of excessive joy. (50)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् प्रविष्टे लङ्कायां कृतार्थे रावणात्मजे।
राघवं परिवार्याथ ररक्षुर्वानरर्षभाः॥ १॥
हनुमानङ्गदो नीलः सुषेणः कुमुदो नलः।
गजो गवाक्षो गवयः शरभो गन्धमादनः॥ २॥
जाम्बवानृषभः स्कन्धो रम्भः शतबलिः पृथुः।
व्यूढानीकाश्च यत्ताश्च द्रुमानादाय सर्वतः॥ ३॥
verses.m: Encompassing Śri Rāma (a scion of Raghu), now that the aforesaid son of Rāvaṇa had gone far into Laṅkā, his purpose accomplished, (nay) having drawn up their ranks in battle array and seizing trees, the foremost among the monkeys and bears, viz., Hanumān, Aṅgada. Nīla, Suṣeṇa, Kumuda, Nala, Gaja, Gavākṣa, Śarabha, Gandhamādana, Jāmbavān, Rṣabha, Skandha, Ramabha, Śatabali and Pṛthu, who were always alert, now guarded Śrī Rāma on all sides (lest some harm might come to him). (1—3)

verses.text:
वीक्षमाणा दिशः सर्वास्तिर्यगूर्ध्वं च वानराः।
तृणेष्वपि च चेष्टत्सु राक्षसा इति मेनिरे॥ ४॥
verses.m: Surveying all the quarters, nay, looking up as well on either side, the monkeys thought that ogres had come even when blades of grass stirred. (4)

verses.text:
रावणश्चापि संहृष्टो विसृज्येन्द्रजितं सुतम्।
आजुहाव ततः सीतारक्षणी राक्षसीस्तदा॥ ५॥
verses.m: Having dismissed his son, who had conquered Indra (the ruler of gods), Rāvaṇa too, who felt highly rejoiced, thereupon summoned the ogresses guarding Sītā. (5)

verses.text:
राक्षस्यस्त्रिजटा चापि शासनात् तमुपस्थिताः।
ता उवाच ततो हृष्टो राक्षसी राक्षसाधिपः॥ ६॥
verses.m: The ogresses (in question) as also Trijaṭā waited upon him in response to his command. Full of joy, Rāvaṇa, the suzerain lord of ogres, thereupon spoke as follows to the aforesaid ogresses: (6)

verses.text:
हताविन्द्रजिताख्यात वैदेह्या रामलक्ष्मणौ।
पुष्पकं तत्समारोप्य दर्शयध्वं रणे हतौ॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Speak to Sītā (the princess of the Videha territory) about Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa having been killed by Indrajit. Placing her in the aerial car, Puṣpaka, then show to her the two princes killed in battle. (7)

verses.text:
यदाश्रयादवष्टब्धा नेयं मामुपतिष्ठते।
सोऽस्या भर्ता सह भ्रात्रा निहतो रणमूर्धनि॥ ८॥
verses.m: “That husband of hers, being proud of whose support she does not submit to me, has been killed alongwith his younger brother in the van of a battle. (8)

verses.text:
निर्विशङ्का निरुद्विग्ना निरपेक्षा च मैथिली।
मामुपस्थास्यते सीता सर्वाभरणभूषिता॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Rid of fear, free from perturbation and having lost all hope of meeting her husband, nay, adorned with all her jewels, Sītā, a princess of Mithilā, shall now wait upon me. (9)

verses.text:
अद्य कालवशं प्राप्तं रणे रामं सलक्ष्मणम्।
अवेक्ष्य विनिवृत्ता सा चान्यां गतिमपश्यती॥ १०॥
अनपेक्षा विशालाक्षी मामुपस्थास्यते स्वयम्।
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा रावणस्य दुरात्मनः॥ ११॥
राक्षस्यस्तास्तथेत्युक्त्वा जग्मुर्वै यत्र पुष्पकम्।
ततः पुष्पकमादाय राक्षस्यो रावणाज्ञया॥ १२॥
अशोकवनिकास्थां तां मैथिलीं समुपानयन्।
तामादाय तु राक्षस्यो भर्तृशोकपराजिताम्॥ १३॥
सीतामारोपयामासुर्विमानं पुष्पकं तदा।
ततः पुष्पकमारोप्य सीतां त्रिजटया सह॥ १४॥
जग्मुर्दर्शयितुं तस्यै राक्षस्यो रामलक्ष्मणौ।
रावणश्चारयामास पताकाध्वजमालिनीम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Having turned back (to the Aśoka grove) on seeing Rāma fallen under the sway of Death with Lakṣmaṇa on the field of battle, and finding no other haven, nay, rid of all hope, the large eyed lady will seek me of her own accord today.” Saying “Amen!” on hearing the aforesaid command of that evil-minded Rāvṇa, the ogresses in question moved to the place where Puṣpaka (the aerial car) was. Then, taking Puṣpaka, the ogresses conducted the car under orders of Rāvaṇa to the presence of the celebrated princess of Mithilā, staying in the Aśoka grove. Taking Sītā, who had been overpowered by grief caused by the report about the death of her husband, the ogresses for their part then helped her to ascend the aerial car, Puṣpaka. Then, placing Sītā alongwith Trijaṭā in Puṣpaka, the ogresses proceeded to show Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa to her. In this way Rāvaṇa caused her to fly over Laṅkā (the city dressed with rows of flags and pennons). (10—15)

verses.text:
प्राघोषयत हृष्टश्च लङ्कायां राक्षसेश्वरः।
राघवो लक्ष्मणश्चैव हताविन्द्रजिता रणे॥ १६॥
verses.m: The delighted Rāvaṇa (the lord of ogres) also had it widely proclaimed in Laṅkā that Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) as also Lakṣmaṇa had been killed in combat by Indrajit. (16)

verses.text:
विमानेनापि गत्वा तु सीता त्रिजटया सह।
ददर्श वानराणां तु सर्वं सैन्यं निपातितम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: Flying in the aerial car with Trijaṭā, Sītā for her part beheld a large army of the monkeys actually destroyed. (17)

verses.text:
प्रहृष्टमनसश्चापि ददर्श पिशिताशनान्।
वानरांश्चातिदुःखार्तान् रामलक्ष्मणपार्श्वतः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Nay, she also found the ogres excessively delighted in mind and the monkeys, sore stricken with agony, standing by the side of Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa. (18)

verses.text:
ततः सीता ददर्शोभौ शयानौ शरतल्पगौ।
लक्ष्मणं चैव रामं च विसंज्ञौ शरपीडितौ॥ १९॥
विध्वस्तकवचौ वीरौ विप्रविद्धशरासनौ।
सायकैश्छिन्नसर्वाङ्गौ शरस्तम्बमयौ क्षितौ॥ २०॥
verses.m: Sītā then saw both the heroes, Lakṣmaṇa and Śrī Rāma, laying unconscious on the ground on a bed of arrows, their armour shattered and bows cast aside. (19-20)

verses.text:
तौ दृष्ट्वा भ्रातरौ तत्र प्रवीरौ पुरुषर्षभौ।
शयानौ पुण्डरीकाक्षौ कुमाराविव पावकी॥ २१॥
शरतल्पगतौ वीरौ तथाभूतौ नरर्षभौ।
दुःखार्ता करुणं सीता सुभृशं विललाप ह॥ २२॥
verses.m: Stricken with agony to behold the two gallant brothers, the foremost of men, who were distinguished heroes and jewels among men and had lotus-like eyes, stretched on a bed of arrows in that wretched plight like the two sons of the fire-god (Śākha and Viśākha) lying on a bed of reeds, Sītā wailed piteously and vehemently. (21-22)

verses.text:
भर्तारमनवद्याङ्गी लक्ष्मणं चासितेक्षणा।
प्रेक्ष्य पांसुषु चेष्टन्तौ रुरोद जनकात्मजा॥ २३॥
verses.m: Gazing on her husband as well as on Lakṣmaṇa tossing about in the dust, the dark-eyed Sītā (Janaka’s daughter) of faultless limbs burst into sobs. (23)

verses.text:
सबाष्पशोकाभिहता समीक्ष्य
तौ भ्रातरौ देवसुतप्रभावौ।
वितर्कयन्ती निधनं तयोः सा
दुःखान्विता वाक्यमिदं जगाद॥ २४॥
verses.m: Observing the aforesaid two brothers, who were powerful as the offspring of gods, and suspecting their death, Sītā, full of tears and agony, and smitten with grief, spoke as follows: (24)

verses.text:
भर्तारं निहतं दृष्ट्वा लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम्।
विललाप भृशं सीता करुणं शोककर्शिता॥ १॥
verses.m: On seeing her husband as well as Lakṣmaṇa, who was endowed with extraordinary might, sturck down, Sītā who was already emaciated through grief lamented piteously and vehemently: (1)

verses.text:
ऊचुर्लाक्षणिका ये मां पुत्रिण्यविधवेति च।
तेऽद्य सर्वे हते रामे ज्ञानिनोऽनृतवादिनः॥ २॥
verses.m: “Wise men, capable of reading the lineaments on the person of an individual, who had predicted with reference to me that I would bear sons and would never be widowed, have all turned out to be liars today in that Śrī Rāma has been killed. (2)

verses.text:
यज्वनो महिषीं ये मामूचुः पत्नीं च सत्रिणः।
तेऽद्य सर्वे हते रामे ज्ञानिनोऽनृतवादिनः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “The wise men who had predicted about me that I should be the crowned consort of a performer of sacrifices and an undertaker of long-term sacrificial performances in which a number of priests officiated have proved to be liars today in that Śrī Rāma has been killed. (3)

verses.text:
वीरपार्थिवपत्नीनां ये विदुर्भर्तृपूजिताम्।
तेऽद्य सर्वे हते रामे ज्ञानिनोऽनृतवादिनः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Those wise men who prophesied about me that I should be held as venerable among the consorts of gallant monarchs and honoured by my husband have all proved to be liars today in that Śrī Rāma has been killed. (4)

verses.text:
ऊचुः संश्रवणे ये मां द्विजाः कार्तान्तिकाः शुभाम्।
तेऽद्य सर्वे हते रामे ज्ञानिनोऽनृतवादिनः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Those wise Brāhmaṇas, well-versed in astrology, who had predicted within my hearing that I should remain happy with my husband have all proved to be liars today in that Śrī Rāma has been killed. (5)

verses.text:
इमानि खलु पद्मानि पादयोर्वै कुलस्त्रियः।
आधिराज्येऽभिषिच्यन्ते नरेन्द्रैः पतिभिः सह॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Indeed here are on my soles the marks of a lotus by virtue of which high-born women are actually consecrated on the imperial throne alongwith their lords, who are rulers of men. (6)

verses.text:
वैधव्यं यान्ति यैर्नार्योऽलक्षणैर्भाग्यदुर्लभाः।
नात्मनस्तानि पश्यामि पश्यन्ती हतलक्षणा॥ ७॥
verses.m: “I do not find on my person those sinister marks by virtue of which women to whom good luck is difficult of access meet with widowhood. Even though seeing propitious marks on my limbs, they are proving ineffectual in my case. (7)

verses.text:
सत्यनामानि पद्मानि स्त्रीणामुक्तानि लक्षणैः।
तान्यद्य निहते रामे वितथानि भवन्ति मे॥ ८॥
verses.m: “The marks of a lotus on the person of women, which have been declared as unfailing in their effect by those who are able to read the bodily marks of a man or woman, are proving false in my case today in that Śrī Rāma has been killed. (8)

verses.text:
केशाः सूक्ष्माः समा नीला भ्रुवौ चासंहते मम।
वृत्ते चारोमके जङ्घे दन्ताश्चाविरला मम॥ ९॥
verses.m: “My locks are fine, of even length and dark, my eyebrows are not joined, nay my shanks are round and hairless and my teeth are closely set. (9)

verses.text:
शङ्खे नेत्रे करौ पादौ गुल्फावूरू समौ चितौ।
अनुवृत्तनखाः स्निग्धाः समाश्चाङ्गुलयो मम॥ १०॥
verses.m: “The pairs of my temporal bones, eyes, hands, feet, ankles and thighs are even-shaped and fleshy; nay, the fingers of both my hands are evenly matched, smooth and provided with rounded and well-proportioned nails. (10)

verses.text:
स्तनौ चाविरलौ पीनौ मामकौ मग्नचूचुकौ।
मग्ना चोत्सेधनी नाभिः पार्श्वोरस्कं च मे चितम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “My breasts too are well-knit and fully developed and have depressed nipples; nay, my navel is deep with the surrounding region elevated; while my flanks and bosom are fleshy. (11)

verses.text:
मम वर्णो मणिनिभो मृदून्यङ्गरुहाणि च।
प्रतिष्ठितां द्वादशभिर्मामूचुः शुभलक्षणाम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “My complexion has the sheen of a polished gem, while the hair on my skin are soft. Nay, those who are able to read the bodily marks of an individual spoke of me as endowed with auspicious marks, in that I touched the ground with my twelve limbs, viz., the ten toes and the two soles. (12)

verses.text:
समग्रयवमच्छिद्रं पाणिपादं च वर्णवत्।
मन्दस्मितेत्येव च मां कन्यालाक्षणिका विदुः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Those capable of interpreting the bodily marks of maidens declared my hands and feet to be rosy, devoid of space between the fingers and toes and with the mark of a barley corn fully manifest on them and also spoke of me as distinguished by a gentle smile, which are all auspicious marks. (13)

verses.text:
आधिराज्येऽभिषेको मे ब्राह्मणैः पतिना सह।
कृतान्तकुशलैरुक्तं तत् सर्वं वितथीकृतम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “It was predicted by Brāhmaṇas well-versed in the principles of astrology that I should be consecrated alongwith my husband on the imperial throne. All that has, however, been falsified. (14)

verses.text:
शोधयित्वा जनस्थानं प्रवृत्तिमुपलभ्य च।
तीर्त्वा सागरमक्षोभ्यं भ्रातरौ गोष्पदे हतौ॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Having scoured Janasthāna (in search of me), nay, having crossed the sea, which is incapable of being disturbed, after securing intelligence about me, the two scions of Raghu have been killed in the attempt to overcome the Māyā (sorcery) of Indrajit (which was like the imprint of a cow’s hoof)! (15)

verses.text:
ननु वारुणमाग्नेयमैन्द्रं वायव्यमेव च।
अस्त्रं ब्रह्मशिरश्चैव राघवौ प्रत्यपद्यत॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Surely Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, the two scions of Raghu, knew the use of the mystic missiles presided over by Varuṇa (the god of water), Agni (the god of fire), Indra (the god of rain) as well as of that presided over by Vāyu (the wind-god) as also the use of the missile presided over by Brahmā (the creator). How, then, did they not resort to the use of these missiles as a last resort? (16)

verses.text:
अदृश्यमानेन रणे मायया वासवोपमौ।
मम नाथावनाथाया निहतौ रामलक्ष्मणौ॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, the protectors of this forlorn creature, who were compeers of Indra, have evidently been killed by Indrajit, who remained invisible on the field of battle through a conjuring trick. (17)

verses.text:
नहि दृष्टिपथं प्राप्य राघवस्य रणे रिपुः।
जीवन् प्रतिनिवर्तेत यद्यपि स्यान्मनोजवः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Having come within the range of sight of Śrī Rama (a scion of Raghu) in an encounter, no enemy could return alive, even though he were endowed with the swiftness of thought. (18)

verses.text:
न कालस्यातिभारोऽस्ति कृतान्तश्च सुदुर्जयः।
यत्र रामः सह भ्रात्रा शेते युधि निपातितः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Since Śrī Rāma lies struck down on the field of battle with his younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa, no burden is too heavy to shoulder for Providence (in the form of the Time-Spirit, who is capable of doing anything). Even ‘Death’ (which brings about the end of all) is not very difficult to conquer for Him. (19)

verses.text:
न शोचामि तथा रामं लक्ष्मणं च महारथम्।
नात्मानं जननीं चापि यथा श्वश्रूं तपस्विनीम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “I do not grieve so much for Śrī Rāma and the great car-warrior Lakṣmaṇa nor for myself nor even for my own mother as for my unfortunate mother-in-law, Kausalyā. (20)

verses.text:
सा तु चिन्तयते नित्यं समाप्तव्रतमागतम्।
कदा द्रक्ष्यामि सीतां च लक्ष्मणं च सराघवम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “She, for her part, always remains absorbed in the thought ‘O, when shall I be able to see Lakṣmaṇa returned to Ayodhyā with Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, having completed his vow of remaining in exile in the woods for fourteen years, as also Sītā?’ ” (21)

verses.text:
परिदेवयमानां तां राक्षसी त्रिजटाब्रवीत्।
मा विषादं कृथा देवि भर्तायं तव जीवति॥ २२॥
verses.m: The ogress Trijaṭā spoke as follows to her while Sītā was wailing as aforesaid: “Do not despair, O godlike lady! Your yonder lord is living. (22)

verses.text:
कारणानि च वक्ष्यामि महान्ति सदृशानि च।
यथेमौ जीवतो देवि भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ॥ २३॥
verses.m: “I shall presently adduce mighty and cogent reasons which lead me to believe that these two brothers, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, are still surviving, O godlike lady! (23)

verses.text:
नहि कोपपरीतानि हर्षपर्युत्सुकानि च।
भवन्ति युधि योधानां मुखानि निहते पतौ॥ २४॥
verses.m: “The ruler having been killed, the faces of the warriors operating on the field of battle are never seized by wrath nor are they animated with joy. (24)

verses.text:
इदं विमानं वैदेहि पुष्पकं नाम नामतः।
दिव्यं त्वां धारयेन्नेदं यद्येतौ गतजीवितौ॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Had these two brothers been dead, O princess of the Videha territory, this aerial car, Puṣpaka by name, celestial as it is, would not in any case have borne you (a widowed lady). (25)

verses.text:
हतवीरप्रधाना हि गतोत्साहा निरुद्यमा।
सेना भ्रमति संख्येषु हतकर्णेव नौर्जले॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Having lost its ardour and devoid of effort, an army, whose heroic leader is dead, actually moves to and fro on the field of battle like a vessel which has lost its helmsman. (26)

verses.text:
इयं पुनरसम्भ्रान्ता निरुद्विग्ना तपस्विनि।
सेना रक्षति काकुत्स्थौ मया प्रीत्या निवेदितौ॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Not at all confused or perturbed, this army of monkeys, however, is guarding Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, the two scions of Kakutstha, who have just now been proclaimed by me out of love as alive, O lady given to austerities! (27)

verses.text:
सा त्वं भव सुविस्रब्धा अनुमानैः सुखोदयैः।
अहतौ पश्य काकुत्स्थौ स्नेहादेतद् ब्रवीमि ते॥ २८॥
verses.m: “As such be you completely reassured on the strength of inferences resulting in joy and find the two scions of Kakutstha alive: I speak this to you out of affection for you. (28)

verses.text:
अनृतं नोक्तपूर्वं मे न च वक्ष्यामि मैथिलि।
चारित्रसुखशीलत्वात् प्रविष्टासि मनो मम॥ २९॥
verses.m: “No falsehood has ever been uttered by me in the past nor shall I ever tell a lie, O princess of Mithilā! You have found your way into my mind due to your amiable disposition which has proved to be a source of delight because of your spotless character. (29)

verses.text:
नेमौ शक्यौ रणे जेतुं सेन्द्रैरपि सुरासुरैः।
तादृशं दर्शनं दृष्ट्वा मया चोदीरितं तव॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “These two princes are not vulnerable to being conquered even by gods and demons combined, including Indra, the ruler of gods. Nay, after observing such indications on the face of the two brothers as also on the face of the warriors guarding them, has the fact of the princes being alive been made known by me to you. (30)

verses.text:
इदं तु सुमहच्चित्रं शरैः पश्यस्व मैथिलि।
विसंज्ञौ पतितावेतौ नैव लक्ष्मीर्विमुञ्चति॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Also see for yourself this very great wonder, O princess of Mithilā that bodily splendour does not completely desert these two princes, even though they have fallen unconscious on the ground hit by the arrows. (31)

verses.text:
प्रायेण गतसत्त्वानां पुरुषाणां गतायुषाम्।
दृश्यमानेषु वक्त्रेषु परं भवति वैकृतम्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “An appalling change generally appears on the features, when being observed, of men whose sands of life have run out and whose life-breath has departed for good. (32)

verses.text:
त्यज शोकं च दुःखं च मोहं च जनकात्मजे।
रामलक्ष्मणयोरर्थे नाद्य शक्यमजीवितुम्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “Banish grief and sorrow as well as infatuation on account of Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, O Janaka’s daughter! It is not possible that they be not living at this moment.” (33)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तस्याः सीता सुरसुतोपमा।
कृताञ्जलिरुवाचेमामेवमस्त्विति मैथिली॥ ३४॥
verses.m: Hearing her assurance, the princess of Mithilā, Sītā, for her part, who resembled a daughter of gods, replied with joined palms to her, “May it be so!” (34)

verses.text:
विमानं पुष्पकं तत्तु संनिवर्त्य मनोजवम्।
दीना त्रिजटया सीता लङ्कामेव प्रवेशिता॥ ३५॥
verses.m: After duly sending back the aforesaid aerial car, Puṣpaka, which was swift as thought, the mournful Sītā was caused by Trijaṭā to enter Laṅkā once more. (35)

verses.text:
ततस्त्रिजटया सार्धं पुष्पकादवरुह्य सा।
अशोकवनिकामेव राक्षसीभिः प्रवेशिता॥ ३६॥
verses.m: Descending from Puspaka with Trijaṭā, she was then urged by the ogresses to enter the Aśoka grove again. (36)

verses.text:
प्रविश्य सीता बहुवृक्षखण्डां
तां राक्षसेन्द्रस्य विहारभूमिम्।
सम्प्रेक्ष्य संचिन्त्य च राजपुत्रौ
परं विषादं समुपाजगाम॥ ३७॥
verses.m: Having gone far into and keenly observing that pleasure ground of Rāvaṇa, the ruler of ogres, planted with numerous clusters of trees, nay, having keenly observed and pondered deeply on the two princes, she gave way to extreme despair. (37)

verses.text:
घोरेण शरबन्धेन बद्धौ दशरथात्मजौ।
निःश्वसन्तौ यथा नागौ शयानौ रुधिरोक्षितौ॥ १॥
सर्वे ते वानरश्रेष्ठाः ससुग्रीवमहाबलाः।
परिवार्य महात्मानौ तस्थुः शोकपरिप्लुताः॥ २॥
verses.m: All the aforesaid jewels among monkeys (mentioned in verses 2-3 of Canto XLVII above) including Sugrīva (their ruler), who were endowed with extraordinary might, stood plunged in grief surrounding the two high-souled sons of Emperor Daśaratha, who were lying bathed in blood, hissing like a pair of serpents, bound, as they were, in a formidable network of arrows. (1-2)

verses.text:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे रामः प्रत्यबुध्यत वीर्यवान्।
स्थिरत्वात् सत्त्वयोगाच्च शरैः संदानितोऽपि सन्॥ ३॥
verses.m: In the meantime, by virtue of his hardihood and being endowed with exceptional courage, the powerful Śrī Rāma, though bound by arrows, regained his consciousness. (3)

verses.text:
ततो दृष्ट्वा सरुधिरं निषण्णं गाढमर्पितम्।
भ्रातरं दीनवदनं पर्यदेवयदातुरः॥ ४॥
verses.m: Beholding his younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa, lying tightly bound with arrows, bathed in blood, his face downcast, Śrī Rāma thereupon lamented as follows, distressed as he was: (4)

verses.text:
किं नु मे सीतया कार्यं लब्धया जीवितेन वा।
शयानं योऽद्य पश्यामि भ्रातरं युधि निर्जितम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “What purpose of mine on earth will be accomplished through Sītā, if recovered, or even through my life if preserved when I perceive my younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa, lying utterly vanquished in combat today? (5)

verses.text:
शक्या सीतासमा नारी मर्त्यलोके विचिन्वता।
न लक्ष्मणसमो भ्राता सचिवः साम्परायिकः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “A consort on a par with Sītā can be found in this world of mortals by me if Iwere to look for her. But a helpful and warlike brother like Lakṣmaṇa cannot be had. (6)

verses.text:
परित्यक्ष्याम्यहं प्राणान् वानराणां तु पश्यताम्।
यदि पञ्चत्वमापन्नः सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “I for my part shall yield up my life while the monkeys stand looking on, if Lakṣmaṇa (who enhances the joy of Sumitrā) meets with dissolution (lit. the disintegration of the five elements). (7)

verses.text:
किं नु वक्ष्यामि कौसल्यां मातरं किं नु कैकयीम्।
कथमम्बां सुमित्रां च पुत्रदर्शनलालसाम्॥ ८॥
विवत्सां वेपमानां च वेपन्तीं कुररीमिव।
कथमाश्वासयिष्यामि यदि यास्यामि तं विना ९॥
verses.m: “What on earth shall I say to mother Kausalyā and what on earth to Kaikeyī? And how, in what words shall I console mother Sumitrā, bereft of her darling, Lakṣmaṇa, nay, sighing for the sight of her son, trembling from agitation and crying like a female osprey, if I return to Ayodhyā without Laksmana? (8-9)

verses.text:
कथं वक्ष्यामि शत्रुघ्नं भरतं च यशस्विनम्।
मया सह वनं यातो विना तेनाहमागतः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “How shall I tell Śatrughna and the illustrious Bharata that I have returned without Lakṣmaṇa, who had accompanied me to the woods? (10)

verses.text:
उपालम्भं न शक्ष्यामि सोढुमम्बासुमित्रया।
इहैव देहं त्यक्ष्यामि नहि जीवितुमुत्सहे॥ ११॥
verses.m: “I shall not be able to endure the blame which will be laid on me by mother Sumitrā. As such, I shall cast my body at this very place since I am not inclined to survive. (11)

verses.text:
धिङ् मां दुष्कृतकर्माणमनार्यं यत्कृते ह्यसौ।
लक्ष्मणः पतितः शेते शरतल्पे गतासुवत्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Woe be to me, an ignoble soul of sinful deeds, on account of whom the aforesaid Lakṣmaṇa lies fallen on a bed of arrows like one whose life has departed! (12)

verses.text:
त्वं नित्यं सुविषण्णं मामाश्वासयसि लक्ष्मण।
गतासुर्नाद्य शक्तोऽसि मामार्तमभिभाषितुम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: Turning towards Lakṣmaṇa “You always comforted me when I felt sore dejected, O Lakṣmaṇa! Your life having departed, as it were, you are, however, not able even to speak to me today, distressed as I am. (13)

verses.text:
येनाद्य बहवो युद्धे निहता राक्षसाः क्षितौ।
तस्यामेवाद्य शूरस्त्वं शेषे विनिहतः शनैः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Gallant as you are, you lie struck down with darts today on the same ground on which numerous ogres have been killed by you in combat this very day! (14)

verses.text:
शयानः शरतल्पेऽस्मिन् सशोणितपरिस्रुतः।
शरभूतस्ततो भासि भास्करोऽस्तमिव व्रजन्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Lying on this bed of arrows, bathed in blood, and converted into a bundle of arrows, as it were, you look like the sun sinking below the horizon with the arrows transfixed in the body appearing like its numberless rays and the blood flowing from the numerous cuts accounting for the red glow of the evening sun. (15)

verses.text:
बाणाभिहतमर्मत्वान्न शक्नोषीह भाषितुम्।
रुजा चाब्रुवतो यस्य दृष्टिरागेण सूच्यते॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Your vital parts having been pierced with arrows, you cannot even speak on this occasion. Nay, even though you are not speaking, your anguish is revealed by the redness of your eyes. (16)

verses.text:
यथैव मां वनं यान्तमनुयातो महाद्युतिः।
अहमप्यनुयास्यामि तथैवैनं यमक्षयम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Even as this prince, who is clothed with an extraordinary splendour, followed me while I was retiring to the woods, so I too shall follow him to the abode of Yama. (17)

verses.text:
इष्टबन्धुजनो नित्यं मां च नित्यमनुव्रतः।
इमामद्य गतोऽवस्थां ममानार्यस्य दुर्नयैः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “He who loved his kinsfolk and was ever devoted to me has reached this state through the misdeeds of my ignoble self today. (18)

verses.text:
सुरुष्टेनापि वीरेण लक्ष्मणेन न संस्मरे।
परुषं विप्रियं चापि श्रावितं तु कदाचन॥ १९॥
verses.m: “I do not recollect that a harsh and even an unpalatable word was ever uttered by the gallant Lakṣmaṇa even when he was deeply provoked. (19)

verses.text:
विससर्जैकवेगेन पञ्चबाणशतानि यः।
इष्वस्त्रेष्वधिकस्तस्मात् कार्तवीर्याच्च लक्ष्मणः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Lakṣmaṇa, who shot five hundred arrows at a stretch, was as such superior even to Kārtavīra (who could do so only with his one thousand arms) in the art of shooting arrows. (20)

verses.text:
अस्त्रैरस्त्राणि यो हन्याच्छक्रस्यापि महात्मनः।
सोऽयमुर्व्यां हतः शेते महार्हशयनोचितः॥ २१॥
verses.m: “The same Lakṣmaṇa, who could tear asunder the missiles even of the mighty Indra, the ruler of gods, and who was deserving of reposing on a precious couch, is lying here struck down on the bare ground! (21)

verses.text:
तत्तु मिथ्या प्रलप्तं मां प्रधक्ष्यति न संशयः।
यन्मया न कृतो राजा राक्षसानां विभीषणः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Since Vibhiṣaṇa has not been enthroned by me as the ruler of ogres, that vain pratting of mine that Vibhīṣaṇa would be installed on the throne of Laṅkā will ever consume me: there is no doubt about it.(22)

verses.text:
अस्मिन् मुहूर्ते सुग्रीव प्रतियातुमितोऽर्हसि।
मत्वा हीनं मया राजन् रावणोऽभिभविष्यति॥ २३॥
verses.m: “You ought to return from this place at this very hour, O Sugrīva; for Rāvaṇa will surely overcome you, knowing you to be bereft of me, O king! (23)

verses.text:
अङ्गदं तु पुरस्कृत्य ससैन्यं सपरिच्छदम्।
सागरं तर सुग्रीव नीलेन च नलेन च॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Placing Aṅgada in the forefront alongwith your army and entourage, recross the sea alongwith Nīla and Nala too, O Sugrīva! (24)

verses.text:
कृतं हि सुमहत्कर्म यदन्यैर्दुष्करं रणे।
ऋक्षराजेन तुष्यामि गोलाङ्गूलाधिपेन च॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Indeed, a very great exploit was accomplished by you on the field of battle—an exploit which was difficult to accomplish for others. I am also satisfied with Jāmbavān (the king of bears) as well as with Gavākṣa (the suzerain lord of Golāṅgūlas). (25)

verses.text:
अङ्गदेन कृतं कर्म मैन्देन द्विविदेन च।
युद्धं केसरिणा संख्ये घोरं सम्पातिना कृतम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Acts of valour were performed by Aṅgada, Mainda and Dwivida too, while a formidable struggle was carried on the field of battle by Kesarī (the father of Hanumān) and Sampātī. (26)

verses.text:
गवयेन गवाक्षेण शरभेण गजेन च।
अन्यैश्च हरिभिर्युद्धं मदर्थे त्यक्तजीवितैः॥ २७॥
verses.m: “A struggle was also carried out in my cause by Gavaya, Gavākṣa, Śarabha and Gaja as also by other monkeys, sacrificing their very lives for my sake. (27)

verses.text:
न चातिक्रमितुं शक्यं दैवं सुग्रीव मानुषैः।
यत्तु शक्यं वयस्येन सुहृदा वा परं मम॥ २८॥
कृतं सुग्रीव तत् सर्वं भवता धर्मभीरुणा।
मित्रकार्यं कृतमिदं भवद्भिर्वानरर्षभाः॥ २९॥
अनुज्ञाता मया सर्वे यथेष्टं गन्तुमर्हथ।
शुश्रुवुस्तस्य ये सर्वे वानराः परिदेवितम्॥ ३०॥
वर्तयांचक्रिरेऽश्रूणि नेत्रैः कृष्णेतरेक्षणाः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Destiny cannot be over-ridden by human beings, O Sugrīva! All that could be done by my best friend or ally has been done by you, scrupulous as you are in the matter of duty, O Sugrīva! The purpose of an ally has been accomplished by you, O Jewel among monkeys! Permitted by me, you should go where you will.” All the tawny-eyed monkeys who heard his lamentation as above dropped tears from their eyes. (28—31)

verses.text:
ततः सर्वाण्यनीकानि स्थापयित्वा विभीषणः।
आजगाम गदापाणिस्त्वरितं यत्र राघवः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Having settled all the forces, Vibhīṣaṇa hastened, mace in hand, to the place where Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) lay. (32)

verses.text:
तं दृष्ट्वा त्वरितं यान्तं नीलाञ्जनचयोपमम्।
वानरा दुद्रुवुः सर्वे मन्यमानास्तु रावणिम्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: Seeing Vibhiṣaṇa, who resembled a mass of collyrium, proceeding in haste to the presence of Śrī Rāma and taking him to be Indrajit (son of Rāvaṇa), all the monkeys took to their heels. (33)

verses.text:
अथोवाच महातेजा हरिराजो महाबलः।
किमियं व्यथिता सेना मूढवातेव नौर्जले॥ १॥
verses.m: Now Sugrīva, the ruler of monkeys, who was endowed with extraordinary energy and possessed of great might, inquired saying: “What for is this army disquieted like a bark caught in a whirlwind at sea?” (1)

verses.text:
सुग्रीवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा वालिपुत्रोऽङ्गदोऽब्रवीत्।
न त्वं पश्यसि रामं च लक्ष्मणं च महारथम्॥ २॥
शरजालाचितौ वीरावुभौ दशरथात्मजौ।
शरतल्पे महात्मानौ शयानौ रुधिरोक्षितौ॥ ३॥
verses.m: Hearing the question of Sugrīva, Aṅgada, son of Vālī, said, “Don’t you see the two high-souled heroic sons of Emperor Daśaratha, Śrī Rāma and the great car-warrior, Lakṣmaṇa, lying on a bed of arrows, covered all over with darts and bathed in blood?” (2-3)

verses.text:
अथाब्रवीद् वानरेन्द्रः सुग्रीवः पुत्रमङ्गदम्।
नानिमित्तमिदं मन्ये भवितव्यं भयेन तु॥ ४॥
verses.m: Thereupon Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, spoke as follows to his son (nephew) Aṅgada: “I do not account this stampede, among the monkeys without any immediate reason, other than the bondage of Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa. There needs must be some danger ahead. (4)

verses.text:
विषण्णवदना ह्येते त्यक्तप्रहरणा दिशः।
पलायन्तेऽत्र हरयस्त्रासादुत्फुल्ललोचनाः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Their faces downcast and eyes distressed with terror, these monkeys are actually fleeing at his juncture in all directions, abandoning their arms. (5)

verses.text:
अन्योन्यस्य न लज्जन्ते न निरीक्षन्ति पृष्ठतः।
विप्रकर्षन्ति चान्योन्यं पतितं लङ्घयन्ति च॥ ६॥
verses.m: “While doing so they do not blush at the sight of one another nor do they look behind. Nay, they drag one another (when interrupted) and leap over a fallen companion (without pausing to pick him up).” (6)

verses.text:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे वीरो गदापाणिर्विभीषणः।
सुग्रीवं वर्धयामास राघवं च जयाशिषा॥ ७॥
verses.m: In the meantime, mace in hand, the heroic Vibhiṣaṇa appeared on the scence and cheered Sugrīva and Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, with benedictions of victory. (7)

verses.text:
विभीषणं च सुग्रीवो दृष्ट्वा वानरभीषणम्।
ऋक्षराजं महात्मानं समीपस्थमुवाच ह॥ ८॥
verses.m: Beholding Vibhīṣaṇa, who had caused panic among the monkeys, Sugrīva, they say, spoke as follows to the high-souled Jāmbavān, the king of bears, who stood near: (8)

verses.text:
विभीषणोऽयं सम्प्राप्तो यं दृष्ट्वा वानरर्षभाः।
द्रवन्त्यायतसंत्रासा रावणात्मजशङ्कया॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Here is Vibhīṣaṇa duly arrived, seeing whom the foremost of monkeys are fleeing under the suspicion that he is Indrajit (son of Rāvaṇa) seized as they are with panic at his very sight. (9)

verses.text:
शीघ्रमेतान् सुसंत्रस्तान् बहुधा विप्रधावितान्।
पर्यवस्थापयाख्याहि विभीषणमुपस्थितम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Quickly rally the yonder monkeys who have fled in many directions, greatly alarmed as they are; inform them of Vibhīṣaṇa, and not Indrajit, being present here”. (10)

verses.text:
सुग्रीवेणैवमुक्तस्तु जाम्बवानृक्षपार्थिवः।
वानरान् सान्त्वयामास संनिवर्त्य प्रधावतः॥ ११॥
verses.m: Duly calling the fugitive monkeys back, when commanded as above by Sugrīva, Jāmbavān, the king of bears, for his part restored them to confidence. (11)

verses.text:
ते निवृत्ताः पुनः सर्वे वानरास्त्यक्तसाध्वसाः।
ऋक्षराजवचः श्रुत्वा तं च दृष्ट्वा विभीषणम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: Shaking off their fear on hearing the call of Jāmbavān and perceiving the well-known Vibhīṣaṇa, all the aforesaid monkeys eventually retraced their steps. (12)

verses.text:
विभीषणस्तु रामस्य दृष्ट्वा गात्रं शरैश्चितम्।
लक्ष्मणस्य तु धर्मात्मा बभूव व्यथितस्तदा॥ १३॥
verses.m: Vibhīṣaṇa for his part, whose mind was given to piety, felt distressed on that occasion to see the person of Śrī Rāma as also of Lakṣmaṇa covered with arrows.(13)

verses.text:
जलक्लिन्नेन हस्तेन तयोर्नेत्रे विमृज्य च।
शोकसम्पीडितमना रुरोद विललाप च॥ १४॥
verses.m: Nay, having washed their eyes with his hand dipped in water, his mind tormented with grief, Vibhiṣaṇa wept and wailed (as follows): (14)

verses.text:
इमौ तौ सत्त्वसम्पन्नौ विक्रान्तौ प्रियसंयुगौ।
इमामवस्थां गमितौ राक्षसैः कूटयोधिभिः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “These two well-known and powerful princes, who are endowed with energy and fond of combat, have been reduced to this predicament by ogres fighting in crafty ways! (15)

verses.text:
भ्रातृपुत्रेण चैतेन दुष्पुत्रेण दुरात्मना।
राक्षस्या जिह्मया बुद्ध्या वञ्चितावृजुविक्रमौ॥ १६॥
verses.m: “The two princes, who were exhibiting their prowess in a guileless manner, have been played foul by this evil-minded nephew of mine, an unworthy son of his father through his crooked judgment characteristic of ogres. (16)

verses.text:
शरैरिमावलं विद्धौ रुधिरेण समुक्षितौ।
वसुधायामिमौ सुप्तौ दृश्येते शल्यकाविव॥ १७॥
verses.m: ‘Pierced fiercely by arrows and bathed in blood, these two aforesaid princes are lying on the ground like two porcupines. (17)

verses.text:
ययोर्वीर्यमुपाश्रित्य प्रतिष्ठा काङ् क्षिता मया।
ताविमौ देहनाशाय प्रसुप्तौ पुरुषर्षभौ॥ १८॥
verses.m: ‘These two celebrated jewels among men, banking on whose prowess installation on the throne of Laṅka was sought by me, are lying fast asleep, as it were, waiting for the dissolution of the body. (18)

verses.text:
जीवन्नद्य विपन्नोऽस्मि नष्टराज्यमनोरथः।
प्राप्तप्रतिज्ञश्च रिपुः सकामो रावणः कृतः॥ १९॥
verses.m: ‘My ambition for sovereignty having been frustrated, I am as good as dead, though alive, nay, having had his vow (of not returning Sītā) fulfilled, the enemy, Rāvaṇa, has been enabled by his son to realize his ambition of retaining Sītā in his possession.’ (19)

verses.text:
एवं विलपमानं तं परिष्वज्य विभीषणम्।
सुग्रीवः सत्त्वसम्पन्नो हरिराजोऽब्रवीदिदम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: Embracing Vibhīṣaṇa, who was lamenting as above, Sugrīva, the ruler of monkeys, who was endowed with energy, reassured him in the following words: (20)

verses.text:
राज्यं प्राप्स्यसि धर्मज्ञ लङ्कायां नेह संशयः।
रावणः सह पुत्रेण स्वकामं नेह लप्स्यते॥ २१॥
verses.m: “You shall attain the sovereignty of Laṅkā, there is no doubt about it, O knower of what is right! With his son Indrajit, Rāvaṇa will not be able to attain the object of his desire in this life. (21)

verses.text:
गरुडाधिष्ठितावेतावुभौ राघवलक्ष्मणौ।
त्यक्त्वा मोहं वधिष्येते सगणं रावणं रणे॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Having shaken off their spell of unconsciousness, and mounted on Garuḍa (the king of birds and the carrier of Lord viṣṇu), both Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) and Lakṣmaṇa will make short work of Rāvaṇa with his hordes on the field of battle.” (22)

verses.text:
तमेवं सान्त्वयित्वा तु समाश्वास्य तु राक्षसम्।
सुषेणं श्वशुरं पार्श्वे सुग्रीवस्तमुवाच ह॥ २३॥
verses.m: Having consoled and reassured the aforesaid ogre, Vibhīsaṇa, in the foregoing words, Sugrīva for his part spoke as follows to his father-in-law, Suṣeṇa, standing by his side: (23)

verses.text:
सह शूरैर्हरिगणैर्लब्धसंज्ञावरिंदमौ।
गच्छ त्वं भ्रातरौ गृह्य किष्किन्धां रामलक्ष्मणौ॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Accompanied by heroic simian troops, proceed you to Kiṣkindhā, taking with you the two brothers, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, the tamers of their enemies, as soon as they have regained consciousness. (24)

verses.text:
अहं तु रावणं हत्वा सपुत्रं सहबान्धवम्।
मैथिलीमानयिष्यामि शक्रो नष्टामिव श्रियम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Having disposed of Rāvaṇa with his sons and relatives, I, for my part, shall bring back Sītā (a princess of Mithilā) even as Indra (the ruler of paradise) recovered his lost royal fortune from the hands of demons.” (25)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वैतद् वानरेन्द्रस्य सुषेणो वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
देवासुरं महायुद्धमनुभूतं पुरातनम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: Hearing this command of Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, Suṣeṇa submitted as follows: “A major conflict which took place between the gods and the demons in the days gone by was witnessed by me. (26)

verses.text:
तदा स्म दानवा देवान् शरसंस्पर्शकोविदान्।
निजघ्नुः शस्त्रविदुषश्छादयन्तो मुहुर्मुहुः॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Concealing themselves by means of conjuring tricks on that occasion, the demons overwhelmed again and again the gods, even though the latter were skilled in aiming at their mark and adept in the use of arms. (27)

verses.text:
तानार्तान् नष्टसंज्ञांश्च गतासूंश्च बृहस्पतिः।
विद्याभिर्मन्त्रयुक्ताभिरोषधीभिश्चिकित्सति ॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Sage Bṛhaspati (the preceptor and arch-priest of gods) restored to health and life the gods who were wounded and rendered unconscious as also those who had lost their life, by means of prayers and remedies accompanied by the recitation of sacred texts. (28)

verses.text:
तान्यौषधान्यानयितुं क्षीरोदं यान्तु सागरम्।
जवेन वानराः शीघ्रं सम्पातिपनसादयः॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Let monkeys headed by Sampāti and Panasa proceed quickly with a swift pace to the ocean of milk to fetch the aforesaid medicines. (29)

verses.text:
हरयस्तु विजानन्ति पार्वती ते महौषधी।
संजीवकरणीं दिव्यां विशल्यां देवनिर्मिताम्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Those monkeys (Sampāti and others) for their part correctly know two great mountain herbs, the wonderful Sañjīvakaraṇī (bringing back to life) and Viśalyā (capable of healing wounds inflicted by arrows), evolved by Brahmā. (30)

verses.text:
चन्द्रश्च नाम द्रोणश्च क्षीरोदे सागरोत्तमे।
अमृतं यत्र मथितं तत्र ते परमौषधी॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “On the bank of the ocean of milk, the foremost of oceans, from which was churned out nectar (the drink of immortality), are two mountains, Candra and Droṇa by name: the aforesaid two great herbs exist there. (31)

verses.text:
तौ तत्र विहितौ देवैः पर्वतौ तौ महोदधौ।
अयं वायुसुतो राजन् हनूमांस्तत्र गच्छतु॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Those two well-known mountains were placed in that ocean by the gods themselves. Let the yonder Hanumān, son of the wind-god, proceed there.” (32)

verses.text:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे वायुर्मेघाश्चापि सविद्युतः।
पर्यस्य सागरे तोयं कम्पयन्निव पर्वतान्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: In the meantime there arose a wind—as well as clouds accompanied by flashes of lightning—which, having whipped up the sea-water, began to shake the mountains, as it were. (33)

verses.text:
महता पक्षवातेन सर्वद्वीपमहाद्रुमाः।
निपेतुर्भग्नविटपाः सलिले लवणाम्भसि॥ ३४॥
verses.m: Their boughs broken by that mighty wind caused by the flutter of wings, large trees of the entire island of Laṅkā fell headlong into the water of the salt sea. (34)

verses.text:
अभवन् पन्नगास्त्रस्ता भोगिनस्तत्रवासिनः।
शीघ्रं सर्वाणि यादांसि जग्मुश्च लवणार्णवम्॥ ३५॥
verses.m: The huge serpents inhabiting that island got alarmed, nay, all the sea-monsters, which had crawled to the shore, quickly (re-) entered the salt sea. (35)

verses.text:
ततो मुहूर्ताद् गरुडं वैनतेयं महाबलम्।
वानरा ददृशुः सर्वे ज्वलन्तमिव पावकम्॥ ३६॥
verses.m: In an instant all the monkeys saw Garuḍa (the king of birds and a carrier of lord Viṣṇu), son of Vinatā, who is endowed with extraordinary might, and resembled a blazing fire in brilliance. (36)

verses.text:
तमागतमभिप्रेक्ष्य नागास्ते विप्रदुद्रुवुः।
यैस्तु तौ पुरुषौ बद्धौ शरभूतैर्महाबलैः॥ ३७॥
verses.m: Perceiving him arrived on the scene, those serpents, for their part, by which, serving as arrows, the aforesaid two personages, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, had been bound and which were endowed with extraordinary might, fled away for good.(37)

verses.text:
ततः सुपर्णः काकुत्स्थौ स्पृष्ट्वा प्रत्यभिनन्द्य च।
विममर्श च पाणिभ्यां मुखे चन्द्रसमप्रभे॥ ३८॥
verses.m: Touching Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, the two scions of Kakutstha, and wishing them victory, Garuḍa, of beautiful wings, then wiped with his hands their faces, which shone like the moon. (38)

verses.text:
वैनतेयेन संस्पृष्टास्तयोः संरुरुहुर्व्रणाः।
सुवर्णे च तनू स्निग्धे तयोराशु बभूवतुः॥ ३९॥
verses.m: Duly touched by Garuḍa (son of Vinatā), their wounds got cicatrized and their bodies immediately turned bright and smooth. (39)

verses.text:
तेजो वीर्यं बलं चौज उत्साहश्च महागुणाः।
प्रदर्शनं च बुद्धिश्च स्मृतिश्च द्विगुणा तयोः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: Their majesty, prowess, strength and splendour as well as dash, perspicacity and intelligence as also memory got redoubled. (40)

verses.text:
तावुत्थाप्य महातेजा गरुडो वासवोपमौ।
उभौ च सस्वजे हृष्टो रामश्चैनमुवाच ह॥ ४१॥
verses.m: Raising the two princes, who were the compeers of Indra (the ruler of gods), Garuḍa, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, joyfully embraced them both; and Śrī Rāma, they say, spoke to him as follows: (41)

verses.text:
भवत्प्रसादाद् व्यसनं रावणिप्रभवं महत्।
उपायेन व्यतिक्रान्तौ शीघ्रं च बलिनौ कृतौ॥ ४२॥
verses.m: “Thanks to your goodwill, we two have by recourse to a remedy passed over the great danger that proceeded from Indrajit (son of Rāvaṇa) and have also been quickly made strong again. (42)

verses.text:
यथा तातं दशरथं यथाजं च पितामहम्।
तथा भवन्तमासाद्य हृदयं मे प्रसीदति॥ ४३॥
verses.m: “My heart rejoices to meet you in the same way as it would on meeting my father, Daśaratha, or my grandfather, Aja. (43)

verses.text:
को भवान् रूपसम्पन्नो दिव्यस्रगनुलेपनः।
वसानो विरजे वस्त्रे दिव्याभरणभूषितः॥ ४४॥
verses.m: “By the way, who are you, richly endowed as you are with bodily charm, decked with celestial garlands and anointed with ethereal unguents, wearing a pair of garments free from dust and adorned with celestial jewels?” (44)

verses.text:
तमुवाच महातेजा वैनतेयो महाबलः।
पतत्रिराजः प्रीतात्मा हर्षपर्याकुलेक्षणम्॥ ४५॥
verses.m: With a delighted mind Garuḍa (son of Vinatā), the king of birds, who was endowed with extraordinary energy and was full of great might, replied as follows to Śrī Rāma, whose eyes were wild with joy: (45)

verses.text:
अहं सखा ते काकुत्स्थ प्रियः प्राणो बहिश्चरः।
गरुत्मानिह सम्प्राप्तो युवयोः साह्यकारणात्॥ ४६॥
verses.m: “I am Garuḍa, your beloved friend, nay, your very breath moving outside, arrived here for your help O scion of Kakutstha! (46)

verses.text:
असुरा वा महावीर्या दानवा वा महाबलाः।
सुराश्चापि सगन्धर्वाः पुरस्कृत्य शतक्रतुम्॥ ४७॥
नेमं मोक्षयितुं शक्ताः शरबन्धं सुदारुणम्।
मायाबलादिन्द्रजिता निर्मितं क्रूरकर्मणा॥ ४८॥
verses.m: “Demons endowed with extraordinary prowess or giants possessed of great might, nay, even gods accompanied by Gandharvas, if they made their appearance here, placing Indra (who is presupposed to have performed a hundred sacrifices in his past life as a condition precedent for his attaining the position of Indra) at their head, would not have been able to undo these most formidable bonds wrought with arrows by Indrajit of ruthless deeds by dint of magic. (47-48)

verses.text:
एते नागाः काद्रवेयास्तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रा विषोल्बणाः।
रक्षोमायाप्रभावेण शरभूतास्त्वदाश्रयाः॥ ४९॥
verses.m: “These snakes, which had fettered you, were no other than the sons of Kadrū with sharp fangs and full of poison, converted into arrows by dint of conjuring tricks employed by the ogre, Indrajit. (49)

verses.text:
सभाग्यश्चासि धर्मज्ञ राम सत्यपराक्रम।
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा समरे रिपुघातिना॥ ५०॥
verses.m: “Indeed you are lucky with your younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa, the destroyer of his foes in combat, O Rāma of unfailing prowess, the knower of what is right! (50)

verses.text:
इमं श्रुत्वा तु वृत्तान्तं त्वरमाणोऽहमागतः।
सहसैवावयोः स्नेहात् सखित्वमनुपालयन्॥ ५१॥
verses.m: “Hearing this news of your having been fettered by snakes, and vindicating the friendship existing between us two, I, for my part, have hastened to this place all at once out of affection for you. (51)

verses.text:
मोक्षितौ च महाघोरादस्मात् सायकबन्धनात्।
अप्रमादश्च कर्तव्यो युवाभ्यां नित्यमेव हि॥ ५२॥
verses.m: “And you both have been liberated from this most formidable bond wrought with arrows. Nay, you should actually remain on your guard all the time. (52)

verses.text:
प्रकृत्या राक्षसाः सर्वे संग्रामे कूटयोधिनः।
शूराणां शुद्धभावानां भवतामार्जवं बलम्॥ ५३॥
verses.m: “All ogres are by nature given to fighting treacherously on the field of battle; while guilelessness is the strength of you gallant souls with a pure mind. (53)

verses.text:
तन्न विश्वसनीयं वो राक्षसानां रणाजिरे।
एतेनैवोपमानेन नित्यं जिह्मा हि राक्षसाः॥ ५४॥
verses.m: “On this very analogy you should never trust the ogres on the field of battle; for ogres are always crooked.” (54)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा तदा रामं सुपर्णः स महाबलः।
परिष्वज्य च सुस्निग्धमाप्रष्टुमुपचक्रमे॥ ५५॥
verses.m: Having spoken as aforesaid and embraced Śrī Rāma most tenderly, the aforesaid Garuḍa, who was endowed with extraordinary might, proceeded to take leave of Śrī Rāma in the following words: (55)

verses.text:
सखे राघव धर्मज्ञ रिपूणामपि वत्सल।
अभ्यनुज्ञातुमिच्छामि गमिष्यामि यथासुखम्॥ ५६॥
verses.m: “I wish to take leave of you, my friend, Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), a knower of what is right and fond even of your enemies! I shall now depart at ease. (56)

verses.text:
न च कौतूहलं कार्यं सखित्वं प्रति राघव।
कृतकर्मा रणे वीर सखित्वं प्रतिवेत्स्यसि॥ ५७॥
verses.m: “And you should not entertain any curiosity about our friendship, O scion of Raghu! On having accomplished your duty on the field of battle you will come to recognize our friendship, O gallant prince! (57)

verses.text:
बालवृद्धावशेषां तु लङ्कां कृत्वा शरोर्मिभिः।
रावणं तु रिपुं हत्वा सीतां त्वमुपलप्स्यसे॥ ५८॥
verses.m: “Having actually emptied Laṅkā of all its male population, except for its youngsters and the aged, with the volleys of your arrows having killed your enemy, Rāvaṇa, you will surely recover Sītā.” (58)

verses.text:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा वचनं सुपर्णः शीघ्रविक्रमः।
रामं च नीरुजं कृत्वा मध्ये तेषां वनौकसाम्॥ ५९॥
प्रदक्षिणं ततः कृत्वा परिष्वज्य च वीर्यवान्।
जगामाकाशमाविश्य सुपर्णः पवनो यथा॥ ६०॥
verses.m: Having made the aforesaid submission in the midst of those monkeys (lit., denizens of the forest), and rid Śrī Rāma of his pain, then walking clockwise round him as a mark of submission and embracing him, the valiant Garuḍa of beautiful wings and swift flight soared to the heavens with the speed of the wind. (59-60)

verses.text:
नीरुजौ राघवौ दृष्ट्वा ततो वानरयूथपाः।
सिंहनादं तदा नेदुर्लाङ्गूलं दुधुवुश्च ते॥ ६१॥
verses.m: Seeing Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, the two scions of Raghu, rid of anguish, the commanders of simian troops thereupon roared like lions at that time and lashed their tails. (61)

verses.text:
ततो भेरीः समाजघ्नुर्मृदङ्गांश्चाप्यवादयन्।
दध्मुः शङ्खान् सम्प्रहृष्टाः क्ष्वेलन्त्यपि यथापुरम्॥ ६२॥
verses.m: The monkeys then beat their kettledrums and played upon their clay tomtoms, blew their conches in excessive joy and began to leap and jump as before. (62)

verses.text:
अपरे स्फोट्य विक्रान्ता वानरा नगयोधिनः।
द्रुमानुत्पाट्य विविधांस्तस्थुः शतसहस्रशः॥ ६३॥
verses.m: Uprooting trees of various species and brandishing them, other valiant monkeys, who fought with trees, stood ready to fight in hundreds of thousands. (63)

verses.text:
विसृजन्तो महानादांस्त्रासयन्तो निशाचरान्।
लङ्काद्वाराण्युपाजग्मुर्योद्धुकामाः प्लवंगमाः॥ ६४॥
verses.m: Emitting piercing cries and frightening the prowlers of the night, the bellicose monkeys reached the gates of Laṅkā. (64)

verses.text:
तेषां सुभीमस्तुमुलो निनादो
बभूव शाखामृगयूथपानाम्।
क्षये निदाघस्य यथा घनानां
नादः सुभीमो नदतां निशीथे॥ ६५॥
verses.m: An extremely appalling and tumultuous clamour arose amongst the aforesaid commanders of simian troops, which resembled the most terrible thundering of clouds rumbling at midnight at the end of summer. (65)

verses.text:
तेषां तु तुमुलं शब्दं वानराणां महौजसाम्।
नर्दतां राक्षसैः सार्धं तदा शुश्राव रावणः॥ १॥
verses.m: Accompanied by ogres, Rāvaṇa for his part heard at that moment the tumultuous noise of those roaring monkeys, who were endowed with extraordinary energy. (1)

verses.text:
स्निग्धगम्भीरनिर्घोषं श्रुत्वा तं निनदं भृशम्।
सचिवानां ततस्तेषां मध्ये वचनमब्रवीत्॥ २॥
verses.m: Hearing that loud noise, producing a merry and deep sound, Rāvaṇa then spoke as follows in the midst of the aforesaid counsellors: (2)

verses.text:
यथासौ सम्प्रहृष्टानां वानराणामुपस्थितः।
बहूनां सुमहान् नादो मेघानामिव गर्जताम्॥ ३॥
सुव्यक्तं महती प्रीतिरेतेषां नात्र संशयः।
तथाहि विपुलैर्नादैश्चुक्षुभे लवणार्णवः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “From the way in which that very great uproar, resembling the thunder of rumbling clouds, has arisen from the innumerable overjoyed monkeys, it is sufficiently evident that their joy is great: there is no doubt about it. That is how the salt sea has been agitated by their mighty shouts. (3-4)

verses.text:
तौ तु बद्धौ शरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।
अयं च सुमहान् नादः शङ्कां जनयतीव मे॥ ५॥
verses.m: “While those two brothers, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, lie bound with sharp arrows, this tremendous outcry gives rise to a suspicion in my mind that the two brothers have been freed from their bondage.” (5)

verses.text:
एवं च वचनं चोक्त्वा मन्त्रिणो राक्षसेश्वरः।
उवाच नैर्ऋतांस्तत्र समीपपरिवर्तिनः॥ ६॥
verses.m: Having addressed the foregoing words to his counsellors, Rāvaṇa (the lord of ogres) spoke as follows to the ogres standing near him on that spot: (6)

verses.text:
ज्ञायतां तूर्णमेतेषां सर्वेषां च वनौकसाम्।
शोककाले समुत्पन्ने हर्षकारणमुत्थितम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Let the cause of rejoicing that has sprung up for all these monkeys (lit., denizens of the woods) when an occasion for grief had already arisen, be speedily found out.” (7)

verses.text:
तथोक्तास्ते सुसम्भ्रान्ताः प्राकारमधिरुह्य च।
ददृशुः पालितां सेनां सुग्रीवेण महात्मना॥ ८॥
verses.m: Scaling the defensive wall, when commanded as above by Rāvaṇa, the ogres, who felt somewhat depressed, beheld the army protected by the high-souled Sugrīva. (8)

verses.text:
तौ च मुक्तौ सुघोरेण शरबन्धेन राघवौ।
समुत्थितौ महाभागौ विषेदुः सर्वराक्षसाः॥ ९॥
verses.m: Nay, all the ogres felt despondent on seeing those two highly fortunate scions of Raghu, viz., Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa fully active, freed, as they were, from their most formidable bondage wrought with arrows. (9)

verses.text:
संत्रस्तहृदयाः सर्वे प्राकारादवरुह्य ते।
विवर्णा राक्षसा घोरा राक्षसेन्द्रमुपस्थिताः॥ १०॥
verses.m: Descending from the defensive wall, all those fierce ogres, who looked pale, greatly frightened as they were at heart, approached Rāvaṇa, the ruler of ogres. (10)

verses.text:
तदप्रियं दीनमुखा रावणस्य च राक्षसाः।
कृत्स्नं निवेदयामासुर्यथावद् वाक्यकोविदाः॥ ११॥
verses.m: Nay, with downcast mien the ogres, who were skilled in speech, faithfully communicated to Rāvaṇa the whole unpleasant tidings in the following words:(11)

verses.text:
यौ ताविन्द्रजिता युद्धे भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।
निबद्धौ शरबन्धेन निष्प्रकम्पभुजौ कृतौ॥ १२॥
विमुक्तौ शरबन्धेन दृश्येते तौ रणाजिरे।
पाशानिव गजौ छित्त्वा गजेन्द्रसमविक्रमौ॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Those two celebrated brothers, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, who are powerful like two lordly elephants, nay, who had been tightly bound by Indrajit with bonds of arrows and whose arms had been pinioned (i.e. unshakeable), are seen on the field of battle, freed from their bonds of arrows like a pair of elephants that have snapped their fetters.” (12-13)

verses.text:
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तेषां राक्षसेन्द्रो महाबलः।
चिन्ताशोकसमाक्रान्तो विवर्णवदनोऽभवत्॥ १४॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid report of those ogres, Rāvaṇa (the lord of ogres), who was endowed with extraordinary might, lost the colour of his face, overwhelmed as he was with anxiety and grief. (14)

verses.text:
घोरैर्दत्तवरैर्बद्धौ शरैराशीविषोपमैः।
अमोघैः सूर्यसंकाशैः प्रमथ्येन्द्रजिता युधि॥ १५॥
तदस्त्रबन्धमासाद्य यदि मुक्तौ रिपू मम।
संशयस्थमिदं सर्वमनुपश्याम्यहं बलम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: He said to himself: “If my adversaries (Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa)—who had been tightly bound in combat by Indrajit with formidable and infallible arrows, which had been conferred on him as boons, which resembled serpents and shone brightly like the sun—have been liberated even on getting bound with missiles, I perceive my entire army in jeopardy. (15-16)

verses.text:
निष्फलाः खलु संवृत्ताः शराः पावकतेजसः।
आदत्तं यैस्तु संग्रामे रिपूणां जीवितं मम॥ १७॥
verses.m: “My darts, bright as fire, by which the life of my adversaries was unmistakably taken away in combat, have surely turned infructuous.” (17)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा तु संक्रुद्धो निःश्वसन्नुरगो यथा।
अब्रवीद् रक्षसां मध्ये धूम्राक्षं नाम राक्षसम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: Having spoken as aforesaid to himself and hissing like a serpent, infuriated as he was, Rāvaṇa commanded the ogre, Dhūmrākṣa by name, in the midst of other ogres as follows : (18)

verses.text:
बलेन महता युक्तो रक्षसां भीमविक्रम।
त्वं वधायाशु निर्याहि रामस्य सह वानरैः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Sally you forth at once with a huge army of ogres for the destruction of Rāma with the monkeys, O ogre of redoubtable prowess !” (19)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तु धूम्राक्षो राक्षसेन्द्रेण धीमता।
परिक्रम्य ततः शीघ्रं निर्जगाम नृपालयात्॥ २०॥
verses.m: Walking round him when commanded as above by the crafty Rāvaṇa (the ruler of ogres), Dhūmrākṣa for his part sallied forth without delay from that palace. (20)

verses.text:
अभिनिष्क्रम्य तद् द्वारं बलाध्यक्षमुवाच ह।
त्वरयस्व बलं शीघ्रं किं चिरेण युयुत्सतः॥ २१॥
verses.m: Issuing from the gate of that palace, he spoke as follows to the Commander-in-Chief of the army: “Mobilize the army speedily; what need is there for delay to a man courting war?” (21)

verses.text:
धूम्राक्षवचनं श्रुत्वा बलाध्यक्षो बलानुगः।
बलमुद्योजयामास रावणस्याज्ञया भृशम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: Hearing the call of Dhūmrākṣa, the Commander-in-Chief, who was followed by a large contingent, quickly mobilized a battalion in obedience to the command of Rāvaṇa. (22)

verses.text:
ते बद्धघण्टा बलिनो घोररूपा निशाचराः।
विनद्यमानाः संहृष्टा धूम्राक्षं पर्यवारयन्॥ २३॥
verses.m: Roaring exultantly, those mighty ogres of terrible aspet with girdles of bells fastened round their waist, ranged round Dhūmrākṣa. (23)

verses.text:
विविधायुधहस्ताश्च शूलमुद्गरपाणयः।
गदाभिः पट्टिशैर्दण्डैरायसैर्मुसलैरपि॥ २४॥
परिघैर्भिन्दिपालैश्च भल्लैः पाशैः परश्वधैः।
निर्ययू राक्षसा घोरा नर्दन्तो जलदा यथा॥ २५॥
verses.m: Carrying weapons of every description such as pikes and mallets in their hands and armed with maces, sharp-edged spears, iron cudgels as well as with clubs, iron bars, Bhindipālas (a kind of sling for forcefully throwing stones), lances, nooses and axes, the redoubtable ogres sallied forth, thundering like clouds. (24-25)

verses.text:
रथैः कवचिनस्त्वन्ये ध्वजैश्च समलंकृतैः।
सुवर्णजालविहितैः खरैश्च विविधाननैः॥ २६॥
हयैः परमशीघ्रैश्च गजैश्चैव मदोत्कटैः।
निर्ययुर्नैर्ऋतव्याघ्रा व्याघ्रा इव दुरासदाः॥ २७॥
verses.m: Clad in mail, other tigers among ogres issued forth, like tigers which are difficult to approach, in chariots magnificently dressed with flags and covered with a lattice-work of gold as well as on the back of donkeys with heads of every description as also exceedingly fleet horses and elephants maddened with ichor. (26-27)

verses.text:
वृकसिंहमुखैर्युक्तं खरैः कनकभूषितैः।
आरुरोह रथं दिव्यं धूम्राक्षः खरनिःस्वनः॥ २८॥
verses.m: Dhūmrākṣa, whose voice resembled the braying of a donkey, mounted a wonderful chariot driven by donkeys with harness of gold and heads resembling those of a wolf and a lion. (28)

verses.text:
स निर्यातो महावीर्यो धूम्राक्षो राक्षसैर्वृतः।
हसन् वै पश्चिमद्वाराद्धनूमान् यत्र तिष्ठति॥ २९॥
verses.m: Surrounded by ogres, the notorious Dhūmrākṣa, who was endowed with extraordinary prowess, actually set forth laughing through the western gate, where Hanumān had taken up his stand. (29)

verses.text:
रथप्रवरमास्थाय खरयुक्तं खरस्वनम्।
प्रयान्तं तु महाघोरं राक्षसं भीमदर्शनम्॥ ३०॥
अन्तरिक्षगताः क्रूराः शकुनाः प्रत्यषेधयन्।
रथशीर्षे महाभीमो गृध्रश्च निपपात ह॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Ferocious birds appearing in the air for their part deterred that exceedingly formidable ogre of terrible aspect, whose voice resembled the braying of a donkey, while he was sallying forth taking his seat in a highly excellent chariot driven by donkeys. Nay, an exceedingly terrible vulture alighted on the top of his chariot; so the tradition goes. (30-31)

verses.text:
ध्वजाग्रे ग्रथिताश्चैव निपेतुः कुणपाशनाः।
रुधिरार्द्रो महान् श्वेतः कबन्धः पतितो भुवि॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Birds feasting on dead bodies and interlocked with one another in combat also descended on the point of his standard. A huge headless lurid trunk, wet with blood, also fell on the ground before him. (32)

verses.text:
विस्वरं चोत्सृजन्नादान् धूम्राक्षस्य निपातितः।
ववर्ष रुधिरं देवः संचचाल च मेदिनी॥ ३३॥
verses.m: The trunk hurled by someone in front of Dhūmrākṣa lay emitting cries discordantly. The rain-god poured down blood and the earth shook. (33)

verses.text:
प्रतिलोमं ववौ वायुर्निर्घातसमनिःस्वनः।
तिमिरौघावृतास्तत्र दिशश्च न चकाशिरे॥ ३४॥
verses.m: The wind blew adversely with a thunder-like roar. And shrouded, as they were, with a mass of darkness, the quarters could not be discerned. (34)

verses.text:
स तूत्पातांस्ततो दृष्ट्वा राक्षसानां भयावहान्।
प्रादुर्भूतान् सुघोरांश्च धूम्राक्षो व्यथितोऽभवत्।
मुमुहू राक्षसाः सर्वे धूम्राक्षस्य पुरःसराः॥ ३५॥
verses.m: Dhūmrākṣa for his part felt perturbed at that time to behold most terrible portents, boding danger to the ogres, which had come to light before him. Nay, all the ogres marching in front of Dhūmrākṣa fainted.(35)

verses.text:
ततः सुभीमो बहुभिर्निशाचरै-
र्वृतोऽभिनिष्क्रम्य रणोत्सुको बली।
ददर्श तां राघवबाहुपालितां
महौघकल्पां बहु वानरीं चमूम्॥ ३६॥
verses.m: Sallying forth in front of his adversaries accompanied as he was by numerous ogres, the mighty and most redoubtable general, who was eager for a fight, beheld that army consisting of innumerable monkeys, nay, looking like the ocean at the time of universal dissolution and protected by the arms of Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu). (36)

verses.text:
धूम्राक्षं प्रेक्ष्य निर्यान्तं राक्षसं भीमविक्रमम्।
विनेदुर्वानराः सर्वे प्रहृष्टा युद्धकाङ्क्षिणः॥ १॥
verses.m: Highly rejoiced, all the monkeys, who were itching for a combat, emitted loud cries on perceiving the ogre general, Dhūmrākṣa of terrible prowess, sallying forth. (1)

verses.text:
तेषां सुतुमुलं युद्धं संजज्ञे कपिरक्षसाम्।
अन्योन्यं पादपैर्घोरैर्निघ्नतां शूलमुद्गरैः॥ २॥
verses.m: An exceedingly tumultuous conflict raged between those monkeys and the ogres, striking the other with formidable trees on one hand and pikes and clubs on the other. (2)

verses.text:
राक्षसैर्वानरा घोरा विनिकृत्ताः समन्ततः।
वानरै राक्षसाश्चापि द्रुमैर्भूमिसमीकृताः॥ ३॥
verses.m: The redoubtable monkeys were mowed down on all sides by the ogres and the ogres too were levelled to the ground by means of trees by the monkeys. (3)

verses.text:
राक्षसास्त्वभिसंक्रुद्धा वानरान् निशितैः शरैः।
विव्यधुर्घोरसंकाशैः कङ्कपत्रैरजिह्मगैः॥ ४॥
verses.m: Highly enraged, the ogres for their part transfixed the monkeys with pointed arrows which were fearful to behold, were furnished with the plumes of a buzzard and flew straight to the target. (4)

verses.text:
ते गदाभिश्च भीमाभिः पट्टिशैः कूटमुद्गरैः।
घोरैश्च परिघैश्चित्रैस्त्रिशूलैश्चापि संश्रितैः॥ ५॥
विदार्यमाणा रक्षोभिर्वानरास्ते महाबलाः।
अमर्षजनितोद्धर्षाश्चक्रुः कर्माण्यभीतवत्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Full of martial ardour born of indignation while being split asunder by the ogres with terrible maces, sharp-edged spears, iron and wooden mallets and formidable iron bars as well as with tridents of various kinds held in the hand, the aforesaid monkeys, who were endowed with extraordinary might, accomplished deeds of valour as though they were intrepid. (5-6)

verses.text:
शरनिर्भिन्नगात्रास्ते शूलनिर्भिन्नदेहिनः।
जगृहुस्ते द्रुमांस्तत्र शिलाश्च हरियूथपाः॥ ७॥
verses.m: Their limbs torn asunder with arrows and having their bodies split asunder with pikes, the aforesaid monkey generals seized hold of trees and rocks on the field of battle. (7)

verses.text:
ते भीमवेगा हरयो नर्दमानास्ततस्ततः।
ममन्थू राक्षसान् वीरान् नामानि च बभाषिरे॥ ८॥
verses.m: Endowed, as they were, with terrific impetuosity, those monkeys crushed the valiant ogres here and there, roaring all the time and proclaimed their names. (8)

verses.text:
तद् बभूवाद्भुतं घोरं युद्धं वानररक्षसाम्।
शिलाभिर्विविधाभिश्च बहुशाखैश्च पादपैः॥ ९॥
verses.m: That terrible conflict between the monkeys and the ogres, carried on with rocks of various kinds and trees consisting of numerous boughs, was wondrous indeed. (9)

verses.text:
राक्षसा मथिताः केचिद् वानरैर्जितकाशिभिः।
प्रवेमू रुधिरं केचिन्मुखै रुधिरभोजनाः॥ १०॥
verses.m: Some ogres were crushed by the monkeys, who had conquered fear; while other ogres, who fed on gore ejected blood from their mouths, being thrashed by monkeys. (10)

verses.text:
पार्श्वेषु दारिताः केचित् केचिद् राशीकृता द्रुमैः।
शिलाभिश्चूर्णिताः केचित् केचिद् दन्तैर्विदारिताः॥ ११॥
verses.m: Some were torn in their sides,while others were reduced to pulp with trees. Still others were pulverized with rocks, while yet others were torn to pieces with teeth. (11)

verses.text:
ध्वजैर्विमथितैर्भग्नैः खड्गैश्च विनिपातितैः।
रथैर्विध्वंसितैः केचिद् व्यथिता रजनीचराः॥ १२॥
verses.m: With their standards broken and crushed, swords struck down, and chariots smashed, some prowlers of the night felt agonized. (12)

verses.text:
गजेन्द्रैः पर्वताकारैः पर्वताग्रैर्वनौकसाम्।
मथितैर्वाजिभिः कीर्णं सारोहैर्वसुधातलम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: The earth’s surface was covered with lordly elephants looking like mountains and horses with their riders crushed with the summits of mountains hurled by the monkeys (lit., dwellers in the woods). (13)

verses.text:
वानरैर्भीमविक्रान्तैराप्लुत्योत्प्लुत्य वेगितैः।
राक्षसाः करजैस्तीक्ष्णैर्मुखेषु विनिदारिताः॥ १४॥
verses.m: The ogres were lacerated in their faces with their nails by the monkeys of redoubtable prowess who were seized with impetuosity and bounded again and again. (14)

verses.text:
विषण्णवदना भूयो विप्रकीर्णशिरोरुहाः।
मूढाः शोणितगन्धेन निपेतुर्धरणीतले॥ १५॥
