यश्चैष जाम्बूनदवज्रजुष्टं
दीप्तं सधूमं परिघं प्रगृह्य।
आयाति रक्षोबलकेतुभूतो
योऽसौ निकुम्भोऽद्भुतघोरकर्मा॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Again, he who comes over there firmly seizing an iron club studded with gold and diamonds and as such radiant as fire and also smoky, studded with sapphires, and who is the principal figure in the army of ogres, is Nikumbha* of prodigious and terrible deeds. (21)

verses.text:
यश्चैष चापासिशरौघजुष्टं
पताकिनं पावकदीप्तरूपम्।
रथं समास्थाय विभात्युदग्रो
नरान्तकोऽसौ नगशृङ्गयोधी॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Again the tall fellow who shines brightly over there, occupying a chariot equipped with a multitude of bows, swords and arrows, nay, distinguished by a flag and blazing like fire is Narāntaka, who fights with mountain tops. (22)

verses.text:
यश्चैष नानाविधघोररूपै-
र्व्याघ्रोष्ट्रनागेन्द्रमृगाश्ववक्त्रैः।
भूतैर्वृतो भाति विवृत्तनेत्रै-
र्योऽसौ सुराणामपि दर्पहन्ता॥ २३॥
यत्रैतदिन्दुप्रतिमं विभाति
छत्रं सितं सूक्ष्मशलाकमग्र्यम्।
अत्रैष रक्षोधिपतिर्महात्मा
भूतैर्वृतो रुद्र इवावभाति॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Surrounded by ghosts of various hideous forms with rolling eyes and heads of tigers, camels, lordly elephants, deer and horses, even as Rudra (the god of destruction) is by genii, stands over there that suzerain lord of ogres, who humbles the pride even of gods and is endowed with extraordinary courage, and over whom shines brightly an excellent white canopy resembling the moon and endowed with slender ribs. (23-24)

verses.text:
असौ किरीटी चलकुण्डलास्यो
नगेन्द्रविन्ध्योपमभीमकायः।
महेन्द्रवैवस्वतदर्पहन्ता
रक्षोधिपः सूर्य इवावभाति॥ २५॥
verses.m: “There shines like the sun the overlord of ogres, who is decked with a diadem, whose countenance is graced with swinging earrings, whose terrible form resembles the Himālaya (the ruler of mountains) and the Vindhya mountains in size and who has humbled the pride of the mighty Indra and Yama (son of the sun-god).” (25)

verses.text:
प्रत्युवाच ततो रामो विभीषणमरिंदमः।
अहो दीप्तमहातेजा रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः॥ २६॥
verses.m: Thereupon Śrī Rāma, the scourge of his enemies, spoke as follows to Vibhīṣaṇa: “Oh! Rāvaṇa, the lord of ogres, is invested with an extraordinary luminous glory! (26)

verses.text:
आदित्य इव दुष्प्रेक्ष्यो रश्मिभिर्भाति रावणः।
न व्यक्तं लक्षये ह्यस्य रूपं तेजःसमावृतम्॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Like the sun, Rāvaṇa is difficult to gaze on because of his rays of light. I do not actually discern his form, fully endowed as it is with effulgence. (27)

verses.text:
देवदानववीराणां वपुर्नैवंविधं भवेत्।
यादृशं राक्षसेन्द्रस्य वपुरेतद् विराजते॥ २८॥
verses.m: “The body even of celestial and demon heroes may not be so bright as the body of the king of ogres is shining brightly. (28)

verses.text:
सर्वे पर्वतसंकाशाः सर्वे पर्वतयोधिनः।
सर्वे दीप्तायुधधरा योधास्तस्य महात्मनः॥ २९॥
verses.m: “The warriors fighting on the side of Rāvaṇa, who is endowed with extraordinary courage, are all mountain-like in size, all fight with tops of mountains and all wield fiery weapons. (29)

verses.text:
विभाति रक्षोराजोऽसौ प्रदीप्तैर्भीमदर्शनैः।
भूतैः परिवृतस्तीक्ष्णैर्देहवद्भिरिवान्तकः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Surrounded by fiery ghosts of terrible aspect, the yonder ruler of ogres looks like Death surrounded by furious genii endowed with hideous forms. (30)

verses.text:
दिष्ट्यायमद्य पापात्मा मम दृष्टिपथं गतः।
अद्य क्रोधं विमोक्ष्यामि सीताहरणसम्भवम्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “By good luck this sinful-minded fellow has come within the range of my sight today. I shall give free vent to my wrath born of Sītā’s abduction today.” (31)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा ततो रामो धनुरादाय वीर्यवान्।
लक्ष्मणानुचरस्तस्थौ समुद्धृत्य शरोत्तमम्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Saying so, nay, taking up his bow and drawing out an excellent arrow from his quiver, the powerful Śrī Rāma, stood with Lakṣmaṇa as his follower. (32)

verses.text:
ततः स रक्षोधिपतिर्महात्मा
रक्षांसि तान्याह महाबलानि।
द्वारेषु चर्यागृहगोपुरेषु
सुनिर्वृतास्तिष्ठत निर्विशङ्काः॥ ३३॥
verses.m: Thereupon that overlord of ogres, who was endowed with great courage, spoke as follows to the aforesaid ogres, who accompanied him and, who were endowed with extraordinary might: “Fully confident and free from apprehension, remain stationed at the main city gates as well as at the gates of the buildings on the principal streets. (33)

verses.text:
इहागतं मां सहितं भवद्भि-
र्वनौकसश्छिद्रमिदं विदित्वा।
शून्यां पुरीं दुष्प्रसहां प्रमथ्य
प्रधर्षयेयुः सहसा समेताः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “Coming to know of my having come this side with you, nay, taking this to be a weak point, and storming the desolate city, which is otherwise difficult to overpower, the monkeys (lit., dwellers in the woods) may, when united, devastate it all of a sudden.” (34)

verses.text:
विसर्जयित्वा सचिवांस्ततस्तान्
गतेषु रक्षःसु यथानियोगम्।
व्यदारयद् वानरसागरौघं
महाझषः पूर्णमिवार्णवौघम्॥ ३५॥
verses.m: Having dismissed his well-known counsellors, and the ogres, who accompanied him, having departed as directed, Rāvaṇa began to split asunder the waters of the sea of monkeys’ army in the same way as a gigantic fish would rend the entire expanse of a sea. (35)

verses.text:
तमापतन्तं सहसा समीक्ष्य
दीप्तेषुचापं युधि राक्षसेन्द्रम्।
महत् समुत्पाट्य महीधराग्रं
दुद्राव रक्षोधिपतिं हरीशः॥ ३६॥
verses.m: Tearing up the huge peak of a mountain on perceiving the aforesaid Rāvaṇa (the ruler of ogres), advancing all of a sudden, armed with a radiant bow and arrows, on the battlefield, Sugrīva, the ruler of monkeys, darted towards the king of ogres. (36)

verses.text:
तच्छैलशृङ्गं बहुवृक्षसानुं
प्रगृह्य चिक्षेप निशाचराय।
तमापतन्तं सहसा समीक्ष्य
चिच्छेद बाणैस्तपनीयपुङ्खैः॥ ३७॥
verses.m: Firmly seizing that mountain top, whose slopes were clothed with numerous trees, he hurled it at Rāvaṇa, the prowler of the night. On perceiving it flying precipitately towards himself, Rāvaṇa, however, tore it asunder with his arrows fitted with golden shafts. (37)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् प्रवृद्धोत्तमसानुवृक्षे
शृङ्गे विदीर्णे पतिते पृथिव्याम्।
महाहिकल्पं शरमन्तकाभं
समादधे राक्षसलोकनाथः॥ ३८॥
verses.m: The aforesaid peak, whose slopes were covered with excellent fully-grown trees, having fallen to the ground torn into pieces, Rāvaṇa (the lord of the ogre world) fitted to his bow an arrow which resembled a huge serpent and looked like Death himself. (38)

verses.text:
स तं गृहीत्वानिलतुल्यवेगं
सविस्फुलिङ्गज्वलनप्रकाशम्।
बाणं महेन्द्राशनितुल्यवेगं
चिक्षेप सुग्रीववधाय रुष्टः॥ ३९॥
verses.m: Taking up that arrow, which rivalled the wind in fury, nay, shone like a fire emitting sparks and vied with the thunderbolt of the mighty Indra (the ruler of gods) in velocity, he discharged it in rage for the destruction of Sugrīva. (39)

verses.text:
स सायको रावणबाहुमुक्तः
शक्राशनिप्रख्यवपुःप्रकाशम्।
सुग्रीवमासाद्य बिभेद वेगाद्
गुहेरिता क्रौञ्चमिवोग्रशक्तिः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: Reaching Sugrīva, who shone with his body, which resembled the thunderbolt of Indra (the ruler of gods), the said arrows, discharged by Rāvaṇa’s arm, pierced him in its flight even as the fierce javelin propelled by Kārtikeya, son of Lord Śiva and the Commander-in-Chief of the celestial army, penetrated the Krauñca mountain. (40)

verses.text:
स सायकार्तो विपरीतचेताः
कूजन् पृथिव्यां निपपात वीरः।
तं वीक्ष्य भूमौ पतितं विसंज्ञं
नेदुः प्रहृष्टा युधि यातुधानाः॥ ४१॥
verses.m: Stupefied when struck by that arrow, that hero, Sugrīva, fell groaning to the ground. Perceiving him fallen to the ground deprived of his senses, the ogres on the battlefield shouted exultantly. (41)

verses.text:
ततो गवाक्षो गवयः सुषेण-
स्त्वथर्षभो ज्योतिमुखो नलश्च।
शैलान् समुत्पाट्य विवृद्धकायाः
प्रदुद्रुवुस्तं प्रति राक्षसेन्द्रम्॥ ४२॥
verses.m: Tearing up crags, Gavākṣa, Gavaya, Suṣeṇa as also Ṛṣabha, Jyotirmukha and Nala of colossal size for their part then rushed towards that lord of ogres. (42)

verses.text:
तेषां प्रहारान् स चकार मोघान्
रक्षोधिपो बाणशतैः शिताग्रैः।
तान् वानरेन्द्रानपि बाणजालै-
र्बिभेद जाम्बूनदचित्रपुङ्खैः॥ ४३॥
ते वानरेन्द्रास्त्रिदशारिबाणै-
र्भिन्ना निपेतुर्भुवि भीमकायाः।
ततस्तु तद् वानरसैन्यमुग्रं
प्रच्छादयामास स बाणजालैः॥ ४४॥
verses.m: With hundreds of sharp-pointed arrows that overlord of ogres rendered their blows ineffectual. He also pierced those monkey-chiefs with streams of arrows endowed with lovely golden shafts. Pierced by the arrows of Rāvaṇa (the enemy of gods), the aforesaid monkey-chiefs of terrifying proportions, however, fell to the ground. Then Rāvaṇa for his part covered that formidable army of monkeys with streams of arrows. (43-44)

verses.text:
ते वध्यमानाः पतिताश्च वीरा
नानद्यमाना भयशल्यविद्धाः।
शाखामृगा रावणसायकार्ता
जग्मुः शरण्यं शरणं स्म रामम्॥ ४५॥
verses.m: And, pierced with the darts of terror, while being struck by Rāvaṇa, the aforesaid heroes fell down shrieking. Hard pressed by the arrows of Rāvaṇa, the monkeys sought Śrī Rāma, who is capable of affording shelter to all, as their refuge. (45)

verses.text:
ततो महात्मा स धनुर्धनुष्मा-
नादाय रामः सहसा जगाम।
तं लक्ष्मणः प्राञ्जलिरभ्युपेत्य
उवाच रामं परमार्थयुक्तम्॥ ४६॥
verses.m: Seizing his bow, the said high-souled Śrī Rāma, who was armed with an excellent bow, went forth all at once. Approaching him with joined palms, Lakṣmaṇa addressed to Rāma the following words consonant with truth: (46)

verses.text:
काममार्य सुपर्याप्तो वधायास्य दुरात्मनः।
विधमिष्याम्यहं चैतमनुजानीहि मां विभो॥ ४७॥
verses.m: “I am fully equal to the destruction of this evil-minded fellow, O noble brother and I shall certainly exterminate him. Pray, grant me leave to do this, O mighty prince!” (47)

verses.text:
तमब्रवीन्महातेजा रामः सत्यपराक्रमः।
गच्छ यत्नपरश्चापि भव लक्ष्मण संयुगे॥ ४८॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma of unfailing prowess, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, replied to him as follows: “Go, O Lakṣmaṇa, and also be strenuous in conflict. (48)

verses.text:
रावणो हि महावीर्यो रणेऽद्भुतपराक्रमः।
त्रैलोक्येनापि संक्रुद्धो दुष्प्रसह्यो न संशयः॥ ४९॥
verses.m: “Indeed, Rāvaṇa is endowed with extraordinary valour and exhibits marvellous prowess in combat. When enraged, he is difficult to withstand even for all the three worlds. (49)

verses.text:
तस्यच्छिद्राणि मार्गस्व स्वच्छिद्राणि च लक्षय।
चक्षुषा धनुषाऽऽत्मानं गोपायस्व समाहितः॥ ५०॥
verses.m: “Seek out his vulnerable points and keep an eye on your own weak points. And remaining wide awake, defend yourself with your eyes as well as with your bow.” (50)

verses.text:
राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा सम्परिष्वज्य पूज्य च।
अभिवाद्य च रामाय ययौ सौमित्रिराहवे॥ ५१॥
verses.m: Hearing the advice of Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, nay, closely embracing and honouring and greeting him, Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā) sallied forth for an encounter with the ogres. (51)

verses.text:
स रावणं वारणहस्तबाहुं
ददर्श भीमोद्यतदीप्तचापम्।
प्रच्छादयन्तं शरवृष्टिजालै-
स्तान् वानरान् भिन्नविकीर्णदेहान्॥ ५२॥
verses.m: He beheld Rāvaṇa with arms resembling the trunks of elephants and his dread and fiery bow uplifted, covering the monkeys with showers of arrows, their bodies torn into pieces thereby. (52)

verses.text:
तमालोक्य महातेजा हनूमान् मारुतात्मजः।
निवार्य शरजालानि विदुद्राव स रावणम्॥ ५३॥
verses.m: Seeing him and intercepting the streams of his arrows by hurling rocks etc., the celebrated Hanumān, an offspring of the wind-god, who was endowed with extraordinary courage, darted towards Rāvaṇa. (53)

verses.text:
रथं तस्य समासाद्य बाहुमुद्यम्य दक्षिणम्।
त्रासयन् रावणं धीमान् हनूमान् वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ ५४॥
verses.m: Approaching his chariot, nay lifting his right arm and menacing him, the sagacious Hanumān spoke to him as follows: (54)

verses.text:
देवदानवगन्धर्वैर्यक्षैश्च सह राक्षसैः।
अवध्यत्वं त्वया प्राप्तं वानरेभ्यस्तु ते भयम्॥ ५५॥
verses.m: “The boon of immunity from death at the hands of gods, demons and Gandharvas (celestial musicians) as also of Yakṣas (a class of demigods) and ogres has been secured by you from Brahmā; but there is danger to you from the monkeys. (55)

verses.text:
एष मे दक्षिणो बाहुः पञ्चशाखः समुद्यतः।
विधमिष्यति ते देहे भूतात्मानं चिरोषितम्॥ ५६॥
verses.m: “Duly raised, this right hand of mine, consisting of five branches (in the shape of the thumb and the four fingers) will expel from your body the Jīvātmā and constituting one’s very Self, which has long dwelt in your body.” (56)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा हनूमतो वाक्यं रावणो भीमविक्रमः।
संरक्तनयनः क्रोधादिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ ५७॥
verses.m: Hearing the challenge of Hanumān, Rāvaṇa of terrible prowess, his eyes inflamed with anger, retorted as follows: (57)

verses.text:
क्षिप्रं प्रहर निःशङ्कं स्थिरां कीर्तिमवाप्नुहि।
ततस्त्वां ज्ञातविक्रान्तं नाशयिष्यामि वानर॥ ५८॥
verses.m: “Strike at once without fear and earn lasting renown. Then I shall destroy you, your prowess having been ascertained thereby, O monkey!” (58)

verses.text:
रावणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा वायुसूनुर्वचोऽब्रवीत्।
प्रहतं हि मया पूर्वमक्षं तव सुतं स्मर॥ ५९॥
verses.m: Hearing the reply of Rāvaṇa, Hanumān (son of the wind-god) rejoined as follows: “Call to your mind your son, Akṣa, having been actually killed by me in the past.” (59)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तो महातेजा रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः।
आजघानानिलसुतं तलेनोरसि वीर्यवान्॥ ६०॥
verses.m: Spoken to as aforesaid, the powerful Rāvaṇa, the lord of ogres, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, gave a blow to the son of the wind-god on the chest.(60)

verses.text:
स तलाभिहतस्तेन चचाल च मुहुर्मुहुः।
स्थितो मुहूर्तं तेजस्वी स्थैर्यं कृत्वा महामतिः॥ ६१॥
आजघान च संक्रुद्धस्तलेनैवामरद्विषम्।
ततः स तेनाभिहतो वानरेण महात्मना॥ ६२॥
दशग्रीवः समाधूतो यथा भूमितलेऽचलः।
संग्रामे तं तथा दृष्ट्वा रावणं तलताडितम्॥ ६३॥
ऋषयो वानराः सिद्धा नेदुर्देवाः सहासुरैः।
अथाश्वस्य महातेजा रावणो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ ६४॥
verses.m: Smacked by him, Hanumān reeled again and again. Shortly recovering his balance, however, the highly intelligent Hanumān, who was endowed with energy, stood firm again and, getting infuriated, struck the enemy of gods with his palm alone. Struck by that high-souled monkey, the celebrated Rāvaṇa, a ten-headed monster, was thereupon violently shaken as a mountain during an earthquake. Seeing the said Rāvaṇa struck so hard in combat, Ṛṣis (the seers of Vedic Mantras), the monkeys, Siddhas (a class of demigods endowed with mystic powers by virtue of their very birth) and gods alongwith demons raised a shout of joy. Recovering his breath, Rāvaṇa, who was endowed with high spirits forthwith said: (61—64)

verses.text:
साधु वानर वीर्येण श्लाघनीयोऽसि मे रिपुः।
रावणेनैवमुक्तस्तु मारुतिर्वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ ६५॥
verses.m: “Well done, O monkey! You are an adversary worthy of my praise in point of valour.” Applauded in these words, Hanumān (son of the wind-god), however, replied as follows: (65)

verses.text:
धिगस्तु मम वीर्यस्य यत् त्वं जीवसि रावण।
सकृत् तु प्रहरेदानीं दुर्बुद्धे किं विकत्थसे॥ ६६॥
verses.m: “Woe be to my valour in that you still survive, O Rāvaṇa! Strike now only once, O evil-minded fellow! Why do you brag? (66)

verses.text:
ततस्त्वां मामको मुष्टिर्नयिष्यति यमक्षयम्।
ततो मारुतिवाक्येन कोपस्तस्य प्रजज्वले॥ ६७॥
verses.m: “My fist will then dispatch you to the abode of Yama, the god of retribution.” Rāvaṇa’s wrath blazed up as a result of Hanumān’s threat. (67)

verses.text:
संरक्तनयनो यत्नान्मुष्टिमावृत्य दक्षिणम्।
पातयामास वेगेन वानरोरसि वीर्यवान्॥ ६८॥
verses.m: Strenuously clenching his right fist, the powerful ogre, his eyes inflamed with anger, struck it with great velocity at the monkey’s chest. (68)

verses.text:
हनूमान् वक्षसि व्यूढे संचचाल पुनः पुनः।
विह्वलं तु तदा दृष्ट्वा हनूमन्तं महाबलम्॥ ६९॥
रथेनातिरथः शीघ्रं नीलं प्रति समभ्यगात्।
राक्षसानामधिपतिर्दशग्रीवः प्रतापवान्॥ ७०॥
verses.m: Struck on his broad chest, Hanumān reeled again and again. Seeing Hanumān, who was endowed with extraordinary might, beside himself with anguish at that time, the fiery Rāvaṇa, a ten-headed monster, a car-warrior of a superior order and the suzerain lord of ogres, however, speedily drove in his chariot towards Nīla. (69-70)

verses.text:
पन्नगप्रतिमैर्भीमैः परमर्माभिभेदनैः।
शरैरादीपयामास नीलं हरिचमूपतिम्॥ ७१॥
verses.m: With his dreaded arrows, resembling serpents and capable of piercing the vital parts of his enemies, he began to torment Nīla, the Commander-in-Chief of the monkeys. (71)

verses.text:
स शरौघसमायस्तो नीलो हरिचमूपतिः।
करेणैकेन शैलाग्रं रक्षोधिपतयेऽसृजत्॥ ७२॥
verses.m: Tearing up the top of a mountain with one hand, Nīla, the Commander-in-Chief of the monkeys, who was hard pressed with streams of arrows, hurled it at Rāvaṇa, the overlord of ogres. (72)

verses.text:
हनूमानपि तेजस्वी समाश्वस्तो महामनाः।
विप्रेक्षमाणो युद्धेप्सुः सरोषमिदमब्रवीत्॥ ७३॥
नीलेन सह संयुक्तं रावणं राक्षसेश्वरम्।
अन्येन युध्यमानस्य न युक्तमभिधावनम्॥ ७४॥
verses.m: Gazing on Rāvaṇa, seeking, as he did, an encounter with him, the brilliant high-minded Hanumān too, who felt fully refreshed by now, angrily spoke as follows to Rāvaṇa, the lord of ogres, already come to grips with Nīla: “It would not be meet and proper to attack one contending with another.” (73-74)

verses.text:
रावणोऽथ महातेजास्तं शृङ्गं सप्तभिः शरैः।
आजघान सुतीक्ष्णाग्रैस्तद् विकीर्णं पपात ह॥ ७५॥
verses.m: Rāvaṇa, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, forthwith struck the said mountain-top with seven exceedingly sharp-pointed arrows and the crag, they say, fell in pieces. (75)

verses.text:
तद् विकीर्णं गिरेः शृङ्गं दृष्ट्वा हरिचमूपतिः।
कालाग्निरिव जज्वाल कोपेन परवीरहा॥ ७६॥
verses.m: Seeing the aforesaid peak shattered, Nīla, the Commander-in-Chief of the monkeys, the destroyer of hostile champions, glowed with wrath like the fire at the time of universal destruction. (76)

verses.text:
सोऽश्वकर्णद्रुमान् शालांश्चूतांश्चापि सुपुष्पितान्।
अन्यांश्च विविधान् वृक्षान् नीलश्चिक्षेप संयुगे॥ ७७॥
verses.m: The said Nīla began to fling aśwakarṇa and sal as well as mango trees, fully in blossom as also other trees of various species in the course of his combat with Rāvaṇa. (77)

verses.text:
स तान् वृक्षान् समासाद्य प्रतिचिच्छेद रावणः।
अभ्यवर्षच्च घोरेण शरवर्षेण पावकिम्॥ ७८॥
verses.m: Finding those trees near, the celebrated Rāvaṇa cut them in pieces and covered Nīla (son of the fire-god) with a formidable hail of shafts. (78)

verses.text:
अभिवृष्टः शरौघेण मेघेनेव महाचलः।
ह्रस्वं कृत्वा ततो रूपं ध्वजाग्रे निपपात ह॥ ७९॥
verses.m: Reducing his form to a diminutive size when rained upon by a hail of shafts as a huge mountain is by a cloud, Nīla thereupon leapt on to the top of Rāvaṇa’s standard. (79)

verses.text:
पावकात्मजमालोक्य ध्वजाग्रे समवस्थितम्।
जज्वाल रावणः क्रोधात् ततो नीलो ननाद च॥ ८०॥
verses.m: Beholding the offspring of the fire-god perched on the point of his standard, Rāvaṇa blazed with fury and Nīla thereupon gave forth a shout. (80)

verses.text:
ध्वजाग्रे धनुषश्चाग्रे किरीटाग्रे च तं हरिम्।
लक्ष्मणोऽथ हनूमांश्च रामश्चापि सुविस्मिताः॥ ८१॥
verses.m: Lakṣmaṇa and Hanumān and again Śrī Rāma too were greatly astonished to see that monkey now on the apex of the banner and now at the end of the bow and again on the peak of the diadem. (81)

verses.text:
रावणोऽपि महातेजाः कपिलाघवविस्मितः।
अस्त्रमाहारयामास दीप्तमाग्नेयमद्भुतम्॥ ८२॥
verses.m: Wonder-struck at the agility of the monkey, Rāvaṇa too, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, invoked the marvellous missile presided over by the fire-god. (82)

verses.text:
ततस्ते चुक्रुशुर्हृष्टा लब्धलक्षाः प्लवंगमाः।
नीललाघवसम्भ्रान्तं दृष्ट्वा रावणमाहवे॥ ८३॥
verses.m: Thereupon those monkeys, who felt rejoiced to see Rāvaṇa nonplussed at the agility of Nīla and had found an occasion for jubilation, shouted with joy. (83)

verses.text:
वानराणां च नादेन संरब्धो रावणस्तदा।
सम्भ्रमाविष्टहृदयो न किंचित् प्रत्यपद्यत॥ ८४॥
verses.m: Provoked by the clamour of the monkeys, his heart possessed with flurry, Rāvaṇa did not know what to do. (84)

verses.text:
आग्नेयेनापि संयुक्तं गृहीत्वा रावणः शरम्।
ध्वजशीर्षस्थितं नीलमुदैक्षत निशाचरः॥ ८५॥
verses.m: Taking up an arrow charged with the missile presided over by the fire-god, the prowler of the night looked at Nīla perched on the tip of his standard. (85)

verses.text:
ततोऽब्रवीन्महातेजा रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः।
कपे लाघवयुक्तोऽसि मायया परया सह॥ ८६॥
verses.m: Rāvaṇa, the lord of ogres, who was endowed with high spirits, then spoke as follows: “You are endowed with agility combined with supreme deceptive power. (86)

verses.text:
जीवितं खलु रक्षस्व यदि शक्तोऽसि वानर।
तानि तान्यात्मरूपाणि सृजसि त्वमनेकशः॥ ८७॥
तथापि त्वां मया मुक्तः सायकोऽस्त्रप्रयोजितः।
जीवितं परिरक्षन्तं जीविताद् भ्रंशयिष्यति॥ ८८॥
verses.m: “Indeed, save your life if you are able to do so, O monkey! Even though you accomplish numerous deeds of various kinds worthy of your own self, nevertheless the arrow charged with a mystic missile and discharged by me will deprive of your life, you, who are sedulously preserving it.” (87-88)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा महाबाहू रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः।
संधाय बाणमस्त्रेण चमूपतिमताडयत्॥ ८९॥
verses.m: Saying so and charging an arrow with a mystic missile, the mighty-armed Rāvaṇa struck Nīla, the Commander-in-Chief, with it. (89)

verses.text:
सोऽस्त्रमुक्तेन बाणेन नीलो वक्षसि ताडितः।
निर्दह्यमानः सहसा स पपात महीतले॥ ९०॥
verses.m: Being burnt all over when struck in the chest with the arrow propelled by a mystic missile, the celebrated Nīla fell to the earth’s surface all at once. (90)

verses.text:
पितृमाहात्म्यसंयोगादात्मनश्चापि तेजसा।
जानुभ्यामपतद् भूमौ न तु प्राणैर्वियुज्यत॥ ९१॥
verses.m: By virtue of his father’s greatness and his own energy, however, Nīla only fell down with his knees to the ground, but was not deprived of his life. (91)

verses.text:
विसंज्ञं वानरं दृष्ट्वा दशग्रीवो रणोत्सुकः।
रथेनाम्बुदनादेन सौमित्रिमभिदुद्रुवे॥ ९२॥
verses.m: Finding the monkey unconscious, Rāvaṇa (the ten-headed monster), who was eager for combat, darted towards Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā) in his chariot, whose rattling resembled the rumbling of clouds. (92)

verses.text:
आसाद्य रणमध्ये तं वारयित्वा स्थितो ज्वलन्।
धनुर्विस्फारयामास राक्षसेन्द्रः प्रतापवान्॥ ९३॥
verses.m: Approaching Lakṣmaṇa after intercepting others and standing in his glory, the powerful Rāvaṇa (the lord of ogres) twanged his bow. (93)

verses.text:
तमाह सौमित्रिरदीनसत्त्वो
विस्फारयन्तं धनुरप्रमेयम्।
अवेहि मामद्य निशाचरेन्द्र
न वानरांस्त्वं प्रतियोद्धुमर्हसि॥ ९४॥
verses.m: Undepressed in spirits, Lakṣmaṇa, the son of Sumitrā, challenged in the following words the ogre, who was twanging his bow: “Be aware of me today, O king of ogres! You ought no longer to fight the monkeys.” (94)

verses.text:
स तस्य वाक्यं प्रतिपूर्णघोषं
ज्याशब्दमुग्रं च निशम्य राजा।
आसाद्य सौमित्रिमुपस्थितं तं
रोषान्वितं वाचमुवाच रक्षः॥ ९५॥
verses.m: Hearing his challenge as well as the formidable twang of his bowstring, generating sonorous vibrations, and drawing near to the aforesaid son of Sumitrā, standing close by, the aforesaid ogre king made the following wrathful reply: (95)

verses.text:
दिष्ट्यासि मे राघव दृष्टिमार्गं
प्राप्तोऽन्तगामी विपरीतबुद्धिः।
अस्मिन् क्षणे यास्यसि मृत्युलोकं
संसाद्यमानो मम बाणजालैः॥ ९६॥
verses.m: “Luckily enough for me you have fallen within my sight—you, who are soon going to meet your end, perverted of mind that you are. Being hard pressed with the streams of my arrows, you will reach the region of death this very moment, O scion of Raghu!” (96)

verses.text:
तमाह सौमित्रिरविस्मयानो
गर्जन्तमुद्वृत्तशिताग्रदंष्ट्रम्।
राजन् न गर्जन्ति महाप्रभावा
विकत्थसे पापकृतां वरिष्ठ॥ ९७॥
verses.m: Not feeling in the least surprised, the son of Sumitrā replied as follows to Rāvaṇa, who was blustering and displaying his fierce and sharp-edged teeth: “Those endowed with extraordinary valour do not bluster, while you are talking boastfully, O prince of sinners! (97)

verses.text:
जानामि वीर्यं तव राक्षसेन्द्र
बलं प्रतापं च पराक्रमं च।
अवस्थितोऽहं शरचापपाणि-
रागच्छ किं मोघविकत्थनेन॥ ९८॥
verses.m: “I know your valour, strength, greatness and prowess too, O ruler of ogres! I stand firmly, arrows and bow in hand; come on, what will you gain by bragging?” (98)

verses.text:
स एवमुक्तः कुपितः ससर्ज
रक्षोधिपः सप्त शरान् सुपुङ्खान्।
ताँल्लक्ष्मणः काञ्चनचित्रपुङ्खै-
श्चिच्छेद बाणैर्निशिताग्रधारैः॥ ९९॥
verses.m: Filled with rage when challenged in these words, Rāvaṇa (the suzerain lord of ogres) shot seven arrows with beautiful plumes. Lakṣmaṇa, however, cut them to pieces with his wonderful gold-shafted, sharp pointed and sharp-headed arrows. (99)

verses.text:
तान् प्रेक्षमाणः सहसा निकृत्तान्
निकृत्तभोगानिव पन्नगेन्द्रान्।
लङ्केश्वरः क्रोधवशं जगाम
ससर्ज चान्यान् निशितान् पृषत्कान्॥ १००॥
verses.m: Perceiving the arrows cut down like lordly serpents, whose coils have been hacked to pieces, Rāvaṇa (the king of Laṅkā) gave way to wrath and shot other sharp arrows. (100)

verses.text:
स बाणवर्षं तु ववर्ष तीव्रं
रामानुजः कार्मुकसम्प्रयुक्तम्।
क्षुरार्धचन्द्रोत्तमकर्णिभल्लैः
शरांश्च चिच्छेद न चुक्षुभे च॥ १०१॥
verses.m: That younger brother of Śrī Rāma for his part showered a piercing hail of arrows by his bow. Nay, he cut asunder the arrows of his enemy with his own arrows of the varieties known by the names of Kṣura, Ardhacandra, the excellent Karṇi and Bhalla, and did not feel perturbed in the least. (101)

verses.text:
स बाणजालान्यपि तानि तानि
मोघानि पश्यंस्त्रिदशारिराजः।
विसिस्मिये लक्ष्मणलाघवेन
पुनश्च बाणान् निशितान् मुमोच॥ १०२॥
verses.m: Finding all those streams of arrows also ineffectual, the ruler of ogres (the enemies of gods) felt astonished at Lakṣmaṇa’s skill and began to discharge pointed arrows anew. (102)

verses.text:
स लक्ष्मणश्चापि शिताञ्शिताग्रान्
महेन्द्रतुल्योऽशनिभीमवेगान्।
संधाय चापे ज्वलनप्रकाशान्
ससर्ज रक्षोधिपतेर्वधाय॥ १०३॥
verses.m: Nay, fitting to his bow sharp arrows with whetted points, flying with terrible velocity of lightning and shining like fire, the celebrated Lakṣmaṇa, too, a compeer of the mighty Indra, shot them for the destruction of Rāvaṇa, the suzerain lord of ogres. (103)

verses.text:
स तान् प्रचिच्छेद हि राक्षसेन्द्रः
शिताञ्शराँल्लक्ष्मणमाजघान।
शरेण कालाग्निसमप्रभेण
स्वयंभुदत्तेन ललाटदेशे॥ १०४॥
verses.m: The aforesaid ruler of ogres, however, cut to pieces those pointed arrows and struck Lakṣmaṇa in the forehead with a shaft resplendent as the fire of Universal Dissolution, gifted to him by Brahmā, the self-born creator. (104)

verses.text:
स लक्ष्मणो रावणसायकार्त-
श्चचाल चापं शिथिलं प्रगृह्य।
पुनश्च संज्ञां प्रतिलभ्य कृच्छ्रा-
च्चिच्छेद चापं त्रिदशेन्द्रशत्रोः॥ १०५॥
verses.m: Grasping his bow feebly when hurt by the arrow of Rāvaṇa, the celebrated Lakṣmaṇa reeled. Regaining his senses with difficulty, however, he tore asunder the bow of the enemy of Indra, the ruler of gods. (105)

verses.text:
निकृत्तचापं त्रिभिराजघान
बाणैस्तदा दाशरथिः शिताग्रैः।
स सायकार्तो विचचाल राजा
कृच्छ्राच्च संज्ञां पुनराससाद॥ १०६॥
verses.m: Lakṣmaṇa (son of Daśaratha) then struck Rāvaṇa (whose bow had been cut to pieces) with three sharp-pointed arrows. Hurt by the shafts, the aforesaid king swooned and recovered his consciousness with difficulty. (106)

verses.text:
स कृत्तचापः शरताडितश्च
मेदार्द्रगात्रो रुधिरावसिक्तः।
जग्राह शक्तिं स्वयमुग्रशक्तिः
स्वयंभुदत्तां युधि देवशत्रुः॥ १०७॥
verses.m: Struck with arrows and bathed in blood, his bow having been cut, and his limbs splattered with fat, Rāvaṇa (the enemy of gods), who was himself endowed with formidable energy, seized on the battlefield a javelin, gifted to him by Brahmā, the self-born creator. (107)

verses.text:
स तां सधूमानलसंनिकाशां
वित्रासनां संयति वानराणाम्।
चिक्षेप शक्तिं तरसा ज्वलन्तीं
सौमित्रये राक्षसराष्ट्रनाथः॥ १०८॥
verses.m: That guardian of the ogre kingdom flung with fury at Lakṣmaṇa that flaming javelin, which shone brightly like a fire crowned with smoke and constituted the terror of the monkeys on the field of battle. (108)

verses.text:
तामापतन्तीं भरतानुजोऽस्त्रै-
र्जघान बाणैश्च हुताग्निकल्पैः।
तथापि सा तस्य विवेश शक्ति-
र्भुजान्तरं दाशरथेर्विशालम्॥ १०९॥
verses.m: Lakṣmaṇa (a younger brother of Bharata) struck the javelin, even as it came flying towards him with weapons and flame-like shafts. Nevertheless that javelin entered the broad chest of Lakṣmaṇa, the aforesaid son of Daśaratha. (109)

verses.text:
स शक्तिमाञ्शक्तिसमाहतः सन्
जज्वाल भूमौ स रघुप्रवीरः।
तं विह्वलन्तं सहसाभ्युपेत्य
जग्राह राजा तरसा भुजाभ्याम्॥ ११०॥
verses.m: Grievously hurt by the javelin, that well-known, powerful and pre-eminent hero among the Raghus began to burn with pain as he lay on the ground. Approaching him all of a sudden while he was losing his consciousness, the king of ogres caught him vehemently in his arms. (110)

verses.text:
हिमवान् मन्दरो मेरुस्त्रैलोक्यं वा सहामरैः।
शक्यं भुजाभ्यामुद्धर्तुं न शक्यो भरतानुजः॥ १११॥
verses.m: But Lakṣmaṇa (a younger brother of Bharata) could not be raised by the same arms of Rāvaṇa, by which the Himālaya, the Mandara and the Meru mountains or even all the three worlds (viz., heaven, earth and the intermediate aerial region) including gods could be easily lifted up. (111)

verses.text:
शक्त्या ब्राह्म्या तु सौमित्रिस्ताडितोऽपि स्तनान्तरे।
विष्णोरमीमांस्यभागमात्मानं प्रत्यनुस्मरत्॥ ११२॥
verses.m: Even though wounded in the space in between the two breasts by a javelin (which originally belonged to Brahmā), Lakṣmaṇa recalled himself to be an inconceivable part of Lord Viṣṇu. (112)

verses.text:
ततो दानवदर्पघ्नं सौमित्रिं देवकण्टकः।
तं पीडयित्वा बाहुभ्यां न प्रभुर्लङ्घनेऽभवत्॥ ११३॥
verses.m: Therefore, even on pressing between his arms Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā), who was capable of crushing the pride of demons, Rāvaṇa (a thorn in the side of gods) was not able to lift him up. (113)

verses.text:
ततः क्रुद्धो वायुसुतो रावणं समभिद्रवत्।
आजघानोरसि क्रुद्धो वज्रकल्पेन मुष्टिना॥ ११४॥
verses.m: Filled with rage, Hanumān, son of the wind-god, thereupon darted towards Rāvaṇa. Full of fury he struck the latter in the chest with his fist, which came as a thunderbolt. (114)

verses.text:
तेन मुष्टिप्रहारेण रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः।
जानुभ्यामगमद् भूमौ चचाल च पपात च॥ ११५॥
verses.m: Under that blow of his fist, Rāvaṇa, the lord of ogres, fell to the floor of his chariot on his knees, reeled and lay prostrate. (115)

verses.text:
आस्यैश्च नेत्रैः श्रवणैः पपात रुधिरं बहु।
विघूर्णमानो निश्चेष्टो रथोपस्थ उपाविशत्॥ ११६॥
verses.m: Blood flowed copiously through his mouths, eyes and ears. Nay, rolling about, he sank motionless into the hinder-part of his chariot. (116)

verses.text:
विसंज्ञो मूर्च्छितश्चासीन्न च स्थानं समालभत्।
विसंज्ञं रावणं दृष्ट्वा समरे भीमविक्रमम्॥ ११७॥
ऋषयो वानराश्चैव नेदुर्देवाश्च सासुराः।
हनूमानथ तेजस्वी लक्ष्मणं रावणार्दितम्॥ ११८॥
आनयद् राघवाभ्याशं बाहुभ्यां परिगृह्य तम्।
वायुसूनोः सुहृत्त्वेन भक्त्या परमया च सः।
शत्रूणामप्यकम्प्योऽपि लघुत्वमगमत् कपेः॥ ११९॥
verses.m: Rāvaṇa fainted, and as such lost his consciousness and could not know where he was. Seeing Rāvaṇa of redoubtable prowess in combat, senseless, the Ṛṣis (seers of Vedic Mantras) as well as the monkeys as also the gods including the demons (invisibly present on the scene) shouted in joy. Clasping Lakṣmaṇa, wounded by Rāvaṇa, with his arms, the courageous Hanumān forthwith brought him to the presence of Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu). Due to Hanumān’s affection and extreme devotion to him, Lakṣmaṇa became light for the former, even though he was unshakable for his enemies. (117—119)

verses.text:
तं समुत्सृज्य सा शक्तिः सौमित्रिं युधि निर्जितम्।
रावणस्य रथे तस्मिन् स्थानं पुनरुपागमत्॥ १२०॥
verses.m: Leaving for good Sumitrā’s son, who had been well-nigh vanquished in battle, the aforesaid javelin returned to its allotted position in the well-known chariot of Rāvaṇa. (120)

verses.text:
रावणोऽपि महातेजाः प्राप्य संज्ञां महाहवे।
आददे निशितान् बाणाञ्जग्राह च महद्धनुः॥ १२१॥
verses.m: Regaining his consciousness in the course of the major conflict, Rāvaṇa too, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, took up sharp arrows and further seized a large bow. (121)

verses.text:
आश्वस्तश्च विशल्यश्च लक्ष्मणः शत्रुसूदनः।
विष्णोर्भागममीमांस्यमात्मानं प्रत्यनुस्मरन्॥ १२२॥
verses.m: Recollecting himself to be an inconceivable part of Lord Viṣṇu, Lakṣmaṇa too, the destroyer of his enemies, regained his consciousness and had his wounds healed up. (122)

verses.text:
निपातितमहावीरां वानराणां महाचमूम्।
राघवस्तु रणे दृष्ट्वा रावणं समभिद्रवत्॥ १२३॥
verses.m: Finding that the huge army of monkeys had its mighty heroes struck down on the battlefield, Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) for his part duly assailed Rāvaṇa. (123)

verses.text:
अथैनमनुसंक्रम्य हनूमान् वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
मम पृष्ठं समारुह्य राक्षसं शास्तुमर्हसि॥ १२४॥
विष्णुर्यथा गरुत्मन्तमारुह्यामरवैरिणम्।
तच्छ्रुत्वा राघवो वाक्यं वायुपुत्रेण भाषितम्॥ १२५॥
अथारुरोह सहसा हनूमन्तं महाकपिम्।
रथस्थं रावणं संख्ये ददर्श मनुजाधिपः॥ १२६॥
verses.m: Approaching him, Hanumān forthwith submitted as follows: “You should subdue the ogre only after climbing on my shoulders even as Lord Viṣṇu tamed Madhu (an enemy of gods) after mounting the back of Garuḍa (the king of birds, His own carrier).” Hearing the aforesaid prayer uttered by Hanumān (son of the wind-god), Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) thereupon precipitately climbed on the shoulders of the great monkey, Hanumān. Śrī Rāma (the suzerain lord of human beings) saw Rāvaṇa mounted on his chariot on the field of battle. (124—126)

verses.text:
तमालोक्य महातेजाः प्रदुद्राव स रावणम्।
वैरोचनमिव क्रुद्धो विष्णुरभ्युद्यतायुधः॥ १२७॥
verses.m: Beholding him, Śrī Rāma, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, rushed furiously towards Rāvaṇa, even as Viṣṇu darted with his discus upraised against the demon Bali, son of Virocana. (127)

verses.text:
ज्याशब्दमकरोत् तीव्रं वज्रनिष्पेषनिष्ठुरम्।
गिरा गम्भीरया रामो राक्षसेन्द्रमुवाच ह॥ १२८॥
verses.m: He caused the string of his bow to make a sharp ringing sound, piercing as a clap of thunder by drawing it and spoke as follows to Rāvaṇa, the ruler of ogres, in a deep voice, so the tradition goes: (128)

verses.text:
तिष्ठ तिष्ठ मम त्वं हि कृत्वा विप्रियमीदृशम्।
क्व नु राक्षसशार्दूल गत्वा मोक्षमवाप्स्यसि॥ १२९॥
verses.m: “Forbear, forbear, O tiger among ogres! Going whither will you get deliverance after giving me such offence? (129)

verses.text:
यदीन्द्रवैवस्वतभास्करान् वा
स्वयंभुवैश्वानरशंकरान् वा।
गमिष्यसि त्वं दशधा दिशो वा
तथापि मे नाद्य गतो विमोक्ष्यसे॥ १३०॥
verses.m: “If you fly for protection either to Indra (the ruler of gods), Yama (son of the sun-god) and the sun-god (himself) or to Brahmā (the self-born creator), the god of fire, or Lord Śiva (who brings prosperity to all) or in the ten directions; nevertheless you shall not escape from my hands today even if gone there. (130)

verses.text:
यश्चैष शक्त्या निहतस्त्वयाद्य
गच्छन् विषादं सहसाभ्युपेत्य।
स एष रक्षोगणराज मृत्युः
सपुत्रपौत्रस्य तवाद्य युद्धे॥ १३१॥
verses.m: “The same Lakṣmaṇa who, on having fallen a prey to insensibility when grievously hurt by you with a javelin today, you having arrived in my presence shall prove to be death not only of yourself but also of your sons and grandsons on the battlefield. (131)

verses.text:
एतेन चात्यद्भुतदर्शनानि
शरैर्जनस्थानकृतालयानि।
चतुर्दशान्यात्तवरायुधानि
रक्षःसहस्राणि निषूदितानि॥ १३२॥
verses.m: “By this adversary of yours, viz., myself, were exterminated with his arrows fourteen thousand ogres of exceedingly weird looks, who had taken up their abode in Janasthāna and pressed excellent weapons into their service.” (132)

verses.text:
राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा राक्षसेन्द्रो महाबलः।
वायुपुत्रं महावेगं वहन्तं राघवं रणे॥ १३३॥
रोषेण महताऽऽविष्टः पूर्ववैरमनुस्मरन्।
आजघान शरैर्दीप्तैः कालानलशिखोपमैः॥ १३४॥
verses.m: Seized with violent anger on hearing the speech of Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), and recollecting his former enmity, Rāvaṇa (the ruler of ogres), who was endowed with extraordinary might, struck with flaming arrows, resembling the tongues of the destructive fire at the time of Universal Dissolution, Hanumān (son of the wind-god), who was full of great impetuosity and bore Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) on the field of battle, severely injuring him. (133-34)

verses.text:
राक्षसेनाहवे तस्य ताडितस्यापि सायकैः।
स्वभावतेजोयुक्तस्य भूयस्तेजोऽभ्यवर्धत॥ १३५॥
verses.m: The vigour of Hanumān, who was endowed with native energy, grew all the more even when he was struck with arrows by the ogre, Rāvaṇa, on the battlefield. (135)

verses.text:
ततो रामो महातेजा रावणेन कृतव्रणम्।
दृष्ट्वा प्लवगशार्दूलं क्रोधस्य वशमेयिवान्॥ १३६॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, was seized with anger on seeing Hanumān (a tiger among the monkeys) wounded by Rāvaṇa. (136)

verses.text:
तस्याभिसंक्रम्य रथं सचक्रं
साश्वध्वजच्छत्रमहापताकम्।
ससारथिं साशनिशूलखड्गं
रामः प्रचिच्छेद शितैः शराग्रैः॥ १३७॥
verses.m: Finding Rāvaṇa, advancing towards his chariots, Śrī Rāma tore it into pieces with its wheels, horses, standard, canopy, huge pennon, charioteer, Aśanis (a kind of missile), pikes and swords with the sharp heads of his arrows. (137)

verses.text:
अथेन्द्रशत्रुं तरसा जघान
बाणेन वज्राशनिसंनिभेन।
भुजान्तरे व्यूढसुजातरूपे
वज्रेण मेरुं भगवानिवेन्द्रः॥ १३८॥
verses.m: Then with his shaft shining brightly as the thunderbolt and Aśani, Śrī Rāma now struck with vehemence Rāvaṇa (the enemy of Indra) in his broad and lovely-looking chest (lit., the space between the arms), even as the mighty Indra would strike the Meru mountain with his thunderbolt. (138)

verses.text:
यो वज्रपाताशनिसंनिपाता-
न्न चुक्षुभे नापि चचाल राजा।
स रामबाणाभिहतो भृशार्त-
श्चचाल चापं च मुमोच वीरः॥ १३९॥
तं विह्वलन्तं प्रसमीक्ष्य रामः
समाददे दीप्तमथार्धचन्द्रम्।
तेनार्कवर्णं सहसा किरीटं
चिच्छेद रक्षोधिपतेर्महात्मा॥ १४०॥
verses.m: That heroic monarch who never felt disturbed, much less shook under the impact of the thunderbolt of Indra or of lightning, reeled when struck by the arrow of Śrī Rāma, greatly agonized as he was and let fall his bow. Seeing him swooning, the high-souled Śrī Rāma forthwith took up a flaming arrow with a crescent-shaped head and hastily shattered with it the diadem of Rāvaṇa (the suzerain lord of ogres), which was bright as the sun. (139-140)

verses.text:
तं निर्विषाशीविषसंनिकाशं
शान्तार्चिषं सूर्यमिवाप्रकाशम्।
गतश्रियं कृत्तकिरीटकूट-
मुवाच रामो युधि राक्षसेन्द्रम्॥ १४१॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma then spoke as follows to the ruler of ogres who closely resembled a venomous snake rid of its poison and was divested of his splendour like the sun whose rays had disappeared and whose glory had departed, his diadems having been torn asunder: (141)

verses.text:
कृतं त्वया कर्म महत् सुभीमं
हतप्रवीरश्च कृतस्त्वयाहम्।
तस्मात् परिश्रान्त इति व्यवस्य
न त्वां शरैर्मृत्युवशं नयामि॥ १४२॥
verses.m: “A great and exceedingly terrible feat has been accomplished by you and my pre-eminent champions have been killed by you. Knowing that you have been fully exhausted thereby, I shall not put you under the sway of Death with my shafts. (142)

verses.text:
प्रयाहि जानामि रणार्दितस्त्वं
प्रविश्य रात्रिंचरराज लङ्काम्।
आश्वस्य निर्याहि रथी च धन्वी
तदा बलं प्रेक्ष्यसि मे रथस्थः॥ १४३॥
verses.m: “I know you stand agonized through continued fighting. Therefore, depart for the present, O king of the rangers of the night! Re-entering Laṅkā and resting awhile, sally forth again, duly mounted on a chariot and armed with a bow, then, remaining seated in your car, you shall witness my might.” (143)

verses.text:
स एवमुक्तो हतदर्पहर्षो
निकृत्तचापः स हताश्वसूतः।
शरार्दितो भग्नमहाकिरीटो
विवेश लङ्कां सहसा स्म राजा॥ १४४॥
verses.m: Consoled in these words, the celebrated king—whose vanity and joy had been crushed, whose bow had been lacerated to pieces, whose horses and charioteer had been killed, whose big diadem had been shattered and who had been wounded with arrows—hastily (re-) entered Laṅkā. (144)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् प्रविष्टे रजनीचरेन्द्रे
महाबले दानवदेवशत्रौ।
हरीन् विशल्यान् सह लक्ष्मणेन
चकार रामः परमाहवाग्रे॥ १४५॥
verses.m: The aforesaid lord of the prowlers of the night, the enemy of gods and demons alike, who was endowed with extraordinary might, having withdrawn, Śrī Rāma with Lakṣmaṇa drew out the arrows from the bodies of the monkeys in the forefront of the vast battle-field. (145)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् प्रभग्ने त्रिदशेन्द्रशत्रौ
सुरासुरा भूतगणा दिशश्च।
ससागराः सर्षिमहोरगाश्च
तथैव भूम्यम्बुचराः प्रहृष्टाः॥ १४६॥
verses.m: On that enemy of Indra (the ruler of gods) having been routed, the gods as well as the guardians of the four quarters including the seas, the Ṛṣis (seers of Vedic Mantras) and large serpents and, even so, the creatures of land and water felt highly rejoiced. (146)

verses.text:
स प्रविश्य पुरीं लङ्कां रामबाणभयार्दितः।
भग्नदर्पस्तदा राजा बभूव व्यथितेन्द्रियः॥ १॥
verses.m: Entering the city of Laṅkā stricken with the fear of Śrī Rāma’s arrows, the king, who had his vanity crushed, felt troubled in mind. (1)

verses.text:
मातंग इव सिंहेन गरुडेनेव पन्नगः।
अभिभूतोऽभवद् राजा राघवेण महात्मना॥ २॥
verses.m: Rāvaṇa, the king was overcome by the high-souled Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) as an elephant is by a lion and a serpent by Garuḍa, the king of birds. (2)

verses.text:
ब्रह्मदण्डप्रतीकानां विद्युच्चलितवर्चसाम्।
स्मरन् राघवबाणानां विव्यथे राक्षसेश्वरः॥ ३॥
verses.m: The king of ogres felt disquieted while recalling the arrows of Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), which resembled Brahmadaṇḍa (a fiery comet appearing at the time of universal dissolution) and emitted an unsteady light like lightning. (3)

verses.text:
स काञ्चनमयं दिव्यमाश्रित्य परमासनम्।
विप्रेक्षमाणो रक्षांसि रावणो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Having taken his seat on his magnificent and excellent throne of gold and letting his gaze wander over the ogres, Rāvaṇa spoke as follows: (4)

verses.text:
सर्वं तत् खलु मे मोघं यत् तप्तं परमं तपः।
यत् समानो महेन्द्रेण मानुषेण विनिर्जितः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “All that asceticism of the supreme type, which was practised by me, has undoubtedly proved infructuous in that I, the equal of the mighty Indra (the ruler of gods) have been utterly defeated by a mere mortal. (5)

verses.text:
इदं तद् ब्रह्मणो घोरं वाक्यं मामभ्युपस्थितम्।
मानुषेभ्यो विजानीहि भयं त्वमिति तत्तथा॥ ६॥
verses.m: “That terrible warning of Brahmā in the words: ‘Know you for certain of danger from humans!’ has now flashed upon me. It is coming true. (6)

verses.text:
देवदानवगन्धर्वैर्यक्षराक्षसपन्नगैः।
अवध्यत्वं मया प्रोक्तं मानुषेभ्यो न याचितम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Immunity from death at the hands of gods, demons, Gandharvas (celestial musicians), Yakṣas (a class of demigods), ogres and serpents was sought by me, but not at the hands of mortals. (7)

verses.text:
तमिमं मानुषं मन्ये रामं दशरथात्मजम्।
इक्ष्वाकुकुलजातेन अनरण्येन यत् पुरा॥ ८ ॥
उत्पत्स्यति हि मद्वंशपुरुषो राक्षसाधम।
यस्त्वां सपुत्रं सामात्यं सबलं साश्वसारथिम्॥ ९ ॥
निहनिष्यति संग्रामे त्वां कुलाधम दुर्मते।
शप्तोऽहं वेदवत्या च यथा सा धर्षिता पुरा॥ १०॥
verses.m: “I conclude this Rāma, an offspring of Daśaratha, to be that mortal of whom mention was made by King Anaraṇya, born in the race of Ikṣwāku, by whom I was formerly cursed in the following words: ‘In my house will undoubtedly be born a man, who will exterminate on the field of battle you with your sons, ministers, army, horses and charioteers, O evil-minded bane of your race, the vilest of ogres!’ I was further cursed by one, Vedavatī, as she was violated by me of old. (8—10)

verses.text:
सेयं सीता महाभागा जाता जनकनन्दिनी।
उमा नन्दीश्वरश्चापि रम्भा वरुणकन्यका॥ ११॥
यथोक्तास्तन्मया प्राप्तं न मिथ्या ऋ षिभाषितम्।
एतदेव समागम्य यत्नं कर्तुमिहार्हथ॥ १२॥
राक्षसाश्चापि तिष्ठन्तु चर्यागोपुरमूर्धसु।
स चाप्रतिमगाम्भीर्यो देवदानवदर्पहा॥ १३॥
ब्रह्मशापाभिभूतस्तु कुम्भकर्णो विबोध्यताम्।
समरे जितमात्मानं प्रहस्तं च निषूदितम्॥ १४॥
ज्ञात्वा रक्षोबलं भीममादिदेश महाबलः।
द्वारेषु यत्नः क्रियतां प्राकारश्चाधिरुह्यताम्॥ १५॥
निद्रावशसमाविष्टः कुम्भकर्णो विबोध्यताम्।
सुखं स्वपिति निश्चिन्तः कामोपहतचेतनः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “The same highly blessed lady has been born as this daughter of Janaka. The result, which Umā (the divine Consort of Lord Śiva), Nandīśwara (a monkey-faced attendant of Lord Śiva), Rambhā (a celestial nymph) and Puñjikasthalā (another celebrated nymph, daughter of Varuṇa) predicted, has also been attained by me.* The prediction made by those endowed with prophetic vision can never be untrue. Knowing this very fact, you ought to strive to conquer the enemy. And let ogres too take up their position on the main roads as well as on the top of gates. Nay, let Kumbhakarṇa for his part, who is unparalleled in profundity and is capable of crushing the vanity of gods and demons alike and who remains overwhelmed with slumber due to the execration of Brahmā, be fully roused.” Knowing himself to have been conquered in combat, and Prahasta to have been killed, Rāvaṇa, who was endowed with extraordinary might, commanded the army of ogres as follows: “Remaining stationed at the gates, let an attempt be made to guard them; and let the defensive walls be scaled (and a watch be kept at the enemy). Also, Kumbhakarṇa be fully roused. His understanding vitiated by lust, he is slumbering at ease, free from all cares. (11—16)

verses.text:
नव सप्त दशाष्टौ च मासान् स्वपिति राक्षसः।
मन्त्रं कृत्वा प्रसुप्तोऽयमितस्तु नवमेऽहनि॥ १७॥
verses.m: “The ogre sleeps for nine, ten or eight months. Having deliberated with me, he for his part fell fast asleep nine months ago from now. (17)

verses.text:
तं तु बोधयत क्षिप्रं कुम्भकर्णं महाबलम्।
स हि संख्ये महाबाहुः ककुदं सर्वरक्षसाम्।
वानरान् राजपुत्रौ च क्षिप्रमेव हनिष्यति॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Therefore speedily rouse Kumbhakarṇa, who is endowed with extraordinary might. That mighty armed ogre, the foremost of all ogres, will undoubtedly strike down at once the monkeys as well as the two princes (Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa).(18)

verses.text:
एष केतुः परं संख्ये मुख्यो वै सर्वरक्षसाम्।
कुम्भकर्णः सदा शेते मूढो ग्राम्यसुखे रतः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Addicted as he is to a vulgar delight in the form of sleep, this insensate Kumbhakarṇa, who is the most distinguished in combat, and is actually the foremost of all ogres—remains ever asleep. (19)

verses.text:
रामेणाभिनिरस्तस्य संग्रामेऽस्मिन् सुदारुणे।
भविष्यति न मे शोकः कुम्भकर्णे विबोधिते॥ २०॥
किं करिष्याम्यहं तेन शक्रतुल्यबलेन हि।
ईदृशे व्यसने घोरे यो न साह्याय कल्पते॥ २१॥
verses.m: “On Kumbhakarṇa being fully roused, the grief preying on those who stand vanquished by Rāma in this most terrible struggle, will cease. Even though he is the equal of Indra in might, what shall I do of him if he is not able to assist me even in such a terrible calamity.” (20-21)

verses.text:
ते तु तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा राक्षसेन्द्रस्य राक्षसाः।
जग्मुः परमसम्भ्रान्ताः कुम्भकर्णनिवेशनम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid speech of Rāvaṇa, the lord of ogres, the said ogres proceeded to the residence of Kumbhakarṇa, extremely puzzled for they did not know how to rouse Kumbhakarṇa before time.(22)

verses.text:
ते रावणसमादिष्टा मांसशोणितभोजनाः।
गन्धं माल्यं महद्भक्ष्यमादाय सहसा ययुः॥ २३॥
verses.m: Taking with them perfumery, garlands and immense food, when duly commanded by Rāvaṇa, the said ogres, who fed on flesh and blood, left all at once for Kumbhakarṇa’s residence. (23)

verses.text:
तां प्रविश्य महाद्वारां सर्वतो योजनायताम्।
कुम्भकर्णगुहां रम्यां पुष्पगन्धप्रवाहिनीम्॥ २४॥
कुम्भकर्णस्य निःश्वासादवधूता महाबलाः।
प्रतिष्ठमानाः कृच्छ्रेण यत्नात् प्रविविशुर्गुहाम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: Having penetrated deep into that lovely subterranean abode of Kumbhakarṇa, which was provided with enormous gates, nay, which was one Yojana (or eight miles) in extent on every side, and from which issued a stream of odour of flowers—the ogres, though endowed with extraordinary might, were pushed back by force of the wind from the nostrils of Kumbhakarṇa and, pressing forward with difficulty, forced their way into the cave with effort. (24-25)

verses.text:
तां प्रविश्य गुहां रम्यां रत्नकाञ्चनकुट्टिमाम्।
ददृशुर्नैर्ऋतव्याघ्राः शयानं भीमविक्रमम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: Penetrating deep into the delightful underground dwelling with its pavement of precious stones and gold, the aforesaid tigers among ogres beheld Kumbhakarṇa of terrible prowess sleeping. (26)

verses.text:
ते तु तं विकृतं सुप्तं विकीर्णमिव पर्वतम्।
कुम्भकर्णं महानिद्रं समेताः प्रत्यबोधयन्॥ २७॥
verses.m: Those ogres for their part collectively began to waken the said Kumbhakarṇa, who, while lying asleep in an unnatural state, looked like a scattered mountain, and was buried in deep slumber. (27)

verses.text:
ऊर्ध्वलोमाञ्चिततनुं श्वसन्तमिव पन्नगम्।
भ्रामयन्तं विनिःश्वासैः शयानं भीमविक्रमम्॥ २८॥
भीमनासापुटं तं तु पातालविपुलाननम्।
शयने न्यस्तसर्वाङ्गं मेदोरुधिरगन्धिनम्॥ २९॥
काञ्चनाङ्गदनद्धाङ्गं किरीटेनार्कवर्चसम्।
ददृशुर्नैर्ऋतव्याघ्रं कुम्भकर्णमरिंदमम्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: They, for their part, found Kumbhakarṇa of terrible prowess, a veritable tiger among the ogres (scions of Nirṛti, the ogre presiding over the south-west) and the tamer of his enemies, hissing like a serpent, nay, making people turn back by the force of his outgoing breaths, while sleeping, distinguished by horrible nostrils and a mouth enormous as Pātāla (the lowest subterranean region), emitting an odour of fat and blood from his unrinsed mouth and shining as the sun because of his diadem, his body covered with bristling hair, all his limbs stretched on a bed and his arms adorned with armlets of gold. (28—30)

verses.text:
ततश्चक्रुर्महात्मानः कुम्भकर्णस्य चाग्रतः।
भूतानां मेरुसंकाशं राशिं परमतर्पणम्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: The gigantic ogres then placed before Kumbhakarṇa a heap of animals, resembling Mount Meru, which was calculated to bring him supreme satiation. (31)

verses.text:
मृगाणां महिषाणां च वराहाणां च संचयान्।
चक्रुर्नैर्ऋतशार्दूला राशिमन्नस्य चाद्भुतम्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: The said tigers among ogres also piled up hillocks of antelopes, buffaloes and swine as well as a prodigious mound of victuals. (32)

verses.text:
ततः शोणितकुम्भांश्च मांसानि विविधानि च।
पुरस्तात् कुम्भकर्णस्य चक्रुस्त्रिदशशत्रवः॥ ३३॥
verses.m: After that the enemies of gods placed before Kumbhakarṇa pails of blood and meats of every variety as well. (33)

verses.text:
लिलिपुश्च परार्घ्येन चन्दनेन परंतपम्।
दिव्यैराश्वासयामासुर्माल्यैर्गन्धैश्च गन्धिभिः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: Again, the ogres daubed Kumbhakarṇa (the scourge of his enemies) with a superb sandal-paste and communicated odour to him through fragrant garlands and sweet perfumes. (34)

verses.text:
धूपगन्धांश्च ससृजुस्तुष्टुवुश्च परंतपम्।
जलदा इव चानेदुर्यातुधानास्ततस्ततः॥ ३५॥
verses.m: They also burnt incense and extolled Kumbhakarṇa, the scourge of his enemies. The ogres also thundered like clouds on every side. (35)

verses.text:
शङ्खांश्च पूरयामासुः शशाङ्कसदृशप्रभान्।
तुमुलं युगपच्चापि विनेदुश्चाप्यमर्षिताः॥ ३६॥
verses.m: Nay, they blew with full cheeks their conches shining brightly like the sun and synchronously raised a tumultuous uproar, seized with anger, as they were. (36)

verses.text:
नेदुरास्फोटयामासुश्चिक्षिपुस्ते निशाचराः।
कुम्भकर्णविबोधार्थं चक्रुस्ते विपुलं स्वरम्॥ ३७॥
verses.m: The rangers of the night roared, clapped on their arms and pushed the limbs of Kumbhakarṇa. They further set up a great clamour in order to awaken him fully. (37)

verses.text:
सशङ्खभेरीपणवप्रणादं
सास्फोटितक्ष्वेलितसिंहनादम्।
दिशो द्रवन्तस्त्रिदिवं किरन्तः
श्रुत्वा विहंगाः सहसा निपेतुः॥ ३८॥
verses.m: On hearing the aforesaid slapping of arms, thundering and leonine roar, combined with the blast of conches and the roll of kettledrums and drums, while flying rapidly in all the ten directions and soaring into the sky, birds fell down all at once. (38)

verses.text:
यदा भृशं तैर्निनदैर्महात्मा
न कुम्भकर्णो बुबुधे प्रसुप्तः।
ततो भुशुण्डीर्मुसलानि सर्वे
रक्षोगणास्ते जगृहुर्गदाश्च॥ ३९॥
verses.m: When the colossal Kumbhakarṇa, who was fast asleep, could not be roused even by means of those aforesaid sounds, repeatedly set up, all those troops of ogres seized hold of Bhuśuṇḍīs (a particular kind of mallet), mallets and maces. (39)

verses.text:
तं शैलशृङ्गैर्मुसलैर्गदाभि-
र्वक्षःस्थले मुद्गरमुष्टिभिश्च।
सुखप्रसुप्तं भुवि कुम्भकर्णं
रक्षांस्युदग्राणि तदा निजघ्नुः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: The mighty ogres then began to strike hard the celebrated Kumbhakarṇa, lying fast asleep comfortably on the ground, with mountain peaks, pestles, maces, mallets and fists too on the chest. (40)

verses.text:
तस्य निःश्वासवातेन कुम्भकर्णस्य रक्षसः।
राक्षसाः कुम्भकर्णस्य स्थातुं शेकुर्न चाग्रतः॥ ४१॥
verses.m: Repulsed by the wind in the form of the outgoing breath of the celebrated ogre, Kumbhakarṇa, however, the ogres could not stand before him. (41)

verses.text:
ततः परिहिता गाढं राक्षसा भीमविक्रमाः।
मृदङ्गपणवान् भेरीः शङ्खकुम्भगणांस्तथा॥ ४२॥
verses.m: Tightly dressed (in order to be able to stand firmly) the aforesaid ogres of terrible prowess began to beat clay tomtoms and drums, kettledrums and pails as well. (42)

verses.text:
दश राक्षससाहस्रं युगपत्पर्यवारयत्।
नीलाञ्जनचयाकारं ते तु तं प्रत्यबोधयन्॥ ४३॥
अभिघ्नन्तो नदन्तश्च न च सम्बुबुधे तदा।
यदा चैनं न शेकुस्ते प्रतिबोधयितुं तदा॥ ४४॥
ततो गुरुतरं यत्नं दारुणं समुपाक्रमन्।
अश्वानुष्ट्रान् खरान् नागाञ्जघ्नुर्दण्डकशाङ् कुशैः॥ ४५॥
भेरीशङ्खमृदङ्गांश्च सर्वप्राणैरवादयन्।
निजघ्नुश्चास्य गात्राणि महाकाष्ठकटंकरैः॥ ४६॥
मुद्गरैर्मुसलैश्चापि सर्वप्राणसमुद्यतैः।
तेन नादेन महता लङ्का सर्वा प्रपूरिता।
सपर्वतवना सर्वा सोऽपि नैव प्रबुध्यते॥ ४७॥
verses.m: Ten thousand ogres surrounded at a time Kumbhakarṇa, who resembled a mass of black coal. Striking him on all sides and roaring, they for their part tried to rouse him; nevertheless he did not wake fully then. Nay, when they could not waken him at that time, they initiated a more effective and violent method (of rousing him) than before. They struck horses, camels, donkeys and elephants with staffs, whips and goads and urged them to tread on him. They also sounded kettledrums, conches and clay tomtoms with all their might—and pounded his limbs with bundles of heavy logs, mallets and pestles too lifted with all their strength. The entire Laṅkā, mountains, woods and all, was filled with that noise; yet Kumbhakarṇa too did not wake at all. (43—47)

verses.text:
ततो भेरीसहस्रं तु युगपत् समहन्यत।
मृष्टकाञ्चनकोणानामसक्तानां समन्ततः॥ ४८॥
verses.m: Then was sounded all at once a thousand of kettledrums ceaselessly beaten with sticks of polished gold on all sides. (48)

verses.text:
एवमप्यतिनिद्रस्तु यदा नैव प्रबुध्यते।
शापस्य वशमापन्नस्ततः क्रुद्धा निशाचराः॥ ४९॥
verses.m: When, however, the ogre, who was wrapt in excessive slumber under the spell of a curse uttered by Brahmā, could not be wakened at all in the aforesaid manner, the prowlers of the night were filled with rage. (49)

verses.text:
ततः कोपसमाविष्टाः सर्वे भीमपराक्रमाः।
तद् रक्षो बोधयिष्यन्तश्चक्रुरन्ये पराक्रमम्॥ ५०॥
verses.m: Completely dominated by anger, all other ogres (of terrible prowess) tried their strength to rouse that ogre. (50)

verses.text:
अन्ये भेरीः समाजघ्नुरन्ये चक्रुर्महास्वनम्।
केशानन्ये प्रलुलुपुः कर्णानन्ये दशन्ति च॥ ५१॥
verses.m: Some beat kettledrums with full force, others raised a shout, still others tore out his hair, while yet others bit his ears. (51)

verses.text:
उदकुम्भशतानन्ये समसिञ्चन्त कर्णयोः।
न कुम्भकर्णः पस्पन्दे महानिद्रावशं गतः॥ ५२॥
verses.m: Some more poured hundreds of pails of water into them. Kumbhakarṇa, however, who had fallen under the sway of deep slumber, did not stir. (52)

verses.text:
अन्ये च बलिनस्तस्य कूटमुद्गरपाणयः।
मूर्ध्नि वक्षसि गात्रेषु पातयन् कूटमुद्गरान्॥ ५३॥
verses.m: Other mighty ogres too, who had mallets studded with nails, in their hands, let their mallets too fall on his head, chest and other limbs. (53)

verses.text:
रज्जुबन्धनबद्धाभिः शतघ्नीभिश्च सर्वतः।
वध्यमानो महाकायो न प्राबुध्यत राक्षसः॥ ५४॥
verses.m: Nay, the colossal ogre did not wake, though being struck on all sides with Śataghnīs (a kind of mace) fastened with cords and thongs. (54)

verses.text:
वारणानां सहस्रं च शरीरेऽस्य प्रधावितम्।
कुम्भकर्णस्तदा बुद्ध्वा स्पर्शं परमबुध्यत॥ ५५॥
verses.m: A thousand of elephants were also made to run up and down his body. Waking only then, he felt a mere touch. (55)

verses.text:
स पात्यमानैर्गिरिशृङ्गवृक्षै-
रचिन्तयंस्तान् विपुलान् प्रहारान्।
निद्राक्षयात् क्षुद्भयपीडितश्च
विजृम्भमाणः सहसोत्पपात॥ ५६॥
verses.m: Tormented by the bugbear of hunger due to interruption in his sleep, though not feeling in the least the heavy blows dealt with the mountain-tops and trees, which were still being made to descend on him, nay, stretching his limbs from drowsiness, he sprang to his feet all at once. (56)

verses.text:
स नागभोगाचलशृङ्गकल्पौ
विक्षिप्य बाहू जितवज्रसारौ।
विवृत्य वक्त्रं वडवामुखाभं
निशाचरोऽसौ विकृतं जजृम्भे॥ ५७॥
verses.m: Stretching out his arms, which resembled the coils of a cobra in length and the peaks of a mountain (in stiffness), nay, which had conquered rivals with an adamantine frame, and opening his mouth, loathsome as a submarine fire, the said ranger of the night yawned. (57)

verses.text:
तस्य जाजृम्भमाणस्य वक्त्रं पातालसंनिभम्।
ददृशे मेरुशृङ्गाग्रे दिवाकर इवोदितः॥ ५८॥
verses.m: The mouth of Kumbhakarṇa, which resembled Pātāla (the lowest subterranean region), while he was repeatedly yawning, appeared like the sun risen over the top of a summit of Mount Meru. (58)

verses.text:
स जृम्भमाणोऽतिबलः प्रबुद्धस्तु निशाचरः।
निःश्वासश्चास्य संजज्ञे पर्वतादिव मारुतः॥ ५९॥
verses.m: Yawning in this way, that prowler of the night, who was endowed with extraordinary might, woke up fully. And breath escaped from his mouth even as he yawned like the wind blowing from a mountain. (59)

verses.text:
रूपमुत्तिष्ठतस्तस्य कुम्भकर्णस्य तद् बभौ।
युगान्ते सर्वभूतानि कालस्येव दिधक्षतः॥ ६०॥
verses.m: The well-known form of Kumbhakarṇa, even as he rose, looked like Kāla (the Time-Spirit) seeking, as it were, to consume all created beings at the time of universal dissolution. (60)

verses.text:
तस्य दीप्ताग्निसदृशे विद्युत्सदृशवर्चसी।
ददृशाते महानेत्रे दीप्ताविव महाग्रहौ॥ ६१॥
verses.m: His enormous eyes, which resembled a blazing fire and were dazzling like lightning, looked like two luminous major planets. (61)

verses.text:
ततस्त्वदर्शयन् सर्वान् भक्ष्यांश्च विविधान् बहून्।
वराहान् महिषांश्चैव बभक्ष स महाबलः॥ ६२॥
verses.m: Thereupon the ogres for their part showed to him all the plentiful victuals of various kinds. The ogre, who was endowed with extraordinary might, ate up the meat of boars as well as buffaloes. (62)

verses.text:
आदद् बुभुक्षितो मांसं शोणितं तृषितोऽपिबत्।
मेदःकुम्भांश्च मद्यांश्च पपौ शक्ररिपुस्तदा॥ ६३॥
verses.m: Feeling hungry, the enemy of Indra (the ruler of gods) ate meat; and, feeling thirsty, he quaffed blood as well as pails of fat and wines at that time. (63)

verses.text:
ततस्तृप्त इति ज्ञात्वा समुत्पेतुर्निशाचराः।
शिरोभिश्च प्रणम्यैनं सर्वतः पर्यवारयन्॥ ६४॥
verses.m: Realizing that he was sated, the rangers of the night then came up before him and, respectfully greeting him with their heads bent low, surrounded him on all sides. (64)

verses.text:
निद्राविशदनेत्रस्तु कलुषीकृतलोचनः।
चारयन् सर्वतो दृष्टिं तान् ददर्श निशाचरान्॥ ६५॥
verses.m: Casting his glance on all sides, Kumbhakarṇa for his part, whose eyes were half-closed due to sleepiness, nay, whose vision was still clouded, looked at the rangers of the night. (65)

verses.text:
स सर्वान् सान्त्वयामास नैर्ऋतान् नैर्ऋतर्षभः।
बोधनाद् विस्मितश्चापि राक्षसानिदमब्रवीत्॥ ६६॥
verses.m: That bull among the ogres (lit., scions of Nirṛti, the ogre presiding over the south-west) soothed all the ogres. And, also astonished at being wakened prematurely, he questioned the ogres as follows: (66)

verses.text:
किमर्थमहमादृत्य भवद्भिः प्रतिबोधितः।
कच्चित् सुकुशलं राज्ञो भयं वा नेह किंचन॥ ६७॥
verses.m: “What for have I been roused by you with effort? I hope all is well with the king and no danger has arisen here. (67)

verses.text:
अथवा ध्रुवमन्येभ्यो भयं परमुपस्थितम्।
यदर्थमेव त्वरितैर्भवद्भिः प्रतिबोधितः॥ ६८॥
verses.m: “Or, without doubt a great peril has come from the enemies, for warding off which I have been hastily woken by you. (68)

verses.text:
अद्य राक्षसराजस्य भयमुत्पाटयाम्यहम्।
दारयिष्ये महेन्द्रं वा शीतयिष्ये तथानलम्॥ ६९॥
verses.m: “I shall uproot the fear of Rāvaṇa, the king of ogres, today. I shall tear asunder the Mahendra mountain or shall freeze fire, if necessary. (69)

verses.text:
न ह्यल्पकारणे सुप्तं बोधयिष्यति मादृशम्।
तदाख्यातार्थतत्त्वेन मत्प्रबोधनकारणम्॥ ७०॥
verses.m: “Surely he would not rouse me, when asleep, for a trivial reason. Therefore, point out to me in reality the cause of waking me.” (70)

verses.text:
एवं ब्रुवाणं संरब्धं कुम्भकर्णमरिंदमम्।
यूपाक्षः सचिवो राज्ञः कृताञ्जलिरभाषत॥ ७१॥
verses.m: To Kumbhakarṇa, the tamer of his enemies, who was speaking as aforesaid, full of rage,Yūpākṣa, a minister of the king, replied as follows with joined palms: (71)

verses.text:
न नो देवकृतं किंचिद् भयमस्ति कदाचन।
मानुषान्नो भयं राजंस्तुमुलं सम्प्रबाधते॥ ७२॥
verses.m: “No danger can ever be brought upon us by gods. A formidable danger from a mortal is, however, pressing hard upon us, O prince! (72)

verses.text:
न दैत्यदानवेभ्यो वा भयमस्ति न नः क्वचित्।
यादृशं मानुषं राजन् भयमस्मानुपस्थितम्॥ ७३॥
verses.m: “The kind of danger which has come upon us, O prince, has never come even from the Daityas (giants) and Dānavas (demons). (73)

verses.text:
वानरैः पर्वताकारैर्लङ्केयं परिवारिता।
सीताहरणसंतप्ताद् रामान्नस्तुमुलं भयम्॥ ७४॥
verses.m: “This city of Laṅkā has been laid siege to by monkeys resembling mountains in size and formidable is the danger to us from Rāma, who is distressed on account of the abduction of his wife, Sītā. (74)

verses.text:
एकेन वानरेणेयं पूर्वं दग्धा महापुरी।
कुमारो निहतश्चाक्षः सानुयात्रः सकुञ्जरः॥ ७५॥
verses.m: “Latterly this large city was set fire to and Prince Akṣa was made short work of, with his elephant and followers, by a single monkey. (75)

verses.text:
स्वयं रक्षोधिपश्चापि पौलस्त्यो देवकण्टकः।
व्रजेति संयुगे मुक्तो रामेणादित्यवर्चसा॥ ७६॥
verses.m: “Nay, even Rāvaṇa himself, a scion of Sage Pulasti, the suzerain lord of ogres and a thorn in the side of gods, was let go in an encounter with the word ‘Depart!’ by Rāma, possessing the splendour of the sun. (76)

verses.text:
यन्न देवैः कृतो राजा नापि दैत्यैर्न दानवैः।
कृतः स इह रामेण विमुक्तः प्राणसंशयात्॥ ७७॥
verses.m: “The king was this time reduced to a plight to which he had never been reduced either by the Daityas or even by Dānavas, and just escaped from a peril to his life.” (77)

verses.text:
स यूपाक्षवचः श्रुत्वा भ्रातुर्युधि पराभवम्।
कुम्भकर्णो विवृत्ताक्षो यूपाक्षमिदमब्रवीत्॥ ७८॥
verses.m: Hearing the report of Yūpākṣa concerning the discomfiture of his elder brother, Kumbhakarṇa with rolling eyes replied to Yūpākṣa as follows: (78)

verses.text:
सर्वमद्यैव यूपाक्ष हरिसैन्यं सलक्ष्मणम्।
राघवं च रणे जित्वा ततो द्रक्ष्यामि रावणम्॥ ७९॥
verses.m: “Conquering this very day, O Yūpākṣa, the entire army of monkeys as also Rāma with Lakṣmaṇa, I shall see Rāvaṇa only then. (79)

verses.text:
राक्षसांस्तर्पयिष्यामि हरीणां मांसशोणितैः।
रामलक्ष्मणयोश्चापि स्वयं पास्यामि शोणितम्॥ ८०॥
verses.m: “I shall gorge the ogres with the flesh and blood of monkeys and shall quaff the blood of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa myself.” (80)

verses.text:
तत् तस्य वाक्यं ब्रुवतो निशम्य
सगर्वितं रोषविवृद्धदोषम्।
महोदरो नैर्ऋतयोधमुख्यः
कृताञ्जलिर्वाक्यमिदं बभाषे॥ ८१॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid reply of Kumbhakarṇa, even as he was speaking, which was full of arrogance, Mahodara, the foremost of ogre warriors, submitted as follows with joined palms to Kumbhakarṇa, whose anger had enhanced his violent temper beyond measure: (81)

verses.text:
रावणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा गुणदोषौ विमृश्य च।
पश्चादपि महाबाहो शत्रून् युधि विजेष्यसि॥ ८२॥
verses.m: “You should conquer the enemies in combat only after hearing the command of Rāvaṇa and weighing the advantages and disadvantages of the course you are going to take, O mighty-armed one!” (82)

verses.text:
महोदरवचः श्रुत्वा राक्षसैः परिवारितः।
कुम्भकर्णो महातेजाः सम्प्रतस्थे महाबलः॥ ८३॥
verses.m: Hearing the advice of Mahodara and surrounded by ogres, Kumbhakarṇa, who was endowed with extraordinary energy and possessed of great might, prepared to depart. (83)

verses.text:
सुप्तमुत्थाप्य भीमाक्षं भीमरूपपराक्रमम्।
राक्षसास्त्वरिता जग्मुर्दशग्रीवनिवेशनम्॥ ८४॥
verses.m: Having roused Kumbhakarṇa of frightful eyes and of terrible aspect and prowess, who was lying asleep, the ogres hastily returned to the palace of Rāvaṇa (the ten-headed monster). (84)

verses.text:
तेऽभिगम्य दशग्रीवमासीनं परमासने।
ऊचुर्बद्धाञ्जलिपुटाः सर्व एव निशाचराः॥ ८५॥
verses.m: Approaching Rāvaṇa, seated on an excellent throne, all the aforesaid ogres submitted to him as follows with joined palms: (85)

verses.text:
कुम्भकर्णः प्रबुद्धोऽसौ भ्राता ते राक्षसेश्वर।
कथं तत्रैव निर्यातु द्रक्ष्यसे तमिहागतम्॥ ८६॥
verses.m: “Kumbhakarṇa, your younger brother, O lord of ogres, is fully awake. How should he proceed? Should he sally forth straight to the battlefield or would you see him arrived here?” (86)

verses.text:
रावणस्त्वब्रवीद्धृष्टो राक्षसांस्तानुपस्थितान्।
द्रष्टुमेनमिहेच्छामि यथान्यायं च पूज्यताम्॥ ८७॥
verses.m: Feeling rejoiced, Rāvaṇa for his part replied to the aforesaid ogres, standing near. “I wish to see him here. Nay, let him be honoured as propriety demands.” (87)

verses.text:
तथेत्युक्त्वा तु ते सर्वे पुनरागम्य राक्षसाः।
कुम्भकर्णमिदं वाक्यमूचू रावणचोदिताः॥ ८८॥
verses.m: Saying “Amen!” and coming back forthwith, all those ogres submitted to Kumbhakarṇa as follows, as commanded by Rāvaṇa: (88)

verses.text:
द्रष्टुं त्वां काङ्क्षते राजा सर्वराक्षसपुङ्गवः।
गमने क्रियतां बुद्धिर्भ्रातरं सम्प्रहर्षय॥ ८९॥
verses.m: “The king, who is a veritable bull among all the ogres, desires to see Your Royal Highness. Therefore, let your mind be made up to depart. Be pleased to bring excessive joy to your elder brother.” (89)

verses.text:
कुम्भकर्णस्तु दुर्धर्षो भ्रातुराज्ञाय शासनम्।
तथेत्युक्त्वा महावीर्यः शयनादुत्पपात ह॥ ९०॥
verses.m: Coming to know the behest of his elder brother, and saying “Be it so,” Kumbhakarṇa for his part, who was difficult to overcome and was endowed with extraordinary prowess, leapt up from his bed: so the tradition goes. (90)

verses.text:
प्रक्षाल्य वदनं हृष्टः स्नातः परमहर्षितः।
पिपासुस्त्वरयामास पानं बलसमीरणम्॥ ९१॥
verses.m: Joyfully washing his face, and feeling extremely delighted on having bathed, he ordered some drink, which was calculated to enhance his strength, to be speedily brought to him from the palace of Rāvaṇa as he was feeling thirsty. (91)

verses.text:
ततस्ते त्वरितास्तत्र राक्षसा रावणाज्ञया।
मद्यं भक्ष्यांश्च विविधान् क्षिप्रमेवोपहारयन्॥ ९२॥
verses.m: Thereupon those ogres, who had gone to summon him, hurriedly brought thither under orders of Rāvaṇa wine and dishes of various kinds in no time. (92)

verses.text:
पीत्वा घटसहस्रे द्वे गमनायोपचक्रमे।
ईषत्समुत्कटो मत्तस्तेजोबलसमन्वितः॥ ९३॥
verses.m: Having quaffed two thousand pails of wine, Kumbhakarṇa, who felt a bit excited and inebriated and was replenished with energy and strength—prepared to depart. (93)

verses.text:
कुम्भकर्णो बभौ रुष्टः कालान्तकयमोपमः।
भ्रातुः स भवनं गच्छन् रक्षोबलसमन्वितः।
कुम्भकर्णः पदन्यासैरकम्पयत मेदिनीम्॥ ९४॥
verses.m: Filled with rage, Kumbhakarṇa looked like Yama (the god of retribution) bent on destroying the creation at the time of universal dissolution. Marching to the palace of his elder brother, surrounded by an army of ogres, the said Kumbhakarṇa shook the earth with his strides. (94)

verses.text:
स राजमार्गं वपुषा प्रकाशयन्
सहस्ररश्मिर्धरणीमिवांशुभिः।
जगाम तत्राञ्जलिमालया वृतः
शतक्रतुर्गेहमिव स्वयंभुवः॥ ९५॥
verses.m: Illuminating the king’s highway with the splendour of his body even as the sun, the thousand-rayed luminary, illumines the earth with its rays, Kumbhakarṇa proceeded to the royal palace surrounded by a circle of joined palms of the ogres accompanying him even as Indra (who is presupposed to have performed a hundred horse-sacrifices in his previous life or lives as a condition precedent to his attaining the position of Indra) would to the abode of Brahmā (the self-born creator). (95)

verses.text:
तं राजमार्गस्थममित्रघातिनं
वनौकसस्ते सहसा बहिःस्थिताः।
दृष्ट्वाप्रमेयं गिरिशृङ्गकल्पं
वितत्रसुस्ते सह यूथपालैः॥ ९६॥
verses.m: Beholding all of a sudden Kumbhakarṇa, the destroyer of his enemies, who was immeasurably tall and looked like the peak of a mountain, marching along the main road, those well-known monkeys (lit., dwellers in the woods), standing outside the city, got alarmed together with their troop-commanders. (96)

verses.text:
केचिच्छरण्यं शरणं स्म रामं
व्रजन्ति केचिद् व्यथिताः पतन्ति।
केचिद् दशश्च व्यथिताः पतन्ति
केचिद् भयार्ता भुवि शेरते स्म॥ ९७॥
verses.m: Some sought Śrī Rāma, who was capable of affording shelter to them, as their asylum; while others fell down, filled with agony. Nay, still others, seized with panic, fled in all directions; while yet others, stricken with fear, lay down on the earth. (97)

verses.text:
तमद्रिशृङ्गप्रतिमं किरीटिनं
स्पृशन्तमादित्यमिवात्मतेजसा।
वनौकसः प्रेक्ष्य विवृद्धमद्भुतं
भयार्दिता दुद्रुविरे यतस्ततः॥ ९८॥
verses.m: Oppressed with fear to behold the prodigy, who resembled the peak of a mountain and was adorned with a diadem, who was touching the sun, as it were, with the brilliance of his person and had grown immensely in size, the monkeys ran hither and thither. (98)

verses.text:
ततो रामो महातेजा धनुरादाय वीर्यवान्।
किरीटिनं महाकायं कुम्भकर्णं ददर्श ह॥ १॥
verses.m: Taking up his bow, the valiant Śrī Rāma, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, beheld the gigantic Kumbhakarṇa, adorned with a diadem. (1)

verses.text:
तं दृष्ट्वा राक्षसश्रेष्ठं पर्वताकारदर्शनम्।
क्रममाणमिवाकाशं पुरा नारायणं यथा॥ २॥
verses.m: Perceiving that prince of ogres, who looked like a mountain, taking strides across space, as it were, like Lord Nārāyaṇa (manifested in the form of Trivikrama, who measured the whole universe in a couple of strides), he became alert. (2)

verses.text:
सतोयाम्बुदसंकाशं काञ्चनाङ्गदभूषणम्।
दृष्ट्वा पुनः प्रदुद्राव वानराणां महाचमूः॥ ३॥
verses.m: Catching sight of the ogre, who closely resembled a cloud charged with rain and was adorned with gold armlets, the huge army of monkeys fled with full speed again. (3)

verses.text:
विद्रुतां वाहिनीं दृष्ट्वा वर्धमानं च राक्षसम्।
सविस्मितमिदं रामो विभीषणमुवाच ह॥ ४॥
verses.m: Seeing the army scared away, and the ogre becoming larger in size, Śrī Rāma with astonishment asked Vibhīṣaṇa as follows: (4)

verses.text:
कोऽसौ पर्वतसंकाशः किरीटी हरिलोचनः।
लङ्कायां दृश्यते वीरः सविद्युदिव तोयदः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Who is that with a diadem and tawny eyes and resembling a mountain? He is seen in Laṅkā, like a cloud riven by lightning. (5)

verses.text:
पृथिव्यां केतुभूतोऽसौ महानेकोऽत्र दृश्यते।
यं दृष्ट्वा वानराः सर्वे विद्रवन्ति ततस्ततः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “The colossal ogre is seen here like a solitary comet on earth, beholding whom all the monkeys are fleeing in every direction. (6)

verses.text:
आचक्ष्व सुमहान् कोऽसौ रक्षो वा यदि वासुरः।
न मयैवंविधं भूतं दृष्टपूर्वं कदाचन॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Please point out to me who that colossus is, an ogre or a demon? No such being was ever seen by me before.” (7)

verses.text:
सम्पृष्टो राजपुत्रेण रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा।
विभीषणो महाप्राज्ञः काकुत्स्थमिदमब्रवीत्॥ ८॥
verses.m: Questioned in these words by Prince Śrī Rāma of unwearied action, the highly sagacious Vibhīṣaṇa replied to Śrī Rāma, a scion of Kakutstha, as follows: (8)

verses.text:
येन वैवस्वतो युद्धे वासवश्च पराजितः।
सैष विश्रवसः पुत्रः कुम्भकर्णः प्रतापवान्।
अस्य प्रमाणसदृशो राक्षसोऽन्यो न विद्यते॥ ९॥
verses.m: “He is the well-known son of sage Viśravā, the fiery Kumbhakarṇa, by whom Yama (son of the sun-god) as well as Indra were vanquished. There is no other ogre vying with him in size. (9)

verses.text:
एतेन देवा युधि दानवाश्च
यक्षा भुजंगाः पिशिताशनाश्च।
गन्धर्वविद्याधरकिंनराश्च
सहस्रशो राघव सम्प्रभग्नाः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “By him were completely routed in their thousands in combat Dānavas (demons) and Yakṣas (a class of demigods), serpents and ogres (lit., flesh-eaters), Gandharvas (celestial musicians), Vidyādharas (celestial artistes) and Kinnaras (semi-divine beings with a human figure and the head of a horse), O scion of Raghu! (10)

verses.text:
शूलपाणिं विरूपाक्षं कुम्भकर्णं महाबलम्।
हन्तुं न शेकुस्त्रिदशाः कालोऽयमिति मोहिताः॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Deluded to think that he was Death personified, the gods could not kill Kumbhakarṇa, who is endowed with extraordinary might and hideous eyes and stood pike in hand. (11)

verses.text:
प्रकृत्या ह्येष तेजस्वी कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः।
अन्येषां राक्षसेन्द्राणां वरदानकृतं बलम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “The yonder Kumbhakarṇa is daring and endowed with extraordinary might by nature. The strength of other ogre chiefs, however, is attributable to boons (conferred on them by gods). (12)

verses.text:
बालेन जातमात्रेण क्षुधार्तेन महात्मना।
भक्षितानि सहस्राणि प्रजानां सुबहून्यपि॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Very many thousands of created beings were devoured by the colossus, oppressed with hunger, while he was yet a new-born babe. (13)

verses.text:
तेषु सम्भक्ष्यमाणेषु प्रजा भयनिपीडिताः।
यान्ति स्म शरणं शक्रं तमप्यर्थं न्यवेदयन्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Sore-stricken with fear on their being devoured by the monster, the created beings sought Indra as their refuge and reported that matter to him. (14)

verses.text:
स कुम्भकर्णं कुपितो महेन्द्रो
जघान वज्रेण शितेन वज्री।
स शक्रवज्राभिहतो महात्मा
चचाल कोपाच्च भृशं ननाद॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Moved to anger, the mighty Indra, who was armed with a thunderbolt, struck Kumbhakarṇa with his sharp thunderbolt. Struck with Indra’s thunderbolt, the colossus reeled and emitted a tremendous roar. (15)

verses.text:
तस्य नानद्यमानस्य कुम्भकर्णस्य रक्षसः।
श्रुत्वा निनादं वित्रस्ताः प्रजा भूयो वितत्रसुः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Hearing the roar of the ogre, Kumbhakarṇa, who was repeatedly roaring, the created beings, who were already greatly afraid, felt frightened all the more. (16)

verses.text:
ततः क्रुद्धो महेन्द्रस्य कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः।
निष्कृष्यैरावताद् दन्तं जघानोरसि वासवम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Tearing out a tusk from the mouth of Airāvata, carrying Indra on its back, the enraged Kumbhakarṇa, who was endowed with extraordinary might, then struck Indra in the breast with it. (17)

verses.text:
कुम्भकर्णप्रहारार्तो विजज्वाल स वासवः।
ततो विषेदुः सहसा देवा ब्रह्मर्षिदानवाः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Agonized by the blow of Kumbhakarṇa, the aforesaid Indra felt tormented. Thereupon the gods, the Brāhmaṇa Ṛṣis and the demons grew despondent all at once. (18)

verses.text:
प्रजाभिः सह शक्रश्च ययौ स्थानं स्वयंभुवः।
कुम्भकर्णस्य दौरात्म्यं शशंसुस्ते प्रजापतेः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Accompanied by those created beings, Indra sought the realm of Brahmā. They complained to Brahmā (the lord of created beings) about the wickedness of Kumbhakarṇa. (19)

verses.text:
प्रजानां भक्षणं चापि देवानां चापि धर्षणम्।
आश्रमध्वंसनं चापि परस्त्रीहरणं भृशम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “They also told him how he devoured created beings, assailed gods, laid waste the hermitages of sages and repeatedly carried off others’ wives. (20)

verses.text:
एवं प्रजा यदि त्वेष भक्षयिष्यति नित्यशः।
अचिरेणैव कालेन शून्यो लोको भविष्यति॥ २१॥
verses.m: “ ‘If he for his part consumes created beings in this way from day to day’, they continued, ‘the world will turn desolate at no distant date.’ (21)

verses.text:
वासवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा सर्वलोकपितामहः।
रक्षांस्यावाहयामास कुम्भकर्णं ददर्श ह॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Hearing the complaint of Indra and others, Brahmā (the grandfather of the entire creation, which owes its origin to his ten mind-born sons) conjured the ogres and saw Kumbhakarṇa too alongwith them: so the tradition goes. (22)

verses.text:
कुम्भकर्णं समीक्ष्यैव वितत्रास प्रजापतिः।
कुम्भकर्णमथाश्वास्तः स्वयंभूरिदमब्रवीत्॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Brahmā (the lord of created beings), got alarmed merely on beholding Kumbhakarṇa. Restored to confidence in the meantime, however, Brahmā (the self-born creator) spoke to him as follows:(23)

verses.text:
ध्रुवं लोकविनाशाय पौलस्त्येनासि निर्मितः।
तस्मात् त्वमद्यप्रभृति मृतकल्पः शयिष्यसे॥ २४॥
verses.m: “ ‘Surely you have been begotten by Viśravā (son of Pulasti, one of my mind-born sons) to the destruction of the world. Therefore, from this day onward you shall remain buried in sleep like one dead.’ (24)

verses.text:
ब्रह्मशापाभिभूतोऽथ निपपाताग्रतः प्रभोः।
ततः परमसम्भ्रान्तो रावणो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Overpowered by the curse pronounced by Brahmā, Kumbhakarṇa forthwith fell down before the king, Rāvaṇa. Exceedingly perturbed, Rāvaṇa thereupon submitted to Brahmā as follows: (25)

verses.text:
प्रवृद्धः काञ्चनो वृक्षः फलकाले निकृत्यते।
न नप्तारं स्वकं न्याय्यं शप्तुमेवं प्रजापते॥ २५॥
verses.m: “ ‘A tree yielding gold (as its fruit) is never hewed down at the time of fructification. It is not equitable on your part to curse your own great grandson as you have done, O lord of created beings! (26)

verses.text:
न मिथ्यावचनश्च त्वं स्वप्स्यत्येव न संशयः।
कालस्तु क्रियतामस्य शयने जागरे तथा॥ २७॥
verses.m: “ ‘And your words can never prove to be false, so that sleep he must: there is no doubt about it. A period of time may kindly be fixed for his sleep as well as for his waking.’ (27)

verses.text:
रावणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा स्वयंभूरिदमब्रवीत्।
शयिता ह्येष षण्मासमेकाहं जागरिष्यति॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Hearing Rāvaṇa’s appeal, Brahmā (the self-born creator) spoke as follows: ‘He shall sleep continuously for six months and shall keep awake only for a day. (28)

verses.text:
एकेनाह्ना त्वसौ वीरश्चरन् भूमिं बुभुक्षितः।
व्यात्तास्यो भक्षयेल्लोकान् संवृद्ध इव पावकः॥ २९॥
verses.m: “ ‘Ranging the earth with his mouth wide open, when hungry, the said hero for his part may consume the world like a swollen fire in the course of a single day.’ (29)

verses.text:
सोऽसौ व्यसनमापन्नः कुम्भकर्णमबोधयत्।
त्वत्पराक्रमभीतश्च राजा सम्प्रति रावणः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Fallen in adversity and afraid of your prowess, this aforesaid king, Rāvaṇa, has just awakened Kumbhakarṇa. (30)

verses.text:
स एष निर्गतो वीरः शिबिराद् भीमविक्रमः।
वानरान् भृशसंक्रुद्धो भक्षयन् परिधावति॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Having emerged from his royal retreat, extremely enraged, this champion of terrible prowess is darting to and fro, devouring the monkeys. (31)

verses.text:
कुम्भकर्णं समीक्ष्यैव हरयोऽद्य प्रदुद्रुवुः।
कथमेनं रणे क्रुद्धं वारयिष्यन्ति वानराः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “The monkeys have run away merely on beholding Kumbhakarṇa today. How then will the monkeys be able to check him on seeing him enraged in combat? (32)

verses.text:
उच्यन्तां वानराः सर्वे यन्त्रमेतत् समुच्छ्रितम्।
इति विज्ञाय हरयो भविष्यन्तीह निर्भयाः॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “Let the monkeys be told that it is a mere mechanical device standing very high, which they see before them. The monkeys will be rid of fear on coming to know this on this occasion.” (33)

verses.text:
विभीषणवचः श्रुत्वा हेतुमत् सुमुखोद्गतम्।
उवाच राघवो वाक्यं नीलं सेनापतिं तदा॥ ३४॥
verses.m: Hearing the speech of Vibhīṣaṇa, which was full of reason and had been made with a pleasing air, Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, spoke to Nīla, the Commander-in-Chief, as follows: (34)

verses.text:
गच्छ सैन्यानि सर्वाणि व्यूह्य तिष्ठस्व पावके।
द्वाराण्यादाय लङ्कायाश्चर्याश्चास्याथ संक्रमान्॥ ३५॥
शैलशृङ्गाणि वृक्षांश्च शिलाश्चाप्युपसंहरन्।
भवन्तः सायुधाः सर्वे वानराः शैलपाणयः॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “Go, disposing all the troops in battle array, nay, occupying the gates, highways and bridges of Laṅkā and getting together mountain-tops, trees and rocks too, stand ready for operation, O son of the fire-god! And, armed with weapons and rocks in hand, you too remain alert, O monkeys!” (35-36)

verses.text:
राघवेण समादिष्टो नीलो हरिचमूपतिः।
शशास वानरानीकं यथावत् कपिकुञ्जरः॥ ३७॥
verses.m: Duly instructed as above, Nīla, the Commander-in-Chief of the simian army, an elephant among the monkeys, commanded the army of the monkeys as it should be. (37)

verses.text:
ततो गवाक्षः शरभो हनूमानङ्गदस्तथा।
शैलशृङ्गाणि शैलाभा गृहीत्वा द्वारमभ्ययुः॥ ३८॥
verses.m: Taking peaks of mountains, Gavākṣa, Śarabha, Hanumān and Aṅgada, who looked like mountains themselves, thereupon marched to the gate of Laṅkā. (38)

verses.text:
रामवाक्यमुपश्रुत्य हरयो जितकाशिनः।
पादपैरर्दयन् वीरा वानराः परवाहिनीम्॥ ३९॥
verses.m: Hearing the command of Śrī Rāma, the heroic monkeys, who were bent upon taking the life of their enemies, and who had assumed a triumphant air, began to strike the hostile army guarding the precincts of the city outside the gates. (39)

verses.text:
ततो हरीणां तदनीकमुग्रं
रराज शैलोद्यतवृक्षहस्तम्।
गिरेः समीपानुगतं यथैव
महन्महाम्भोधरजालमुग्रम् ॥ ४०॥
verses.m: Carrying rocks and uplifted trees in their hands, that formidable army of monkeys shone precisely like a terrible and huge mass of clouds hanging close to a mountain. (40)

verses.text:
स तु राक्षसशार्दूलो निद्रामदसमाकुलः।
राजमार्गं श्रिया जुष्टं ययौ विपुलविक्रमः॥ १॥
