verses.m: Heavy with sleep and inebriety, that tiger among the ogres, for his part, who was endowed with immense prowess, marched along the king’s highway which was full of splendour. (1)

verses.text:
राक्षसानां सहस्रैश्च वृतः परमदुर्जयः।
गृहेभ्यः पुष्पवर्षेण कीर्यमाणस्तदा ययौ॥ २॥
verses.m: Nay, surrounded by thousands of ogres, Kumbhakarṇa (who was exceedingly difficult to conquer) moved on, being covered all along with a shower of flowers from the houses lining the road. (2)

verses.text:
स हेमजालविततं भानुभास्वरदर्शनम्।
ददर्श विपुलं रम्यं राक्षसेन्द्रनिवेशनम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: He saw the vast and lovely abode of Rāvaṇa (the ruler of ogres), which was covered with a lattice-work of gold and as such looked bright as the sun. (3)

verses.text:
स तत्तदा सूर्य इवाभ्रजालं
प्रविश्य रक्षोधिपतेर्निवेशनम्।
ददर्श दूरेऽग्रजमासनस्थं
स्वयंभुवं शक्र इवासनस्थम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Penetrating deep into the residence of Rāvaṇa (the suzerain lord of ogres), even as the sun would disappear into a mass of clouds, he saw from afar his elder brother, Rāvaṇa, seated on his throne, even as Indra would behold Brahmā (the self-born creator) sitting on his seat. (4)

verses.text:
भ्रातुः स भवनं गच्छन् रक्षोगणसमन्वितः।
कुम्भकर्णः पदन्यासैरकम्पयत मेदिनीम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Proceeding to the dwelling of his elder brother, duly accompanied by a host of ogres, Kumbhakarṇa caused the earth to tremble with his strides. (5)

verses.text:
सोऽभिगम्य गृहं भ्रातुः कक्ष्यामभिविगाह्य च।
ददर्शोद्विग्नमासीनं विमाने पुष्पके गुरुम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Reaching the palace of his elder brother, and stepping beyond the enclosure, he beheld his elder brother seated in his aerial car, Puṣpaka, in a perturbed state. (6)

verses.text:
अथ दृष्ट्वा दशग्रीवः कुम्भकर्णमुपस्थितम्।
तूर्णमुत्थाय संहृष्टः संनिकर्षमुपानयत्॥ ७॥
verses.m: Getting up immediately on seeing Kumbhakarṇa arrived, Rāvaṇa (the ten-headed monster), who felt highly rejoiced, brought him to his side. (7)

verses.text:
अथासीनस्य पर्यङ्के कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः।
भ्रातुर्ववन्दे चरणौ किं कृत्यमिति चाब्रवीत्॥ ८॥
verses.m: Kumbhakarṇa, who was endowed with extraordinary might, forthwith bowed down at the feet of his elder brother, reclining on a couch, and inquired, “What service is required of me?” (8)

verses.text:
उत्पत्य चैनं मुदितो रावणः परिषस्वजे।
स भ्रात्रा सम्परिष्वक्तो यथावच्चाभिनन्दितः॥ ९॥
verses.m: Springing up from his seat once more, Rāvaṇa, who was filled with joy, clasped him to his bosom. In this way he was tightly embraced by his elder brother and duly hailed with joy. (9)

verses.text:
कुम्भकर्णः शुभं दिव्यं प्रतिपेदे वरासनम्।
स तदासनमाश्रित्य कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः॥ १०॥
संरक्तनयनः क्रोधाद् रावणं वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
किमर्थमहमादृत्य त्वया राजन् प्रबोधितः॥ ११॥
verses.m: Kumbhakarṇa occupied a splendid, heavenly, excellent seat. Having taken up his position on that seat, the said Kumbhakarṇa, who was endowed with extraordinary might, submitted as follows to Rāvaṇa, his eyes blood-red with anger: “What for have I been awakened by you with effort, O king? (10-11)

verses.text:
शंस कस्माद् भयं तेऽत्र को वा प्रेतो भविष्यति।
भ्रातरं रावणः क्रुद्धं कुम्भकर्णमवस्थितम्॥ १२॥
रोषेण परिवृत्ताभ्यां नेत्राभ्यां वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
अद्य ते सुमहान् कालः शयानस्य महाबल॥ १३॥
सुषुप्तस्त्वं न जानीषे मम रामकृतं भयम्।
एष दाशरथिः श्रीमान् सुग्रीवसहितो बली॥ १४॥
समुद्रं लङ्घयित्वा तु मूलं नः परिकृन्तति।
हन्त पश्यस्व लङ्कायां वनान्युपवनानि च॥ १५॥
सेतुना सुखमागत्य वानरैकार्णवं कृतम्।
ये राक्षसा मुख्यतमा हतास्ते वानरैर्युधि॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Say from whom springs your fear and who is going to die (at my hands today).” His eyes rolling through indignation, Rāvaṇa spoke as follows to his younger brother, Kumbhakarṇa, firmly seated by his side: “A very long time has rolled past you till now, while you remained asleep, O brother, endowed with extraordinary might! Having remained buried in deep slumber, you could not know of the fear that has been engendered for me by Rāma. Having crossed the sea, this glorious and mighty son of Daśaratha, accompanied by Sugrīva, for his part is cutting at our very roots. Alas! see how after arriving with ease in Laṅkā, the groves and gardens in Laṅkā have been converted into a single sea of monkeys. Those ogres who were the foremost leaders have been killed by the monkeys in combat. (12—16)

verses.text:
वानराणां क्षयं युद्धे न पश्यामि कथंचन।
न चापि वानरा युद्धे जितपूर्वाः कदाचन॥ १७॥
verses.m: “I do not, however, envisage the destruction of the monkeys on the battlefield in anyway. Nor have the monkeys been conquered at any time before. (17)

verses.text:
तदेतद् भयमुत्पन्नं त्रायस्वेह महाबल।
नाशय त्वमिमानद्य तदर्थं बोधितो भवान्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Such is the fear engendered by Rāma. Save us at this juncture, O brother, endowed with extraordinary might! You destroy them today. For this you have been awakened. (18)

verses.text:
सर्वक्षपितकोशं च स त्वमभ्युपपद्य माम्।
त्रायस्वेमां पुरीं लङ्कां बालवृद्धावशेषिताम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Nay, obliging me, whose resources have been totally exhausted, save you as such this city of Laṅkā, in which children and the aged alone have been left. (19)

verses.text:
भ्रातुरर्थे महाबाहो कुरु कर्म सुदुष्करम्।
मयैवं नोक्तपूर्वो हि भ्राता कश्चित् परंतप॥ २०॥
verses.m: “For the sake of your brother myself, O mighty-armed one, accomplish a feat which is very difficult to accomplish (for others). Surely no brother was requested by me like this ever before, O scourge of your enemies! (20)

verses.text:
त्वय्यस्ति मम च स्नेहः परा सम्भावना च मे।
देवासुरेषु युद्धेषु बहुशो राक्षसर्षभ॥ २१॥
त्वया देवाः प्रतिव्यूह्य निर्जिताश्चासुरा युधि॥ २२॥
verses.m: “There is affection in my heart for you and my supreme hope is also fastened on you. On many an occasion in the wars between the gods and demons, O bull among the ogres, were the gods as well as the demons utterly routed by you on the battlefield after joining the opposite ranks. (21-22)

verses.text:
तदेतत् सर्वमातिष्ठ वीर्यं भीमपराक्रम।
नहि ते सर्वभूतेषु दृश्यते सदृशो बली॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Therefore accomplish all the aforesaid deeds of valour, O brother of terrific prowess! Indeed, no one mighty as you is seen among all created beings. (23)

verses.text:
कुरुष्व मे प्रियहितमेतदुत्तमं
यथाप्रियं प्रियरण बान्धवप्रिय।
स्वतेजसा व्यथय सपत्नवाहिनीं
शरद्घनं पवन इवोद्यतो महान्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Do this supreme, helpful act and service to me keeping in view your love for me, O lover of war and lover of kins-folk! Torment the hostile army with your fiery spirit in the same way as an active, mighty wind would dissipate an autumnal cloud.” (24)

verses.text:
तस्य राक्षसराजस्य निशम्य परिदेवितम्।
कुम्भकर्णो बभाषेदं वचनं प्रजहास च॥ १॥
verses.m: Hearing the lament of Rāvaṇa (the king of ogres), Kumbhakarṇa heartily laughed and made the following reply: (1)

verses.text:
दृष्टो दोषो हि योऽस्माभिः पुरा मन्त्रविनिर्णये।
हितेष्वनभियुक्तेन सोऽयमासादितस्त्वया॥ २॥
verses.m: “The same disaster which was actually envisaged by us before while taking the final decision after consultation with Vibhīṣaṇa and others has now been reaped by you, who were distrustful towards your well-wishers. (2)

verses.text:
शीघ्रं खल्वभ्युपेतं त्वां फलं पापस्य कर्मणः।
निरयेष्वेव पतनं यथा दुष्कृतकर्मणः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Speedily enough has the fruit of your sinful deed in the shape of Sītā’s abduction come upon you, even as damnation would visit a person of sinful deeds. (3)

verses.text:
प्रथमं वै महाराज कृत्यमेतदचिन्तितम्।
केवलं वीर्यदर्पेण नानुबन्धो विचारितः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Initially, of course, was this course of action not weighed by you. Nor was the consequence taken into account in the sheer pride of your prowess, O great king ! (4)

verses.text:
यः पश्चात्पूर्वकार्याणि कुर्यादैश्वर्यमास्थितः।
पूर्वं चोत्तरकार्याणि न स वेद नयानयौ॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Confident of his power, he who defers duties which ought to be performed earlier and accomplishes earlier, duties which can be deferred, does not know what is right and what is wrong. (5)

verses.text:
देशकालविहीनानि कर्माणि विपरीतवत्।
क्रियमाणानि दुष्यन्ति हवींष्यप्रयतेष्विव॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Actions which are performed without regard to time and place prove disastrous like those done at an adverse time and place, even as oblations poured into fires which have not been consecrated get foiled. (6)

verses.text:
त्रयाणां पञ्चधा योगं कर्मणां यः प्रपद्यते।
सचिवैः समयं कृत्वा स सम्यग् वर्तते पथि॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Holding consultation with his ministers, he who takes into consideration the five aspects* of the threefold† duties with reference to hostile kings, moves along the right path. (7)

verses.text:
यथागमं च यो राजा समयं च चिकीर्षति।
बुध्यते सचिवैर्बुद्ध्या सुहृदश्चानुपश्यति॥ ८॥
verses.m: “A king who seeks to determine his duty in accordance with the science of polity and perceives his friends too alongwith the ministers understands aright. (8)

verses.text:
धर्ममर्थं हि कामं वा सर्वान् वा रक्षसां पते।
भजेत पुरुषः काले त्रीणि द्वन्द्वानि वा पुनः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Indeed a man should pursue virtue, worldly gain or sensuous pleasure or all the three combined, or, again, two of them at a time at the appointed time,‡ O lord of ogres ! (9)

verses.text:
त्रिषु चैतेषु यच्छ्रेष्ठं श्रुत्वा तन्नावबुध्यते।
राजा वा राजमात्रो वा व्यर्थं तस्य बहुश्रुतम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Extensive learning on the part of a sovereign or a crown prince, who, having heard of that viz., virtue, which is the foremost of the above-named three, does not recognize it as such, is in vain. (10)

verses.text:
उपप्रदानं सान्त्वं च भेदं काले च विक्रमम्।
योगं च रक्षसां श्रेष्ठ तावुभौ च नयानयौ॥ ११॥
काले धर्मार्थकामान् यः सम्मन्त्र्य सचिवैः सह।
निषेवेतात्मवाँल्लोके न स व्यसनमाप्नुयात्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “The self-controlled king who, having duly deliberated with his ministers, bestows gifts, takes to (expedients of) conciliation and, sowing dissension among the hostile ranks, exhibits prowess, O prince of ogres, or resorts to them (all) together and takes recourse both to right action and the reverse of it at the right time and pursues virtue, worldly gain and sensuous pleasure at the proper time never meets with disaster in the world. (11-12)

verses.text:
हितानुबन्धमालोक्य कुर्यात् कार्यमिहात्मनः।
राजा सहार्थतत्त्वज्ञैः सचिवैर्बुद्धिजीविभिः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “A king should take action only after considering what is salutary in consequence to him, in consultation with his ministers, who make their living by their intelligence and know the reality of things. (13)

verses.text:
अनभिज्ञाय शास्त्रार्थान् पुरुषाः पशुबुद्धयः।
प्रागल्भ्याद् वक्तुमिच्छन्ति मन्त्रिष्वभ्यन्तरीकृताः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “People whose mental level is in no way higher than that of beasts and yet who have been allowed to take their seat among the counsellors, desire all the same to express their views through sheer impudence, without fully knowing the import of the scriptures. (14)

verses.text:
अशास्त्रविदुषां तेषां कार्यं नाभिहितं वचः।
अर्थशास्त्रानभिज्ञानां विपुलां श्रियमिच्छताम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “The advice tendered by such people, who having no knowledge of the scriptures, are equally ignorant of the science of wealth and seek immense wealth ought not to be followed. (15)

verses.text:
अहितं च हिताकारं धार्ष्ट्याज्जल्पन्ति ये नराः।
अवश्यं मन्त्रबाह्यास्ते कर्तव्याः कृत्यदूषकाः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Men who tender unwholesome advice in a salutary garb through sheer impudence should be excluded from deliberation as they mar the very purpose of the deliberation. (16)

verses.text:
विनाशयन्तो भर्तारं सहिताः शत्रुभिर्बुधैः।
विपरीतानि कृत्यानि कारयन्तीह मन्त्रिणः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Getting united with shrewd enemies, evil-minded counsellors in this world prevail upon their master to undertake wrong actions in order to bring him to ruin. (17)

verses.text:
तान् भर्ता मित्रसंकाशानमित्रान् मन्त्रनिर्णये।
व्यवहारेण जानीयात् सचिवानुपसंहितान्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “A ruler should make out the reality of those ministers who have been won over by the enemy to their side through bribe etc., and as such are enemies, though appearing as friends, through their actual behaviour when a final decision is being taken after deliberation. (18)

verses.text:
चपलस्येह कृत्यानि सहसानुप्रधावतः।
छिद्रमन्ये प्रपद्यन्ते क्रौञ्चस्य खमिव द्विजाः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Aliens find out the weakness of a ruler who is (easily) led away by false appearances and rushes headlong into actions, even as birds discover the hole made by the lance of Skanda, the Commander-in-Chief of the gods, in the Krauñca mountain. (19)

verses.text:
यो हि शत्रुमवज्ञाय आत्मानं नाभिरक्षति।
अवाप्नोति हि सोऽनर्थान् स्थानाच्च व्यवरोप्यते॥ २०॥
verses.m: “A king who, disregarding the enemy, does not actually protect himself, undoubtedly meets with reverses and is dragged down from his position. (20)

verses.text:
यदुक्तमिह ते पूर्वं प्रियया मेऽनुजेन च।
तदेव नो हितं वाक्यं यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु॥ २१॥
verses.m: “The advice alone which was tendered to you on a previous occasion by your beloved consort, Mandodarī, as well as by my younger brother, Vibhīṣaṇa, is salutary to us. However, do as you will.” (21)

verses.text:
तत् तु श्रुत्वा दशग्रीवः कुम्भकर्णस्य भाषितम्।
भ्रुकुटिं चैव संचक्रे क्रुद्धश्चैनमभाषत॥ २२॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid speech of Kumbhakarṇa, Rāvaṇa (the ten-headed monster) for his part frowned and filled with rage spoke to him as follows: (22)

verses.text:
मान्यो गुरुरिवाचार्यः किं मां त्वमनुशाससे।
किमेवं वाक्श्रमं कृत्वा यद् युक्तं तद् विधीयताम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Why do you instruct me like a father or a teacher worthy of respect? What avail is it to weary your tongue as you have done? Let that which is meet be done. (23)

verses.text:
विभ्रमाच्चित्तमोहाद् वा बलवीर्याश्रयेण वा।
नाभिपन्नमिदानीं यद् व्यर्था तस्य पुनः कथा॥ २४॥
verses.m: “It is futile at this hour to repeat that counsel which was not accepted by me at that time through misconception, obtuseness of understanding or through dependence on my strength and prowess. (24)

verses.text:
अस्मिन् काले तु यद् युक्तं तदिदानीं विचिन्त्यताम्।
गतं तु नानुशोचन्ति गतं तु गतमेव हि॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Let that alone which is advisable at this moment may now be thoroughly investigated. The wise do not at all grieve for the bygone. The bygone is after all irretrievably bygone, no doubt. (25)

verses.text:
ममापनयजं दोषं विक्रमेण समीकुरु।
यदि खल्वस्ति मे स्नेहो विक्रमं वाधिगच्छसि॥ २६॥
यदि कार्यं ममैतत्ते हृदि कार्यतमं मतम्।
स सुहृद् यो विपन्नार्थं दीनमभ्युपपद्यते॥ २७॥
स बन्धुर्योऽपनीतेषु साहाय्यायोपकल्पते।
तमथैवं ब्रुवाणं स वचनं धीरदारुणम्॥ २८॥
रुष्टोऽयमिति विज्ञाय शनैः श्लक्ष्णमुवाच ह।
अतीव हि समालक्ष्य भ्रातरं क्षुभितेन्द्रियम्॥ २९॥
कुम्भकर्णः शनैर्वाक्यं बभाषे परिसान्त्वयन्।
शृणु राजन्नवहितो मम वाक्यमरिंदम॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Nullify with your prowess the evil sprung from my misconduct, if at all there exists love in you for me or if you recognize your own prowess or this purpose of mine is deemed by you in your heart of hearts as supremely worth accomplishing. A friend is he who obliges an afflicted soul, whose fortune is at stake. And a kinsman is he, who is able to render help to those who have deviated from the right course.” Concluding about Rāvaṇa, who was speaking in grave and harsh tones as above, that he was angry, Kumbhakarṇa gently submitted to him in soothing words as follows: Clearly perceiving his elder brother exceedingly agitated in mind in reality, Kumbhakarṇa slowly submitted to him as follows, restoring him to confidence in everyway: “Listen, O king, to my submission, O scourge of your enemies ! (26—30)

verses.text:
अलं राक्षसराजेन्द्र संतापमुपपद्य ते।
रोषं च सम्परित्यज्य स्वस्थो भवितुमर्हसि॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “It is no use your giving way to agony, O suzerain lord of ogres! Nay, shaking off anger completely, you ought to be your normal self again. (31)

verses.text:
नैतन्मनसि कर्तव्यं मयि जीवति पार्थिव।
तमहं नाशयिष्यामि यत् कृते परितप्यते॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Such despondency should not be entertained in your mind so long as I live, O ruler of the earth! I shall exterminate him on whose account you feel agonized. (32)

verses.text:
अवश्यं तु हितं वाच्यं सर्वावस्थं मया तव।
बन्धुभावादभिहितं भ्रातृस्नेहाच्च पार्थिव॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “Salutary advice, of course, needs must be tendered by me to you under all circumstances. And that which is good to you, has been spoken by me through kinship and brotherly affection, O ruler of the earth ! (33)

verses.text:
सदृशं यच्च कालेऽस्मिन् कर्तुं स्नेहेन बन्धुना।
शत्रूणां कदनं पश्य क्रियमाणं मया रणे॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “Nay, see that which is fit to be done out of affection at this juncture by a brother, viz., the wholesale destruction of the enemy in combat. (34)

verses.text:
अद्य पश्य महाबाहो मया समरमूर्धनि।
हते रामे सह भ्रात्रा द्रवन्तीं हरिवाहिनीम्॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “See today, O mighty-armed brother, the army of monkeys fleeing, on Rāma being killed by me with his brother in the forefront of battle. (35)

verses.text:
अद्य रामस्य तद् दृष्ट्वा मयाऽऽनीतं रणाच्छिरः।
सुखी भव महाबाहो सीता भवतु दुःखिता॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “Feel gratified today to see the well-known head of Rāma brought by me from the field of battle, O mighty-armed brother ! And let Sītā feel agonized in her turn. (36)

verses.text:
अद्य रामस्य पश्यन्तु निधनं सुमहत् प्रियम्।
लङ्कायां राक्षसाः सर्वे ये ते निहतबान्धवाः॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “Let all those ogres in Laṅkā whose kinsfolk have been killed in combat witness today the death of Rāma, which will be something exceedingly welcome to them.(37)

verses.text:
अद्य शोकपरीतानां स्वबन्धुवधशोचिनाम्।
शत्रोर्युधि विनाशेन करोम्यश्रुप्रमार्जनम्॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “Through the destruction of the enemy in battle, I shall dry today the tears of those who are bewailing the loss of their kinsfolk and are overcome with grief on that account. (38)

verses.text:
अद्य पर्वतसंकाशं ससूर्यमिव तोयदम्।
विकीर्णं पश्य समरे सुग्रीवं प्लवगेश्वरम्॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “See today Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, who closely resembles a mountain (in size), thrown about, bathed in blood, on the battlefield like a cloud illumined by the evening sun. (39)

verses.text:
कथं च राक्षसैरेभिर्मया च परिसान्त्वितः।
जिघांसुभिर्दाशरथिं व्यथसे त्वं सदानघ॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “Nay, why do you feel vexed all the time, O sinless one, though reassured by these ogres as well as by myself, who are eager to kill Rāma (son of Daśaratha)? (40)

verses.text:
मां निहत्य किल त्वां हि निहनिष्यति राघवः।
नाहमात्मनि संतापं गच्छेयं राक्षसाधिप॥ ४१॥
verses.m: “Surely, Rāma, a scion of Raghu, will be able to kill you only after killing me. I, however, never give way to misgiving on that account, O suzerain lord of ogres ! (41)

verses.text:
कामं त्विदानीमपि मां व्यादिश त्वं परंतप।
न परः प्रेक्षणीयस्ते युद्धायातुलविक्रम॥ ४२॥
verses.m: “Therefore, command me at will to wage war even at this moment, O scourge of your enemies! No one else should be sought for by you for this purpose, O incomparable hero ! (42)

verses.text:
अहमुत्सादयिष्यामि शत्रूंस्तव महाबलान्।
यदि शक्रो यदि यमो यदि पावकमारुतौ॥ ४३॥
तानहं योधयिष्यामि कुबेरवरुणावपि।
गिरिमात्रशरीरस्य शितशूलधरस्य मे॥ ४४॥
नर्दतस्तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रस्य बिभीयाद् वै पुरंदरः।
अथ वा त्यक्तशस्त्रस्य मृद्गतस्तरसा रिपून्॥ ४५॥
न मे प्रतिमुखः कश्चित् स्थातुं शक्तो जिजीविषुः।
नैव शक्त्या न गदया नासिना निशितैः शरैः॥ ४६॥
verses.m: “I shall exterminate your enemies, though endowed with extraordinary might. Even if it is Indra, the ruler of gods, or, again, if it is Yama, the god of retribution, or even if they are the god of fire and the wind-god, I shall contend with them, nay, even with Kubera and Varuṇa. Even Indra, the destroyer of citadels, will dread me, endowed as I am with a body as big as a mountain and pointed teeth and wielding a sharpened pike for a weapon, even as I roar. Again, none will be able to withstand, if he wishes to survive, even if I begin to crush the enemies with impetuosity, abandoning the arms. I shall in no case fight with a javelin, nor with a mace, nor, again, with a sword, much less with whetted shafts. (43—46)

verses.text:
हस्ताभ्यामेव संरभ्य हनिष्यामि सवज्रिणम्।
यदि मे मुष्टिवेगं स राघवोऽद्य सहिष्यति॥ ४७॥
ततः पास्यन्ति बाणौघा रुधिरं राघवस्य मे।
चिन्तया तप्यसे राजन् किमर्थं मयि तिष्ठति॥ ४८॥
verses.m: “Getting enraged, I shall make short work of Rāma, even if he is accompanied by Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, with my bare hands. If the said scion of Raghu will be able to withstand the force of my fists today, the volleys of my arrows will in that case drink the blood of Rāma. Why do you feel tormented with anxiety, O king, so long as I exist! (47-48)

verses.text:
सोऽहं शत्रुविनाशाय तव निर्यातुमुद्यतः।
मुञ्च रामाद् भयं घोरं निहनिष्यामि संयुगे॥ ४९॥
राघवं लक्ष्मणं चैव सुग्रीवं च महाबलम्।
हनूमन्तं च रक्षोघ्नं येन लङ्का प्रदीपिता॥ ५०॥
verses.m: “I, for my part, am prepared to sally forth for the extermination of your enemies. Give up the violent fear proceeding from Rāma. I shall without doubt make short work on the battlefield of Rāma (a scion of Raghu) as well as of Lakṣmaṇa as also of Sugrīva, who is endowed with extraordinary might, and shall also dispose of Hanumān, the destroyer of ogres, by whom Laṅkā was set on fire. (49-50)

verses.text:
हरींश्च भक्षयिष्यामि संयुगे समुपस्थिते।
असाधारणमिच्छामि तव दातुं महद् यशः॥ ५१॥
verses.m: “Nay, I shall devour the monkeys when a struggle is quite at hand. I wish to confer uncommon and great glory on you. (51)

verses.text:
यदि चेन्द्राद् भयं राजन् यदि चापि स्वयंभुवः।
ततोऽहं नाशयिष्यामि नैशं तम इवांशुमान्॥ ५२॥
verses.m: “Again, if fear of Indra (the ruler of gods) and even of Brahmā (the self-born creator) haunts you, I shall forthwith drive it away even as the sun disperses the darkness of the night. (52)

verses.text:
अपि देवाः शयिष्यन्ते मयि क्रुद्धे महीतले।
यमं च शमयिष्यामि भक्षयिष्यामि पावकम्॥ ५३॥
verses.m: “Even gods will fall flat on the earth’s surface on my getting enraged. Nay, I shall quell Yama, the god of retribution, and devour the god of fire. (53)

verses.text:
आदित्यं पातयिष्यामि सनक्षत्रं महीतले।
शतक्रतुं वधिष्यामि पास्यामि वरुणालयम्॥ ५४॥
verses.m: “I shall hurl down on the earth the sun alongwith the constellations. Nay, I shall kill Indra (who is presupposed to have performed a hundred horse-sacrifices in his previous birth or births as a condition precedent for his attaining Indrahood) and drink up the ocean (the abode of Varuṇa, the god of water). (54)

verses.text:
पर्वतांश्चूर्णयिष्यामि दारयिष्यामि मेदिनीम्।
दीर्घकालं प्रसुप्तस्य कुम्भकर्णस्य विक्रमम्॥ ५५॥
अद्य पश्यन्तु भूतानि भक्ष्यमाणानि सर्वशः।
न त्विदं त्रिदिवं सर्वमाहारो मम पूर्यते॥ ५६॥
verses.m: “I shall pulverize mountains and rend the earth. Let the created beings who are going to be devoured by me on all sides witness the prowess of Kumbhakarṇa (myself), who remained fast asleep for long, i.e., till now. If all the three worlds, viz., heaven, earth and the intermediate region, are offered to me as food, my stomach will not be filled thereby. (55-56)

verses.text:
वधेन ते दाशरथेः सुखावहं
सुखं समाहर्तुमहं व्रजामि।
निहत्य रामं सह लक्ष्मणेन
खादामि सर्वान् हरियूथमुख्यान्॥ ५७॥
verses.m: “Through the destruction of Rāma (son of Daśaratha), I proceed to bring to you happiness which may prove conducive to more and more happiness in future. After killing Rāma alongwith Lakṣmaṇa, I shall devour all the leaders of monkey troops.(57)

verses.text:
रमस्व राजन् पिब चाद्य वारुणीं
कुरुष्व कृत्यानि विनीय दुःखम्।
मयाद्य रामे गमिते यमक्षयं
चिराय सीता वशगा भविष्यति॥ ५८॥
verses.m: “Revel, O king, and drink wine today. Nay, banishing agony, discharge your duties. When Rāma is dispatched by me to the abode of Yama, the god of retribution, today, Sītā will submit to your will for long.” (58)

verses.text:
तदुक्तमतिकायस्य बलिनो बाहुशालिनः।
कुम्भकर्णस्य वचनं श्रुत्वोवाच महोदरः॥ १॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid braggadocio of the colossal and mighty Kumbhakarṇa, who was adorned with brawny arms, Mahodara spoke as follows: (1)

verses.text:
कुम्भकर्ण कुले जातो धृष्टः प्राकृतदर्शनः।
अवलिप्तो न शक्नोषि कृत्यं सर्वत्र वेदितुम्॥ २॥
verses.m: “Though born in a noble race, you are insolent and arrogant and possessed of an unsophisticated intellect and as such unable to know what should be done under all circumstances. (2)

verses.text:
नहि राजा न जानीते कुम्भकर्ण नयानयौ।
त्वं तु कैशोरकाद् धृष्टः केवलं वक्तुमिच्छसि॥ ३॥
verses.m: “It is not that His Majesty does not know what is politic and what is impolitic, O Kumbhakarṇa! You are, however, insolent from your very juvenescence and only feel inclined to speak. (3)

verses.text:
स्थानं वृद्धिं च हानिं च देशकालविधानवित्।
आत्मनश्च परेषां च बुध्यते राक्षसर्षभः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Rāvaṇa, a bull among the ogres, is conversant with the laws of time and place and knows his own progress, decline and status quo, as well as of the enemies. (4)

verses.text:
यत् त्वशक्यं बलवता वक्तुं प्राकृतबुद्धिना।
अनुपासितवृद्धेन कः कुर्यात् तादृशं बुधः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “What wise man would, however, attempt to undertake that which cannot be achieved by one who is possessed of an unsophisticated intellect and has not waited upon his elders. (5)

verses.text:
यांस्तु धर्मार्थकामांस्त्वं ब्रवीषि पृथगाश्रयान्।
अवबोद्धुं स्वभावेन नहि लक्षणमस्ति तान्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “The capacity to know virtue, worldly gain and sensuous pleasure in their true character does not exist in you in that you speak of them as incompatible (lit., existing in different individuals). (6)

verses.text:
कर्म चैव हि सर्वेषां कारणानां प्रयोजनम्।
श्रेयः पापीयसां चात्र फलं भवति कर्मणाम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Again, action is the root of all the three means to happiness, viz., virtue, worldly gain and sensuous pleasure; moreover, the fruit of actions, both noble and exceedingly sinful, in this world accrues to the same agent. (7)

verses.text:
निःश्रेयसफलावेव धर्मार्थावितरावपि।
अधर्मानर्थयोः प्राप्तं फलं च प्रत्यवायिकम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Virtue in the shape of muttering of prayers, meditation etc., which have no dependence on wealth, and the performance of sacrifices and practice of charity etc., for the accomplishment of which wealth is indispensable, though conducive to final beatitude alone, if pursued in a disinterested spirit, also lead, if pursued with some interested motive, to goals other than final beatitude such as heavenly bliss and worldly prosperity. From the omission of an obligatory virtue follow unrighteousness and evil, and alongwith them, the bitter fruit of the offence of omission. (8)

verses.text:
ऐहलौकिकपारक्यं कर्म पुंभिर्निषेव्यते।
कर्माण्यपि तु कल्याणि लभते काममास्थितः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “The fruit of past actions, good or bad, is reaped by living beings in this as well as in the other world. He, however, who remains sedulously devoted to actions with a view to attaining sensuous pleasure perceptibly enjoys blessings even in this life and not hereafter as in the case of virtue and material gain. (9)

verses.text:
तत्र क्लृप्तमिदं राज्ञा हृदि कार्यं मतं च नः।
शत्रौ हि साहसं यत् तत् किमिवात्रापनीयते॥ १०॥
verses.m: “In such circumstances the pursuit of sensuous pleasure (in the form of retaining Sītā and trying to win her over), which has been cherished by the king in his heart and is also approved of by us, must be indulged in by him*. What wrong is there in accomplishing that which is surely to be a daring act against the enemy? (10)

verses.text:
एकस्यैवाभियाने तु हेतुर्यः प्राहृतस्त्वया।
तत्राप्यनुपपन्नं ते वक्ष्यामि यदसाधु च॥ ११॥
verses.m: “As for the reason, viz., your extraordinary might, which you have adduced for marching all alone for an encounter, I shall presently point out to you what is ill-considered and wrong about it. (11)

verses.text:
येन पूर्वं जनस्थाने बहवोऽतिबला हताः।
राक्षसा राघवं तं त्वं कथमेको जयिष्यसि॥ १२॥
verses.m: “How will you be able to conquer single-handed that scion of Raghu by whom numerous ogres endowed with exceeding might were made short work of in Janasthāna in the past? (12)

verses.text:
ये पूर्वं निर्जितास्तेन जनस्थाने महौजसः।
राक्षसांस्तान् पुरे सर्वान् भीतानद्य न पश्यसि॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Don’t you see all those ogres, endowed with extraordinary strength, who were put to flight by him in the past in Janasthāna, living in fear in the city even today? (13)

verses.text:
तं सिंहमिव संक्रुद्धं रामं दशरथात्मजम्।
सर्पं सुप्तमहो बुद्ध्वा प्रबोधयितुमिच्छसि॥ १४॥
verses.m: “You desire to meet in combat Rāma, an offspring of Daśaratha, who is like an enraged lion, and knowingly seek to awaken a serpent which is asleep. (14)

verses.text:
ज्वलन्तं तेजसा नित्यं क्रोधेन च दुरासदम्।
कस्तं मृत्युमिवासह्यमासादयितुमर्हति॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Who would dare to encounter Rāma, who is ever burning with spirit, and is difficult to approach in fury and unbearable as Death? (15)

verses.text:
संशयस्थमिदं सर्वं शत्रोः प्रतिसमासने।
एकस्य गमनं तात नहि मे रोचते भृशम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “This entire army of ogres would be involved in danger on standing face to face with the aforesaid enemy. In such circumstances, O beloved one, your going alone to meet Rāma does not find favour with me at all. (16)

verses.text:
हीनार्थस्तु समृद्धार्थं को रिपुं प्राकृतं यथा।
निश्चितं जीवितत्यागे वशमानेतुमिच्छति॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Bereft of resources, who would feel inclined to reduce to submission an enemy, who is rich in resources and determined to lay down his life, as a common enemy? (17)

verses.text:
यस्य नास्ति मनुष्येषु सदृशो राक्षसोत्तम।
कथमाशंससे योद्धुं तुल्येनेन्द्रविवस्वतोः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “How do you wish to enter into combat with him, who is an equal of Indra and the sun-god, and whose compeer there is none among human beings, O prince of ogres?” (18)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा तु संरब्धं कुम्भकर्णं महोदरः।
उवाच रक्षसां मध्ये रावणं लोकरावणम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: Having spoken thus to the enraged Kumbhakarṇa, Mahodara for his part submitted as follows in the midst of other ogres to Rāvaṇa, who made people cry by his tyranny: (19)

verses.text:
लब्ध्वा पुरस्ताद् वैदेहीं किमर्थं त्वं विलम्बसे।
यदीच्छसि तदा सीता वशगा ते भविष्यति॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Having laid your hands already on Sītā (a princess of the Videha territory), why do you procrastinate? Sītā will submit to your will the moment you would have her do so. (20)

verses.text:
दृष्टः कश्चिदुपायो मे सीतोपस्थानकारकः।
रुचितश्चेत् स्वया बुद्ध्या राक्षसेन्द्र ततः शृणु॥ २१॥
verses.m: “A means of bringing her round has been discovered by me. Listen to it, O lord of ogres ! Ponder it with your intellect and act according to it if it is found acceptable. (21)

verses.text:
अहं द्विजिह्वः संह्रादी कुम्भकर्णो वितर्दनः।
पञ्च रामवधायैते निर्यान्तीत्यवघोषय॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Have it proclaimed by beat of drum that Dwijihwa, Saṁhrādī, Kumbhakarṇa, Vitardana and myself—these five are going forth to kill Rāma. (22)

verses.text:
ततो गत्वा वयं युद्धं दास्यामस्तस्य यत्नतः।
जेष्यामो यदि ते शत्रून् नोपायैः कार्यमस्ति नः॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Sallying forth, we shall then give battle to him with zeal. If we are able to conquer your enemies, no purpose of ours will be served by other expedients. (23)

verses.text:
अथ जीवति नः शत्रुर्वयं च कृतसंयुगाः।
ततः समभिपत्स्यामो मनसा यत् समीक्षितम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “If, however, our enemy survives the encounter and we too survive after we have fought a battle with him, then we shall fall back upon the plan which has been revolved by us in the mind. (24)

verses.text:
वयं युद्धादिहैष्यामो रुधिरेण समुक्षिताः।
विदार्य स्वतनुं बाणै रामनामाङ्कितैः शरैः॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Bathed in blood on having our body cruelly torn with deadly darts marked with the name of Rāma (engraved on them), we shall return from the battlefield to this place. (25)

verses.text:
भक्षितो राघवोऽस्माभिर्लक्ष्मणश्चेति वादिनः।
ततः पादौ ग्रहीष्यामस्त्वं नः कामं प्रपूरय॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Then we shall clasp your feet saying, ‘Rāma (a scion of Raghu) as well as Lakṣmaṇa have been devoured by us.’ Pray, fully grant you our desire. (26)

verses.text:
ततोऽवघोषय पुरे गजस्कन्धेन पार्थिव।
हतो रामः सह भ्रात्रा ससैन्य इति सर्वतः॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Then have it proclaimed by beat of drum on all sides on the back of an elephant O ruler of the earth, that Rāma has been got rid of alongwith Lakṣmaṇa and his army. (27)

verses.text:
प्रीतो नाम ततो भूत्वा भृत्यानां त्वमरिंदम।
भोगांश्च परिवारांश्च कामान् वसु च दापय॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Getting pleased, as it were, O tamer of your enemies, cause you to be bestowed on your servants objects of enjoyment and other desired objects as well as slaves and gold. (28)

verses.text:
ततो माल्यानि वासांसि वीराणामनुलेपनम्।
पेयं च बहु योधेभ्यः स्वयं च मुदितः पिब॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Then confer garlands, garments, cosmetics and drink on champions and abundant gifts to other warriors and also drink yourself joyfully. (29)

verses.text:
ततोऽस्मिन् बहुलीभूते कौलीने सर्वतो गते।
भक्षितः ससुहृद् रामो राक्षसैरिति विश्रुते॥ ३०॥
प्रविश्याश्वास्य चापि त्वं सीतां रहसि सान्त्वयन्।
धनधान्यैश्च कामैश्च रत्नैश्चैनां प्रलोभय॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Approaching Sītā in private and also restoring her to confidence, nay, conciliating her, when the thick rumour that Rāma, with his brother and accomplices has been devoured by the ogres reaches everywhere and is clearly heard even by Sītā, tempt her with offers of gold and grain as also luxuries and precious stones. (30-31)

verses.text:
अनयोपधया राजन् भूयः शोकानुबन्धया।
अकामा त्वद्वशं सीता नष्टनाथा गमिष्यति॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Imposed upon by means of this trick, which will further intensify her grief, Sītā, though lacking in love for you, will submit to your will because of her having lost her protector, O king! (32)

verses.text:
रमणीयं हि भर्तारं विनष्टमधिगम्य सा।
नैराश्यात् स्त्रीलघुत्वाच्च त्वद्वशं प्रतिपत्स्यते॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “Actually believing her lovely husband to have perished, she will in despair accept dependence on you due to womanly frailty. (33)

verses.text:
सा पुरा सुखसंवृद्धा सुखार्हा दुःखकर्शिता।
त्वय्यधीनं सुखं ज्ञात्वा सर्वथैव गमिष्यति॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “Realizing her happiness as depending on you alone, Sītā, who has been brought up in (the lap of) prosperity in the past, is deserving of felicity and is already tormented with agony, will completely submit to your will. (34)

verses.text:
एतत् सुनीतं मम दर्शनेन
रामं हि दृष्ट्वैव भवेदनर्थः।
इहैव ते सेत्स्यति मोत्सुको भू-
र्महानयुद्धेन सुखस्य लाभः॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “This will be the best course to my mind. Disaster in the shape of death is sure to come to you as soon as you behold Rāma. Therefore, don’t be eager for an encounter. Great enjoyment of bliss will accrue to you in Laṅkā itself without a struggle. (35)

verses.text:
अनष्टसैन्यो ह्यनवाप्तसंशयो
रिपुं त्वयुद्धेन जयञ्जनाधिपः।
यशश्च पुण्यं च महान्महीपते
श्रियं च कीर्तिं च चिरं समश्नुते॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “Conquering his enemies without a contest, a mighty ruler of the earth for his part fully enjoys for long renown and religious merit too, as also prosperity and placidity, without meeting with danger, O overlord of the people, his army too remaining intact.” (36)

verses.text:
स तथोक्तस्तु निर्भर्त्स्य कुम्भकर्णो महोदरम्।
अब्रवीद् राक्षसश्रेष्ठं भ्रातरं रावणं ततः॥ १॥
verses.m: Upbraiding Mahodara, when spoken to as aforesaid, Kumbhakarṇa for his part then submitted as follows to his elder brother, Rāvaṇa, the foremost of ogres: (1)

verses.text:
सोऽहं तव भयं घोरं वधात् तस्य दुरात्मनः।
रामस्याद्य प्रमार्जामि निर्वैरो हि सुखी भव॥ २॥
verses.m: “For what I am, I shall without doubt dispel today your formidable fear by killing that evil-minded fellow, Rāma. Rid of animosity, be happy. (2)

verses.text:
गर्जन्ति न वृथा शूरा निर्जला इव तोयदाः।
पश्य सम्पद्यमानं तु गर्जितं युधि कर्मणा॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Heroes do not thunder in vain like clouds bereft of water. Note for your part the roar which is going to be emitted by me on the battlefield through action. (3)

verses.text:
न मर्षयन्ति चात्मानं सम्भावयितुमात्मना।
अदर्शयित्वा शूरास्तु कर्म कुर्वन्ति दुष्करम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Warriors do not seek to glorify themselves with their own lips. On the other hand, they accomplish deeds which are hard to accomplish, without displaying them. (4)

verses.text:
विक्लवानां ह्यबुद्धीनां राज्ञां पण्डितमानिनाम्।
रोचते त्वद्वचो नित्यं कथ्यमानं महोदर॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Your advice, even while it is being tendered, would undoubtedly appeal at all times to kings who are cowardly and devoid of intellect and account themselves wise, O Mahodara! (5)

verses.text:
युद्धे कापुरुषैर्नित्यं भवद्भिः प्रियवादिभिः।
राजानमनुगच्छद्भिः सर्वं कृत्यं विनाशितम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “All undertakings have always been marred by you people, who are cowards in combat, utter pleasing words and say ditto to the king during deliberations. (6)

verses.text:
राजशेषा कृता लङ्का क्षीणः कोशो बलं हतम्।
राजानमिममासाद्य सुहृच्चिह्नममित्रकम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “The king alone is left in Laṅkā that has been divested of its population, its exchequer depleted, and army destroyed. Nay, having found access to this king, enemies, masquerading as friends, have gathered round him. (7)

verses.text:
एष निर्याम्यहं युद्धमुद्यतः शत्रुनिर्जये।
दुर्नयं भवतामद्य समीकर्तुं महाहवे॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Bent on conquering the enemy, I hereby sally forth to the battlefield in order to redeem in a major conflict today the disastrous policy initiated by you all.” (8)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तवतो वाक्यं कुम्भकर्णस्य धीमतः।
प्रत्युवाच ततो वाक्यं प्रहसन् राक्षसाधिपः॥ ९॥
verses.m: Laughing heartily, Rāvaṇa, the suzerain lord of ogres, then replied as follows to the submission of the sagacious Kumbhakarṇa, who had just spoken as aforesaid : (9)

verses.text:
महोदरोऽयं रामात् तु परित्रस्तो न संशयः।
न हि रोचयते तात युद्धं युद्धविशारद॥ १०॥
verses.m: “This Mahodara for his part is greatly afraid of Rāma: there is no doubt about it. Surely he does not relish war, O dear brother, well-versed in the art of warfare ! (10)

verses.text:
कश्चिन्मे त्वत्समो नास्ति सौहृदेन बलेन च।
गच्छ शत्रुवधाय त्वं कुम्भकर्ण जयाय च॥ ११॥
verses.m: “There is none equal to you in affection and might in my eyes. As such march you to the battlefield for the destruction of the enemy and attaining victory, O Kumbhakarṇa! (11)

verses.text:
शयानः शत्रुनाशार्थं भवान् सम्बोधितो मया।
अयं हि कालः सुमहान् राक्षसनामरिंदम॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Asleep as you were, you have been duly awakened by me for the extermination of the enemies; for, the present is an exceedingly momentous period for the ogres, O tamer of enemies! (12)

verses.text:
संगच्छ शूलमादाय पाशहस्त इवान्तकः।
वानरान् राजपुत्रौ च भक्षयादित्यतेजसौ॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Therefore, taking a pike, duly proceed to the battlefield as Death would, with a noose in hand. Nay, devour the monkeys as well as the two princes, bright as the sun. (13)

verses.text:
समालोक्य तु ते रूपं विद्रविष्यन्ति वानराः।
रामलक्ष्मणयोश्चापि हृदये प्रस्फुटिष्यतः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Vividly perceiving your very form, the monkeys will flee away, and the hearts of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa will break asunder.” (14)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा महातेजाः कुम्भकर्णं महाबलम्।
पुनर्जातमिवात्मानं मेने राक्षसपुङ्गवः॥ १५॥
verses.m: Having spoken thus to Kumbhakarṇa, who was endowed with extraordinary might, Rāvaṇa (a bull among ogres), who was possessed of great energy, thought himself regenerated. (15)

verses.text:
कुम्भकर्णबलाभिज्ञो जानंस्तस्य पराक्रमम्।
बभूव मुदितो राजा शशाङ्क इव निर्मलः॥ १६॥
verses.m: Fully aware of Kumbhakarṇa’s might and knowing, as he did, his prowess, the king felt delighted and shone like the cloudless moon. (16)

verses.text:
इत्येवमुक्तः संहृष्टो निर्जगाम महाबलः।
राज्ञस्तु वचनं श्रुत्वा योद्धुमुद्युक्तवांस्तदा॥ १७॥
verses.m: Spoken to in these words, Kumbhakarṇa, who was endowed with extraordinary might, sallied forth, highly rejoiced. Nay, hearing the king’s speech at that time, he for his part prepared to fight. (17)

verses.text:
आददे निशितं शूलं वेगाच्छत्रुनिबर्हणः।
सर्वं कालायसं दीप्तं तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: The ogre, who was capable of destroying his enemies, vigorously seized a whetted and flaming dart, which was all made of iron and was embellished with refined gold. (18)

verses.text:
इन्द्राशनिसमप्रख्यं वज्रप्रतिमगौरवम्।
देवदानवगन्धर्वयक्षपन्नगसूदनम् ॥ १९॥
verses.m: It shone like Indra’s thunderbolt and was equally heavy and was capable of destroying gods, Dānavas, Gandharvas (celestial musicians), Yakṣas (a class of demi-gods) and Nāgas (semi-divine beings credited with a human face and the tail of a serpent). (19)

verses.text:
रक्तमाल्यमहादामं स्वतश्चोद्गतपावकम्।
आदाय विपुलं शूलं शत्रुशोणितरञ्जितम्॥ २०॥
कुम्भकर्णो महातेजा रावणं वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
गमिष्याम्यहमेकाकी तिष्ठत्विह बलं मम॥ २१॥
verses.m: It was wreathed in garlands of crimson flowers and emitted flames by itself. Taking the enormous dart which was stained with the gore of his enemies, Kumbhakarṇa, who was endowed with extraordinary energy submitted as follows to Rāvaṇa: “I will proceed alone. Let my army remain here. (20-21)

verses.text:
अद्य तान् क्षुधितः क्रुद्धो भक्षयिष्यामि वानरान्।
कुम्भकर्णवचः श्रुत्वा रावणो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Feeling hungry and enraged, I shall devour the monkeys today.” Hearing the submission of Kumbhakarṇa, Rāvaṇa replied as follows: (22)

verses.text:
सैन्यैः परिवृतो गच्छ शूलमुद्गरपाणिभिः।
वानरा हि महात्मानः शूराः सुव्यवसायिनः॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Go out accompanied by troops carrying pikes and mallets in their hands; for the monkeys are gigantic, valiant and full of great perseverance. (23)

verses.text:
एकाकिनं प्रमत्तं वा नयेयुर्दशनैः क्षयम्।
तस्मात् परमदुर्धर्षः सैन्यैः परिवृतो व्रज।
रक्षसामहितं सर्वं शत्रुपक्षं निषूदय॥ २४॥
verses.m: “They are sure to destroy with their teeth anyone who is alone or off one’s guard. Therefore, go out surrounded by troops. Rendered exceedingly difficult to assail you in this way, exterminate the entire army of the enemy, which is so pernicious to the ogres.” (24)

verses.text:
अथासनात् समुत्पत्य स्रजं मणिकृतान्तराम्।
आबबन्ध महातेजाः कुम्भकर्णस्य रावणः॥ २५॥
verses.m: Springing up from his throne, Rāvaṇa, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, now placed round the neck of Kumbhakarṇa a gold necklace interspersed with gems. (25)

verses.text:
अङ्गदान्यङ्गुलीवेष्टान् वराण्याभरणानि च।
हारं च शशिसंकाशमाबबन्ध महात्मनः॥ २६॥
verses.m: He also placed on the person of the colossus armlets, rings, other excellent jewels as well as a pearl necklace sparkling as the moon. (26)

verses.text:
दिव्यानि च सुगन्धीनि माल्यदामानि रावणः।
गात्रेषु सज्जयामास श्रोत्रयोश्चास्य कुण्डले॥ २७॥
verses.m: Rāvaṇa further placed on his different limbs wonderful fragrant garlands and suspended earrings in his ears. (27)

verses.text:
काञ्चनाङ्गदकेयूरनिष्काभरणभूषितः।
कुम्भकर्णो बृहत्कर्णः सुहुतोऽग्निरिवाबभौ॥ २८॥
verses.m: Thus adorned with gold armlets, bracelets and Niṣkas (an ornament for the neck), Kumbhakarṇa, who was distinguished by large ears, shone like fire, well-fed with oblations. (28)

verses.text:
श्रोणीसूत्रेण महता मेचकेन व्यराजत।
अमृतोत्पादने नद्धो भुजङ्गेनेव मन्दरः॥ २९॥
verses.m: Decked with an enormous dark-blue girdle, he shone brightly like Mount Mandara encircled by Vāsuki, the king of serpents, at the time of churning nectar out of the milk ocean. (29)

verses.text:
स काञ्चनं भारसहं निवातं
विद्युत्प्रभं दीप्तमिवात्मभासा।
आबध्यमानः कवचं रराज
संध्याभ्रसंवीत इवाद्रिराजः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Donning an impenetrable golden coat-of-mail capable of resisting heavy blows, nay, brilliant as lightning and flaming with its native effulgence, he shone like the western mountain, the king of mountains, encircled by evening clouds. (30)

verses.text:
सर्वाभरणसर्वाङ्गः शूलपाणिः स राक्षसः।
त्रिविक्रमकृतोत्साहो नारायण इवाबभौ॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Decked all over his limbs with all kinds of jewels and pike in hand, that ogre trod like Lord Nārāyaṇa, (in His all-embracing form) determined to take the three long strides which were intended to cover the entire universe. (31)

verses.text:
भ्रातरं सम्परिष्वज्य कृत्वा चापि प्रदक्षिणम्।
प्रणम्य शिरसा तस्मै प्रतस्थे स महाबलः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Tightly embracing his elder brother and also going round him as a token of respect clockwise and respectfully bowing down to him, Kumbhakarṇa, who was endowed with extraordinary might, sallied forth. (32)

verses.text:
तमाशीर्भिः प्रशस्ताभिः प्रेषयामास रावणः।
शङ्खदुन्दुभिनिर्घोषैः सैन्यैश्चापि वरायुधैः॥ ३३॥
verses.m: Rāvaṇa bid him proceed with excellent benedictions to the sound of conches and drums and also alongwith troops armed with the best of weapons. (33)

verses.text:
तं गजैश्च तुरंगैश्च स्यन्दनैश्चाम्बुदस्वनैः।
अनुजग्मुर्महात्मानो रथिनो रथिनां वरम्॥ ३४॥
verses.m: Gigantic car-warriors followed that prince of car-warriors on the back of elephants and horses as also in chariots, emitting a thunder-like sound. (34)

verses.text:
सर्पैरुष्ट्रैः खरैश्चैव सिंहद्विपमृगद्विजैः।
अनुजग्मुश्च तं घोरं कुम्भकर्णं महाबलम्॥ ३५॥
verses.m: Ogres also accompanied the celebrated and redoubtable Kumbhakarṇa, who was endowed with extraordinary might, on serpents, camels and donkeys too as well as on lions, elephants, antelopes and birds. (35)

verses.text:
स पुष्पवर्षैरवकीर्यमाणो
धृतातपत्रः शितशूलपाणिः।
मदोत्कटः शोणितगन्धमत्तो
विनिर्ययौ दानवदेवशत्रुः॥ ३६॥
verses.m: Being covered with showers of blossoms, a parasol held over his head, nay, bearing a pointed pike in his hand, excited by drink and maddened by the smell of blood, that enemy of demons and gods alike sallied forth in state. (36)

verses.text:
पदातयश्च बहवो महानादा महाबलाः।
अन्वयू राक्षसा भीमा भीमाक्षाः शस्त्रपाणयः॥ ३७॥
रक्ताक्षाः सुबहुव्यामा नीलाञ्जनचयोपमाः।
शूलानुद्यम्य खड्गांश्च निशितांश्च परश्वधान्॥ ३८॥
भिन्दिपालांश्च परिघान् गदाश्च मुसलानि च।
तालस्कन्धांश्च विपुलान् क्षेपणीयान् दुरासदान्॥ ३९॥
verses.m: Lifting up pikes and swords as well as whetted axes as also Bhindipālas (small javelins thrown by the hand), iron clubs and maces and mallets, enormous trunks of palmyra trees and slings which were difficult to meet, and raising a great uproar, numerous formidable ogres with hideous coppery eyes, endowed with extraordinary might, measuring very many Vyāmas* in height, and resembling a mass of collyrium in hue, also followed him on foot, weapon in hand. (37—39)

verses.text:
अथान्यद्वपुरादाय दारुणं घोरदर्शनम्।
निष्पपात महातेजाः कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: Now assuming another formidable form, terrible to look at, Kumbhakarṇa, who was endowed with extraordinary energy and possessed of great might, rushed forth. (40)

verses.text:
धनुःशतपरीणाहः स षट्शतसमुच्छ्रितः।
रौद्रः शकटचक्राक्षो महापर्वतसंनिभः॥ ४१॥
संनिपत्य च रक्षांसि दग्धशैलोपमो महान्।
कुम्भकर्णो महावक्त्रः प्रहसन्निदमब्रवीत्॥ ४२॥
verses.m: Nay, deploying the ogres in battle-array, the mighty Kumbhakarṇa, who was now a hundred bows in breadth and six hundred in height, was fierce with eyes resembling the wheels of a chariot and presented the appearance of a huge mountain (in size), was endowed with an enormous mouth and looked like a charred mountain in hue, spoke as follows, laughing heartily as he spoke: (41-42)

verses.text:
अद्य वानरमुख्यानां तानि यूथानि भागशः।
निर्दहिष्यामि संक्रुद्धः पतङ्गानिव पावकः॥ ४३॥
verses.m: “Filled with fury, I shall severally consume today, even as a flame would consume moths, the battalions of the foremost of monkeys. (43)

verses.text:
नापराध्यन्ति मे कामं वानरा वनचारिणः।
जातिरस्मद्विधानां सा पुरोद्यानविभूषणम्॥ ४४॥
verses.m: “The monkeys, who are wont to roam about in the woods, have never given me offence of their own will. The species, in fact, serve as an ornament of the urban gardens of people like us. (44)

verses.text:
पुररोधस्य मूलं तु राघवः सहलक्ष्मणः।
हते तस्मिन् हतं सर्वं तं वधिष्यामि संयुगे॥ ४५॥
verses.m: “The cause of the city being besieged, however, is Rāma (a scion of Raghu) accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa? I shall, therefore, first of all get rid of him in combat. He being disposed of, all will be destroyed.” (45)

verses.text:
एवं तस्य ब्रुवाणस्य कुम्भकर्णस्य राक्षसाः।
नादं चक्रुर्महाघोरं कम्पयन्त इवार्णवम्॥ ४६॥
verses.m: While the bellicose Kumbhakarṇa was speaking in this strain, the ogres, who accompanied him, raised an exceedingly terrible uproar, agitating the sea, as it were. (46)

verses.text:
तस्य निष्पततस्तूर्णं कुम्भकर्णस्य धीमतः।
बभूवुर्घोररूपाणि निमित्तानि समन्ततः॥ ४७॥
verses.m: Even as the said Kumbhakarṇa, who was full of intelligence, rushed forth with impetuosity, portents of fearful aspect appeared on all sides. (47)

verses.text:
उल्काशनियुता मेघा बभूवुर्गर्दभारुणाः।
ससागरवना चैव वसुधा समकम्पत॥ ४८॥
verses.m: Clouds ashy in colour like donkeys appeared alongwith shooting stars and strokes of lightning. And the earth too, with its seas and forests, violently shook. (48)

verses.text:
घोररूपाः शिवा नेदुः सज्वालकवलैर्मुखैः।
मण्डलान्यपसव्यानि बबन्धुश्च विहंगमाः॥ ४९॥
verses.m: She-jackals of hideous aspect howled with flaming morsels in their mouths. And birds flew in circle round from right to left. (49)

verses.text:
निष्पपात च गृध्रोऽस्य शूले वै पथि गच्छतः।
प्रास्फुरन्नयनं चास्य सव्यो बाहुरकम्पत॥ ५०॥
verses.m: A vulture actually alighted on his pike as he was marching along the road. His left eye twitched and his left arm throbbed. (50)

verses.text:
निष्पपात तदा चोल्का ज्वलन्ती भीमनिःस्वना।
आदित्यो निष्प्रभश्चासीन्न वाति च सुखोऽनिलः॥ ५१॥
verses.m: Nay, a flaming meteor then fell with a terrible crash. The sun too lost its brilliance and no delightful wind blew. (51)

verses.text:
अचिन्तयन् महोत्पातानुदितान् रोमहर्षणान्।
निर्ययौ कुम्भकर्णस्तु कृतान्तबलचोदितः॥ ५२॥
verses.m: Not minding in the least the mighty portents, which appeared and which made one’s hair stand on end, Kumbhakarṇa, however, sallied forth, propelled as he was by the force of destiny. (52)

verses.text:
स लङ्घयित्वा प्राकारं पद्भ्यां पर्वतसंनिभः।
ददर्शाभ्रघनप्रख्यं वानरानीकमद्भुतम्॥ ५३॥
verses.m: Having crossed the defensive wall with his feet alone, the ogre, who closely resembled a mountain in height, surveyed the wonderful army of the monkeys, which looked like a mass of clouds. (53)

verses.text:
ते दृष्ट्वा राक्षसश्रेष्ठं वानराः पर्वतोपमम्।
वायुनुन्ना इव घना ययुः सर्वा दिशस्तदा॥ ५४॥
verses.m: Beholding the foremost of ogres, who resembled a mountain, the monkeys immediately dispersed in all directions even like clouds propelled by wind. (54)

verses.text:
तद् वानरानीकमतिप्रचण्डं
दिशो द्रवद्भिन्नमिवाभ्रजालम्।
स कुम्भकर्णः समवेक्ष्य हर्षा-
न्ननाद भूयो घनवद्घनाभः॥ ५५॥
verses.m: Perceiving that most powerful army of monkeys scattered to the four quarters, like a mass of clouds, melting away, the notorious Kumbhakarṇa who also looked like a cloud, repeatedly emitted a roar like thunder. (55)

verses.text:
ते तस्य घोरं निनदं निशम्य
यथा निनादं दिवि वारिदस्य।
पेतुर्धरण्यां बहवः प्लवङ्गा
निकृत्तमूला इव शालवृक्षाः॥ ५६॥
verses.m: Hearing his terrible roar, which resembled the rumbling of a cloud in the sky, numerous monkeys fell to the ground like sal trees whose roots have been severed. (56)

verses.text:
विपुलपरिघवान् स कुम्भकर्णो
रिपुनिधनाय विनिःसृतो महात्मा।
कपिगणभयमाददत् सुभीमं
प्रभुरिव किंकरदण्डवान् युगान्ते॥ ५७॥
verses.m: Armed with a huge iron club in addition to a pike, and causing tremendous fear to the simian ranks, that colossal Kumbhakarṇa rushed forth for the destruction of the enemy, even like Lord Kālarudra (the god of destruction appearing in a dark form at the time of universal dissolution) armed with his rod of punishment waiting upon him in a living form like a servant, at the end of the world cycle. (57)

verses.text:
स लङ्घयित्वा प्राकारं गिरिकूटोपमो महान्।
निर्ययौ नगरात् तूर्णं कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः॥ १॥
ननाद च महानादं समुद्रमभिनादयन्।
विजयन्निव निर्घातान् विधमन्निव पर्वतान्॥ २॥
verses.m: Stepping across the defensive wall, the gigantic Kumbhakarṇa, who resembled the peak of a mountain and was endowed with extraordinary might, rapidly issued out of the city and emitted a tremendous roar, making the sea reverberate, nay, causing mountains to quake and drowning thunder-claps, as it were. (1-2)

verses.text:
तमवध्यं मघवता यमेन वरुणेन वा।
प्रेक्ष्य भीमाक्षमायान्तं वानरा विप्रदुद्रुवुः॥ ३॥
verses.m: Perceiving that ogre of fierce eyes—who could not be killed by Indra (the ruler of gods), Yama (the god of retribution) or even by Varuṇa (the god of water)—approaching, the monkeys stampeded. (3)

verses.text:
तांस्तु विप्रद्रुतान् दृष्ट्वा राजपुत्रोऽङ्गदोऽब्रवीत्।
नलं नीलं गवाक्षं च कुमुदं च महाबलम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Seeing them put to flight, Prince Aṅgada for his part spoke as follows to Nala, Nīla and Gavākṣa, as also to Kumuda, who was endowed with extraordinary might : (4)

verses.text:
आत्मनस्तानि विस्मृत्य वीर्याण्यभिजनानि च।
क्व गच्छत भयत्रस्ताः प्राकृता हरयो यथा॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Forgetting your well-known exploits and high pedigree, where are you fleeing panic-stricken like ordinary monkeys? (5)

verses.text:
साधु सौम्या निवर्तध्वं किं प्राणान् परिरक्षथ।
नालं युद्धाय वै रक्षो महतीयं विभीषिका॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Enough, O good fellows ! Please return. Why do you defend your lives? Surely this ogre is not capable of contending with us; he is a great bugbear. (6)

verses.text:
महतीमुत्थितामेनां राक्षसानां विभीषिकाम्।
विक्रमाद् विधमिष्यामो निवर्तध्वं प्लवङ्गमाः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “We shall dispel by our prowess this colossal nightmare of the ogres, come into being. Therefore, come back, O monkeys!” (7)

verses.text:
कृच्छ्रेण तु समाश्वस्य संगम्य च ततस्ततः।
वृक्षान् गृहीत्वा हरयः सम्प्रतस्थू रणाजिरे॥ ८॥
verses.m: Regaining confidence somehow and getting together once more from here and there, and seizing hold of trees, the monkeys for their part duly proceeded to the battlefield. (8)

verses.text:
ते निवर्त्य तु संरब्धाः कुम्भकर्णं वनौकसः।
निजघ्नुः परमक्रुद्धाः समदा इव कुञ्जराः॥ ९॥
प्रांशुभिर्गिरिशृङ्गैश्च शिलाभिश्च महाबलाः।
पादपैः पुष्पिताग्रैश्च हन्यमानो न कम्पते॥ १०॥
verses.m: Turning back extremely enraged and determined to fight, the aforesaid monkeys (lit., dwellers in the woods), who were endowed with extraordinary might and looked like elephants in rut, hit him with lofty mountain peaks and rocks as well as with trees whose crests were covered with blossom. Though being hit (as above), Kumbhakarṇa, however, was not shaken. (9-10)

verses.text:
तस्य गात्रेषु पतिता भिद्यन्ते बहवः शिलाः।
पादपाः पुष्पिताग्राश्च भग्नाः पेतुर्महीतले॥ ११॥
verses.m: Fallen on his limbs, numerous rocks got split asunder, and trees with blossomed crests fell shattered on the earth’s surface. (11)

verses.text:
सोऽपि सैन्यानि संक्रुद्धौ वानराणां महौजसाम्।
ममन्थ परमायत्तो वनान्यग्निरिवोत्थितः॥ १२॥
verses.m: Highly enraged and supremely active, Kumbhakarṇa too began to destroy the ranks of the monkeys, although they were endowed with extraordinary vigour, even as a forest fire burst into flames would consume forests. (12)

verses.text:
लोहितार्द्रास्तु बहवः शेरते वानरर्षभाः।
निरस्ताः पतिता भूमौ ताम्रपुष्पा इव द्रुमाः॥ १३॥
verses.m: Fallen like trees with coppery blossom when tossed up by the ogre, numerous bulls among monkeys lay senseless on the ground, bespattered with blood. (13)

verses.text:
लङ्घयन्तः प्रधावन्तो वानरा नावलोकयन्।
केचित् समुद्रे पतिताः केचिद् गगनमास्थिताः॥ १४॥
verses.m: Leaping while running fast, the monkeys did not look ahead or behind or sideways, so that some dropped into the sea while others remained sailing in the air. (14)

verses.text:
वध्यमानास्तु ते वीरा राक्षसेन च लीलया।
सागरं येन ते तीर्णाः पथा तेनैव दुद्रुवुः॥ १५॥
verses.m: Nay, while being struck by the ogre in mere sport, the monkey heroes for their part fled along the same route by which they had crossed the sea. (15)

verses.text:
ते स्थलानि तदा निम्नं विवर्णवदना भयात्।
ऋक्षा वृक्षान् समारूढाः केचित् पर्वतमाश्रिताः॥ १६॥
verses.m: They rushed towards the plains, taking a downward course, their faces rendered pale through fear. The bears climbed up trees, while others sought asylum on mountains. (16)

verses.text:
ममज्जुरर्णवे केचिद् गुहाः केचित् समाश्रिताः।
निपेतुः केचिदपरे केचिन्नैवावतस्थिरे।
केचिद् भूमौ निपतिताः केचित् सुप्ता मृता इव॥ १७॥
verses.m: Some monkeys and bears got drowned in the sea, while others took shelter in caves. Some others fell down, while others could not stand firmly. Some more fell flat on the ground, while others lay stretched as though they were dead. (17)

verses.text:
तान् समीक्ष्याङ्गदो भग्नान् वानरानिदमब्रवीत्।
अवतिष्ठत युध्यामो निवर्तध्वं प्लवंगमाः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Seeing them routed, Aṅgada spoke to them as follows: “Stay. We shall fight. Return, O monkeys ! (18)

verses.text:
भग्नानां वो न पश्यामि परिक्रम्य महीमिमाम्।
स्थानं सर्वे निवर्तध्वं किं प्राणान् परिरक्षथ॥ १९॥
verses.m: “I do not see any refuge for you, routed as you are, even if you range this entire globe. Therefore, come back. Why do you seek to preserve your life? (19)

verses.text:
निरायुधानां क्रमतामसङ्गगतिपौरुषाः।
दारा ह्युपहसिष्यन्ति स वै घातः सुजीवताम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “O monkeys ! whose movement or valour knows no obstruction, your very wives will ridicule you if you run away abandoning your arms. That would be death indeed even for those leading an easy life. (20)

verses.text:
कुलेषु जाताः सर्वेऽस्मिन् विस्तीर्णेषु महत्सु च।
क्व गच्छत भयत्रस्ताः प्राकृता हरयो यथा।
अनार्याः खलु यद्भीतास्त्यक्त्वा वीर्यं प्रधावत॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Even though you are all born in widely spread and noble families, where are you fleeing panic-stricken like ordinary monkeys? You are indeed unworthy in that you are fleeing terrified, casting your prowess to the wind. (21)

verses.text:
विकत्थनानि वो यानि भवद्भिर्जनसंसदि।
तानि वः क्व नु यातानि सोदग्राणि हितानि च॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Where have those braggadocios of yours melted away, in which you indulged in a popular assembly, as also your tall claims of friendly acts done to your master? (22)

verses.text:
भीरोः प्रवादाः श्रूयन्ते यस्तु जीवति धिक्कृतः।
मार्गः सत्पुरुषैर्जुष्टः सेव्यतां त्यज्यतां भयम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Words of reproach are heard with reference to a coward, saying ‘Woe to him who lives even though censured by good men!’ Let the path trodden by the virtuous be followed and let fear be shaken off. (23)

verses.text:
शयामहे वा निहताः पृथिव्यामल्पजीविताः।
प्राप्नुयामो ब्रह्मलोकं दुष्प्रापं च कुयोधिभिः॥ २४॥
verses.m: “If, in the event of our span of life being brief, we lie down killed by the enemy, we shall attain the realm of Brahmā, which is difficult to attain for bad warriors, who are afraid of an encounter. (24)

verses.text:
अवाप्नुयामः कीर्तिं वा निहत्वा शत्रुमाहवे।
निहता वीरलोकस्य भोक्ष्यामो वसु वानराः॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Killing the enemy in combat, we shall acquire glory. If struck down, on the other hand, we shall enjoy the riches of Brahmaloka, the realm attained by heroes, O monkeys! (25)

verses.text:
न कुम्भकर्णः काकुत्स्थं दृष्ट्वा जीवन् गमिष्यति।
दीप्यमानमिवासाद्य पतङ्गो ज्वलनं यथा॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Kumbhakarṇa will never escape alive on coming face to face with Śrī Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha) any more than a moth on approaching a blazing fire. (26)

verses.text:
पलायनेन चोद्दिष्टाः प्राणान् रक्षामहे वयम्।
एकेन बहवो भग्ना यशो नाशं गमिष्यति॥ २७॥
verses.m: “If, though distinguished in war, we preserve our life by fleeing, when routed by one, even though many, our glory will come to an end.” (27)

verses.text:
एवं ब्रुवाणं तं शूरमङ्गदं कनकाङ्गदम्।
द्रवमाणास्ततो वाक्यमूचुः शूरविगर्हितम्॥ २८॥
verses.m: To the said heroic Aṅgada, who was adorned with armlets of gold, even while he was speaking as aforesaid, the monkeys, who were still fleeing, made the following reply, which was condemned by the valiant: (28)

verses.text:
कृतं नः कदनं घोरं कुम्भकर्णेन रक्षसा।
न स्थानकालो गच्छामो दयितं जीवितं हि नः॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Terrible havoc has been made of us by the ogre Kumbhakarṇa. It is not the moment to stay. We are going; for life is dear to us.” (29)

verses.text:
एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं सर्वे ते भेजिरे दिशः।
भीमं भीमाक्षमायान्तं दृष्ट्वा वानरयूथपाः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Having uttered only so many words, all the aforesaid commanders of monkey troops scattered in all directions on seeing the redoubtable ogre with frightful eyes coming. (30)

verses.text:
द्रवमाणास्तु ते वीरा अङ्गदेन बलीमुखाः।
सान्त्वनैश्चानुमानैश्च ततः सर्वे निवर्तिताः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Though still fleeing, all the aforesaid heroic monkeys for their part were then caused to return from where they were by Aṅgada by means of heartening words and arguments too establishing the invincibility of Śrī Rāma. (31)

verses.text:
प्रहर्षमुपनीताश्च वालिपुत्रेण धीमता।
आज्ञाप्रतीक्षास्तस्थुश्च सर्वे वानरयूथपाः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Nay, restored to their high spirits, by the sagacious Aṅgada (son of Vālī), all the (aforesaid) commanders of monkey troops stood awaiting his command. (32)

verses.text:
ऋषभशरभमैन्दधूम्रनीलाः
कुमुदसुषेणगवाक्षरम्भताराः।
द्विविदपनसवायुपुत्रमुख्या-
स्त्वरिततराभिमुखं रणं प्रयाताः॥ ३३॥
verses.m: Ṛṣabha, Śarabha, Mainda, Dhūmra and Nīla, Kumuda, Suṣeṇa, Gavākṣa, Rambha and Tāra headed by Dwivida, Panasa and Hanumān (son of the wind-god), marched ahead to the battle-field with quicker steps. (33)

verses.text:
ते निवृत्ता महाकायाः श्रुत्वाङ्गदवचस्तदा।
नैष्ठिकीं बुद्धिमास्थाय सर्वे संग्रामकाङ् क्षिणः॥ १॥
verses.m: Having arrived at a firm resolution, all those giants returned on hearing the exhortation of Aṅgada, longing for an encounter. (1)

verses.text:
समुदीरितवीर्यास्ते समारोपितविक्रमाः।
पर्यवस्थापिता वाक्यैरङ्गदेन बलीयसा॥ २॥
verses.m: Reminded of their past valour, and restored to confidence by means of his words by the exceedingly mighty Aṅgada, they exhibited their prowess once more.(2)

verses.text:
प्रयाताश्च गता हर्षं मरणे कृतनिश्चयाः।
चक्रुः सुतुमुलं युद्धं वानरास्त्यक्तजीविताः॥ ३॥
verses.m: Having returned to Aṅgada and been restored to their spirits, the monkeys who had staked their life and were resolved to die, carried on a fierce struggle. (3)

verses.text:
अथ वृक्षान् महाकायाः सानूनि सुमहान्ति च।
वानरास्तूर्णमुद्यम्य कुम्भकर्णमभिद्रवन्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Lifting up huge trees and mountain peaks, the colossal monkeys now rushed towards Kumbhakarṇa with all speed. (4)

verses.text:
कुम्भकर्णः सुसंक्रुद्धो गदामुद्यम्य वीर्यवान्।
धर्षयन् स महाकायः समन्ताद् व्यक्षिपद् रिपून्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Raising his mace and displaying his audacity, the valiant and gigantic Kumbhakarṇa, who got extremely enraged, struck down the enemies on all sides. (5)

verses.text:
शतानि सप्त चाष्टौ च सहस्राणि च वानराः।
प्रकीर्णाः शेरते भूमौ कुम्भकर्णेन ताडिताः॥ ६॥
verses.m: Struck by Kumbhakarṇa, eight thousand and seven hundred monkeys lay thrown about on the gound. (6)

verses.text:
षोडशाष्टौ च दश च विंशत्त्रिंशत्तथैव च।
परिक्षिप्य च बाहुभ्यां खादन् स परिधावति।
भक्षयन् भृशसंक्रुद्धो गरुडः पन्नगानिव॥ ७॥
verses.m: Folding in his arms as many as sixteen, eight or ten or twenty and, likewise, even thirty monkeys at a time, extremely infuriated, he ran about devouring them, even as Garuḍa would wheel round consuming serpents. (7)

verses.text:
कृच्छ्रेण च समाश्वस्ताः संगम्य च ततस्ततः।
वृक्षाद्रिहस्ता हरयस्तस्थुः संग्राममूर्धनि॥ ८॥
verses.m: Restored to confidence with great difficulty, nay, rallying from here and there, trees and mountain-tops in hand, the monkeys remained standing in the forefront of the battle. (8)

verses.text:
ततः पर्वतमुत्पाट्य द्विविदः प्लवगर्षभः।
दुद्राव गिरिशृङ्गाभं विलम्ब इव तोयदः॥ ९॥
verses.m: Tearing up a rock, Dwivida, a bull among the monkeys, who looked like a threatening cloud, darted towards Kumbhakarṇa, who resembled a mountain peak. (9)

verses.text:
तं समुत्पाट्य चिक्षेप कुम्भकर्णाय वानरः।
तमप्राप्य महाकायं तस्य सैन्येऽपतत् ततः॥ १०॥
verses.m: Tearing up a rock, the monkey flung it at Kumbhakarṇa. Missing the colossus, the rock, however, fell on his army instead. (10)

verses.text:
ममर्दाश्वान् गजांश्चापि रथांश्चापि गजोत्तमान्।
तानि चान्यानि रक्षांसि एवं चान्यद्गिरेः शिरः॥ ११॥
verses.m: It crushed the horses as well as the elephants as also the chariots and lordly elephants; while another mountain peak crushed other well-known ogres. (11)

verses.text:
तच्छैलवेगाभिहतं हताश्वं हतसारथिम्।
रक्षसां रुधिरक्लिन्नं बभूवायोधनं महत्॥ १२॥
verses.m: That vast battle-field, on which havoc was played by the tremendous velocity of the rock, horses killed and charioteers struck down, got wetted with the blood of ogres. (12)

verses.text:
रथिनो वानरेन्द्राणां शरैः कालान्तकोपमैः।
शिरांसि नर्दतां जह्रुः सहसा भीमनिःस्वनाः॥ १३॥
verses.m: Emitting a terrible roar, car-warriors precipitately severed the heads of the yelling monkey chiefs with their arrows, which were deadly like the destructive darts appearing at the time of universal dissolution. (13)

verses.text:
वानराश्च महात्मानः समुत्पाट्य महाद्रुमान्।
रथानश्वान् गजानुष्ट्रान् राक्षसानभ्यसूदयन्॥ १४॥
verses.m: Uprooting large trees, the gigantic monkeys too in their turn began to destroy the chariots, horses, elephants, camels and ogres. (14)

verses.text:
हनूमाञ्शैलशृङ्गाणि शिलाश्च विविधान् द्रुमान्।
ववर्ष कुम्भकर्णस्य शिरस्यम्बरमास्थितः॥ १५॥
verses.m: Remaining stationed in the air, Hanumān, for his part, rained mountain peaks, rocks and trees of every kind on the head of Kumbhakarṇa. (15)

verses.text:
तानि पर्वतशृङ्गाणि शूलेन स बिभेद ह।
बभञ्ज वृक्षवर्षं च कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः॥ १६॥
verses.m: The said Kumbhakarṇa, who was endowed with extraordinary might, split those mountain peaks and intercepted the shower of trees with his pike. (16)

verses.text:
ततो हरीणां तदनीकमुग्रं
दुद्राव शूलं निशितं प्रगृह्य।
तस्थौ स तस्यापततः परस्ता-
न्महीधराग्रं हनुमान् प्रगृह्य॥ १७॥
verses.m: Firmly seizing hold of his sharpened pike, he then rushed towards that formidable army of monkeys. Tightly holding a mountain peak, the celebrated Hanumān stood before him even as he advanced. (17)

verses.text:
स कुम्भकर्णं कुपितो जघान
वेगेन शैलोत्तमभीमकायम्।
संचुक्षुभे तेन तदाभिभूतो
मेदार्द्रगात्रो रुधिरावसिक्तः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Getting enraged, Hanumān struck with vehemence Kumbhakarṇa, who was endowed with a body formidable as the foremost of hills. Overpowered by that blow, the ogre was thoroughly upset, and bespattered with fat and bathed in blood.(18)

verses.text:
स शूलमाविध्य तडित्प्रकाशं
गिरिं यथा प्रज्वलिताग्निशृङ्गम्।
बाह्वन्तरे मारुतिमाजघान
गुहोऽचलं क्रौञ्चमिवोग्रशक्त्या॥ १९॥
verses.m: Brandishing his pike which was bright as lightning, and resembled a mountain crowned with a blazing fire, he struck with it Hanumān (son of the wind-god) in the breast (lit., the space between the arms), even as Kārtikeya (son of Lord Śiva) struck the Krauñca mountain with his formidable javelin. (19)

verses.text:
स शूलनिर्भिन्नमहाभुजान्तरः
प्रविह्वलः शोणितमुद्वमन् मुखात्।
ननाद भीमं हनुमान् महाहवे
युगान्तमेघस्तनितस्वनोपमम् ॥ २०॥
verses.m: Ejecting blood from his mouth, Hanumān, who was thrown completely out of his wits, his broad chest being pierced with a pike by Kumbhakarṇa, gave forth in that major conflict a terrific cry of anguish, which resembled the thunder-clap of clouds at the end of the world-cycle. (20)

verses.text:
ततो विनेदुः सहसा प्रहृष्टा
रक्षोगणास्तं व्यथितं समीक्ष्य।
प्लवंगमास्तु व्यथिता भयार्ताः
प्रदुद्रुवुः संयति कुम्भकर्णात्॥ २१॥
verses.m: Highly rejoiced to see him agonized, the ranks of ogres forthwith burst into a loud cheer; while the monkeys, who were seized with agony and stricken with fear of Kumbhakarṇa, fled from the battlefield. (21)

verses.text:
ततस्तु नीलो बलवान् पर्यवस्थापयन् बलम्।
प्रविचिक्षेप शैलाग्रं कुम्भकर्णाय धीमते॥ २२॥
verses.m: Restoring his army to confidence, the mighty Nīla for his part then flung with vehemence a mountain peak at the intelligent Kumbhakarṇa. (22)

verses.text:
तदापतन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य मुष्टिनाभिजघान ह।
मुष्टिप्रहाराभिहतं तच्छैलाग्रं व्यशीर्यत।
सविस्फुलिङ्गं सज्वालं निपपात महीतले॥ २३॥
verses.m: Seeing it approaching, the latter struck it with his fist. Struck with a blow of his fist, that mountain peak was split into pieces and dropped on the earth’s surface emitting sparks and flames. (23)

verses.text:
ऋषभः शरभो नीलो गवाक्षो गन्धमादनः।
पञ्च वानरशार्दूलाः कुम्भकर्णमुपाद्रवन्॥ २४॥
verses.m: Five tigers among monkeys, viz., Ṛṣabha, Śarabha, Nīla, Gavākṣa and Gandhamādana attacked Kumbhakarṇa. (24)

verses.text:
शैलैर्वृक्षैस्तलैः पादैर्मुष्टिभिश्च महाबलाः।
कुम्भकर्णं महाकायं निजघ्नुः सर्वतो युधि॥ २५॥
verses.m: Endowed with extraordinary might the aforesaid monkeys struck the colossal Kumbhakarṇa on all sides with crags, trees, the palms of their hands, feet and fists on the battlefield. (25)

verses.text:
स्पर्शानिव प्रहारांस्तान् वेदयानो न विव्यथे।
ऋषभं तु महावेगं बाहुभ्यां परिषस्वजे॥ २६॥
verses.m: Feeling the aforesaid blows as no more than soft touches, he did not experience any pain at all. And he encircled Ṛṣabha, who was full of great impetuosity, with his arms. (26)

verses.text:
कुम्भकर्णभुजाभ्यां तु पीडितो वानरर्षभः।
निपपातर्षभो भीमः प्रमुखागतशोणितः॥ २७॥
verses.m: Pressed hard with the arms of Kumbhakarṇa, however, the redoubtable Ṛṣabha, a veritable bull among the monkeys, fell down, blood having oozed from his mouth in profusion. (27)

verses.text:
मुष्टिना शरभं हत्वा जानुना नीलमाहवे।
आजघान गवाक्षं तु तलेनेन्द्ररिपुस्तदा।
पादेनाभ्यहनत् क्रुद्धस्तरसा गन्धमादनम्॥ २८॥
verses.m: Striking Śarabha with his fist, Kumbhakarṇa (the enemy of Indra) hit Nīla with his knee on the battlefield and slapped Gavākṣa. Then, filled with rage, he kicked Gandhamādana with vehemence. (28)

verses.text:
दत्तप्रहारव्यथिता मुमुहुः शोणितोक्षिताः।
निपेतुस्ते तु मेदिन्यां निकृत्ता इव किंशुकाः॥ २९॥
verses.m: Agonized by the blows dealt by Kumbhakarṇa, they all fainted and fell to the ground, drenched in blood, like Kiṁśuka trees, bearing red blossom that have been cut down. (29)

verses.text:
तेषु वानरमुख्येषु पातितेषु महात्मसु।
वानराणां सहस्राणि कुम्भकर्णं प्रदुद्रुवुः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: The aforesaid gigantic leaders of monkeys having been struck down, thousands of monkeys darted towards Kumbhakarṇa. (30)

verses.text:
तं शैलमिव शैलाभाः सर्वे तु प्लवगर्षभाः।
समारुह्य समुत्पत्य ददंशुश्च महाबलाः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Jumping and climbing on him, even as one would ascend a mountain, all the leaders of monkeys for their part, who themselves looked like mountains and were endowed with extraordinary might, began to bite him, too. (31)

verses.text:
तं नखैर्दशनैश्चापि मुष्टिभिर्बाहुभिस्तथा।
कुम्भकर्णं महाबाहुं निजघ्नुः प्लवगर्षभाः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: The foremost of monkeys attacked the said Kumbhakarṇa, who was endowed with mighty arms, with their nails and teeth as also with their fists and arms. (32)

verses.text:
स वानरसहस्रैस्तु विचितः पर्वतोपमः।
रराज राक्षसव्याघ्रो गिरिरात्मरुहैरिव॥ ३३॥
verses.m: Covered by thousands of monkeys that mountain-like tiger among ogres looked charming like a mountain overgrown with trees. (33)

verses.text:
बाहुभ्यां वानरान् सर्वान् प्रगृह्य स महाबलः।
भक्षयामास संक्रुद्धो गरुडः पन्नगानिव॥ ३४॥
verses.m: Tightly seizing hold of all the monkeys with his arms, highly enraged as he was, Kumbhakarṇa, who was endowed with extraordinary might, began to devour them even as Garuḍa would devour serpents. (34)

verses.text:
प्रक्षिप्ताः कुम्भकर्णेन वक्त्रे पातालसंनिभे।
नासापुटाभ्यां संजग्मुः कर्णाभ्यां चैव वानराः॥ ३५॥
verses.m: Thrust into his mouth, which closely resembled Pātāla (the nethermost subterranean region), by Kumbhakarṇa, the monkeys issued forth through his nostrils as well as through his ears. (35)

verses.text:
भक्षयन् भृशसंक्रुद्धो हरीन् पर्वतसंनिभः।
बभञ्ज वानरान् सर्वान् संक्रुद्धो राक्षसोत्तमः॥ ३६॥
verses.m: While devouring the monkeys, highly enraged as he was, the prince of ogres, who looked like a mountain and repeatedly mutilated the monkeys. (36)

verses.text:
मांसशोणितसंक्लेदां कुर्वन् भूमिं स राक्षसः।
चचार हरिसैन्येषु कालाग्निरिव मूर्च्छितः॥ ३७॥
verses.m: Covering the earth with flesh and blood, the said ogre ranged through the simian ranks like the augmented fire of universal dissolution. (37)

verses.text:
वज्रहस्तो यथा शक्रः पाशहस्त इवान्तकः।
शूलहस्तो बभौ युद्धे कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः॥ ३८॥
verses.m: Pike in hand, Kumbhakarṇa, who was endowed with extraordinary might, shone like Indra (the ruler of gods) holding the thunderbolt in his hand, or like Death, bearing a noose in his hand. (38)

verses.text:
यथा शुष्काण्यरण्यानि ग्रीष्मे दहति पावकः।
तथा वानरसैन्यानि कुम्भकर्णो ददाह सः॥ ३९॥
verses.m: The ill-famed Kumbhakarṇa consumed the simian ranks even as a forest fire would consume dry forests in summer. (39)

verses.text:
ततस्ते वध्यमानास्तु हतयूथाः प्लवंगमाः।
वानरा भयसंविग्ना विनेदुर्विकृतैः स्वरैः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: Wild with terror, the aforesaid monkeys for their part, who moved about leaping, and who had lost many of their battalions, yelled in unnatural tones while being destroyed as above by Kumbhakarṇa. (40)

verses.text:
अनेकशो वध्यमानाः कुम्भकर्णेन वानराः।
राघवं शरणं जग्मुर्व्यथिता भिन्नचेतसः॥ ४१॥
verses.m: Agonized and dispirited while being exterminated in large numbers by Kumbhakarṇa, the monkeys sought Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, as their refuge. (41)

verses.text:
प्रभग्नान् वानरान् दृष्ट्वा वज्रहस्तात्मजात्मजः।
अभ्यधावत वेगेन कुम्भकर्णं महाहवे॥ ४२॥
verses.m: Seeing the monkeys completely routed, the son of Vālī (sprung from the loins of Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt) rushed with impetuosity at Kumbhakarṇa in the great struggle. (42)

verses.text:
शैलशृङ्गं महद् गृह्य विनदन् स मुहुर्मुहुः।
त्रासयन् राक्षसान् सर्वान् कुम्भकर्णपदानुगान्॥ ४३॥
चिक्षेप शैलशिखरं कुम्भकर्णस्य मूर्धनि।
स तेनाभिहतो मूर्ध्नि शैलेनेन्द्ररिपुस्तदा॥ ४४॥
कुम्भकर्णः प्रजज्वाल क्रोधेन महता तदा।
सोऽभ्यधावत वेगेन वालिपुत्रममर्षणः॥ ४५॥
verses.m: Seizing hold of a huge mountain peak, roaring again and again and frightening all the ogres who followed the footsteps of Kumbhakarṇa, he flung the mountain top on Kumbhakarṇa’s head. Struck on the head with that crag, Kumbhakarṇa, the well-known enemy of Indra, burnt up with great rage. The intolerant ogre then rushed at Aṅgada (son of Vālī) with vehemence. (43—45)

verses.text:
कुम्भकर्णो महानादस्त्रासयन् सर्ववानरान्।
शूलं ससर्ज वै रोषादङ्गदे तु महाबलः॥ ४६॥
verses.m: Making a great noise, and terrifying all the monkeys, Kumbhakarṇa for his part who was endowed with extraordinary might, forthwith hurled his pike in rage at Aṅgada. (46)

verses.text:
तदापतन्तं बलवान् युद्धमार्गविशारदः।
लाघवान्मोक्षयामास बलवान् वानरर्षभः॥ ४७॥
verses.m: The mighty Aṅgada, a bull among the monkeys, who was an adept in the technique of warfare, dodged the approaching pike with agility. (47)

verses.text:
उत्पत्य चैनं तरसा तलेनोरस्यताडयत्।
स तेनाभिहतः कोपात् प्रमुमोहाचलोपमः॥ ४८॥
verses.m: Nay, jumping up, he gave the ogre a blow with vehemence on the chest. Struck by Aṅgada with fury, the ogre, who resembled a mountain (in size), fainted. (48)

verses.text:
स लब्धसंज्ञोऽतिबलो मुष्टिं संगृह्य राक्षसः।
अपहस्तेन चिक्षेप विसंज्ञः स पपात ह॥ ४९॥
verses.m: Doubling his fist, when he regained his senses, the notorious ogre, who was endowed with exceeding might, dealt a blow with the back of his hand, and Aṅgada fell down unconscious: so the tradition goes. (49)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् प्लवगशार्दूले विसंज्ञे पतिते भुवि।
तच्छूलं समुपादाय सुग्रीवमभिदुद्रुवे॥ ५०॥
verses.m: Seizing that pike, when the aforesaid tiger among monkeys had dropped unconscious on the ground, the ogre rushed towards Sugrīva. (50)

verses.text:
तमापतन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य कुम्भकर्णं महाबलम्।
उत्पपात तदा वीरः सुग्रीवो वानराधिपः॥ ५१॥
verses.m: Perceiving the notorious Kumbhakarṇa, who was endowed with extraordinary might, approaching, the heroic Sugrīva, the suzerain lord of monkeys, bounded in the air. (51)

verses.text:
स पर्वताग्रमुत्क्षिप्य समाविध्य महाकपिः।
अभिदुद्राव वेगेन कुम्भकर्णं महाबलम्॥ ५२॥
verses.m: Lifting up a mountain peak and flourishing it, that mighty monkey darted towards Kumbhakarṇa, who was possessed of great might. (52)

verses.text:
तमापतन्तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य कुम्भकर्णः प्लवंगमम्।
तस्थौ विवृत्तसर्वाङ्गो वानरेन्द्रस्य सम्मुखः॥ ५३॥
verses.m: Perceiving that monkey advancing, Kumbhakarṇa stood facing the lord of monkeys, with all his limbs braced. (53)

verses.text:
कपिशोणितदिग्धाङ्गं भक्षयन्तं महाकपीन्।
कुम्भकर्णं स्थितं दृष्ट्वा सुग्रीवो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ ५४॥
verses.m: Seeing Kumbhakarṇa who stood devouring the colossal monkeys and whose limbs were smeared with their blood, Sugrīva spoke to him as follows : (54)

verses.text:
पातिताश्च त्वया वीराः कृतं कर्म सुदुष्करम्।
भक्षितानि च सैन्यानि प्राप्तं ते परमं यशः॥ ५५॥
verses.m: “A feat exceedingly difficult to perform has been accomplished by you, in that champions have been struck down, battalions devoured and the highest renown attained by you. (55)

verses.text:
त्यज तद् वानरानीकं प्राकृतैः किं करिष्यसि।
सहस्वैकं निपातं मे पर्वतस्यास्य राक्षस॥ ५६॥
verses.m: “Let alone that army of monkeys. What are you to do with the rank and file? Stand only the exclusive impact of this mountain going to be hurled by me, O ogre!” (56)

verses.text:
तद् वाक्यं हरिराजस्य सत्त्वधैर्यसमन्वितम्।
श्रुत्वा राक्षसशार्दूलः कुम्भकर्णोऽब्रवीद् वचः॥ ५७॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid challenge of Sugrīva (the ruler of monkeys), which was full of courage and fortitude, Kumbhakarṇa, a tiger among ogres, made the following reply: (57)

verses.text:
प्रजापतेस्तु पौत्रस्त्वं तथैवर्क्षरजःसुतः।
धृतिपौरुषसम्पन्नस्तस्माद् गर्जसि वानर॥ ५८॥
verses.m: “You are a grandson of Brahmā (the lord of created beings) and even so son of Ṛkṣarajā (sprung from the yawn of Brahmā) and richly endowed with fortitude and valour. Hence you roar, O monkey!” (58)

verses.text:
स कुम्भकर्णस्य वचो निशम्य
व्याविध्य शैलं सहसा मुमोच।
तेनाजघानोरसि कुम्भकर्णं
शैलेन वज्राशनिसंनिभेन॥ ५९॥
verses.m: Hearing the reply of Kumbhakarṇa and balancing the mountain top, Sugrīva precipitately discharged it, and struck Kumbhakarṇa in the chest with that crag, resembling the thunderbolt and a shooting star. (59)

verses.text:
तच्छैलशृङ्गं सहसा विभिन्नं
भुजान्तरे तस्य तदा विशाले।
ततो विषेदुः सहसा प्लवंगा
रक्षोगणाश्चापि मुदा विनेदुः॥ ६०॥
verses.m: The aforesaid crag forthwith smashed on his huge chest all at once. The monkeys thereupon despaired all of a sudden, while the ranks of the ogres thundered with joy. (60)

verses.text:
स शैलशृङ्गाभिहतश्चुकोप
ननाद रोषाच्च विवृत्य वक्त्रम्।
व्याविध्य शूलं स तडित्प्रकाशं
चिक्षेप हर्यृक्षपतेर्वधाय॥ ६१॥
verses.m: Struck with that mountain top, the ogre flew into a rage and dilating his mouth in anger, roared again and again. Nay, flourishing his pike, which flashed as lightning, he hurled it for the destruction of Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys and bears. (61)

verses.text:
तत् कुम्भकर्णस्य भुजप्रणुन्नं
शूलं शितं काञ्चनधामयष्टिम्।
क्षिप्रं समुत्पत्य निगृह्य दोर्भ्यां
बभञ्ज वेगेन सुतोऽनिलस्य॥ ६२॥
verses.m: Bounding at once and seizing hold with his arms of that sharp pike propelled by Kumbhakarṇa’s arm, whose shaft was adorned with chains of gold, Hanumān (son of the wind-god) broke it with vehemence. (62)

verses.text:
कृतं भारसहस्रस्य शूलं कालायसं महत्।
बभञ्ज जानुमारोप्य तदा हृष्टः प्लवंगमः॥ ६३॥
verses.m: Placing on his knee that huge iron pike, which was made of iron weighing a thousand Bhāras*, the monkey joyfully broke it at once. (63)

verses.text:
शूलं भग्नं हनुमता दृष्ट्वा वानरवाहिनी।
हृष्टा ननाद बहुशः सर्वतश्चापि दुद्रुवे॥ ६४॥
verses.m: Rejoiced to see the pike broken by Hanumān, the army of monkeys repeatedly roared and rushed up from all sides. (64)

verses.text:
बभूवाथ परित्रस्तो राक्षसो विमुखोऽभवत्।
सिंहनादं च ते चक्रुः प्रहृष्टा वनगोचराः।
मारुतिं पूजयांचक्रुर्दृष्ट्वा शूलं तथागतम्॥ ६५॥
verses.m: The ogre, on the other hand, got dismayed and downcast; while highly rejoiced monkeys (lit., rangers of the woods) roared like lions and applauded the son of the wind-god, on beholding the pike broken into pieces. (65)

verses.text:
स तत् तथा भग्नमवेक्ष्य शूलं
चुकोप रक्षोधिपतिर्महात्मा।
उत्पाट्य लङ्कामलयात् स शृङ्गं
जघान सुग्रीवमुपेत्य तेन॥ ६६॥
verses.m: That colossal overlord of ogres, Kumbhakarṇa, flew into a rage on seeing that pike broken in that wise by Hanumān. Tearing off a peak of the Malaya mountain standing in the vicinity of Laṅkā and approaching Sugrīva, he struck him with it. (66)

verses.text:
स शैलशृङ्गाभिहतो विसंज्ञः
पपात भूमौ युधि वानरेन्द्रः।
तं वीक्ष्य भूमौ पतितं विसंज्ञं
नेदुः प्रहृष्टा युधि यातुधानाः॥ ६७॥
verses.m: Struck with the crag, that ruler of monkeys fell senseless on the battlefield. Highly rejoiced to see him fallen unconscious on the battleground, the ogres let forth a roar of triumph. (67)

verses.text:
समभ्युपेत्याद्भुतघोरवीर्यं
स कुम्भकर्णो युधि वानरेन्द्रम्।
जहार सुग्रीवमभिप्रगृह्य
यथानिलो मेघमिव प्रचण्डः॥ ६८
verses.m: Approaching on the battlefield Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, who was endowed with marvellous and terrific prowess, nay, pressing him in his arm-pit, the notorious Kumbhakarṇa bore him away even as a tempestuous wind would sweep away a cloud. (68)

verses.text:
स तं महामेघनिकाशरूप-
मुत्पाट्य गच्छन् युधि कुम्भकर्णः।
रराज मेरुप्रतिमानरूपो
मेरुर्यथा व्युच्छ्रितघोरशृङ्गः॥ ६९॥
