verses.m: Departing after lifting up Sugrīva, whose form resembled a huge cloud, the said Kumbhakarṇa, who was endowed with a form resembling Mount Meru (in size), shone on the battlefield like the said Mount Meru, distinguished by its exceedingly lofty and formidable peak. (69)

verses.text:
ततस्तमादाय जगाम वीरः
संस्तूयमानो युधि राक्षसेन्द्रः।
शृण्वन् निनादं त्रिदिवालयानां
प्लवङ्गराजग्रहविस्मितानाम् ॥ ७०॥
verses.m: Seizing hold of Sugrīva, the heroic Kumbhakarṇa (the lord of ogres) left for Laṅkā, being duly extolled by the ogres on the battlefield and hearing the outcry of gods (the denizens of heaven) who were taken aback at the capture of Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys. (70)

verses.text:
ततस्तमादाय तदा स मेने
हरीन्द्रमिन्द्रोपममिन्द्रवीर्यः।
अस्मिन् हते सर्वमिदं हतं स्यात्
सराघवं सैन्यमितीन्द्रशत्रुः॥ ७१॥
verses.m: Having seized hold at that moment of the aforesaid ruler of monkeys, Sugrīva, who vied with Indra (the ruler of gods), that enemy of Indra, Kumbhakarṇa, who was endowed with the valour of Indra, thereupon concluded that, Sugrīva having been killed, this entire army of monkeys, including Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), would be automatically destroyed. (71)

verses.text:
विद्रुतां वाहिनीं दृष्ट्वा वानराणामितस्ततः।
कुम्भकर्णेन सुग्रीवं गृहीतं चापि वानरम्॥ ७२॥
हनूमांश्चिन्तयामास मतिमान् मारुतात्मजः।
एवं गृहीते सुग्रीवे किं कर्तव्यं मया भवेत्॥ ७३॥
verses.m: Beholding the army of monkeys scattered here and there and the monkey Sugrīva, too, captured by Kumbhakarṇa, the sagacious Hanumān, sprung from the loins of the wind-god, thought to himself: ‘What should be done by me when Sugrīva has been captured in this way? (72-73)

verses.text:
यद्धि न्याय्यं मया कर्तुं तत् करिष्याम्यसंशयम्।
भूत्वा पर्वतसंकाशो नाशयिष्यामि राक्षसम्॥ ७४॥
verses.m: ‘I shall undoubtedly do that which is fit to be done by me. Growing to the size of a mountain, I shall kill the ogre. (74)

verses.text:
मया हते संयति कुम्भकर्णे
महाबले मुष्टिविशीर्णदेहे।
विमोचिते वानरपार्थिवे च
भवन्तु हृष्टाः प्लवगाः समग्राः॥ ७५॥
verses.m: ‘When Kumbhakarṇa, who is endowed with extraordinary might, has been killed by me in a duel, his body being shattered with my fist, and the king of monkeys delivered, let all the monkeys feel rejoiced. (75)

verses.text:
अथवा स्वयमप्येष मोक्षं प्राप्स्यति वानरः।
गृहीतोऽयं यदि भवेत् त्रिदशैः सासुरोरगैः॥ ७६॥
verses.m: ‘Or, this monkey, Sugrīva, will win his freedom back himself, even if he is captured by gods including demons and Nāgas (serpent-demons having the face of a man and the tail of a serpent). (76)

verses.text:
मन्ये न तावदात्मानं बुध्यते वानराधिपः।
शैलप्रहाराभिहतः कुम्भकर्णेन संयुगे॥ ७७॥
verses.m: ‘Struck with the blow of a crag by Kumbhakarṇa on the battlefield, the overlord of monkeys, I presume, is not yet conscious of his self. (77)

verses.text:
अयं मुहूर्तात् सुग्रीवो लब्धसंज्ञो महाहवे।
आत्मनो वानराणां च यत् पथ्यं तत् करिष्यति॥ ७८॥
verses.m: ‘Having regained his senses in a short while, in this major conflict, this Sugrīva will do what is good for himself as well as for the monkeys. (78)

verses.text:
मया तु मोक्षितस्यास्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः।
अप्रीतिश्च भवेत् कष्टा कीर्तिनाशश्च शाश्वतः॥ ७९॥
verses.m: ‘Grievous displeasure will certainly be caused to the high-souled Sugrīva on his being delivered by me, nay, his reputation will be lost forever. (79)

verses.text:
तस्मान्मुहूर्तं काङ्क्षिष्ये विक्रमं मोक्षितस्य तु।
भिन्नं च वानरानीकं तावदाश्वासयाम्यहम्॥ ८०॥
verses.m: ‘I shall for my part, therefore, await awhile the exhibition of prowess on his part on his being restored to freedom. Till then I shall restore to confidence the scattered army of the monkeys.’ (80)

verses.text:
इत्येवं चिन्तयित्वाथ हनूमान् मारुतात्मजः।
भूयः संस्तम्भयामास वानराणां महाचमूम्॥ ८१॥
verses.m: Pondering thus, Hanumān, sprung from the loins of the wind-god, once more brought firmness to the huge army of the monkeys. (81)

verses.text:
स कुम्भकर्णोऽथ विवेश लङ्कां
स्फुरन्तमादाय महाहरिं तम्।
विमानचर्यागृहगोपुरस्थैः
पुष्पाग्र्यवर्षैरभिपूज्यमानः ॥ ८२॥
verses.m: Bearing the great monkey, Sugrīva, who had now begun to shake, the notorious Kumbhakarṇa now entered Laṅkā, being hailed on all sides by people dwelling in seven-storeyed mansions, houses lining the roads and the gates of buildings with showers of excellent flowers. (82)

verses.text:
लाजगन्धोदवर्षैस्तु सेच्यमानः शनैः शनैः।
राजवीथ्यास्तु शीतत्वात् संज्ञां प्राप महाबलः॥ ८३॥
verses.m: Being gently sprinkled with showers of fried grains of paddy and scented water and due to the coolness of the king’s highway, Sugrīva, who was endowed with extraordinary might, gradually regained consciousness. (83)

verses.text:
ततः स संज्ञामुपलभ्य कृच्छ्राद्
बलीयसस्तस्य भुजान्तरस्थः।
अवेक्षमाणः पुरराजमार्गं
विचिन्तयामास मुहुर्महात्मा॥ ८४॥
verses.m: Having regained consciousness with difficulty, while yet in the arms of Kumbhakarṇa, who was endowed with exceeding might, and gazing on the king’s highway in the city, Sugrīva, the high-souled monkey, then repeatedly pondered as follows: (84)

verses.text:
एवं गृहीतेन कथं नु नाम
शक्यं मया सम्प्रतिकर्तुमद्य।
तथा करिष्यामि यथा हरीणां
भविष्यतीष्टं च हितं च कार्यम्॥ ८५॥
verses.m: ‘How on earth can it at all be possible to retaliate at this moment for me, who have been taken captive in this way? Therefore, I shall take action in such a way as may prove agreeable and advantageous to the monkeys.’ (85)

verses.text:
ततः कराग्रैः सहसा समेत्य
राजा हरीणाममरेन्द्रशत्रोः।
खरैश्च कर्णौ दशनैश्च नासां
ददंश पादैर्विददार पार्श्वौ॥ ८६॥
verses.m: Reaching this conclusion, the king of monkeys tore off with his sharp nails all of a sudden the lower end of the ears of Kumbhakarṇa, the enemy of the ruler of gods, nay, bit off the latter’s nose with his teeth and split open his sides with the nails of his toes. (86)

verses.text:
स कुम्भकर्णो हृतकर्णनासो
विदारितस्तेन रदैर्नखैश्च।
रोषाभिभूतः क्षतजार्द्रगात्रः
सुग्रीवमाविध्य पिपेष भूमौ॥ ८७॥
verses.m: Overwelmed with anger when deprived of a part of his ears and nose by Sugrīva and split open in the sides with the latter’s teeth and nails, his limbs bespattered with blood, nay, spinning Sugrīva down, the notorious Kumbhakarṇa pounded him with ferocity against the ground. (87)

verses.text:
स भूतले भीमबलाभिपिष्टः
सुरारिभिस्तैरभिहन्यमानः।
जगाम खं कन्दुकवज्जवेन
पुनश्च रामेण समाजगाम॥ ८८॥
verses.m: Rubbed against the earth’s surface by Kumbhakarṇa, who was endowed with terrific might, and while being struck by those enemies of gods (who stood by his side), Sugrīva bounced in the air like a ball and got re-united with all speed with Śrī Rāma. (88)

verses.text:
कर्णनासाविहीनस्तु कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः।
रराज शोणितोत्सिक्तो गिरिः प्रस्रवणैरिव॥ ८९॥
verses.m: Deprived of the lower ends of his ears and nose and bathed in blood, Kumbhakarṇa for his part, who was endowed with extraordinary might, shone like a mountain with springs. (89)

verses.text:
शोणितार्द्रो महाकायो राक्षसो भीमदर्शनः।
युद्धायाभिमुखो भूयो मनश्चक्रे निशाचरः॥ ९०॥
verses.m: Drenched in blood, the colossal and terrible-looking ogre, a ranger of the night, made up his mind once more to fight with his face turned towards the enemy. (90)

verses.text:
अमर्षाच्छोणितोद्गारी शुशुभे रावणानुजः।
नीलाञ्जनचयप्रख्यः ससंध्य इव तोयदः॥ ९१॥
verses.m: Vomiting blood in indignation, Kumbhakarṇa (a younger brother of Rāvaṇa) who resembled a mass of collyrium, shone like an evening cloud with a reddish tinge. (91)

verses.text:
गते च तस्मिन् सुरराजशत्रुः
क्रोधात् प्रदुद्राव रणाय भूयः।
अनायुधोऽस्मीति विचिन्त्य रौद्रो
घोरं तदा मुद्गरमाससाद॥ ९२॥
verses.m: Nay, Sugrīva having escaped, Kumbhakarṇa (an enemy of the ruler of gods) furiously rushed for an encounter once more. Reflecting within himself that ‘I am weaponless’. the ferocious ogre then seized hold of a formidable mallet. (92)

verses.text:
ततः स पुर्याः सहसा महौजा
निष्क्रम्य तद् वानरसैन्यमुग्रम्।
बभक्ष रक्षो युधि कुम्भकर्णः
प्रजा युगान्ताग्निरिव प्रवृद्धः॥ ९३॥
verses.m: Issuing all of a sudden from the city, the aforesaid ogre, Kumbhakarṇa, who was endowed with extraordinary vigour, then began to consume the redoubtable army of monkeys on the battlefied even as the fire swollen at the end of the world-cycle would consume created beings. (93)

verses.text:
बुभुक्षितः शोणितमांसगृध्नुः
प्रविश्य तद् वानरसैन्यमुग्रम्।
चखाद रक्षांसि हरीन् पिशाचा-
न्नृक्षांश्च मोहाद् युधि कुम्भकर्णः।
यथैव मृत्युर्हरते युगान्ते
स भक्षयामास हरींश्च मुख्यान्॥ ९४॥
verses.m: Penetrating deep into that formidable army of monkeys, Kumbhakarṇa, who, being famished, was covetous of flesh and blood, began to devour ogres, monkeys, fiends and bears (alike) on the battlefield through infatuation. Nay, he ate up, among others, the principal monkeys in the same way as Death sweeps away living beings at the end of the world-cycle. (94)

verses.text:
एकं द्वौ त्रीन् बहून् क्रुद्धो वानरान् सह राक्षसैः।
समादायैकहस्तेन प्रचिक्षेप त्वरन् मुखे॥ ९५॥
verses.m: Seizing together with one hand, one, two, three or more monkeys alongwith ogres, the ogre hastily thrust them into his mouth. (95)

verses.text:
सम्प्रस्रवंस्तदा मेदः शोणितं च महाबलः।
वध्यमानो नगेन्द्राग्रैर्भक्षयामास वानरान्॥ ९६॥
verses.m: Pouring forth in streams fat and blood from the corners of his mouth at that time, the ogre feasted on the monkeys even while being struck with peaks of the foremost of mountains. (96)

verses.text:
ते भक्ष्यमाणा हरयो रामं जग्मुस्तदा गतिम्।
कुम्भकर्णो भृशं क्रुद्धः कपीन् खादन् प्रधावति॥ ९७॥
verses.m: While being devoured by the ogre, the aforesaid monkeys sought Śrī Rāma as their refuge at that time. Kumbhakarṇa, on the other hand, who was highly enraged, ran about with all speed devouring the monkeys. (97)

verses.text:
शतानि सप्त चाष्टौ च विंशत्त्रिंशत् तथैव च।
सम्परिष्वज्य बाहुभ्यां खादन् विपरिधावति॥ ९८॥
verses.m: Tightly enfolding with his arms as many as seven and eight, nay, twenty, thirty and even so hundreds at a time, he ran fast devouring them on all sides. (98)

verses.text:
मेदोवसाशोणितदिग्धगात्रः
कर्णावसक्तग्रथितान्त्रमालः।
ववर्ष शूलानि सुतीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रः
कालो युगान्तस्थ इव प्रवृद्धः॥ ९९॥
verses.m: His limbs besmeared with fat, marrow and blood and wreaths of tangled entrails hung over his ears, the ogre, who was endowed with exceptionally sharp teeth, rained darts (on the monkeys) even like Kāla, the Time-Spirit, grown immensely (in size) at the end of the world-cycle. (99)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् काले सुमित्रायाः पुत्रः परबलार्दनः।
चकार लक्ष्मणः क्रुद्धो युद्धं परपुरंजयः॥ १००॥
verses.m: At that juncture, Lakṣmaṇa, son of Sumitrā, the scourage of hostile forces and the conqueror of hostile citadels commenced fighting in rage. (100)

verses.text:
स कुम्भकर्णस्य शरान् शरीरे सप्त वीर्यवान्।
निचखानाददे चान्यान् विससर्ज च लक्ष्मणः॥ १०१॥
verses.m: The valliant Lakṣmaṇa, dug seven arrows into the person of Kumbhakarṇa. He took up more and discharged them too. (101)

verses.text:
पीड्यमानस्तदस्त्रं तु विशेषं तत् स राक्षसः।
ततश्चुकोप बलवान् सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः॥ १०२॥
verses.m: Being tormented (by the arrows), the aforesaid ogre for his part put an end to these missiles of Lakṣmaṇa with his own. Thereupon the mighty Lakṣmaṇa (who enhanced the joy of Sumitrā, his mother) flew into a rage. (102)

verses.text:
अथास्य कवचं शुभ्रं जाम्बूनदमयं शुभम्।
प्रच्छादयामास शरैः संध्याभ्रमिव मारुतः॥ १०३॥
verses.m: He then completely covered the glittering and charming golden armour of Kumbhakarṇa with his arrows even as the wind would make an evening cloud completely disappear by dispersing it. (103)

verses.text:
नीलाञ्जनचयप्रख्यः शरैः काञ्चनभूषणैः।
आपीड्यमानः शुशुभे मेघैः सूर्य इवांशुमान्॥ १०४॥
verses.m: Being covered by arrows decked with gold, the ogre, who resembled a mass of collyrium, shone like the sun with its rays being screened by clouds. (104)

verses.text:
ततः स राक्षसो भीमः सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनम्।
सावज्ञमेव प्रोवाच वाक्यं मेघौघनिःस्वनः॥ १०५॥
verses.m: Thereupon that terrible ogre, whose voice resembled the rumbling of a multitude of clouds spoke as follows to Lakṣmaṇa (who enhanced the joy of his mother, Sumitrā) rather disdainfully: (105)

verses.text:
अन्तकस्याप्यकष्टेन युधि जेतारमाहवे।
युध्यता मामभीतेन ख्यापिता वीरता त्वया॥ १०६॥
verses.m: “Valour has surely been exhibited by you on the battlefield while giving battle undauntedly to me, who would conquer even Death in an encounter without difficulty. (106)

verses.text:
प्रगृहीतायुधस्येह मृत्योरिव महामृधे।
तिष्ठन्नप्यग्रतः पूज्यः किमु युद्धप्रदायकः॥ १०७॥
verses.m: “Worthy of honour is he who is able in this world even to face me, a rival of Death ready for a major conflict, weapon in hand, much more so, the one who gives battle to me. (107)

verses.text:
ऐरावतं समारूढो वृतः सर्वामरैः प्रभुः।
नैव शक्रोऽपि समरे स्थितपूर्वः कदाचन॥ १०८॥
verses.m: “Duly mounted on his elephant, Airāvata and surrounded by all the gods, even the mighty Indra never stood before me in an encounter in the past. (108)

verses.text:
अद्य त्वयाहं सौमित्रे बालेनापि पराक्रमैः।
तोषितो गन्तुमिच्छामि त्वामनुज्ञाप्य राघवम्॥ १०९॥
verses.m: “Gratified by you with your feats of valour today, O son of Sumitrā, even though you are a youngster, yet I wish to meet Rāma (a sion of Raghu), taking leave of you. (109)

verses.text:
यत् तु वीर्यबलोत्साहैस्तोषितोऽहं रणे त्वया।
राममेवैकमिच्छामि हन्तुं यस्मिन् हते हतम्॥ ११०॥
verses.m: “Inasmuch as I have been gratified by you with your prowess, strength and martial ardour in combat, I, for my part, seek precisely to kill Rāma alone; for, when he is dispatched, the entire army of monkeys will stand destroyed. (110)

verses.text:
रामे मयात्र निहते येऽन्ये स्थास्यन्ति संयुगे।
तानहं योधयिष्यामि स्वबलेन प्रमाथिना॥ १११॥
verses.m: “When Rāma has been got rid of by me in this struggle, I shall force those others, who will remain on the battlefield, to fight with my devastating army.” (111)

verses.text:
इत्युक्तवाक्यं तद् रक्षः प्रोवाच स्तुतिसंहितम्।
मृधे घोरतरं वाक्यं सौमित्रिः प्रहसन्निव॥ ११२॥
verses.m: To that exceedingly formidable ogre, when he had made this boastful reply, Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā) addressed the following rejoinder, full of praise, on the battlefield, as though heartily laughing: (112)

verses.text:
यस्त्वं शक्रादिभिर्देवैरसह्यः प्राप्य पौरुषम्।
तत् सत्यं नान्यथा वीर दृष्टस्तेऽद्य पराक्रमः॥ ११३॥
verses.m: “Your assertion that, having acquired extraordinary prowess, you have grown irresistible for even gods headed by Indra, their ruler, is true; it is not otherwise, O champion! Your valour has been witnessed by me today. (113)

verses.text:
एष दाशरथी रामस्तिष्ठत्यद्रिरिवाचलः।
इति श्रुत्वा ह्यनादृत्य लक्ष्मणं स निशाचरः॥ ११४॥
अतिक्रम्य च सौमित्रिं कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः।
राममेवाभिदुद्राव कम्पयन्निव मेदिनीम्॥ ११५॥
verses.m: “Here stands Śrī Rāma, son of Daśaratha, immovable as a mountain.” Hearing this rejoinder, nay, disregarding Lakṣmaṇa and passing him by, that prowler of the night, Kumbhakarṇa, who was endowed with extraordinary might, rushed towards Śrī Rāma alone, causing the earth to shake even as he sped along. (114-115)

verses.text:
अथ दाशरथी रामो रौद्रमस्त्रं प्रयोजयन्।
कुम्भकर्णस्य हृदये ससर्ज निशितान् शरान्॥ ११६॥
verses.m: Making use of mystic missile presided over by Rudra (the god of destruction), Śrī Rāma, son of Daśaratha, forthwith dug pointed arrows into the breast of Kumbhakarṇa. (116)

verses.text:
तस्य रामेण विद्धस्य सहसाभिप्रधावतः।
अङ्गारमिश्राः क्रुद्धस्य मुखान्निश्चेरुरर्चिषः॥ ११७॥
verses.m: As the latter darted in fury all at once towards Śrī Rāma, when hurt by him, flames mixed with embers shot forth from his mouth. (117)

verses.text:
रामास्त्रविद्धो घोरं वै नर्दन् राक्षसपुङ्गवः।
अभ्यधावत संक्रुद्धो हरीन् विद्रावयन् रणे॥ ११८॥
verses.m: Highly enraged when pierced by the arrows of Śrī Rāma, Kumbhakarṇa (a veritable bull among the ogres) rushed towards him terribly roaring and dispersing the monkeys on the battle-field. (118)

verses.text:
तस्योरसि निमग्नास्ते शरा बर्हिणवाससः।
हस्ताच्चास्य परिभ्रष्टा गदा चोर्व्यां पपात ह॥ ११९॥
verses.m: Adorned with peacock’s plumes, the said arrows disappeared into his breast. Nay, fallen from his hand, his mace too dropped to the ground; so the tradition goes. (119)

verses.text:
आयुधानि च सर्वाणि विप्रकीर्यन्त भूतले।
स निरायुधमात्मानं यदा मेने महाबलः॥ १२०॥
मुष्टिभ्यां च कराभ्यां च चकार कदनं महत्।
स बाणैरतिविद्धाङ्गः क्षतजेन समुक्षितः।
रुधिरं परिसुस्राव गिरिः प्रस्रवणं यथा॥ १२१॥
verses.m: All his other weapons too were scattered on the earth’s surface. When the ogre, who was endowed with extraordinary might, realized himself to be unarmed, he played great havoc among the monkeys with his fists and hands too. His limbs pierced beyond measure with arrows and bathed in blood, he poured forth blood even as a mountain would pour out streams. (120-121)

verses.text:
स तीव्रेण च कोपेन रुधिरेण च मूर्च्छितः।
वानरान् राक्षसानृक्षान् खादन् स परिधावति॥ १२२॥
verses.m: Overcome with violent anger and covered all over with blood as well, the notorious ogre ran about devouring the monkeys, ogres and bears alike. (122)

verses.text:
अथ शृङ्गं समाविध्य भीमं भीमपराक्रमः।
चिक्षेप राममुद्दिश्य बलवानन्तकोपमः॥ १२३॥
verses.m: Firmly seizing hold of a formidable mountain peak, the mighty ogre, who was endowed with terrific prowess and resembled Death himself, hurled it towards Śrī Rāma. (123)

verses.text:
अप्राप्तमन्तरा रामः सप्तभिस्तमजिह्मगैः।
चिच्छेद गिरिशृङ्गं तं पुनः संधाय कार्मुकम्॥ १२४॥
verses.m: Making use of his well-known bow once more, Śrī Rāma, however, split that mountain peak, while it was still on its way and had not yet reached him, with seven straight going arrows. (124)

verses.text:
ततस्तु रामो धर्मात्मा तस्य शृङ्गं महत् तदा।
शरैः काञ्चनचित्राङ्गैश्चिच्छेद भरताग्रजः॥ १२५॥
verses.m: Thereupon Śrī Rāma, the elder brother of Bharata, for his part, whose mind was set on virtue, split up the huge mountain peak, hurled by the ogre, with golden-stripped arrows. (125)

verses.text:
तन्मेरुशिखराकारं द्योतमानमिव श्रिया।
द्वे शते वानराणां च पतमानमपातयत्॥ १२६॥
verses.m: While falling down, the aforesaid crag, which looked like a peak of Mount Meru and was shining, as it were, with splendour, knocked down two hundred monkeys too. (126)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् काले स धर्मात्मा लक्ष्मणो राममब्रवीत्।
कुम्भकर्णवधे युक्तो योगान् परिमृशन् बहून्॥ १२७॥
verses.m: At that moment the celebrated Lakṣmaṇa, whose mind was set on virtue, nay, who had been attentive all the time and who was busy devising numerous plans of killing Kumbhakarṇa submitted as follows to Śrī Rāma: (127)

verses.text:
नैवायं वानरान् राजन् न विजानाति राक्षसान्।
मत्तः शोणितगन्धेन स्वान् परांश्चैव खादति॥ १२८॥
verses.m: “Intoxicated, as he is, with the smell of blood, this fellow, O prince, can no longer discriminate the monkeys and ogres and is indiscriminately devouring friends and foes alike. (128)

verses.text:
साध्वेनमधिरोहन्तु सर्वतो वानरर्षभाः।
यूथपाश्च यथा मुख्यास्तिष्ठन्त्वस्मिन् समन्ततः॥ १२९॥
verses.m: “Let the foremost of the monkeys as well as the commanders of troops climb straight upon him from all sides and duly stay on him. (129)

verses.text:
अद्यायं दुर्मतिः काले गुरुभारप्रपीडितः।
प्रचरन् राक्षसो भूमौ नान्यान् हन्यात् प्लवंगमान्॥ १३०॥
verses.m: “Sore oppressed by the heavy weight of the monkeys, this evil-minded ogre will no longer be able to kill the other monkeys while moving about on the earth.” (130)

verses.text:
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा राजपुत्रस्य धीमतः।
ते समारुरुहुर्हृष्टाः कुम्भकर्णं महाबलाः॥ १३१॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid direction of the sagacious prince, the monkeys, who were endowed with extraordinary might, climbed joyfully upon Kumbhakarṇa. (131)

verses.text:
कुम्भकर्णस्तु संक्रुद्धः समारूढः प्लवंगमैः।
व्यधूनयत् तान् वेगेन दुष्टहस्तीव हस्तिपान्॥ १३२॥
verses.m: Highly enraged when climbed upon by the monkeys, Kumbhakarṇa for his part shook them off with vehemence as a refractory elephant would shake off his mahout. (132)

verses.text:
तान् दृष्ट्वा निर्धुतान् रामो रुष्टोऽयमिति राक्षसम्।
समुत्पपात वेगेन धनुरुत्तममाददे॥ १३३॥
verses.m: Finding them shaken off and concluding that the ogre was enraged, Śrī Rāma darted towards him with impetuosity, holding in his hand his excellent bow. (133)

verses.text:
क्रोधरक्तेक्षणो धीरो निर्दहन्निव चक्षुषा।
राघवो राक्षसं वेगादभिदुद्राव वेगितः।
यूथपान् हर्षयन् सर्वान् कुम्भकर्णबलार्दितान्॥ १३४॥
verses.m: He eyes red with fury, as if he was going to burn his adversary with his very glance, and seized with impetuosity, the intrepid Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) rushed towards the ogre with vehemence bringing delight to all his troop-commanders, who were oppressed by the might of Kumbhakarṇa. (134)

verses.text:
स चापमादाय भुजंगकल्पं
दृढज्यमुग्रं तपनीयचित्रम्।
हरीन् समाश्वास्य समुत्पपात
रामो निबद्धोत्तमतूणबाणः॥ १३५॥
verses.m: Taking in his hand his formidable bow, which resembled a serpent, was strung with a stout cord and looked charming with its ornamental crust of gold, nay, fully restoring the monkeys to confidence, the celebrated Śrī Rāma bounded forward, a quiver full of excellent arrows fastened at his back. (135)

verses.text:
स वानरगणैस्तैस्तु वृतः परमदुर्जयैः।
लक्ष्मणानुचरो वीरः सम्प्रतस्थे महाबलः॥ १३६॥
verses.m: Surrounded by the aforesaid troops of monkeys who were extremely difficult to conquer, the aforesaid hero, who was endowed with extraordinary might, duly proceeded to meet Kumbhakarṇa, followed by Lakṣmaṇa. (136)

verses.text:
स ददर्श महात्मानं किरीटिनमरिंदमम्।
शोणिताप्लुतरक्ताक्षं कुम्भकर्णं महाबलः॥ १३७॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma, who was endowed with extraordinary might, saw the colossal Kumbhakarṇa, the tamer of his enemies, adorned with a diadem and bathed in blood, his eyes red with fury. (137)

verses.text:
सर्वान् समभिधावन्तं यथा रुष्टं दिशागजम्।
मार्गमाणं हरीन् क्रुद्धं राक्षसैः परिवारितम्॥ १३८॥
verses.m: Surrounded by ogres and hunting for the monkeys, full of rage, he was pursuing them all like a furious elephant guarding one of the quarters. (138)

verses.text:
विन्ध्यमन्दरसंकाशं काञ्चनाङ्गदभूषणम्।
स्रवन्तं रुधिरं वक्त्राद् वर्षमेघमिवोत्थितम्॥ १३९॥
verses.m: Adorned with armlets of gold, he resembled the Vindhya or the Mandara mountain (in size) and was sprouting blood from his mouth even like a towering cloud pouring down rain. (139)

verses.text:
जिह्वया परिलिह्यन्तं सृक्किणी शोणितोक्षिते।
मृद्गन्तं वानरानीकं कालान्तकयमोपमम्॥ १४०॥
verses.m: With his tongue he was licking the corners of his mouth, which were wet with blood, and was crushing the army of monkeys even like Yama (the god of retribution) figuring as Death at the time of universal dissolution. (140)

verses.text:
तं दृष्ट्वा राक्षसश्रेष्ठं प्रदीप्तानलवर्चसम्।
विस्फारयामास तदा कार्मुकं पुरुषर्षभः॥ १४१॥
verses.m: Seeing that prince of ogres, who shone like inflamed fire, Śrī Rāma, the foremost of men, forthwith pulled the string of his bow. (141)

verses.text:
स तस्य चापनिर्घोषात् कुपितो राक्षसर्षभः।
अमृष्यमाणस्तं घोषमभिदुद्राव राघवम्॥ १४२॥
verses.m: Enraged to hear the twang of his bow, and unable to bear that sound, that bull among the ogres rushed towards Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu).* (142)

verses.text:
ततस्तु वातोद्धतमेघकल्पं
भुजंगराजोत्तमभोगबाहुः।
तमापतन्तं धरणीधराभ-
मुवाच रामो युधि कुम्भकर्णम्॥ १४३॥
verses.m: Thereupon Śrī Rāma for his part, whose arms resembled in thickness and length the coils of Vāsuki (the king of serpents) spoke on the battle-field as follows to the said Kumbhakarṇa, who came rushing like a cloud driven by the wind and resembled a mountain (in size): (143)

verses.text:
आगच्छ रक्षोऽधिप मा विषाद-
मवस्थितोऽहं प्रगृहीतचापः।
अवेहि मां राक्षसवंशनाशनं
यस्त्वं मुहूर्ताद् भविता विचेताः॥ १४४॥
verses.m: “Come, O lord of ogres! Don’t give way to despondency. I stand with my bow held firmly in my hand. Know me to be the destroyer of the ogre race. You too would be deprived of your life after a short while.” (144)

verses.text:
रामोऽयमिति विज्ञाय जहास विकृतस्वनम्।
अभ्यधावत संक्रुद्धो हरीन् विद्रावयन् रणे॥ १४५॥
verses.m: Coming to know that he was Śrī Rāma, the ogre laughed in an unnatural tone and rushed forward in great rage, scattering the monkeys on the battle-field. (145)

verses.text:
दारयन्निव सर्वेषां हृदयानि वनौकसाम्।
प्रहस्य विकृतं भीमं स मेघस्तनितोपमम्॥ १४६॥
कुम्भकर्णो महातेजा राघवं वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
नाहं विराधो विज्ञेयो न कबन्धः खरो न च।
न वाली न च मारीचः कुम्भकर्णः समागतः॥ १४७॥
verses.m: Heartily laughing in an unnatural and hideous way, producing a sound like the rumbling of a cloud, and, therefore, rending as it were the hearts of all the monkeys (lit., the dwellers in the wood s). Kumbhakarṇa, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, spoke to Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) as follows: “I should neither be accounted Virādha nor Kabandha nor Khara nor Vālī nor Mārica. It is Kumbhakarṇa arrived here. (146-147)

verses.text:
पश्य मे मुद्गरं भीमं सर्वं कालायसं महत्।
अनेन निर्जिता देवा दानवाश्च पुरा मया॥ १४८॥
verses.m: “Behold my dreadful and mighty club wrought entirely of iron. With this gods and demons were formely conquered by me. (148)

verses.text:
विकर्णनास इति मां नावज्ञातुं त्वमर्हसि।
स्वल्पापि हि न मे पीडा कर्णनासाविनाशनात्॥ १४९॥
verses.m: “You ought not to hold me in contempt in that I have been deprived of my nose and ears. Not the least pain is experienced by me due to the loss of my ears and nose.(149)

verses.text:
दर्शयेक्ष्वाकुशार्दूल वीर्यं गात्रेषु मेऽनघ।
ततस्त्वां भक्षयिष्यामि दृष्टपौरुषविक्रमम्॥ १५०॥
verses.m: “Exhibit your prowess on my limbs, O tiger among the Ikṣwākus! I shall then devour you as soon as your manliness and prowess have been witnessed (by me), O sinless warrior!” (150)

verses.text:
स कुम्भकर्णस्य वचो निशम्य
रामः सुपुङ्खान् विससर्ज बाणान्।
तैराहतो वज्रसमप्रवेगै-
र्न चुक्षुभे न व्यथते सुरारिः॥ १५१॥
verses.m: Hearing the braggadocio of Kumbhakarṇa, Śrī Rāma shot plumed arrows at him; struck with those arrows, which flew with tremendous speed, vying with the speed of lightning, Kumbhakarṇa (the enemy of gods) felt neither disturbed nor agonized. (151)

verses.text:
यैः सायकैः सालवरा निकृत्ता
वाली हतो वानरपुङ्गवश्च।
ते कुम्भकर्णस्य तदा शरीरं
वज्रोपमा न व्यथयाम्प्रचक्रुः॥ १५२॥
verses.m: Those very arrows by which the foremost of sal trees were cut down and Vālī, a veritable bull among the monkeys, killed, and which vied with the thunderbolt in velocity did not cause much pain and discomfort to the body of Kumbhakarṇa on that occasion. (152)

verses.text:
स वारिधारा इव सायकांस्तान्
पिबन् शरीरेण महेन्द्रशत्रुः।
जघान रामस्य शरप्रवेगं
व्याविध्य तं मुद्गरमुग्रवेगम्॥ १५३॥
verses.m: Drinking up through his body those aforesaid arrows as a mountain would drink up so many torrents of water, nay, flourishing his afore-mentioned club with terrible speed, Kumbhakarṇa (the enemy of the mighty Indra), obstructed the tremendous speed of Śrī Rāma’s arrows. (153)

verses.text:
ततस्तु रक्षः क्षतजानुलिप्तं
वित्रासनं देवमहाचमूनाम्।
व्याविध्य तं मुद्गरमुग्रवेगं
विद्रावयामास चमूं हरीणाम्॥ १५४॥
verses.m: Brandishing with fearful speed the aforesaid club, which caused terror to the mighty celestial forces and was smeared with blood, the ogre, for his part, scattered the army of the monkeys. (154)

verses.text:
वायव्यमादाय ततोऽपरास्त्रं
रामः प्रचिक्षेप निशाचराय।
समुद्गरं तेन जहार बाहुं
स कृत्तबाहुस्तुमुलं ननाद॥ १५५॥
verses.m: Taking up another mystic missile, presided over by the wind-god, Śrī Rāma then shot it against the prowler of the night, severed with it his right arm with which he held the mace. His arm thus cut off, the ogre let out an uproarious cry. (155)

verses.text:
स तस्य बाहुर्गिरिशृङ्गकल्पः
समुद्गरो राघवबाणकृत्तः।
पपात तस्मिन् हरिराजसैन्ये
जघान तां वानरवाहिनीं च॥ १५६॥
verses.m: Severed by the arrow of Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, that arm of Kumbhakarṇa, which resembled a mountain-peak fell alongwith the mace on the army of Śugrīva, the king of monkeys, and killed well-nigh a regiment of the monkeys. (156)

verses.text:
ते वानरा भग्नहतावशेषाः
पर्यन्तमाश्रित्य तदा विषण्णाः।
प्रपीडिताङ्गा ददृशुः सुघोरं
नरेन्द्ररक्षोऽधिपसंनिपातम् ॥ १५७॥
verses.m: Taking their stand by the side of the fallen arm, those monkeys who had escaped being mutilated or killed by that arm, although their limbs had all the same been squeezed by the impact of the arm and who were feeling despondent, witnessed at that moment the most terrible combat of Śrī Rāma, a ruler of men, and Kumbhakarṇa, the overlord of the ogres. (157)

verses.text:
स कुम्भकर्णोऽस्त्रनिकृत्तबाहु-
र्महासिकृत्ताग्र इवाचलेन्द्रः।
उत्पाटयामास करेण वृक्षं
ततोऽभिदुद्राव रणे नरेन्द्रम्॥ १५८॥
verses.m: With his arm torn off by the missile, the said Kumbhakarṇa looked like a huge mountain whose summit had been cloven with a big sword. He tore up a palmyra tree with his other arm and then rushed towards Śrī Rāma, a ruler of men, on the field of battle. (158)

verses.text:
तं तस्य बाहुं सहतालवृक्षं
समुद्यतं पन्नगभोगकल्पम्।
ऐन्द्रास्त्रयुक्तेन जघान रामो
बाणेन जाम्बूनदचित्रितेन॥ १५९॥
verses.m: With an arrow decked with gold and charged with a mystic missile presided ever by Indra (the ruler of gods), Śrī Rāma severed his uplifted arm, which held the palmyra tree and looked like the coils of a serpent. (159)

verses.text:
स कुम्भकर्णस्य भुजो निकृत्तः
पपात भूमौ गिरिसंनिकाशः।
विचेष्टमानो निजघान वृक्षा-
ञ्शैलाञ्शिलावानरराक्षसांश्च ॥ १६०॥
verses.m: When torn off, that arm of Kumbhakarṇa which resembled a mountain (in size), fell tossing about on the ground and crushed under its weight many trees, crags, rocks, monkeys and ogres, even as it fell. (160)

verses.text:
तं छिन्नबाहुं समवेक्ष्य रामः
समापतन्तं सहसा नदन्तम्।
द्वावर्धचन्द्रौ निशितौ प्रगृह्य
चिच्छेद पादौ युधि राक्षसस्य॥ १६१॥
verses.m: Beholding him rushing violently all at once with a roar, both his arms severed, and seizing hold of two sharp crescent shaped arrows Śrī Rāma severed the ogre’s feet as well on the battle-field. (161)

verses.text:
तौ तस्य पादौ प्रदिशो दिशश्च
गिरेर्गुहाश्चैव महार्णवं च।
लङ्कां च सेनां कपिराक्षसानां
विनादयन्तौ विनिपेततुश्च॥ १६२॥
verses.m: The feet of the ogre also precipitately fell down, making the four quarters as well as the four intermediate corners, nay, even the caves of the Trikūta mountain as also the vast sea, the city of Laṅka and the armies of the monkeys and ogres resound with the thud. (162)

verses.text:
निकृत्तबाहुर्विनिकृत्तपादो
विदार्य वक्त्रं वडवामुखाभम्।
दुद्राव रामं सहसाभिगर्जन्
राहुर्यथा चन्द्रमिवान्तरिक्षे॥ १६३॥
verses.m: Dilating his mouth, incandescent as the submarine fire, the ogre, who had his arms torn off and his feet, too, severed, rushed vehemently, raising savage cries, towards Śrī Rāma, even as Rāhu would towards the full-moon in the sky. (163)

verses.text:
अपूरयत् तस्य मुखं शिताग्रै
रामः शरैर्हेमपिनद्धपुङ्खैः।
सम्पूर्णवक्त्रो न शशाक वक्तुं
चुकूज कृच्छ्रेण मुमूर्च्छ चापि॥ १६४॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma filled his mouth with sharp-pointed arrows provided with gold-encrusted shafts. With his mouth fully packed, he could not speak and even moaned with difficulty and swooned too. (164)

verses.text:
अथाददे सूर्यमरीचिकल्पं
स ब्रह्मदण्डान्तककालकल्पम्।
अरिष्टमैन्द्रं निशितं सुपुङ्खं
रामः शरं मारुततुल्यवेगम्॥ १६५॥
verses.m: The celebrated Śrī Rāma now took up a sharpened arrow with charming feathers, which was effulgent as a sunbeam, nay, which resembled the rod of Brahmā, the creator, and the destructive Kāla (Time-Spirit), was fatal to the enemies, was charged with a missile presided over by Indra, the ruler of gods, and vied with the wind in speed. (165)

verses.text:
तं वज्रजाम्बूनदचारुपुङ्खं
प्रदीप्तसूर्यज्वलनप्रकाशम्।
महेन्द्रवज्राशनितुल्यवेगं
रामः प्रचिक्षेप निशाचराय॥ १६६॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma discharged against the prowler of the night that arrow, whose shaft was inlaid with diamonds and gold, nay, which was brilliant as the dazzling sun and fire set ablaze and which resembled the thunderbolt of the mighty Indra, and the weapon Aśani. (166)

verses.text:
स सायको राघवबाहुचोदितो
दिशःस्वभासा दश सम्प्रकाशयन्।
विधूमवैश्वानरभीमदर्शनो
जगाम शक्राशनिभीमविक्रमः॥ १६७॥
verses.m: Illumining the ten directions with its effulgence, the aforesaid arrow, propelled by the arm of Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, which was formidable of aspect like a smokeless fire, flew with terrific speed, which vied with the thunderbolt of Indra, the ruler of gods. (167)

verses.text:
स तन्महापर्वतकूटसंनिभं
सुवृत्तदंष्ट्रं चलचारुकुण्डलम्।
चकर्त रक्षोऽधिपतेः शिरस्तदा
यथैव वृत्रस्य पुरा पुरंदरः॥ १६८॥
verses.m: The aforesaid arrow immediately tore off the well-known head of Kumbhakarṇa (the overlord of ogres), which closely resembled the peak of a huge mountain, was distinguished by beautifully globular teeth and swinging lovely earrings, even as Indra (the destroyer of citadels) severed the head of Vṛtra in the hoary past. (168)

verses.text:
कुम्भकर्णशिरो भाति कुण्डलालंकृतं महत्।
आदित्येऽभ्युदिते रात्रौ मध्यस्थ इव चन्द्रमाः॥ १६९॥
verses.m: Adorned with a pair of earrings, Kumbhakarṇa’s enormous head shone like the moon located in mid heavens when the constellation Punarvasu (presided over by Aditi, the mother of gods and consisting of twin-stars) has risen at the close of night. (169)

verses.text:
तद् रामबाणाभिहतं पपात
रक्षःशिरः पर्वतसंनिकाशम्।
बभञ्ज चर्यागृहगोपुराणि
प्राकारमुच्चं तमपातयच्च॥ १७०॥
verses.m: Torn off by Śrī Rāma’s arrow, the aforesaid head of the ogre, which closely resembled the peak of a mountain, fell down and demolished the buildings on the king’s highway as well as their gates and pulled down the high defensive wall (even as it fell). (170)

verses.text:
तच्चातिकायं हिमवत् प्रकाशं
रक्षस्तदा तोयनिधौ पपात।
ग्राहान् परान् मीनवरान् भुजंगमान्
ममर्द भूमिं च तथा विवेश॥ १७१॥
verses.m: And the colonel ogre (himself) who shone like the Himālaya mountain (in size) forthwith fell into the sea. There it crushed under its weight the principal alligators, the foremost of fishes and aquatic serpents and entered the bowels of the earth. (171)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् हते ब्राह्मणदेवशत्रौ
महाबले संयति कुम्भकर्णे।
चचाल भूर्भूमिधराश्च सर्वे
हर्षाच्च देवास्तुमुलं प्रणेदुः॥ १७२॥
verses.m: The aforesaid Kumbhakarṇa, the enemy of the Brāhmanas and gods, who was endowed with extraordinary might, having been killed in combat, the earth as well as all the mountains shook and the gods raised an uproarious shout of joy. (172)

verses.text:
ततस्तु देवर्षिमहर्षिपन्नगाः
सुराश्च भूतानि सुपर्णगुह्यकाः।
सयक्षगन्धर्वगणा नभोगताः
प्रहर्षिता रामपराक्रमेण॥ १७३॥
verses.m: Thereupon celestial sages, eminent Ṛṣis (the seers of Vedic Mantras) and serpents as also gods, genii, Suparṇas (a class of bird-like beings of a semi-divine character), Guhyakas (another class of demi-gods) including hosts of Yakṣas and Gandharvas (celestial musicians) standing in the air felt highly rejoiced at the prowess of Śrī Rāma. (173)

verses.text:
ततस्तु ते तस्य वधेन भूरिणा
मनस्विनो नैर्ऋतराजबान्धवाः।
विनेदुरुच्चैर्व्यथिता रघूत्तमं
हरिं समीक्ष्यैव यथा मतंगजाः॥ १७४॥
verses.m: At the very sight of Śrī Rāma, the foremost of the Raghus, the well-known kinsfolk of Rāvaṇa (the king of ogres) for their part, who, though resolute of mind, were pained by the momentous fall of Kumbhakarṇa, and let out loud cries even as elephants would at the sight of a lion. (174)

verses.text:
स देवलोकस्य तमो निहत्य
सूर्यो यथा राहुमुखाद् विमुक्तः।
तथा व्यभासीद्धरिसैन्यमध्ये
निहत्य रामो युधि कुम्भकर्णम्॥ १७५॥
verses.m: Having made short work of Kumbhakarṇa in combat, the celebrated Śrī Rāma shone brightly in the midst of the simian ranks in the same way as the sun would when delivered from the mouth of Rāhu, after dispersing the darkness of the celestial world. (175)

verses.text:
प्रहर्षमीयुर्बहवश्च वानराः
प्रबुद्धपद्मप्रतिमैरिवाननैः।
अपूजयन् राघवमिष्टभागिनं
हते रिपौ भीमबले नृपात्मजम्॥ १७६॥
verses.m: Numerous monkeys, who were distinguished by faces resembling full-blown lotuses, experienced great joy on an enemy endowed with terrible might having been got rid of, and extolled Prince Rāma, who had achieved their desired end. (176)

verses.text:
स कुम्भकर्णं सुरसैन्यमर्दनं
महत्सु युद्धेषु कदाचनाजितम्।
ननन्द हत्वा भरताग्रजो रणे
महासुरं वृत्रमिवामराधिपः॥ १७७॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma, the elder brother of Bharata,felt rejoiced on having disposed of in combat Kumbhakarṇa, the destroyer of celestial armies, who had never been conquered in major conflicts, even as Indra, the suzerain lord of gods, did on making short work of the mighty demon, Vṛtra. (177)

verses.text:
कुम्भकर्णं हतं दृष्ट्वा राघवेण महात्मना।
राक्षसा राक्षसेन्द्राय रावणाय न्यवेदयन्॥ १॥
verses.m: Seeing Kumbhakarṇa killed by the the high-souled Śrī Rāma. the ogres present on the field of battle reported the matter in the following words to Rāvaṇa, the ruler of ogres: (1)

verses.text:
राजन् स कालसंकाशः संयुक्तः कालकर्मणा।
विद्राव्य वानरीं सेनां भक्षयित्वा च वानरान्॥ २॥
प्रतपित्वा मुहूर्तं तु प्रशान्तो रामतेजसा।
कायेनार्धप्रविष्टेन समुद्रं भीमदर्शनम्॥ ३॥
निकृत्तनासाकर्णेन विक्षरद्रुधिरेण च।
रुद्ध्वा द्वारं शरीरेण लङ्कायाः पर्वतोपमः॥ ४॥
कुम्भकर्णस्तव भ्राता काकुत्स्थशरपीडितः।
अगण्डभूतो विवृतो दावदग्ध इव द्रुमः॥ ५॥
verses.m: ‘Having scattered the simian ranks and devoured the monkeys and exhibited his prowess for a space, O king, Kumbhakarṇa, who vied with Yama (the god of retribution) has been claimed by death. Tormented by the arrows of Rāma (a scion of Kākutstha), nay, quelled by his superior strength, your celebrated younger brother, Kumbhakarṇa for his part, who resembled a mountain in size, lies reduced to a headless and limbless mass, resembling a tree scorched by a forest conflagration, with his trunk half submerged in the terrible-looking sea and blocking the main gate of Laṅka with his head, which has its nose and ears lopped off and from which blood is streaming profusely.” (2—5)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा विनिहतं संख्ये कुम्भकर्णं महाबलम्।
रावणः शोकसंतप्तो मुमोह च पपात च॥ ६॥
verses.m: Tormented with grief on hearing of Kumbhakarṇa, who was endowed with extraordinary might, having been struck down dead in combat, Rāvaṇa fainted and sank down. (6)

verses.text:
पितृव्यं निहतं श्रुत्वा देवान्तकनरान्तकौ।
त्रिशिराश्चातिकायश्च रुरुदुः शोकपीडिताः॥ ७॥
verses.m: Afflicted with grief on hearing of their uncle having been killed, Rāvaṇa’s sons, Devāntaka and Narāntaka, Triśira and Atikāya too burst into a wail. (7)

verses.text:
भ्रातरं निहतं श्रुत्वा रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा।
महोदरमहापार्श्वौ शोकाक्रान्तौ बभूवतुः॥ ८॥
verses.m: Rāvaṇa’s half-brothers, Mahodara and Mahāpārśwa were overwhelmed with grief on hearing of their half-borther, Kumbhakarṇa, having been killed by Śrī Rāma of unwearied action. (8)

verses.text:
ततः कृच्छ्रात् समासाद्य संज्ञां राक्षसपुङ्गवः।
कुम्भकर्णवधाद् दीनो विललापाकुलेन्द्रियः॥ ९॥
verses.m: Regaining consciousness with difficulty, Rāvaṇa (a bull among the ogres), who felt miserable due to Kumbhakarṇa’s fall, then began to wail as follows, distracted in mind as he was: (9)

verses.text:
हा वीर रिपुदर्पघ्न कुम्भकर्ण महाबल।
त्वं मां विहाय वै दैवाद् यातोऽसि यमसादनम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Alas, having deserted me, O heroic Kumbhakarṇa who crushed the pride of your enemies and were endowed with extraordinary might, you have, by divine will, actually departed to the abode of Death! (10)

verses.text:
मम शल्यमनुद्धृत्य बान्धवानां महाबल।
शत्रुसैन्यं प्रताप्यैकः क्व मां संत्यज्य गच्छसि॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Having tormented the hostile army and leaving me, whither are you going alone without extracting the thorn from my side as well as from that of my kinsfolk, O ogre endowed with extraordinary might? (11)

verses.text:
इदानीं खल्वहं नास्मि यस्य मे पतितो भुजः।
दक्षिणोऽयं समाश्रित्य न बिभेमि सुरासुरात्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Surely, I shall no longer survive now that this right arm of mine, depending on whom I had no fear of any god or demon, has fallen. (12)

verses.text:
कथमेवंविधो वीरो देवदानवदर्पहा।
कालाग्निप्रतिमो ह्यद्य राघवेण रणे हतः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “I wonder how such a warrior, who quelled the pride of the gods and the demons alike and who resembled the fire of destruction at the time of universal dissolution, has been killed in combat by Rāma today. (13)

verses.text:
यस्य ते वज्रनिष्पेषो न कुर्याद् व्यसनं सदा।
स कथं रामबाणार्तः प्रसुप्तोऽसि महीतले॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Afflicted by the arrows of Rāma, how are you, the celebrated warrior, whom not even a stroke of lightning ever caused any harm, lying buried in eternal sleep on the earth’s surface? (14)

verses.text:
एते देवगणाः सार्धमृषिभिर्गगने स्थिताः।
निहतं त्वां रणे दृष्ट्वा निनदन्ति प्रहर्षिताः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Standing in space greatly delighted to see you killed in battle, the yonder hosts of gods alongwith Ṛṣis are raising a shout of applause. (15)

verses.text:
ध्रुवमद्यैव संहृष्टा लब्धलक्षाः प्लवंगमाः।
आरोक्ष्यन्तीह दुर्गाणि लङ्काद्वाराणि सर्वशः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Highly rejoiced on having found a suitable opportunity, the monkeys will on this occasion assuredly scale this very day the gates of Laṅkā, which were difficult of access heretofore, on all sides. (16)

verses.text:
राज्येन नास्ति मे कार्यं किं करिष्यामि सीतया।
कुम्भकर्णविहीनस्य जीविते नास्ति मे मतिः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “No purpose of mine will be served any longer by a kingdom and what shall I do with Sītā? Nay, bereft of Kumbhakarṇa, I have no mind even to preserve my life. (17)

verses.text:
यद्यहं भ्रातृहन्तारं न हन्मि युधि राघवम्।
ननु मे मरणं श्रेयो न चेदं व्यर्थजीवितम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “If I do not kill in combat Rāma (a scion of Raghu), the destroyer of my brother, surely death is best for me; but in no case this life has no meaning for me now. (18)

verses.text:
अद्यैव तं गमिष्यामि देशं यत्रानुजो मम।
नहि भ्रातॄन् समुत्सृज्य क्षणं जीवितुमुत्सहे॥ १९॥
verses.m: “I shall proceed this very day to that region where my younger brother, Kumbhakarṇa, is. Indeed, sending away my brothers, I dare not survive even for an instant. (19)

verses.text:
देवा हि मां हसिष्यन्ति दृष्ट्वा पूर्वापकारिणम्।
कथमिन्द्रं जयिष्यामि कुम्भकर्ण हते त्वयि॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Surely on seeing me, who have wronged them in the past, the gods will mock me. Now that you have been killed, how shall I, O Kumbhakarṇa, be able to conquer Indra, the ruler of gods? (20)

verses.text:
तदिदं मामनुप्राप्तं विभीषणवचः शुभम्।
यदज्ञानान्मया तस्य न गृहीतं महात्मनः॥ २१॥
verses.m: “This calamity, which was adumbrated by that high-souled Vibhiṣaṇa, has fallen upon me only because his wholesome advice was not accepted by me through ignorance. (21)

verses.text:
विभीषणवचस्तावत् कुम्भकर्णप्रहस्तयोः।
विनाशोऽयं समुत्पन्नो मां व्रीडयति दारुणः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Ever since the cruel end of Kumbhakarṇa and Prahasta came about the other day, the admonition of Vibhīṣaṇa is making me blush. (22)

verses.text:
तस्यायं कर्मणः प्राप्तो विपाको मम शोकदः।
यन्मया धार्मिकः श्रीमान् स निरस्तो विभीषणः॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Since the pious and fortunate Vibhīṣaṇa was expelled by me, this bitter fruit of that action, which is a source of grief, has come to me.” (23)

verses.text:
इति बहुविधमाकुलान्तरात्मा
कृपणमतीव विलप्य कुम्भकर्णम्।
न्यपतदपि दशाननो भृशार्त-
स्तमनुजमिन्द्ररिपुं हतं विदित्वा॥ २४॥
verses.m: Having thus lamented piteously and profusely in various ways on coming to know of his aforesaid younger brother, Kumbhakarṇa, an enemy of Indra, having been killed, Rāvaṇa (the ten-headed monster), whose inmost mind was agitated, sank down sore distressed. (24)

verses.text:
एवं विलपमानस्य रावणस्य दुरात्मनः।
श्रुत्वा शोकाभिभूतस्य त्रिशिरा वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Hearing the utterance of the evil-minded Rāvaṇa, who was lamenting as aforesaid, overcome as he was with grief, Triśirā (one of his sons) submitted as follows: (1)

verses.text:
एवमेव महावीर्यो हतो नस्तातमध्यमः।
न तु सत्पुरुषा राजन् विलपन्ति यथा भवान्॥ २॥
verses.m: “It is quite true that Kumbhakarṇa (the middle of our father and uncles), who was endowed with extraordinary prowess, has been killed. Good men, however, do not wail as you are doing, O king! (2)

verses.text:
नूनं त्रिभुवनस्यापि पर्याप्तस्त्वमसि प्रभो।
स कस्मात् प्राकृत इव शोचस्यात्मानमीदृशम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Surely you are capable of conquering even the three worlds. O lord! As such why do you, like a common man, allow yourself to be overwhelmed with grief in this way? (3)

verses.text:
ब्रह्मदत्तास्ति ते शक्तिः कवचं सायको धनुः।
सहस्रखरसंयुक्तो रथो मेघसमस्वनः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “A javelin bestowed on you by Brahmā (the creator), nay, a coat of mail, an arrow, a bow, all gifted by Brahmā as well as a chariot provided with a thousand donkeys and emitting a sound resembling the rumbling of a cloud, still continue in your possession. (4)

verses.text:
त्वयासकृद्धि शस्त्रेण विशस्ता देवदानवाः।
स सर्वायुधसम्पन्नो राघवं शास्तुमर्हसि॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Gods and Dānavas (giants) have actually been killed by you with a single weapon more than once. As such you can chastise Rāma when equipped with all sorts of weapons. (5)

verses.text:
कामं तिष्ठ महाराज निर्गमिष्याम्यहं रणे।
उद्धरिष्यामि ते शत्रून् गरुडः पन्नगानिव॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Stay on in Laṅkā if you will, O great king! I will sally forth to the field of battle and root out your enemies, even as Garuḍa, the king of birds, would uproot serpents. (6)

verses.text:
शम्बरो देवराजेन नरको विष्णुना यथा।
तथाद्य शयिता रामो मया युधि निपातितः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Struck down by me on the battle-field, Rāma shall fall this day in the same way as did the demon, Śambara, overthrown by Indra (the ruler of gods) and Naraka* by Lord Viṣṇu.” (7)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा त्रिशिरसो वाक्यं रावणो राक्षसाधिपः।
पुनर्जातमिवात्मानं मन्यते कालचोदितः॥ ८॥
verses.m: Hearing the assurance of Triśirā, Rāvaṇa, the suzerain lord of ogres, as impelled by Destiny, thought himself as though born anew. (8)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा त्रिशिरसो वाक्यं देवान्तकनरान्तकौ।
अतिकायश्च तेजस्वी बभूवुर्युद्धहर्षिताः॥ ९॥
verses.m: Hearing the speech of Triśirā, Devāntaka and Narāntaka as also Atikāya, who was full of martial ardour, got impatient for an encounter. (9)

verses.text:
ततोऽहमहमित्येवं गर्जन्तो नैर्ऋतर्षभाः।
रावणस्य सुता वीराः शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमाः॥ १०॥
verses.m: Thereupon the valiant sons of Rāvaṇa, who were veritable bulls among the ogres and equalled Indra, the ruler of gods, in prowess, stood roaring with the words “I will lead! I will take the lead!!” (10)

verses.text:
अन्तरिक्षगताः सर्वे सर्वे मायाविशारदाः।
सर्वे त्रिदशदर्पघ्नाः सर्वे समरदुर्मदाः॥ ११॥
verses.m: All were capable of coursing in the air, all were adept in conjuring tricks, all were able to crush the pride of gods and all were fierce in combat. (11)

verses.text:
सर्वे सुबलसम्पन्नाः सर्वे विस्तीर्णकीर्तयः।
सर्वे समरमासाद्य न श्रूयन्ते स्म निर्जिताः॥ १२॥
देवैरपि सगन्धर्वैः सकिंनरमहोरगैः।
सर्वेऽस्त्रविदुषो वीराः सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः।
सर्वे प्रवरविज्ञानाः सर्वे लब्धवरास्तथा॥ १३॥
verses.m: All were richly endowed with great might, all enjoyed widespread renown. All were such as had never been heard of as vanquished even by gods accompanied by Gandharvas (celestial musicians) and united with Kinnaras (another class of demigods credited with a human figure and the head of a horse or with a horse’s body and head of a man) on reaching the battlefield. All were adept in the use of mystic missiles and were heroic, all were skilled in warfare, all were endowed with great wisdom of the scriptures and all had received boons by virtue of their austerities. (12-13)

verses.text:
स तैस्तथा भास्करतुल्यवर्चसैः
सुतैर्वृतः शत्रुबलश्रियार्दनैः।
रराज राजा मघवान् यथामरै-
र्वृतो महादानवदर्पनाशनैः॥ १४॥
verses.m: Surrounded as aforesaid by his said sons, who vied with the sun in brilliance and were capable of crushing the might and glory of the enemy, King Rāvaṇa shone as Indra, surrounded by immortals, capable of quelling the vanity of mighty Dānavas. (14)

verses.text:
स पुत्रान् सम्परिष्वज्य भूषयित्वा च भूषणैः।
आशीर्भिश्च प्रशस्ताभिः प्रेषयामास वै रणे॥ १५॥
verses.m: Closely embracing his aforesaid sons, nay, decking them with ornaments and enriching them with auspicious benedictions, he actually sent them out for an encounter. (15)

verses.text:
युद्धोन्मत्तं च मत्तं च भ्रातरौ चापि रावणः।
रक्षणार्थं कुमाराणां प्रेषयामास संयुगे॥ १६॥
verses.m: He also dispatched his two brothers, Yuddhonmatta (better known as Mahāpārśwa) and Matta (more familiarly known as Mahodara) to the field of battle for the defence of the princes. (16)

verses.text:
तेऽभिवाद्य महात्मानं रावणं लोकरावणम्।
कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणं चैव महाकायाः प्रतस्थिरे॥ १७॥
verses.m: Saluting the gigantic Rāvaṇa, (who made people screem with terror) and also walking clockwise about him as a token of submission, those colossal warriors departed for the battle-field. (17)

verses.text:
सर्वौषधीभिर्गन्धैश्च समालभ्य महाबलाः।
निर्जग्मुर्नैर्ऋतश्रेष्ठाः षडेते युद्धकाङ्क्षिणः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Anointing themselves with all the ten medicinal herbs (credited with the property of warding off injury caused by weapons) as well as with perfumes, the following six jewels among the ogres, who were endowed with extraordinary might, and longed for a fight, sallied forth: (18)

verses.text:
त्रिशिराश्चातिकायश्च देवान्तकनरान्तकौ।
महोदरमहापार्श्वौ निर्जग्मुः कालचोदिताः॥ १९॥
verses.m: Triśirā and Atikāya, Devāntaka and Narāntaka, Mahodara and Mahāpārśwa set out under the sway of destiny. (19)

verses.text:
ततः सुदर्शनं नागं नीलजीमूतसंनिभम्।
ऐरावतकुले जातमारुरोह महोदरः॥ २०॥
verses.m: Thereupon Mahodara mounted an elephant, Sudarśana by name, closely resembling a dark cloud in hue and born in the race of Airāvata, the transport of Indra, the ruler of gods. (20)

verses.text:
सर्वायुधसमायुक्तस्तूणीभिश्चाप्यलंकृतः।
रराज गजमास्थाय सवितेवास्तमूर्धनि॥ २१॥
verses.m: Taking his seat on the elephant, nay, equipped with all kinds of weapons and furnished with quivers too, he shone like the sun on the summit of the western mountain and as such about to disappear. (21)

verses.text:
हयोत्तमसमायुक्तं सर्वायुधसमाकुलम्।
आरुरोह रथश्रेष्ठं त्रिशिरा रावणात्मजः॥ २२॥
verses.m: Triśirā, sprung from the loins of Rāvaṇa, ascended an excellent chariot drawn by the best of horses and fully equipped with all kinds of weapons. (22)

verses.text:
त्रिशिरा रथमास्थाय विरराज धनुर्धरः।
सविद्युदुल्कः सज्वालः सेन्द्रचाप इवाम्बुदः॥ २३॥
verses.m: Taking his seat in the chariot, Triśirā, who carried a bow, shone brightly like a rainy cloud attended by lightning, meteors, light and rainbow. (23)

verses.text:
त्रिभिः किरीटैस्त्रिशिराः शुशुभे स रथोत्तमे।
हिमवानिव शैलेन्द्रस्त्रिभिः काञ्चनपर्वतैः॥ २४॥
verses.m: With his three diadems adorning his three heads, Triśirā shone in his excellent chariot like the Himālaya, the lord of mountains, with its three golden offshoots constituting its peaks. (24)

verses.text:
अतिकायोऽतितेजस्वी राक्षसेन्द्रसुतस्तदा।
आरुरोह रथश्रेष्ठं श्रेष्ठः सर्वधनुष्मताम्॥ २५॥
सुचक्राक्षं सुसंयुक्तं स्वनुकर्षं सुकूबरम्।
तूणीबाणासनैर्दीप्तं प्रासासिपरिघाकुलम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: Then Atikāya another son of Rāvaṇa (the ruler of ogres), the foremost of all archers, who was full of exceeding martial ardour, mounted his superb chariot with excellent wheels and axles, magnificent horses, strong Anukarṣas (axle-trees) and stout Kūbaras (poles to which the yoke is fixed), nay, radiant with quivers and bows and fully furnished with spears, swords and clubs studded or tipped with iron. (25-26)

verses.text:
स काञ्चनविचित्रेण किरीटेन विराजता।
भूषणैश्च बभौ मेरुः प्रभाभिरिव भासयन्॥ २७॥
verses.m: With his sparkling coronet encrusted with gold and ornaments, he looked like Mount Meru shining in its own splendour. (27)

verses.text:
स रराज रथे तस्मिन् राजसूनुर्महाबलः।
वृतो नैर्ऋतशार्दूलैर्वज्रपाणिरिवामरैः॥ २८॥
verses.m: Surrounded by the foremost of ogres, the said prince, who was endowed with extraordinary might, shone in that chariot like Indra, who carries the thunderbolt in his hand, surrounded by immortals. (28)

verses.text:
हयमुच्चैःश्रवःप्रख्यं श्वेतं कनकभूषणम्।
मनोजवं महाकायमारुरोह नरान्तकः॥ २९॥
verses.m: Narāntaka ascended a huge white horse resembling Uccaihśravā, the mount of Indra, evolved out of the churning of the ocean of milk, nay, harnessed with gold and swift as thought. (29)

verses.text:
गृहीत्वा प्रासमुल्काभं विरराज नरान्तकः।
शक्तिमादाय तेजस्वी गुहः शिखिगतो यथा॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Holding a spear shining as a meteor, Narāntaka shone brightly like the glorious Kārtikeya, son of Lord Śiva mounted on his peacock taking a javelin in his hand. (30)

verses.text:
देवान्तकः समादाय परिघं हेमभूषणम्।
परिगृह्य गिरिं दोर्भ्यां वपुर्विष्णोर्विडम्बयन्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Firmly grasping his club tipped with iron and decked with gold, Devāntaka stood resembling the figure of Lord Viṣṇu holding (as he did) the Mandara mountain in His arms while proceeding to churn the ocean of milk for drawing out nectar. (31)

verses.text:
महापार्श्वो महातेजा गदामादाय वीर्यवान्।
विरराज गदापाणिः कुबेर इव संयुगे॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Bearing a mace, the valiant Mahāpārśwa, who was endowed with martial ardour, shone brightly like Kubera (the god of riches) standing mace in hand on the field of battle. (32)

verses.text:
ते प्रतस्थुर्महात्मानोऽमरावत्याः सुरा इव।
तान् गजैश्च तुरङ्गैश्च रथैश्चाम्बुदनिःस्वनैः॥ ३३॥
अनूत्पेतुर्महात्मानो राक्षसाः प्रवरायुधाः।
ते विरेजुर्महात्मानः कुमाराः सूर्यवर्चसः॥ ३४॥
किरीटिनः श्रिया जुष्टा ग्रहा दीप्ता इवाम्बरे।
प्रगृहीता बभौ तेषां शस्त्राणामवलिः सिता॥ ३५॥
शरदभ्रप्रतीकाशा हंसावलिरिवाम्बरे।
मरणं वापि निश्चित्य शत्रूणां वा पराजयम्॥ ३६॥
इति कृत्वा मतिं वीराः संजग्मुः संयुगार्थिनः।
जगर्जुश्च प्रणेदुश्च चिक्षिपुश्चापि सायकान्॥ ३७॥
जगृहुश्च महात्मानो निर्यान्तो युद्धदुर्मदाः।
क्ष्वेडितास्फोटितानां वै संचचालेव मेदिनी॥ ३८॥
रक्षसां सिंहनादैश्च संस्फोटितमिवाम्बरम्।
तेऽभिनिष्क्रम्य मुदिता राक्षसेन्द्रा महाबलाः॥ ३९॥
ददृशुर्वानरानीकं समुद्यतशिलानगम्।
हरयोऽपि महात्मानो ददृशू राक्षसं बलम्॥ ४०॥
हस्त्यश्वरथसम्बाधं किङ्किणीशतनादितम्।
नीलजीमूतसंकाशं समुद्यतमहायुधम्॥ ४१॥
verses.m: The aforesaid colossi sallied forth (from Laṅkā) as did gods from Amarāvatī (the city of immortals, the capital of heaven). Gigantic ogres armed with superb weapons rushed at their heels on the back of elephants and horses as well as in chariots, thundering like clouds. Wearing diadems on their heads, nay, resplendent as the sun and endowed with splendour, those colossal princes shone brightly like planets glowing in the heavens. The white row of weapons lightly grasped by them shone like a flock of cranes shining like autumnal clouds in the sky. Making up their mind either to embrace death positively or to rout the enemies, the champions proceeded in search of an encounter. While sallying forth, the colossi, who were fierce in combat, thundered and roared and seized arrows and also discharged them. The earth for its part violently shook as it were, thanks to their roars and their clapping of arms. Nay, the sky got breached as it were by the leonine roars of the ogres. Sallying forth with joy, those leaders of ogres, who were endowed with extraordinary might, beheld the simian army standing with uplifted rocks and trees. The gigantic monkeys too saw the army of ogres crowded with elephants, horses and chariots and rendered noisy by hundreds of circlets of tiny bells worn by their animals as well as by the ogres themselves, nay, resembling a mass of dark clouds and carrying huge uplifted weapons. (33—41)

verses.text:
दीप्तानलरविप्रख्यैर्नैर्ऋतैः सर्वतो वृतम्।
तद् दृष्ट्वा बलमायातं लब्धलक्षाः प्लवङ्गमाः॥ ४२॥
समुद्यतमहाशैलाः सम्प्रणेदुर्मुहुर्मुहुः।
अमृष्यमाणा रक्षांसि प्रतिनर्दन्त वानराः॥ ४३॥
verses.m: Seeing that army—flanked as it was on all sides by ogres, brilliant as a flaming fire or the sun—arrived, the monkeys, who had found an objective for their attack, thundered again and again with huge uplifted rocks in their hands. Intolerant of the roars of the ogres, the monkeys roared in return. (42-43)

verses.text:
ततः समुत्कृष्टरवं निशम्य
रक्षोगणा वानरयूथपानाम्।
अमृष्यमाणाः परहर्षमुग्रं
महाबला भीमतरं प्रणेदुः॥ ४४॥
verses.m: Hearing the exceptionally loud roar of the leaders of monkey troops, the ogre ranks, who were endowed with extraordinary might and could not brook the riotous festivity of their enemies, roared all the more fiercely. (44)

verses.text:
ते राक्षसबलं घोरं प्रविश्य हरियूथपाः।
विचेरुरुद्यतैः शैलैर्नगाः शिखरिणो यथा॥ ४५॥
verses.m: Penetrating deep into the formidable army of ogres, the leaders of monkey troops ranged with uplifted crags like mountains crowned with peaks. (45)

verses.text:
केचिदाकाशमाविश्य केचिदुर्व्यां प्लवङ्गमाः।
रक्षस्सैन्येषु संक्रुद्धाः केचिद् द्रुमशिलायुधाः॥ ४६॥
verses.m: Springing in the air, armed with trees and rocks, and feeling enraged at the ogre troops, some monkeys reconnoitred there, while seizing trees with huge stems, other bulls among monkeys ranged on the earth. The ferocious fight which ensued between the ogres and the monkeys was terrible. (46-47)

verses.text:
द्रुमांश्च विपुलस्कन्धान् गृह्य वानरपुङ्गवाः।
तद् युद्धमभवद् घोरं रक्षोवानरसंकुलम्॥ ४७॥
ते पादपशिलाशैलैश्चक्रुर्वृष्टिमनूपमाम्।
बाणौघैर्वार्यमाणाश्च हरयो भीमविक्रमाः॥ ४८॥
verses.m: While being intercepted by the ogres with volleys of arrows, the said monkeys of redoubtable prowess discharged an unparalleled shower of trees, rocks and crags. (48)

verses.text:
सिंहनादान् विनेदुश्च रणे राक्षसवानराः।
शिलाभिश्चूर्णयामासुर्यातुधानान् प्लवङ्गमाः॥ ४९॥
निर्जघ्नुः संयुगे क्रुद्धाः कवचाभरणावृतान्।
केचिद् रथगतान् वीरान् गजवाजिगतानपि॥ ५०॥
निर्जघ्नुः सहसाऽऽप्लुत्य यातुधानान् प्लवङ्गमाः।
शैलशृङ्गान्विताङ्गास्ते मुष्टिभिर्वान्तलोचनाः॥ ५१॥
चेलुः पेतुश्च नेदुश्च तत्र राक्षसपुङ्गवाः।
राक्षसाश्च शरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्बिभिदुः कपिकुञ्जरान्॥ ५२॥
शूलमुद्गरखड्गैश्च जघ्नुः प्रासैश्च शक्तिभिः।
अन्योन्यं पातयामासुः परस्परजयैषिणः॥ ५३॥
रिपुशोणितदिग्धाङ्गास्तत्र वानरराक्षसाः।
ततः शैलैश्च खड्गैश्च विसृष्टैर्हरिराक्षसैः॥ ५४॥
मुहूर्तेनावृता भूमिरभवच्छोणितोक्षिता।
विकीर्णैः पर्वताकारै रक्षोभिरभिमर्दितैः।
आसीद् वसुमती पूर्णा तदा युद्धमदान्वितैः॥ ५५॥
verses.m: Nay, the ogres and monkeys alike emitted leonine roars on the field of battle. Furious in combat, the monkeys pounded the ogres—who were clad in armour and decked with ornaments—with rocks and killed them. Springing up all of a sudden, some monkeys, for their part, killed the heroic ogres seated in their chariots and mounted on the back of elephants and horses. Their bodies covered by mountain-peaks, and eyes stuck out by the blows of fists of the monkeys, the foremost of the ogres on the battle-field staggered and fell and shrieked. The ogres too pierced the foremost among the monkeys with their sharp arrows and struck them with pikes, mallets and swords as also with lances and javelins. Their limbs stained with the blood of their enemies, the monkeys as well as the ogres, who were eager to conquer one another, struk one another down on the battle-field. In an instant thereupon the field of battle was covered with crags and swords thrown by the monkeys and the ogres, and got drenched with blood. The battle-field was at that time littered with ogres looking like mountains and drunk with martial ardour, who had been crushed by the monkeys and were lying scattered in pieces. (49—55)

verses.text:
आक्षिप्ताः क्षिप्यमाणाश्च भग्नशैलाश्च वानराः।
पुनरङ्गैस्तदा चक्रुरासन्ना युद्धमद्भुतम्॥ ५६॥
verses.m: Already thrown out of order and still being thrown out of order by the ogres, at that time, the monkeys, whose rocks had been shattered, once more put up a wonderful fight with their limbs alone at close quarters. (56)

verses.text:
वानरान् वानरैरेव जघ्नुस्ते नैर्ऋतर्षभाः।
राक्षसान् राक्षसैरेव जघ्नुस्ते वानरा अपि॥ ५७॥
verses.m: The aforesaid ogre chiefs struck the monkeys with other monkeys, while the said monkeys too struck the ogres with other ogres. (57)

verses.text:
आक्षिप्य च शिलाः शैलाञ्जघ्नुस्ते राक्षसास्तदा।
तेषां चाच्छिद्य शस्त्राणि जघ्नू रक्षांसि वानराः॥ ५८॥
verses.m: Nay, snatching the rocks and crags from the hands of the monkeys, the aforesaid ogres struck their enemies with them; and tearing the weapons of the ogres, the monkeys, in their turn, struck the ogres with them. (58)

verses.text:
निर्जघ्नुः शैलशृङ्गैश्च बिभिदुश्च परस्परम्।
सिंहनादान् विनेदुश्च रणे राक्षसवानराः॥ ५९॥
verses.m: On the field of battle the ogres as well as the monkeys struck one another with mountain-peaks, cut them asunder and emitted leonine roars. (59)

verses.text:
छिन्नवर्मतनुत्राणा राक्षसा वानरैर्हताः।
रुधिरं प्रसृतास्तत्र रससारमिव द्रुमाः॥ ६०॥
verses.m: Their shields and armours broken, the ogres struck by the monkeys shed blood profusely on the field of battle even as trees exude their sap. (60)

verses.text:
रथेन च रथं चापि वारणेनापि वारणम्।
हयेन च हयं केचिन्निर्जघ्नुर्वानरा रणे॥ ६१॥
verses.m: Nay, some monkeys struck down on the battle-field a chariot with another chariot, an elephant too with another elephant, and a horse with another horse. (61)

verses.text:
क्षुरप्रैरर्धचन्द्रैश्च भल्लैश्च निशितैः शरैः।
राक्षसा वानरेन्द्राणां बिभिदुः पादपान् शिलाः॥ ६२॥
verses.m: By means of their sharp arrows with a sharp horse-shoe-shaped head, those with a crescent-shaped head and those with a spear-like head, the ogres shattered the trees and rocks of monkey chiefs. (62)

verses.text:
विकीर्णाः पर्वतास्तैश्च द्रुमच्छिन्नैश्च संयुगे।
हतैश्च कपिरक्षोभिर्दुर्गमा वसुधाभवत्॥ ६३॥
verses.m: The earth became difficult to tread on, strewn as it was with mountains which had been thrown as also with trees which had been cut down and with the monkeys and ogres that had been killed. (63)

verses.text:
ते वानरा गर्वितहृष्टचेष्टाः
संग्राममासाद्य भयं विमुच्य।
युद्धं स्म सर्वे सह राक्षसैस्ते
नानायुधाश्चक्रुरदीनसत्त्वाः ॥ ६४॥
verses.m: Reaching the field of battle and leaving behind all fear, all the aforesaid monkeys, whose demeanour was full of pride and martial ardour, nay, who were armed with various weapons snatched from the ogres and their own in the shape of trees, rocks, teeth and nails and were ever undepressed in spirit, waged war with the ogres. (64)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् प्रवृत्ते तुमुले विमर्दे
प्रहृष्यमाणेषु वलीमुखेषु।
निपात्यमानेषु च राक्षसेषु
महर्षयो देवगणाश्च नेदुः॥ ६५॥
verses.m: While that tumultuous conflict going on, the monkeys were feeling exultant and the ogres were being struck down, the great Ṛsis and hosts of gods shouted joyously. (65)

verses.text:
ततो हयं मारुततुल्यवेग-
मारुह्य शक्तिं निशितां प्रगृह्य।
नरान्तको वानरसैन्यमुग्रं
महार्णवं मीन इवाविवेश॥ ६६॥
verses.m: Mounting his horse, swift as the wind, and tightly grasping his sharpened javelin, Narāntaka thereupon plunged into the formidable simian army even as a fish would enter the ocean. (66)

verses.text:
स वानरान् सप्त शतानि वीरः
प्रासेन दीप्तेन विनिर्बिभेद।
एकः क्षणेनेन्द्ररिपुर्महात्मा
जघान सैन्यं हरिपुङ्गवानाम्॥ ६७॥
verses.m: That gigantic champion pierced single-handed seven hundred monkeys with his effulgent spear. In this way that enemy of Indra (the ruler of gods) exterminated the army of the monkey chiefs in a trice. (67)

verses.text:
ददृशुश्च महात्मानं हयपृष्ठप्रतिष्ठितम्।
चरन्तं हरिसैन्येषु विद्याधरमहर्षयः॥ ६८॥
verses.m: Nay, Vidyādharas (heavenly artists) and great Ṛṣis saw the colossus moving in the midst of monkey troops, seated on horseback. (68)

verses.text:
स तस्य ददृशे मार्गो मांसशोणितकर्दमः।
पतितैः पर्वताकारैर्वानरैरभिसंवृतः॥ ६९॥
verses.m: The pathway carved out by him was found full of mire in the form of flesh and blood and covered with monkeys, resembling mountains that had fallen. (69)

verses.text:
यावद् विक्रमितुं बुद्धिं चक्रुः प्लवगपुङ्गवाः।
तावदेतानतिक्रम्य निर्बिभेद नरान्तकः॥ ७०॥
verses.m: Slipping past the monkey chiefs even as they thought of displaying their valour, Narāntaka clove their ranks. (70)

verses.text:
ज्वलन्तं प्रासमुद्यम्य संग्रामाग्रे नरान्तकः।
ददाह हरिसैन्यानि वनानीव विभावसुः॥ ७१॥
verses.m: Uplifting his flaming lance in the van of the battle, Narāntaka consumed the monkey troops even as fire would burn up forests. (71)

verses.text:
यावदुत्पाटयामासुर्वृक्षान् शैलान् वनौकसः।
तावत् प्रासहताः पेतुर्वज्रकृत्ता इवाचलाः॥ ७२॥
verses.m: Struck with his lance, the monkeys fell like mountains uprooted by lightning, even as they tore up trees and crags. (72)

verses.text:
दिक्षु सर्वासु बलवान् विचचार नरान्तकः।
प्रमृद्नन् सर्वतो युद्धे प्रावृट्काले यथानिलः॥ ७३॥
verses.m: Crushing down everything, the mighty Narāntaka ranged over the battle-field on all sides even as the wind in the rainy season. (73)

verses.text:
न शेकुर्धावितुं वीरा न स्थातुं स्पन्दितुं भयात्।
उत्पतन्तं स्थितं यान्तं सर्वान् विव्याध वीर्यवान्॥ ७४॥
verses.m: The monkey heroes could neither flee nor stand nor move through fear. The valiant ogre, Narāntaka, pierced all with his lance no matter whether one was springing up, stationary or moving. (74)

verses.text:
एकेनान्तककल्पेन प्रासेनादित्यतेजसा।
भग्नानि हरिसैन्यानि निपेतुर्धरणीतले॥ ७५॥
verses.m: Struck down by that one lance, which looked like Death and was bright as the sun, the simian ranks fell down on the earth’s surface. (75)

verses.text:
वज्रनिष्पेषसदृशं प्रासस्याभिनिपातनम्।
न शेकुर्वानराः सोढुं ते विनेदुर्महास्वनम्॥ ७६॥
verses.m: The monkeys could not stand the impact of the lance, which resembled the stroke of lightning. Hence they cried loudly. (76)

verses.text:
पततां हरिवीराणां रूपाणि प्रचकाशिरे।
वज्रभिन्नाग्रकूटानां शैलानां पततामिव॥ ७७॥
verses.m: The forms of the monkey heroes falling down shone brightly like the mountains which fell down even as their peaks were shattered by the thunderbolt of Indra. (77)

verses.text:
ये तु पूर्वं महात्मानः कुम्भकर्णेन पातिताः।
ते स्वस्था वानरश्रेष्ठाः सुग्रीवमुपतस्थिरे॥ ७८॥
verses.m: Those high-souled jewels among the monkeys, who for their part had been struck down by Kumbhakarṇa earlier, sought the presence of Sugrīva, now that they were their normal selves again. (78)

verses.text:
प्रेक्षमाणः स सुग्रीवो ददृशे हरिवाहिनीम्।
नरान्तकभयत्रस्तां विद्रवन्तीं यतस्ततः॥ ७९॥
verses.m: Looking all-round, the said Sugrīva saw the simian army running helter-skelter in all directions, stricken, as it was, with the fear of Narāntaka. (79)

verses.text:
विद्रुतां वाहिनीं दृष्ट्वा स ददर्श नरान्तकम्।
गृहीतप्रासमायान्तं हयपृष्ठप्रतिष्ठितम्॥ ८०॥
verses.m: Seeing the army in stampede, he now beheld Narāntaka, mounted on horseback, advancing with a lance held by him. (80)

verses.text:
दृष्ट्वोवाच महातेजाः सुग्रीवो वानराधिपः।
कुमारमङ्गदं वीरं शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमम्॥ ८१॥
verses.m: Perceiving him, Sugrīva, the suzerain lord of monkeys, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, spoke as follows to the gallant Prince, Aṅgada, a compeer of Indra, the ruler of gods, in prowess: (81)

verses.text:
गच्छैनं राक्षसं वीरं योऽसौ तुरगमास्थितः।
क्षोभयन्तं हरिबलं क्षिप्रं प्राणैर्वियोजय॥ ८२॥
verses.m: “March against the younder heroic ogre, striking terror into the simian army, I mean, the fellow who is seen mounted on the back of a horse over there, and speedily deprive him of his life-breath.” (82)

verses.text:
स भर्तुर्वचनं श्रुत्वा निष्पपाताङ्गदस्तदा।
अनीकान्मेघसंकाशादंशुमानिव वीर्यवान्॥ ८३॥
verses.m: Hearing the command of his master, the valiant Aṅgada rushed forth at once from his army, which resembled a huge cloud, even as the sun would break away from a cloud. (83)

verses.text:
शैलसंघातसंकाशो हरीणामुत्तमोऽङ्गदः।
रराजाङ्गदसंनद्धः सधातुरिव पर्वतः॥ ८४॥
verses.m: Adorned with armlets of gold, Angada, the foremost of monkeys, who closely resembled a mass of rocks, glittered like a mountain with its metallic veins. (84)

verses.text:
निरायुधो महातेजाः केवलं नखदंष्ट्रवान्।
नरान्तकमभिक्रम्य वालिपुत्रोऽब्रवीद् वचः॥ ८५॥
verses.m: Approaching Narāntaka, Aṅgada (son of Vālī), who, though endowed with extraordinary energy, was wholly unarmed except for his nails and teeth, spoke to him as follows: (85)

verses.text:
तिष्ठ किं प्राकृतैरेभिर्हरिभिस्त्वं करिष्यसि।
अस्मिन् वज्रसमस्पर्शं प्रासं क्षिप्र ममोरसि॥ ८६॥
verses.m: “Tarry! What will you do with these common monkeys? Throw your spear, whose impact is hard to bear like that of lightning, at this breast of mine.” (86)

verses.text:
अङ्गदस्य वचः श्रुत्वा प्रचुक्रोध नरान्तकः।
संदश्य दशनैरोष्ठं निःश्वस्य च भुजंगवत्।
अभिगम्याङ्गदं क्रुद्धो वालिपुत्रं नरान्तकः॥ ८७॥
verses.m: Hearing the challenge of Aṅgada, Narāntaka flew into a rage. Biting his lip with his teeth and hissing like a serpent, the furious Narāntaka stood facing Aṅgada, son of Vāli. (87)

verses.text:
स प्रासमाविध्य तदाङ्गदाय
समुज्ज्वलन्तं सहसोत्ससर्ज।
स वालिपुत्रोरसि वज्रकल्पे
बभूव भग्नो न्यपतच्च भूमौ॥ ८८॥
verses.m: Brandishing his flaming lance, he hurled it all of a sudden at Aṅgada. The spear, however, broke against the breast of Aṅgada (son of Vāli), which was hard as adamant, and fell to the ground. (88)

verses.text:
तं प्रासमालोक्य तदा विभग्नं
सुपर्णकृत्तोरगभोगकल्पम्।
तलं समुद्यम्य स वालिपुत्र-
स्तुरंगमस्याभिजघान मूर्ध्नि॥ ८९॥
verses.m: Seeing that lance shattered at that moment like the coils of a serpent sundered by Garuḍa of beautiful wings, and duly raising his palm, the aforesaid son of Vālī violently struck with it at the head of Narāntaka’s horse. (89)

verses.text:
निमग्नपादः स्फुटिताक्षितारो
निष्क्रान्तजिह्वोऽचलसंनिकाशः।
स तस्य वाजी निपपात भूमौ
तलप्रहारेण विकीर्णमूर्धा॥ ९०॥
verses.m: Its feet having sunk deep into the earth, the pupils of its eyes burst asunder, its tongue hung out and its skull smashed by the stroke of his palm, the said horse of Narāntaka, which looked like a mountain, fell to the ground. (90)

verses.text:
नरान्तकः क्रोधवशं जगाम
हतं तुरंगं पतितं समीक्ष्य।
स मुष्टिमुद्यम्य महाप्रभावो
जघान शीर्षे युधि वालिपुत्रम्॥ ९१॥
verses.m: Gazing on his horse fallen dead, Narāntaka flew into a rage. Raising his fist, the ogre, who was endowed with extraordinary might, struck Aṅgada (son of Valī) on his head on the field of battle. (91)

verses.text:
अथाङ्गदो मुष्टिविशीर्णमूर्धा
सुस्राव तीव्रं रुधिरं भृशोष्णम्।
मुहुर्विजज्वाल मुमोह चापि
संज्ञां समासाद्य विसिस्मिये च॥ ९२॥
verses.m: His skull having been smashed by the blow of the ogre’s fist, Aṅgada forthwith shed exceedingly hot blood profusely. He felt a burning sensation and also swooned now and again and, on regaining consciousness, felt wonder-struck. (92)

verses.text:
अथाङ्गदो मृत्युसमानवेगं
संवर्त्य मुष्टिं गिरिशृङ्गकल्पम्।
निपातयामास तदा महात्मा
नरान्तकस्योरसि वालिपुत्रः॥ ९३॥
verses.m: Clenching his fist, whose vehemence equalled the vehemence of Death, and which descended like a mountain-peak, Aṅgada, the high-souled son of Vālī, then immediately brought it down on Narāntaka’s breast.(93)

verses.text:
स मुष्टिनिर्भिन्ननिमग्नवक्षा
ज्वाला वमञ्शोणितदिग्धगात्रः।
नरान्तको भूमितले पपात
यथाचलो वज्रनिपातभग्नः॥ ९४॥
verses.m: His chest having been split asunder by the blow of Aṅgada’s fist and having sunk deep, and his limbs stained with blood, Narāntaka fell to the earth’s surface vomitting flaming blood like a mountain shattered by a stroke of lightning. (94)

verses.text:
तदान्तरिक्षे त्रिदशोत्तमानां
वनौकसां चैव महाप्रणादः।
बभूव तस्मिन् निहतेऽग्र्यवीर्ये
नरान्तके वालिसुतेन संख्ये॥ ९५॥
verses.m: When the aforesaid Narāntake, who was foremost in prowess, was killed by Aṅgada (son of Vālī) in the encounter, a great shout of joy rose from the foremost of gods in the heavens as well as from the monkeys on the battle-field. (95)

verses.text:
अथाङ्गदो राममनःप्रहर्षणं
सुदुष्करं तं कृतवान् हि विक्रमम्।
विसिस्मिये सोऽप्यथ भीमकर्मा
पुनश्च युद्धे स बभूव हर्षितः॥ ९६॥
verses.m: Aṅgada actually performed on this occassion the aforesaid feat of valour which was exceedingly difficult to perform and which brought excessive delight to the mind of Śrī Rāma, so much so that the latter too was struck with wonder. Nay, Aṅgada of terrific valiant deeds was infused with vigour once more for a fight. (96)

verses.text:
नरान्तकं हतं दृष्ट्वा चुक्रुशुर्नैर्ऋतर्षभाः।
देवान्तकस्त्रिमूर्धा च पौलस्त्यश्च महोदरः॥ १॥
verses.m: Seeing Narāntaka killed, Devāntaka and Triśirā, a scion of Pulasti, as well as Mahodara, who were veritable bulls among the ogres (scions of Nirṛti), cried. (1)

verses.text:
आरूढो मेघसंकाशं वारणेन्द्रं महोदरः।
वालिपुत्रं महावीर्यमभिदुद्राव वेगवान्॥ २॥
verses.m: Mounted on the foremost of elephants, which closely resembled a cloud, Mahodara, who was full of impetuosity, darted towards Aṅgada (son of Vālī), who was endowed with extraordinary prowess. (2)

verses.text:
भ्रातृव्यसनसंतप्तस्तदा देवान्तको बली।
आदाय परिघं घोरमङ्गदं समभिद्रवत्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Seizing a formidable club tipped with iron, the mighty Devāntaka, who felt distressed on account of the fall of his brother, Narāntaka, forthwith rushed straight towards Aṅgada. (3)

verses.text:
रथमादित्यसंकाशं युक्तं परमवाजिभिः।
आस्थाय त्रिशिरा वीरो वालिपुत्रमथाभ्यगात्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Taking his seat in a chariot effulgent as the sun and drawn by excellent horses, the valiant Triśirā too marched against Aṅgada (son of Vālī). (4)

verses.text:
स त्रिभिर्देवदर्पघ्नै राक्षसेन्द्रैरभिद्रुतः।
वृक्षमुत्पाटयामास महाविटपमङ्गदः॥ ५॥
verses.m: Attacked by the three ogre-chiefs, who were capable of crushing the pride of gods, the aforesaid Aṅgada pulled up a tree with mighty boughs. (5)

verses.text:
देवान्तकाय तं वीरश्चिक्षेप सहसाङ्गदः।
महावृक्षं महाशाखं शक्रो दीप्तामिवाशनिम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: The gallant Aṅgada precipitately hurled that huge tree with immense branches at Devāntaka even as Indra would hurl his flaming thunderbolt. (6)

verses.text:
त्रिशिरास्तं प्रचिच्छेद शरैराशीविषोपमैः।
स वृक्षं कृत्तमालोक्य उत्पपात तदाङ्गदः॥ ७॥
verses.m: Triśirā tore the tree into pieces with his arrows resembling venomous serpents. Seeing the tree severed, the said Aṅgada forthwith sprang up. (7)

verses.text:
स ववर्ष ततो वृक्षाञ्शिलाश्च कपिकुञ्जरः।
तान् प्रचिच्छेद संक्रुद्धस्त्रिशिरा निशितैः शरैः॥ ८॥
verses.m: That elephant among the monkeys thereupon showered trees and rocks. Getting enraged, Triśirā tore them into pieces with his whetted shafts. (8)

verses.text:
परिघाग्रेण तान् वृक्षान् बभञ्ज स महोदरः।
त्रिशिराश्चाङ्गदं वीरमभिदुद्राव सायकैः॥ ९॥
verses.m: The notorious Mahodara shattered those trees with the head of his club, while Triśirā attacked the heroic Aṅgada with his arrows. (9)

verses.text:
गजेन समभिद्रुत्य वालिपुत्रं महोदरः।
जघानोरसि संक्रुद्धस्तोमरैर्वज्रसंनिभैः॥ १०॥
verses.m: Hotly pursuing, on the back of his elephant, the son of Vālī, Mahodara struck him in the breast with clubs, which flashed as lightning, enraged as he was. (10)

verses.text:
देवान्तकश्च संक्रुद्धः परिघेण तदाङ्गदम्।
उपगम्याभिहत्याशु व्यपचक्राम वेगवान्॥ ११
verses.m: Approaching Aṅgada and striking him with his club, infuriated as he was, the agile Devāntaka quickly retreated. (11)

verses.text:
स त्रिभिर्नैर्ऋतश्रेष्ठैर्युगपत् समभिद्रुतः।
न विव्यथे महातेजा वालिपुत्रः प्रतापवान्॥ १२॥
verses.m: Simultaneously attacked by the three jewels among ogres, the mighty son of Vālī, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, did not feel the least alarmed. (12)

verses.text:
स वेगवान् महावेगं कृत्वा परमदुर्जयः।
तलेन समभिद्रुत्य जघानास्य महागजम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: Exhibiting extraordinary impetuosity and duly assaulting the huge elephant of Mahodara, the agile Aṅgada, who was exceedingly difficult to conquer, struck it with his palm. (13)

verses.text:
तस्य तेन प्रहारेण नागराजस्य संयुगे।
पेततुर्नयने तस्य विननाश स कुञ्जरः॥ १४॥
verses.m: As a result of that blow dealt by Aṅgada on the field of battle, the eyes of that lordly elephant fell down and the said elephant perished. (14)

verses.text:
विषाणं चास्य निष्कृष्य वालिपुत्रो महाबलः।
देवान्तकमभिद्रुत्य ताडयामास संयुगे॥ १५॥
verses.m: Pulling out a tusk of the elephant and darting agairst Devāntaka, the son of Vālī, Aṅgada, who was endowed with extraordinary might, dealt him a blow with it on the battlefield. (15)

verses.text:
स विह्वलस्तु तेजस्वी वातोद्धूत इव द्रुमः।
लाक्षारससवर्णं च सुस्राव रुधिरं महत्॥ १६॥
verses.m: Thrown into disorder like a tree shaken by the wind, the heroic ogre for his part shed profuse blood which had a colour resembling that of lacquer. (16)

verses.text:
अथाश्वास्य महातेजाः कृच्छ्राद् देवान्तकोबली।
आविध्य परिघं वेगादाजघान तदाङ्गदम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: Recovering his breath with difficulty and brandishing his club with impetuosity, the mighty Devāntaka, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, then struck Aṅgada with it. (17)

verses.text:
परिघाभिहतश्चापि वानरेन्द्रात्मजस्तदा।
जानुभ्यां पतितो भूमौ पुनरेवोत्पपात ह॥ १८॥
verses.m: Though struck with the club and fallen on his knees to the ground, Aṅgada (son of the king of monkeys), they say, forthwith sprang up once more. (18)

verses.text:
तमुत्पतन्तं त्रिशिरास्त्रिभिर्बाणैरजिह्मगैः।
घोरैर्हरिपतेः पुत्रं ललाटेऽभिजघान ह॥ १९॥
verses.m: While he was doing so, Triśirā struck Aṅgada (son of the Lord of the monkeys) with three formidable straight-going arrows on the brow; so the legend goes. (19)

verses.text:
ततोऽङ्गदं परिक्षिप्तं त्रिभिर्नैर्ऋतपुङ्गवैः।
हनूमानथ विज्ञाय नीलश्चापि प्रतस्थतुः॥ २०॥
verses.m: Finding him surrounded by three of the foremost of ogres, Hanumān as well as Nīla then set out at once to help him. (20)

verses.text:
ततश्चिक्षेप शैलाग्रं नीलस्त्रिशिरसे तदा।
तद् रावणसुतो धीमान् बिभेद निशितैः शरैः॥ २१॥
verses.m: Thereupon Nīla forthwith hurled a mountain-peak at Triśira. The sagacious son of Rāvaṇa, however, shattered it with his whetted shafts. (21)

verses.text:
तद्बाणशतनिर्भिन्नं विदारितशिलातलम्।
सविस्फुलिङ्गं सज्वालं निपपात गिरेः शिरः॥ २२॥
verses.m: Smashed by hundreds of arrows discharged by Triśirā, the mountain-peak, which had all its rocky bases split up, fell down with sparks and flames that rose from it. (22)

verses.text:
स विजृम्भितमालोक्य हर्षाद् देवान्तको बली।
परिघेणाभिदुद्राव मारुतात्मजमाहवे॥ २३॥
verses.m: Witnessing with joy the exploit of Triśirā in the form of smashing the mountain-peak, the mighty Devāntaka assaulted Hanumān (son of the wind-god) with a club on the battle-field. (23)

verses.text:
तमापतन्तमुत्पत्य हनूमान् कपिकुञ्जरः।
आजघान तदा मूर्ध्नि वज्रकल्पेन मुष्टिना॥ २४॥
verses.m: Springing up, Hanumān, an elephant among the monkeys, forthwith struck on the head Devāntaka even as he was rushing forward, with his fist, which was hard as adamant. (24)

verses.text:
शिरसि प्राहरद् वीरस्तदा वायुसुतो बली।
नादेनाकम्पयच्चैव राक्षसान् स महाकपिः॥ २५॥
verses.m: The valiant and mighty son of the wind-god, Hanumān, then dealt a blow on Devāntaka head once more and by means of his roar that great monkey positively caused the ogres to tremble. (25)

verses.text:
स मुष्टिनिष्पिष्टविभिन्नमूर्धा
निर्वान्तदन्ताक्षिविलम्बिजिह्वः।
देवान्तको राक्षसराजसूनु-
र्गतासुरुर्व्यां सहसा पपात॥ २६॥
verses.m: His skull shattered by the blow of Hanumān’s fist, nay, his teeth, eyes and lolling tongue forced out, Devāntaka, son of Rāvaṇa (the ruler of ogres) precipitately fell dead on the ground. (26)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् हते राक्षसयोधमुख्ये
महाबले संयति देवशत्रौ।
क्रुद्धस्त्रिशीर्षा निशितास्त्रमुग्रं
ववर्ष नीलोरसि बाणवर्षम्॥ २७॥
verses.m: When that enemy of gods, the foremost of ogre-warriors, who was endowed with extraordinary might, was killed in the encounter with the monkeys, the furious Triśirā discharged on the breast of Nīla a fearful shower of whetted arrows. (27)

verses.text:
महोदरस्तु संक्रुद्धः कुञ्जरं पर्वतोपमम्।
भूयः समधिरुह्याशु मन्दरं रश्मिवानिव॥ २८॥
ततो बाणमयं वर्षं नीलस्योपर्यपातयत्।
गिरौ वर्षं तडिच्चक्रचापवानिव तोयदः॥ २९॥
verses.m: Quickly mounting once more an elephant resembling a mountain, even as the sun would ascend the Mandara mountain, the infuriated Mahodara for his part thereupon let fall a hail of arrows on Nīla even as a rainy cloud distinguished by a circle of lightning and a rainbow would pour a shower on a mountain. (28-29)

verses.text:
ततः शरौघैरभिवृष्यमाणो
विभिन्नगात्रः कपिसैन्यपालः।
नीलो बभूवाथ विसृष्टगात्रो
विष्टम्भितस्तेन महाबलेन॥ ३०॥
verses.m: While being covered on all sides with volleys of arrows, Nīla, the commander-in-Chief of the simian army, whose limbs were pierced by said arrows forthwith found his body inert, rendered powerless as he was by the ogre, who was endowed with extraordinary might. (30)

verses.text:
ततस्तु नीलः प्रतिलब्धसंज्ञः
शैलं समुत्पाट्य सवृक्षखण्डम्।
ततः समुत्पत्य महोग्रवेगो
महोदरं तेन जघान मूर्ध्नि॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Tearing up a crag covered with a thicket, and then springing up, Nīla for his part, who had now regained his consciousness, and who was endowed with terrific impetuosity, struck Mahodara with it on the head, (31)

verses.text:
ततः स शैलाभिनिपातभग्नो
महोदरस्तेन महाद्विपेन।
व्यामोहितो भूमितले गतासुः
पपात वज्राभिहतो यथाद्रिः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Smashed by the impact of the crag alongwith the aforesaid huge elephant, and rendered unconscious, the said Mahodara fell dead on the earth’s surface like a mountain struck by lightning. (32)

verses.text:
पितृव्यं निहतं दृष्ट्वा त्रिशिराश्चापमाददे।
हनूमन्तं च संक्रुद्धो विव्याध निशितैः शरैः॥ ३३॥
verses.m: Enraged to see his uncle, Mahodara, killed, Triśirā seized his bow and pierced Hanumān with his whetted shafts. (33)

verses.text:
