स वायुसूनुः कुपितश्चिक्षेप शिखरं गिरेः।
त्रिशिरास्तच्छरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्बिभेद बहुधा बली॥ ३४॥
verses.m: Full of fury the aforesaid son of the wind-god flung a mountain-peak at the ogre. The mighty Triśirā, however, split it with his sharp arrows into several pieces. (34)

verses.text:
तद् व्यर्थं शिखरं दृष्ट्वा द्रुमवर्षं तदा कपिः।
विससर्ज रणे तस्मिन् रावणस्य सुतं प्रति॥ ३५॥
verses.m: Finding the aforesaid mountain-peak ineffectual, the monkey, Hanumān, then hurled a shower of trees on the son of Rāvaṇa, Triśirā, in that combat. (35)

verses.text:
तमापतन्तमाकाशे द्रुमवर्षं प्रतापवान्।
त्रिशिरा निशितैर्बाणैश्चिच्छेद च ननाद च॥ ३६॥
verses.m: The powerful Triśirā, however, tore with his whetted shafts that shower of trees falling through the airspace, and roared too. (36)

verses.text:
हनूमांस्तु समुत्पत्य हयं त्रिशिरसस्तदा।
विददार नखैः क्रुद्धो नागेन्द्रं मृगराडिव॥ ३७॥
verses.m: Springing up in fury, Hanumān for his part then tore the horse of Triśirā with his nails even as a lion (lit., the king of beasts) would claw a lordly elephant. (37)

verses.text:
अथ शक्तिं समासाद्य कालरात्रिमिवान्तकः।
चिक्षेपानिलपुत्राय त्रिशिरा रावणात्मजः॥ ३८॥
verses.m: Seizing hold of his javelin, even as Death would take in his service Kālarātri (a sister of Kāla, the deity presiding over the night of destruction at the end of the world cycle), Triśirā, sprung from the lions of Rāvaṇa, hurled it at the son of the wind-god. (38)

verses.text:
दिवः क्षिप्तामिवोल्कां तां शक्तिं क्षिप्तामसङ्गताम्।
गृहीत्वा हरिशार्दूलो बभञ्ज च ननाद च॥ ३९॥
verses.m: Catching that javelin flung by Triśirā, which came unobstructed like a meteor shot from the heavens, Hanumān (a tiger among the monkeys) snapped it and roared, too. (39)

verses.text:
तां दृष्ट्वा घोरसंकाशां शक्तिं भग्नां हनूमता।
प्रहृष्टा वानरगणा विनेदुर्जलदा यथा॥ ४०॥
verses.m: Seeing that javelin of formidable aspect destroyed by Hanumān, the simian hosts felt overjoyed and thundered like rainy clouds. (40)

verses.text:
ततः खड्गं समुद्यम्य त्रिशिरा राक्षसोत्तमः।
निचखान तदा खड्गं वानरेन्द्रस्य वक्षसि॥ ४१॥
verses.m: Lifting up his sword, Triśirā, the foremost of ogres, thereupon immediately hit with vehemence the breast of the monkey-chief, Hanumān. (41)

verses.text:
खड्गप्रहाराभिहतो हनूमान् मारुतात्मजः।
आजघान त्रिमूर्धानं तलेनोरसि वीर्यवान्॥ ४२॥
verses.m: Wounded by the thrust of his sword, the valiant Hanumān, sprung from the loins of the wind-god, struck the ogre,Triśirā, with his palm on the breast. (42)

verses.text:
स तलाभिहतस्तेन स्रस्तहस्तायुधो भुवि।
निपपात महातेजास्त्रिशिरास्त्यक्तचेतनः॥ ४३॥
verses.m: Slapped by him, though endowed with extraordinary energy, Triśirā dropped unconscious to the ground, the weapon in his hand having slipped. (43)

verses.text:
स तस्य पततः खड्गं तमाच्छिद्य महाकपिः।
ननाद गिरिसंकाशस्त्रासयन् सर्वराक्षसान्॥ ४४॥
verses.m: Snatching away that sword of the ogre even as he was falling down, the mighty monkey, Hanumān, who looked like a mountain, let out a roar, striking terror in all the ogres. (44)

verses.text:
अमृष्यमाणस्तं घोषमुत्पपात निशाचरः।
उत्पत्य च हनूमन्तं ताडयामास मुष्टिना॥ ४५॥
verses.m: Unable to bear that roar, the prowler of the night sprang on his feet; and, jumping up, he struck Hanumān with his fist. (45)

verses.text:
तेन मुष्टिप्रहारेण संचुकोप महाकपिः।
कुपितश्च निजग्राह किरीटे राक्षसर्षभम्॥ ४६॥
verses.m: The great monkey flew into a rage at the aforesaid blow to Triśirā’s fist and, full of fury, seized hold of Triśirā (the foremost of ogres) by his head covered with a diadem. (46)

verses.text:
स तस्य शीर्षाण्यसिना शितेन
किरीटजुष्टानि सकुण्डलानि।
क्रुद्धः प्रचिच्छेद सुतोऽनिलस्य
त्वष्टुः सुतस्येव शिरांसि शक्रः॥ ४७॥
verses.m: Getting enraged, that son of the wind-god completely severed with his sharp sword all the three heads of Triśirā, covered with diadems and adorned with ear-rings, in the same way as Indra, the ruler of gods, lopped off in in the past the three heads of Viśwarūpa, son of Twaṣṭā. (47)

verses.text:
तान्यायताक्षाण्यगसंनिभानि
प्रदीप्तवैश्वानरलोचनानि।
पेतुः शिरांसीन्द्ररिपोः पृथिव्यां
ज्योतींषि मुक्तानि यथार्कमार्गात्॥ ४८॥
verses.m: The aforesaid heads of Triśirā (an enemy of Indra), which were distinguished by enormous sense-organs (appertures of the eyes, ears and nose) were huge as rocks and had eyes glowing like a flaming fire—fell to the ground like stars fallen down from the sky (lit., the orbit of the sun). (48)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् हते देवरिपौ त्रिशीर्षे
हनूमता शक्रपराक्रमेण।
नेदुः प्लवंगाः प्रचचाल भूमी
रक्षांस्यथो दुद्रुविरे समन्तात्॥ ४९॥
verses.m: When that enemy of gods, Triśirā, was killed by Hanumān, who was endowed with the prowess of Indra (the ruler of gods), the monkey, Hanumān, roared in triumph, the earth shook and the ogres took to their heels on all sides. (49)

verses.text:
हतं त्रिशिरसं दृष्ट्वा तथैव च महोदरम्।
हतौ प्रेक्ष्य दुराधर्षौ देवान्तकनरान्तकौ॥ ५०॥
चुकोप परमामर्षी मत्तो राक्षसपुङ्गवः।
जग्राहार्चिष्मतीं चापि गदां सर्वायसीं तदा॥ ५१॥
हेमपट्टपरिक्षिप्तां मांसशोणितफेनिलाम्।
विराजमानां विपुलां शत्रुशोणिततर्पिताम्॥ ५२॥
तेजसा सम्प्रदीप्ताग्रां रक्तमाल्यविभूषिताम्।
ऐरावतमहापद्मसार्वभौमभयावहाम् ॥ ५३॥
verses.m: Finding Triśirā killed and Mahodara too and likewise perceiving Devāntaka and Narāntaka, who were difficult to overpower, made short work of, the highly indignant Matta (more popularly known by the name of Mahāpārśwa) a veritable bull among the ogres, flew into a rage and forthwith seized hold of a huge flaming and glittering mace entirely made of iron, though plated with gold, which was covered with foam of flesh and blood when used against the enemy and had been saturated with the enemy’s blood, whose head was inflamed with lustre, which was decked with crimson flowers and brought terror to Airāvata, Mahāpadma and Sārvabhauma (three of the four elephants supporting the four quarters). (50—53)

verses.text:
गदामादाय संक्रुद्धो मत्तो राक्षसपुङ्गवः।
हरीन् समभिदुद्राव युगान्ताग्निरिव ज्वलन्॥ ५४॥
verses.m: Seizing the mace, filled with fury, and flaring up like the fire of universal destruction at the end of the world cycle, Matta, a veritable bull among the ogres, scattered the monkeys. (54)

verses.text:
अथर्षभः समुत्पत्य वानरो रावणानुजम्।
मत्तानीकमुपागम्य तस्थौ तस्याग्रतो बली॥ ५५॥
verses.m: Springing up and approaching Mattānīka (Mahāpārśwa), a younger brother of Rāvaṇa, the mighty monkey Ṛṣabha stood facing him. (55)

verses.text:
तं पुरस्तात् स्थितं दृष्ट्वा वानरं पर्वतोपमम्।
आजघानोरसि क्रुद्धो गदया वज्रकल्पया॥ ५६॥
verses.m: Enraged to behold that monkey, who looked like a mountain, standing in front of him, the ogre struck him on the chest with his mace, which was hard as adamant. (56)

verses.text:
स तयाभिहतस्तेन गदया वानरर्षभः।
भिन्नवक्षाः समाधूतः सुस्राव रुधिरं बहु॥ ५७॥
verses.m: Struck by him with that mace and staggered, that bull among the monkeys, who had his chest cleft, shed copious blood. (57)

verses.text:
स सम्प्राप्य चिरात् संज्ञामृषभो वानरेश्वरः।
क्रुद्धो विस्फुरमाणौष्ठो महापार्श्वमुदैक्षत॥ ५८॥
verses.m: Fully regaining consciousness after a long time, Rṣabha, the monkey-chief, cast a glance at Mahāpārśwa, enraged as he was, his lips quivering with rage. (58)

verses.text:
स वेगवान् वेगवदभ्युपेत्य
तं राक्षसं वानरवीरमुख्यः।
संवर्त्य मुष्टिं सहसा जघान
बाह्वन्तरे शैलनिकाशरूपः॥ ५९॥
verses.m: Approaching that ogre with impetuosity and clenching his fist, that agile leader of monkey heroes, whose exterior presented the appearance of a mountain, precipitately struck him on the chest (lit. the space between the two arms). (59)

verses.text:
स कृत्तमूलः सहसेव वृक्षः
क्षितौ पपात क्षतजोक्षिताङ्गः।
तां चास्य घोरां यमदण्डकल्पां
गदां प्रगृह्याशु तदा ननाद॥ ६०॥
verses.m: Like a tree whose roots have been severed, the ogre suddenly fell to the ground, bathed all over in blood. Nay, quickly seizing hold of that formidable mace of the ogre, which resembled the rod of Yama (the god of retribution), the monkey, Ṛṣabha, forthwith roared. (60)

verses.text:
मुहूर्तमासीत् स गतासुकल्पः
प्रत्यागतात्मा सहसा सुरारिः।
उत्पत्य संध्याभ्रसमानवर्ण-
स्तं वारिराजात्मजमाजघान॥ ६१॥
verses.m: For a while Mahāpārśwa remained all but dead. Springing on his feet all of a sudden, his lifµe-breath having returned, the enemy of gods, whose colour resembled that of an evening cloud, struck the aforesaid son of the lord of waters, Ṛṣabha. (61)

verses.text:
स मूर्च्छितो भूमितले पपात
मुहूर्तमुत्पत्य पुनः ससंज्ञः।
तामेव तस्याद्रिवराद्रिकल्पां
गदां समाविध्य जघान संख्ये॥ ६२॥
verses.m: The monkey lay unconscious on the earth’s surface awhile. Springing up, when he was conscious again, and brandishing that very mace of the ogre, which looked like a rock of the foremost of mountains, Rṣabha struck him with it on the battle-field. (62)

verses.text:
सा तस्य रौद्रा समुपेत्य देहं
रौद्रस्य देवाध्वरविप्रशत्रोः।
बिभेद वक्षः क्षतजं च भूरि
सुस्राव धात्वम्भ इवाद्रिराजः॥ ६३॥
verses.m: Reaching the body of that ferocious enemy of gods, sacrificial performances and Brāhmaṇas, that terrible mace clove his breast; and the ogre shed profuse blood even as the Himālaya mountain (the lord of mountains) lets out water charged with minerals (like ochre). (63)

verses.text:
अभिदुद्राव वेगेन गदां तस्य महात्मनः।
तां गृहीत्वा गदां भीमामाविध्य च पुनः पुनः॥ ६४॥
मत्तानीकं महात्मा स जघान रणमूर्धनि।
स स्वया गदया भग्नो विशीर्णदशनेक्षणः॥ ६५॥
निपपात तदा मत्तो वज्राहत इवाचलः।
विशीर्णनयने भूमौ गतसत्त्वे गतायुषि।
पतिते राक्षसे तस्मिन् विद्रुतं राक्षसं बलम्॥ ६६॥
verses.m: The ogre now darted towards the mace held in the hand of that gigantic monkey, Rṣabha. Clutching that terrible mace and brandishing it again and again, the high-souled Rṣabha struck Mahāpārśwa with it in the forefront of the battle. Smashed with his own mace, his teeth and eyes fallen down, Matta (Mahāpārśwa) forthwith dropped down like a mountain struck with lightning. When that ogre, whose eyes had been crushed, dropped unconcious and lifeless on the ground, the army of ogres fled. (64—66)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् हते भ्रातरि रावणस्य
तन्नैर्ऋतानां बलमर्णवाभम्।
त्यक्तायुधं केवलजीवितार्थं
दुद्राव भिन्नार्णवसंनिकाशम्॥ ६७॥
verses.m: When the aforesaid younger brother of Rāvaṇa was killed, the aforesaid army of ogres (the scions of Nirṛti), which resembled an ocean, fled for life, casting away weapons, and presenting the appearance of an ocean which has burst its shores. (67)

verses.text:
स्वबलं व्यथितं दृष्ट्वा तुमुलं लोमहर्षणम्।
भ्रातृं ृश्च निहतान् दृष्ट्वा शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमान्॥ १॥
पितृव्यौ चापि संदृश्य समरे संनिपातितौ।
युद्धोन्मत्तं च मत्तं च भ्रातरौ राक्षसोत्तमौ॥ २॥
चुकोप च महातेजा ब्रह्मदत्तवरो युधि।
अतिकायोऽद्रिसंकाशो देवदानवदर्पहा॥ ३॥
verses.m: Seeing his own army—which created uproars in the hostile ranks and caused the enemy’s hair to stand on end—in trouble, nay, finding his brothers, who were equal to Indra in prowess, killed, and also witnessing has uncles, the two brothers Yuddhonmatta (Mahodara) and Matta (Mahāpārśwa) the foremost of ogres, struck down in combat, Atikāya, who was endowed with extraordinary energy and resembled a mountain (in size), who had crushed the pride of gods and demons alike and on whom Brahmā, the creator, had bestowed a boon of invincibility, flew into a rage on the field of battle. (1—3)

verses.text:
स भास्करसहस्रस्य संघातमिव भास्वरम्।
रथमारुह्य शक्रारिरभिदुद्राव वानरान्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Ascending his chariot, brilliant as a concatenation of a thousand suns, that enemy of Indra (the ruler of gods) darted towards the monkeyṣ (4)

verses.text:
स विस्फार्य तदा चापं किरीटी मृष्टकुण्डलः।
नाम संश्रावयामास ननाद च महास्वनम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Twanging his bow, Atikāya, who was adorned with a diadem and polished earrings, forthwith proclaimed his name and emitted a tremendous roar. (5)

verses.text:
तेन सिंहप्रणादेन नामविश्रावणेन च।
ज्याशब्देन च भीमेन त्रासयामास वानरान्॥ ६॥
verses.m: By that leonine roar, the proclamation of his name and the terrible ringing sound caused by the plucking of his bowstring, he struck terror in the monkeys. (6)

verses.text:
ते दृष्ट्वा देहमाहात्म्यं कुम्भकर्णोऽयमुत्थितः।
भयार्ता वानराः सर्वे संश्रयन्ते परस्परम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: Thinking on beholding the immensity of his proportions that it was Kumbhakarṇa who had sprung into life again, and stricken with fear, all the aforesaid monkeys sought shelter, one with the other. (7)

verses.text:
ते तस्य रूपमालोक्य यथा विष्णोस्त्रिविक्रमे।
भयाद् वानरयोधास्ते विद्रवन्ति ततस्ततः॥ ८॥
verses.m: Witnessing his colossal form, resembling the form assumed by Lord Viṣṇu at the time of measuring the three worlds with His strides, those celebrated monkey warriors fled in various directions through panic. (8)

verses.text:
तेऽतिकायं समासाद्य वानरा मूढचेतसः।
शरण्यं शरणं जग्मुर्लक्ष्मणाग्रजमाहवे॥ ९॥
verses.m: Confused in mind on reaching the presence of Atikāya, the aforesaid monkeys sought Śrī Rāma (the eldest brother of Lakṣmaṇa), who was capable of affording shelter to them, as their refuge on the field of battle. (9)

verses.text:
ततोऽतिकायं काकुत्स्थो रथस्थं पर्वतोपमम्।
ददर्श धन्विनं दूराद् गर्जन्तं कालमेघवत्॥ १०॥
verses.m: Thereupon Śrī Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha) beheld from afar Atikāya, who resembled a mountain in size, seated in a chariot, armed with a bow, and rumbling like a cloud appearing at the time of universal dissolution. (10)

verses.text:
स तं दृष्ट्वा महाकायं राघवस्तु सुविस्मितः।
वानरान् सान्त्वयित्वा च विभीषणमुवाच ह॥ ११॥
verses.m: The aforesaid Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, for his part felt greatly amazed to behold that colossus and reassuring the monkeys, they say, spoke as follows to Vibhīṣaṇa: (11)

verses.text:
कोऽसौ पर्वतसंकाशो धनुष्मान् हरिलोचनः।
युक्ते हयसहस्रेण विशाले स्यन्दने स्थितः॥ १२॥
य एष निशितैः शूलैः सुतीक्ष्णैः प्रासतोमरैः।
अर्चिष्मद्भिर्वृतो भाति भूतैरिव महेश्वरः॥ १३॥
कालजिह्वाप्रकाशाभिर्य एषोऽभिविराजते।
आवृतो रथशक्तीभिर्विद्युद्भिरिव तोयदः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Who is that archer, closely resembling a mountain, with leonine eyes, seated in a vast chariot drawn by a thousand horses, who in the midst of whetted pikes, very sharp and flaming spears and lances, shines over there like Lord Śiva surrounded by genii, and who amidst the javelins placed in his chariot and gleaming like the tongues of Kāla (the Time-Spirit) is shining brightly like a cloud encircled by flashes of lightning? (12—14)

verses.text:
धनूंषि चास्य सज्जानि हेमपृष्ठानि सर्वशः।
शोभयन्ति रथश्रेष्ठं शक्रचापमिवाम्बरम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Nay, bows with golden backs ranged on every side (in his chariot) adorn his excellent chariot in the same way as rainbow would adorn the sky. (15)

verses.text:
य एष रक्षःशार्दूलो रणभूमिं विराजयन्।
अभ्येति रथिनां श्रेष्ठो रथेनादित्यवर्चसा॥ १६॥
verses.m: “This tiger among the ogres, the foremost of car-warriors, is advancing in his chariot resplendent as the sun, illuminating the battle-field! (16)

verses.text:
ध्वजशृङ्गप्रतिष्ठेन राहुणाभिविराजते।
सूर्यरश्मिप्रभैर्बाणैर्दिशो दश विराजयन्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “He is distinguished by an emblem of Rāhu installed on the point of his standard and is lighting up the ten directions with his arrows possessing the splendour of sunbeams. (17)

verses.text:
त्रिनतं मेघनिर्ह्रादं हेमपृष्ठमलंकृतम्।
शतक्रतुधनुःप्रख्यं धनुश्चास्य विराजते॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Nay, his triply curved golden-backed and ornamented bow, shining as the rainbow, whose twang resembles the thundering of a cloud, is casting its splendour all round. (18)

verses.text:
सध्वजः सपताकश्च सानुकर्षो महारथः।
चतुःसादिसमायुक्तो मेघस्तनितनिःस्वनः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Provided with a standard, flags and axle-tree, his huge chariot, which is driven by four charioteers, his chariot is emitting a sound resembling the thundering of a cloud. (19)

verses.text:
विंशतिर्दश चाष्टौ च तूणास्य रथमास्थिताः।
कार्मुकाणि च भीमानि ज्याश्च काञ्चनपिङ्गलाः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Twenty quivers, ten dreadful bows and eight bowstrings, golden and reddish-brown of hue, lie arranged in his chariot. (20)

verses.text:
द्वौ च खड्गौ च पार्श्वस्थौ प्रदीप्तौ पार्श्वशोभितौ।
चतुर्हस्तत्सरुयुतौ व्यक्तहस्तदशायतौ॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Nay, hanging on its sides, two flaming swords, clearly ten cubits long and provided with hilts measuring four cubits are casting their splendour on his two sides. (21)

verses.text:
रक्तकण्ठगुणो धीरो महापर्वतसंनिभः।
कालः कालमहावक्त्रो मेघस्थ इव भास्करः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “With a red garland adorning his neck, a mouth enormous as that of Death, the resolute ogre, resembling a huge mountain and dark of hue, looks like the sun veiled by a cloud. (22)

verses.text:
काञ्चनाङ्गदनद्धाभ्यां भुजाभ्यामेष शोभते।
शृङ्गाभ्यामिव तुङ्गाभ्यां हिमवान् पर्वतोत्तमः॥ २३॥
verses.m: “By virtue of his arms adorned with gold armlets, the yonder ogre shines like the Himālaya, the foremost of mountains, with two lofty peaks. (23)

verses.text:
कुण्डलाभ्यामुभाभ्यां च भाति वक्त्रं सुभीषणम्।
पुनर्वस्वन्तरगतं परिपूर्णो निशाकरः॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Nay, with both ear-rings, his most dreadful countenance shines like the full moon appearing between the two stars constituting the constellation Punarvasu. (24)

verses.text:
आचक्ष्व मे महाबाहो त्वमेनं राक्षसोत्तमम्।
यं दृष्ट्वा वानराः सर्वे भयार्ता विद्रुता दिशः॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Introduce you to me, O mighty-armed one, this jewel among the ogres, seeing whom the monkeys have all fled panic-stricken in all directions.” (25)

verses.text:
स पृष्टो राजपुत्रेण रामेणामिततेजसा।
आचचक्षे महातेजा राघवाय विभीषणः॥ २६॥
verses.m: Questioned as aforesaid by Prince Śrī Rāma of immense energy, Vibhiṣaṇa, who too was endowed with extraordinary energy, submitted as follows to Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu: (26)

verses.text:
दशग्रीवो महातेजा राजा वैश्रवणानुजः।
भीमकर्मा महात्मा हि रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः॥ २७॥
verses.m: “The ten-headed and gigantic King Rāvaṇa, a younger (half-) brother of Kubera, son of Viśravā, the lord of ogres, who is endowed with extraordinary energy, is well known for his terrific exploits. (27)

verses.text:
तस्यासीद् वीर्यवान् पुत्रो रावणप्रतिमो बले।
वृद्धसेवी श्रुतिधरः सर्वास्त्रविदुषां वरः॥ २८॥
verses.m: “To him was born a valiant son, who is a compeer of Rāvaṇa in might, has waited upon his elders, has mastered the Vedas and is the foremost of all those well-versed in the use of mystic missiles. (28)

verses.text:
अश्वपृष्ठे नागपृष्ठे खड्गे धनुषि कर्षणे।
भेदे सान्त्वे च दाने च नये मन्त्रे च सम्मतः॥ २९॥
verses.m: “He is highly esteemed in riding on horse-back as well as on the back of an elephant, in the use of a sword, as well as of a bow, in pulling the string of a bow, in sowing dissension in the enemy’s ranks and making peace, as also in making gifts, in political wisdom as well as in counsel. (29)

verses.text:
यस्य बाहुं समाश्रित्य लङ्का भवति निर्भया।
तनयं धान्यमालिन्या अतिकायमिमं विदुः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “People know this warrior as Atikāya, son of Dhānyamālinī (another consort of Rāvaṇa) resting on whose arm Laṅkā feels secure. (30)

verses.text:
एतेनाराधितो ब्रह्मा तपसा भावितात्मना।
अस्त्राणि चाप्यवाप्तानि रिपवश्च पराजिताः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Brahmā, the creator, was propitiated by this ogre of purified intellect through askesis; nay, mystic missiles of various kinds were acquired from the aforesaid god by way of boons and enemies subdued. (31)

verses.text:
सुरासुरैरवध्यत्वं दत्तमस्मै स्वयंभुवा।
एतच्च कवचं दिव्यं रथश्च रविभास्वरः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Exemption from death at the hands of gods and demons alike has been granted in his favour by Brahmā (the self-born creator) as well as this heavenly armour as also this chariot, bright as the sun. (32)

verses.text:
एतेन शतशो देवा दानवाश्च पराजिताः।
रक्षितानि च रक्षांसि यक्षाश्चापि निषूदिताः॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “Gods and devils too have been overcome by him in hundreds, nay, ogres have been protected and Yakṣas (a class of demigods), too, have been exterminated. (33)

verses.text:
वज्रं विष्टम्भितं येन बाणैरिन्द्रस्य धीमता।
पाशः सलिलराजस्य युद्धे प्रतिहतस्तथा॥ ३४॥
एषोऽतिकायो बलवान् राक्षसानामथर्षभः।
स रावणसुतो धीमान् देवदानवदर्पहा॥ ३५॥
verses.m: Here is the notorious Atikāya, the mighty and intelligent son of Rāvaṇa, a veritable bull among the ogres and the queller of the pride of gods and devils, by whom, wise as he is, was the thunderbolt of Indra stayed with his arrows and the noose of Varuṇa, the lord of waters, was repelled in combat. (34-35)

verses.text:
तदस्मिन् क्रियतां यत्नः क्षिप्रं पुरुषपुङ्गव।
पुरा वानरसैन्यानि क्षयं नयति सायकैः॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “Therefore, O bull among men, let your efforts be speedily directed towards him before he brings the monkey troops to an end with his arrows.” (36)

verses.text:
ततोऽतिकायो बलवान् प्रविश्य हरिवाहिनीम्।
विस्फारयामास धनुर्ननाद च पुनः पुनः॥ ३७॥
verses.m: Penetrating deep into the simian ranks, the mighty Atikāya thereupon twanged his bow and roared again and again. (37)

verses.text:
तं भीमवपुषं दृष्ट्वा रथस्थं रथिनां वरम्।
अभिपेतुर्महात्मानः प्रधाना ये वनौकसः॥ ३८॥
verses.m: Beholding that ogre of fearful proportions, the foremost of car-warriors, seated in his chariot, those gigantic monkeys, who ranked foremost, rushed to meet him. (38)

verses.text:
कुमुदो द्विविदो मैन्दो नीलः शरभ एव च।
पादपैर्गिरिशृङ्गैश्च युगपत् समभिद्रवन्॥ ३९॥
verses.m: Kumuda, Dwivida, Mainda, Nīla and Śarabha too assailed him all at once with trees and mountain-peaks. (39)

verses.text:
तेषां वृक्षांश्च शैलांश्च शरैः कनकभूषणैः।
अतिकायो महातेजाश्चिच्छेदास्त्रविदां वरः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: Atikāya, however, the foremost of those well versed in the use of mystic missiles, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, tore the trees and crags hurled by monkeys with his shafts decked with gold. (40)

verses.text:
तांश्चैव सर्वान् स हरीन् शरैः सर्वायसैर्बली।
विव्याधाभिमुखान् संख्ये भीमकायो निशाचरः॥ ४१॥
verses.m: That mighty ogre (lit., a prowler of the night) of tremendous proportions also pierced all those monkeys, who stood facing him on the battle-field, with his arrows entirely made of iron. (41)

verses.text:
तेऽर्दिता बाणवर्षेण भिन्नगात्राः पराजिताः।
न शेकुरतिकायस्य प्रतिकर्तुं महाहवे॥ ४२॥
verses.m: Hard pressed by his hail of arrows and worsted, their limbs broken, they could not resist Atikāya in that major conflict. (42)

verses.text:
तत् सैन्यं हरिवीराणां त्रासयामास राक्षसः।
मृगयूथमिव क्रुद्धो हरिर्यौवनदर्पितः॥ ४३॥
verses.m: The ogre struck terror in that army of monkey champions even as a furious lion, puffed up with pride of youth, would strike terror in a flock of deer. (43)

verses.text:
स राक्षसेन्द्रो हरियूथमध्ये
नायुध्यमानं निजघान कंचित्।
उत्पत्य रामं स धनुःकलापी
सगर्वितं वाक्यमिदं बभाषे॥ ४४॥
verses.m: That ruler of ogres would not strike anyone among the simian ranks who was not fighting. Rushing towards Śrī Rāma, the ogre, who was armed with a bow and quiver, addressed the following proud challenge to him: (44)

verses.text:
रथे स्थितोऽहं शरचापपाणि-
र्न प्राकृतं कंचन योधयामि।
यस्यास्ति शक्तिर्व्यवसाययुक्तो
ददातु मे शीघ्रमिहाद्य युद्धम्॥ ४५॥
verses.m: “Seated in a chariot with an arrow and a bow in my hands, I would not give battle to a common warrior. Let him, who has strength and is endowed with martial ardour, speedily give fight to me on this field of battle today.” (45)

verses.text:
तत् तस्य वाक्यं ब्रुवतो निशम्य
चुकोप सौमित्रिरमित्रहन्ता।
अमृष्यमाणश्च समुत्पपात
जग्राह चापं च ततः स्मयित्वा॥ ४६॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforeesaid challenge of Atikāya, even as he was uttering it, Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā), the destroyer of his enemies, flew into a rage. Nay, not enduring his utterance, he darted forward, and then seized his bow disdainfully. (46)

verses.text:
क्रुद्धः सौमित्रिरुत्पत्य तूणादाक्षिप्य सायकम्।
पुरस्तादतिकायस्य विचकर्ष महद्धनुः॥ ४७॥
verses.m: Springing up in fury and pulling a shaft from his quiver, the son of Sumitrā, Lakṣmaṇa, stretched his huge bow to full length before Atikāya. (47)

verses.text:
पूरयन् स महीं सर्वामाकाशं सागरं दिशः।
ज्याशब्दो लक्ष्मणस्योग्रस्त्रासयन् रजनीचरान्॥ ४८॥
verses.m: Filling the entire earth, the airspace, the ocean as well as the quarters, and striking terror in the prowlers of the night, the twang of Lakṣmaṇa’s bowstring was terrible. (48)

verses.text:
सौमित्रेश्चापनिर्घोषं श्रुत्वा प्रतिभयं तदा।
विसिस्मिये महातेजा राक्षसेन्द्रात्मजो बली॥ ४९॥
verses.m: The mighty Atikāya, sprung from the loins of the king of orgres, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, was astonished on that occasion to hear the fearful twang of the bow of Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā). (49)

verses.text:
तदातिकायः कुपितो दृष्ट्वा लक्ष्मणमुत्थितम्।
आदाय निशितं बाणमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ ५०॥
verses.m: Enraged to behold Lakṣmaṇa active and seizing hold of a whetted shaft, Atikāya then spoke to Lakṣmaṇa as follows: (50)

verses.text:
बालस्त्वमसि सौमित्रे विक्रमेष्वविचक्षणः।
गच्छ किं कालसंकाशं मां योधयितुमिच्छसि॥ ५१॥
verses.m: “You are still a youngster, O son of Sumitra, unskilled in exhibiting valour. Therefore, depart! Why do you seek to measure your strength with me, a replica of Kāla (the Time-Spirit)? (51)

verses.text:
नहि मद्बाहुसृष्टानां बाणानां हिमवानपि।
सोढुमुत्सहते वेगमन्तरिक्षमथो मही॥ ५२॥
verses.m: “Not even the Himālaya mountain, nor the atmosphere nor even the earth can withstand the force of the arrows discharged by my arm. (52)

verses.text:
सुखप्रसुप्तं कालाग्निं विबोधयितुमिच्छसि।
न्यस्य चापं निवर्तस्व प्राणान्न जहि मद्गतः॥ ५३॥
verses.m: “Do you seek to rouse the fire of universal dissolution, comfortably buried in slumber? Casting away your bow, go back. Confronting me, do not lose your life. (53)

verses.text:
अथवा त्वं प्रतिस्तब्धो न निवर्तितुमिच्छसि।
तिष्ठ प्राणान् परित्यज्य गमिष्यसि यमक्षयम्॥ ५४॥
verses.m: “Or, if, being stubborn, you do not wish to return, tarry. Yielding up your life, you shall proceed to the abode of Yama (the god of retribution). (54)

verses.text:
पश्य मे निशितान् बाणान् रिपुदर्पनिषूदनान्।
ईश्वरायुधसंकाशांस्तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणान् ॥ ५५॥
verses.m: “Behold my whetted shafts, capable of crushing the pride of the enemy, nay, resembling the weapon, trident of Lord Śiva, and decked with refined gold. (55)

verses.text:
एष ते सर्पसंकाशो बाणः पास्यति शोणितम्।
मृगराज इव क्रुद्धो नागराजस्य शोणितम्।
इत्येवमुक्त्वा संक्रुद्धः शरं धनुषि संदधे॥ ५६॥
verses.m: “This arrow, resembling a serpent, shall quaff your blood even as a furious lion would drink the blood of a lordly elephant.” Having spoken as aforesaid, Atikāya, who was seized with fury, put an arrow to his bow. (56)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वातिकायस्य वचः सरोषं
सगर्वितं संयति राजपुत्रः।
स संचुकोपातिबलो मनस्वी
उवाच वाक्यं च ततो महार्थम्॥ ५७॥
verses.m: Hearing the furious and proud utterance of Atikāya on the field of battle, the high-minded Prince Laksmaṇa, who was endowed with surpassing strength, flew into a rage and then made the following reply, which was full of great significance: (57)

verses.text:
न वाक्यमात्रेण भवान् प्रधानो
न कत्थनात् सत्पुरुषा भवन्ति।
मयि स्थिते धन्विनि बाणपाणौ
निदर्शयस्वात्मबलं दुरात्मन्॥ ५८॥
verses.m: “You cannot claim to be pre-eminent by mere speech nor can people become good men through sheer braggadocio. While I stand before you armed with a bow, arrow in hand, demonstrate your strength, O evil-minded one! (58)

verses.text:
कर्मणा सूचयात्मानं न विकत्थितुमर्हसि।
पौरुषेण तु यो युक्तः स तु शूर इति स्मृतः॥ ५९॥
verses.m: “Reveal yourself through your action; you ought not to blow your own trumpet. He alone who is actually endowed with prowess is recognized as a hero. (59)

verses.text:
सर्वायुधसमायुक्तो धन्वी त्वं रथमास्थितः।
शरैर्वा यदि वाप्यस्त्रैर्दर्शयस्व पराक्रमम्॥ ६०॥
verses.m: “Fully equipped with all kinds of weapons and armed with a bow, you are seated in a chariot. Therefore, manifest your prowess either with your arrows or with your mystic missiles. (60)

verses.text:
ततः शिरस्ते निशितैः पातयिष्याम्यहं शरैः।
मारुतः कालसम्पक्वं वृन्तात् तालफलं यथा॥ ६१॥
verses.m: “Then shall I strike down your head with my whetted shafts even as the wind detaches a palm fruit ripened in process of time from its stem. (61)

verses.text:
अद्य ते मामका बाणास्तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणाः।
पास्यन्ति रुधिरं गात्राद् बाणशल्यान्तरोत्थितम्॥ ६२॥
verses.m: “My arrows decked with refined gold shall drink the blood ejected from your body through the holes made by the points of my arrows. (62)

verses.text:
बालोऽयमिति विज्ञाय न चावज्ञातुमर्हसि।
बालो वा यदि वा वृद्धो मृत्युं जानीहि संयुगे॥ ६३॥
verses.m: “Nor should you underestimate me thinking that I am a mere boy. Whether I am a child or grown-up, know me to be your death on the field of battle. (63)

verses.text:
बालेन विष्णुना लोकास्त्रयः क्रान्तास्त्रिविक्रमैः।
लक्ष्मणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा हेतुमत् परमार्थवत्।
अतिकायः प्रचुक्रोध बाणं चोत्तममाददे॥ ६४॥
verses.m: “The three worlds were covered in three strides of Lord Viṣṇu, descended as Lord Vāmana, while He was yet a child.” Hearing the reply of Lakṣmaṇa, which was full of reason and contained the whole truth, Atikāya flew into a rage and laid hold of an excellent arrow. (64)

verses.text:
ततो विद्याधरा भूता देवा दैत्या महर्षयः।
गुह्यकाश्च महात्मानस्तद् युद्धं द्रष्टुमागमन्॥ ६५॥
verses.m: Thereupon Vidyādharas (heavenly artistes), ghosts, gods, giants and eminent Ṛṣis (seers of Vedic Mantras) as well as high-minded Guhyakas, Yakṣas arrived to witness the duel. (65)

verses.text:
ततोऽतिकायः कुपितश्चापमारोप्य सायकम्।
लक्ष्मणाय प्रचिक्षेप संक्षिपन्निव चाम्बरम्॥ ६६॥
verses.m: Putting an arrow to his bow, Atikāya thereupon furiously discharged it against Lakṣmaṇa, shrinking up space as it were. (66)

verses.text:
तमापतन्तं निशितं शरमाशीविषोपमम्।
अर्धचन्द्रेण चिच्छेद लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा॥ ६७॥
verses.m: Lakṣman, the destroyer of hostile champions, however, split with his arrow, having a crescent-shaped head, that sharpened shaft, which came flying like a venomous serpent. (67)

verses.text:
तं निकृत्तं शरं दृष्ट्वा कृत्तभोगमिवोरगम्।
अतिकायो भृशं क्रुद्धः पञ्च बाणान् समादधे॥ ६८॥
verses.m: Enraged to find that arrow torn like a serpent whose hood has been severed, Atikāya fitted five arrows to his bow. (68)

verses.text:
तान् शरान् सम्प्रचिक्षेप लक्ष्मणाय निशाचरः।
तानप्राप्तान् शितैर्बाणैश्चिच्छेद भरतानुजः॥ ६९॥
verses.m: The ranger of the night, Atikāya, discharged the aforesaid arrows with full force against Lakṣmaṇa. The younger brother of Bharata, Lakṣmaṇa, however, split them with his whetted arrows while they had not yet reached him. (69)

verses.text:
स तान् छित्त्वा शितैर्बाणैर्लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा।
आददे निशितं बाणं ज्वलन्तमिव तेजसा॥ ७०॥
verses.m: Having torn them with his sharp arrows, Lakṣmaṇa, the destroyer of hostile champions, seized a whetted shaft, which was flaming as it were with splendour. (70)

verses.text:
तमादाय धनुःश्रेष्ठे योजयामास लक्ष्मणः।
विचकर्ष च वेगेन विससर्ज च सायकम्॥ ७१॥
verses.m: Laying hold of it, Lakṣmaṇa set it to his excellent bow, pulled its string to full stretch and shot the shaft with impetuosity. (71)

verses.text:
पूर्णायतविसृष्टेन शरेण नतपर्वणा।
ललाटे राक्षसश्रेष्ठमाजघान स वीर्यवान्॥ ७२॥
verses.m: Nay, with that flat-jointed arrow, which was discharged after the string had been stretched to full length, the valiant Lakṣmaṇa struck Atikāya (the foremost of ogres) in the brow. (72)

verses.text:
स ललाटे शरो मग्नस्तस्य भीमस्य रक्षसः।
ददृशे शोणितेनाक्तः पन्नगेन्द्र इवाचले॥ ७३॥
verses.m: Sunk into the forehead of that terrible ogre and stained with blood, that arrow looked like a ruler of serpents clinging to a mountain. (73)

verses.text:
राक्षसः प्रचकम्पेऽथ लक्ष्मणेषु प्रपीडितः।
रुद्रबाणहतं घोरं यथा त्रिपुरगोपुरम्॥ ७४॥
verses.m: Severely injured by the shaft of Lakṣmaṇa, the ogre forthwith shook violently like the formidable gate of Tripura (a city built of gold, silver and iron in the heaven, in the airspace as well as on the earth by the demon Maya and burnt by Rudra) struck with the arrow of Rudra (the god of destruction).(74)

verses.text:
चिन्तयामास चाश्वास्य विमृश्य च महाबलः।
साधु बाणनिपातेन श्लाघनीयोऽसि मे रिपुः॥ ७५॥
verses.m: Nay, recovering his breath and reflecting for a moment, the ogre, who was endowed with extraordinary might, contemplated upon his course of action. “By discharging this arrow against me, as you have done, you have turned out an enemy eminently worthy of praise by me!” (75)

verses.text:
विधायैवं विदार्यास्यं नियम्य च महाभुजौ।
स रथोपस्थमास्थाय रथेन प्रचचार ह॥ ७६॥
verses.m: Distending his mouth and speaking to him as aforesaid, nay, controlling his mighty arms and taking his seat in the rear of the chariot, he pressed forward in his chariot. (76)

verses.text:
एवं त्रीन् पञ्च सप्तेति सायकान् राक्षसर्षभः।
आददे संदधे चापि विचकर्षोत्ससर्ज च॥ ७७॥
verses.m: Atikāya, a bull among the ogres, seized hold of one, three, five and seven arrows (respectively) and put them to his bow, stretched the string to full length and let them fly. (77)

verses.text:
ते बाणाः कालसंकाशा राक्षसेन्द्रधनुश्च्युताः।
हेमपुङ्खा रविप्रख्याश्चक्रुर्दीप्तमिवाम्बरम्॥ ७८॥
verses.m: Shot from the bow of Atikāya (a ruler of ogres), those golden-feathered arrows, which resembled Death and shone like the sun, set the firmament ablaze, as it were. (78)

verses.text:
ततस्तान् राक्षसोत्सृष्टान् शरौघान् राघवानुजः।
असम्भ्रान्तः प्रचिच्छेद निशितैर्बहुभिः शरैः॥ ७९॥
verses.m: Remaining unruffled, the younger brother of Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) thereupon cut off with his numerous whetted shafts the aforesaid volleys of arrows discharged by the ogre. (79)

verses.text:
ताञ्शरान् युधि सम्प्रेक्ष्य निकृत्तान् रावणात्मजः।
चुकोप त्रिदशेन्द्रारिर्जग्राह निशितं शरम्॥ ८०॥
verses.m: Duly perceiving those arrows cut down on the field of battle. Atikāya (sprung from the loins of Rāvaṇa), an enemy of Indra, the ruler of gods, flew into a rage and took hold of a sharpened arrow. (80)

verses.text:
स संधाय महातेजास्तं बाणं सहसोत्सृजत्।
तेन सौमित्रिमायान्तमाजघान स्तनान्तरे॥ ८१॥
verses.m: Putting that arrow to his bow, Atikāya, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, precipitately shot it. With that he struck Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā), as he was aiming at his breast. (81)

verses.text:
अतिकायेन सौमित्रिस्ताडितो युधि वक्षसि।
सुस्राव रुधिरं तीव्रं मदं मत्त इव द्विपः॥ ८२॥
verses.m: Hit in the breast by Atikāya on the battlefield, Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā) began to bleed profusely even as an elephant in rut would discharge ichor. (82)

verses.text:
स चकार तदात्मानं विशल्यं सहसा विभुः।
जग्राह च शरं तीक्ष्णमस्त्रेणापि समाददे॥ ८३॥
verses.m: The all-powerful Laksmaṇa (who was a part manifestation of Lord Viṣṇu) then speedily rid himself of the shaft, seized hold of a sharp arrow and also charged it with a mystic spell. (83)

verses.text:
आग्नेयेन तदास्त्रेण योजयामास सायकम्।
स जज्वाल तदा बाणो धनुष्यस्य महात्मनः॥ ८४॥
verses.m: On that occasion he charged his arrow with the missile presided over by the god of fire. Placed on the bow of the high-souled prince, that arrow shot forth flames. (84)

verses.text:
अतिकायोऽतितेजस्वी रौद्रमस्त्रं समाददे।
तेन बाणं भुजङ्गाभं हेमपुङ्खमयोजयत्॥ ८५॥
verses.m: Atikāya, who was endowed with surpassing energy, pressed into service a fearful mystic missile and charged a serpent-like golden-feathered arrow with it. (85)

verses.text:
तदस्त्रं ज्वलितं घोरं लक्ष्मणः शरमाहितम्।
अतिकायाय चिक्षेप कालदण्डमिवान्तकः॥ ८६॥
verses.m: In the meantime, Lakṣmaṇa shot at Atikāya that flaming and formidable arrow in the form of a mystic missile charged with occult power, even as Death would hurl his rod of destruction. (86)

verses.text:
आग्नेयास्त्राभिसंयुक्तं दृष्ट्वा बाणं निशाचरः।
उत्ससर्ज तदा बाणं रौद्रं सूर्यास्त्रयोजितम्॥ ८७॥
verses.m: Seeing the arrow charged with a missile presided over by the god of fire, the prowler of the night, Atikāya, forthwith discharged an arrow charged with a missile presided over by the sun-god. (87)

verses.text:
तावुभावम्बरे बाणावन्योन्यमभिजघ्नतुः।
तेजसा सम्प्रदीप्ताग्रौ क्रुद्धाविव भुजङ्गमौ॥ ८८॥
verses.m: Both the aforesaid arrows, whose heads were flaming with fire, struck each other in space like two furious serpents. (88)

verses.text: तावन्योन्यं विनिर्दह्य पेततुः पृथिवीतले॥ ८९॥
verses.m: Having burnt each other, they fell to the earth’s surface. (89)

verses.text:
निरर्चिषौ भस्मकृतौ न भ्राजेते शरोत्तमौ।
तावुभौ दीप्यमानौ स्म न भ्राजेते महीतले॥ ९०॥
verses.m: The two excellent arrows, even though they were both glowing, did not shine forth any longer on the earth’s surface, in that they had ceased to emit flames and had been reduced to ashes. (90)

verses.text:
ततोऽतिकायः संक्रुद्धस्त्वाष्ट्रमैषीकमुत्सृजत्।
ततश्चिच्छेद सौमित्रिरस्त्रमैन्द्रेण वीर्यवान्॥ ९१॥
verses.m: Seized with fury, Atikāya thereupon discharged an arrow of reed charged with a missile presided over by Twaṣṭā (the architect of gods). The valiant son of Sumitrā, Lakṣmaṇa, thereupon split it with a missile presided over by Indra, ruler of gods. (91)

verses.text:
ऐषीकं निहतं दृष्ट्वा कुमारो रावणात्मजः।
याम्येनास्त्रेण संक्रुद्धो योजयामास सायकम्॥ ९२॥
verses.m: Enraged to find his arrow of reed struck down by Lakṣmaṇa, Prince Atikāya, sprung from the loins of Rāvaṇa, charged an arrow with a missile presided over by Yama (the god of retribution). (92)

verses.text:
ततस्तदस्त्रं चिक्षेप लक्ष्मणाय निशाचरः।
वायव्येन तदस्त्रेण निजघान स लक्ष्मणः॥ ९३॥
verses.m: The ranger of the night then shot it at Lakṣmaṇa. The celebrated Lakṣmaṇa, however, struck it down with a missile presided over by the wind-god. (93)

verses.text:
अथैनं शरधाराभिर्धाराभिरिव तोयदः।
अभ्यवर्षत संक्रुद्धो लक्ष्मणो रावणात्मजम्॥ ९४॥
verses.m: Seized with fury, Lakṣmaṇa now covered this son of Rāvaṇa with hails of arrows even as a rainy cloud would cover one with torrents. (94)

verses.text:
तेऽतिकायं समासाद्य कवचे वज्रभूषिते।
भग्नाग्रशल्याः सहसा पेतुर्बाणा महीतले॥ ९५॥
verses.m: Duly reaching Atikāya, those arrows, however, had their points at the uppper end shattered against his coat of mail, which was encrusted with diamonds, and precipitately fell to the earth’s surface. (95)

verses.text:
तान्मोघानभिसम्प्रेक्ष्य लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा।
अभ्यवर्षत बाणानां सहस्रेण महायशाः॥ ९६॥
verses.m: Perceiving them infructuous, the illustrious Lakṣmaṇa, the destroyer of hostile champions, covered him with a thousand arrows. (96)

verses.text:
स वृष्यमाणो बाणौघैरतिकायो महाबलः।
अवध्यकवचः संख्ये राक्षसो नैव विव्यथे॥ ९७॥
verses.m: Though being covered with volleys of arrows on the battle-field, the aforesaid ogre, Atikāya, who was endowed with extraordinary might and whose cuirass was invulnerable, did not feel tormented at all. (97)

verses.text:
शरं चाशीविषाकारं लक्ष्मणाय व्यपासृजत्।
स तेन विद्धः सौमित्रिर्मर्मदेशे शरेण ह॥ ९८ ॥
मुहूर्तमात्रं निःसंज्ञो ह्यभवच्छत्रुतापनः।
ततः संज्ञामुपालभ्य चतुर्भिः सायकोत्तमैः॥ ९९ ॥
निजघान हयान् संख्ये सारथिं च महाबलः।
ध्वजस्योन्मथनं कृत्वा शरवर्षैररिंदमः॥ १००॥
verses.m: Nay, he discharged an arrow resembling a venomous serpent at Lakṣmaṇa. Pierced in a vital part by that arrow, the said son of Sumitrā, the tormentor of his enemies, actually fainted awhile: so the tradition goes. Tearing off the standard of his enemy with hails of his arrows on regaining his consciousness, Laksmaṇa, the tamer of his adversaries, who was endowed with extraordinary might, struck down on the battle-field the horses as well as the charioteer of Atikāya with four excellent arrows. (98—100)

verses.text:
असम्भ्रान्तः स सौमित्रिस्ताञ्शरानभिलक्षितान्।
मुमोच लक्ष्मणो बाणान् वधार्थं तस्य रक्षसः॥ १०१॥
verses.m: Remaining unconfounded, the celebrated Lakṣmaṇa, son of Sumitrā, discharged some well-known and selected arrows for the destruction of that ogre. (101)

verses.text:
न शशाक रुजं कर्तुं युधि तस्य नरोत्तमः।
अथैनमभ्युपागम्य वायुर्वाक्यमुवाच ह॥ १०२॥
verses.m: Lakṣmaṇa, the foremost of men, could not, however, inflict any injury on his person in combat. Approaching him, the wind-god presently spoke to him as follows, so the tradition goes: (102)

verses.text:
ब्रह्मदत्तवरो ह्येष अवध्यकवचावृतः।
ब्राह्मेणास्त्रेण भिन्ध्येनमेष वध्यो हि नान्यथा।
अवध्य एष ह्यन्येषामस्त्राणां कवची बली॥ १०३॥
verses.m: “This ogre, on whom a boon having been conferred by Brahmā, the creator, is actually clad in impenetrable armour. Therefore, pierce him with a missile presided over by Brahmā; for the cannot be killed otherwise. Protected with armour and full of might as he is, he is incapable of being killed with other missiles.” (103)

verses.text:
ततस्तु वायोर्वचनं निशम्य
सौमित्रिरिन्द्रप्रतिमानवीर्यः।
समादधे बाणमथोग्रवेगं
तद्ब्राह्ममस्त्रं सहसा नियुज्य॥ १०४॥
verses.m: Hearing the admonition of the wind-god and pressing into service the well-known missile presided over by Brahmā (the creator), the son of Sumitrā for his part, who was a compeer of Indra (the ruler of gods) in prowess, thereupon precipitately fitted to his bow an arrow of terrific velocity. (104)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् वरास्त्रे तु नियुज्यमाने
सौमित्रिणा बाणवरे शिताग्रे।
दिशश्च चन्द्रार्कमहाग्रहाश्च
नभश्च तत्रास ररास चोर्वी॥ १०५॥
verses.m: While that excellent missile, presided over by Brahmā, was for its part being infused into the foremost of arrows with a sharp point by the son of Sumitrā, the four quarters as well as the moon and the sun and the other major planets as also the vault of heaven shook and the earth creaked. (105)

verses.text:
तं ब्रह्मणोऽस्त्रेण नियुज्य चापे
शरं सपुङ्खं यमदूतकल्पम्।
सौमित्रिरिन्द्रारिसुतस्य तस्य
ससर्ज बाणं युधि वज्रकल्पम्॥ १०६॥
verses.m: Having charged that arrow, feathers and all, with the missile presided over by Brahmā, the creator, and placed it on his bow, the son of Sumitrā discharged that shaft, which now looked like a messenger of Death and was hard as adamant, at the aforesaid son of Rāvaṇa (an enemy of Indra) on the field of battle. (106)

verses.text:
तं लक्ष्मणोत्सृष्टविवृद्धवेगं
समापतन्तं श्वसनोग्रवेगम्।
सुपर्णवज्रोत्तमचित्रपुङ्खं
तदातिकायः समरे ददर्श॥ १०७॥
verses.m: Atikāya forthwith beheld on the battlefield the arrow shot by Lakṣmaṇa, which possessed the terrific velocity of the wind, was provided with lovely feathers resembling the wings of Garuḍa (the king of birds) and decked with excellent diamonds—flying towards Atikāya with redoubled speed. (107)

verses.text:
तं प्रेक्षमाणः सहसातिकायो
जघान बाणैर्निशितैरनेकैः।
स सायकस्तस्य सुपर्णवेग-
स्तथातिवेगेन जगाम पार्श्वम्॥ १०८॥
verses.m: Closely observing it, Atikāya forcibly struck it with numerous whetted shafts. Possessing as it did the swiftness of Garuḍa, that arrow none the less drew near him with terrific speed. (108)

verses.text:
तमागतं प्रेक्ष्य तदातिकायो
बाणं प्रदीप्तान्तककालकल्पम्।
जघान शक्त्यृष्टिगदाकुठारैः
शूलैः शरैश्चाप्यविपन्नचेष्टः॥ १०९॥
verses.m: Perceiving that flaming arrow terrible as Death and the Time-Spirit arrived, Atikāya forthwith struck it with javelins, spears, maces and axes as also with pikes and arrows with unceasing endeavour. (109)

verses.text:
तान्यायुधान्यद्भुतविग्रहाणि
मोघानि कृत्वा स शरोऽग्निदीप्तः।
प्रगृह्य तस्यैव किरीटजुष्टं
तदातिकायस्य शिरो जहार॥ ११०॥
verses.m: Rendering all the aforesaid weapons of wonderful shapes ineffectual, and transfixing the head of the selfsame Atikāya, which was covered with a diadem, that arrow blazing like fire forthwith severed it. (110)

verses.text:
तच्छिरः सशिरस्त्राणं लक्ष्मणेषुप्रमर्दितम्।
पपात सहसा भूमौ शृङ्गं हिमवतो यथा॥ १११॥
verses.m: Cut off by the arrow of Lakṣmaṇa, the aforesaid head with its diadem precipitately fell to the ground like a peak of the Himālaya mountain. (111)

verses.text:
तं भूमौ पतितं दृष्ट्वा विक्षिप्ताम्बरभूषणम्।
बभूवुर्व्यथिताः सर्वे हतशेषा निशाचराः॥ ११२॥
verses.m: All the ogres who had escaped being killed, felt distressed to behold the prince fallen on the ground, his raiment and adornments in disarray. (112)

verses.text:
ते विषण्णमुखा दीनाः प्रहारजनितश्रमाः।
विनेदुरुच्चैर्बहवः सहसा विस्वरैः स्वरैः॥ ११३॥
verses.m: With their faces downcast, nay, feeling miserable and exhausted with blows, many of them burst into a loud wail in discordant tone. (113)

verses.text:
ततस्तत्परितं याता निरपेक्षा निशाचराः।
पुरीमभिमुखा भीता द्रवन्तो नायके हते॥ ११४॥
verses.m: Their leader having been killed, the rangers of the night, who had now become listless, hastily withdrew running from that place, frightened as they were, with their faces turned towards the city. (114)

verses.text:
प्रहर्षयुक्ता बहवस्तु वानराः
प्रफुल्लपद्मप्रतिमाननास्तदा।
अपूजयँल्लक्ष्मणमिष्टभागिनं
हते रिपौ भीमबले दुरासदे॥ ११५॥
verses.m: Filled with extreme delight on their enemy, who was endowed with terrible might and was difficult to approach, having been killed, numerous monkeys for their part, whose faces resembled full-blown lotuses, forthwith paid their homage to Lakṣmaṇa, who had secured victory for them. (115)

verses.text:
अतिबलमतिकायमभ्रकल्पं
युधि विनिपात्य स लक्ष्मणः प्रहृष्टः।
त्वरितमथ तदा स रामपार्श्वं
कपिनिवहैश्च सुपूजितो जगाम॥ ११६॥
verses.m: Greatly rejoiced and highly honoured by hosts of monkeys on having struck down in a duel Atikāya, who was endowed with surpassing might and looked like a mass of cloud, the aforesaid celebrated Lakṣmaṇa forthwith hastily sought the presence of Śrī Rāma on that occasion. (116)

verses.text:
अतिकायं हतं श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणेन महात्मना।
उद्वेगमगमद् राजा वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: On hearing of Atikāya having been killed by the high-souled Lakṣmaṇa, the king of Laṅkā gave way to anxiety and spoke as follows: (1)

verses.text:
धूम्राक्षः परमामर्षी सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः।
अकम्पनः प्रहस्तश्च कुम्भकर्णस्तथैव च॥ २॥
एते महाबला वीरा राक्षसा युद्धकाङ् क्षिणः।
जेतारः परसैन्यानां परैर्नित्यापराजिताः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Dhūmrākṣa, who was supremely intolerant, as well as Akampana, the foremost of all those skilled in the use of arms, as also Prahasta and, even so, Kumbhakarṇa—these gallant ogres, the conquerors of hostile forces, were endowed with extraordinary might, nay, longed for combat and remained ever unconquered by their enemies. (2-3)

verses.text:
ससैन्यास्ते हता वीरा रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा।
राक्षसाः सुमहाकाया नानाशस्त्रविशारदाः॥ ४॥
verses.m: The aforesaid valiant ogres of tremendous proportions, who were well-versed in the use of all weapons, have been killed with their battalions by Rāma of unwearied action. (4)

verses.text:
अन्ये च बहवः शूरा महात्मानो निपातिताः।
प्रख्यातबलवीर्येण पुत्रेणेन्द्रजिता मम॥ ५॥
तौ भ्रातरौ तदा बद्धौ घोरैर्दत्तवरैः शरैः।
यन्न शक्यं सुरैः सर्वैरसुरैर्वा महाबलैः॥ ६॥
मोक्तुं तद्बन्धनं घोरं यक्षगन्धर्वपन्नगैः।
तन्न जाने प्रभावैर्वा मायया मोहनेन वा॥ ७॥
verses.m: Many other heroes of gigantic proportions have also been struck down. The aforesaid two brothers, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, were bound the other day with formidable arrows, on which boons of infallibility had been conferred by Brahmā, by my eldest son, Indrajit, whose strength and prowess are widely known. That formidable bond of theirs, which could not be undone by all the gods or even by demons endowed with extraordinary might nor even by Yakṣas (a class of demigods), Gandharvas (celestial musicians) and Nāgas (a class of semi-divine beings having the face of a man and the tail of a serpent) became free by virtue of their superhuman powers or some conjuring trick or magical charm, which I do not know. (5—7)

verses.text:
शरबन्धाद् विमुक्तौ तौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।
ये योधा निर्गताः शूरा राक्षसा मम शासनात्॥ ८ ॥
ते सर्वे निहता युद्धे वानरैः सुमहाबलैः।
तं न पश्याम्यहं युद्धे योऽद्य रामं सलक्ष्मणम्॥ ९ ॥
नाशयेत् सबलं वीरं ससुग्रीवं विभीषणम्।
अहो सुबलवान् रामो महदस्त्रबलं च वै॥ १०॥
यस्य विक्रममासाद्य राक्षसा निधनं गताः।
तं मन्ये राघवं वीरं नारायणमनामयम्॥ ११॥
तद्भयाद्धि पुरी लङ्का पिहितद्वारतोरणा।
अप्रमत्तैश्च सर्वत्र गुल्मे रक्ष्या पुरी त्वियम्॥ १२॥
अशोकवनिका चैव यत्र सीताभिरक्ष्यते।
निष्क्रमो वा प्रवेशो वा ज्ञातव्यः सर्वदैव नः॥ १३॥
verses.m: The aforesaid two brothers, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, got liberated anyhow from the network of arrows. Nay, all the gallant ogre warriors who sallied forth at my command were killed in combat by the monkeys, who are endowed with exceptional might. “I do not see the warrior who should be able to make short work in combat today of the heroic Rāma with Lakṣmaṇa and his army as well as Vibhīṣaṇa accompanied by Sugrīva. Oh, really great is the power of Rāma’s missiles and exceptionally mighty is Rāma, on reaching the range of whose prowess the ogres have met their death. I recognize that heroic scion of Raghu to be no other than Lord Nārāyaṇa, who is proof against all ailment. Indeed, it is through fear of him that Laṅkā has its doors and outer gates ever closed. Nay, let this city of Laṅkā for its part, and especially the Aśoka grove, where Sītā is being guarded on all sides, be defended alongwith its garrisons by you, who have survived destruction, remaining vigilant all the time. Every exit from and entry into the city and the grove must be definitely known by us at all times. (8—13)

verses.text:
यत्र यत्र भवेद् गुल्मस्तत्र तत्र पुनः पुनः।
सर्वतश्चापि तिष्ठध्वं स्वैः स्वैः परिवृता बलैः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Wherever there is a garrison, exit and entry should be checked again and again. Surrounded by your respective troops, remain posted on all sides. (14)

verses.text:
द्रष्टव्यं च पदं तेषां वानराणां निशाचराः।
प्रदोषे वार्धरात्रे वा प्रत्यूषे वापि सर्वशः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Nay, the movements of the aforesaid monkeys should be watched by you, O prowlers of the night, in every way, whether there is dusk or midnight or even sunrise. (15)

verses.text:
नावज्ञा तत्र कर्तव्या वानरेषु कदाचन।
द्विषतां बलमुद्युक्तमापतत् किं स्थितं यथा॥ १६॥
verses.m: “No indifference should be shown to the monkeys at any time. It should be constantly observed whether the hostile army is zealously active, is advancing towards Laṅkā or stands where it was.” (16)

verses.text:
ततस्ते राक्षसाः सर्वे श्रुत्वा लङ्काधिपस्य तत्।
वचनं सर्वमातिष्ठन् यथावत् तु महाबलाः॥ १७॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid command of Rāvaṇa, the suzerain lord of Laṅkā, all those ogres for their part, who were endowed with extraordinary might, duly carried it out forthwith in its entirety. (17)

verses.text:
तान् सर्वान् हि समादिश्य रावणो राक्षसाधिपः।
मन्युशल्यं वहन् दीनः प्रविवेश स्वमालयम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: Having duly enjoined them all as aforesaid, Rāvaṇa, the suzerain lord of ogres, actually penetrated deep into his palace, carrying the thorn of wrath in his bosom, miserable as he was. (18)

verses.text:
ततः स संदीपितकोपवह्नि-
र्निशाचराणामधिपो महाबलः।
तदेव पुत्रव्यसनं विचिन्तयन्
मुहुर्मुहुश्चैव तदा विनिःश्वसन्॥ १९॥
verses.m: The fire of wrath having been inflamed in him, that suzerain lord of ogres, who was endowed with extraordinary might, then remained brooding on the self same fall of his son, Atikāya, and also sighing again and again at that time. (19)

verses.text:
ततो हतान् राक्षसपुङ्गवांस्तान्
देवान्तकादित्रिशिरोऽतिकायान्।
रक्षोगणास्तत्र हतावशिष्टा-
स्ते रावणाय त्वरिताः शशंसुः॥ १॥
verses.m: Those ogre hosts who had survived those who had been killed, thereupon hastily reported to Rāvaṇa about the well-known bulls among ogres as had been made short work of, viz., Devāntaka, Triśirā, Atikāya and others. (1)

verses.text:
ततो हतांस्तान् सहसा निशम्य
राजा महाबाष्पपरिप्लुताक्षः।
पुत्रक्षयं भ्रातृवधं च घोरं
विचिन्त्य राजा विपुलं प्रदध्यौ॥ २॥
verses.m: Hearing all of a sudden of those who had been killed, the king found his eyes bathed in copious tears. Brooding on the destruction of his sons as well as on the terrible fall of his brothers, the king became exceedingly thoughtful. (2)

verses.text:
ततस्तु राजानमुदीक्ष्य दीनं
शोकार्णवे सम्परिपुप्लुवानम्।
रथर्षभो राक्षसराजसूनु-
स्तमिन्द्रजिद् वाक्यमिदं बभाषे॥ ३॥
verses.m: Perceiving the king disconsolate and deeply plunged in an ocean of grief, Indrajit for his part, the eldest son of Rāvaṇa, the ruler of ogres, and the foremost of car-warriors, thereupon submitted to him as follows: (3)

verses.text:
न तात मोहं परिगन्तुमर्हसे
यत्रेन्द्रजिज्जीवति नैर्ऋतेश।
नेन्द्रारिबाणाभिहतो हि कश्चित्
प्राणान् समर्थः समरेऽभिपातुम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “While Indrajit, your son, is alive, O lord of ogres (the progeny of Nirṛti), you ought not to give way to despair, dear father; for, struck with the arrows of Indra’s enemy (in my person) none is able to preserve his life on the battlefield. (4)

verses.text:
पश्याद्य रामं सह लक्ष्मणेन
मद्बाणनिर्भिन्नविकीर्णदेहम्।
गतायुषं भूमितले शयानं
शितैः शरैराचितसर्वगात्रम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Behold Rāma lying dead alongwith Lakṣmaṇa on the earth’s surface today, his body thrown about, torn to pieces by my shafts, and covered all over with my sharp arrows clinging fast to it (the body). (5)

verses.text:
इमां प्रतिज्ञां शृणु शक्रशत्रोः
सुनिश्चितां पौरुषदैवयुक्ताम्।
अद्यैव रामं सह लक्ष्मणेन
संतर्पयिष्यामि शरैरमोघैः॥ ६ ॥
verses.m: “Listen to the following vow of Indra’s enemy (myself), which is fully determined and is backed by manliness and divine blessing: I shall this very day overwhelm Rāma alongwith Lakṣmaṇa with my arrows that never miss their target. (6)

verses.text:
अद्येन्द्रवैवस्वतविष्णुरुद्र-
साध्याश्च वैश्वानरचन्द्रसूर्याः।
द्रक्ष्यन्ति मे विक्रममप्रमेयं
विष्णोरिवोग्रं बलियज्ञवाटे॥ ७ ॥
verses.m: “Today Indra (the ruler of gods), Yama (son of the sun-god), Viṣṇu (the Protector of the universe), Rudra (the god of destruction) and the Sādhyas (a class of gods), the god of fire, the moon-god and the sun-god will witness my immeasurable prowess even as they did the terrible prowess of Viṣṇu (as a dwarf in the form of measuring the entire universe in a couple of strides) in the enclosure where a sacrifice was being performed by the demon king, Bali.” (7)

verses.text:
स एवमुक्त्वा त्रिदशेन्द्रशत्रु-
रापृच्छ्य राजानमदीनसत्त्वः।
समारुरोहानिलतुल्यवेगं
रथं खरश्रेष्ठसमाधियुक्तम्॥ ८ ॥
verses.m: Having bragged as aforesaid, and taking leave of the king, that enemy of Indra (the ruler of gods), who was undepressed in spirit, duly ascended his chariot, swift as the wind, which was drawn by donkeys and was equipped with implements of war (in the shape of a bow, sword etc.). (8)

verses.text:
समास्थाय महातेजा रथं हरिरथोपमम्।
जगाम सहसा तत्र यत्र युद्धमरिंदमः॥ ९ ॥
verses.m: Duly taking his seat in the chariot, which resembled the chariot of Indra, Indrajit (the tamer of his enemies), who was endowed with extraordinary energy, precipitately sought the battlefield. (9)

verses.text:
तं प्रस्थितं महात्मानमनुजग्मुर्महाबलाः।
संहर्षमाणा बहवो धनुःप्रवरपाणयः॥ १०॥
verses.m: Showing great enthusiasm, numerous ogres, who were endowed with extraordinary might and carried excellent bows in their hands, followed the gigantic prince, even as he departed. (10)

verses.text:
गजस्कन्धगताः केचित् केचित् परमवाजिभिः।
व्याघ्रवृश्चिकमार्जारखरोष्ट्रैश्च भुजङ्गमैः॥ ११॥
वराहैः श्वापदैः सिंहैर्जम्बुकैः पर्वतोपमैः।
काकहंसमयूरैश्च राक्षसा भीमविक्रमाः॥ १२॥
verses.m: Some ogres of terrible prowess rode on the back of elephants, while others rode on the back of excellent horses, tigers, scorpions, cats, donkeys and camels as well as on (the back of) serpents, boars, beasts of prey such as lions, jackals as large as hills, as also on the back of crows, swans and peacocks. (11-12)

verses.text:
प्रासपट्टिशनिस्त्रिंशपरश्वधगदाधराः।
भुशुण्डिमुद्गरायष्टिशतघ्नीपरिघायुधाः ॥ १३॥
verses.m: They carried lances, sharp-edged spears, swords, axes and maces and were armed with Bhuśuṇḍis (probably a kind of fire-arm), mallets, Āyaṣṭis, Śataghnīs (a stone or cylindrical piece of wood studded with iron pikes) and Parighas (an iron bludgeon or club studded with iron). (13)

verses.text:
स शङ्खनिनदैः पूर्णैर्भेरीणां चापि निःस्वनैः।
जगाम त्रिदशेन्द्रारिराजिं वेगेन वीर्यवान्॥ १४॥
verses.m: Accompanied by full blasts of conches as well as by the sounds of kettledrums, that valiant enemy of Indra (the ruler of gods) proceeded with all speed to the field of battle. (14)

verses.text:
स शङ्खशशिवर्णेन छत्रेण रिपुसूदनः।
रराज प्रतिपूर्णेन नभश्चन्द्रमसा यथा॥ १५॥
verses.m: With his parasol white as conch and the moon, that destroyer of his enemies shone like the firmament with the full moon. (15)

verses.text:
वीज्यमानस्ततो वीरो हैमैर्हेमविभूषणः।
चारुचामरमुख्यैश्च मुख्यः सर्वधनुष्मताम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: The hero, who was the foremost of all archers and was decked with gold ornaments, was being fanned at that time with the foremost of lovely whisks with handles of gold. (16)

verses.text:
स तु दृष्ट्वा विनिर्यान्तं बलेन महता वृतम्।
राक्षसाधिपतिः श्रीमान् रावणः पुत्रमब्रवीत्॥ १७॥
verses.m: Seeing his son, Indrajit, sallying forth surrounded by a huge army, the glorious Rāvaṇa, the suzerain lord of ogres, for his part spoke to him as follows: (17)

verses.text:
त्वमप्रतिरथः पुत्र त्वया वै वासवो जितः।
किं पुनर्मानुषं धृष्यं निहनिष्यसि राघवम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “There is no warrior who can stand as your rival, my son; by you Indra (the ruler of gods) was actually conquered. Much more will you (be able to) kill a mortal, Rāma (a scion of Raghu), who is subject to being assailed.” (18)

verses.text:
तथोक्तो राक्षसेन्द्रेण प्रत्यगृह्णान्महाशिषः।
ततस्त्विन्द्रजिता लङ्का सूर्यप्रतिमतेजसा॥ १९॥
रराजाप्रतिवीर्येण द्यौरिवार्केण भास्वता।
स सम्प्राप्य महातेजा युद्धभूमिमरिंदमः॥ २०॥
स्थापयामास रक्षांसि रथं प्रति समन्ततः।
ततस्तु हुतभोक्तारं हुतभुक्सदृशप्रभः॥ २१॥
जुहुवे राक्षसश्रेष्ठो विधिवन्मन्त्रसत्तमैः।
स हविर्लाजसत्कारैर्माल्यगन्धपुरस्कृतैः॥ २२॥
जुहुवे पावकं तत्र राक्षसेन्द्रः प्रतापवान्।
शस्त्राणि शरपत्राणि समिधोऽथ बिभीतकाः॥ २३॥
लोहितानि च वासांसि स्रुवं कार्ष्णायसं तथा।
स तत्राग्निं समास्तीर्य शरपत्रैः सतोमरैः॥ २४॥
छागस्य कृष्णवर्णस्य गलं जग्राह जीवतः।
सकृदेव समिद्धस्य विधूमस्य महार्चिषः॥ २५॥
बभूवुस्तानि लिङ्गानि विजयं यान्यदर्शयन्।
प्रदक्षिणावर्तशिखस्तप्तकाञ्चनसंनिभः ॥ २६॥
हविस्तत् प्रतिजग्राह पावकः स्वयमुत्थितः।
सोऽस्त्रमाहारयामास ब्राह्ममस्त्रविशारदः॥ २७॥
धनुश्चात्मरथं चैव सर्वं तत्राभ्यमन्त्रयत्।
तस्मिन्नाहूयमानेऽस्त्रे हूयमाने च पावके।
सार्कग्रहेन्दुनक्षत्रं वितत्रास नभस्थलम्॥ २८॥
verses.m: Encouraged as aforesaid by the ruler of ogres, the prince gladly accepted his mighty blessings. Thereupon Laṅkā for its part shone with Indrajit, who vied with the sun in brilliance and who was matchless in valour, even as the firmament with the brilliant sun. Duly reaching the battlefield, Indrajit, the tamer of his foes, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, ranged the ogres around his chariot on all sides. Thereupon Indrajit, the foremost of ogres, who vied with the god of fire in brilliance, worshipped the fire according to the traditional rites, while reciting the best of Mantras (sacred texts). Having worshipped the sacred fire on the battlefield with offerings of parched grains of rice preceded by flowers and sandal-paste, that mighty ogre chief poured oblation into it. In that sacrificial performance weapons served the purpose of reeds (which are strewn about the fire to ward off evil forces), nay, chips of a Bibhītaka tree served as fuel for the sacrificial fire, again red pieces of cloth alone were used and the sacrificial ladle was made of iron. Duly strewing the fire there with reeds (in the form of other weapons) accompanied by lances, Indrajit elasped the neck of a live goat of dark hue (for offering it to the fire). From the fire, which was set ablaze by that offering having been thrown into it but once, and was free from smoke and had burst into mighty flames, appeared such signs as had betokened victory in the past. Risen into view, the god of fire, who shone brightly like refined gold and whose flames turned towards the right, accepted that offering in person. Indrajit, who was an adept in the use of mystic missiles, invoked the missile presided over by Brahmā, the creator, and charged the bow as well as his chariot and all with the invocatory spell on the field of battle. While that missile was being invoked and the sacrificial fire was being propitiated through oblations, the vault of heaven including the sun, the moon and other planets and lunar mansions shook with fear. (19—28)

verses.text:
स पावकं पावकदीप्ततेजा
हुत्वा महेन्द्रप्रतिमप्रभावः।
सचापबाणासिरथाश्वसूतः
खेऽन्तर्दधेऽऽत्मानमचिन्त्यवीर्यः ॥ २९॥
verses.m: Having propitiated the fire with offerings, Indrajit, who was flaming with lustre like fire and vied with the mighty Indra, the ruler of gods, in might, and who was endowed with inconceivable prowess, hid himself from view in the sky with bow, arrows, sword, chariot, horses, charioteer and all. (29)

verses.text:
ततो हयरथाकीर्णं पताकाध्वजशोभितम्।
निर्ययौ राक्षसबलं नर्दमानं युयुत्सया॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Thereupon the army of ogres, which was crowded with horses and chariots and graced with pennants and flags, sallied forth roaring with a longing to fight. (30)

verses.text:
ते शरैर्बहुभिश्चित्रैस्तीक्ष्णवेगैरलंकृतैः।
तोमरैरङ्कुशैश्चापि वानराञ्जघ्नुराहवे॥ ३१॥
verses.m: They began to strike the monkeys on the battlefield with many wonderful and ornamented arrows of great velocity, lances and goads, too. (31)

verses.text:
रावणिस्तु सुसंक्रुद्धस्तान् निरीक्ष्य निशाचरान्।
हृष्टा भवन्तो युध्यन्तु वानराणां जिघांसया॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Keenly observing those prowlers of the night, Indrajit, son of Rāvaṇa, for his part, who was highly enraged, said to them, “Be of good cheer and fight with the intention of making short work of the monkeys.” (32)

verses.text:
ततस्ते राक्षसाः सर्वे गर्जन्तो जयकाङ् क्षिणः।
अभ्यवर्षंस्ततो घोरं वानरान् शरवृष्टिभिः॥ ३३॥
verses.m: Roaring and longing for a victory, all those ogres thereupon terribly covered the monkeys on all sides with hails of arrows. (33)

verses.text:
स तु नालीकनाराचैर्गदाभिर्मुसलैरपि।
रक्षोभिः संवृतः संख्ये वानरान् विचकर्ष ह॥ ३४॥
verses.m: Remaining concealed from view by the ogres, Indrajit for his part began to destroy the monkeys on the battlefield with his Nālīkas (broad-headed arrows), steel arrows, maces and clubs too: so the tradition goes. (34)

verses.text:
ते वध्यमानाः समरे वानराः पादपायुधाः।
अभ्यवर्षन्त सहसा रावणिं शैलपादपैः॥ ३५॥
verses.m: While being struck on the battlefield by Indrajit, as aforesaid, all the monkeys, who were armed with trees, covered the son of Rāvaṇa all of a sudden (where he stood concealed and from where he discharged his arrows and other weapons) with crags and trees. (35)

verses.text:
इन्द्रजित् तु तदा क्रुद्धो महातेजा महाबलः।
वानराणां शरीराणि व्यधमद् रावणात्मजः॥ ३६॥
verses.m: Seized with wrath, the exceptionally mighty Indrajit, son of Rāvaṇa, for his part, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, then began to tear into pieces the bodies of the monkeys. (36)

verses.text:
शरेणैकेन च हरीन् नव पञ्च च सप्त च।
बिभेद समरे क्रुद्धो राक्षसान् सम्प्रहर्षयन्॥ ३७॥
verses.m: Nay, filled with rage, Indrajit pierced with a single arrow as many as nine, five and seven monkeys, respectively, on the field of battle, bringing excessive delight to the ogres. (37)

verses.text:
स शरैः सूर्यसंकाशैः शातकुम्भविभूषणैः।
वानरान् समरे वीरः प्रममाथ सुदुर्जयः॥ ३८॥
verses.m: The heroic Indrajit, who was exceedingly difficult to conquer, exterminated the monkeys on the field of battle with his arrows, which glittered like the sun and were decorated with gold. (38)

verses.text:
ते भिन्नगात्राः समरे वानराः शरपीडिताः।
पेतुर्मथितसंकल्पाः सुरैरिव महासुराः॥ ३९॥
verses.m: Overwhelmed by the arrows, the aforesaid monkeys, whose limbs were pierced, and whose designs had been frustrated, fell like great demons oppressed by gods with their arrows. (39)

verses.text:
ते तपन्तमिवादित्यं घोरैर्बाणगभस्तिभिः।
अभ्यधावन्त संक्रुद्धाः संयुगे वानरर्षभाः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: Highly enraged, the said bulls among the monkeys, rushed on the field of battle in the direction of Indrajit, who was blazing like the sun with his rays in the form of arrows. (40)

verses.text:
ततस्तु वानराः सर्वे भिन्नदेहा विचेतसः।
व्यथिता विद्रवन्ति स्म रुधिरेण समुक्षिताः॥ ४१॥
verses.m: Bathed in blood, their bodies mutilated, nay, agonized and distressed, all the monkeys for their part thereupon stampeded. (41)

verses.text:
रामस्यार्थे पराक्रम्य वानरास्त्यक्तजीविताः।
नर्दन्तस्तेऽनिवृत्तास्तु समरे सशिलायुधाः॥ ४२॥
verses.m: Having exhibited their prowess, the monkeys, who had staked their lives in the cause of Śrī Rāma, did not retrace their steps and kept roaring on the battlefield, armed with rocks. (42)

verses.text:
ते द्रुमैः पर्वताग्रैश्च शिलाभिश्च प्लवंगमाः।
अभ्यवर्षन्त समरे रावणिं समवस्थिताः॥ ४३॥
verses.m: Remaining firm on the battlefield, the aforesaid monkeys began to cover the son of Rāvaṇa with trees, mountain peaks and rocks. (43)

verses.text:
तं द्रुमाणां शिलानां च वर्षं प्राणहरं महत्।
व्यपोहत महातेजा रावणिः समितिंजयः॥ ४४॥
verses.m: Indrajit, son of Rāvaṇa, who was ever victorious in combat and was endowed with extraordinary energy, dispersed that mighty and deadly hail of trees and rocks. (44)

verses.text:
ततः पावकसंकाशैः शरैराशीविषोपमैः।
वानराणामनीकानि बिभेद समरे प्रभुः॥ ४५॥
verses.m: The mighty ogre thereupon began to split the simian ranks on the battlefield with his arrows, which shone brightly as fire and resembled venomous serpents. (45)

verses.text:
अष्टादशशरैस्तीक्ष्णैः स विद्ध्वा गन्धमादनम्।
विव्याध नवभिश्चैव नलं दूरादवस्थितम्॥ ४६॥
verses.m: Having pierced Gandhamādana with eighteen penetrating arrows, he struck Nala too, standing some way off, with nine others. (46)

verses.text:
सप्तभिस्तु महावीर्यो मैन्दं मर्मविदारणैः।
पञ्चभिर्विशिखैश्चैव गजं विव्याध संयुगे॥ ४७॥
verses.m: Indrajit, who was endowed with extraordinary prowess, for his part assailed Mainda with seven shafts, which tore his vital parts and pierced Gaja on the battlefield with five. (47)

verses.text:
जाम्बवन्तं तु दशभिर्नीलं त्रिंशद्भिरेव च।
सुग्रीवमृषभं चैव सोऽङ्गदं द्विविदं तथा॥ ४८॥
घोरैर्दत्तवरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्निष्प्राणानकरोत् तदा।
अन्यानपि तथा मुख्यान् वानरान् बहुभिः शरैः॥ ४९॥
अर्दयामास संक्रुद्धः कालाग्निरिव मूर्च्छितः।
स शरैः सूर्यसंकाशैः सुमुक्तैः शीघ्रगामिभिः॥ ५०॥
वानराणामनीकानि निर्ममन्थ महारणे।
आकुलां वानरीं सेनां शरजालेन पीडिताम्॥ ५१॥
हृष्टः स परया प्रीत्या ददर्श क्षतजोक्षिताम्।
पुनरेव महातेजा राक्षसेन्द्रात्मजो बली॥ ५२॥
verses.m: He for his part struck Jāmbavān with ten and Nīla with thirty arrows; and with dreadful and sharp arrows, on which a boon of infallibility had been bestowed by Brahmā he forthwith rendered lifeless as it were Sugrīva as well as Ṛṣabha, Aṅgada and Dwivida. Infuriated like the swollen fire of universal destruction, he tormented likewise with many shafts other leading monkeys too. With his swift-going arrows shot with skill and shining brightly like the sun he thoroughly agitated the simian ranks in that major conflict. Feeling rejoiced, that mighty son of the king of ogres, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, beheld once more with supreme gratification the army of monkeys overwhelmed with a rain of arrows and, therefore, agitated and bathed in blood. (48—52)

verses.text:
संसृज्य बाणवर्षं च शस्त्रवर्षं च दारुणम्।
ममर्द वानरानीकं परितस्त्विन्द्रजिद् बली॥ ५३॥
verses.m: Pouring a hail of shafts and a cruel shower of missiles, the mighty Indrajit crushed the army of monkeys on all sides. (53)

verses.text:
स्वसैन्यमुत्सृज्य समेत्य तूर्णं
महाहवे वानरवाहिनीषु।
अदृश्यमानः शरजालमुग्रं
ववर्ष नीलाम्बुधरो यथाम्बु॥ ५४॥
verses.m: Leaving the part of space above his own army and moving speedily to the space above the monkey forces in that major conflict while remaining still invisible, Indrajit let fall a formidable hail of shafts even as a dark rainy cloud would pour water. (54)

verses.text:
ते शक्रजिद्बाणविशीर्णदेहा
मायाहता विस्वरमुन्नदन्तः।
रणे निपेतुर्हरयोऽद्रिकल्पा
यथेन्द्रवज्राभिहता नगेन्द्राः॥ ५५॥
verses.m: Victims of his conjuring tricks, their bodies torn into pieces by the arrows of Indrajit, the aforesaid monkeys, who resembled mountains in size, fell in the fray shrieking in discordant tones like lordly mountains struck by the thunderbolt of Indra, the ruler of gods. (55)

verses.text:
ते केवलं संददृशुः शिताग्रान्
बाणान् रणे वानरवाहिनीषु।
मायाविगूढं च सुरेन्द्रशत्रुं
न चात्र तं राक्षसमप्यपश्यन्॥ ५६॥
verses.m: They perceived only sharp-pointed shafts descending in the course of the conflict on the simian ranks. They could not, however, see there that ogre, the enemy of Indra (the ruler of gods), who remained fully concealed by his magical power. (56)

verses.text:
ततः स रक्षोधिपतिर्महात्मा
सर्वा दिशो बाणगणैः शिताग्रैः।
प्रच्छादयामास रविप्रकाशै-
र्विदारयामास च वानरेन्द्रान्॥ ५७॥
verses.m: Thereupon that gigantic ruler of ogres thickly covered all the four quarters with volleys of his sharp-pointed shafts, shining like the sun, and destroyed the monkey chiefs. (57)

verses.text:
स शूलनिस्त्रिंशपरश्वधानि
व्याविद्धदीप्तानलसप्रभाणि।
सविस्फुलिङ्गोज्ज्वलपावकानि
ववर्ष तीव्रं प्लवगेन्द्रसैन्ये॥ ५८॥
verses.m: He let fall on the army of monkey chiefs a violent shower of pikes, swords and axes, shining like a swollen and flaming fire and shooting forth incandescent flames with sparks. (58)

verses.text:
ततो ज्वलनसंकाशैर्बाणैर्वानरयूथपाः।
ताडिताः शक्रजिद्बाणैः प्रफुल्ला इव किंशुकाः॥ ५९॥
verses.m: Struck with the arrows of Indrajit—arrows which shone brightly as fire—the monkey generals thereupon looked like Kiṁśuka trees bearing crimson flowers. (59)

verses.text:
तेऽन्योन्यमभिसर्पन्तो निनदन्तश्च विस्वरम्।
राक्षसेन्द्रास्त्रनिर्भिन्ना निपेतुर्वानरर्षभाः॥ ६०॥
verses.m: Gliding towards one another when pierced by the missiles of Indrajit, the ruler of ogres, the aforesaid bulls among monkeys fell down screaming in discordant tones. (60)

verses.text:
उदीक्षमाणा गगनं केचिन्नेत्रेषु ताडिताः।
शरैर्विविशुरन्योन्यं पेतुश्च जगतीतले॥ ६१॥
verses.m: Struck with arrows in their eyes while looking up towards the sky, some monkeys clasped one another and fell down on the earth’s surface. (61)

verses.text:
हनूमन्तं च सुग्रीवमङ्गदं गन्धमादनम्।
जाम्बवन्तं सुषेणं च वेगदर्शिनमेव च॥ ६२॥
मैन्दं च द्विविदं नीलं गवाक्षं गवयं तथा।
केसरिं हरिलोमानं विद्युद्दंष्ट्रं च वानरम्॥ ६३॥
सूर्याननं ज्योतिर्मुखं तथा दधिमुखं हरिम्।
पावकाक्षं नलं चैव कुमुदं चैव वानरम्॥ ६४॥
प्रासैः शूलैः शितैर्बाणैरिन्द्रजिन्मन्त्रसंहितैः।
विव्याध हरिशार्दूलान् सर्वांस्तान् राक्षसोत्तमः॥ ६५॥
verses.m: With lances, pikes and sharp arrows charged with sacred formula (Mantras), Indrajit, the foremost of ogres, pierced all the well-known tigers among monkeys, viz., Hanumān and Sugrīva, Aṅgada, Gandhamādana, Jāmbavān and Suṣeṇa as well as Vegadarśi and Mainda, Dwivida, Nīla, Gavākṣa, Gavaya and Kesari, Harilomā and the monkey Vidyudda√ṣṭra, Sūryānana, Jyotirmukha, and the monkey Dadhimukha, Pāvakākṣa as also Nala as well as the monkey Kumuda. (62—65)

verses.text:
स वै गदाभिर्हरियूथमुख्यान्
निर्भिद्य बाणैस्तपनीयवर्णैः।
ववर्ष रामं शरवृष्टिजालैः
सलक्ष्मणं भास्कररश्मिकल्पैः॥ ६६॥
verses.m: Having wounded the leaders of monkey hosts with his maces and arrows of a golden hue, he actually covered Śrī Rāma as well as Lakṣmaṇa with showers of shafts shining like sunbeams. (66)

verses.text:
स बाणवर्षैरभिवृष्यमाणो
धारानिपातानिव तानचिन्त्य।
समीक्षमाणः परमाद्भुतश्री-
रामस्तदा लक्ष्मणमित्युवाच॥ ६७॥
verses.m: Not minding the arrows any more than torrents of rain, while being covered with showers of shafts, and gazing on Lakṣmaṇa, the celebrated Śrī Rāma, who was shining with a prodigious splendour, spoke as follows to him at that moment: (67)

verses.text:
असौ पुनर्लक्ष्मण राक्षसेन्द्रो
ब्रह्मास्त्रमाश्रित्य सुरेन्द्रशत्रुः।
निपातयित्वा हरिसैन्यमस्मान्-
शितैः शरैरर्दयति प्रसक्तम्॥ ६८॥
verses.m: “Falling back upon the missile presided over by Brahmā (the creator), which has been secured by him, O Lakṣmaṇa, and striking down the army of monkeys, the yonder prince of ogres, an avowed enemy of Indra (the ruler of gods), is now tormenting us with his sharp arrows. (68)

verses.text:
स्वयंभुवा दत्तवरो महात्मा
समाहितोऽन्तर्हितभीमकायः।
कथं नु शक्यो युधि नष्टदेहो
निहन्तुमद्येन्द्रजिदुद्यतास्त्रः ॥ ६९॥
verses.m: “How can the highly intelligent Indrajit—on whom a boon of invincibility has been bestowed by Brahmā (the self-born creator), nay, who is steadfast of purpose and has concealed his terrible form and who stands with his weapons uplifted, even though his body is invisible—be struck down in combat today? (69)

verses.text:
मन्ये स्वयंभूर्भगवानचिन्त्य-
स्तस्यैतदस्त्रं प्रभवश्च योऽस्य।
बाणावपातं त्वमिहाद्य धीमन्
मया सहाव्यग्रमनाः सहस्व॥ ७०॥
verses.m: “I know the self-born Lord Brahmā—who is the source (the creator) of this universe—is inconceivable in his essence and the missile used is presided over by him. Therefore, remaining undisturbed in mind, O wise one, endure you with me today the hail of arrows on this spot. (70)

verses.text:
प्रच्छादयत्येष हि राक्षसेन्द्रः
सर्वा दिशः सायकवृष्टिजालैः।
एतच्च सर्वं पतिताग्र्यशूरं
न भ्राजते वानरराजसैन्यम्॥ ७१॥
verses.m: “Indeed this prince of ogres is thickly covering all the four quarters with the showers of his shafts. And this entire army of Sugrīva, the ruler of monkeys, whose leading heroes have fallen, looks charming no more. (71)

verses.text:
आवां तु दृष्ट्वा पतितौ विसंज्ञौ
निवृत्तयुद्धौ हतहर्षरोषौ।
ध्रुवं प्रवेक्ष्यत्यमरारिवास-
मसौ समासाद्य रणाग्र्यलक्ष्मीम्॥ ७२॥
verses.m: “Finding us fallen unconscious and bereft of joy and anger, having desisted from fighting, nay, winning laurels in combat, he will surely return to Laṅkā, the abode of the enemies of gods.” (72)

verses.text:
ततस्तु ताविन्द्रजितोऽस्त्रजालै-
र्बभूवतुस्तत्र तदा विशस्तौ।
स चापि तौ तत्र विषादयित्वा
ननाद हर्षाद् युधि राक्षसेन्द्रः॥ ७३॥
verses.m: Thereupon the two princes for their part got grievously hurt on the battlefield by the missiles of Indrajit on that occasion. And, having reduced the two brothers to straits in that struggle, that prince of ogres shouted for joy. (73)

verses.text:
ततस्तदा वानरसैन्यमेवं
रामं च संख्ये सह लक्ष्मणेन।
विषादयित्वा सहसा विवेश
पुरीं दशग्रीवभुजाभिगुप्ताम्।
संस्तूयमानः स तु यातुधानैः
पित्रे च सर्वं हृषितोऽभ्युवाच॥ ७४॥
verses.m: Having prostrated in combat as aforesaid the army of monkeys as well as Śrī Rāma alongwith Lakṣmaṇa on that occasion, Indrajit thereupon withdrew all at once to the city protected by the arms of Rāvaṇa, the ten-headed monster. Nay, filled with delight while being duly extolled by ogres, he for his part related everything in extenso to his father. (74)

verses.text:
तयोस्तदासादितयो रणाग्रे
मुमोह सैन्यं हरियूथपानाम्।
सुग्रीवनीलाङ्गदजाम्बवन्तो
न चापि किंचित् प्रतिपेदिरे ते॥ १॥
verses.m: On the two brothers having been knocked down senseless in the forefront of battle, the army of the monkey troop-commanders got nonplussed. Nor could the celebrated Sugrīva, Nīla, Aṅgada and Jāmbavān do anything. (1)

verses.text:
ततो विषण्णं समवेक्ष्य सर्वं
विभीषणो बुद्धिमतां वरिष्ठः।
उवाच शाखामृगराजवीरा-
नाश्वासयन्नप्रतिमैर्वचोभिः ॥ २॥
verses.m: Observing everyone despondent, Vibhīṣaṇa, the foremost of the wise, thereupon spoke as follows, reassuring the champions of Sugrīva, the ruler of monkeys, with his incomparable words: (2)

verses.text:
मा भैष्ट नास्त्यत्र विषादकालो
यदार्यपुत्रौ ह्यवशौ विषण्णौ।
स्वयंभुवो वाक्यमथोद्वहन्तौ
यत्सादिताविन्द्रजितास्त्रजालैः ॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Do not be afraid, there is no occasion for despondency at this moment; because the two sons of Daśaratha are actually feeling helpless and afflicted and have allowed themselves to be overwhelmed by the missiles of Indrajit, honouring as they did the spell sacred to the self-born creator, with which the missile presided over by him has been invoked. (3)

verses.text:
तस्मै तु दत्तं परमास्त्रमेतत्
स्वयंभुवा ब्राह्मममोघवीर्यम्।
तन्मानयन्तौ युधि राजपुत्रौ
निपातितौ कोऽत्र विषादकालः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “This supreme missile of unfailing potency presided over by Brahmā has for its part been bestowed on him (Indrajit) by the self-born creator himself and the two princes have been overthrown in combat, honouring as they did the aforesaid missile. What occasion is there for despondency in this event?” (4)

verses.text:
ब्राह्ममस्त्रं ततो धीमान् मानयित्वा तु मारुतिः।
विभीषणवचः श्रुत्वा हनूमानिदमब्रवीत्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Hearing the speech of Vibhīṣaṇa and paying honour to the missile presided over by Brahmā, the creator, the sagacious Hanumān, son of the wind-god, for his part then spoke as follows: (5)

verses.text:
अस्मिन्नस्त्रहते सैन्ये वानराणां तरस्विनाम्।
यो यो धारयते प्राणांस्तं तमाश्वासयावहे॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Let us two restore to confidence whosoever is still breathing in this army of powerful monkeys, which has been struck down by the missile shot by Indrajit.” (6)

verses.text:
तावुभौ युगपद् वीरौ हनूमद्राक्षसोत्तमौ।
उल्काहस्तौ तदा रात्रौ रणशीर्षे विचेरतुः॥ ७॥
verses.m: Torch in hand, both the aforesaid heroes, Hanumān alongwith Vibhīṣaṇa, the foremost ogre, then began to range the battlefield together at night. (7)

verses.text:
भिन्नलाङ्गूलहस्तोरुपादाङ्गुलिशिरोधरैः।
स्रवद्भिः क्षतजं गात्रैः प्रस्रवद्भिः समन्ततः॥ ८॥
पतितैः पर्वताकारैर्वानरैरभिसंवृताम्।
शस्त्रैश्च पतितैर्दीप्तैर्ददृशाते वसुंधराम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: The two warriors saw the earth covered all over with monkeys resembling mountains—who lay fallen on earth, letting out blood from their bodies whose tails, hands, thighs, feet, fingers and necks had been severed, and who were discharging urine all round—as well as with flaming weapons that had fallen. (8-9)

verses.text:
सुग्रीवमङ्गदं नीलं शरभं गन्धमादनम्।
जाम्बवन्तं सुषेणं च वेगदर्शिनमेव च॥ १०॥
मैन्दं नलं ज्योतिर्मुखं द्विविदं चापि वानरम्।
विभीषणो हनूमांश्च ददृशाते हतान् रणे॥ ११॥
verses.m: Vibhīṣaṇa and Hanumān saw struck down on the battlefield Sugrīva, Aṅgada, Nīla, Śarabha, Gandhamādana, Jāmbavān and Suṣeṇa as well as Vegadarśī, Mainda, Nala, Jyotirmukha and the monkey Dwivida too. (10-11)

verses.text:
सप्तषष्टिर्हताः कोट्यो वानराणां तरस्विनाम्।
अह्नः पञ्चमशेषेण वल्लभेन स्वयंभुवः॥ १२॥
verses.m: By the fifth and last* period of the day (viz., evening) sixty-seven crores of powerful monkeys were laid prostrate by the missile cherished by Brahmā (the self-born creator). (12)

verses.text:
सागरौघनिभं भीमं दृष्ट्वा बाणार्दितं बलम्।
मार्गते जाम्बवन्तं च हनूमान् सविभीषणः॥ १३॥
verses.m: Looking on the formidable army—which resembled the tide of a sea—overwhelmed by the shafts of Indrajit, Hanumān, accompanied by Vibhīṣaṇa, began to search for Jāmbavān. (13)

verses.text:
स्वभावजरया युक्तं वृद्धं शरशतैश्चितम्।
प्रजापतिसुतं वीरं शाम्यन्तमिव पावकम्॥ १४॥
दृष्ट्वा समभिसंक्रम्य पौलस्त्यो वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
कच्चिदार्य शरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्न प्राणा ध्वंसितास्तव॥ १५॥
verses.m: Seeing the heroic Jāmbavān, a son of Brahmā, the lord of creation—who was naturally weighed down by age and was advanced in wisdom, too, nay, who was covered with hundreds of shafts and looked like a dying fire—and duly approaching him, Vibhīṣaṇa (a scion of Pulasti, one of the mind-born sons of Brahmā), spoke to him as follows: “I hope, O venerable Sir, that your life has not been put an end to by the penetrating shafts shot by Indrajit.” (14-15)

verses.text:
विभीषणवचः श्रुत्वा जाम्बवानृक्षपुङ्गवः।
कृच्छ्रादभ्युद्गिरन् वाक्यमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ १६॥
verses.m: Hearing the question of Vibhīṣaṇa and uttering words with difficulty, Jāmbavān, the foremost of the bears, replied as follows: (16)

verses.text:
नैर्ऋतेन्द्र महावीर्य स्वरेण त्वाभिलक्षये।
विद्धगात्रः शितैर्बाणैर्न त्वां पश्यामि चक्षुषा॥ १७॥
verses.m: “O Vibhīṣaṇa (a ruler of ogres), who are endowed with extraordinary prowess, I recognize you by your voice alone. Pierced all over with sharp arrows, I no longer see you with my eyes. (17)

verses.text:
अञ्जना सुप्रजा येन मातरिश्वा च सुव्रत।
हनूमान् वानरश्रेष्ठः प्राणान् धारयते क्वचित्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Does Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys, because of whom Añjanā, his mother, and the wind-god, his procreator, are recognized as blessed parents, still survive anywhere, O pious, one?” (18)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा जाम्बवतो वाक्यमुवाचेदं विभीषणः।
आर्यपुत्रावतिक्रम्य कस्मात् पृच्छसि मारुतिम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: Hearing the query of Jāmbavān, Vibhīṣaṇa made the following reply: “Passing over the two sons of Daśaratha, wherefore do you inquire about Hanumān (son of the wind-god)? (19)

verses.text:
नैव राजनि सुग्रीवे नाङ्गदे नापि राघवे।
आर्य संदर्शितः स्नेहो यथा वायुसुते परः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “The way in which the utmost affection has been clearly manifested by you for Hanumān, son of the wind-god, has not at all been shown for King Sugrīva, nor for Aṅgada, nor even for Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu.” (20)

verses.text:
विभीषणवचः श्रुत्वा जाम्बवान् वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
शृणु नैर्ऋतशार्दूल यस्मात् पृच्छामि मारुतिम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: Hearing the observation of Vibhīṣaṇa, Jāmbavān replied as follows: “Listen, O tiger among the ogres (lit, the progeny of Nirṛti), why I inquire solely about Hanumān, son of the wind-god: (21)

verses.text:
अस्मिञ्जीवति वीरे तु हतमप्यहतं बलम्।
हनूमत्युज्झितप्राणे जीवन्तोऽपि मृता वयम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: “If this hero, Hanumān, for his part is still breathing, our army is intact, even though destroyed. If Hanumān, on the other hand, has given up the ghost, we are all dead, even though living. (22)

verses.text:
धरते मारुतिस्तात मारुतप्रतिमो यदि।
वैश्वानरसमो वीर्ये जीविताशा ततो भवेत्॥ २३॥
