verses.m: “By good fortune you have caught my sight here. You were sought by me even as an ordinary animal is sought by a lion afflicted with hunger, O Rāma! (13)

verses.text:
अद्य मद्बाणवेगेन प्रेतराड्विषयं गतः।
ये त्वया निहताः शूराः सह तैश्च वसिष्यसि॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Nay, having reached the realm of Yama (the ruler of the departed) through the impetuosity of my arrows today, you shall dwell with those very champions who have been killed by you. (14)

verses.text:
बहुनात्र किमुक्तेन शृणु राम वचो मम।
पश्यन्तु सकला लोकास्त्वां मां चैव रणाजिरे॥ १५॥
verses.m: “What will be gained through much talk on this topic? Listen, O Rāma to my advice. Let all people see you as well as me trying our strength on the field of battle. (15)

verses.text:
अस्त्रैर्वा गदया वापि बाहुभ्यां वा रणाजिरे।
अभ्यस्तं येन वा राम वर्ततां तेन वा मृधम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Let our trial of strength commence on the battlefield with mystic missiles, or with maces or with arms, or with any other weapon with which you may have carried on your military practice, O Rāma!” (16)

verses.text:
मकराक्षवचः श्रुत्वा रामो दशरथात्मजः।
अब्रवीत् प्रहसन् वाक्यमुत्तरोत्तरवादिनम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: Heartily laughing on hearing the challenge of Makarākṣa, Śrī Rāma, sprung from the loins of Emperor Daśaratha, replied as follows to the ogre, who was speaking further and further without interruption: (17)

verses.text:
कत्थसे किं वृथा रक्षो बहून्यसदृशानि ते।
न रणे शक्यते जेतुं विना युद्धेन वाग्बलात्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Why do you indulge in self-praise in vain, O ogre? Many things have been said by you, which are unworthy of you. No victory can be scored on the battlefield by sheer force of speech without an encounter. (18)

verses.text:
चतुर्दश सहस्राणि रक्षसां त्वत्पिता च यः।
त्रिशिरा दूषणश्चापि दण्डके निहतो मया॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Fourteen thousand of ogres as also Khara, who was your father, Triśirā and Dūṣaṇa too were killed by me in the Daṇḍaka forest. (19)

verses.text:
स्वाशिताश्चापि मांसेन गृध्रगोमायुवायसाः।
भविष्यन्त्यद्य वै पाप तीक्ष्णतुण्डनखाङ् कुशाः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Nay, vultures, jackals and crows with sharp beaks and goad-like claws were sated with their flesh. Today too they shall likewise be sated with your flesh, O sinful one!” (20)

verses.text:
राघवेणैवमुक्तस्तु मकराक्षो महाबलः।
बाणौघानमुचत् तस्मै राघवाय रणाजिरे॥ २१॥
verses.m: Spoken to in these words by Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), Makarākṣa for his part, who was endowed with extraordinary might, shot volleys of shafts on the aforesaid scion of Raghu on the field of battle. (21)

verses.text:
ताञ्छराञ्छरवर्षेण रामश्चिच्छेद नैकधा।
निपेतुर्भुवि विच्छिन्ना रुक्मपुङ्खाः सहस्रशः॥ २२॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma, however, tore those arrows into pieces with a hail of arrows. The ogre’s arrows, which were provided with shafts of gold, fell to the ground, when torn in thousands. (22)

verses.text:
तद् युद्धमभवत् तत्र समेत्यान्योन्यमोजसा।
खरराक्षसपुत्रस्य सूनोर्दशरथस्य च॥ २३॥
verses.m: On their meeting each other at close quarters, a notable encounter furiously raged between Makarākṣa (son of the ogre Khara) and Śrī Rāma (son of Daśaratha). (23)

verses.text:
जीमूतयोरिवाकाशे शब्दो ज्यातलयोरिव।
धनुर्मुक्तः स्वनोऽन्योन्यं श्रूयते च रणाजिरे॥ २४॥
verses.m: The sound released by the bows as produced by the friction of the hands and the bow-string (of the two warriors) was mutually heard on the field of battle on that occasion, like the rumbling of clouds in space. (24)

verses.text:
देवदानवगन्धर्वाः किंनराश्च महोरगाः।
अन्तरिक्षगताः सर्वे द्रष्टुकामास्तदद्भुतम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: Gods, devils and Gandharvas (celestial musicians), Kinnaras (a class of demigods with a human figure and the head of a horse) and huge serpents stood in the air to witness that astounding combat. (25)

verses.text:
विद्धमन्योन्यगात्रेषु द्विगुणं वर्धते बलम्।
कृतप्रतिकृतान्योन्यं कुरुतां तौ रणाजिरे॥ २६॥
verses.m: The limbs of both were pierced by each other, yet their strength was redoubled. The two warriors inflicted wounds on each other on the battlefield and each returned the blows of the other. (26)

verses.text:
राममुक्तांस्तु बाणौघान् राक्षसस्त्वच्छिनद् रणे।
रक्षोमुक्तांस्तु रामो वै नैकधा प्राच्छिनच्छरैः॥ २७॥
verses.m: The ogre for his part actually tore the volleys of shafts shot by Śrī Rāma; while Śrī Rāma actually split into pieces with his arrows the shafts discharged by the ogre. (27)

verses.text:
बाणौघवितताः सर्वा दिशश्च प्रदिशस्तथा।
संछन्ना वसुधा चैव समन्तान्न प्रकाशते॥ २८॥
verses.m: All the four quarters as well as the intermediate points were covered with volleys of shafts; nay, the earth itself was entirely obscured on all sides and could not be seen. (28)

verses.text:
ततः क्रुद्धो महाबाहुर्धनुश्चिच्छेद संयुगे।
अष्टाभिरथ नाराचैः सूतं विव्याध राघवः॥ २९॥
verses.m: Full of anger, the mighty-armed Śrī Rāma thereupon split asunder the bow of Makarākṣa in the course of the combat. The scion of Raghu further pierced the charioteer with as many as eight steel arrows. (29)

verses.text:
भित्त्वा रथं शरै रामो हत्वा अश्वानपातयत्।
विरथो वसुधास्थः स मकराक्षो निशाचरः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Having split asunder the chariot with his arrows and struck the horses, he laid them low. Deprived of his chariot, that prowler of the night, Makarākṣa, stood on the ground. (30)

verses.text:
तत्तिष्ठद् वसुधां रक्षः शूलं जग्राह पाणिना।
त्रासनं सर्वभूतानां युगान्ताग्निसमप्रभम्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Standing on the ground, the aforesaid ogre seized hold of his pike, which struck terror into all created beings and shone like the fire at the end of the world-cycle. (31)

verses.text:
दुरवापं महच्छूलं रुद्रदत्तं भयंकरम्।
जाज्वल्यमानमाकाशे संहारास्त्रमिवापरम्॥ ३२॥
यं दृष्ट्वा देवताः सर्वा भयार्ता विद्रुता दिशः।
विभ्राम्य च महच्छूलं प्रज्वलन्तं निशाचरः॥ ३३॥
स क्रोधात् प्राहिणोत् तस्मै राघवाय महाहवे।
तमापतन्तं ज्वलितं खरपुत्रकराच्च्युतम्॥ ३४॥
बाणैश्चतुर्भिराकाशे शूलं चिच्छेद राघवः।
स भिन्नो नैकधा शूलो दिव्यहाटकमण्डितः।
व्यशीर्यत महोल्केव रामबाणार्दितो भुवि॥ ३५॥
verses.m: Nay, brandishing the great flaming pike, which was difficult to lay one’s hands on and had been bestowed on him by Rudra (the god of destruction), which inspired terror and shone brightly in the air like another weapon of universal destruction and seeing which all the gods fled panic-stricken in all directions—the night-stalker furiously hurled it against Śrī Rāma in that major conflict. Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, split with four arrows that flaming pike discharged from the hand of Khara’s son, even as it came flying and while it was still in the air. Struck by the arrows of Śrī Rāma and split into many pieces, the aforesaid pike, which was decked with ethereal gold, crumbled on the ground like a colossal meteor. (32—35)

verses.text:
तच्छूलं निहतं दृष्ट्वा रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा।
साधु साध्विति भूतानि व्याहरन्ति नभोगताः॥ ३६॥
verses.m: Seeing that pike destroyed by Śrī Rāma of unwearied action, the beings standing in the air cried out: “Well done! Bravo!!” (36)

verses.text:
तं दृष्ट्वा निहतं शूलं मकराक्षो निशाचरः।
मुष्टिमुद्यम्य काकुत्स्थं तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत्॥ ३७॥
verses.m: Seeing that pike destroyed and raising his fist, the prowler of the night, Makarākṣa, called out to Śrī Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha), “Wait, tarry!” (37)

verses.text:
स तं दृष्ट्वा पतन्तं तु प्रहस्य रघुनन्दनः।
पावकास्त्रं ततो रामः संदधे तु शरासने॥ ३८॥
verses.m: Seeing him advancing and laughing heartily, Śrī Rāma, the delight of the Raghus, for his part thereupon put to his bow a mystic missile presided over by the god of fire. (38)

verses.text:
तेनास्त्रेण हतं रक्षः काकुत्स्थेन तदा रणे।
संछिन्नहृदयं तत्र पपात च ममार च॥ ३९॥
verses.m: Struck on the battlefield with that missile by Śrī Rāma, a scion of Kakutstha, the ogre, who had his heart split open, fell down then and there and died. (39)

verses.text:
दृष्ट्वा ते राक्षसाः सर्वे मकराक्षस्य पातनम्।
लङ्कामेव प्रधावन्त रामबाणभयार्दिताः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: Stricken with fear of Śrī Rāma’s arrows on witnessing the fall of Makarākṣa, all the ogres present ran away straight to Laṅkā.(40)

verses.text:
दशरथनृपसूनुबाणवेगै
रजनिचरं निहतं खरात्मजं तम्।
प्रददृशुरथ देवताः प्रहृष्टा
गिरिमिव वज्रहतं यथा विकीर्णम्॥ ४१॥
verses.m: Highly rejoiced, the gods present at the scene watched the aforesaid night-ranger, the son of Khara, killed by the force of the shafts of Śrī Rāma (son of King Daśaratha), and resembling a mountain struck by lightning and shattered. (41)

verses.text:
मकराक्षं हतं श्रुत्वा रावणः समितिंजयः।
रोषेण महताविष्टो दन्तान् कटकटाय्य च॥ १॥
कुपितश्च तदा तत्र किं कार्यमिति चिन्तयन्।
आदिदेशाथ संक्रुद्धो रणायेन्द्रजितं सुतम्॥ २॥
verses.m: Possessed with violent anger, on hearing of Makarākṣa having been killed, and grinding his teeth in rage, reflecting as to what should be done on that occasion and in that situation, Rāvaṇa, who had (always) been victorious in war, and was filled with fury, forthwith enjoined in the following words his eldest son, Indrajit, to take the field: (1-2)

verses.text:
जहि वीर महावीर्यौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।
अदृश्यो दृश्यमानो वा सर्वथा त्वं बलाधिकः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Remaining invisible or visible (as you please), make short work, O heroic prince, of the two brothers, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, who are endowed with extraordinary prowess; for you are in every way superior to them in might. (3)

verses.text:
त्वमप्रतिमकर्माणमिन्द्रं जयसि संयुगे।
किं पुनर्मानुषौ दृष्ट्वा न वधिष्यसि संयुगे॥ ४॥
verses.m: “You have conquered in combat even Indra, the ruler of gods, of incomparable deeds. Will you not then be able to kill two mortals on seeing them on the battlefield?” (4)

verses.text:
तथोक्तो राक्षसेन्द्रेण प्रतिगृह्य पितुर्वचः।
यज्ञभूमौ स विधिवत् पावकं जुहुवेन्द्रजित्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Bowing to the command of his father when enjoined as aforesaid by Rāvaṇa, the ruler of ogres, the said Indrajit poured oblations into the sacred fire with due ceremony on the sacrificial ground. (5)

verses.text:
जुह्वतश्चापि तत्राग्निं रक्तोष्णीषधराः स्त्रियः।
आजग्मुस्तत्र सम्भ्रान्ता राक्षस्यो यत्र रावणिः॥ ६॥
verses.m: Even as he was pouring oblations into the sacred fire, ogresses working as female attendants at the sacrifice and carrying red turbans (for the use of the priests), nay, seized with a flurry, arrived on the spot where the son of Rāvaṇa was. (6)

verses.text:
शस्त्राणि शरपत्राणि समिधोऽथ बिभीतकाः।
लोहितानि च वासांसि स्रुवं कार्ष्णायसं तथा॥ ७॥
verses.m: Weapons such as a lance served as blades of Śara grass for being spread around the sacrificial fire, chips of wood of the Bibhītaka tree (a species of myrobalan tree) which serve as wooden sticks to feed the sacrificial fire, in its place red robes and iron ladles were used in that sacrifice. (7)

verses.text:
सर्वतोऽग्निं समास्तीर्य शरपत्रैः सतोमरैः।
छागस्य सर्वकृष्णस्य गलं जग्राह जीवतः॥ ८॥
verses.m: Having strewn the ground on all sides of the fire with other weapons accompanied by lances, the ogre seized hold with reeds of the neck of a live goat entirely black and consigned it to the fire. (8)

verses.text:
सकृद्धोमसमिद्धस्य विधूमस्य महार्चिषः।
बभूवुस्तानि लिङ्गानि विजयं दर्शयन्ति च॥ ९॥
verses.m: Such omens as betokened triumph, appeared in the smokeless fire which burst into mighty flames when it was fully aroused by that single offering. (9)

verses.text:
प्रदक्षिणावर्तशिखस्तप्तहाटकसंनिभः।
हविस्तत् प्रतिजग्राह पावकः स्वयमुत्थितः॥ १०॥
verses.m: Burst into view in person, the god of fire, who was shooting out flames towards the right and who shone brightly like refined gold, received that offering. (10)

verses.text:
हुत्वाग्निं तर्पयित्वाथ देवदानवराक्षसान्।
आरुरोह रथश्रेष्ठमन्तर्धानगतं शुभम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: Having offered oblations to the fire and gratified the gods, devils and ogres connected with a sacrifice carried out with a malevolent intention, Indrajit ascended an excellent and splendid chariot capable of going out of sight. (11)

verses.text:
स वाजिभिश्चतुर्भिस्तु बाणैस्तु निशितैर्युतः।
आरोपितमहाचापः शुशुभे स्यन्दनोत्तमः॥ १२॥
verses.m: Drawn by four horses, nay, provided with whetted shafts and with a mighty bow placed on it, that excellent chariot looked charming. (12)

verses.text:
जाज्वल्यमानो वपुषा तपनीयपरिच्छदः।
मृगैश्चन्द्रार्धचन्द्रैश्च स रथः समलंकृतः॥ १३॥
verses.m: With its appurtenances of gold the aforesaid chariot glittered on account of its frame and was decorated with carved images of antelopes, full moons and crescents.(13)

verses.text:
जाम्बूनदमहाकम्बुर्दीप्तपावकसंनिभः।
बभूवेन्द्रजितः केतुर्वैदूर्यसमलंकृतः॥ १४॥
verses.m: Provided with large rings of gold and adorned with cat’s-eye gems, the standard of Indrajit shone like a flaming fire. (14)

verses.text:
तेन चादित्यकल्पेन ब्रह्मास्त्रेण च पालितः।
स बभूव दुराधर्षो रावणिः सुमहाबलः॥ १५॥
verses.m: Nay, protected by that chariot, effulgent as the sun, as well as by the missile presided over by Brahmā (the creator), the aforesaid son of Rāvaṇa, who was endowed with exceptional might, was difficult to overpower. (15)

verses.text:
सोऽभिनिर्याय नगरादिन्द्रजित् समितिंजयः।
हुत्वाग्निं राक्षसैर्मन्त्रैरन्तर्धानगतोऽब्रवीत्॥ १६॥
verses.m: Issuing out of the city and having acquired the power of going out of sight by pouring oblations into the sacred fire with the utterance of spells sacred to Nirṛti (the progenitor of the race of ogres), the said ogre, Indrajit, who had always been victorious in war, bragged as follows: (16)

verses.text:
अद्य हत्वा रणे यौ तौ मिथ्या प्रव्रजितौ वने।
जयं पित्रे प्रदास्यामि रावणाय रणेऽधिकम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Having made short work of two mortal princes, who have passed their exile in the forest in vain, I shall indeed secure an eminent victory for my father, Rāvaṇa, today. (17)

verses.text:
अद्य निर्वानरामुर्वीं हत्वा रामं च लक्ष्मणम्।
करिष्ये परमां प्रीतिमित्युक्त्वान्तरधीयत॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Having rid the earth of monkeys and dispatched Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, I shall bring supreme felicity to my father today.” Saying so, he became invisible. (18)

verses.text:
आपपाताथ संक्रुद्धो दशग्रीवेण चोदितः।
तीक्ष्णकार्मुकनाराचैस्तीक्ष्णस्त्विन्द्ररिपू रणे॥ १९॥
verses.m: Directed by Rāvaṇa, the ten-headed monster, and equipped with a fierce bow and steel shafts, the ardent adversary of Indra, for his part now rushed furiously into the fray. (19)

verses.text:
स ददर्श महावीर्यौ नागौ त्रिशिरसाविव।
सृजन्ताविषुजालानि वीरौ वानरमध्यगौ॥ २०॥
verses.m: He beheld the two heroic princes (Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa), who were endowed with extraordinary prowess and resembled two three-headed serpents* standing in the midst of monkeys and discharging volleys of arrows. (20)

verses.text:
इमौ ताविति संचिन्त्य सज्यं कृत्वा च कार्मुकम्।
संततानेषुधाराभिः पर्जन्य इव वृष्टिमान्॥ २१॥
verses.m: Concluding that they were the two princes whom he was seeking, nay, stringing his bow, the ogre covered the quarters with streams of arrows as a raining cloud would with torrents of rain. (21)

verses.text:
स तु वैहायसरथो युधि तौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।
अचक्षुर्विषये तिष्ठन् विव्याध निशितैः शरैः॥ २२॥
verses.m: Seated in his aerial car, and remaining out of sight, Indrajit for his part pierced with whetted shafts the two princes, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, standing on the battlefield below. (22)

verses.text:
तौ तस्य शरवेगेन परीतौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।
धनुषी सशरे कृत्वा दिव्यमस्त्रं प्रचक्रतुः॥ २३॥
verses.m: Fitting arrows to their bows when covered by the fury of his shafts, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa revealed divine missiles. (23)

verses.text:
प्रच्छादयन्तौ गगनं शरजालैर्महाबलौ।
तमस्त्रैः सूर्यसंकाशैर्नैव पस्पर्शतुः शरैः॥ २४॥
verses.m: Though covering the sky with streams of arrows, the two princes, who were endowed with extraordinary might, could not even touch Indrajit with their arrows, charged with mystic missiles and effulgent as the sun. (24)

verses.text:
स हि धूमान्धकारं च चक्रे प्रच्छादयन्नभः।
दिशश्चान्तर्दधे श्रीमान् नीहारतमसा वृताः॥ २५॥
verses.m: Nay, the glorious prince actually brought about, by dint of conjuring tricks, darkness accompanied by smoke, thereby obscuring the sky and also rendered the quarters invisible, enveloped as they were by him with the darkness of fog. (25)

verses.text:
नैव ज्यातलनिर्घोषो न च नेमिखुरस्वनः।
शुश्रुवे चरतस्तस्य न च रूपं प्रकाशते॥ २६॥
verses.m: Even though he kept moving about, neither the sound produced by the impact of his palm on the bow-string, nor the sound of his chariot’s wheels or the clattering of hoofs of the horses, could be heard, nor did his form come to view. (26)

verses.text:
घनान्धकारे तिमिरे शिलावर्षमिवाद्भुतम्।
स ववर्ष महाबाहुर्नाराचशरवृष्टिभिः॥ २७॥
verses.m: In the midst of the thick darkness, which rendered one blind, the mighty-armed prince appeared to discharge a marvellous shower of rocks with hails of his steel arrows. (27)

verses.text:
स रामं सूर्यसंकाशैः शरैर्दत्तवरैर्भृशम्।
विव्याध समरे क्रुद्धः सर्वगात्रेषु रावणिः॥ २८॥
verses.m: Getting enraged, the aforesaid son of Rāvaṇa grievously pierced Śrī Rāma on the battlefield in all limbs with arrows, effulgent as the sun, which had been bestowed (on him) by way of a boon. (28)

verses.text:
तौ हन्यमानौ नाराचैर्धाराभिरिव पर्वतौ।
हेमपुङ्खान् नरव्याघ्रौ तिग्मान् मुमुचतुः शरान्॥ २९॥
verses.m: While being hit with steel arrows as a pair of mountains with torrents, the two celebrated tigers among men shot piercing golden-shafted arrows. (29)

verses.text:
अन्तरिक्षे समासाद्य रावणिं कङ्कपत्रिणः।
निकृत्य पतगा भूमौ पेतुस्ते शोणिताप्लुताः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Duly reaching the son of Rāvaṇa in the air and piercing him, those shafts, adorned with the plumes of a buzzard, fell to the ground soaked in blood. (30)

verses.text:
अतिमात्रं शरौघेण दीप्यमानौ नरोत्तमौ।
तानिषून् पततो भल्लैरनेकैर्विचकर्ततुः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Shining beyond measure with a mass of arrows (clinging to their body), the two foremost of men began to tear asunder those arrows which were falling on them with numerous arrows called by the name of Bhallas. (31)

verses.text:
यतो हि ददृशाते तौ शरान् निपतिताञ्छ्रितान्।
ततस्तु तौ दाशरथी ससृजातेऽस्त्रमुत्तमम्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Those two sons of Daśaratha for their part directed their excellent missiles in the direction from which they saw the aforesaid sharp arrows dropping. (32)

verses.text:
रावणिस्तु दिशः सर्वा रथेनातिरथोऽपतत्।
विव्याध तौ दाशरथी लघ्वस्त्रो निशितैः शरैः॥ ३३॥
verses.m: Indrajit, son of Rāvaṇa, for his part, who was a superior car-warrior, and was swift in discharging missiles, coursed in his chariot on all sides, pierced the aforesaid two sons of Daśaratha with whetted shafts. (33)

verses.text:
तेनातिविद्धौ तौ वीरौ रुक्मपुङ्खैः सुसंहतैः।
बभूवतुर्दाशरथी पुष्पिताविव किंशुकौ॥ ३४॥
verses.m: Pierced deeply with well-crafted golden-shafted arrows, those heroic sons of Daśaratha appeared like two Kiṁśuka trees in blossom. (34)

verses.text:
नास्य वेगगतिं कश्चिन्न च रूपं धनुः शरान्।
न चास्य विदितं किंचित् सूर्यस्येवाभ्रसम्प्लवे॥ ३५॥
verses.m: None could perceive the rapid movement nor the form, much less the bow and arrows of Indrajit. Nor could anything about him be known any more than the position of the sun when the sky is thickly overcast with clouds. (35)

verses.text:
तेन विद्धाश्च हरयो निहताश्च गतासवः।
बभूवुः शतशस्तत्र पतिता धरणीतले॥ ३६॥
verses.m: Nay, pierced and struck down by him on the battlefield, monkeys dropped dead on the earth’s surface in hundreds. (36)

verses.text:
लक्ष्मणस्तु ततः क्रुद्धो भ्रातरं वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
ब्राह्ममस्त्रं प्रयोक्ष्यामि वधार्थं सर्वरक्षसाम्॥ ३७॥
verses.m: Roused to anger, Lakṣmaṇa for his part thereupon submitted as follows to his eldest brother, Śrī Rāma: “I shall now fall back upon the mystic missile presided over by Brahmā (the creator) with a view to the destruction of all the ogres.” (37)

verses.text:
तमुवाच ततो रामो लक्ष्मणं शुभलक्षणम्।
नैकस्य हेतो रक्षांसि पृथिव्यां हन्तुमर्हसि॥ ३८॥
verses.m: Thereupon Śrī Rāma admonished in the following words the aforesaid Lakṣmaṇa, who was endowed with auspicious bodily marks: “To get square with one individual you ought not to exterminate all the ogres on the surface of the earth. (38)

verses.text:
अयुध्यमानं प्रच्छन्नं प्राञ्जलिं शरणागतम्।
पलायमानं मत्तं वा न हन्तुं त्वमिहार्हसि॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “You ought not to kill on this earth one who is not actually fighting, lies hidden, has come for protection with joined palms, is fleeing for life or is intoxicated. (39)

verses.text:
तस्यैव तु वधे यत्नं करिष्यामि महाभुज।
आदेक्ष्यावो महावेगानस्त्रानाशीविषोपमान्॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “I for one shall make an earnest endeavour for the destruction of Indrajit alone, O mighty-armed one! We two shall press into service mystic missiles endowed with great impetuosity and resembling venomous serpents. (40)

verses.text:
तमेनं मायिनं क्षुद्रमन्तर्हितरथं बलात्।
राक्षसं निहनिष्यन्ति दृष्ट्वा वानरयूथपाः॥ ४१॥
verses.m: “On seeing him the commanders of monkey troops will forcibly kill this petty ogre, who is skilled in conjuring tricks and whose chariot remains invisible. (41)

verses.text:
यद्येष भूमिं विशते दिवं वा
रसातलं वापि नभस्तलं वा।
एवं विगूढोऽपि ममास्त्रदग्धः
पतिष्यते भूमितले गतासुः॥ ४२॥
verses.m: “Consumed by my mystic missiles, he will fall dead on the ground even if he makes his way into the earth or into heaven, enters the subterranean world or penetrates the vault of heaven, and remains completely hidden in the aforesaid manner.” (42)

verses.text:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा वचनं महार्थं
रघुप्रवीरः प्लवगर्षभैर्वृतः।
वधाय रौद्रस्य नृशंसकर्मण-
स्तदा महात्मा त्वरितं निरीक्षते॥ ४३॥
verses.m: Having made the foregoing speech, which was full of great significance, the high-souled Śrī Rāma, the foremost hero of the Raghus, who was surrounded by the foremost of the monkeys, now began to reflect on the speedy means of putting an end to the fierce ogre of cruel deeds. (43)

verses.text:
विज्ञाय तु मनस्तस्य राघवस्य महात्मनः।
स निवृत्याहवात् तस्मात् प्रविवेश पुरं ततः॥ १॥
verses.m: Withdrawing from that encounter on divining the intention of that high-souled scion of Raghu, Indrajit for his part thereupon re-entered the city. (1)

verses.text:
सोऽनुस्मृत्य वधं तेषां राक्षसानां तरस्विनाम्।
क्रोधताम्रेक्षणः शूरो निर्जगामाथ रावणिः॥ २॥
verses.m: Recalling the destruction of those mighty ogres, the heroic son of Rāvaṇa sallied forth for an encounter immediately, his eyes blood-shot through anger. (2)

verses.text:
स पश्चिमेन द्वारेण निर्ययौ राक्षसैर्वृतः।
इन्द्रजित् सुमहावीर्यः पौलस्त्यो देवकण्टकः॥ ३॥
verses.m: Surrounded by other ogres, the notorious Indrajit, a scion of Sage Pulastya (one of the nine mind-born sons of Brahmā entrusted with the duty of creating the world) and a thorn in the side of gods, who was endowed with exceptional prowess, issued through the western gate. (3)

verses.text:
इन्द्रजित्तु ततो दृष्ट्वा भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।
रणायाभ्युद्यतौ वीरौ मायां प्रादुष्करोत् तदा॥ ४॥
verses.m: Seeing the two gallant brothers, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, prepared for an encounter in everyway, Indrajit for his part thereupon revealed on that occasion his proficiency in conjuring tricks. (4)

verses.text:
इन्द्रजित्तु रथे स्थाप्य सीतां मायामयीं तदा।
बलेन महतावृत्य तस्या वधमरोचयत्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Placing an illusory living image of Sītā on his chariot and with a huge army surrounding it, he intended to kill her. (5)

verses.text:
मोहनार्थं तु सर्वेषां बुद्धिं कृत्वा सुदुर्मतिः।
हन्तुं सीतां व्यवसितो वानराभिमुखो ययौ॥ ६॥
verses.m: Making up his mind to hoodwink all who were present there, and resolved to kill ‘Sītā’, the exceptionally evil-minded ogre for his part advanced to meet the monkeys. (6)

verses.text:
तं दृष्ट्वा त्वभिनिर्यान्तं सर्वे ते काननौकसः।
उत्पेतुरभिसंक्रुद्धाः शिलाहस्ता युयुत्सवः॥ ७॥
verses.m: Infuriated to see him sallying forth for an encounter, all those denizens of the forest rushed towards him with rocks in their hands, agitated as they were to fight. (7)

verses.text:
हनूमान् पुरतस्तेषां जगाम कपिकुञ्जरः।
प्रगृह्य सुमहच्छृङ्गं पर्वतस्य दुरासदम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: Seizing hold of an enormous mountain peak, which was difficult even to reach for others, Hanumān, an elephant among the monkeys, marched at their head. (8)

verses.text:
स ददर्श हतानन्दां सीतामिन्द्रजितो रथे।
एकवेणीधरां दीनामुपवासकृशाननाम्॥ ९॥
परिक्लिष्टैकवसनाममृजां राघवप्रियाम्।
रजोमलाभ्यामालिप्तैः सर्वगात्रैर्वरस्त्रियम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: He beheld in the chariot of Indrajit the cheerless and wretched ‘Sītā’, the darling of Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), a lovely lady, wearing a single tress, clad in a single soiled garment and unadorned, all her limbs covered with dust and mud and her face emaciated through fasts. (9-10)

verses.text:
तां निरीक्ष्य मुहूर्तं तु मैथिलीमध्यवस्य च।
बभूवाचिरदृष्टा हि तेन सा जनकात्मजा॥ ११॥
verses.m: Gazing on her awhile and concluding her to be no other than Sītā, a princess of Mithilā, Hanumān for his part became melancholy. He took no time in recognizing her inasmuch as Sītā, daughter of Janaka, had been seen by him before long. (11)

verses.text:
अब्रवीत् तां तु शोकार्तां निरानन्दां तपस्विनीम्।
दृष्ट्वा रथस्थितां दीनां राक्षसेन्द्रसुतश्रिताम्॥ १२॥
किं समर्थितमस्येति चिन्तयन् स महाकपिः।
सह तैर्वानरश्रेष्ठैरभ्यधावत रावणिम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: Seeing that joyless and miserable ascetic woman seated in the chariot stricken with grief, under the sway of Indrajit (son of the ruler of ogres), and wondering what his intention might be in bringing her in his chariot to the battlefield, that great monkey for his part spoke about it to the leaders of monkeys and rushed towards the son of Rāvaṇa with those monkey leaders. (12-13)

verses.text:
तद् वानरबलं दृष्ट्वा रावणिः क्रोधमूर्च्छितः।
कृत्वा विकोशं निस्त्रिंशं मूर्ध्नि सीतामकर्षयत्॥ १४॥
verses.m: Filled with rage on seeing that simian army rushing towards him and unsheathing his sword, Indrajit (son of Rāvaṇa) pulled ‘Sītā’ by the hair on her head. (14)

verses.text:
तां स्त्रियं पश्यतां तेषां ताडयामास राक्षसः।
क्रोशन्तीं राम रामेति मायया योजितां रथे॥ १५॥
verses.m: The ogre began to strike that woman, who had been placed in the chariot by dint of legerdemain, and was crying “Rāma! O Rāma”, while the monkeys stood looking on. (15)

verses.text:
गृहीतमूर्धजां दृष्ट्वा हनूमान् दैन्यमागतः।
दुःखजं वारि नेत्राभ्यामुत्सृजन् मारुतात्मजः॥ १६॥
verses.m: Dropping tears of agony from his eyes on perceiving her seized by the hair, Hanumān, sprung from the loins of the wind-god, gave way to affliction. (16)

verses.text:
तां दृष्ट्वा चारुसर्वाङ्गीं रामस्य महिषीं प्रियाम्।
अब्रवीत् परुषं वाक्यं क्रोधाद् रक्षोधिपात्मजम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: Beholding that cherished consort of Śrī Rāma, who was lovely of all limbs, he angrily addressed the following harsh rebuke to Indrajit (son of the suzerain lord of ogres): (17)

verses.text:
दुरात्मन्नात्मनाशाय केशपक्षे परामृशः।
ब्रह्मर्षीणां कुले जातो राक्षसीं योनिमाश्रितः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “It is to your own destruction, O evil-minded one, that you have seized her by the hair on her head. Though descended in the line of Brāhmaṇa Ṛṣis (seers of Vedic Mantras), you have lived in the womb of an ogress. (18)

verses.text:
धिक् त्वां पापसमाचारं यस्य ते मतिरीदृशी।
नृशंसानार्य दुर्वृत्त क्षुद्र पापपराक्रम।
अनार्यस्येदृशं कर्म घृणा ते नास्ति निर्घृण॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Woe be to you of sinful conduct, in whom such a resolve has taken place. O cruel, ignoble and mean scoundrel of sinful prowess, such an act is worthy of a barbarian alone. Obviously there is no pity in you, O ruthless one! (19)

verses.text:
च्युता गृहाच्च राज्याच्च रामहस्ताच्च मैथिली।
किं तवैषापराद्धा हि यदेनां हंसि निर्दय॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Torn from her home, and her kingdom too as well as from the protection of Śrī Rāma, what wrong has this princess of Mithilā done to you that you are killing her, O pitiless one? (20)

verses.text:
सीतां हत्वा तु न चिरं जीविष्यसि कथंचन।
वधार्ह कर्मणा तेन मम हस्तगतो ह्यसि॥ २१॥
verses.m: “After dispatching Sītā you shall undoubtedly not survive long in any case. It is due to such a deed that you have actually fallen into my hands, O creature deserving of death! (21)

verses.text:
ये च स्त्रीघातिनां लोका लोकवध्यैश्च कुत्सिताः।
इह जीवितमुत्सृज्य प्रेत्य तान् प्रति लप्स्यसे॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Yielding up your life in this world, you shall after death descend to those worlds which are the lot of killers of women and are condemned even by those who deserve to be killed by the people.” (22)

verses.text:
इति ब्रुवाणो हनुमान् सायुधैर्हरिभिर्वृतः।
अभ्यधावत् सुसंक्रुद्धो राक्षसेन्द्रसुतं प्रति॥ २३॥
verses.m: Speaking thus and attended by monkeys equipped with weapons of destruction such as trees and rocks, Hanumān rushed in great fury towards Indrajit, son of the ruler of ogres. (23)

verses.text:
आपतन्तं महावीर्यं तदनीकं वनौकसाम्।
रक्षसां भीमकोपानामनीकेन न्यवारयत्॥ २४॥
verses.m: With an army of ogres of redoubtable fury Indrajit intercepted that army of the monkeys (lit., dwellers in the woods), which was endowed with extraordinary prowess and was advancing towards him. (24)

verses.text:
स तां बाणसहस्रेण विक्षोभ्य हरिवाहिनीम्।
हनूमन्तं हरिश्रेष्ठमिन्द्रजित् प्रत्युवाच ह॥ २५॥
verses.m: Having caused a stir in that simian army with his thousand arrows, the aforesaid Indrajit, they say, replied as follows to Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys: (25)

verses.text:
सुग्रीवस्त्वं च रामश्च यन्निमित्तमिहागताः।
तां वधिष्यामि वैदेहीमद्यैव तव पश्यतः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “I am going to make short work this very day, while you stand looking on, of that Sītā (a princess of the Videha territory), for whose sake Sugrīva as well as you and Rāma have come hither. (26)

verses.text:
इमां हत्वा ततो रामं लक्ष्मणं त्वां च वानर।
सुग्रीवं च वधिष्यामि तं चानार्यं विभीषणम्॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Having disposed her of, I shall then make short work of Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa and yourself, O monkey, as also of Sugrīva as well as of that unworthy, Vibhīṣaṇa. (27)

verses.text:
न हन्तव्याः स्त्रियश्चेति यद् ब्रवीषि प्लवंगम।
पीडाकरममित्राणां यच्च कर्तव्यमेव तत्॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Nay, what you have said just now, viz., that women should not be killed, is quite correct, O monkey! But that which causes annoyance to one’s enemies need must be done.” (28)

verses.text:
तमेवमुक्त्वा रुदतीं सीतां मायामयीं च ताम्।
शितधारेण खड्गेन निजघानेन्द्रजित् स्वयम्॥ २९॥
verses.m: Nay, having spoken as aforesaid to Hanumān, Indrajit personally made short work with his sharp-edged sword, of that illusory Sītā, who had been sobbing all the while. (29)

verses.text:
यज्ञोपवीतमार्गेण छिन्ना तेन तपस्विनी।
सा पृथिव्यां पृथुश्रोणी पपात प्रियदर्शना॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Split asunder by him diagonally that poor lady of broad hips and pleasing aspect sank on the ground. (30)

verses.text:
तामिन्द्रजित् स्त्रियं हत्वा हनूमन्तमुवाच ह।
मया रामस्य पश्येमां प्रियां शस्त्रनिषूदिताम्।
एषा विशस्ता वैदेही निष्फलो वः परिश्रमः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Having killed that illusory woman, Indrajit spoke as follows to Hanūmān: “Behold this darling of Rāma destroyed by me with a weapon. Here is Sītā, a princess of Videha territory killed. Now vain is your exertion to secure her.” (31)

verses.text:
ततः खड्गेन महता हत्वा तामिन्द्रजित्स्वयम्।
हृष्टः स रथमास्थाय ननाद च महास्वनम्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Nay, mounting his chariot after he had personally done ‘her’ to death with his mighty sword, Indrajit joyfully raised a loud shout. (32)

verses.text:
वानराः शुश्रुवुः शब्दमदूरे प्रत्यवस्थिताः।
व्यादितास्यस्य नदतस्तद्दुर्गं संश्रितस्य तु॥ ३३॥
verses.m: Arrayed not far from him, the monkeys heard his roar even as he shouted with his mouth wide open while comfortably seated in that aerial chariot, which was actually difficult of access for otherss. (33)

verses.text:
तथा तु सीतां विनिहत्य दुर्मतिः
प्रहृष्टचेताः स बभूव रावणिः।
तं हृष्टरूपं समुदीक्ष्य वानरा
विषण्णरूपाः समभिप्रदुद्रुवुः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: Having disposed of Sītā as aforesaid, that evil-minded son of Rāvaṇa for his part felt greatly rejoiced in mind. Assuming a melancholy air on seeing him cheerful of aspect, the monkeys fled en masse precipitately. (34)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा तु भीमनिर्ह्रादं शक्राशनिसमस्वनम्।
वीक्ष्यमाणा दिशः सर्वा दुद्रुवुर्वानरा भृशम्॥ १॥
verses.m: Hearing the terrible roar of Indrajit, the monkeys for their part fled with great speed in all directions, gazing on Indrajit whose roar resembled the peal of thunder. (1)

verses.text:
तानुवाच ततः सर्वान् हनूमान् मारुतात्मजः।
विषण्णवदनान् दीनांस्त्रस्तान् विद्रवतः पृथक्॥ २॥
verses.m: Hanumān, sprung from the loins of the wind-god, thereupon spoke as follows to all those monkeys, who wore melancholy looks, were feeling miserable and alarmed and were fleeing singly: (2)

verses.text:
कस्माद् विषण्णवदना विद्रवध्वं प्लवंगमाः।
त्यक्तयुद्धसमुत्साहाः शूरत्वं क्व नु वो गतम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Having lost your zeal for fighting, why are you fleeing with a downcast mien, O monkey? Where on earth has your valour gone? (3)

verses.text:
पृष्ठतोऽनुव्रजध्वं मामग्रतो यान्तमाहवे।
शूरैरभिजनोपेतैरयुक्तं हि निवर्तितुम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Return, close on my heels, to the battle while I am marching ahead. It is ill-advised indeed for champions of noble descent to shrink back from the battlefield.” (4)

verses.text:
एवमुक्ताः सुसंक्रुद्धा वायुपुत्रेण धीमता।
शैलशृङ्गान् द्रुमांश्चैव जगृहुर्हृष्टमानसाः॥ ५॥
verses.m: Admonished in these words by the sagacious son of the wind-god, the monkeys, who now felt delighted in mind, seized hold of mountain-peaks and trees as well in great fury. (5)

verses.text:
अभिपेतुश्च गर्जन्तो राक्षसान् वानरर्षभाः।
परिवार्य हनूमन्तमन्वयुश्च महाहवे॥ ६॥
verses.m: Nay, surrounding Hanumān on all sides, the leaders of monkeys followed him in the great fight and rushed roaring towards the ogres. (6)

verses.text:
स तैर्वानरमुख्यैस्तु हनूमान् सर्वतो वृतः।
हुताशन इवार्चिष्मानदहच्छत्रुवाहिनीम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: Surrounded on all sides by those monkey leaders, the said Hanumān began to annihilate the hostile army like a flaming fire. (7)

verses.text:
स राक्षसानां कदनं चकार सुमहाकपिः।
वृतो वानरसैन्येन कालान्तकयमोपमः॥ ८॥
verses.m: Accompanied by the simian army, that exceptionally mighty monkey, who resembled Yama assuming the role of Death at the time of universal dissolution, played havoc among the ogres. (8)

verses.text:
स तु शोकेन चाविष्टः कोपेन महता कपिः।
हनूमान् रावणिरथे महतीं पातयच्छिलाम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: Filled with inordinate grief and anger, the aforesaid monkey, Hanumān, for his part hurled a huge rock on the chariot of Indrajit (son of Rāvaṇa). (9)

verses.text:
तामापतन्तीं दृष्ट्वैव रथः सारथिना तदा।
विधेयाश्वसमायुक्तः विदूरमपवाहितः॥ १०॥
verses.m: The moment his charioteer saw the rock coming towards the chariot, the chariot, which was drawn by obedient horses, was now driven aside to a long distance by him. (10)

verses.text:
तमिन्द्रजितमप्राप्य रथस्थं सहसारथिम्।
विवेश धरणीं भित्त्वा सा शिला व्यर्थमुद्यता॥ ११॥
verses.m: Failing to reach the aforesaid Indrajit seated in his chariot alongwith the charioteer, the rock in question, which was employed in vain, entered the bowels of the earth after splitting it open. (11)

verses.text:
पतितायां शिलायां तु व्यथिता रक्षसां चमूः।
निपतन्त्या च शिलया राक्षसा मथिता भृशम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: As the rock fell, the army of the ogres for its part felt disquieted; nay, the ogres were violently crushed by the rock even as it fell. (12)

verses.text:
तमभ्यधावन् शतशो नदन्तः काननौकसः।
ते द्रुमांश्च महाकाया गिरिशृङ्गाणि चोद्यताः॥ १३॥
verses.m: Monkeys (lit., dwellers in the woods) in their hundreds rushed roaring towards Indrajit. Nay, seizing hold of trees and mountain-tops too, those colossal monkeys became fully active. (13)

verses.text:
क्षिपन्तीन्द्रजितं संख्ये वानरा भीमविक्रमाः।
वृक्षशैलमहावर्षं विसृजन्तः प्लवंगमाः॥ १४॥
शत्रूणां कदनं चक्रुर्नेदुश्च विविधैः स्वनैः।
वानरैस्तैर्महाभीमैर्घोररूपा निशाचराः॥ १५॥
वीर्यादभिहता वृक्षैर्व्यचेष्टन्त रणक्षितौ।
स सैन्यमभिवीक्ष्याथ वानरार्दितमिन्द्रजित्॥ १६॥
प्रगृहीतायुधः क्रुद्धः परानभिमुखो ययौ।
स शरौघानवसृजन् स्वसैन्येनाभिसंवृतः॥ १७॥
जघान कपिशार्दूलान् सुबहून् दृढविक्रमः।
शूलैरशनिभिः खड्गैः पट्टिशैः शूलमुद्गरैः॥ १८॥
verses.m: The monkeys of redoubtable prowess began to rail Indrajit on the battlefield. Nay, discharging a mighty shower of trees and rocks, the monkeys created havoc among the enemies and shouted in various tones. Vehemently struck on all sides with trees by those exceptionally redoubtable monkeys, the rangers of the night of hideous aspect rolled about restlessly on the battlefield. Seizing hold of his weapons in fury on perceiving the army handled roughly by the monkeys, the aforesaid Indrajit forthwith marched against the enemies. Discharging streams of arrows while surrounded by his contingent, Indrajit of unyielding prowess struck numerous tigers among the monkeys with pikes, Aśanis, swords, sharp-edged spears and Kūṭamudgaras (a concealed weapon similar to a mallet). (14—18)

verses.text:
ते चाप्यनुचरांस्तस्य वानरा जघ्नुराहवे।
सुस्कन्धविटपैः शैलैः शिलाभिश्च महाबलः॥ १९॥
हनूमान् कदनं चक्रे रक्षसां भीमकर्मणाम्।
संनिवार्य परानीकमब्रवीत् तान् वनौकसः॥ २०॥
हनूमान् संनिवर्तध्वं न नः साध्यमिदं बलम्।
त्यक्त्वा प्राणान् विचेष्टन्तो रामप्रियचिकीर्षवः॥ २१॥
यन्निमित्तं हि युध्यामो हता सा जनकात्मजा।
इममर्थं हि विज्ञाप्य रामं सुग्रीवमेव च॥ २२॥
तौ यत् प्रतिविधास्येते तत् करिष्यामहे वयम्।
इत्युक्त्वा वानरश्रेष्ठो वारयन् सर्ववानरान्॥ २३॥
शनैः शनैरसंत्रस्तः सबलः संन्यवर्तत।
ततः प्रेक्ष्य हनूमन्तं व्रजन्तं यत्र राघवः॥ २४॥
स होतुकामो दुष्टात्मा गतश्चैत्यं निकुम्भिलाम्।
निकुम्भिलामधिष्ठाय पावकं जुहवेन्द्रजित्॥ २५॥
verses.m: Those monkeys too killed his followers in combat. Hanumān, on the other hand, who was endowed with extraordinary might, played havoc among the ogres of terrible deeds with sal trees distinguished by excellent trunks and boughs as well as with rocks. Keeping the hostile army back, Hanumān spoke as follows to those monkeys (lit., dwellers in the woods): “Retreat! This army need not be conquered by us any more. That daughter of Janaka—for whom indeed we have fought so far, risking our lives and making a special effort to win, seeking as we did to do what is pleasing to Śrī Rāma—has been killed. Making this fact known to Śrī Rāma as well as to Sugrīva, we shall certainly do that which they will enjoin us to do in return.” Perceiving Hanumān withdrawing to the place where Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) was, the evil-minded ogre proceeded to the sanctuary known by the name of Nikumbhilā, seeking as he did to pour oblations into the sacred fire. Reaching Nikumbhilā, Indrajit poured oblations into the sacred fire. (19—25)

verses.text:
यज्ञभूम्यां ततो गत्वा पावकस्तेन रक्षसा।
हूयमानः प्रजज्वाल होमशोणितभुक् तदा॥ २६॥
verses.m: While being propitiated with oblations by that ogre on arriving at the sacrificial ground, the sacrificial fire blazed up on consuming the oblations of blood on that occasion. (26)

verses.text:
सार्चिःपिनद्धो ददृशे होमशोणिततर्पितः।
संध्यागत इवादित्यः सुतीव्रोऽग्निः समुत्थितः॥ २७॥
verses.m: Swollen up when propitiated with oblations of blood, the fierce fire, which resembled the evening sun, was seen wrapped in flames. (27)

verses.text:
अथेन्द्रजिद् राक्षसभूतये तु
जुहाव हव्यं विधिना विधानवित्।
दृष्ट्वा व्यतिष्ठन्त च राक्षसास्ते
महासमूहेषु नयानयज्ञाः॥ २८॥
verses.m: For the prosperity of the ogres in general, Indrajit for his part, who was well-versed in the technique pertaining to sacrifices, forthwith poured oblations into the sacrificial fire according to the scriptural ordinance. Nay, beholding this, the well-known ogres, who knew what was right and wrong in major conflicts, stood firm by his side. (28)

verses.text:
राघवश्चापि विपुलं तं राक्षसवनौकसाम्।
श्रुत्वा संग्रामनिर्घोषं जाम्बवन्तमुवाच ह॥ १॥
verses.m: Nay, hearing that great tumult following the encounter between the ogres and the monkeys (lit., dwellers in the woods), Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) too spoke as follows to Jāmbavān: (1)

verses.text:
सौम्य नूनं हनुमता कृतं कर्म सुदुष्करम्।
श्रूयते च यथा भीमः सुमहानायुधस्वनः॥ २॥
verses.m: “From the way in which a terrible and exceptionally loud rattling of arms is heard, it appears that a feat exceedingly difficult (to perform for others) has undoubtedly been performed by Hanumān, O dear one! (2)

verses.text:
तद्गच्छ कुरु साहाय्यं स्वबलेनाभिसंवृतः।
क्षिप्रमृक्षपते तस्य कपिश्रेष्ठस्य युध्यतः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Therefore, accompanied by your own army (of bears), go and instantly lend your aid, O lord of bears, to that prince of monkeys, who is fighting.” (3)

verses.text:
ऋक्षराजस्तथेत्युक्त्वा स्वेनानीकेन संवृतः।
आगच्छत्पश्चिमं द्वारं हनूमान् यत्र वानरः॥ ४॥
verses.m: Saying “Amen”, and surrounded by his own army, Jāmbavān (the lord of bears) sought the western gate, where the monkey, Hanumān, was. (4)

verses.text:
अथायान्तं हनूमन्तं ददर्शर्क्षपतिस्तदा।
वानरैः कृतसंग्रामैः श्वसद्भिरभिसंवृतम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: The lord of bears forthwith saw Hanumān returning at that time accompanied by monkeys, who had given fight and were sighing (on account of grief caused by the destruction of ‘Sītā’). (5)

verses.text:
दृष्ट्वा पथि हनूमांश्च तदृक्षबलमुद्यतम्।
नीलमेघनिभं भीमं संनिवार्य न्यवर्तत॥ ६॥
verses.m: Beholding that redoubtable army of bears, resembling a dark cloud, on their way, ready for an encounter, and effectively intercepting it, Hanumān retreated with them all. (6)

verses.text:
स तेन सह सैन्येन संनिकर्षं महायशाः।
शीघ्रमागम्य रामाय दुःखितो वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ ७॥
verses.m: Speedily seeking the presence of Śrī Rāma with that army, the highly illustrious Hanumān sorrowfully submitted to him as follows: (7)

verses.text:
समरे युध्यमानानामस्माकं प्रेक्षतां च सः।
जघान रुदतीं सीतामिन्द्रजिद्रावणात्मजः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “While we, who were carrying on a fight on the battlefield, stood looking on, that offspring of Rāvaṇa, Indrajit, killed ‘Sītā’, even though she continued to weep. (8)

verses.text:
उद्भ्रान्तचित्तस्तां दृष्ट्वा विषण्णोऽहमरिंदम।
तदहं भवतो वृत्तं विज्ञापयितुमागतः॥ ९॥
verses.m: Bewildered in mind and dejected on seeing her, O tamer of enemies, I have come back to break the aforesaid news to you.” (9)

verses.text:
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा राघवः शोकमूर्च्छितः।
निपपात तदा भूमौ छिन्नमूल इव द्रुमः॥ १०॥
verses.m: Rendered insensible through grief on hearing the aforesaid submission of Hanumān, Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) forthwith fell to the ground like a tree whose roots have been severed. (10)

verses.text:
तं भूमौ देवसंकाशं पतितं दृश्य राघवम्।
अभिपेतुः समुत्पत्य सर्वतः कपिसत्तमाः॥ ११॥
आसिञ्चन् सलिलैश्चैनं पद्मोत्पलसुगन्धिभिः।
प्रदहन्तमसंहार्यं सहसाग्निमिवोत्थितम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: Seeing that scion of Raghu, who looked like a god, fallen, the leaders of monkeys hastened towards him springing from all sides and sprinkled him with water fragrant with the scent of lotuses and lilies even as one would sprinkle an inextinguishable fire which has just flared up, all of a sudden and is burning all. (11-12)

verses.text:
तं लक्ष्मणोऽथ बाहुभ्यां परिष्वज्य सुदुःखितः।
उवाच राममस्वस्थं वाक्यं हेत्वर्थसंयुतम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: Encircling Śrī Rāma with his arms, Lakṣmaṇa, who was seized with great agony, forthwith addressed to Śrī Rāma, who was feeling ill at ease, the following submission, which was full of reason and fraught with meaning: (13)

verses.text:
शुभे वर्त्मनि तिष्ठन्तं त्वामार्य विजितेन्द्रियम्।
अनर्थेभ्यो न शक्नोति त्रातुं धर्मो निरर्थकः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Virtue, O worthy brother, cannot save you, who are sticking to the noble path and have fully mastered the senses, from reverses and is, therefore, useless. (14)

verses.text:
भूतानां स्थावराणां च जङ्गमानां च दर्शनम्।
यथास्ति न तथा धर्मस्तेन नास्तीति मे मतिः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Just as joy is experienced by created beings, both inanimate and animate, virtue is not likewise perceived to be the cause of their happiness. Hence virtue is not the cause of happiness: such is my conclusion. (15)

verses.text:
यथैव स्थावरं व्यक्तं जङ्गमं च तथाविधम्।
नायमर्थस्तथा युक्तस्त्वद्विधो न विपद्यते॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Even as it is evident that the inanimate creation is happy (without the concomitant practice of virtue), the animate creation too is happy likewise. Therefore, the presumption that virtue alone prospers is not warranted; for, in that case a purely virtuous man like you would not suffer. (16)

verses.text:
यद्यधर्मो भवेद्भूतो रावणो नरकं व्रजेत्।
भवांश्च धर्मसंयुक्तो नैव व्यसनमाप्नुयात्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Had unrighteousness been effective, Rāvaṇa should have descended into hell; while you, who are endowed with virtue, would never suffer adversity. (17)

verses.text:
तस्य च व्यसनाभावाद्व्यसनं चागते त्वयि।
धर्मो भवत्यधर्मश्च परस्परविरोधिनौ॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Nay, since Rāvaṇa is free from calamity, while you have met with misfortune, virtue and vice, which were the contraries of each other, have changed the roles with each other (the one turning into the other). (18)

verses.text:
धर्मेणोपलभेद्धर्ममधर्मं चाप्यधर्मतः।
यद्यधर्मेण युज्येयुर्येष्वधर्मः प्रतिष्ठितः॥ १९॥
न धर्मेण वियुज्येरन्नाधर्मरुचयो जनाः।
धर्मेणाचरतां तेषां तथा धर्मफलं भवेत्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “If one invariably attained the fruit of virtue, viz., happiness through virtue and likewise the fruit of unrighteousness alone through unrighteousness, those in whom unrighteousness is rooted would be burdened with the fruit of unrighteousness, viz., suffering. Nor would people who have no leaning towards unrighteousness would be ever deprived of the fruit of virtue, viz., joy. Nay, the fruit of virtue alone would accrue to those holding by the latter. (19-20)

verses.text:
यस्मादर्था विवर्धन्ते येष्वधर्मः प्रतिष्ठितः।
क्लिश्यन्ते धर्मशीलाश्च तस्मादेतौ निरर्थकौ॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Since the resources of those in whom unrighteousness is rooted, develop, while those who are given to the practice of virtue suffer; hence these two viz., righteousness and unrighteousness are useless. (21)

verses.text:
वध्यन्ते पापकर्माणो यद्यधर्मेण राघव।
वधकर्महतोऽधर्मः स हतः कं वधिष्यति॥ २२॥
verses.m: If it is alleged that those of sinful deeds are destroyed by their own unrighteousness, O scion of Raghu, the unrighteousness itself, consisting as it does in an act of killing etc., will be forthwith destroyed inasmuch as an action is momentary. Whom will that unrighteousness destroy, which is itself destroyed in the course of three seconds? (22)

verses.text:
अथवा विहितेनायं हन्यते हन्ति चापरम्।
विधिः स लिप्यते तेन न स पापेन कर्मणा॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Or, if a man is destroyed by recourse to a malevolent ritual prescribed in the scriptures or kills another by recourse to such a ritual, the destiny (alone) which is engendered by the aforesaid ritual is tainted by that sinful act and not the agent. (23)

verses.text:
अदृष्टप्रतिकारेण अव्यक्तेनासता सता।
कथं शक्यं परं प्राप्तुं धर्मेणारिविकर्षण॥ २४॥
verses.m: “How can another, viz., the person going to be destroyed, be reached, O destroyer of enemies, by righteousness in the form of a malevolent ritual, which, being unconscious, has never known how to retaliate, is unmanifest and is, therefore, as good as non-existent? (24)

verses.text:
यदि सत्स्यात्सतां मुख्य नासत्स्यात् तव किंचन।
त्वया यदीदृशं प्राप्तं तस्मात् तन्नोपपद्यते॥ २५॥
verses.m: “If a good destiny (engendered by a virtuous act) existed, O jewel among the virtuous, no evil would ever accrue to you. Since, however, such evil has been reaped by you, therefore, the hypothesis that the destiny engendered by good acts is real is not proved.* (25)

verses.text:
अथवा दुर्बलः क्लीबो बलं धर्मोऽनुवर्तते।
दुर्बलो हृतमर्यादो न सेव्य इति मे मतिः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “If being feeble and ineffective, virtue needs the help of might, the former, which lacks strength and has been deprived of its capacity, should no longer be pursued: such is my view. (26)

verses.text:
बलस्य यदि चेद्धर्मो गुणभूतः पराक्रमैः।
धर्ममुत्सृज्य वर्तस्व यथा धर्मे तथा बले॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Giving up the predominance of virtue by plucking up courage, if the former is subordinate to might, depend on might as you do now on virtue. (27)

verses.text:
अथ चेत्सत्यवचनं धर्मः किल परंतप।
अनृतं त्वय्यकरणे किं न बद्धस्त्वया विना॥ २८॥
verses.m: If, on the other hand, it is urged by you that virtue in the form of redeeming the truthfulness of your father is being followed by you, O scourge of your enemies, your father was disunited from you by force of the mendacity which was resorted to by him in not redeeming his announcement made regarding installing you as the Prince Regent. Were you not bound by that announcement too? (28)

verses.text:
यदि धर्मो भवेद्भूत अधर्मो वा परंतप।
न स्म हत्वा मुनिं वज्री कुर्यादिज्यां शतक्रतुः॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Had virtue alone been worth pursuing (to the exclusion of unrighteousness) or unrighteousness (to the exclusion of virtue), O scourge of your enemies, Indra (who is presupposed to have performed a hundred horse-sacrifices as a condition precedent to his attaining Indrahood), the wielder of the thunderbolt, would not have performed a horse-sacrifice (to atone for the sin of having killed a Brāhmaṇa) on killing a hermit (viz., Viśwarūpa, son of Twaṣṭā*). (29)

verses.text:
अधर्मसंश्रितो धर्मो विनाशयति राघव।
सर्वमेतद्यथाकामं काकुत्स्थ कुरुते नरः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Virtue destroys enemies only when united with strength (something other than virtue), O scion of Raghu! Therefore, a wise man takes recourse to every such means (viz., virtue and strength both) at will, O scion of Kakutstha! (30)

verses.text:
मम चेदं मतं तात धर्मोऽयमिति राघव।
धर्ममूलं त्वया छिन्नं राज्यमुत्सृजता तदा॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Nay my opinion is that righteousness consists in such recourse to both the aforesaid expedients (viz., virtue and strength). The very roots of Dharma in the shape of earthly gain have been severed by you in that you spurned sovereignty the other day (when it was being offered to you). (31)

verses.text:
अर्थेभ्योऽथ प्रवृद्धेभ्यः संवृत्तेभ्यस्ततस्ततः।
क्रियाः सर्वाः प्रवर्तन्ते पर्वतेभ्य इवापगाः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Even as streams flow from mountains, all undertakings (those conducive to union with God as well as those conducive to material enjoyment) follow from richesbrought from place to place and augmented. (Those carried on in a disinterested spirit lead to union with God, while those actuated by interested motives make for enjoyment).(32)

verses.text:
अर्थेन हि विमुक्तस्य पुरुषस्याल्पचेतसः।
विच्छिद्यन्ते क्रियाः सर्वा ग्रीष्मे कुसरितो यथा॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “All the undertakings of a man of meagre intelligence, forsaken by wealth, are interrupted even like small streams in summer. (33)

verses.text:
सोऽयमर्थं परित्यज्य सुखकामः सुखैधितः।
पापमाचरते कर्तुं तदा दोषः प्रवर्तते॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “Renouncing wealth within easy reach, a man brought up in comfort and seeking comfort then proceeds to commit sin (in the shape of thieving etc.,) and evil (in the form of punishment) follows from it. (34)

verses.text:
यस्यार्थास्तस्य मित्राणि यस्यार्थास्तस्य बान्धवाः।
यस्यार्थाः स पुमाँल्लोके यस्यार्थाः स च पण्डितः॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “Friends gather round him in whom riches abide; kinsfolk too stand by him in whom riches have found their way. He alone is honourable, in whom riches find their place; nay, he alone is learned, in whom riches have found their abode. (35)

verses.text:
यस्यार्थाः स च विक्रान्तो यस्यार्थाः स चबुद्धिमान्।
यस्यार्थाः स महाभागो यस्यार्थाः स गुणाधिकः॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “Nay, he alone is gallant, to whom riches have flown; and he alone is clever, in whom riches have come to stay. He alone is highly fortunate, in whom riches exist; again he alone is superior in excellences, in whom riches have found their receptacle. (36)

verses.text:
अर्थस्यैते परित्यागे दोषाः प्रव्याहृता मया।
राज्यमुत्सृजता धीर येन बुद्धिस्त्वया कृता॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “The evils attendant on the abjuration of wealth have been dwelt upon by me here in the shape of their contraries (verses 35-36 above). The ground on which the resolve was made by you to sacrifice your all, while forswearing the kingdom, O resolute one, is not known to me. (37)

verses.text:
यस्यार्था धर्मकामार्थास्तस्य सर्वं प्रदक्षिणम्।
अधनेनार्थकामेन नार्थः शक्यो विचिन्विता॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “The other ends too in the shape of—virtue and pleasure—of a man in whom riches abide are easily accomplished; nay, everything turns exceedingly favourable to him. Wealth, however, cannot be attained without endeavour by a penniless man seeking wealth and even hunting for it. (38)

verses.text:
हर्षः कामश्च दर्पश्च धर्मः क्रोधः शमो दमः।
अर्थादेतानि सर्वाणि प्रवर्तन्ते नराधिप॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “Delight and sensuous pleasure, pride, virtue, anger and control of the mind and the senses—all these become effective through wealth alone, O ruler of men! (39)

verses.text:
येषां नश्यत्ययं लोकश्चरतां धर्मचारिणाम्।
तेऽर्थास्त्वयि न दृश्यन्ते दुर्दिनेषु यथा ग्रहाः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “Those riches due to renunciation of which worldly happiness of those practising austerities and treading the path of virtue goes to the dogs are not found in you any more than the nine planets are seen on cloudy days. (40)

verses.text:
त्वयि प्रव्रजिते वीर गुरोश्च वचने स्थिते।
रक्षसापहृता भार्या प्राणैः प्रियतरा तव॥ ४१॥
verses.m: “While you have been in exile, faithful to the pledge of your father, your consort, who was dearer to you than life itself, was borne away by the ogre, Rāvaṇa, O heroic prince! (41)

verses.text:
तदद्य विपुलं वीर दुःखमिन्द्रजिता कृतम्।
कर्मणा व्यपनेष्यामि तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ राघव॥ ४२॥
verses.m: “I shall fully dispel with my exploits today the great agony caused by Indrajit, O gallant prince! Therefore, rise, O scion of Raghu!(42)

verses.text:
उत्तिष्ठ नरशार्दूल दीर्घबाहो धृतव्रत।
किमात्मानं महात्मानमात्मानं नावबुध्यसे॥ ४३॥
verses.m: “Get up, O tiger among men! Why don’t you recognize yourself to be the Supreme Spirit, endowed with vast intelligence, O long-armed prince, who have kept your vows?(43)

verses.text:
अयमनघ तवोदितः प्रियार्थं
जनकसुतानिधनं निरीक्ष्य रुष्टः।
सरथगजहयां सराक्षसेन्द्रां
भृशमिषुभिर्विनिपातयामि लङ्काम्॥ ४४॥
verses.m: “This submission has been made by me to win your pleasure. Enraged to learn about the destruction of Janaka’s daughter, I shall completely destroy with my arrows Laṅkā with its chariots, elephants and horses, alongwith Rāvaṇa, the ruler of ogres, O sinless one!” (44)

verses.text:
राममाश्वासमाने तु लक्ष्मणे भ्रातृवत्सले।
निक्षिप्य गुल्मान् स्वस्थाने तत्रागच्छद् विभीषणः॥ १॥
नानाप्रहरणैर्वीरैश्चतुर्भिरभिसंवृतः।
नीलाञ्जनचयाकारैर्मातंगैरिव यूथपैः॥ २॥
verses.m: Having restored the simian troops to their position while Lakṣmaṇa, who was so fond of his elder brother, was reassuring Śrī Rāma, Vibhīṣaṇa for his part made his appearance there, surrounded by four champions armed with various weapons and resembling elephants, who were leaders of their herds and looked like heaps of collyrium. (1-2)

verses.text:
सोऽभिगम्य महात्मानं राघवं शोकलालसम्।
वानरांश्चापि ददृशे बाष्पपर्याकुलेक्षणान्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Approaching the high-souled Lakṣmaṇa, a scion of Raghu, he found him entirely given up to grief and the monkeys too with their eyes full of tears. (3)

verses.text:
राघवं च महात्मानमिक्ष्वाकुकुलनन्दनम्।
ददर्श मोहमापन्नं लक्ष्मणस्याङ्कमाश्रितम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: He also beheld the high-souled Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, the delight of Ikṣwāku’s race, fallen into a swoon and lying in the lap of Lakṣmaṇa. (4)

verses.text:
व्रीडितं शोकसंतप्तं दृष्ट्वा रामं विभीषणः।
अन्तर्दुःखेन दीनात्मा किमेतदिति सोऽब्रवीत्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Vibhīṣaṇa felt depressed in spirits due to mental anguish on seeing Śrī Rāma put out of countenance and tormented with grief. He said, “What is this?” (5)

verses.text:
विभीषणमुखं दृष्ट्वा सुग्रीवं तांश्च वानरान्।
लक्ष्मणोवाच मन्दार्थमिदं बाष्पपरिप्लुतः॥ ६॥
verses.m: Fixing his gaze on the face of Vibhīṣaṇa and looking at Sugrīva and the celebrated monkeys, Lakṣmaṇa, who was bathed in tears, spoke in the following terse language: (6)

verses.text:
हता इन्द्रजिता सीता इति श्रुत्वैव राघवः।
हनूमद्वचनात् सौम्य ततो मोहमुपाश्रितः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Immediately on hearing through the words of Hanumān that Sītā has been killed by Indrajit, Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, O friend, has fallen into a swoon for that reason.” (7)

verses.text:
कथयन्तं तु सौमित्रिं संनिवार्य विभीषणः।
पुष्कलार्थमिदं वाक्यं विसंज्ञं राममब्रवीत्॥ ८॥
verses.m: Restraining the son of Sumitrā even while he was speaking, Vibhīṣaṇa, for his part, made the following submission, which was full of ample meaning, to Śrī Rāma, who was lying unconscious: (8)

verses.text:
मनुजेन्द्रार्तरूपेण यदुक्तस्त्वं हनूमता।
तदयुक्तमहं मन्ये सागरस्येव शोषणम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “I hold that what you have been told by Hanumān with a sorrowful mien, O ruler of men, to be absurd as the drying up of the sea. (9)

verses.text:
अभिप्रायं तु जानामि रावणस्य दुरात्मनः।
सीतां प्रति महाबाहो न च घातं करिष्यति॥ १०॥
verses.m: “I, for my part, know the design of the evil-minded Rāvaṇa with reference to Sītā, O mighty-armed one! He would never cause her to be killed. (10)

verses.text:
याच्यमानः सुबहुशो मया हितचिकीर्षुणा।
वैदेहीमुत्सृजस्वेति न च तत् कृतवान् वचः॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Nay, even though being solicited very often by me, who wished well of him, in the words: ‘Give up the princess of the Videha territory!’ he would never heed that advice of mine. (11)

verses.text:
नैव साम्ना न दानेन न भेदेन कुतो युधा।
सा द्रष्टुमपि शक्येत नैव चान्येन केनचित्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “She cannot even be perceived in any wise, much less killed, by anyone else by recourse to persuasion, gift or sowing dissension, much less by recourse to war. (12)

verses.text:
वानरान् मोहयित्वा तु प्रतियातः स राक्षसः।
मायामयीं महाबाहो तां विद्धि जनकात्मजाम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “That ogre, Indrajit, for his part withdrew from the battlefield after hoodwinking the monkeys. Know that daughter of Janaka, who was seemingly killed by him, to be illusory, O mighty-armed one! (13)

verses.text:
चैत्यं निकुम्भिलामद्य प्राप्य होमं करिष्यति।
हुतवानुपयातो हि देवैरपि सवासवैः॥ १४॥
दुराधर्षो भवत्येष संग्रामे रावणात्मजः।
तेन मोहयता नूनमेषा माया प्रयोजिता॥ १५॥
विघ्नमन्विच्छता तत्र वानराणां पराक्रमे।
ससैन्यास्तत्र गच्छामो यावत्तन्न समाप्यते॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Duly reaching the sanctuary known by the name of Nikumbhilā today, he will pour oblations into the sacred fire. Having returned after pouring oblations into the sacred fire, Indrajit, sprung from the loins of Rāvaṇa, will undoubtedly prove difficult to overcome in battle even for gods including Indra, the ruler of gods. Surely this conjuring trick (in the shape of killing an illusory living effigy of Sītā) was employed by him in order to put us off the scent, anticipating, as he did, interruption in his sacrificial performance at the hands of the monkeys in the event of their prowess remaining unchecked on the battlefield. We shall, therefore, proceed to that place with an army while the sacrificial performance is not yet over. (14—16)

verses.text:
त्यजैनं नरशार्दूल मिथ्या संतापमागतम्।
सीदते हि बलं सर्वं दृष्ट्वा त्वां शोककर्शितम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Shake off, O tiger among men, this agony which has come upon you without any real cause. Seeing you stricken with grief, the entire army is feeling distressed. (17)

verses.text:
इह त्वं स्वस्थहृदयस्तिष्ठ सत्त्वसमुच्छ्रितः।
लक्ष्मणं प्रेषयास्माभिः सह सैन्यानुकर्षिभिः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Very elevated as you are in courage, stay you here, confident at heart, and dispatch Lakṣmaṇa with us, who are taking the army alongwith us. (18)

verses.text:
एष तं नरशार्दूलो रावणिं निशितैः शरैः।
त्याजयिष्यति तत्कर्म ततो वध्यो भविष्यति॥ १९॥
verses.m: “With his whetted shafts this tiger among men will compel the aforesaid son of Rāvaṇa to discontinue that ritual; then he will be prone to being dispatched. (19)

verses.text:
तस्यैते निशितास्तीक्ष्णाः पत्रिपत्राङ्गवाजिनः।
पतत्त्रिण इवासौम्याः शराः पास्यन्ति शोणितम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “These whetted and piercing arrows of Lakṣmaṇa, which fly swiftly, furnished as they are with the limbs of birds in the form of their feathers, will drink Indrajit’s blood like cruel birds. (20)

verses.text:
तत् संदिश महाबाहो लक्ष्मणं शुभलक्षणम्।
राक्षसस्य विनाशाय वज्रं वज्रधरो यथा॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Therefore, O mighty-armed one, dispatch Lakṣmaṇa, who is endowed with auspicious bodily marks, for the destruction of the ogre, Indrajit, even as Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, would employ the thunderbolt for the destruction of his enemies, the demons. (21)

verses.text:
मनुजवर न कालविप्रकर्षो
रिपुनिधनं प्रति यत्क्षमोऽद्य कर्तुम्।
त्वमतिसृज रिपोर्वधाय वज्रं
दिविजरिपोर्मथने यथा महेन्द्रः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Since, O jewel among human beings (the progeny of Manu), loss of time in compassing the death of the enemy, Indrajit, is no longer desirable in anyway, send Lakṣmaṇa for making short work of the enemy even as the mighty Indra, the ruler of gods, would hurl his thunderbolt for the destruction of an enemy of gods (lit., those born in heaven). (22)

verses.text:
समाप्तकर्मा हि स राक्षसर्षभो
भवत्यदृश्यः समरे सुरासुरैः।
युयुत्सता तेन समाप्तकर्मणा
भवेत् सुराणामपि संशयो महान्॥ २३॥
verses.m: “On concluding the ritual, that prince of ogres will turn invisible on the battlefield to gods and demons alike. There will be great danger even to gods in fighting with him when he has concluded the ritual and feels inclined to fight.” (23)

verses.text:
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा राघवः शोककर्शितः।
नोपधारयते व्यक्तं यदुक्तं तेन रक्षसा॥ १॥
verses.m: Even on hearing the aforesaid submission of Vibhīṣaṇa, Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), who was stricken with grief, could not make out clearly what was submitted by that ogre. (1)

verses.text:
ततो धैर्यमवष्टभ्य रामः परपुरंजयः।
विभीषणमुपासीनमुवाच कपिसंनिधौ॥ २॥
verses.m: Plucking up courage, Śrī Rāma, the conqueror of hostile citadels, spoke as follows to Vibhīṣaṇa, seated by his side, in the presence of the monkey, Hanumān: (2)

verses.text:
नैर्ऋताधिपते वाक्यं यदुक्तं ते विभीषण।
भूयस्तच्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि ब्रूहि यत्ते विवक्षितम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “I wish to hear once more, O suzerain lord of ogres (lit., the progeny of Nirṛti, the ogre presiding over the south-west), that submission which was made by you, O Vibhīṣaṇa! Repeat that which was sought to be conveyed by you.” (3)

verses.text:
राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः।
यत् तत् पुनरिदं वाक्यं बभाषेऽथ विभीषणः॥ ४॥
verses.m: Hearing the command of Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, Vibhīṣaṇa, who was skilled in expression, forthwith repeated as follows the same submission, which was made by him before: (4)

verses.text:
यथाऽऽज्ञप्तं महाबाहो त्वया गुल्मनिवेशनम्।
तत् तथानुष्ठितं वीर त्वद्वाक्यसमनन्तरम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Immediately after your command, the marshalling of troops was done by me in the same way as was enjoined by you, O mighty-armed hero! (5)

verses.text:
तान्यनीकानि सर्वाणि विभक्तानि समन्ततः।
विन्यस्ता यूथपाश्चैव यथान्यायं विभागशः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “All those troops have been divided and arrayed all-round and their commanders too have been allotted their respective posts according to their rank. (6)

verses.text:
भूयस्तु मम विज्ञाप्यं तच्छृणुष्व महाप्रभो।
त्वय्यकारणसंतप्ते संतप्तहृदया वयम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Now hear, O mighty lord, that which remains to be submitted by me yet. When you are afflicted without any cause, we too feel pained at heart. (7)

verses.text:
त्यज राजन्निमं शोकं मिथ्या संतापमागतम्।
यदियं त्यज्यतां चिन्ता शत्रुहर्षविवर्धिनी॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Therefore, shake off, O prince, this grief and agony, which have appeared in you without any ostensible reason. This anxiety too should be given up inasmuch as it considerably enhances the joy of the enemy. (8)

verses.text:
उद्यमः क्रियतां वीर हर्षः समुपसेव्यताम्।
प्राप्तव्या यदि ते सीता हन्तव्याश्च निशाचराः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Let a strenuous and continuous effort be made, O hero, and let enthusiasm be fully resorted to, if Sītā is to be recovered by you and the rangers of the night are to be exterminated. (9)

verses.text:
रघुनन्दन वक्ष्यामि श्रूयतां मे हितं वचः।
साध्वयं यातु सौमित्रिर्बलेन महता वृतः॥ १०॥
निकुम्भिलायां सम्प्राप्तं हन्तुं रावणिमाहवे।
धनुर्मण्डलनिर्मुक्तैराशीविषविषोपमैः ॥ ११॥
शरैर्हन्तुं महेष्वासो रावणिं समितिंजयः।
तेन वीरेण तपसा वरदानात् स्वयंभुवः।
अस्त्रं ब्रह्मशिरः प्राप्तं कामगाश्च तुरङ्गमाः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Pray, listen carefully, O delight of the Raghus, to my salutary counsel, which I am presently going to submit. Accompanied by a huge army, this son of Sumitrā should proceed to dispatch in an encounter Indrajit, son of Rāvaṇa, duly arrived in the sanctuary of Nikumbhilā. Lakṣmaṇa, who is armed with a mighty bow, who has ever been victorious in combat, is capable of killing the son of Rāvaṇa with the arrows deadly as the poison of a venomous serpent, shot from his bow, which assumes a circular shape when stretched at full length. A mystic missile known by the name of Brahmaśira (so-called because it is presided over by Brahmā) as well as horses coursing at his will has been well-nigh secured* by that hero by virtue of a boon granted by Brahmā (the self-born creator) pleased with his asceticism. (10—12)

verses.text:
स एष किल सैन्येन प्राप्तः किल निकुम्भिलाम्।
यद्युत्तिष्ठेत् कृतं कर्म हतान् सर्वांश्च विद्धि नः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Nay, they say he has already actually reached Nikumbhilā with his army. If he gets up after concluding the ritual undertaken by him, take us all as killed. (13)

verses.text:
निकुम्भिलामसम्प्राप्तमकृताग्निं च यो रिपुः।
त्वामाततायिनं हन्यादिन्द्रशत्रो स ते वधः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “ ‘That enemy of yours who strikes you while you are marching against him with a stretched bow, and while you have not yet reached the foot of the banyan tree known by the name of Nikumbhilā or even while you have not yet propitiated the fire, will prove to be the cause of your death, O enemy of Indra!’ (14)

verses.text:
वरो दत्तो महाबाहो सर्वलोकेश्वरेण वै।
इत्येवं विहितो राजन् वधस्तस्यैष धीमतः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Such was the boon granted in his favour by Brahmā, the ruler of all the worlds, O mighty-armed prince, and in this way has the end of that sagacious ogre been ordained. (15)

verses.text:
वधायेन्द्रजितो राम संदिशस्व महाबलम्।
हते तस्मिन् हतं विद्धि रावणं ससुहृद्गणम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Therefore, depute, O Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, who is endowed with extraordinary might, for compassing the destruction of Indrajit. When he is killed, take Rāvaṇa as killed with the host of his kinsfolk.” (16)

verses.text:
विभीषणवचः श्रुत्वा रामो वाक्यमथाब्रवीत्।
जानामि तस्य रौद्रस्य मायां सत्यपराक्रम॥ १७॥
verses.m: Hearing the plea of Vibhīṣaṇa, Śrī Rāma forthwith made the following reply: “I am aware, O ogre of unfailing prowess, of the conjuring skill practised by that fierce ogre. (17)

verses.text:
स हि ब्रह्मास्त्रवित् प्राज्ञो महामायो महाबलः।
करोत्यसंज्ञान् संग्रामे देवान् सवरुणानपि॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Skilled in the use of the mystic missile presided over by Brahmā (the creator) and highly intelligent, nay, a great master of conjuring tricks and endowed with extraordinary might, he can actually render unconscious in combat even gods including Varuṇa. (18)

verses.text:
तस्यान्तरिक्षे चरतः सरथस्य महायशः।
न गतिर्ज्ञायते वीर सूर्यस्येवाभ्रसम्प्लवे॥ १९॥
verses.m: “When he drives in the air in his chariot, his movement, O highly illustrious hero, cannot be perceived any more than that of the sun coursing behind a mass of clouds.” (19)

verses.text:
राघवस्तु रिपोर्ज्ञात्वा मायावीर्यं दुरात्मनः।
लक्ष्मणं कीर्तिसम्पन्नमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ २०॥
verses.m: Knowing, as he did, the power of the conjuring tricks of the evil-minded enemy, Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, for his part spoke as follows to the illustrious Lakṣmaṇa: (20)

verses.text:
यद् वानरेन्द्रस्य बलं तेन सर्वेण संवृतः।
हनूमत्प्रमुखैश्चैव यूथपैः सह लक्ष्मण॥ २१॥
जाम्बवेनर्क्षपतिना सह सैन्येन संवृतः।
जहि तं राक्षससुतं मायाबलसमन्वितम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Surrounded by the entire army which stands at the disposal of Sugrīva, the ruler of monkeys, and also accompanied by troop-commanders with Hanumān as their leader and protected by Jāmbavān, the lord of bears, who, too, will be accompanied by an army, make short work, O Lakṣmaṇa, of that son of an ogre, rich in the power of magic. (21-22)

verses.text:
अयं त्वां सचिवैः सार्धं महात्मा रजनीचरः।
अभिज्ञस्तस्य मायानां पृष्ठतोऽनुगमिष्यति॥ २३॥
verses.m: “This high-souled night-ranger, Vibhīṣaṇa, who is fully aware of his conjuring tricks, will follow you at your heels with his ministers.” (23)

verses.text:
राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणः सविभीषणः।
जग्राह कार्मुकश्रेष्ठमन्यद् भीमपराक्रमः॥ २४॥
verses.m: Hearing the command of Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, Lakṣmaṇa of redoubtable prowess, who was accompanied by Vibhīṣaṇa, took up another bow, the foremost of bows. (24)

verses.text:
संनद्धः कवची खड्गी सशरी वामचापभृत्।
रामपादावुपस्पृश्य हृष्टः सौमित्रिरब्रवीत्॥ २५॥
verses.m: Touching the feet of Śrī Rāma and feeling delighted, Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā), who was fully equipped for an encounter, clad in armour and armed with a sword and excellent arrows, and bore the bow in his left hand, submitted as follows: (25)

verses.text:
अद्य मत्कार्मुकोन्मुक्ताः शरा निर्भिद्य रावणिम्।
लङ्कामभिपतिष्यन्ति हंसाः पुष्करिणीमिव॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Piercing Indrajit (son of Rāvaṇa) today, the arrows shot from my bow will drop into Laṅkā even as swans descend into a lotus-pond. (26)

verses.text:
अद्यैव तस्य रौद्रस्य शरीरं मामकाः शराः।
विधमिष्यन्ति भित्त्वा तं महाचापगुणच्युताः॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Splitting the body of that violent ogre when shot from the string of my mighty bow, my arrows will make short work of him this very day.” (27)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा तु वचनं द्युतिमान् भ्रातुरग्रतः।
स रावणिवधाकांक्षी लक्ष्मणस्त्वरितं ययौ॥ २८॥
verses.m: Having made the aforesaid submission in the presence of his eldest brother, Śrī Rāma, the brilliant Lakṣmaṇa for his part departed with all speed, longing as he did to dispose of Indrajit, son of Rāvaṇa. (28)

verses.text:
सोऽभिवाद्य गुरोः पादौ कृत्वा चापि प्रदक्षिणम्।
निकुम्भिलामभिययौ चैत्यं रावणिपालितम्॥ २९॥
verses.m: Having saluted the feet of his eldest brother and also walked round him clockwise, he set out for the sanctuary of Nikumbhilā, protected by Indrajit, son of Rāvaṇa. (29)

verses.text:
विभीषणेन सहितो राजपुत्रः प्रतापवान्।
कृतस्वस्त्ययनो भ्रात्रा लक्ष्मणस्त्वरितो ययौ॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Accompanied by Vibhīṣaṇa, the mighty Prince, Lakṣmaṇa, for whom Mantras invoking good-luck were recited by his own eldest brother, hastened away. (30)

verses.text:
वानराणां सहस्रैस्तु हनूमान् बहुभिर्वृतः।
विभीषणश्च सामात्यो लक्ष्मणं त्वरितं ययौ॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Hanumān, who was surrounded by several thousands of monkeys, and Vibhīṣaṇa, who was accompanied by his ministers, followed Lakṣmaṇa quickly. (31)

verses.text:
महता हरिसैन्येन सवेगमभिसंवृतः।
ऋक्षराजबलं चैव ददर्श पथि विष्ठितम्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: Followed with impetuosity by a large army of monkeys, Lakṣmaṇa also beheld the army of Jāmbavān, the ruler of bears, stationed on the way. (32)

verses.text:
स गत्वा दूरमध्वानं सौमित्रिर्मित्रनन्दनः।
राक्षसेन्द्रबलं दूरादपश्यद् व्यूहमाश्रितम्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: Having covered a great distance, Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā), the delight of his friends, perceived from afar the army of Rāvaṇa, the ruler of ogres, ranged in battle-array. (33)

verses.text:
स सम्प्राप्य धनुष्पाणिर्मायायोगमरिंदमः।
तस्थौ ब्रह्मविधानेन विजेतुं रघुनन्दनः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: Duly reaching Nikumbhilā, that tamer of his enemies, Lakṣmaṇa (the delight of the Raghus), stood, bow in hand, to vanquish utterly Indrajit (who took recourse to conjuring tricks as an expedient in war) in conformity with Brahmā’s ordinance in the form of the boon granted by him in favour of Indrajit (vide verse 14 above). (34)

verses.text:
विभीषणेन सहितो राजपुत्रः प्रतापवान्।
अङ्गदेन च वीरेण तथानिलसुतेन च॥ ३५॥
विविधममलशस्त्रभास्वरं तद्
ध्वजगहनं गहनं महारथैश्च।
प्रतिभयतममप्रमेयवेगं
तिमिरमिव द्विषतां बलं विवेश॥ ३६॥
verses.m: Accompanied by Vibhīṣaṇa as also by the valiant Aṅgada as well as by Hanumān (son of the wind-god), the mighty prince, Lakṣmaṇa, penetrated that heterogeneous army of the enemy, which was resplendent with spotless weapons and thick with ensigns, and which abounded in huge chariots, was exceedingly formidable and was endowed with immeasurable impetuosity—even as one would penetrate a thick veil of darkness. (35-36)

verses.text:
अथ तस्यामवस्थायां लक्ष्मणं रावणानुजः।
परेषामहितं वाक्यमर्थसाधकमब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: In that situation Vibhīṣaṇa, the youngest brother of Rāvaṇa, forthwith tendered to Lakṣmaṇa an advice, which was conducive to his interest and detrimental to the enemies. (1)

verses.text:
यदेतद् राक्षसानीकं मेघश्यामं विलोक्यते।
एतदायोध्यतां शीघ्रं कपिभिश्च शिलायुधैः॥ २॥
verses.m: “Let this army of ogres, which is seen here, dark as a cloud, be quickly engaged in battle by the monkeys, using rocks as their weapon. (2)

verses.text:
तस्यानीकस्य महतो भेदने यत लक्ष्मण।
राक्षसेन्द्रसुतोऽप्यत्र भिन्ने दृश्यो भविष्यति॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Nay, make an effort in the direction of overthrowing that mighty army, O Lakṣmaṇa! When the yonder army is destroyed, Indrajit, son of the ruler of ogres, too will become visible here. (3)

verses.text:
स त्वमिन्द्राशनिप्रख्यैः शरैरवकिरन् परान्।
अभिद्रवाशु यावद् वै नैतत् कर्म समाप्यते॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Therefore, so long as this undertaking of Indrajit is not actually carried through, promptly assail you the enemies, covering them with your arrows resembling the thunderbolt of Indra, the ruler of gods. (4)

verses.text:
जहि वीर दुरात्मानं मायापरमधार्मिकम्।
रावणिं क्रूरकर्माणं सर्वलोकभयावहम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Destroy, O hero, the evil-minded and unrighteous Indrajit, son of Rāvaṇa, of cruel deeds, who is given up to conjuring tricks and is the terror of all the worlds.” (5)

verses.text:
विभीषणवचः श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणः शुभलक्षणः।
ववर्ष शरवर्षेण राक्षसेन्द्रसुतं प्रति॥ ६॥
verses.m: Hearing the counsel of Vibhīṣaṇa, Lakṣmaṇa, who was endowed with auspicious bodily marks, began to cover the army of ogres with a rain of shafts in order that it may descend on Indrajit, son of the ruler of ogres. (6)

verses.text:
ऋक्षाः शाखामृगाश्चैव द्रुमप्रवरयोधिनः।
अभ्यधावन्त सहितास्तदनीकमवस्थितम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: Bears and monkeys, too, who fought with big trees in this hands, rushed together towards that army drawn up in battle-array. (7)

verses.text:
राक्षसाश्च शितैर्बाणैरसिभिः शक्तितोमरैः।
अभ्यवर्तन्त समरे कपिसैन्यजिघांसवः॥ ८॥
verses.m: Eager to exterminate the simian army, ogres too launched a counter-attack on the battlefield with their sharp arrows, swords, javelins and lances. (8)

verses.text:
स सम्प्रहारस्तुमुलः संजज्ञे कपिरक्षसाम्।
शब्देन महता लङ्कां नादयन् वै समन्ततः॥ ९॥
verses.m: That encounter between the monkeys and ogres proved to be a tumultuous one, rendering Laṅkā noisy, as it did on all sides with its mighty uproar. (9)

verses.text:
शस्त्रैश्च विविधाकारैः शितैर्बाणैश्च पादपैः।
उद्यतैर्गिरिशृङ्गैश्च घोरैराकाशमावृतम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: The sky on that battlefield was covered with weapons of various shapes as well as with sharp arrows and uplifted trees and formidable mountain-peaks. (10)

verses.text:
राक्षसा वानरेन्द्रेषु विकृताननबाहवः।
निवेशयन्तः शस्त्राणि चक्रुस्ते सुमहद्भयम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: Directing their weapons towards the monkey-chiefs, ogres of mis-shapen faces and arms created great terror. (11)

verses.text:
तथैव सकलैर्वृक्षैर्गिरिशृङ्गैश्च वानराः।
अभिजघ्नुर्निजघ्नुश्च समरे सर्वराक्षसान्॥ १२॥
verses.m: The monkeys, too, likewise, wounded and struck down all the ogres on the battlefield with full trees and mountain-peaks. (12)

verses.text:
ऋक्षवानरमुख्यैश्च महाकायैर्महाबलैः।
रक्षसां युध्यमानानां महद्भयमजायत॥ १३॥
verses.m: A great fear was caused among the ogres, fighting as they did with the foremost of bears and monkeys endowed with gigantic forms and extraordinary might. (13)

verses.text:
स्वमनीकं विषण्णं तु श्रुत्वा शत्रुभिरर्दितम्।
उदतिष्ठत दुर्धर्षः स कर्मण्यननुष्ठिते॥ १४॥
verses.m: Hearing of his own army being dispirited, assailed as it was heavily by the enemy, Indrajit, who was difficult to overpower, got up even while the ritual had not yet been carried through. (14)

verses.text:
वृक्षान्धकारान्निर्गत्य जातक्रोधः स रावणिः।
आरुरोह रथं सज्जं पूर्वयुक्तं सुसंयतम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Emerging from the darkness occasioned by the trees in whose shade he was pouring oblations into the sacred fire, the aforesaid Indrajit (son of Rāvaṇa), whose indignation was aroused by the disconcerting report, mounted his firmly equipped chariot, to which horses had already been harnessed and stood ready. (15)

verses.text:
स भीमकार्मुकशरः कृष्णाञ्जनचयोपमः।
रक्तास्यनयनो भीमो बभौ मृत्युरिवान्तकः॥ १६॥
verses.m: With his coppery face and red eyes, the redoubtable ogre, who was armed with a formidable bow and arrow and resembled a heap of black collyrium, looked like the all-destroying Death. (16)

verses.text:
दृष्ट्वैव तु रथस्थं तं पर्यवर्तत तद् बलम्।
रक्षसां भीमवेगानां लक्ष्मणेन युयुत्सताम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: Immediately on seeing him seated in his chariot, the aforesaid army of ogres of terrible impetuosity, who were eager to fight with Lakṣmaṇa, ranged round Indrajit. (17)

verses.text:
तस्मिंस्तु काले हनुमानरुजत् स दुरासदम्।
धरणीधरसंकाशो महावृक्षमरिंदमः॥ १८॥
verses.m: At that time the celebrated Hanumān, the tamer of his enemies, for his part, who resembled a mountain, uprooted a huge tree, which was difficult to wield. (18)

verses.text:
स राक्षसानां तत् सैन्यं कालाग्निरिव निर्दहन्।
चकार बहुभिर्वृक्षैर्निःसंज्ञं युधि वानरः॥ १९॥
verses.m: Consuming that army of ogres like the fire of universal destruction, the aforesaid monkey, Hanumān, rendered it unconscious on the battlefield by battering it with numerous trees. (19)

verses.text:
विध्वंसयन्तं तरसा दृष्ट्वैव पवनात्मजम्।
राक्षसानां सहस्राणि हनूमन्तमवाकिरन्॥ २०॥
verses.m: Immediately on perceiving the son of the wind-god playing havoc with his might, thousands of ogres pounded Hanumān with a hail of weapons. (20)

verses.text:
शितशूलधराः शूलैरसिभिश्चासिपाणयः।
शक्तिहस्ताश्च शक्तीभिः पट्टिशैः पट्टिशायुधाः॥ २१॥
परिघैश्च गदाभिश्च कुन्तैश्च शुभदर्शनैः।
शतशश्च शतघ्नीभिरायसैरपि मुद्गरैः॥ २२॥
घोरैः परशुभिश्चैव भिन्दिपालैश्च राक्षसाः।
मुष्टिभिर्वज्रकल्पैश्च तलैरशनिसंनिभैः॥ २३॥
अभिजघ्नुः समासाद्य समन्तात् पर्वतोपमम्।
तेषामपि च संक्रुद्धश्चकार कदनं महत्॥ २४॥
verses.m: Approaching Hanumān, who looked like a mountain, ogres bearing pointed pikes struck him on all sides with pikes, those carrying swords in their hands, with swords; those carrying javelins in their hands, with javelins; those armed with sharp-edged spears, with spears; and others with iron bludgeons and maces as also with bright-looking spears and Śataghnīs (stones or cylindrical pieces of wood studded with iron spikes and used as a missile) in their hundreds, as also with steel hammers and even so with formidable axes and Bhindipālas (a kind of sling for throwing stones) as also with their fists, which descended like lightning, and slaps, which fell like the thunderbolt. Seized with a fury, Hanumān played great havoc even among them. (21—24)

verses.text:
स ददर्श कपिश्रेष्ठमचलोपममिन्द्रजित्।
सूदमानमसंत्रस्तममित्रान् पवनात्मजम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: The notorious Indrajit beheld Hanumān (sprung from the loins of the wind-god), the foremost of the monkeys, who resembled a mountain, fearlessly destroying his adversaries. (25)

verses.text:
स सारथिमुवाचेदं याहि यत्रैष वानरः।
क्षयमेव हि नः कुर्याद् राक्षसानामुपेक्षितः॥ २६॥
verses.m: He spoke to his charioteer as follows: “Drive to the spot where the yonder monkey is seen. If ignored, he will undoubtedly compass the destruction of all of us, ogres.” (26)

verses.text:
इत्युक्तः सारथिस्तेन ययौ यत्र स मारुतिः।
वहन् परमदुर्धर्षं स्थितमिन्द्रजितं रथे॥ २७॥
verses.m: Transporting Indrajit, who was exceedingly difficult to overcome, seated as he was in the chariot, when commanded as aforesaid by him, the charioteer drove in his chariot to the place where that son of the wind-god was. (27)

verses.text:
सोऽभ्युपेत्य शरान् खड्गान् पट्टिशांश्च परश्वधान्।
अभ्यवर्षत दुर्धर्षः कपिमूर्धनि राक्षसः॥ २८॥
verses.m: Going near, that ogre, who was difficult to overpower, let fall arrows, swords, sharp-edged spears and axes on the head of the monkey, Hanumān. (28)

verses.text:
तानि शस्त्राणि घोराणि प्रतिगृह्य स मारुतिः।
रोषेण महताविष्टो वाक्यं चेदमुवाच ह॥ २९॥
verses.m: Being attacked with those deadly weapons on his own head, they say, that son of the wind-god was seized with great fury and spoke as follows: (29)

verses.text:
युध्यस्व यदि शूरोऽसि रावणात्मज दुर्मते।
वायुपुत्रं समासाद्य न जीवन् प्रतियास्यसि॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Fight if you are a hero, O evil-minded Indrajit (sprung from the loins of Rāvaṇa)! Having met the son of the wind-god in me, you shall not be able to return alive. (30)

verses.text:
बाहुभ्यां सम्प्रयुध्यस्व यदि मे द्वन्द्वमाहवे।
वेगं सहस्व दुर्बुद्धे ततस्त्वं रक्षसां वरः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Strive with me with your arms, if you enter into a duel with me on the field of battle. Withstand my impetuosity, O evil-minded one! Then only will you be accounted as the foremost of the ogres.” (31)

verses.text:
हनूमन्तं जिघांसन्तं समुद्यतशरासनम्।
रावणात्मजमाचष्टे लक्ष्मणाय विभीषणः॥ ३२॥
